title: The shipped step description drifts from the sentence drill.mjs measures the client under, and nothing goes red
description:
FAIL-OPEN in the check, plus a FALSE-CLAIM in two places that assert the coupling exists. Found by /code-review lens 4 over 0923016..HEAD.

tools/jscheck/drill.mjs:53-75 (PAGE.steps) holds a COPY of each step's description, and the arm at ~:440 measures the client against it ('the step's description rounds figures this column still supports').

TWO PLACES CLAIM SOMETHING HOLDS THEM EQUAL, and neither does:
  docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md -- 'drill.mjs carries a copy that a Go test holds to it field by field'
  tools/jscheck/drill.mjs header -- 'TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone is what keeps it honest from the other side'
MEASURED: export_test.go:1200-1233 pins views() against a Go literal IN THE TEST. It never reads drill.mjs. drill.mjs feeds its own PAGE.steps into the vm as CONFIG.steps, so the client is measured under the FIXTURE's sentence, not the site's.

MUTATION (lens 4): reword 'is half the fund column' to 'is a third of the fund column' in BOTH pkg/cmd/export/data.go:607 and pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go. Then:
  go test ./pkg/cmd/export ./internal/export  -> GREEN
  make js                                     -> 130 PASS / 0 FAIL
  make site                                   -> dist/index.html ships 'General Fund alone is a third of the fund column'
Restored; git status clean. So a reworded sentence reaches the reader with every gate green.

ab0b99e's 'the shipped <desc> was compared byte for byte with drill.mjs's copy' was a ONE-TIME MANUAL COMPARISON and is the only thing that has ever held them equal.

THE FIX HAS A PRECEDENT IN THIS SAME RANGE: harness.mjs's residualDeclaration() parses the Go source rather than spelling a copy. AGENTS.md, 'The node boundary': jscheck reaches into the shipped artifact rather than copying, because a copy checks the copy and lets the original drift.

FIX IN THIS PASS.
close_reason: Fixed in b5c7830. harness.mjs gains stepDescriptions(), which parses the Description fields out of pkg/cmd/export/data.go the way parseResidualLiteral parses the residual set, and drill.mjs's PAGE.steps takes both sentences from it instead of spelling copies. Its guard counts twice with the second count NOT presupposing the first pattern's shape, which is fisc-0flg's lesson applied in the same commit. The two claims that asserted the coupling existed were corrected rather than deleted: drill.mjs's header now says which fields the Go test holds and which it does not, and the contract doc says the same. Mutation, the one that proved the defect: reword 'is half the fund column' in data.go and in export_test.go's literal together -> Go tests still green, make js exit 1 on both columns.

title: A carried mark loses the spine's caveat: transfers/in and transfers/out are drawn at depth 1 with the qualification dropped
description:
WRONG-OUTPUT. Found by /code-review lens 3 over 0923016..HEAD; re-verified here with my own probe over both fiscal columns.

site/app.js:2668 caveatsFor reads only projection.metadata.caveats -- the caveats of the document being DRAWN. site/app.js:2641 caveatHref reads only the rung's step refs. carryResidual copies the spine's links AND their endpoint nodes into the rung; it does not carry the spine's caveats about them.

PROBE, run here through drill.mjs's own opened() over both committed columns and removed afterwards:
  sankey      (FY 2025-26)  depth0 caveatsFor transfers/in  = [transfer-legs-unpaired]
                            depth1 transfers/in DRAWN = true, caveatsFor = []
                            depth1 transfers/out DRAWN = true, caveatsFor = []
  sankey-2027 (FY 2026-27)  identical in both directions.
Residual node present at depth 1 in both.

MEASURED SETUP: testdata/sankey.golden.json declares caveat transfer-legs-unpaired with applies_to [transfers/in, transfers/out]. testdata/fund-flows.golden.json declares no caveat naming either -- its only applies_to list is only-the-general-fund-is-decomposed over five fund-group ids and fund/100. So at depth 1 the drawn document knows nothing about the spine endpoints the rung borrowed from it.

WHAT THE READER GETS: opens the General Fund, sees a Transfers In mark and a carried link panel reading 'printed by the city ... PDF p66', and the qualification the spine attaches to exactly that figure is gone. Lens 3 also measured caveatHref('working-capital-is-a-stock') = '' at depth 1, so even a caveat that WERE returned would have no link.

THIS IS fisc-ko1j.13 FROM THE OTHER SIDE. That bead fixed the DRAWN document's refs at a rung. This is the OTHER document's caveats, on marks the rung borrows from it.

AGENTS.md, 'Provenance invariants': a figure that cannot carry its qualification is not the figure the city printed. FIX IN THIS PASS, with the jscheck arm that would have caught it.
close_reason: Fixed in b5c7830. A carried node records the document it came from (carried_from, set by carryResidual); caveatsFor filters that document's caveats for such a mark and caveatHref resolves its anchor through the year's refs rather than the rung's, with the carried flag threaded from the caller because the id there is a caveat's and the question is about the node. Measured after, both columns: transfers/in and transfers/out keep [transfer-legs-unpaired] at depth 1 and link to caveats.html#caveat-sankey--transfer-legs-unpaired and #caveat-sankey-2027--transfer-legs-unpaired; the drawn fund/100 still resolves to its step document's anchor, so fisc-ko1j.13's fix is intact. The jscheck arm shipped in the same commit pins all of that per column, and the existing badge arm was narrowed to a non-carried node so it keeps testing what it was written for. Mutation: revert caveatsFor to the drawn document alone -> both new arms red, make js exit 1.

title: The per-year step join accepts a document of the wrong fiscal year, and its comment claims it cannot
description:
FAIL-OPEN, plus a FALSE-CLAIM in the comment above it. Found by /code-review lens 2 over 0923016..HEAD; re-verified here with my own probe.

internal/export/export.go:955 says 'THE PER-YEAR JOIN IS EXACT OR REFUSED'. MEASURED: 'exact' means only that the key set equals View.YearStems, that the opening year's entry agrees with Projection, and that each target was built. NOTHING COMPARES THE STEP DOCUMENT'S FISCAL YEAR TO THE YEAR ON SCREEN.

PROBE, run here and removed (internal/export/zz_lens2_probe_test.go, the well-formed two-year chain from TestAStepsPerYearJoinIsExactOrRefused with one edit):
  YearProjections: {"sankey": "fund-flows", "sankey-2027": "fund-flows"}
  export.Write(...) -> err=nil, ACCEPTED, index.html written.
A reader on FY2026-27 clicks a fund group and is shown FY2025-26's funds, with no error anywhere.

WHY THE SHIPPED SITE IS RIGHT TODAY: views() joins the steps on project.Column, and TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone pins that map. So the defect is in the seam, not in the output -- but the seam is what validate exists to be.

WHY THE EXISTING TABLE MISSES IT: TestAStepsPerYearJoinIsExactOrRefused (views_test.go:2827-2842) has rows for a missing entry, an unlisted stem, an unbuilt target, a map on a same-document step, and the OPENING year disagreeing with Projection. The opening year is protected only incidentally, by the 'one step cannot draw two documents for one year' arm. The non-opening year is protected by nothing, and there is no row for it.

THE DATA IS ALREADY THERE: both goldens carry metadata.fiscal_year and basis (measured: fund-flows 2026/adopted, fund-flows-2027 2027/adopted), and page.go:1208-1214's stepDocument decodes generated_by, sources and caveats and not those. stepDocuments already refuses a builder mismatch at page.go:1263-1267; the fiscal-year arm is its sibling.

FIX IN THIS PASS, with the row that would have caught it.
close_reason: Fixed in b5c7830. stepDocument decodes metadata.fiscal_year and basis; stepDocuments refuses a step document whose column differs from the year on screen, beside the generated_by arm it is the sibling of, and both call sites pass the year's own decoded column. Compared against the decoded column rather than the stem's spelling, because two stems here differ only by suffix. TestAStepsPerYearJoinIsExactOrRefused gains the row the table was missing -- a year pointed at the other column's step document -- and the existing opening-year row is left alone because it is refused by a different arm for a different reason. Mutation: remove the arm -> 'Write accepted a year pointed at the other column's step document'.

title: [bug] A fact's id is hashed from Row.Label while row_label publishes PrintedLabel(): two-anchor rows collide
description:
internal/fact/fact.go builds the published RowLabel from PrintedLabel() but
hashes the ID from the BARE Label:

  RowLabel:  v.Row.PrintedLabel()          // Label + " " + LabelTail
  ID:        MakeID(..., v.Row.Label, ...) // Label only

So a fact's id is keyed on a string that is NOT the row_label it publishes. Two
rows sharing a Label and differing only in LabelTail -- exactly the case
Row.LabelTail was added for -- produce the SAME id.

CONFIRMED, not theoretical. internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml rule
p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a carries the two rows p76 prints as

  Transfer From Wastewater   to Stormwater             ...
  Transfer From Wastewater   to Wastewater Replacement ...

Both hash to fisc-f-e638ee25b997 for FY2026. CheckUniqueIDs then fails the
build.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A DUPLICATE. The whole point of Row.LabelTail (landed
2026-08-21, "a row may be named by two published anchors") was to make p76
mappable, and Row.Identity() already exists and returns Label + "\x1f" +
LabelTail precisely because "uniqueness is enforced on this rather than on
Label, because two rows may legitimately share a source fund and differ only in
their destination" (internal/mapping/rule.go:330-334). The resolver knows this.
The fact model does not.

It also contradicts the fact-id-needs-the-row-label memory, which records that
row_label is in the id tuple BECAUSE a category is not unique within a rule. The
id currently carries a label that is not the published one, so the property that
memory asserts does not hold for any two-anchor row.

BLOCKS fisc-5gk.3.1 -- publishing p76 is the thing LabelTail was built for and
it cannot succeed until this is fixed.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is not obvious which way: MakeID should take
PrintedLabel() (matching what is published) or Identity() (matching what the
resolver enforces uniqueness on). They differ in the separator only, but the id
is content-addressed and permanent, so the choice is a published claim. Note
either choice CHANGES NO EXISTING FACT ID: no row in
mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml carries a label_tail, so
facts.jsonl must stay byte-identical -- and that is the test.

Found by /code-review over the 8 commits ahead of origin/main, 2026-08-22, and
confirmed by reading fact.go and rule.go.
acceptance_criteria: two rows differing only in label_tail get distinct ids; the transfers-p76 fixture builds without a CheckUniqueIDs failure; facts.jsonl is byte-identical because no shipped rule uses label_tail; the choice between PrintedLabel() and Identity() is recorded with its reason
close_reason: Landed in 3589fa2 with a fifth site neither bead named (canonicalRows pairing on Label, colliding RowIndex with omissions). MakeID takes PrintedLabel(); the reasoning and its accepted cost are in the doc comment.

comments.author: Jon Crussell
comments.text:
DECIDED: MakeID takes Row.PrintedLabel(), not Row.Identity() and not Row.Label.
fact.FromValues now passes v.Row.PrintedLabel(), which is the same string the
record publishes as row_label. The reasoning is written into fact.MakeID's doc
comment; in short:

1. AN ID MUST BE RECOMPUTABLE FROM THE RECORD IT NAMES. facts.jsonl is the
   audit trail and the id is a content address; a reader holding one line has
   to be able to re-derive its id from the fields printed on that line.
   Identity() is not one of those fields, and it cannot be recovered from
   row_label either -- "A B" could be one anchor or two. Hashing Identity()
   would leave the id keyed on a string that appears nowhere in the corpus.

2. THE TUPLE SEPARATOR MUST NOT OCCUR INSIDE A COMPONENT. That is the invariant
   MakeID's own comment rests on ("joining on a character that occurs in the
   data would let two different tuples hash identically"), and the
   fact-id-needs-the-row-label memory records the \x1f join as deliberate.
   Identity() carries a \x1f of its own; PrintedLabel() joins its anchors with
   a space and cannot.

The counter-argument -- "the resolver enforces uniqueness on Identity(), so the
id should use it" -- is answered by noticing the two uniqueness properties are
different questions asked in different places. The resolver needs "no two rows
of this rule are the same row on the page"; the id needs "no two published facts
are indistinguishable to a reader of facts.jsonl". They can disagree exactly
once: two rows with distinct identities that print the same label, e.g.
{label: "A B"} and {label: "A", label_tail: "B"}. Those two facts publish one
row_label and are indistinguishable in the data WHATEVER their ids are, so that
is a defect to refuse, not to route around. parse.go now refuses it directly
("two rows print as %q"), with CheckUniqueIDs as the backstop, and both notions
are enforced in the place each belongs.

Also fixed: fact.go's comment claiming "the label ... the parser already
enforces as unique" -- true of Identity() only -- now states both properties.

EVIDENCE. Mutating the call site back to v.Row.Label:
  TestTwoAnchorRowsGetDistinctIDs: p76 facts collide: id fisc-f-1057b78cfb78 is
  claimed twice: rule "p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a" p76 says $0.00, rule
  "p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a" p76 says $1,056,357.00 (both are
  livermore-budget-fy2026-2027 transfers/in enterprise FY2024 actual)
  TestIDIsBuiltFromTheLabelTheFactPublishes: id = fisc-f-d416a4715f4c, want
  fisc-f-2213cf22723f: the id must be a function of the published row_label
  "Transfer From Wastewater to Stormwater"

The colliding pair is rows 2 and 4 of p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a, both
labelled "Transfer From Wastewater" -- to Stormwater and to LAVWMA / Wastewater.
(The description named "to Wastewater Replacement"; that row carries no source
in the fixture, so it was never the second half of the collision.) The fixture
now builds with distinct ids, FY2026:
  fisc-f-ddd73cd88b5d  "Transfer From General Fund to Stormwater"
  fisc-f-61c80098e07b  "Transfer From Wastewater to Stormwater"
  fisc-f-20865cc38977  "to Wastewater Replacement"
  fisc-f-d042561b60b7  "Transfer From Wastewater to LAVWMA / Wastewater"

facts/facts.jsonl is byte-identical to the committed file (no shipped rule
carries a label_tail), and fisc verify is 20 passed / 0 failed / 5 vacuous /
1 skipped.

title: pp.167-170 have no decided scope either: fisc-aes's gap, one schedule over
description:
fisc-aes exists because fisc-u2v's 2026-08-21 decision covers pp.127-140 and the
scope `revenue-by-fund` ONLY, and never names a scope for p76. THE SAME GAP
EXISTS FOR pp.167-170 AND NOBODY FILED IT.

VERIFIED: `bd search scope` returns eight beads -- fisc-aes, fisc-u2v,
fisc-1wr.4, fisc-gkv, fisc-5gk.3.1, fisc-5gk.6, byob-security.5, byob-config.1
-- and not one of them decides a scope string for the department x object
schedule.

WHAT IS THERE INSTEAD IS AN ASSUMPTION. fisc-1wr.2's 2026-08-21 note says
"Once the scope axis exists, fisc-5gk.2's pp.167-170 facts carry their own
scope and are NOT IN THE SPINE GRAPH AT ALL". That sentence is load-bearing for
three separate conclusions in this backlog -- it is why fisc-1wr.2's expenditure
clause is declared blinded, why the netCells refusal (internal/project/sankey.go
:531-538) is NOT a fisc-5gk.2 blocker, and why 196 department-bearing facts are
expected not to reach the spine graph. All three rest on a scope nobody chose.

THE FAILURE IT ALLOWS is fisc-u2v's mechanism on the expenditure side, and it
is the same quiet one. pp.167-170's 49 object rows tie to the p66 spine EXACTLY
per object category in all four columns -- Wages & Benefits 81,801,011 /
83,825,633, Services & Supplies 62,849,791 / 65,188,946, total 144,650,802 /
149,014,579. That exactness is what makes doubling silent: an author writing
`scope: all-funds-gross` gets a General Fund expenditure of 289,301,604 with
every check green, because netCells keys on (kind, category, fundGroup) and the
spine cell and the detail cell are the same key.

WHAT TO SETTLE, mirroring fisc-aes:
- the scope string (e.g. expenditure-by-department), and its unprojectedScopes
  entry with a reason;
- that its reconciliation is a TIER 1 ZERO-TOLERANCE identity, not a tolerance:
  the four object categories tie to the cent, so expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine
  is the same shape as revenue-detail-ties-to-spine and needs the same
  union-of-keys and kind-restriction treatment (fisc-u2v DEFECTs 1 and 2);
- whether the department axis affects the scope at all, or whether department is
  purely a row_path component within one scope. netCells refuses a
  department-bearing fact outright today, so the answer determines whether that
  refusal is reachable.

Found while planning the backlog waves, 2026-08-22, by checking whether
fisc-aes's argument generalises. It does.
acceptance_criteria: a scope string for pp.167-170 is decided and recorded here with its unprojectedScopes reason; its reconciliation against the spine is declared tier 1 zero tolerance; whether department participates in the scope axis is answered; a test asserts GF Wages & Benefits publishes 81,801,011 and not 163,602,022
notes:
2026-08-23 THE unprojectedScopes REASON TEXT THIS BEAD WROTE OVERSTATES ITS OWN CHECK, corrected when the entry landed (fisc-5gk.2).

SECTION (1) SPECIFIES: 'expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles all 196 facts against spine facts that ARE graph-checked.'

IT RECONCILES 98. The schedule publishes 49 object rows x 4 columns, and pp.66-67 print only the two ADOPTED columns -- this bead's own section (2) says so ('only FY2026 and FY2027 adopted are RECONCILED against the spine, because pp.66-67 print no actual or revised column'), so the two halves of the decision disagreed. The FY2023-24 actual and FY2024-25 revised facts reconcile against the schedule's own printed totals at build time and against nothing on the spine.

It matters more than a normal wording slip because fisc verify PRINTS THE REASON STRING VERBATIM on the facts-are-projected line, so the overstatement was published on every run. The landed text now says '98 of its 196' and names why the other half has nothing to tie to.

A SECOND CORRECTION, to a sentence this bead inherited from fisc-u2v (3): 'for each (fiscal_year, basis) present in BOTH scopes'. Read as an intersection -- which is the natural reading and the one an implementer writes -- that lets the DETAIL opt out of a column by dropping it. Measured with a spine carrying two years and a detail carrying one: the check passes, one cell examined, a whole year of General Fund expenditure unreconciled. That is fisc-u2v's own DEFECT 2 (union of keys, never a skip) at the pair level rather than the category level.

THE RULE, as landed: THE SPINE DECIDES WHICH PAIRS MUST BE RECONCILED. A spine column with no detail behind it is a gap in the MAPPING and fails. A detail column with no spine column is a gap in the DOCUMENT and is reported in the summary as unreconciled. The asymmetry runs one way only. fisc-5gk.1 and fisc-5gk.3.1 must not copy the 'present in both' wording.
close_reason: Decided: scope expenditure-by-department for pp.167-170, department is a row_path component and not a scope axis, tier-1 zero-tolerance reconciliation restricted to kind=expenditure AND fund_group=general. Joint note with fisc-aes recorded 2026-08-23; 49 object rows re-summed off the pages. Test clause moved to fisc-5gk.2.

title: p76 transfers have no scope: fisc-u2v decided revenue only
description:
fisc-5gk.3.1 lists as its blocker on fisc-u2v: "The scope axis, the same
question as fisc-u2v but for transfers rather than revenue detail, and it must
reconcile AGAINST the spine rather than sum with it."

fisc-u2v's 2026-08-21 decision covers pp.127-140 and the scope `revenue-by-fund`
ONLY. It never names a scope for p76. fisc-4rh's decision of the same date
covers fact shape, id collision and the pairing id -- not scope. So bd reports
fisc-5gk.3.1's blocker as satisfied when the question it depends on is
unanswered.

THE FAILURE THIS ALLOWS, and it is quiet.

An author finding no scope decision reads Options.Scope's doc and writes
`scope: all-funds-gross`. p76's 176 facts join the spine projection. fisc-5gk.3
ALREADY PROVED every destination fund group ties to p66-67's TRANSFER IN cell
exactly -- which is precisely what makes the doubling silent. netCells sums
them: (transfer_in, transfers/in, general) 480,400 -> 960,800; transfer_out
general 10,037,797 -> 20,075,594; and the published transfer_residual_cents
moves from $38,086,737 to roughly double.

headline-transfer-residual and link-values-tie-to-facts both stay GREEN -- they
tie the graph to the facts it was built from, not to the document. That is
fisc-u2v's mechanism verbatim, one schedule over.

AND THE ONE CHECK THAT WOULD SEE IT IS EXEMPT THERE. fisc-u2v's
revenue-detail-ties-to-spine declares exactly one exception:
(transfer_in, transfers/in, general), because pp.127-130 print no GF Transfers
In row. That is the SAME KEY the doubled GF leg lands on.

WHAT TO SETTLE
- the scope string (e.g. transfers-by-fund), and its unprojectedScopes entry
  with a reason;
- its own reconciliation against the spine -- p76 ties to the cent on both
  budget columns and to the spine's TRANSFER IN / TRANSFER OUT rows exactly
  (fisc-5gk.3), so like the revenue side this is a TIER 1 ZERO-TOLERANCE
  identity, not a tolerance;
- and consequently that fisc-u2v's acceptance test D ("unprojectedScopes holds
  exactly the one entry") is reworded to "exactly the entries declared, one per
  mapped non-spine schedule, each with a reason". As written it collides with
  this bead and with fisc-5gk.2's.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-21.
acceptance_criteria: p76 has a decided scope string recorded here; it reconciles against the spine as a tier-1 identity; fisc-u2v's exactly-one-entry test is reworded; a test asserts the GF transfer-in leg is 480,400 and not 960,800
notes:
2026-08-24 CORRECTION, found in peer review of the p76 landing plan and
re-derived off testdata/pages/budget-p0076.txt against data/funds.yaml. Two
claims in section (2) are wrong. The DECISION stands; the reasoning under it
does not.

(1) THE OUT-SIDE TABLE CONFLATES CAPITAL INTO SPECIAL REVENUE. It gives FY2026
special-revenue 1,028,200 and capital 0. But Traffic Impact Fee (510), County
Measure D (550) and State - Gas Tax (560) are type: capital in data/funds.yaml,
and p76 lists all three as payers. The true detail split is:

  FY2026   capital 211,150      special-revenue 817,050    (sum 1,028,200)
  FY2027   capital 217,485      special-revenue 800,550    (sum 1,018,035)

data/funds.yaml's own header already said this -- "the capital funds Transfers
Out (181,971 / 210,500 / 211,150 / 217,485) is exactly p76 Traffic Imp Fee +
State Gas Tax + Measure D each year" -- so the table contradicts a figure this
repository had already derived.

(2) "IN FY2026-27 IT IS IMPOSSIBLE" IS FALSE. The bead says p76 itemises
1,018,035 of special-revenue-sourced transfers against a p67 special-revenue
TRANSFER OUT of 900,550, "which would require a NEGATIVE to-CIP of -117,485".
1,018,035 is the NON-MAJOR total, not the special-revenue part. Both years split
cleanly:

  FY2026   capital 28,584,740 - 211,150 = 28,373,590
           special-revenue 1,137,050 - 817,050 = 320,000     sum 28,693,590
  FY2027   capital 36,047,736 - 217,485 = 35,830,251
           special-revenue 900,550 - 800,550 = 100,000       sum 35,930,251

and those sums are p0073.txt:56 and p0075.txt:56 exactly.

CLAUSE (c) STILL STANDS, ON A DIFFERENT AND BETTER GROUND. pp.72-75 print
to-CIP per major fund and then ONE aggregate line for all non-major funds, so a
per-group constant would be DERIVED by difference from p67 while the pair is
PUBLISHED. That is this project's own rule, not an impossibility claim -- and it
is the stronger argument, because it does not depend on an arithmetic that turns
out to be wrong.

WHERE THE ERROR HAD SPREAD. docs/sankey-contract.md shipped the wrong
decomposition as a table, with the sentence "Capital and Internal Service pay
nothing p76 lists". mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml claimed the city
"itemises nowhere" what pp.72-75 print under a heading.
internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go carried it in a comment. All three
corrected in 19bb265, together with the arithmetic that was missing:
TestP76SourcesDecomposeTheResidualByFundType resolves every payer through
registry.FundByLabel and asserts spine_TRANSFER_OUT == p76_paid + to_CIP for all
six groups in both budget years. Proven failable -- restoring the shipped pair
reddens it, and the sum-to-residual clause stays green, because the error moved
money between two rows of one total. That is why nothing caught it for four
commits.

(3) THE unprojectedScopes REASON IN SECTION (1) OVERSTATES, which is the exact
failure mode the memory detail-ties-to-spine-shape (4) warns about and which
fisc-brx already committed once. It says the check "reconciles every fact
against spine facts that ARE graph-checked". The IN side does. The OUT side
reconciles only after adding a hand-typed constant read off pp.72-75, which are
not mapped and not fixtures; and the permanent in-leg is "reconciled" as a
published zero against an absent spine column. verify prints that string
verbatim on every run. Re-word it before it lands.
close_reason: Decided: scope transfers-by-fund for p76, tier-1 zero-tolerance reconciliation in three clauses, unprojectedScopes entry lands with fisc-5gk.3.1. Joint note with fisc-brx recorded 2026-08-23; figures re-verified off the pages. Test clause moved to fisc-5gk.3.1.

title: Revenue-detail scope: pp.127-140 double-count the spine unless the scope axis is decided
description:
Mapping pp.127-140 the obvious way publishes DOUBLE the city's General Fund
revenue, and every check stays green. This bead must be decided before any YAML
is written for fisc-5gk.1.

THE MECHANISM

internal/project/sankey.go:545 keys cells on (kind, category, fundGroup).
data/taxonomy.yaml holds 25 slugs, ALL category-level -- there is no slug for a
revenue line item. So each of p127's thirteen property-tax detail rows must
carry category: taxes/property, fund_group: general, which is the SAME cellKey
as the p66 spine fact. netCells sums them.

They are the same money. Verified:
  p0066.txt:13  Property Taxes (General Fund) FY2025-26 = 64,143,762
  p0127.txt:37  Total Property Taxes          FY2025-26 = 64,143,762

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT

- headline-ties-to-facts and link-values-tie-to-facts tie the graph to the facts
  it was built FROM, not to the document.
- Build-time CheckTotals is per-part; the p66 part and the p127 part each pass
  against their own printed totals.
- The result is a plausible wrong value, which is the exact defect class this
  project exists to prevent.

THE TWO OPTIONS, BOTH WITH A COST

(a) scope: all-funds-gross -- silently doubles GF revenue. Unacceptable.

(1) THE SCOPE STRING: `revenue-by-fund`, covering ALL of pp.127-140.

Not two scopes. Not all-funds-gross. And emphatically NOT `all-funds-gross-detail`
-- that string is verbatim the incident recorded in internal/check/coverage.go
:10-23, and adopting it would make that doc comment read as describing the real
scope rather than the near-miss it warns about.

Options.Scope's own doc (internal/project/project.go:82-88) already says scope
"selects the schedule a fact came from" and is "the guard that keeps a second
schedule's facts out of a projection built for the citywide spine". This applies
existing semantics; it does not invent an axis.

No `/` in the string: fact.ColumnPath (internal/fact/fact.go:160-176) falls back
to the rule's scope when a column carries no fund dimension, so a scope with a
slash would be indistinguishable from a column path. Every detail column will
carry a fund so the fallback never fires -- but the near-miss should not exist.

WHY pp.131-140 SHARE THE SCOPE WITH pp.127-130. They cannot double-count each
other: the General Fund has no section on pp.131-140 and pp.127-130 have no other
fund -- disjoint BY FUND, not by convention. And only TOGETHER do they reproduce
all six spine columns; split them and neither half can state completeness, and
the reconciliation degrades into two partial claims with a gap between them where
a third schedule could land unnoticed.

Counter-argument, stated fairly: the row semantics genuinely differ. A p127 row
is a line item BELOW a category; a p133 row IS a category. That is real, and it
is why someone would split the scope. It is answered by fields that already
exist -- the difference is carried by row_label vs category and by fund, both in
MakeID's tuple. Promoting it to a scope puts a guard where there is no hazard,
costs the six-group tie, and by the same logic would force a third scope for the
single `Oth Financing Source` row on p139.

The line item is the fact's row_label. Its category stays one of the ten spine
slugs. data/taxonomy.yaml ALREADY DECIDED THIS in prose -- its HIERARCHY section
says the hierarchy is "deliberately NOT used below the ten revenue categories...
Those detail lines are a rule's `label`, not a `category`. Giving each one a slug
would invent a classification the city does not make and would double the surface
on which two spellings of the same thing can drift apart." fact.MakeID's doc
comment (internal/fact/fact.go:118-125) already anticipates the thirteen p127
lines sharing one category and being told apart by label. Both were written for
this bead. RATIFIED, not relitigated.

this bead's problem and makes it worse. Add `subcategory` to cellKey and property
tax becomes FOURTEEN cells -- the spine's one plus thirteen -- all in the graph,
all summed into AllFundsGrossRevenueCents. The published headline is STILL
128,287,524, and now the node list is wrong too. Line-item identity is ORTHOGONAL
to the double-count. Only the scope axis closes it.

(3) HOW THE DETAIL RECONCILES AGAINST THE SPINE: a new TIER 1 check,
`revenue-detail-ties-to-spine`, reading Subject.Facts directly rather than any
graph, registered immediately after &factsAreProjected{} (internal/check/check.go
:179).

For each (fiscal_year, basis) present in BOTH scopes -- today FY2026 and FY2027
adopted only; pp.66-67 print no actual or revised column, so the detail's
FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 columns have no counterpart and are NOT reconciled --
group both scopes' facts by {kind, category, fund_group} and assert the sums are
EQUAL.

Three properties make this the right shape:
- The key IS cellKey's tuple, so the check is visibly the mechanism's negative:
  it asserts equality on precisely the tuple the collision would have happened on.
- A key present on only one side must sum to ZERO, which disposes of the ~40
  empty cells (p67 prints a dash for taxes/property under capital; pp.131-140
  print no such row) without a table of exceptions.
- Exactly ONE declared exception, in Go, with its reason:
  (transfer_in, transfers/in, general), for the missing GF Transfers In row.

This is a strictly STRONGER form of fisc-1wr.2's promoted clause for the revenue

(4) unprojectedScopes GAINS EXACTLY ONE ENTRY -- forced, not chosen.

A projection landing WITH the facts was the preferred answer and it cannot be
had: fisc-gxa.2 DEPENDS ON fisc-5gk.1, and fisc-oxf (schema v2, finest-grain
links) is where a fund-tier graph belongs. The facts must land before anything
draws them. Inverting that edge to keep the map empty would be worse than the
entry.

What makes the entry an honest declaration rather than a hole: coverage.go's own
comment says exempted facts are "still checked by everything above the projection
line", and here that is not a consolation but the whole coverage --
revenue-detail-ties-to-spine ties all 924 facts, cell by cell, to spine facts
that ARE graph-checked. The declaration exempts them from the graph checks and
hands them to a stronger one. describeDeclared (coverage.go:145-156) prints the
count and reason on every fisc verify run, so it is loud.

ADD THE STALE-DECLARATION FAILURE IN THE SAME CHANGE. factsAreProjected consults
the map only for UNPROJECTED facts, so the moment fisc-gxa.2 projects this scope

(2) THE ROW AND FACT COUNTS ARE RIGHT; THE TOTAL-ROW COUNT AND DEFECT 4's
ASSERTABLE COUNT ARE NOT.

231 data rows confirmed (92 on pp.127-130, 139 on pp.131-140), so 924 facts
confirmed. But "The other 81 printed rows are `Total <category>` / `Total <fund>`
lines" double-counts: there are 81 printed Total rows ALTOGETHER, of which 79 are
rule-level totals (10 category totals on pp.127-130, 69 fund totals on
pp.131-140) and 2 are cross-rule ROLLUPS -- Total General Fund (p0130.txt:40) and
Total Sources (p0140.txt:52).

DEFECT 4's "~74 assertable, not 81" is now stale in the other direction, because
fisc-w0o landed rule-level multi-part CheckTotals. The count is 80 OF 81: all 79
rule totals, plus the p130 rollup, and only p140's Total Sources unassertable
(fisc-wev, settled 2026-08-24 -- see also that bead for a second, independent
reason the rollup channel is the only one available here).

DEFECT 4's straddle list is also over-counted. It names six blocks; only FOUR
have rows on two pages -- Other Taxes (p127->128), State - Gas Tax (p133->134),
Open Space Acquisition & Mgmt (p138->139), General Liability (p139->140). The
other two are different shapes and need different rules:

  - Contributions Outsourced: its heading and its ONE row are both on p129; only
    the printed total is on p130 (p0130.txt:8, immediately after that page's
    column header). It needs total_spans_parts with a bearer part that maps ZERO
    active rows -- a path nothing in the tree exercises today.
  - City Street Sweeping Fee: its heading is on p137 but its rows AND its printed
    total are both on p138 (p0138.txt:12). It is an ORDINARY single-part p138
    rule, and its section anchor cannot be its own heading.

So five rules need total_spans_parts, not six.

(3) "THE ~40 EMPTY CELLS" IS 62, AND THE COUNT MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS LOAD-BEARING.

Section (3) says "A key present on only one side must sum to ZERO, which disposes
of the ~40 empty cells". Measured against the committed spine facts, keyed on
{kind, category, fund_group} for FY2026 and FY2027 adopted inside the
{revenue, transfer_in} restriction: ZERO value differences, and 62 one-sided keys
-- 58 spine-only keys publishing a zero fact, 2 spine-only keys publishing real
money (the declared exception, at FY2026 480,400 and FY2027 486,735), and 4
detail-only keys, all zero: (revenue, other-financing-sources, special-revenue)
in both years and (transfer_in, transfers/in, permanent) in both years.

The number is worth correcting because a landing plan reached the opposite
conclusion from it. Reading DEFECT 2's "iterate the UNION of keys" together with
"~40", one plan proposed testing PRESENCE BEFORE VALUE so a zero-vs-absent cell
would be reported. Do not: that turns all 62 into findings, including the
permanent-funds cell fisc-u8o exists to tolerate and the eleventh category, which
has no spine counterpart in any year. Section (3)'s own sentence is the
instruction -- compare values first, and a one-sided key ties at zero. If the
asymmetry is worth surfacing it belongs in the check's SUMMARY as a count, which
is where the landed expenditure check puts its unreconciled pairs.

(4) THE DECLARED EXCEPTION IS TWO KEYS, AND THE 2026-08-23 CORRECTION IS NOT
BLOCKING.

The exception is (transfer_in, transfers/in, general) in BOTH reconciled years --
FY2026 480,400 and FY2027 486,735 -- not one key.

And the same plan read the 2026-08-23 correction as making revenue-detail-ties-
to-spine unlandable before fisc-5gk.3.1: "FAILS if that scope carries no fact on
that key" was taken to mean fisc verify is red until p76 lands. That reads only
the first branch. The correction's own closing sentence gives the second: "if no
scope covers it, the exception must say in words that the cell is unreconciled."
No scope covers it today, so the compliant declaration today is the words, naming
transfers-by-fund (fisc-aes / fisc-5gk.3.1) as what tightens it into a
cross-scope assertion when it lands. Nothing about this bead blocks on that one.

Worth strengthening while writing it, and checkable today: the exception should
also assert the DETAIL side is absent on that key. Left as a bare exemption it
would silently excuse a detail-side General Fund transfers-in fact, which is the
half of the hole the unconditional form leaves open.

Nothing else in the decision or in the four earlier correction notes changes. The
six-fund-group measurement was re-derived a THIRD time for this note, by summing
the 69 printed fund totals by fund group against p0063.txt:16-21's Table 2:
FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 tie exactly in all six groups. See fisc-wev for the two
FY2024-25 discrepancies (fisc-zl9, fisc-94b), neither of which touches a column
this bead's check reconciles.
close_reason:
Decided and now landed with fisc-5gk.1 (13751ff). All four points this bead asked
to settle held up against the pages: the scope string revenue-by-fund, line-item
identity as row_label rather than new slugs, a tier-1 reconciliation against the
spine rather than a sum with it, and one unprojectedScopes entry.

Seven correction notes in total. The last, 2026-08-24, records three
measurements of this bead's own that were wrong in ways an implementer would
have copied: all seven stated_total_deltas signs in DEFECT 5 are inverted (Cents
is stated minus mapped, so p127 declares +100 and not -1); DEFECT 4's list of six
straddles is four, because Contributions Outsourced and City Street Sweeping Fee
are different shapes; and "the ~40 empty cells" is 62, which matters because a
landing plan reasoned from it toward testing presence before value and that
would have turned all 62 into findings.

Also recorded there: the exception is two keys and not one, and the 2026-08-23
correction never blocked this lane -- "fails if that scope carries no fact on
that key" is its first branch and "if no scope covers it, the exception must say
in words that the cell is unreconciled" is its second, which is the compliant
declaration today.

The acceptance criterion's test exists: TestRevenueDetailAtSpineScopeWouldDouble
TheGeneralFund pins 12,828,752,400 against the published 6,414,376,200.

title: Structural remainder: cell relocation and dropped-column detection
description:
fisc-1wr.5 lands in two pieces. The parent's artifact/registry drift and the cross-language Normalize agreement are implementable at spine-only coverage and land in Wave A. These two want a settled resolver, so they land after the geometry column guard (fisc-yqv.2) and the coverage lanes.

CELL RELOCATION -- independently re-resolve each fact by its identity tuple (doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path, fiscal_year, basis) and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This is the check that replaced a tautological earlier draft: hashing a fact's token and then asserting the token matches can never fail. Asking the RULES where that cell is TODAY is a question the committed file cannot answer for itself. Two outcomes worth distinguishing: an id absent from the re-resolved index means the cell this fact names no longer exists; an id present at a different page/offset/token means the table moved, and the finding names both positions.

Reuses the resolver memoization from fisc-uv6, so verify still resolves each part once rather than a third time.

DROPPED COLUMN -- if a page's text carries a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column'. ACFR p34 loses one silently. Note this overlaps with fisc-yqv.2's column_headers, which catches a dropped column at resolve time; this catches it over already-built facts, which is the case where the rules were not re-run.
acceptance_criteria: a fact whose row moved is reported with both positions and is distinguishable from a fact whose cell no longer exists; the relocation pass adds no additional resolve of any part; ACFR p34's shape is a test case
notes:
2026-08-18 NOTE from fisc-yqv.2. This bead's dropped-column half cites ACFR p34
as the page that loses a column silently, and says the overlap with
fisc-yqv.2's column_headers is that the resolver catches it at resolve time
while this catches it over already-built facts.

Measured: ACFR p34 is one of the 124 pages where the -layout line structure and
the geometry clustering disagree, so the resolver's column guard can NEVER run
there. It refuses the page rather than catching the drop. The overlap is smaller
than it looks and this bead is the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.
See fisc-gmx.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan -- but revisit immediately after fisc-5gk.2. Cell relocation is worth little over 240 facts from 2 pages; after both coverage lanes land there are roughly 1,580 facts across 18 more pages, which is when 'independently re-resolve each fact and assert the position matches' starts earning its keep. This bead's own note calls it the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.

title: Re-anchor the spine: 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts
description:
The claim that -layout lets the section_ordinal/stop_at workarounds go is WRONG. section_ordinal: 4 is still needed (still four occurrences of 'FY 2026-27'); stop_at: '$' is still needed (p67 still prints no TOTAL REVENUES: label); and 'line anchors' describes a resolver feature that does not exist -- anchor is a raw strings.Index (resolve.go:206) and nothing in internal/mapping is line-aware.

What breaks, all fail-closed, 5 of 10 parts:
1. MULTI-SPACE HEADER ANCHORS (3 parts: spine-expenditures p67, spine-transfers-out p67, spine-fund-balance p67). -layout prints 'Capital Funds' + 15 spaces + 'Debt Service Funds'; the single-spaced section string no longer occurs. Re-anchor to section: 'Internal Service Funds', section_ordinal: 2.
2. PAGE FOOTERS (4 parts). xberg's strip_repeating_text deleted them; -layout emits 'BUDGET FY 2025-27      Page 62'. Every part with no stop_at now swallows it. The footer carries a bare '62' which amount.Parse accepts as $62, so this is corpus-wide: every 'runs to end of page' part needs an explicit stop_at.

The mapping file's ~80-line prose preamble describes the xberg single-line shape throughout and needs rewriting, not patching.
acceptance_criteria: 240 facts, 24 columns tied, every amount_cents identical to the pre-migration values
notes: DONE (working tree, uncommitted). 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts, exactly as the bead predicted. (1) spine-expenditures p67, (2) spine-transfers-out p67, (3) spine-fund-balance p67: section 'Capital Funds Debt Service Funds Special Revenue Funds Internal Service Funds' -> 'Internal Service Funds\n', section_ordinal 2 unchanged. The bead's suggested fix was right but incomplete: the trailing newline matters, because it turns 'the last name on the header line' from a hope into a claim -- without it a fifth fund group would resolve to a start mid-header, with it the anchor disappears and fails closed. (4) spine-transfers-out p66, (5) spine-transfers-out p67, (6) spine-fund-balance p66, (7) spine-fund-balance p67: added stop_at 'BUDGET FY 2025-27'. section_ordinal 4 and stop_at '$' both re-verified as still required: p67 prints 'FY 2026-27' exactly 4 times and 'TOTAL REVENUES:' zero times. ~80-line preamble rewritten, not patched. PROOF: 240 facts / 240 distinct ids / sum(amount_cents)=255588874000, id sequence and every amount_cents byte-identical to HEAD baseline; only offset (all 240) and token (10, all '\\-' -> '-' zero cells on p67 capital FY2027) differ. 4 of 10 parts tie, 24 columns, parts_unchecked unchanged at the 6 no-total_row parts. All 240 offsets land on their token in the new page file and every token is a whole whitespace-delimited page token (no fragments). All five control totals re-derive by hand from the new page text. fisc export reproduces sankey.golden.json byte for byte apart from metadata.generated_by. go test ./... green, golangci-lint 0 issues, gofmt clean. Also corrected now-false prose in internal/mapping/rule.go (SectionOrdinal doc claimed the schedule is on one line of extracted text), testdata/README.md and docs/agents/conventions.md. Cannot bd close: blocked by open fisc-yqv.3.
close_reason: 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts. Three p67 parts moved off a spelled-out header string (-layout spaces it 14/15/9 on one half and 15/14/9 on the other) to section: 'Internal Service Funds\n' + ordinal 2. Four parts with no stop_at gained one: the running footer 'BUDGET FY 2025-27  Page 62' carries a bare 62 that amount.Parse accepts as $62. Counts re-verified independently: 'Internal Service Funds' x2, 'FY 2026-27' x4, 'TOTAL REVENUES:' x0 on p67, so ordinal 4 and stop_at '$' are still required rather than assumed. 240 facts, ids and amount_cents identical to baseline, sum 255588874000, 24 columns tie, sankey.json matches the golden but for its build stamp. Preamble rewritten, not patched.

title: Rewrite tools/extract.py on poppler; re-extract all three docs
description:
poppler-utils replaces xberg in requirements.txt.

KEEP (load-bearing): sorted output, canonical JSON, atomic writes, clean_output of stale files before writing, and the rule that Python never reads data/sources.yaml (two parties recording the sha256 independently is a real check).

DROP (xberg shape): xberg_version, config, config_sha256, table_count, pages_with_tables, NORMALIZER_VERSION.

NEW ANSWER NEEDED: poppler has no structured error channel. It writes 'Syntax Warning: Bad annotation destination' to stderr and exits 0. Record the poppler version and captured stderr per document; do not claim manifest.errors works as before.

PUBLISH PAGE TEXT AS .txt NOT .md: GitHub renders .md in the blob view and collapses the runs of spaces that ARE the grid, which would silently break the provenance deep links fisc-gxa.5 depends on. Carry the rename through corpus.go:217, export/page.go:311, site/app.js:282, export_test.go:197, and the now-false comments at corpus.go:219 and rule.go:30.
close_reason: extract.py rewritten on poppler 24.02.0, stdlib only. All 786 pages re-extracted; byte-identical across runs, locales, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH/PYTHONHASHSEED. Determinism verified by a third party on an independent re-run. schema_version bumped to 2 on both sides after review found that leaving it at 1 made a broken reader SILENT: Open() succeeded, then Page(n) returned ErrNotFound, which corpus.go documents as the normal 'no such page' case. Bumping it surfaced a real latent bug -- corpus.SchemaVersion was validating both the manifest and each table JSON, two independent contracts sharing one constant. poppler has no structured error channel; stderr is captured per invocation and the docstring says plainly that an empty errors list is not a promise every page came out whole.

title: Column-position guard in the resolver
description:
With geometry available, a value must fall within its column's x-range, derived from the header line. This is the actual payoff of the extractor switch: adopting a layout-preserving extractor and then reading it with a whitespace tokenizer (tokens(), resolve.go:744, which records byte offset only and no column position) throws away the reason for switching.

Without this guard the sparse pages produce plausible wrong values rather than errors.
acceptance_criteria: a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654 fails closed naming the row
notes:
2026-08-18 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AMENDED. The original read, verbatim:

  "a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure
  to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654
  reads correctly"

The last clause is unmeetable and this bead's own notes already said why: six of
PB200654's eight cells print a "-" that is in NO substrate, because they are
drawn as non-text. No column guard recovers a mark the PDF never wrote. Closing
on "reads correctly" would have published a false claim, so the clause moved to
fisc-8ln (whose AC lost its "or fails closed" escape in the same edit, or the
obligation would have belonged to no open bead).

The first clause is met in its fails-closed branch, which is the only branch this
lane can demonstrate: geometry is a pure CROSS-CHECK here and never selects which
tokens a row consumes, so a blank cell yields a refusal rather than a correctly
placed figure. "Resolves the figure to column 3" needs band-driven selection,
which is filed with the sparse relaxation.

WHAT LANDED, in six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only); corpus.Doc.Geometry;
the doc interface at three methods; the verbatim-copy fixture tables generalised
to {document, artifact} over both substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part,
per-page and cross-file validation; the guard itself in internal/mapping/geometry.go;
and column_headers on all ten published spine parts.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN ON THIS BEAD, each with its evidence:

(1) The count guard was NOT relaxed. The design said geometry "NECESSARILY
relaxes" positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues. That is true of
SPARSE pages and no mapped part is sparse: p66's data lines carry four value
words each and p67's carry eight, on all 24 of them, dashes included. Relaxing
would have traded the guard that caught fisc-c00 for a replacement exercised only
by the dense pages that never needed it.

(2) The gutter is the FIRST COLUMN HEADER'S x0, not the midpoint to the label
header. The design's own counterexamples refute the design: CIP p40's wrap word
"and" ends at 228.6 and CIP p29's "REVITILIZATION" at 234.85, both RIGHT of the
midpoints (213.16 and 218.67), so both would have filed into band 0. First-header-x0
(238.87 and 245.10) excludes them and keeps every real value, including the bare
leading "$" glyphs. Clearances are thin on CIP and are recorded in the code:
9.46pt left and 3.81pt right on p40.

(3) No column_headers_ordinal. The full ordered header sequence occurs exactly
once page-wide on 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167, 168, 169, 170, CIP 40 and CIP 29 --
with zero unconsumed words right of the first match on every one. Shipping five
validation branches and a selection branch that no fixture can reach, inside the
guard everything else is about to trust, was the worse trade. Ambiguity is a
refusal naming the candidate lines. Filed for when a page forces it.

(4) No geom.ErrNoGeometry sentinel. corpus.ErrNotFound already means "the
manifest does not list this artifact", and a second sentinel would have put the
artifact reader's vocabulary in the leaf that exists so mapping need not import it.

(5) Substrate agreement is BYTE equality, not the design's "normalized text".
Normalizing would paper over a genuine disagreement, and the point of a second
witness is that it is allowed to disagree.

MEASUREMENTS THE DESIGN GOT WRONG, corrected here:

- Filing by header overlap misfiles 19-30 "on the mapped pages" -- it misfiles
  ZERO on pp.66/67. Over the eight measured pages the two rules disagree on 24
  tokens: 19 zero dashes (p127, p167, p168, p169, CIP p40), 2 bare "$" glyphs and
  3 footer tokens. The doc comment and TestOverlapFilingLosesZeroDashes carry the
  corrected figure.
- The line-grouping 1:1 with -layout is NOT a corpus property. It fails on 124 of
  786 pages, and 99 more fail token agreement. No page in current or near-term
  scope fails either, and the guard refuses the rest rather than reading them
  approximately. Do not write a corpus-wide assertion of it; it is false.
- p67 has 33 non-blank lines but 24 DATA lines.

fisc-j5p's hypothesis was disproved and is recorded on that bead.
close_reason:
The column guard is live over the published citywide spine, and all 240 facts and
facts/facts.jsonl are byte-identical with it on -- what changed is what is
checked, not what is published.

Six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only, the -bbox reader and the band
model); corpus.Doc.Geometry; the mapping doc interface at three methods, with the
argument for a required method over a type assertion written down; both
verbatim-copy fixture tests generalised to {document, artifact} tables over both
substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part, per-page and cross-file
validation; the guard in internal/mapping/geometry.go; column_headers on all ten
published spine parts; and the CIP p29/p40 tests.

Evidence: spineFacts 240 and spineTiedColumns 24 with the guard on, every balance
identity and headline figure unmoved, facts.jsonl and sankey.golden.json
byte-identical, fisc verify 19 passed 0 failed.

The guard is not inert, and that is asserted rather than hoped: a rule that names
only the last three of p66's four printed headers is refused naming the row, the
token, its x-position and the column the page actually prints it in; a header pair
in the wrong order is refused as an order claim; a part one column short of the
page is refused because the header line carries a header no column claims; and a
one-column part whose two rows were fused onto one printed line is caught by the
line count, which is the case no other check can see.

AC amended and the original preserved in the notes above, along with the five
deviations from the design and the three measurements on this bead that turned
out to be wrong. Follow-ups filed: fisc-gmx (substrate disagreement, 223 of 786
pages), band-driven selection with the sparse count relaxation, StatedTotals'
substrate inconsistency, column_headers_ordinal, and the two-grid page.

title: Emit both -layout text and -bbox geometry
description:
pdftotext -layout alone CANNOT distinguish an empty cell from an absent one: on a sparse wide grid a blank cell yields no token at all. CIP p40 row PB200654 prints two figures with six blanks between and -layout gives exactly two tokens. labelledValues takes toks[:ncols] (resolve.go:378), so a figure silently lands in the wrong column -- a plausible wrong value, which is what this project fails closed on, and it makes 'absent is not zero' unenforceable. xberg's tables/*.json grid was the only artifact carrying that geometry, and pp.131-140 / pp.167-170 (the Stage 2 targets) are the sparse ones.

-bbox is also the only way to keep one existing claim reproducible: the mapping file justifies its corrected omitted_rows: [] on p67 with 'pdftotext -bbox puts ten revenue rows here at the same ten y-positions' -- the fisc-c00 evidence.

Emit pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) plus geometry/pNNNN.json (word boxes from -bbox). Strictly more useful than xberg's tables; replaces them rather than sitting beside them.
acceptance_criteria: geometry/pNNNN.json carries per-word text + bbox for every page of all three docs; a sparse-grid page (CIP p40) can be read column-correctly using it
notes: 2026-08-18 CORRECTION, from peer review of the landing plan. This bead's premise that pp.131-140 and pp.167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably FALSE. All 18 pages in that scope were checked against the emitted -bbox geometry: every data row carries exactly 4 value tokens, with '-' printed in every zero cell. They are uniformly dense. The -bbox substrate and the column guard built on it (fisc-yqv.2) are therefore not justified by any page currently in scope -- the poppler migration itself (fisc-yqv.3) IS, and demonstrably worked (p130 recovered 13 rows xberg lost). Recording the distinction so the guard's cost is not retro-justified by the extractor's success.
close_reason: Emits pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) + geometry/pNNNN.json (-bbox word boxes), replacing tables/. Geometry verified sufficient for column identity: CIP p40 PB202617's lone 500,000 at x=391.1 sits under FY 2026-27 (369.9-418.9), where a whitespace read would have filed it under FY 2024-25. Word encoding flattened to [x0,y0,x1,y1,text] after review: 18.7 -> 8.2 MiB, 41.3 bytes/word. Geometry does NOT recover a value absent from the text layer -- see fisc-8ln.

title: [epic] E0 Extraction replacement: pdftotext replaces xberg
description:
The committed xberg artifacts have silently lost data rows on exactly the pages the POC needs: PDF p167 prints a ~40-line department x object grid and pages/p0167.md retains 7; p130 prints 13 Miscellaneous Revenue detail rows and p0130.md retains 0. This is the fisc-c00 failure class, and Part.OmittedRows' doc comment forbids absorbing it in a rule -- if rows go missing between the PDF and the artifact, fix extraction.

A scratch migration replacing all 786 pages with pdftotext -layout output confirmed: all 240 spine facts reproduce with identical amount_cents AND identical ids, sankey.json matches the golden except its build stamp, all 24 columns still tie, every headline control total re-derives, output is byte-identical across runs and locales. Of 583 grouped-value tokens xberg produced that -layout does not, every one is an xberg corruption (dash-glued negatives, split digits, a lost decimal).

Ends with all three docs re-extracted, the spine re-anchored, and the money proven identical cell by cell.
close_reason: E0 complete, 6/6. pdftotext -layout plus -bbox geometry replaced xberg across all three documents; the spine was re-anchored (7 edits across 5 of 10 parts); the table substrate and markdown residue are gone. Verified in peer review of the landing plan that the rewrite did what it was for: p130's 13 Miscellaneous Revenue rows, of which xberg retained 0, are all present in the poppler artifact. One correction recorded on fisc-yqv.1: its premise that pp.131-140 and 167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably false -- all 18 pages carry exactly 4 value tokens per row.

title: StatedTotals cannot read a totals row glued to the next data row
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals cannot be read. The extracted page puts the TOTAL EXPENDITURES row and the TRANSFER OUT row on ONE physical line:

  ... 1,070,500 1,115,510 $1,061,355 $969,934 $6,984,597 $6,969,898 $19,267,561 $11,808,000 $25,077,367 $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals anchors a label-less part on stop_at ('$') and asks amountRun for the first MAXIMAL run of exactly len(columns) parsable amounts within that line. Sixteen amounts follow the anchor -- the 8 totals plus the 8 transfer-out figures -- so the maximal run is 16, never 8, and the read fails with ErrNotFound.

That is indistinguishable from 'the totals row moved', which is a genuine hard failure, so it cannot be waved through. p67's revenue totals (line 15) and total-sources (line 17) each have exactly 8 amounts after their anchor, which is why only this one part fails.

The document already distinguishes the two rows typographically: totals rows are $-prefixed and data rows are bare. internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml relies on that convention already ('the totals row is the first line whose figures are prefixed with $ -- every data row above it is bare'). The resolver does not use it.
design:
In amountRun, when a maximal run is not the wanted length AND the run begins with a $-prefixed token, also consider that run's $-prefixed PREFIX. Return it if it is exactly the wanted length.

Deliberately additive: the existing maximal-run result is computed first and preferred, so a line the resolver reads today reads identically. The new branch can only turn a failure into a success. That rules out a regression on the pages where totals are only partially $-marked, which fail closed as before.
acceptance_criteria: p67's spine-expenditures part ties its 8 column totals; p66's labelled totals and p67's revenue totals are unchanged; a line whose $-prefixed prefix is the wrong width still fails.
close_reason: Fixed: amountRun considers a run's $-prefixed prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. Deliberately additive -- the maximal run is computed and preferred first, so every line that read before reads identically and the new branch can only turn a failure into a success. p67 spine-expenditures now ties its 8 columns; the spine ties 24 of 24. Regression test TestCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunSurvivesAGluedDataRow covers the glued line, a wrong-width $-prefix, and an unchanged bare run.

title: Extraction dropped a data row: xberg strip_repeating_text eats identical rows
description:
Budget Book PDF p67 prints TEN revenue rows; data/extracted/.../pages/p0067.md carried only NINE (72 tokens where 10 rows x 8 columns = 80). Verified with 'pdftotext -bbox -f 67 -l 67': p67's revenue rows sit at y = 194, 210, 226, 241, 257, 273, 289, 304, 320, 336 -- the SAME ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows. The document omits nothing.

Rows 8-10 (Sales Taxes, Fines & Forfeitures, Licenses & Permits) are three consecutive all-dash lines. xberg's content_filter.strip_repeating_text defaults to true; it is a header/footer dedup heuristic and it treated the third identical DATA row as repeating boilerplate. Setting content_filter.strip_repeating_text=false restores all three (80 tokens, verified).

This matters far beyond one row. The project had recorded the loss as a property of the DOCUMENT -- docs/m0-spike.md finding #4, the omitted_rows comment in internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml, the OmittedRows doc comment in internal/mapping/rule.go, and fisc-mq4.7's own description all say p67 'omits' an all-zero row. It does not. Declaring it via Part.OmittedRows ('rows absent from THIS part') would launder a pipeline defect into a permanent published assertion about the City's budget, and row_label is inside fact.MakeID, so the affected facts would carry a coin-flip label.

The resolver's positional count guard (internal/mapping/resolve.go positionalValues) was CORRECTLY firing. It is the only reason this was caught.

title: Rebuild-and-diff facts.jsonl in CI
description: CI runs 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' and byte-compares the result against the committed facts.jsonl. Without this, a hand-edited facts.jsonl passes CI and the deployed site is built from different numbers than the audit trail -- the one thing a provenance gate must prevent. Pure Go, so it costs nothing and preserves the no-LFS-in-CI property.
notes: 2026-08-17 IMPLEMENTATION DEVIATION, deliberate: the description says 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)', which the tool refuses by design -- --output is resolved against the repository root and validateRepoPath (pkg/cmd/build/build.go:130) rejects absolute paths. The CI job builds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl instead (bin/ is gitignored and make clean already owns it, so the rebuild leaves the tree exactly as checked out) and compares with cmp, not 'git diff --exit-code'. cmp because git diff compares through the .gitattributes 'text eol=lf' clean filter rather than the bytes, and because the git diff form would leave the committed fact store overwritten in the workspace on failure. Recorded so the next reader does not 'fix' it back toward the description.
close_reason: The facts job rebuilds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl and byte-compares with cmp against the committed facts/facts.jsonl. Deviation from the description's literal 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' recorded in the notes -- the tool refuses absolute output paths by design.

title: Structural checks: drift, cell relocation, dropped column
description:
- artifact drift: any data/extracted file whose sha256 differs from its manifest entry; any manifest whose source_sha256 differs from the registry; any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin
- registry drift (--full only): recomputed PDF sha256 vs sources.yaml
- CELL RELOCATION: independently re-resolve each fact by row_path + column_path and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This REPLACES a check that was tautological in an earlier draft -- hashing content and then asserting the content matched can never fail independently. A mismatch means the table shifted, which is precisely the event nothing else detects.
- dropped-column detection: if a page's text has a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column' (ACFR p34 loses a column silently)

Default verify needs NO PDFs and NO Python; --full adds registry drift and runs monthly with lfs: true.
notes:
ALSO: cross-language normalizer agreement. internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one and a Go reader that normalized differently would compute different hashes for identical content.

One divergence is known and deliberate: extract.py applies Unicode NFKC, Go does not (that would mean a golang.org/x/text dependency, byob-release.10, for a transform that changes nothing in this corpus -- all 382 committed tables hash identically either way). This check is what catches it if that stops being true. The Go doc comment on Normalize cites this bead.
2026-08-17 THE CROSS-LANGUAGE NORMALIZE CHECK IS MOOT. This bead's note asks for 'cross-language normalizer agreement: internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one.' That premise died with the poppler migration (fisc-yqv.3): normalize_cell no longer exists, and tools/extract.py now writes raw 'pdftotext -layout' bytes plus -bbox geometry with NO cell normalization anywhere. The manifest hashes those raw bytes, so there is no Python normalizer for Go to agree with and nothing for the check to compare. Same staleness class as fisc-9lp.

The underlying worry is still real but has moved: amount.Normalize is now the ONLY normalizer in the pipeline, applied on the Go side at parse time, so a change to it changes what parses without changing any artifact hash. That is a unit-test concern (internal/amount already has TestNormalizeUnifiesDashes) rather than a cross-language one. The deliberate NFKC divergence the note mentions no longer exists either, because the Python side does no NFKC.

Dropped from the A4 lane rather than built. Also dropped: 'any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin' -- the field is extractor_version (currently 3) plus poppler_version ('24.02.0'), and both are checked.
2026-08-17 LANE A4 LANDED (uncommitted in the main tree; not closed -- the remainder is fisc-1wr.5.1). Four tier-0 structural checks in internal/check/structural.go, first in All()'s order:

artifacts-match-manifest -- hashes all 1572 files under data/extracted/ against the sha256 and bytes their manifest records, BOTH directions: changed bytes, a listed file that is gone, and a present file the manifest does not list. manifest.json is excluded (it cannot hash itself) and that is documented.
manifest-matches-source-registry -- each manifest's source_sha256/source_bytes/source_file against data/sources.yaml, plus the two document-id sets being the same set (a source with no extraction, an extraction with no source). No PDF: two independently written claims.
extraction-toolchain-pinned -- extractor_version and poppler_version against corpus.PinnedExtractorVersion (3) and PinnedPopplerVersion ('24.02.0'). Mutual agreement between the three docs is NOT separately asserted: each is compared to one constant, so agreement follows and a second finding would be a consequence of the first. schema_version stays gated in corpus.Open (a load failure, not a finding) because at another schema the artifact namespace itself differs.
source-pdfs-match-both-records (Full) -- the FIRST check with Full()==true, so StatusSkipped is now reachable end to end. Recomputes each data/pdf sha256 and compares against BOTH sources.yaml and the manifest. Three states, told apart: wrong bytes = FAIL (a claim about the corpus); an unsmudged Git LFS pointer or an absent file = ERROR naming the file and carrying 'git lfs pull' inline in the message (a claim about the checkout; the hint is inline because ErrHint.Error() drops it and a check's error becomes the report Summary). A pointer's oid is compared to the registry so the report says whether fetching would even reconcile the tree.

WHERE THE PIN LIVES: internal/corpus, beside SchemaVersion, as PinnedExtractorVersion/PinnedPopplerVersion. Not requirements.txt: that file is prose no Go code reads and says in as many words that poppler 'is not pinned the way a pip requirement would be'. requirements.txt now cross-references the Go constants.

New: cmdutil.ExtractedDir (corpus's private const promoted); corpus.ManifestFile, Artifacts() (replacing ArtifactPaths/Artifact), Tree(), SourceFile/SourceBytes/ExtractorVersion/PopplerVersion; registry.LoadSources + Source (strict, schema-gated, the first Go reader of the whole sources.yaml); Subject.Extractions/Sources/SourcePDFs, and Load hashes data/pdf only under Full.

Every check proven failable by mutating a file on disk (internal/check/structural_test.go, 12 mutation tests + the four --full states). Verified by neutering all four checks at once: exactly those 12 tests go red. No test needs Python, the network, or the LFS files -- the --full tests synthesize their own tiny source documents and rewrite the registry and manifests to match.

Default verify still needs no PDFs: 17 pass, 5 vacuous, 1 SKIPPED with its reason, exit 0. --full: 18 pass, exit 0. CI needed no change (confirmed: the default run over a tree with a deleted PDF still exits 0); ci.yml's header note now records that --full exists and that scheduling it is fisc-gxa.5's. Also fixed a grammar bug the lane made reachable: 'N check need --full'.

NOT built, per the scope change already on this bead: cross-language Normalize agreement (moot), cell relocation and dropped-column (fisc-1wr.5.1).
2026-08-17 ROUND 2, after peer review. Blocker and all five must/should-fixes addressed; still uncommitted, still not closed.

BLOCKER (the artifact map was checked for consistency and never for completeness) -- two new tier-0 checks, and fisc-6r5 folded in:
- extraction-emitted-every-page: page_count vs one pages/pNNNN.txt and one geometry/pNNNN.json per page, both directions (a page with no artifact, and an artifact for no page). Its own check rather than a clause of the sweep, because the sweep counts ARTIFACTS in the thousands aggregated across documents and an emptied extraction is invisible in an aggregate; this counts DOCUMENTS and prints every document's page count in the passing summary. page_count is not self-certifying, so it is witnessed twice: manifest-matches-source-registry now also compares it against sources.yaml's hand-written 'pages:', and registry.LoadSources refuses pages <= 0 -- which closes zeroing both sides.
- extractor-reported-no-errors: manifest.errors non-empty fails, naming stage/page/message. corpus now decodes errors, warnings and blank_page_count (it decoded none of them). Warnings are NOT failures -- all three docs carry some, 8 in total -- but are counted into the passing summary with the blank page count, because decoding them and saying nothing is how 'reading the warnings is the human's job' becomes nobody's.

MUST-FIX, comments that claimed more than the code did:
- The --full doc comment no longer claims to make the chain 'terminate in something nobody typed'. It now says what --full genuinely adds (bytes that disagree with the records: corruption, truncation, an unrecorded swap) and states plainly that correcting both records TO the file passes while the pages are still the old document's -- demonstrated by this package's own repoWithPDFs, which is exactly that state.

Now counts one subject per COMPARISON (factVocabulary's shape): '6 records over 3 source documents hashed: 3 data/sources.yaml entries and 3 extraction manifests'. Remove an extraction and it reads 3 and 2.
- The artifactsMatchManifest doc comment no longer says manifest.json 'is not unvouched-for'. It now says a matching hash witnesses drift SINCE EXTRACTION and nothing more; that a consistent edit of page plus manifest entry passes; that no check in this project reads the bytes of a non-cited page or of ANY of the 786 geometry artifacts; and which of the manifest's fields are compared against a second record and which are not. fisc reanchor is named as fisc-mq4.6 and not built.

Added the truncation test (comparePDF's two size branches were unreachable by a byte-flip) and a test for the sweep's unreadable-directory ERROR path (chmod 0, skipped as root).

19 mutation tests now; neutering all six checks at once turns exactly those 19 red. Default verify: 19 pass, 5 vacuous, 1 skipped, exit 0. --full: 20 pass, exit 0. facts.jsonl byte-identical, golden untouched, make fmt/vet/test/lint and -race clean.

NOT done, per instruction: the Load(fs.FS) refactor (filed separately), cell relocation and dropped-column (fisc-1wr.5.1).
2026-08-17 PARENT LANDED (commit 9a0d58a). Six tier-0 checks: artifacts-match-manifest, manifest-matches-source-registry, extraction-toolchain-pinned, extraction-emitted-every-page, extractor-reported-no-errors, source-pdfs-match-both-records (--full). Remaining in fisc-1wr.5.1: cell relocation and dropped-column detection. Cross-language Normalize agreement dropped as moot (see the note above). Not closing this bead until .1.1 lands.

title: Tier 4: coverage ratchet per (fiscal_year, basis, scope)
description:
A committed coverage_floor; verify fails if measured coverage drops below it. THIS IS WHAT LETS THE GATE LAND BEFORE MAPPING FINISHES: green at 10% coverage, regressions still blocked, floor raised as E7 progresses. Without it, 'department sums match fund totals' would be red throughout the longest epic, and a permanently red gate gets commented out.

Same treatment for transfers: a transfer-unmatched residual node under a coverage floor, since budgets often state aggregate transfers-in without matching per-fund transfers-out.
notes:
The coverage ratchet is deferred; it does not block fisc-gxa.1, which shipped. The edge assumed a projection should not exist until coverage could be ratcheted, but the ratchet's purpose is to stop coverage REGRESSING and there was no coverage to regress from.

Its second paragraph did land early, in changed form: the transfer-unmatched residual. Transfers out $59,612,734 against in $21,525,997 because p76 is unmapped, and rather than a residual node the projection publishes headline.transfer_residual_cents -- a synthetic link would have unbalanced whichever transfer node it touched, and splitting the 59.6M into matched and unmatched portions would publish a division the city never printed. It still goes stale-red when p76 lands.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan. A coverage ratchet over 2 mapped pages of 786 measures nothing; it becomes meaningful once fisc-5gk.1 and .2 have established a coverage history. This bead already carried its own deferral reasoning -- now recorded in the graph as a defer date so bd ready stops offering it.

title: Tier 1: exact, zero-tolerance checks
description: Internal to our own pipeline, so exactness is legitimate: every transfer_id has two equal legs; the graph is acyclic; every link's value_cents equals the sum of its fact_ids; every fund/department/category resolves in funds.yaml/taxonomy.yaml; facts.jsonl is sorted; no ID collisions; AGGREGATION INVARIANCE (the total at every tier depth equals the total at every other depth, which catches double-parented and orphaned nodes); and every derived:true node has a rationale and source_note.

title: Map the p66-67 spine only: all-funds control totals
description:
PROVEN: 136 facts map cleanly from Budget Book PDF pp.66-67 and all 16 column totals tie EXACTLY to the document's own printed totals (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007).

Structure: rows are 'label followed by N numbers'. p66 carries the labels and the General Fund + Enterprise columns (4 values per row). p67 carries Capital, Debt Service, Special Revenue and Internal Service (8 values per row) with NO labels -- identity is positional from p66.

p67 OMITS NO ROW AND DECLARES NO omitted_rows (fisc-c00). pdftotext -bbox shows it printing all ten revenue rows at the same ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows; an extractor deleting one of three identical all-dash rows is what made the 'Licenses & Permits' line look absent. The count is 136 real printed cells, not 128 real values plus 8 invented zeros.

Build the Sankey skeleton from the spine FIRST so the balance checks exist before the detail does. A working reference implementation is in docs/m0-spike/spine.py -- note it maps revenues only from p67 and skips that page's expenditure block.

title: fisc build emitting facts.jsonl
description: Options struct + NewCmdBuild(f, runF) + private buildRun per byob-command-shape.1; Options.Validate() first, failing with FlagErrorf before any side effects (byob-input-validation.5).
