title: Fact model: content-addressed IDs, specified total order
description:
ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, deliberately EXCLUDING amount_cents and any row/col index -- so a corrected amount is a modified line rather than delete+add, and an upstream row insertion does not renumber the file. An ID collision is a hard build error: two rules claiming the same cell is a real bug.

facts.jsonl total order: (doc_id, page, row_path, column_path, rule_id). Struct-based emission with fixed key order, no omitempty, LF, trailing newline, .gitattributes text eol=lf. verify checks the file is sorted, which catches nondeterminism in CI for free.
close_reason: internal/fact. ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|row_label|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, unit-separator joined so component boundaries cannot shift. row_label is in the tuple because row_path is NOT unique within a rule: p127 prints 13 detail lines all classified taxes/property, and taxonomy.yaml is explicit those are a label not a category -- review caught the collision and it is now a test. Excludes amount and any index, so a corrected figure is a modified line and an inserted row renumbers nothing. Order is the specified (doc_id,page,row_path,column_path,rule_id) EXTENDED by (fiscal_year,basis,id): the specified five tie for two columns of one schedule, and a non-total order defeats the sortedness check it exists to enable. Declared omissions do NOT become facts -- absent is not zero -- so the spine is 128 published facts plus 8 declared absences. amount_cents is always as-printed and sign is presentation, never an instruction to negate.

title: Locator resolution + ambiguity errors listing candidates
description:
Locator = identity, content-INDEPENDENT. For text: {page, section, row_label, ordinal}. For tables: {page, ordinal_on_page, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid} where label_fingerprint hashes only non-numeric tokens (strip [0-9,.$()%-]) and the centroid rounds to ~10pt.

Why this is separate from the integrity hash: 16 ACFR tables are byte-identical duplicates of another (one 12-way group across pp.12-23; the Budget Book has a 20-way group), so a content hash is NOT an identity. Resolution must require a unique best match; ambiguity or no-match is a hard error printing the top three candidates with their pages and first rows, via ErrHint (byob-errors.2).
notes:
NEXT STEP after fisc-mq4.1 (rule schema, landed). internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml is a working target: the M0 spike proved 136 facts come out of Budget Book pp.66-67 with all 16 column totals tying EXACTLY to the totals the document prints (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007). A reference implementation is committed at docs/m0-spike/spine.py.

Rule.ExpectedValues(part) is the count a positional read must find -- 72 on p67, not 80, because the all-zero Licenses & Permits row is omitted. A mismatch must be a hard error naming the page, never a best-effort read.
close_reason: Resolver lands in internal/mapping/resolve.go with internal/corpus as the artifact reader. Text locator is {page, section, section_ordinal, stop_at}; ordinal is mandatory because REVENUES:/EXPENDITURES: each occur twice on p66. Table locator is {ordinal, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid}, and a (page,ordinal) miss is always ErrNotFound -- never a fingerprint search that resolves elsewhere, since ACFR p12/p13 are identical in fingerprint, content hash AND bbox. Ambiguity/not-found list up to 3 candidates with line and context via ErrHint. Proven: 128 values from pp.66-67, 16/16 column totals tie exactly.

title: Rule schema + parser (substrate: text|table|manual)
description:
Page text is the PRIMARY substrate: tables miss 46% of the Budget Book's money pages, including the spine (p66-67), the transfer schedule (p76), and revenue-by-fund (p127-140). Typed string enums, not iota, for anything crossing YAML/JSON (byob-typed-string-enums-sql).

M0 spike findings that the schema MUST accommodate:
 - a logical table can span pages, and the continuation page may carry NO row labels at all (p67 is a positional continuation of p66)
 - the continuation page OMITS rows that are all-zero across its columns, so a naive positional zip silently shifts every label after the gap. Rules need an explicit omitted_rows declaration plus a row-count assertion that fails loudly on mismatch.
 - column identity is (fund_group, fiscal_year), addressed by a column_path, not by a single header string (headers span two rows and Table.columns is always empty)
close_reason: Rule schema + parser landed with review fixes. Schema expresses the spine's label-less continuation and omitted rows; validation rejects duplicate columns, multi-document files, unclassified rows and circular block anchors.

title: tools/extract.py with a deterministic serializer
description:
Standalone Python run via 'make extract' -- Go NEVER shells out to it, so there is no embedded script and no exception to the pure-Go rule (byob-release.8).

Config verified to work offline with no model download:
  {use_cache: False, disable_ocr: True, output_format: 'markdown',
   pages: {extract_pages: True}, pdf_options: {extract_tables: True, extract_metadata: True}}

Determinism requirements (these are what make committed artifacts stable):
 - sort tables by (page_number, y0, x0); do NOT trust doc.tables order (ACFR p34 emits one logical table as three fragments in REVERSE document order)

 - record n_cols per table and the page-text line each row came from
 - do NOT treat processing_warnings as a quality signal: it was empty on both documents despite a silently dropped column

Emit pages/pNNNN.md (the PRIMARY substrate) and tables/pNNNN-tNN.json.

title: internal/amount: strict fail-closed grammar + case table
description:
The most bug-prone code in the project; lands BEFORE any mapping rule exists.

Observed corruption modes that must be REJECTED or handled explicitly:
 1. digits split by whitespace: '2 40,000' for 240,000 (CIP p40) -- REJECT
 2. em-dash-as-zero glued to the next column: ACFR p54 '48,030,349 | -1,315,352 | 49,345,701' where the true reading is +1,315,352 -- REJECT a leading '-' not preceded by a column boundary
 3. '$' bleeding one cell right: p68 ['Wastewater $ ', '27,799,694 $ ', ...] -- strip orphaned $
 4. parenthesis negatives: '(71.8)' -- negative
 5. '-' means zero; '' means ABSENT -- different meanings, both occur, must not be conflated
 6. units vary (dollars/thousands/millions) and come from the rule, not the token
 7. NEW from the M0 spike: '\\-' (backslash-escaped dash) appears in the extracted markdown as a distinct zero token

Amounts are integer cents, never float. Table-driven tests with google/go-cmp per byob-testing.2, in the same commit per byob-testing.4.
close_reason: internal/amount landed: strict fail-closed grammar, all 7 corruption modes, corpus-validated. Confirmed the glued-dash corruption independently on ACFR p177 by row arithmetic.

title: A category window's centre prints a gross-of-reductions figure no page prints and calls it printed by the city
description:
WRONG-OUTPUT, reachable today. Found by the app.js audit pass of fisc-lghb, measured by driving the shipped site/app.js over fisc export's bytes at ebdb422.

Open Property Taxes on either column. d3-sankey sizes the centre at the sum of every ribbon INTO it, and markContra (site/app.js:3105) has already drawn each reduction forward at its magnitude, so the centre's value is positive lines PLUS |reductions|:

  FY2025-26  positive lines 86,444,753 + reductions 16,985,339 = 103,430,092 on the mark; the NET is 69,459,414 (= 86,444,753 - 16,985,339), which is what the overview labels the same node one click earlier.
  FY2026-27  90,641,523 + 17,749,679 = 108,391,202 on the mark; the net is 72,891,844.

NO PAGE PRINTS EITHER SIDE OF THAT COMPARISON, which is why the defect is the words and not the arithmetic. Budget Book p127's "Total Property Taxes" row prints 64,143,762 (FY2026 adopted) and 67,416,730 (FY2027 adopted) -- the General Fund's share alone. The spine's revenue/taxes/property node adds special-revenue's 5,315,652 / 5,475,114 to reach the 69,459,414 / 72,891,844 the overview labels it at, and 103,430,092 / 108,391,202 are artefacts of drawing signed lines at magnitude. Re-measured off fisc export at ebdb422: the drill-down's ribbons into revenue/taxes/property sum to 8,644,475,300 cents positive and -1,698,533,900 negative, netting the spine node's 6,945,941,400 exactly.

What the reader gets, read off the DOM the page built:
  - the mark's tspans: ["Property Taxes", "  $103.4M"] with NO diamond -- nodeFlags (site/app.js:3276) marks only d.derived, and the centre is a published node;
  - the tooltip and the detail panel (site/app.js:4998, 5078): chip 'printed by the city' beside the figure $103,430,092, then contraNote's '◇ our reading: $16,985,339 of this is printed as reductions, so $69,459,414 net of them';
  - nodeDescription (site/app.js:4742): 'Property Taxes, total $103,430,092, printed by the city, our reading: ...'.

The defect is not the drawing; it is the words 'printed by the city' and the bare label beside a figure the city did not print, on a mark with no diamond. markContra's own comment records the gross height as the design ('THE CENTRE'S FIGURE IS GROSS OF ITS REDUCTIONS, and contraNote says so on the mark'). AGENTS.md: an inferred value presented as a published one is a defect however good the chart looks. columnShare on the same tooltip already gets this right ('◇ our 21.4% of this column').

WHAT NEEDS DOING is a decision, and it is Go's to make under fisc-0ws9 (the same class: contraNote composes the net in the client): either the centre's figure is the net and the reductions are drawn so the mark's height is the net (the figure the overview labels it at), or the mark keeps its gross height and every surface that names its figure says '◇ our gross of reductions' rather than 'printed by the city'. Either way the label tspan and nodeFlags need the same answer, and tools/jscheck/chart.mjs's arm (c) -- which asserts a tspan equals fmtShortSigned(markCents(d)) -- must pin the chosen figure rather than d3's value.

Mutation for the fix: on FY2025-26's Property Taxes window, the centre's tooltip must not contain 'printed by the city' next to 103,430,092, and the arm must go red when contraNote is deleted.

Reachable at every revenue category with a contra line; on the committed corpus that is revenue/taxes/property in both columns (the only window whose ribbons carry contra, measured over all 196 answered rungs).

title: e13-sankey-merge's review loop, owed once at the merge over the whole range
description:
AGENTS.md, "Review is a loop, not a pass": on a branch of several lanes the loop runs ONCE AT THE MERGE, over the whole range, not once per lane. That is owed and has never been run. Every lane on this branch deferred it by that rule.

THE RANGE IS main..HEAD. Re-measured 2026-09-20 with the walk landed: 145 commits, 180 files, 73,479 insertions against 10,671 deletions. Pin the range to two commit ids before starting and start at <first>^.

THE LEVER IS /code-review ultra, which launches a multi-agent cloud review of the branch. It is user-triggered and billed; an agent cannot start it. A range this size is not a single-pass subject, so expect the first pass to be the expensive one and the later passes to run over the fixes.

THE LOOP, and the parts sessions skip:
  - Triage every finding as WRONG-OUTPUT, FAIL-OPEN, FALSE-CLAIM, DESIGN or HYGIENE before fixing anything.
  - Fix WRONG-OUTPUT and FAIL-OPEN in the pass; FILE the other three, unless the fix is one line in a file the pass is already touching. A pass that fixes everything writes 150-450 unreviewed lines, and those lines are where the next pass's findings come from.
  - Each fix lands with the test that would have caught it, in the same commit as its review.
  - make pre-commit and the lane's mutation proofs green before re-reviewing.
  - Re-review the range INCLUDING the fixes. This is the step that finds most.
  - Stop when a pass returns no WRONG-OUTPUT and no FAIL-OPEN finding, not when it returns nothing. Three passes minimum, five maximum.
  - The last pass's own fix ships unreviewed unless something is done about it: give that diff a narrow extra pass, or keep it small enough to say why it needs none (fisc-i92i is what happens when neither is done).
  - Every finding not fixed becomes a bead in the same session, before reporting.

A FINDING THAT TOUCHES A GOLDEN gets one extra step: regenerate, then read the diff against a rule cheap enough to check by eye, before re-reviewing. There is deliberately no -update flag in this repo.

WHAT REVIEW DOES NOT COVER, so it is not mistaken for the whole gate: that the amount parser rejects the right tokens, that extraction is byte-deterministic, that mapped rows sum to the totals the documents print, and that a locator still resolves. Those are corpus scans and arithmetic against published figures, and they stay mandatory whether or not a review ran.

THE WALK IS IN SCOPE, WHICH IT WAS NOT WHEN THIS BEAD WAS FILED. fisc-phtp.2 landed on this branch in two commits on 2026-09-20 -- the membership and then the marks -- and fisc-r0t6's emitter-fidelity test with them. That is the newest and least-reviewed work in the range and three of the four seams it touches are reader-facing: which nodes a window holds, what a derived mark is worth, and what the page refuses when the two disagree.

title: The rung answer's emitter fidelity is untested in Go: four mutations of what it writes down ship green
description:
THE FOUR MUTATIONS THAT STILL SHIP GREEN ARE A GO TEST GAP, NOT A MISSING CROSS-LANGUAGE WITNESS. Owner's ruling 2026-09-20: Go owns the correctness of what it emits and JavaScript is tested to render it without errors. The two do not check each other's work.

THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL FRAMING -- "choose the rung answer's second party" -- treated tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's membership arm as a guarantee being lost. It was scaffolding for a boundary violation: the arm existed only because site/app.js duplicated the walk. When the duplication goes, the arm has nothing to compare and that is correct, not a regression.

WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS WRITING, and it is all in Go. The four survivors -- an id dropped from a column no later step opens, a mark moved to another declared tier, every derived mark's cents perturbed by one, an endpoint dropped from a residual's ends -- share one shape: each perturbs WHAT THE EMITTER WRITES DOWN, after every internal cross-check has run. That is emitter fidelity.

THE TEST THAT CATCHES THEM, and why it is not the re-derivation internal/check/check.go warns about: assert the artifact against export.ReachOf, export.ResidualOf and export.GapOf CALLED DIRECTLY BY THE TEST, not against a second run of rungsOf. A mutation inside rungsOf's assembly then has only one side moving. The primitives themselves are held by their own fixture tests in internal/export, which is the layer below. A bug in ReachOf is that layer's to catch; a bug in what rungsOf wrote down is this one's.

SCOPE: pkg/cmd/export/rungs_test.go. Each arm ships with its mutation, run with testdata/rungs.json REGENERATED from the mutated walk so no byte pin can catch it -- the method docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md records. Update that document's matrix in the same commit.

BLOCKS fisc-phtp.2 only in the sense that it should land first; the walk does not depend on it structurally.
notes:
2026-09-20, THREE OF THE SEVEN ARE CLOSED AND FOUR REMAIN, so this bead's subject is now 9b, 11b, 12 and 13. Landed in TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes and re-measured by the method docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md sets out -- artifact regenerated from the mutated walk, rungs.mjs's membership arm blinded: (14) the mirror of the parentage guard, 106 findings; (4) every id an outward column draws is a node that step's own document holds at that tier, 106 findings; (5a) a carried id is derived or a declared endpoint and a counted id is neither, 110 findings.

WHAT THAT DOES NOT CLOSE, AND IT IS THIS BEAD'S WHOLE POINT. None of the three reads a figure. Mutation 12 -- every derived mark's in_cents and out_cents perturbed by one -- was re-run with all three in place and is STILL GREEN: the artifact regenerates with seven perturbed cents per column and go test -race ./... passes. The arithmetic witness this bead is about is unbuilt and undecided, and 9b (an id dropped from a column no later step opens) is covered by neither it nor the three above.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE MEASUREMENT AS WRITTEN. The brief for the membership guard said every id in draws[].ids is a node the STEP'S OWN document holds at that tier. That is false of the kept half: 39 of the sankey column's centre and flank ids name a fund group department-spending never mentions, because the kept half comes off the chart on screen. Outward columns are held to the step's own document; the kept half is held to the documents the column reads, which is the weaker claim and is stated as such in the test.
close_reason: Closed by TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatTheReachPrimitivesAnswer in pkg/cmd/export/rungs_test.go: each rung's path and step are taken as the artifact states them, and what its columns hold and what marks stand beside them are recomputed from export.ReachOf, export.ResidualOf and export.GapOf called by the test, over a window rebuilt from each rung's parent. All four surviving mutations -- 9b, 11b, 12, 13 -- go red with testdata/rungs.json regenerated from the mutated walk, and go test ./... shows this is the only test in the tree that reddens for any of them. One finding: moving a mark one column OUTWARD is inert, because every mark already stands at the last declared tier or the first; the live mutation moves it inward. docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md's matrix now reads eighteen caught, two inert, none green. What is still unwitnessed is the primitives' answer against the documents, which stays fisc-4lsx's arithmetic.

title: The fold is the client's fitting step: Go declares what may fold, the client decides how much fits
description:
DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-19. Go dictates what CAN be folded; the client decides HOW to fold, based on space. Folding is fit-to-viewport; what exists in a column is not.

WHAT DECLARES IT, and why this needed no new mechanism: DrillStep.Caps (a TierCap per tier -- the cap, and the plural noun its tail is counted in) and DrillStep.Widen, both in internal/export/export.go, already ship to the client in CONFIG.steps. site/app.js's expandable reads step.caps and activeTiers reads step.widen. Go was always declaring what may fold; it was additionally doing the fitting.

WHAT APPLIES IT: capColumn and foldDocument in site/app.js. They stay.

WHAT THE RUNG ANSWER SAYS: what each column HOLDS, unfolded, once per rung. It carries no cap, no hidden count, no candidates count and no column-budget dimension.

NO RIBBONS SHIP, and this is the part that looks unsafe and is not. A merged ribbon's cents is computed in the browser and fisc verify cannot witness it. The licence: every SUMMAND is a published figure link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses -- each unfolded ribbon's value_cents is in the projection document the client has already fetched, with its own fact_ids -- and the MEMBERSHIP is Go's. So the client can only add witnessed numbers, never invent one.

THE LICENCE DOES NOT REACH THE DERIVED MARKS. A residual's cents is a difference and a gap's is a shortfall; neither is a sum over published summands. Those stay Go's, computed by internal/export/marks.go and carried on the rung answer.

WHY THIS IS NOT fisc-hz2u's CANDIDATE (b) REVIVED. (b) was refused because it put a RULE on the client -- which ribbons are in the file and which are to be found elsewhere -- and a rule the client applies can be wrong in silence. There is no such rule here: no ribbons are in the file at all, and the membership is given outright rather than inferred.

WHAT IT COSTS, stated rather than discovered: the merged figure a reader sees on a folded ribbon is not covered by the gate AGENTS.md points them at. fisc-4lsx carries that.
close_reason: DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-19, and recorded as its own bead because it reverses fisc-hz2u rather than refining it. Go dictates what CAN be folded -- DrillStep.Caps and DrillStep.Widen, which already ship in CONFIG.steps -- and the client decides how much fits. capColumn and foldDocument stay in site/app.js. The rung answer says what each column HOLDS, unfolded, once per rung: no cap, no hidden count, no column-budget dimension. No ribbons ship; the client folds, so the client sums, licensed by every summand being a figure link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses over a membership Go states. The licence does not reach the derived marks, which stay Go's. Implemented under fisc-qics and fisc-phtp.2.

title: tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs and chart.mjs read rung schema 4, and the artifact is at 5
description:
tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs and tools/jscheck/chart.mjs gate on rung schema 4; the artifact is 5. site/app.js's RUNGS_SCHEMA (site/app.js:1493) is 4 too, and loadRungs refuses any other, so the page would refuse the served answer.

THE BUMP IS NOT A CONSTANT EDIT, and treating it as one is the fail-open shape. The fields both arms read -- width, cap, candidates, hidden -- are gone from the artifact, and rungs.mjs's comparison is per column budget. Rewrite the arms against 'what the column holds' first; the constant means nothing until then.

WHAT rungs.mjs SHOULD ASSERT INSTEAD, since it can no longer hold the client's fold to Go's: the client draws only ids Go named, and its tail stands for exactly the complement. Re-derive its counters so the module cannot report PASS over a comparison it did not make.

Second half of the migration fisc-phtp.2 carries; not a separate lane.
close_reason: Both arms were rewritten against a column that says what it HOLDS before either constant moved. rungs.mjs compares the membership app.js's own filter reached against Go's ids, expanding every fold first so a capped column can be asked at all, and holds the fit to the step's declared cap; chart.mjs stopped reading a tail's existence off the artifact and reads it off the DOM. The schema pins in both modules and site/app.js followed.

title: Go's rung walk answers only the capped chart, so a reader who expands a folded column and opens a mark inside it is on a rung nothing answers
description:
The emitter half is done: the walk descends the unfolded chart and answers every rung a reader can reach. The client half is not, so the defect still reaches a reader.

WHAT REMAINS: site/app.js reads rung schema 4 against an artifact at 5 and would refuse the served answer outright. fisc-kume carries the arms and the constant; fisc-22qj carries the completeness arm that could not see this bug.

THE ARM THAT HOLDS THE FIX, so it is not weakened by accident: every rung's path[len-1] must appear in its parent rung's ids or carried, in pkg/cmd/export's artifact test. Restoring a ranked truncation over the emitted column takes it red, one line per rung that stops being answered.
notes: THE MARKS ARE FOLD-INVARIANT, measured rather than argued, and worth keeping because the next session to touch ResidualOf or GapOf would otherwise re-derive it: every path the old artifact answered at both 3 and 4 columns carried byte-identical marks at both, including the three whose fold engaged under a mark. So marks are emitted once per rung and do not need a column budget.
close_reason: The client half: site/app.js reads schema 5, and the suite now drives the space the emitter answers. rungs.mjs expands every folded column before taking a rung's offers, which reaches all 196 answered rungs at both budgets with none left over either way -- so the expand-then-open click a reader makes is a click a check drives.

title: Do the drawn ribbons join the rung answer, and if so which ones
description:
GATES fisc-phtp.2's THIRD STAGE (windowFor and the marks' splice). Raised and measured 2026-09-19 while landing fisc-phtp.1.

THE QUESTION. The rung answer ships ids per column per budget and the derived marks with their amounts. It ships NO ribbons. The client looks a node's record up in the projection document it already fetched, so ids are enough for MARKS. They are not enough for RIBBONS: a ribbon the fold merged, the cap re-pointed at a tail, or a mark spliced carries a value that is a SUM, and no document prints it. A client computing that sum is computing a published figure fisc verify cannot witness -- the same argument that put the marks' cents on Go's side.

MEASURED at 3542854, off ./bin/fisc export over the committed store, gzip at Go's DefaultCompression, against the served rungs.json's own 13,234 gzipped:

  300 rungs carry 1,582 drawn ribbons in all, 5.3 per rung
  ALL ribbons      raw +358,408   gzip +20,699   (+156.4%)
  DERIVED only     raw  +21,004   gzip  +2,054   (+15.5%)

THE SPLIT IS THE ANSWER: only 96 of the 1,582 drawn ribbons -- 6.1% -- carry a value that is not already printed verbatim, by source, target, kind and cents, in either the step's own document or the chart the rung above left on screen. The other 93.9% the client can look up in a file it has already fetched. So publishing every ribbon costs ten times what publishing the ones that need publishing costs.

HOW 'PRINTED VERBATIM' WAS TESTED, so the figure can be re-derived: each drawn ribbon's (source, target, kind, value_cents) was looked for in the step's document g and in the chart on screen. A match against the chart on screen is not a document printing it -- that chart is the rung above's answer, which under this design is also Go's -- so the 96 is a floor on what Go must publish and not a ceiling.

THE CANDIDATES.
  (a) Ship every drawn ribbon. Simplest client, no lookup rule, +20,699 gzipped.
  (b) Ship only the ribbons no document prints. +2,054 gzipped, and the client looks the rest up by (source, target, kind). Costs a rule for WHICH ribbons are in the file, and that rule is a thing that can be wrong in silence -- a ribbon Go thought was printed and is not would be drawn at a value the client invented.
  (c) Ship none and let the client fold. Refused by the argument above; it is what fisc-phtp.2 exists to delete.

WHAT (b) WOULD NEED TO BE SAFE, and it is the reason this is a decision and not a size comparison: the arm that catches the silent case. A check that every drawn ribbon is either in the file or matches a document ribbon EXACTLY, run Go-side over the artifact, is what makes the omission auditable rather than assumed.

NOT URGENT FOR STAGES 1 AND 2. foldDocument and capColumn are answerable from the ids that already ship. This blocks only the third stage.
notes: 2026-09-19: superseded by fisc-lwh5, which carries the ruling and its argument. This bead's measurements of what the ribbons would have cost (+20,699 gzipped for all 1,582 drawn ribbons, +2,054 for the 96 whose value no document prints) still stand and are why the question was worth asking.
close_reason:
DECIDED (a) BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-19: the drawn ribbons join the rung answer. Go emits them with their values and the client trusts them.

THE PRINCIPLE THAT DECIDES IT, and it is why the measurement was never the question: everything is checked on the Go side and trusted on the JavaScript side; JavaScript decides only what to RENDER, based on what the user does. That is AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders' applied to a ribbon exactly as it was applied to a derived mark's cents.

WHY CANDIDATE (b) IS REFUSED RATHER THAN MERELY NOT CHOSEN. Shipping only the 96 ribbons no document prints, and having the client look the other 1,486 up by (source, target, kind), is cheaper on the wire -- +2,054 gzipped against +20,699 -- but it puts a RULE on the client: which ribbons are in the file and which are to be found elsewhere. A rule the client applies is a rule that can be wrong in silence, and a ribbon Go wrongly believed was printed would be drawn at a value the client invented. The saving buys a second place where a published figure is decided.

THE COST, MEASURED AND ACCEPTED, at 3542854 off ./bin/fisc export over the committed store, gzipped at Go's DefaultCompression: the rung answer goes from 13,234 to 33,933, +20,699 for 1,582 drawn ribbons over 300 rungs. Against what the site already ships -- 172,565 for the nineteen documents in dist/data -- and against the per-year structure at ~24,000 for the default year, that is affordable and was not the deciding factor either way.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS AND WHAT IT OBLIGES. fisc-phtp.2's later stages can now delete foldDocument's merge, capColumn's re-pointing and the marks' splices rather than keeping them client-side. The obligation is the one every published figure here carries: a ribbon's cents emitted by Go is a figure fisc verify should be able to witness, which is fisc-4lsx's question and now has a second subject.

The membership stage in flight does not ship ribbons and is unaffected; Go emitting the links is its own later commit.

title: fisc verify witnesses neither the per-year structures nor the served rung answer
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.1 (62b8615, 51bca4a). The site now serves structure-<fy>.json per fiscal year and rungs.json at the site root. Two Go tests hold them -- TestTheStructureShipsOnTheAssetChannelAndIsMeasured and TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes -- and `fisc verify` holds neither.

WHY THAT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE. AGENTS.md's gate is 'fisc verify', and the project's claim is that every figure published carries a provenance pointer and that verify fails if any link in the chain breaks. The rung answer now PUBLISHES figures: the derived marks' cents. A test in pkg/cmd/export is a build-time check on the exporter; it is not the gate a reader is told guards the published site.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a decision rather than an obvious yes: a check over a file that exists only after export has a different subject from every check in internal/check, which run over facts and projections. The honest options are (a) a check that the served rung answer's marks re-derive from the projections it was built from, (b) leaving it to the exporter's tests and saying so in AGENTS.md, or (c) folding it into fisc-phtp.2, where the client starts DEPENDING on those cents.

Relates to fisc-phtp.2, which is when a reader first sees a figure that came from this file.
notes:
2026-09-19, WHAT IS AND IS NOT WITNESSABLE HERE, settled by fisc-lwh5.

THE MERGED RIBBONS ARE NOT THIS BEAD'S SUBJECT AND CANNOT BE. The client folds, so the client sums, and a merged ribbon's cents is computed in the browser where fisc verify cannot reach it. That is a deliberate trade: every SUMMAND is a published figure link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses, and the MEMBERSHIP is Go's, so the client can only add witnessed numbers. There is no artifact for an arithmetic check to run over, because the merge happens nowhere this package can see.

SO OPTION (b) IS THE HONEST ANSWER FOR THE RIBBONS, and it was not before: say in AGENTS.md what a reader is and is not promised about a folded ribbon's figure, rather than implying a check covers it.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, and is this bead's original subject: the per-year structures and the served rung answer are held only by pkg/cmd/export's tests, not by the gate. The rung answer still publishes the DERIVED MARKS' cents -- a residual's difference, a gap's shortfall -- and fisc-lwh5's licence does not reach those, because they are not sums over published summands. They are the figures option (a) would witness.
2026-09-20, THE NUMBER THIS BEAD WAS WAITING FOR. Measured on e13-sankey-merge at e577338 and written up in docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md: with tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's membership arm blinded and testdata/rungs.json regenerated from the mutated walk each time, perturbing every derived mark's in_cents and out_cents by one cent is GREEN across make pre-commit, the export tests and the node suite. So is moving a mark to a different tier the step does declare, and so is dropping one endpoint from every residual's ends. Option (a) is what those three want, and its independence argument is now stated rather than assumed: the sum is over published summands link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses, so it is a claim about the documents the walk did not compute, which internal/check/check.go's own argument distinguishes from a re-derivation. Whether the subject may be a post-export file is still this bead's open question. fisc-r0t6 carries the wider measurement.
2026-09-20, THE SUBJECT IS NOW ON THE DEPLOY PATH AND NOT ONLY IN testdata/. fisc-phtp.2 landed: site/app.js reads which nodes each column holds and what each derived mark is worth out of the served rung answer, so every figure this bead names as unwitnessed by fisc verify is one a reader is shown rather than one a fixture holds. The client refuses a chart whose carried ribbons do not come to the answered figure, which catches a document that drifted from the answer -- it cannot catch the answer itself being wrong, which is this bead.
2026-09-22, THE GAP IS PUBLISHED AS A PROMISE TO THE READER, which moves this
from a missing check to a false claim on screen.

site/app.js's markGap gives every gap mark a source_note ending: "`fisc verify`
holds that difference to the figure the reason above declares." That sentence is
rendered into the page for a reader who clicks the mark.

MEASURED AT 74dddf2: no check fisc verify runs names a gap or a rung. The gate
line is 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, and none of the names in it
has a gap as its subject. docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md says the same thing
from the other side -- a derived mark's cents is "the one figure on this artifact
that a reader is shown and that `fisc verify` does not reach" -- and names this
bead while doing so.

SO THE SITE TELLS A READER THE PROJECT'S HEADLINE GUARANTEE COVERS A FIGURE IT
DOES NOT COVER. What holds those cents today is a Go test in pkg/cmd/export,
which is a build-time check on the exporter and not the gate a reader is pointed
at. That is this bead's option (a) with a reason attached, and it is why the
priority moved.

TWO WAYS TO MAKE THE SENTENCE TRUE, and they are not equivalent: land the check,
or say what actually holds the figure. The second is a one-line edit and is
honest; it is also the weaker outcome, because the sentence is only worth
printing if something can go red.

THE SENTENCE IS COMPOSED IN THE CLIENT, which is fisc-mx5o -- so whoever corrects
it should decide whether the correction belongs in JavaScript at all, or whether
the prose moves to Go in the same change and the sentence is then written where
the check that would hold it lives.

title: Delete the client's shaping: app.js reads Go's answer instead of recomputing it
description:
STAGE 3 OF fisc-phtp, split out 2026-09-19, and THE LAST THING TO LAND.

DELETE, replaced by a lookup into the rung answer: filterLinks, sideOf, windowFor, carryResidual, markGap. shapeFor becomes 'find my rung, read its columns'.

KEEP, and capColumn and foldDocument are the two that surprise: d3-sankey positions and layOut, tooltips, focus, transitions, the year control, the paint functions -- AND the fold. Go declares what CAN be folded, through DrillStep.Caps and DrillStep.Widen, which already ship in CONFIG.steps; the client decides how much fits and merges the ribbons of what did not. Ranking a column against a cap is fitting, and fitting is the client's. What MOVES stays in JavaScript.

A CLIENT THAT FOLDS MUST SUM, and the licence is narrower than it looks: a merged ribbon's cents is not witnessed by fisc verify, which is allowed only because every SUMMAND is a published figure link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses and the MEMBERSHIP is Go's, so the client can add witnessed numbers and never invent one. It does not reach the derived marks -- a residual's cents is a difference and a gap's a shortfall, and both stay Go's.

THIS IS BLOCKED ON fisc-xsc8 FOR A REASON THAT IS EASY TO MISS. tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs is an EQUIVALENCE arm: it drills the client and compares what app.js drew against Go's committed answer. The moment the client READS that answer instead of recomputing it, the arm compares the artifact against itself and GOES GREEN BY CONSTRUCTION -- checks that cannot fail, in the strongest guarantee this branch has, arriving disguised as a passing suite. That is the 'green because the gate fired' shape AGENTS.md says to hunt for.

So the rendering arm has to exist BEFORE the deletion, not after: every node in Go's answer reaches a mark, every link a ribbon, and nothing is drawn that the answer does not name. fisc-xsc8 is that arm and is already measured.

WHAT REPLACES THE EQUIVALENCE ARM, to be stated in the commit rather than left implicit: the Go side's own artifact test stops corroborating and becomes load-bearing, and rungs.mjs changes from 'the client agrees' to 'the client draws only what it was given, and its tail stands for exactly the rest'.
acceptance_criteria: The named functions are gone from site/app.js and shapeFor is a lookup; the chart draws identically, proven by the rendering arm rather than by eye. tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs no longer compares the client's computation to Go's -- because there is none -- and says so in its header, with its vacuity counters re-derived so the module cannot report PASS against an answer it never read. Mutation: remove one id from the served rung answer and the chart loses that mark, caught by the rendering arm; blind the arm's collection and it goes red on its own counters.
notes:
WHAT foldDocument AND capColumn ACTUALLY DO, read off site/app.js rather than off this bead, because summarising them from the staging is how this bead got its delete-list wrong. foldDocument does not only decide which nodes survive: it MERGES ribbons -- summing value_cents, unioning fact_ids, and unioning locators keyed doc-page so two legs read off one page collapse to one citation. capColumn re-points a folded node's ribbons at the tail, which then merge the same way. sideOf's order is filter, cap, fold, and each of the three transforms ribbons as well as selecting nodes. The fold is one thing, not two, which is why moving half of it was never available.

THE HALF-MIGRATED WINDOW, while it is open: rungs.json is at schema 5 and site/app.js and the two artifact-reading jscheck modules are at 4, so make js is RED on the schema gate BY DESIGN and every other gate is green. fisc-kume closes it.2026-09-20, STAGED IN TWO COMMITS by the owner's decision, and the split is not arbitrary: carryResidual (153 lines) and markGap (58) carry their own arithmetic and are 211 of the ~433, so the second commit can be dropped if time runs short without leaving a half-migrated client.

  COMMIT 1, MEMBERSHIP. filterLinks, sideOf, windowFor and shapeFor stop deriving which nodes a window holds and read draws[].ids. This is what makes site/app.js's rung fetch an input rather than a gate, and it closes fisc-2sow as a side effect.

  COMMIT 2, THE MARKS. carryResidual and markGap come out; the client reads the marks Go already emits with their cents, roles, tiers and ends.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE, and it is settled: capColumn and foldDocument. Go declares what MAY fold through DrillStep.Caps and DrillStep.Widen; the client fits. See fisc-lwh5.

WHAT HAPPENS TO tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's MEMBERSHIP ARM, stated so it is not mistaken for a regression: it compared the client's own derivation against Go's answer, and when the derivation goes the arm has nothing to compare. That is correct. Go owns the correctness of what it emits (fisc-r0t6) and JavaScript is tested to render it without errors (chart.mjs). They do not check each other's work. Delete the arm rather than leaving it green by construction, and say in the commit that its subject is gone.
close_reason: Landed in two commits, membership then the marks. site/app.js no longer derives what a window holds or what stands beside it: shapeFor looks the rung up by year stem and step key (answeredRung), heldFor turns draws[] into an id-to-column map each half is filtered by (heldBy), and carryResidual and markGap read the mark's id, role, column and cents off the rung and draw them. capColumn and foldDocument stay, per fisc-lwh5 -- Go declares what MAY fold through Caps and Widen and the client fits. filterFromNode is gone and filterToNode survives for the declared root of an overview, which Go answers no rung for. What replaced the equivalence arms: the page refuses a chart whose carried ribbons do not come to the figure it was answered, whose gap does not, whose mark id it would not compose, or whose path or step the answer does not name; rungs.mjs's membership, split and marks arms are deleted because their subject is gone rather than left green by construction. Two defects the stages found: the lookup was keyed on the fetched document's projection name, which is the same string in every year, so FY2026-27 was answered out of FY2025-26's column; and a config declaring another step for a path drew the marks of the step the answer was computed from.

title: Emit what the client renders: per-year structures, and the rung answer carrying the derived marks' amounts
description:
STAGE 1 OF fisc-phtp, split out 2026-09-19. Go already computes everything here; this stage is the decision to SHIP it. site/app.js is not touched and the equivalence arm in tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs stays a real comparison throughout, which is what makes this stage safe to land alone.

TWO ARTIFACTS, both decided on fisc-kbuo (read its 2026-09-19 notes, not its description):

(1) THE STRUCTURE, ONE PER FISCAL YEAR. dist/structure.json ships today at 868,612 raw and nothing in app.js reads it; pkg/cmd/export/data.go:28 is the only mention in the tree. Measured minified and gzipped: the whole structure is 66,438, its scaffolding (levels, cuts, identities, views) is 5,449, and the facts partition cleanly on fiscal_year -- 594/594/430/430 of 2,048, no fact in two years -- so scaffolding plus the default year is 26,623. Ship the scaffolding always and one year's facts per file.

(2) THE RUNG ANSWER, which is testdata/rungs.json's content as a served artifact rather than a fixture. It must carry what the client needs to draw without deriving: the ids per column per budget, and THE DERIVED MARKS WITH THEIR AMOUNTS. The marks' cents are published figures; a client that computes them is computing figures fisc verify cannot witness.

THE COLUMN BUDGET NEEDS NO FETCH and no decision: Go answers both in one artifact (rungWidths = {3,4}) and the client holds both, so 3-to-4 is a local lookup.

THE YEAR IS THE ONLY FETCH, and it reuses a path that exists and is guarded: showYear already tells drew, superseded and failed apart, overtaken request included, with a jscheck arm on all three.
acceptance_criteria: The per-year structures and the rung answer are built by fisc export into dist/, with schema versions bumped and pkg/cmd/export's artifact tests extended -- including vacuity guards of the shape TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes already carries, so an artifact carrying no mark, one year, or one budget is refused. site/app.js is unchanged in this stage and tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs still compares the client's own computation against Go's. Mutation: perturb one served figure and the Go artifact test goes red naming it.
notes:
2026-09-19, LANDED at 62b8615 and 51bca4a on e13-sankey-merge. Gates off that tree: make pre-commit exit 0; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped; facts/facts.jsonl unmoved; site/app.js and tools/jscheck untouched.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S TEXT, MEASURED.

(1) THE VIEWS DO NOT ALL SPAN ALL YEARS, which this bead does not say and which every per-year partition has to answer. Measured over the built structure: sankey and transfers-by-fund admit facts in FY2026 and FY2027 only; fund-flows, department-spending and department-funding span all four. structure.Build refuses a view that admits no fact, on the argument that an absent view and an empty one cannot mean one thing, so a part inherits that: a view with no fact in a year is OMITTED from that year's part. That asymmetry is also what makes the test's vacuity guard real rather than decorative -- one part omits a view and another carries every view, so the omission arm cannot go unexercised.

(2) 'THE FACTS PARTITION 594/594/430/430 OF 2,048' IS THE STRUCTURE DOCUMENT'S ADMITTED FACTS, NOT THE STORE'S. facts/facts.jsonl holds 2,382 facts spanning 2016-2027; the balance is of years and rows no view admits and was never in the structure. The partition of the document is confirmed at 430/430/594/594.

(3) 'SCHEMA VERSIONS BUMPED' IS TRUE OF THE STRUCTURE AND NOT OF THE RUNG ANSWER. DocumentSchemaVersion went 1 -> 2 and gained fiscal_year. The rung answer's wire content did not change, so it stays at 4 and testdata/rungs.json came out byte-identical -- which is the point, because the fixture now pins the SERVED bytes rather than a second call of rungsOf, and a bump with no content change would have been a false claim about the wire plus an edit to tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs that this stage had no reason to make.

WHAT THE EQUIVALENCE ARM STILL DOES, read off the make js run at 51bca4a: 227 and 228 columns over 76 rungs for FY2025-26 at 3 and 4 budgets, 221 and 222 over 74 for FY2026-27 -- the client still computing its own answer and still being held to Go's. That is what makes this stage safe to land alone, and it is what fisc-phtp.2 will take away.

FINDINGS FILED: fisc-ionw, fisc-4lsx, fisc-d7t0, fisc-1f7k, fisc-j1dz.
close_reason:
Landed at 62b8615 (per-year structures) and 51bca4a (the served rung answer) on e13-sankey-merge. The site ships structure-<fy>.json for each of the four fiscal years at schema 2 -- scaffolding verbatim in each part, that year's facts re-indexed, a view admitting no fact of the year omitted rather than shipped empty -- and rungs.json at the site root, byte-identical to testdata/rungs.json at schema 4. TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes now pins the fixture to the bytes buildAll SERVES rather than to a second call of rungsOf, so a buildAll that dropped the file can no longer leave that pin green.

site/app.js and tools/jscheck are untouched and tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs is still a real comparison -- 227/228 columns over 76 rungs for FY2025-26 and 221/222 over 74 for FY2026-27 -- which is what made this stage safe to land alone. Gates off the integrated tree: make pre-commit exit 0; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped; facts/facts.jsonl and testdata/ unmoved; no golden moved.

Three corrections to the bead's own text are in its notes, the load-bearing one being that the views do not all span all years. Findings filed: fisc-ionw, fisc-4lsx, fisc-d7t0, fisc-1f7k, fisc-j1dz. fisc-phtp.2 carries a new note on what the rung answer does and does not supply it.

title: The shaping moves to Go: the walk app.js recomputes, and the fold it keeps
description:
THE BOUNDARY IS A RULE IN AGENTS.md, 'Go vets, JavaScript renders'. This bead is the distance between that rule and the tree.

MEASURED at a9a2ca2 over site/app.js's 5,825 lines: 42 functions totalling ~2,141 lines (37%) decide WHAT is drawn rather than how it looks. The largest are carryResidual 206, capColumn 180, foldDocument 164, sideOf 111, windowFor 105, markGap 91, filterLinks 78, shapeFor 63. That is a floor, not a ceiling: the scan matched 'function name(' and missed the arrow-defined helpers.

NOT ALL OF IT MOVES, AND THE TWO EXCEPTIONS ARE THE BIGGEST. capColumn and foldDocument are FITTING, not shaping: Go declares what CAN be folded, through DrillStep.Caps and DrillStep.Widen, and the client decides how much fits in the space it has. Subtract them and the lane is the other 40 functions. Read the measurement as the size of the question, not as the size of the work.

THE TELL IS testdata/rungs.json. It is Go's vetted answer for every rung -- which columns are drawn and which ids each holds -- and it is a TEST FIXTURE. Under this boundary that file is the PAYLOAD. The only reason it has to be a fixture is that the client independently recomputes the same answer, so something has to prove the two agree.

WHICH MEANS internal/export/reach.go (Fold, ReachOf) and internal/export/chart.go are not a check that happens to mirror the client -- they are the implementation of the WALK, in the right language. What gets deleted is the client's copy of the walk, never its fold.

WHAT STAYS IN JS, so this is not read as 'move app.js to Go': d3-sankey positions and layOut, tooltips, focus, transitions, the year control, the paint functions, and the fold. About 63% of the file, plus the two functions above.

WHY SHAPING ENDED UP CLIENT-SIDE, and what that does and does not excuse: it is interaction-dependent -- windowFor runs on click, capColumn depends on a column budget that depends on viewport width. The second of those is a real reason and is why the fold stays. The first is not: the rung walk enumerates the whole reachable space, and it is finite, committed and verified.

Relates to fisc-rx1d, which carries the audit of which of app.js's paths no jscheck module drives.
notes:
WHAT THIS LANE STILL OWES BEYOND THE PORT: the marks' prose. A residual's rationale and page citation and a gap's rationale are built from labels and locators export.DecodeGraph drops, and drill.mjs pins them. Whichever side composes the words after the rewrite, that is the one piece of the two marks no Go test computes.

THE STAGE ORDER IS A CORRECTNESS CONSTRAINT, NOT A PLAN. tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs is an equivalence arm; the moment the client reads Go's answer instead of recomputing it, that arm compares the artifact against itself and cannot fail. The rendering arm (fisc-xsc8) must exist BEFORE the deletion (fisc-phtp.2). A lane that inverts them is a change nothing can see go wrong, which AGENTS.md's node boundary refuses to open review on. Tolerating a half-migrated site makes the arm MORE necessary, not less: a green suite over a visibly broken site is recoverable, a green suite over a subtly wrong one is not.

THE SITE NEED NOT BE FULLY FUNCTIONAL AT EACH COMMIT on this branch, by the owner's standing permission; full functionality is owed at the merge. THE GATES ARE NOT RELAXED WITH IT: make pre-commit exit 0, fisc verify passing, facts/facts.jsonl unmoved. Nothing in this lane touches facts or the provenance chain, so a red gate here means something went wrong that has nothing to do with a half-migrated client.

AND ONE THING THAT GETS HARDER: with goldens moving on most commits, 'regenerate, then read the diff by eye' degrades into 'regenerate'. Each commit says which goldens it expected to move and confirms nothing else did.
close_reason: Both stages landed and the boundary is in the tree. site/app.js decides no longer WHICH nodes a window holds (fisc-phtp.2 commit 1) nor WHICH marks stand beside them, where, or at what figure (commit 2); it reads Go's rung answer and draws it, refusing a chart that disagrees. What stayed is what fisc-lwh5 decided: capColumn and foldDocument, d3-sankey's positions and layOut, the tooltips, focus, transitions, the year control and the paint functions. The prose this bead's notes said the lane owed is settled on the client side -- a residual's rationale and page citation and a gap's rationale are composed from labels and locators the walk drops, and drill.mjs pins them per column. testdata/rungs.json is the payload now and not only a fixture: it is served to the page byte for byte.

title: The containment check has no exception channel, so it cannot be registered in fisc verify yet
description:
internal/structure lands with the comparison built and proven in Go tests, and
is NOT registered in internal/check. This bead is what registering it needs, so
the gap is filed rather than implied.

WHY IT CANNOT BE REGISTERED AS IT STANDS. Two pairs report a residual that is
correct arithmetic and a declared exception in the check it generalises:

  revenue-detail -> spine        136 cells, 2 disagree
      Both are (transfers/in, general), one per published column. pp.127-140
      print no General Fund transfer in; p76 does.
      internal/check/revenuedetail.go:94 declares this and prints the figure --
      480,400 in FY2026.

  transfers-detail -> spine       26 cells, 8 disagree
      pp.66-67's TRANSFER OUT includes transfers to CIP that p76 does not list.
      internal/check/transfersdetail.go:72 carries a `toCIP` add-back table and
      splits the out side into three clauses; this comparison is one clause, so
      it reports what the other two absorb.

Registering it now would make `fisc verify` fail on money that reconciles.

WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT SETTLES, and it corrects the claim in the plan that filed
fisc-c4ip: the containment check replaces the twelve checks' MACHINERY -- the
per-pair key type, restriction type, comparison loop and one-sided accounting --
and it does NOT replace their ARGUMENTS. Each schedule's exceptions are claims
about the pages and survive any rewrite. internal/check/detailtie.go's own
header says the same thing from the other side: "the checks themselves stay one
per file, because what is worth reading about each of them is the argument for
ITS schedule -- and that argument does not generalise even though the arithmetic
does." That sentence was right and is now measured.

SO THE REMAINING DESIGN is fisc-c4ip acceptance (b): how a declared exception
differs from a tolerance, and why the difference is checkable. The shape to beat
is resolveRevenueExceptions (internal/check/revenuedetail.go:191-325), whose
first arm asserts THE SCHEDULE DOES PRINT THE ROW -- an exemption for a cell
nobody prints exempts nothing, and is a false claim that outlives the scope that
was to retire it.

ALSO STILL OPEN before registration: the five edits a new check needs
(All() in internal/check/check.go, a row in TestTheCommittedCorpusVacuitySplit,
a row plus the Counts literal plus the separate lenient.Counts.Vacuous assertion
in checks_test.go, and a declaredVacuous entry if it is vacuous).
close_reason: L3.4 landed on e13-sankey-merge (child of bb83d33): the containment check had been registered in L3.1 and the twelve are now deleted against it, nine outright and three kept (see fisc-c4ip's notes for the one-by-one). What this bead measured held: containment replaced the MACHINERY and the ARGUMENTS moved into structure.BudgetBookExceptions by name, each held to its cited page line by TestEveryExceptionResidualIsPrintedWhereItSaysItIs. resolveRevenueExceptions' first arm is Reconcile's 'names a cell neither produces' arm. Forced past the open dependency on fisc-c4ip, which stays open as the decision record. Off the run: fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, 0 errored.

title: One containment check replaces twelve: every cut is an antichain, every parent sums or declares a residual
description:
The check-side half of the structure decisions. It is the one that decides
whether this is a real simplification or a rename.

THE CLAIM. Of the 52 checks registered in internal/check/check.go:165-224,
twelve exist only to police the flat scope model and are replaced by one
containment check:

  projection-scopes-are-disjoint   internal/check/scopepairs.go -- 468 lines,
                                   three arms, TWO hand-maintained tables
                                   (reconciledScopes:41, disjointScopes:59)
  facts-are-projected              with unprojectedScopes (coverage.go:73-135),
                                   a single map entry whose reason string runs
                                   to roughly 1,900 words, printed every run
  published-projection-built
  documents-are-checked
  and the eight reconciliation checks:
    expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine, revenue-detail-ties-to-spine,
    transfers-detail-ties-to-spine, funding-sources-tie-to-spine,
    departmentwide-ties-to-spine, revenue-lines-tie-to-their-categories,
    drill-reconciles-across-documents, spending-window-reconciles

ALL EIGHT ASSERT THE SAME PROPOSITION: a coarse cut equals the sum of a finer
cut. internal/check/detailtie.go:78-88 says so in the tree's own words --
detailKey "is deliberately the tuple internal/project's netCells keys on, minus
the slice: these checks are the negative of that function's collision."

THE OTHER FORTY. 23 read facts and artifacts only and do not change by one line,
including both independent witnesses (check.go:40-45): fact-token-reparses and
fact-offset-points-at-token. 17 get re-pointed at a cut, and four of those
(node-tiers-are-declared, node-hierarchy-well-formed, constraint-tier-vocabulary,
graph-acyclic) ALREADY read a cut of a hierarchy and pass over 10 documents.

THIS IS MOSTLY DELETION, which is the evidence the lock-in was structural.

THE EXCEPTION IT MUST CARRY. fisc-av0w: p0067's Internal Service column
disagrees with five other printed schedules by $250,000. That is a
printed-document contradiction, not a modelling artifact, and it survives any
rewrite. A containment check that absorbs it into a tolerance destroys a real
finding -- AGENTS.md, "Fail closed on ambiguity".

SEQUENCING, AND IT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: the containment check ships and is green
BEFORE any of the twelve is deleted. Deleting first leaves the store unguarded
while every suite reports green, which is the vacuity failure
internal/check/vacuity.go exists to name.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded answer to: (a) the containment check's exact proposition and its
arms; (b) how a declared residual differs from a tolerance, and why the
difference is checkable; (c) how fisc-av0w's $250,000 is carried as a named
exception rather than absorbed; (d) the mutation for each arm -- specifically,
dropping `fund` from the containment key must resurrect the 37 cellKey-grain
collisions and the check must NAME them; (e) which of the twelve are deleted and
which are re-pointed, one by one.
notes:
2026-09-17 L3.1 LANDED (commit after 96fda0d: cuts-tie-along-the-lattice registered, nothing deleted). Two things the tree contradicted in this bead and the plan, both measured by probing Contain over every refining pair of the six cuts rather than the two structure_test.go pinned:

(A) CONTAIN COULD NOT REACH TWO OF THE FIVE RECONCILIATIONS. departmentwide (department-by-category) and funding-sources (fund-by-department) do not refine the spine's level; they MEET it strictly below both (at category and at fund-group). Contain refused every non-refining pair as peers, so departmentwide-ties-to-spine and funding-sources-tie-to-spine -- the two that carry fisc-av0w -- were replaced by nothing. Fixed: structure.Compare relates a pair as Containment (refining) or Agreement (meeting below both), and an Agreement's columns are decided by the cut declared Reference (the spine); a pair with no reference is refused. title: A view is a cut of the structure: what declares one, and how the headline becomes a named cut
description:
The third of the structure decisions. fisc-0qyo makes grain explicit; fisc-n6yq
decides tree-or-DAG; this one decides what a DOCUMENT becomes once neither scope
nor populated-axis pattern is carrying grain.

THE PROPOSAL. A view is a CUT: an antichain of the grain lattice plus a subtree.
sankey.json becomes (grain = fund_group x category, subtree = all funds);
fund-flows.json becomes a deeper cut of the same structure. The Sankey is one
visualization of a cut, not the product.

WHAT IT REPLACES. project.Options.Scopes, PublishedDocuments()
(internal/project/project.go:165-280) and the six builder interfaces
(internal/check/subject.go:866-871) all collapse into one declaration.

THE HEADLINE IS THE HARD PART, and fisc-l25's surviving argument is exactly here:
Headline accumulates PER CELL (internal/project/sankey.go:681,683,691,693,700)
with no notion of grain, so adding `fund` to cellKey is necessary and not
sufficient. The proposal is that a headline becomes a NAMED CUT -- a total is a
sum over one antichain, and asking for a total over a non-antichain is refused
rather than computed. That is what makes fisc-l25's failure mode
(headline-ties-to-facts re-sums the same facts and reports GREEN on a doubled
number) impossible rather than merely avoided.

THE ACCEPTANCE ARITHMETIC. Whatever is decided, these four published figures must
come out unchanged, and that equality is the test:
  all_funds_gross_revenue_cents      29,996,900,700   ($299,969,007.00)
  all_funds_gross_expenditure_cents  25,409,541,200   ($254,095,412.00)
  internal_transfer_in_cents          2,152,599,700    ($21,525,997.00)
  internal_transfer_out_cents         5,961,273,400    ($59,612,734.00)
Measured at 8aa9116 from facts/facts.jsonl, FY2026 adopted, and live in
internal/project/sankey_test.go:74,103.

AND THE CUTS ALREADY AGREE. revenue 299,969,007 under the fund-group cut (60
facts) and the fund cut (216 facts), delta 0 in each of the six fund groups;
expenditure 254,095,412 under three independent decompositions (24, 78 and 72
facts along different axes). The structure is not being invented -- it is being
written down.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded answer to: (a) what syntax declares a cut, and where it lives; (b) how
a headline is named and how a non-antichain request is refused; (c) the four
published figures above, produced by the new path and compared to the old; (d)
which of internal/project's 19 documents become cuts and which, if any, stay
hand-built; (e) whether a cut is materialised on disk or computed on read.
notes:
2026-09-17 L3.3 LANDED (Lane 3, the commit after 6e40270), against the five acceptance criteria:

(a) WHAT DECLARES A CUT, AND WHERE. structure.Cut in internal/structure/cuts.go: name, scope (and rules, for the one scope printing two grains), level, kinds, fund groups, bases, department tier, placeholders -- each a claim about the pages, held to the store by ValidateCuts. A view is structure.View, built by NewView/ViewOf from a scope set over the declared cuts and identities; every scope in the store is a cut (AllCuts, TestEveryScopeInTheStoreIsACut).

(b) HOW A HEADLINE IS NAMED, AND HOW A NON-ANTICHAIN IS REFUSED. sankey.Graph builds structure.ViewOf("headline", o.Scopes) BEFORE it sums anything, and the four figures are headlineOver(view, facts) -- a sum over the facts the view admits -- not accumulated per cell as the links are drawn. NewView refuses a set holding a cut beside one that decomposes it over money both print, with both cuts and the shared kinds named; the spine beside pp.127-140 is refused as 'view "headline" is not an antichain: "revenue-detail" (fund-by-category) decomposes "spine" (fund-group-by-category) and both print [revenue transfer_in], so a total over both counts that money twice', read off projections-build in the binary. pp.127-140 beside pp.167-170 (the drill-down) is NOT refused: one prints revenue and the other expenditure.

(c) THE FOUR FIGURES, PRODUCED BY THE NEW PATH: 29,996,900,700 / 25,409,541,200 / 2,152,599,700 / 5,961,273,400, pinned in TestTheHeadlineIsANamedCut and unchanged; all ten testdata/*.golden.json byte-identical.

(d) WHICH DOCUMENTS ARE VIEWS. Every document that publishes a total or draws flows is constructed as a view by peers-overlap-only-by-declared-identity's new arm over s.Projections: the two spine years, the four drill-down columns, the four cross-tab columns, the four funding-source columns and the two transfer-network columns. The series documents -- revenue-trends, changes-in-fund-balances, fund-balances -- publish no total and are NOT views; fund-balances in particular straddles two grains by rule (two cuts, one of which decomposes the other by level and not by money, since 'other governmental' is every fund but the General Fund) and a view over it would be refused. project.PublishedDocuments and the six builder interfaces in internal/check/subject.go stay hand-built: they are document SHAPES (graph, series, drill, cross-tab), not grains, and collapsing them is fisc-<see below>.

(e) MATERIALISED OR COMPUTED. Computed on read: a view is a predicate over facts (View.Admits), built from declarations at each Graph call; nothing is written to disk for it.

ALSO: project.cellKey now carries the fund. Measured: a fund-bearing rule mis-scoped to the spine, which used to build a doubled General Fund property tax (128,287,524 for 64,143,762) with every graph check green, is now refused at build by checkDistinctLinks ('two external links from revenue/taxes/property'). TestRevenueDetailAtSpineScopeWouldDoubleTheGeneralFund became TestRevenueDetailAtSpineScopeIsRefusedByTheKey.
2026-09-18 THE OWNER'S INTENT, recorded against this bead because it is the one that decides what a view IS: see the whole city budget, drill into specific sub-funds, and visually see how money moves, with a restriction that includes only nodes upstream or downstream of an anchor such as the General Fund.

THE FIRST TWO MAP ONTO WHAT EXISTS -- the spine at depth 0, and the declared drill chain. THE THIRD IS NOT THIS BEAD'S SUBJECT and must not be folded into it: a cut here is an antichain of the CONTAINMENT lattice plus a subtree, which is how finely money is decomposed, and 'upstream/downstream of X' follows RIBBONS. Two different graphs. Conflating them is how a total over a non-antichain gets computed, which is exactly what NewView now refuses. Filed as fisc-unuk, with three decisions already taken: a lens restricts what is drawn and never what is summed; a walk stops at a transfer edge, because transfers make the flow graph cyclic; and Go precomputes closures for declared anchors.

ALSO, FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the acceptance criteria (a) through (e) are ANSWERED in the note of 2026-09-17 above, off L3.3. What holds this bead open is the dependency on fisc-0qyo, not an unanswered question -- and fisc-n6yq was force-closed past that same dependency with a stated reason. Decide whether that applies here rather than re-deriving (a)-(e).

AND THE NOTE OF 2026-09-17 CARRIES A POINTER TO NOTHING: its paragraph (d) ends 'collapsing them is fisc-<see below>', and no bead id was ever written in. Whatever that was to name is untracked.

The bead was filed; only the backfill into this note was missed. The work is tracked and was never untracked.

  (a) cut syntax        landed, structure.Cut in internal/structure/cuts.go; the collapse this bead PROPOSED and L3.3 declined is fisc-wkj8 (P3, open).
  (b) headline naming   landed, structure.ViewOf + NewView's antichain refusal, pinned by TestTheHeadlineIsANamedCut.

title: One movement printed from two ends: the structure is a DAG, or a tree drops a reading
description:
MUST BE ANSWERED BEFORE ANY STRUCTURE IS BUILT, because it decides whether the
stitched structure is a tree or a DAG, and that is not a detail that can be
retrofitted.

THE MEASUREMENT, over all 2382 facts at 8aa9116, all years and bases. On the key
(fiscal_year, basis, kind, category, fund_group, fund, department), exactly two
scope pairs share any key at all:

  revenue-by-fund + transfers-by-fund   22 shared keys
      revenue-by-fund   42,183,495.00
      transfers-by-fund 42,183,495.00    IDENTICAL TO THE CENT
      (11 keys per published year x 2 years; all transfer_in / transfers/in;
       funds 400, 401, 402, 610, 622, 640, 642, 470, 210, 288, 310)

  all-funds-gross + transfers-by-fund    2 shared keys -- NOT a real pair.
      This one is an artifact of the fund==0 sentinel and is fisc-0qyo's
      subject, not this bead's. Once grain is explicit it disappears.

SO THERE IS EXACTLY ONE. pp.127-140 print these movements at the RECEIVING fund;
p76 prints the same movements at the PAYING end. Same money, same amount, two
independent readings with two independent provenance chains.

WHY A TREE GETS IT WRONG. Containment says a node has one parent and a parent is
the sum of its children. This figure has two parents in two different
decompositions. A tree either drops one reading -- losing p76's provenance, which
is the citation a reader clicking through would land on -- or keeps both and
doubles $21,045,597 per year in any cut that spans them.

THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS THE CONTAINMENT CASE. Every one of the five
reconciledScopes entries (internal/check/scopepairs.go:41) is a refinement: a
coarse cut equals the sum of a finer one, deltas of 0. This is the one place
where two readings are PEERS rather than parent and child.

ALREADY ACKNOWLEDGED IN THE TREE: internal/check/scopepairs.go:98-105 documents
the relationship, and the shipped sankey.json caveat "transfer-legs-unpaired"
says in the reader's words that no link here carries a transfer_id.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded answer to: (a) one node with two locator sets, or two nodes joined by
an explicit same-figure identity edge; (b) what a cut does when it would traverse
both readings -- refuse, pick one by declared preference, or carry the identity
and count once; (c) which check witnesses it, and its mutation (planting a second
reading with a DIFFERENT amount must go red, not merge silently); (d) whether the
answer generalises, i.e. what happens when p76 and pp.127-140 disagree on a
figure, which they do not today.
notes:
2026-09-15 The all-funds-gross + transfers-by-fund pair in the description is confirmed to be sentinel noise and not a second DAG edge: both sides carry fund=0 for different reasons (see fisc-0qyo's note of the same date, which quotes the mapping declaring the absence). Once fund absence is representable, this bead has exactly ONE subject: revenue-by-fund + transfers-by-fund, 22 keys, 42,183,495.00 identical on both sides.
2026-09-17 THE ALL-FUNDS-GROSS PAIR DID NOT DISAPPEAR, correcting this bead's
note of 2026-09-15 and the sequencing sentence in 1f3880b's commit message. Both
predicted the pair would vanish once fund absence was representable. Re-measured
at 1f3880b over facts/facts.jsonl on
(fiscal_year, basis, kind, category, fund_group, fund, department):

  revenue-by-fund + transfers-by-fund   22 shared keys, 42,183,495.00 both sides
  all-funds-gross + transfers-by-fund    2 shared keys, STILL

  2026|adopted|transfer_in|transfers/in|enterprise|NULL|
    all-funds-gross   spine-transfers-in           p66 '13,247,000' 1324700000
    transfers-by-fund p76-transfers-in-enterprise  p76 '-'                   0

WHY THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG. c549eeb made both sides null, not one. The spine's
"this grain has no fund axis" and p76's "this row's fund resolved to nothing" are
still one numeral on a fact. What separates them is the RULE's grain --
spine-transfers-in declares fund-group-by-category, p76-transfers-in-enterprise
declares fund-by-category -- so they separate inside internal/structure, whose
Key carries Level (containment.go:18-24), and nowhere else. fisc-0qyo's answer of
2026-09-15 said the two absences are distinct and both needed; that holds. What
did not hold is the inference that the second one alone dissolves this pair.

SO THIS BEAD HAS ONE SUBJECT AND IT IS THE ONE PREDICTED, reached by a different
route: revenue-by-fund + transfers-by-fund. Both scopes' rules declare
grain: fund-by-category -- all 79 and all 5 of them -- so the two readings are
PEERS at one level, not parent and child. The tree-or-DAG framing in the
description assumed they sat at different places in a containment hierarchy.
Measured, they sit at the same one.

ALSO MEASURED: one of the 22 keys carries TWO transfers-by-fund facts (fund 610,
'Transfer From General Fund to Stormwater' 2,787,000 and 'Transfer From
Wastewater to Stormwater' 460,000). A key is not unique even within a scope.
structure.project already sums within a key (containment.go:66-69).
2026-09-17 ANSWERED by the owner, against all four acceptance criteria.

(a) TWO PEER CELLS JOINED BY AN EXPLICIT SAME-FIGURE IDENTITY EDGE, not one node
with two locator sets. Each reading keeps its own locator chain -- pp.127-140 at
the receiving fund, p76 at the paying end -- because p76 is the citation a reader
clicking a transfer OUT would land on, and merging the cells would leave a
disagreement between the documents nowhere to live but a build error.

IDENTITY IS A NEW RELATION AND NOT A ROW IN refinements. Measured against the
lattice as shipped at 513ed04: an equal-axes edge would PASS validateLattice,
because notSubset (lattice.go:211) is non-strict and returns "" on equal sets --
but declaring it symmetrically trips the cycle check at :203-206. So refinements
cannot express it either way round, and the containment DAG stays what it is:
every edge directional, every edge axis-subset-checked. The lattice as shipped
needs no change; this bead's "tree or DAG" is answered at the INSTANCE level, not
the level level, and refinements was already a DAG (LevelFundByDepartmentByCategory
has three parents, lattice.go:86-92).

(b) A CUT THAT WOULD TRAVERSE BOTH READINGS IS REFUSED unless it declares which
reading it takes. Fail closed, per AGENTS.md "Fail closed on ambiguity". Not a
declared preference table, which is the hand-maintained shape fisc-c4ip claims
containment replaces; and not silent count-once, which would make a cut not the
sum of its parts with no arithmetic on the page witnessing the collapse. This is
what makes fisc-l25's failure mode -- re-sum the same facts, report green on a
doubled number -- a construction error rather than something a table avoids.

(c) A NEW REGISTERED CHECK WITNESSES IT, over every pair of cuts at one level,
projected to that level inside Comparable's intersected restriction
(containment.go:161). Three arms: an overlapping coordinate key covered by NO
declared identity is a finding; an overlapping key under a declared identity
whose amounts DIFFER is a finding; a declared identity producing ZERO overlapping
keys is refused, for the same reason arm 1 of resolveRevenueExceptions
(internal/check/revenuedetail.go:203) asserts the schedule does print the row --
an exemption for a cell nobody prints exempts nothing (fisc-ytyw).

Mutation, three arms: plant a second transfers-by-fund reading with a DIFFERENT
amount -> red, naming the key and both amounts; delete the identity declaration
-> 22 findings; declare an identity over a pair sharing no key -> refused by arm 3.

(d) IT GENERALISES, AND THE DISAGREEING CASE ALREADY EXISTS -- correcting this
bead's "which they do not today", which is true of p76 against pp.127-140 and not
of the store. acfr-general-fund-summary also sits at fund-group-by-category, the
spine's own level. fisc-tlbp measured 15 shared cells at netCells' coarse
(kind, category, fund_group) key against 0 at the six-field one, and
internal/check/departmentwide_test.go:353-356 still carries the pair as an open
gap in those words: "the two disagree under one key and agree under the other, so
neither `reconciled` nor `disjoint` is honestly assertable". Under this answer
they are peers with unequal amounts, which is arm 2: a finding, not a merge.

WHERE IT LANDS: Lane 3 commit L3.2, a new internal/structure/identity.go plus the
check, registered and green BEFORE internal/check/scopepairs.go is deleted in
L3.4. That ordering is the point -- see the next note.
