Closed with --force because the dependency fisc-0qyo is an owner-decision bead left open with its own note saying it is closed out in code (Lane 2) and its remaining subject is fisc-y723's horn; the blocker is not this bead's to close.

title: Grain is explicit on the fact, or it stays encoded twice implicitly and neither encoding determines it
description:
SUPERSEDES the mechanics of fisc-gkv and fisc-l25 (both noted 2026-09-15 with
what was re-measured; neither is reopened). This is the decision that unlocks one
stitched, provenance-carrying structure with the Sankey as a viz over it.

THE PROBLEM. A fact's GRAIN -- the set of axes the figure is a total over -- is
never stated. It is encoded twice, implicitly: as the `scope` string, and as
WHICH COORDINATE AXES ARE LEFT EMPTY. Measured over all 2382 facts at 8aa9116,
NEITHER ENCODING DETERMINES IT:

(1) ONE SCOPE, TWO GRAINS. acfr-fund-balances splits by rule, not by scope:
    acfr-p0167-general-fund-balances       n=50, fund_group="general"
    acfr-p0167-other-governmental-fund-balances  n=40, fund_group=""
    The "" is not absence -- it is "all other governmental funds, aggregated",
    a COARSER GRAIN under the same scope.

(2) TWO SCOPES, ONE PATTERN. expenditure-by-department and
    department-funding-sources both populate all five axes, and are different
    grains: the first is fund 100 only (1 fund, 23 departments, 4 object
    categories); the second spans 63 funds and 11 departments at one category.

(3) THE SENTINEL COLLIDES TWO GRAINS ON ONE NUMERAL, and this is the sharpest
    evidence. internal/project/fundflows.go:883-887 calls `fund == 0` "the
    no-fund sentinel". All 240 all-funds-gross facts carry fund=0 meaning
    "this figure is at fund-group grain; there is no fund axis". Two
    transfers-by-fund facts carry fund=0 meaning "no fund resolved for this
    row". On the key (kind, category, fund_group, fund, department) they
    COLLIDE, per year:

      (2026, adopted, transfer_in, transfers/in, enterprise, 0, "")
        all-funds-gross    p66 spine-transfers-in          '13,247,000'  13,247,000.00
        transfers-by-fund  p76 p76-transfers-in-enterprise '-'                    0.00

    A printed $13.2M total and a printed dash, at one address. Over both
    published years: 2 keys, 26,577,000.00 against 0.00. This is AGENTS.md's
    "Absent is not zero" violated on a COORDINATE axis rather than an amount --
    and note the second fact carries BOTH zeros, amount_cents=0 (the dash, a
    real printed zero) and fund=0 (absence). Two propositions, one numeral,
    one record.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. With grain explicit, cellKey keys on
(grain, coordinates), a spine cell can never land on a detail cell's address,
and "a total" is a sum over one ANTICHAIN of the grain lattice -- which makes
double-counting a type error rather than something projection-scopes-are-disjoint
hand-declares pair by pair. Measured: shared fine keys between all-funds-gross
and revenue-by-fund is 0; at cellKey's grain (which drops `fund`,
internal/project/sankey.go:587-591) it is 37. The data does not collide; the key
does.

WHAT IT COSTS. No fact id moves: MakeID (internal/fact/fact.go:186-192) hashes
(doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path, fiscal_year, basis) and
`scope` is not in the tuple. Every line of facts.jsonl rewrites; no identity
changes; fact-ids-recompute stays green. fact.Read uses DisallowUnknownFields
(fact.go:518), so the migration cannot be silent.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded answer to: (a) what the grain VALUE is -- an ordered axis set, a named
lattice level, or something else; (b) how a rule declares it in mappings/*.yaml;
(c) what happens to Fact.Scope -- retained as a schedule name, or retired; (d)
whether `fund == 0` is retired in the same change, and what replaces it; (e) how
acfr-fund-balances' two grains are told apart once grain is explicit.
notes:
2026-09-15 SHARPENED BY TWO FURTHER MEASUREMENTS. The decision is narrower and
easier than the description above suggests.

(A) GRAIN IS A PROPERTY OF A RULE, 161 RULES OUT OF 161. Measured over all 2382
facts: exactly one rule emits more than one populated-axis pattern, and it is
p76-transfers-in-enterprise -- whose two off-pattern facts are the SAME two
sentinel facts described above. So grain does not need to be inferred per fact
and does not need a new per-fact axis-set: a rule reads one table at one grain,
and the declaration site is the rule in mappings/*.yaml. That is where the
`scope:` key already sits (mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml:3116).

(B) THE ABSENCE IS ALREADY DECLARED, AND `int` DESTROYS IT. The LAVWMA row is
not an unresolved fund -- it is a DECLARED absence, with a test. The rule's own
comment at mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml:3148-3155 reads:

  "NO fund ON THIS ROW. 'LAVWMA / Wastewater Connection' names a joint powers
   authority, not a City fund; data/funds.yaml has no entry and no alias for it,
   and internal/registry/fundlabel_test.go asserts by name that it resolves to
   nothing -- deliberately, because the alternative is silently picking
   Wastewater Connection Fees (623). The column's fund_group stands alone, which
   ColumnPath emits and which is addressable. Both budget figures are '-',
   published zeros (fisc-30j)."

The row omits `fund:` on purpose and a test asserts it. Then Fact.Fund is `int`
(internal/fact/fact.go:71), so the declared absence and the spine's "this grain
has no fund axis" both arrive as 0 and collide on a key -- 13,247,000.00 against
a printed dash.

SO THE INFORMATION EXISTS AT THE DECLARATION SITE AND IS LOST IN THE
REPRESENTATION. This is not "infer grain better"; it is "carry what the mapping
already says". That makes the decision two narrower questions:
  - how a rule states its grain, beside the `scope:` key it already states;
  - what type Fact.Fund becomes so that an absent fund is absent rather than 0
    (and note this is a THIRD meaning to keep apart from amount_cents=0, which
    on this same row is a real printed zero read from a dash).

AGENTS.md, "Absent is not zero": amount.Parse already returns ErrAbsent for
exactly this distinction on the AMOUNT axis. The coordinate axes have no
equivalent.
2026-09-15 ANSWERED by the owner: (a) a rule states its grain as a NAMED LATTICE LEVEL (grain: fund-group-by-category), with the level set and the lattice's parent/child edges declared centrally and once, so the containment check reads the lattice rather than inferring refinement from axis-set inclusion and an undeclared level is refused by name; (b) Fact.Fund becomes *int, nil is absent -- smallest diff, keeps fund numeric for data/funds.yaml lookups, at the cost of fund being the one coordinate axis with its own absence idiom. NOTE THESE ARE TWO DISTINCT ABSENCES and both are needed: the grain says WHICH AXES EXIST (the spine has no fund axis at all), and within an axis that exists, nil says THIS ROW HAS NO VALUE (the LAVWMA row). Neither subsumes the other.
2026-09-16 THREE MEASUREMENTS THAT MOVE THIS BEAD'S COST, AND ONE DECISION TAKEN.
Nothing built yet; these were taken while planning Lanes 2-5.

(1) THE DECLARATION SITE IS 163 RULES, NOT 161. mappings/*.yaml carries 177
`- id:` list items = 163 rules (each with a `scope:`) + 14 rollups. 161 emit
facts, which is the number note (A) of 2026-09-15 measured and is a count of
fact-EMITTING rules. The two that emit none are acfr-p0177-debt-by-type
(mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml:460) and acfr-p0169-other-financing
(:729), both deliberately publishing nothing yet (fisc-9tn4, fisc-qyrw).
A grain declared over zero facts cannot be checked against the store -- it is
fisc-ytyw's shape, "an exemption for a cell nobody prints exempts nothing".
So the parser must REFUSE a grain on those two, not tolerate one.

(2) "WHAT IT COSTS" IS NO LONGER THE PLAN. The description says "Every line of
facts.jsonl rewrites". Owner decided 2026-09-16 that grain lives on the RULE
and not on the fact, for now: internal/check already holds []*mapping.File
(internal/check/subject.go:340), so a grain declared beside `scope:` is
reachable from every check without touching a fact. internal/structure/cut.go's
LevelOfRule (:56) reads the declaration and KEEPS ruleAxes (:25) as the
comparison, so declared-versus-derived disagreement is red -- which is the only
thing that makes the declaration worth having. facts.jsonl does not move for
grain. Filed as fisc-<tbd> is NOT what happened: the fact-side carry is filed
as its own bead, referenced below.

(3) THE SENTINEL RETIREMENT MOVES 864 LINES, NOT 2382. Measured:
`grep -c '"fund":0' facts/facts.jsonl` = 864 of 2382. That is the whole of
Lane 2's facts.jsonl churn once grain is rule-side.

ALSO DECIDED 2026-09-16: the *int propagates to the wire. project.Series.Fund
(internal/project/trends.go) becomes *int with fact.Fact.Fund, because
dist/data/changes-in-fund-balances.json (22 values) and fund-balances.json
(9 values) publish "fund": 0 on every series today -- all ACFR fund-balance
facts carry no fund. Stopping at the fact would leave the sentinel one hop
downstream in internal/project, which is what this bead was filed to kill.
docs/acfr-history-contract.md moves with them.

HAZARD FOUND WHILE SIZING, and it is the sharpest seam in the lane.
fact.ColumnPath (internal/fact/fact.go:238) reads mapping.Column.Fund != 0 --
the SAME sentinel, on a different type -- and its output is component 5 of
MakeID's hashed tuple. An agent retiring the sentinel "properly" tidies
mapping.Column.Fund (internal/mapping/rule.go:832) in the same pass, ColumnPath
changes, and EVERY AFFECTED FACT ID MOVES WHILE fact-ids-recompute STAYS GREEN
-- it hashes the new tuple and agrees with itself. The only artifact that
catches it is a sorted id-set diff between the old and new facts.jsonl. So
mapping.Column.Fund, Counterpart.Fund (:865), Row.Fund (:920) and ColumnPath
are all OUT OF SCOPE for the sentinel retirement.
The fact-side carry referred to in (2) above is filed as fisc-y723, which
records what rule-side gives up and the three conditions that would reopen it.
(Read past the "fisc-<tbd>" placeholder in (2); fisc-y723 is the id.)
2026-09-16 LANE 2 LANDED, in two commits, and this bead's remaining subject is
only the horn recorded in fisc-y723.

c549eeb feat(fact) + feat(project) + fix(export): an absent fund is null, not 0.
  fact.Fact.Fund and project.Series.Fund are *int. Measured: facts.jsonl moved
  864 of 2,382 lines, every one "fund":0 -> "fund":null and nothing else on the
  line; sorted id-set diff empty; all ten testdata/*.golden.json byte-identical.
  The wire moved where the facts have no fund and nowhere else --
  changes-in-fund-balances.json 22 of 22 series and fund-balances.json 9 of 9,
  both previously 0, while revenue-trends.json's 231 fund values were none of
  them 0 and are unmoved. mapping.Column.Fund, Counterpart.Fund, Row.Fund and
  fact.ColumnPath deliberately keep the sentinel: fisc-12jt.

e777ea2 feat(mapping) + feat(structure): a rule declares the grain it reads its
  table at. `grain:` beside `scope:` on 161 rules; Rule.publishes() makes the
  presence requirement decidable at parse time; internal/structure keeps
  ruleAxes as the comparison and LevelOfRule refuses four disagreements.
  Measured: the 161 rules carrying `grain:` are exactly the 161 rule_ids
  facts.jsonl carries, and the two refused (acfr-p0177-debt-by-type,
  acfr-p0169-other-financing) are exactly the two that publish nothing.
  facts.jsonl UNMOVED -- the cost this bead's description put at "every line
  rewrites" was not paid.

WHAT THE GRAIN VALUES WITNESS, AND WHAT THEY DO NOT. The 161 values were written
by hand, destroyed mid-lane by a `git checkout` of the two rule files while the
work was uncommitted, and regenerated from the axes each rule's facts populate.
Regeneration reproduced the pre-loss distribution exactly (84 fund-by-category,
34 fund-by-department-by-category, 29 department-by-category, 10
fund-group-by-category, 4 category), which is the evidence it is faithful -- but
each value therefore equals its derivation by construction. The declared-versus-
derived comparison witnesses FUTURE drift, not the initial transcription. If a
later lane wants the declaration to be an independent reading of the pages, that
is a re-read of 161 schedules and it has not been done. The revert hazard is
recorded as the memory revert-a-mutation-without-git-checkout.

SEQUENCING NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS UP fisc-n6yq: it depends on this bead, not the
other way round, and this bead is now closed out in code. Its own note of
2026-09-15 said the all-funds-gross + transfers-by-fund pair was sentinel noise
that disappears once fund absence is representable -- fund absence is now
representable, so that pair should be re-measured to confirm it is gone before
the tree-or-DAG answer is written.

The refusal of a document over two scopes restating one figure is structure.NewView (a cut set that is not an antichain over money both print, or that holds both readings of an identity without naming one) and the peer check's view arm, which constructs every projection's scope set as a view.

title: tools/jscheck draws no chart, so every class, attribute and handler render() writes is unobservable
description:
DESIGN. Found while building fisc-ko1j.12.5 (W4), which needed to check what a node is DRAWN as and what a gesture on it DOES.

MEASURED DIRECTLY, not inferred. harness.mjs's domStub answers no "#chart" selector -- querySelector returns null for anything nothing planted -- so the real vendored d3 lays every selection render() builds over a null node. D3.select("#chart").size() is 0, .append("g") returns a size-0 selection, and an .attr() accessor is invoked ZERO times. Nothing is created, no attribute is written, and .on() registers no handler.

WHAT THAT COSTS. Every one of these is written by render() and readable by no check: nodeClass's class, nodeFlags' marker text, aria-label, aria-pressed, aria-keyshortcuts, tabindex, role, the rect and label geometry, and every pointer/focus/blur/click/keydown/dblclick handler. layout.mjs already says so at its LABEL_SELECTION pin; harness.mjs's KNOWN_SELECTORS entry for g.node says answering it 'would need the stub to model the <g> elements render() appends to the SVG, which no check needs yet'. W4 is the wave where that became false.

HOW W4 ROUTED AROUND IT, which is the pattern and also the complaint: the three gestures were extracted from render()'s closures into named functions (clickNode, doubleClickNode, keyNode) purely so a check could reach them, and drill.mjs's GESTURE_WIRING pins the seven lines of render() that use them AS TEXT. A source-text pin fails when someone edits the line and passes when the line is right but the selection it sits on is empty -- it witnesses spelling, not behaviour.

PLANTING #chart DOES NOT FIX IT AND IS THE TRAP. Measured: with a stub node planted, setAttribute and addEventListener work, but d3's creatorInherit reads this.ownerDocument and this.namespaceURI, which node() defines neither of, so render() THROWS at svg.append('g') -- and app.js converts that into a refusal banner. A check would then be green-because-the-gate-fired, which is the shape AGENTS.md's 'Prove it can fail' names.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: ownerDocument + namespaceURI on the stub's node(), and a byClass grammar that answers bare tags and compounds -- 'g', 'path.link', 'g.node', 'g.node rect'. Then KNOWN_SELECTORS' two 'unanswered' entries (g.node, button) both close, restoreFocus's real path runs, applyEmphasis's legend loop runs, and W4's four arms could assert the drawn DOM instead of the functions behind it.

Neighbours: fisc-rx1d's audit of which app.js paths no module drives; fisc-6at (nothing here renders CSS).
notes:
2026-09-19, RAISED P2 -> P1: this bead now GATES fisc-phtp.2, the deletion of the client's shaping, and a P2 blocking a P1 is the inversion AGENTS.md's 'Priority drifts' section says to look for.

WHY IT GATES IT. tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs is an equivalence arm -- it drills the client and compares what app.js DREW against Go's committed answer. Once the client reads that answer instead of recomputing it, the arm compares the artifact against itself and goes green by construction: eight checks that cannot fail, in the strongest guarantee this branch has, arriving disguised as a passing suite. This bead's arm -- every class, attribute and handler render() writes, currently unobservable because domStub answers no '#chart' selector -- is what will witness the client afterwards. It is the only thing that will.
2026-09-19, TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S TEXT, MEASURED WHILE LANDING IT.

(1) 'applyEmphasis's LEGEND LOOP' IS setIsolated's. This bead's WHAT IT WOULD TAKE paragraph predicts that answering the bare 'button' selector makes applyEmphasis's legend loop run. It does not: applyEmphasis() queries only the chart. The loop over el('legend').querySelectorAll('button') is setIsolated's, and it now runs for real -- a click on the General Fund mark sets aria-pressed on exactly one of the six buttons buildLegend created. harness.mjs's KNOWN_SELECTORS note carried the same misattribution and was corrected with it.

(2) 'restoreFocus's REAL PATH RUNS' IS HALF TRUE. Its chart branch does now: after Escape back to the overview, focus lands on a real g.node where before it landed nowhere. Its entry gate focusInChart() is still unreachable from the realistic state, because the stub's node has no contains(), so chart.contains(mark) is not a function and a reader focused on a mark reads as focus not being in the chart. Filed as fisc-2ial.

ALSO MEASURED, and it is the finding the lane did not go looking for: reverting insertBefore to its old unshift form does not reorder the DOM, it CORRUPTS it. d3's order() re-attaches without detaching, so 25 marks answered a g.node lookup 49 times and 58 ribbons answered path.link 115 times -- with both id SETS still agreeing, which is a duplication no set comparison can see. insertBefore now detaches and the rendering arm counts DISTINCT marks. The same non-detaching shape remains in appendChild, append, prepend and replaceChildren: fisc-pu1k.
CORRECTION to the close reason above: the classList finding is fisc-uyc2, not fisc-9sbb, which names no bead. The filed set is fisc-2ial, fisc-uyc2, fisc-tkn7, fisc-pu1k, fisc-pf17, fisc-e3r1.
close_reason:
Landed at af63b3e (the stub draws) and 4d9db66 (the arm that reads what it drew) on e13-sankey-merge. domStub's nodes carry ownerDocument and namespaceURI so d3's creatorInherit no longer throws, document.querySelector answers an #id out of getElementById so D3.select('#chart') resolves to a real node, insertBefore honours its reference argument and detaches first, and the selector grammar answers bare tags, tag.class and one descendant pair. KNOWN_SELECTORS' key set is unchanged -- only g.node and button moved from unanswered to parsed.

tools/jscheck/chart.mjs is the rendering arm: over 10 states per published year at both budgets it holds 138 marks, 194 ribbons, 1242 attributes and 68 fired handlers to what the chart actually drew -- every node the layout lays reaching a mark and every mark one Go accounts for, every link a ribbon with a path a width and a name, the class role tabindex aria-pressed aria-keyshortcuts aria-label rect and tspans render() writes, the gestures by DISPATCH rather than by source text, and on every state that no refusal banner stands where a chart should. Each arm's ok requires its own counter, and (a) additionally requires a folded tail and a client-drawn mark to have been exercised.

PROVEN IT CAN FAIL, including one mutation run at integration that the lane did not: making render() draw graph.nodes.slice(1) -- the exact fisc-phtp.2 failure mode of a client holding the right ids and failing to draw one -- takes four checks red, naming fund-balance/draw as laid and never drawn and naming the ribbon left hanging off it. NOTHING ELSE IN THE SUITE CAUGHT IT. Removing an id from testdata/rungs.json, deleting an aria-keyshortcuts line, blinding the DOM reader and removing the #chart answer are each red too, the last two on the arms' own counters rather than green with nothing compared.

Gates off the integrated tree: make pre-commit exit 0; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped. site/app.js, testdata/, drill.mjs and layout.mjs byte-identical to the branch point; no golden moved. make js went 11s to 28s because render() now draws in every module.

Two corrections to this bead's text are in its notes. Findings filed: fisc-2ial, fisc-9sbb, fisc-tkn7, fisc-pu1k, fisc-pf17, fisc-e3r1.

title: residualDeclaration's every-entry-accounted-for guard cannot see a key both regexes miss
description:
FAIL-OPEN in a guard, plus a FALSE-CLAIM in its comment. Found by /code-review lens 4 over 0923016..HEAD; re-verified here by reading both regexes.

tools/jscheck/harness.mjs:651-679. The comment says it 'throws on a shape it does not recognise rather than return a partial set', and the inline comment says 'a reason written in a shape the regex cannot follow is a throw and not a missing endpoint'.

MEASURED: the key count is (m[1].match(/^\t"[^"]+": /gm) || []).length -- a tab then a QUOTED key. The entry regex also requires a quoted key. So a key in any shape neither follows is skipped by BOTH, got === keys still holds, and the parse returns a partial set in silence. The guard is vacuous for exactly the shape it exists for; what it actually catches is a malformed REASON, which is its other arm.

MUTATION (lens 4): rename "transfers/out": to transfersOut: in internal/check/drillreconcile.go -> residualDeclaration() returned 4 entries and did NOT throw.

NO WRONG OUTPUT SHIPS TODAY: make js still went red (6 FAIL) under that mutation, because every declared endpoint is carried on some pinned group, so the downstream arms caught it. The guard is what did not fire.

FIX: count entry lines by a pattern that does not presuppose the quoting -- lens 4 suggests ^\t\S+: -- so a key the entry regex cannot parse makes got !== keys. Mind the blank lines between entries when writing it.

FIX IN THIS PASS: it is a two-line change in a file this pass is already touching.
close_reason: Fixed in b5c7830. The key count is now /^\t(?!\/\/)\S/gm -- an entry begins at one tab and a non-space, continuations are indented further -- so a key the entry pattern cannot parse makes got !== keys and throws. The parse moved into an exported parseResidualLiteral(src) over source text, so it is drivable over a literal the tree does not contain; residualDeclaration() is now the file read plus that call. The arm went into seam.mjs, which is where checks on the harness itself live, with three cases: a well-formed literal parses 2 of 2 and does not throw, an unquoted key throws rather than returning 1 of 2, an empty reason throws. Mutation: restore the old ^\t" count -> the new arm red, make js exit 1.

title: DrillStep.Residual reaches the wire by a json tag nothing checks: json:"-" leaves every test green
description:
TEST-GAP at the export seam. Found by /code-review lens 2 over 0923016..HEAD.

internal/export/export.go:537 -- the Residual field's json tag is the only thing putting the residual on FISC_CONFIG, and 41b3d9d's central claim is that 'the packager ships it on step 0 of FISC_CONFIG.steps'.

MUTATION (lens 2, M5): change the tag to json:"-" and both Go packages stay GREEN.
  - TestViewsOpensOnTheSpine... pins views()'s Go struct against check.ResidualNodes(), which is upstream of the tag.
  - TestAStepsDocumentIsCitedByThePageThatOpensIt round-trips cfg.Steps, but its fixture carries no Residual, so a dropped key round-trips equal.
  - On the node side tools/jscheck/drill.mjs:58 reads PAGE.steps[0].residual from residualDeclaration(), parsed out of the GO SOURCE and fed into the harness sandbox. No jscheck module reads dist/index.html's FISC_CONFIG (grep over tools/jscheck: index.html.tmpl reads only).

So both sides check the declaration and neither checks the wire between them. This is the 'green because the gate fired' shape in AGENTS.md, 'Prove it can fail', at a seam rather than in a check.

CHEAPEST FIX: give the round-trip test's fixture a Residual, so the tag is on the asserted path.
notes:
2026-09-12, re-derived against 096962a (lane D of E13). THE PREMISE HOLDS AND
THE FIX IS NOW THREE LINES.

Lane D gave DrillStep four more fields -- Key, After, Side, Role -- all
json:"-", and pinned their ABSENCE from the wire in the very test this bead
names. That pin is built the way this bead asks for: it reads configBlob off a
packaged page rather than round-tripping a Go fixture, decodes into
[]export.DrillStep, cmp.Diffs the WHOLE struct against the declared steps with
the four fields zeroed, and guards its own vacuity --

    if steps[0].Key == "" {
        t.Fatal("the declared step carries no key, so the comparison below
                 asserts nothing")
    }

So a json:"key" added without a client to read it goes red.

THIS DOES NOT RETIRE THIS BEAD. The fixture's step still sets no Residual, so
wantOnWire and cfg.Steps are both the zero value whichever tag Residual carries,
and the M5 mutation stays green exactly as recorded. Absence is pinned for four
fields and presence is pinned for none.

WHAT CHANGED IS THE COST. The cheapest fix this bead already proposed -- put a
Residual on the round-trip fixture -- now lands beside a working comparison and
an anti-vacuity assert to copy: give the fixture's step a Residual, leave it OUT
of the zeroed set in wantOnWire, and add the sibling of the Key guard so the
assertion cannot go vacuous if that Residual is ever dropped.
2026-09-17, L3.4: unaffected. check.ResidualNodes() is unchanged; its declaration moved from drillreconcile.go to internal/check/residual.go and tools/jscheck/harness.mjs reads the literal from there.

The bead's own mutation is the proof: retagging Residual json:"-" leaves go test ./internal/export ./pkg/cmd/export green, exactly as the bead measured, and the arm reddens with '1 declared and not shipped [residual]'. It found three more of the same shape while being pointed at DrillStep -- keep, widen and noun are shipped by Go, read by app.js, and were declared by the typedef for none of them. title: drill-reconciles-across-documents' Description() claims an outflow identity it holds for one group in six
description:

title: The figure comes first: hero above the chart, the apparatus disclosed
description:

title: history.html and balances.html say 'as audited' over the ACFR section the ACFR labels (Unaudited)
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD (6ad828f..cab0c73), verified in the corpus this session.

The two new reader pages assert audit assurance the source document explicitly disclaims:

- pkg/cmd/export/data.go, the changes view: Title "Ten years of Livermore's money, as audited" and a lede reading "from the audit the city publishes each year"; the balances view's lede says "The audited balance...".
- site/history.html.tmpl: "audited years" and "All 10 columns are audited results of the same process".
- The 310 facts from pp.167-169 carry basis: audited (mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml, 5e474ae), so the column chips print "audited" under every year.

Measured against the document:

- data/extracted/livermore-acfr-fy2025/pages/p0161.txt is the section divider and reads, in full: "Statistical Section (Unaudited)".
- p0029.txt, the auditor's report: "The other information comprises the introductory and statistical sections but does not include the basic financial statements and our auditor's report thereon. Our opinions on the basic financial statements do not cover the other information, and we do not express an opinion or any form of assurance thereon."
- The string "unaudited" appears in no tracked doc or mapping. docs/acfr-statistical-section.md surveys all 28 tables of this section and never records that the section carries this label.

Mitigation, measured: FY2025 does tie to the audited basic statements -- p52 prints the same five General Fund components (5,273,139 / 6,758,239 / 17,364,162 / 31,037,869 / 26,610,167) and p54 prints FUND BALANCES-ENDING 87,043,576, equal to p167's 2025 column summed. But the corpus can witness that for FY2025 alone; the other nine columns rest on the unaudited section.

This is not WRONG-OUTPUT -- every cell equals the fact it cites and the facts tie to the pages. It is the provenance sentence around them.

Decision needed before a fix, because the options differ in scope:
(1) reword the prose only (title, two ledes, template sentences), leaving basis: audited;
(2) re-basis the 310 facts (mapping.BasisActual exists), which moves facts.jsonl and every golden;
(3) keep both and ship a caveat quoting p161's "(Unaudited)" and p29's disclaimer, which is the option that adds a fact about the document rather than removing a claim.

Land whichever with the survey doc recording the section's label, since that omission is why nothing caught this.
close_reason: Landed as option (3) of the three the bead offered: the section's own label ships as a caveat rather than the prose being reworded or the facts re-based. caveatStatisticalSectionIsUnaudited is published; docs/acfr-history-contract.md:40-42 records that internal/export reads it and labels the column chips and cell tooltips 'unaudited'; README.md:59 and data/sources.yaml:59 quote p161's '(Unaudited)' and p29's opinion scope. Measured: 'as audited' and 'audited results of the same process' are gone from every view and template. NOTE FOR A FUTURE READER: internal/structure/cuts.go:120 still reads 'ten audited years' and the scope keeps Bases: audited, which is option (3) holding the basis and disclosing the label, not a survivor of the defect. Reopen if the re-basis was intended instead.

title: AGENTS.md keeps the rules; the evidence moves to docs/
description:
AGENTS.md is 1126 lines and arrives in every session via CLAUDE.md's @import. It was 690 at 5794a60 on 2026-08-29 -- +63% in seven days -- and the only commit that ever shrank it is d6ff0c7 (-32).

THE SPLIT IS BY KIND, NOT BY TOPIC, which is what keeps it from repeating the docs/agents/ failure 5794a60 deleted: a rule is stated once, in AGENTS.md; a docs/ evidence file states what was measured and NEVER says what to do. Two files that both state a rule can disagree about the rule; a file that states no rule can only go out of date about the world.

This also resolves rather than contradicts AGENTS.md:267-273, which says docs/ is the weakest home because it does not arrive in context. That is correct and it survives: it is the reason the RULES stay. Only the arguments stop being injected. And docs/sankey-contract.md:11-13 is a third category -- a contract is a specification of an artifact, whose home is next to the code that produces it.

New: docs/review-loop-evidence.md, docs/prose-claims-evidence.md, docs/extraction-boundary.md, docs/agents-md-charter.md.

Deleted rather than moved: the ~55-line labelledValues summary, which ends by saying three attempts to summarise that function were wrong three ways and not to trust it over the code. Moving a paragraph the tree has declared unreliable is not preserving evidence.

Three internal duplications collapse: 495-499 with 679-691, 484-491 with 979-993, 748-755 with 197-206.

Blocked on the anchor gate, so a heading rename cannot silently falsify the 11 in-tree citations.

Also worth recording against the plan this bead carries: the file landed at 486 lines, not the ~305 the skeleton budgeted -- 438 of them non-generated. The excess is why-clauses kept on bullets where the bare imperative read as arbitrary. fisc-6lfh is the falsification of that judgement.

Closed with --force: the blocker fisc-ak39 stays open for its three unlanded arms, but the arm this bead needed -- the AGENTS.md section anchors -- shipped first, exactly so a heading rename could not silently falsify the tree's citations. It caught four the day it landed.

title: tools/doccheck: the AGENTS.md anchors, the evidence-doc backlinks and the line budget become gates
description:
Four arms, one Go binary, following tools/beadrefs/main.go's house pattern (hand-declared exemptions with staleness guards that fail when an exemption loses its subject).

A. Comment-block length. Over cmd internal pkg site tools, .go/.mjs/.js. Threshold 40, and 60 for a package doc comment. Measured before writing the tool: blocks at 20+=136, 25+=70, 30+=45, 35+=29, 40+=20, 50+=8, 60+=5. At 40 the finding set is 20, which is lane-sized rather than beadrefs' first-run 73. LENGTH IS A PROXY FOR KIND AND IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- a 39-line essay passes, a 45-line transcribed column grid fails and needs an exemption. Say so in the package comment. Maintenance rule: if the exemption list passes twelve, the threshold is wrong; raise it, do not grow the list.

B. AGENTS.md section anchors. A citation of the form AGENTS.md, "X" must resolve to a heading OR A BOLD LEAD PHRASE -- "History's home is git" is bold text at AGENTS.md:863, not a heading, and four sites cite it, two of them strings a failing gate prints to a terminal. All 11 quoted citations resolve today, so this arm lands GREEN and goes red the first time a heading is renamed.

C. Evidence-doc contract. A declared evidenceDocs map: the file exists, opens with the evidence marker naming a section that exists, and AGENTS.md links it exactly once. Reverse direction too: a marker file nobody declared is a failure.

D. AGENTS.md line budget. Guards regrowth -- the file went 690 to 1126 in seven days. Not an intrinsic count of the tree's contents: it is a threshold pinned by the check that re-measures it.

Not an arm of narration: that target's memory arm warns-and-continues when bd cannot answer, and mixing a hard gate into a sometimes-skipping target makes green unreadable. doccheck resolves against committed files only.
notes:
PARTIAL LANDING, f1691a3^..9b09b88. Arm B only.

LANDED -- arm B, the AGENTS.md section anchors. tools/doccheck resolves a citation against headings, their post-colon tails, and bold LEAD phrases (line, bullet or numbered item). Wired into make pre-commit, its own CI job, and pages-build's needs. It caught a real orphan the same session it landed, and five review passes hardened it: blockquote furniture, whole-file lazy bold pairing that crosses a lone asterisk, lead-phrase-only anchors, a zero-citation floor, and an exemption for its own fixtures with a staleness guard.

NOT LANDED:
  Arm A, comment-block length. Still specified above; the 40/60 thresholds and the measured distribution stand.
  Arm C, the evidence-doc contract. Now partly overtaken by fisc-hcad, which is the narrower and more urgent half -- five source comments were re-pointed at docs/ paths that nothing checks.
  Arm D, the AGENTS.md line budget. The file is 486 lines and nothing stops it growing back; docs/agents-md-charter.md says so explicitly rather than claiming a gate that does not exist.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT: it says 'the committed tree carries thirteen citations'. citePattern finds 19 real ones, 27 before this command's own fixtures were exempted. Thirteen was the count with docs/ and its own files excluded, which it does not do. And the printed-to-a-terminal count in the arm-B paragraph says two; it is four, counting tools/beadrefs and doccheck's own failure message.
2026-09-19, released: this bead was assigned on 2026-09-05 and never worked past arm B, so bd ready could not see it for a fortnight. Re-derived against the tree: tools/doccheck/main.go:49 and :543 still say the opening markers and the backlinks belong to this bead, so arms A and C are open exactly as the PARTIAL LANDING note describes. Unassigned so it is claimable again.
close_reason:
Split, not finished. Arm B -- the AGENTS.md section anchors -- LANDED at f1691a3^..9b09b88 and is wired into make pre-commit, its own CI job and pages-build's needs; it caught a real orphan the session it landed and five review passes hardened it. The three surviving arms are now their own beads, each priced on its own evidence and each carrying this bead's measurements for its arm:
  fisc-ak39.1  P3  comment-block length (the 20-findings-at-40 distribution)

MEASURED 2026-09-19, and it is why arm D is P3 rather than P1: the file was 1126 lines when this bead was filed against that growth and is 513 now. This bead's own note said 486, so it has grown 27 lines since -- kept in ak39.3, since slow regrowth is the argument for the gate rather than against it.
