title: make hooks installs into .git/hooks, which core.hooksPath makes git ignore
description:
core.hooksPath is set to .beads/hooks by bd, so git never reads .git/hooks at all. make hooks (Makefile:237-249) writes .git/hooks/pre-commit.fisc, symlinks .git/hooks/pre-commit to it, and prints 'installed .git/hooks/pre-commit -> pre-commit.fisc (runs make pre-commit)'. Both files exist in this checkout dated Aug 29 and neither has ever run: the local fmt/vet/narration/beadrefs/test gate is inert.

FAIL-OPEN plus FALSE-CLAIM in one artifact, and the second occurrence of the same defect in this target -- Makefile:223-227 records that CLAUDE.md and docs/agents/workflow.md once described the symlink as though it were already there.

Fix: resolve the real hook dir; refuse rather than write into a tool-managed one (a fisc block inside a bd-managed file reproduces the generated-block problem one level down); read the dir back from git after installing and compare before printing.

CI is unaffected -- it is the real gate.
close_reason:
Fixed in 783f943. The path now comes from 'git rev-parse --git-path hooks', the printed claim is read back from the file git will execute before it is printed, and the target refuses a tracked hooks directory -- which is this checkout's case, so 'make hooks' now installs nothing here and says why.

MEASURED WHILE FIXING IT, and worth recording because it changes the premise the target was written on: .beads/hooks holds SIX TRACKED FILES. 'a hook cannot be committed' is false here, so the reason not to install is not that it would be lost but that it would be SHARED -- a committed hook makes 'make pre-commit' mandatory for everyone who has bd, including a contributor with no Go toolchain. That is the opposite of the convenience this target is documented to be.

The local gate had never run in this checkout since 29 August. Every 'ran make pre-commit' in that window was manual or did not happen; CI was unaffected.

title: A part that prints no stated total should DECLARE it, not be inferred from the rule's shape
description:
FOUND BY /code-review on the FIFTH pass over the fisc-eaic lane, at the cap, and
filed rather than patched because three consecutive passes found a fail-open in
this one arm and each fix was a new guess at the same predicate.

THE ARM. fact-offset-is-not-a-stated-total reports a finding when a rule's
declared total resolves to no line, because a lost span is a printed total the
check can no longer refuse a fact on. It cannot refuse every non-resolution:
FOURTEEN committed parts legitimately resolve none.

  11  total_spans_parts rules -- the total prints on the block's LAST page, so
      the earlier parts cannot find it
   3  label-less parts anchoring on the block TERMINATOR -- spine-transfers-in
      on p67's fund-group header line, spine-transfers-out and
      spine-fund-balance on the running footer "BUDGET FY 2025-27 Page 63"

THE THREE GUESSES, each measured red after it shipped:
  1. `rule.TotalRow != "" && resolved == 0` -- a MULTI-PART rule losing one
     part's span still passed. Break spine-revenues' total_row: PASS at 161
     lines, no finding.
  2. `len(failures) > 0` over all parts -- turned the three ordinary label-less
     parts into three findings on a clean corpus.
  3. `!rule.TotalSpansParts && p.LabelsFrom == 0 && rule.TotalRow != ""` -- the
     current one. Measured: break each of the 11 spanning rules' total_row in
     turn and TEN of them are hidden, the check reporting pass. The one that is
     caught, div-general-services, is caught by accident, because a rollup
     happens to cover it. The LabelsFrom clause hides spine-revenues p67 and
     spine-expenditures p67 the same way.

WHY A FOURTH PREDICATE IS THE WRONG MOVE. Every one of these infers "should this
part have had a span?" from the rule's SHAPE. The question is not answerable from
the shape -- it is a claim about the document, and the corpus already has the
right idiom for exactly this: declaredVacuous (internal/check/vacuity.go) and
unprojectedScopes (internal/check/coverage.go) both make the exemption a
DECLARATION carrying a reason and the bead that retires it, and both fail when a
declaration stops being true. A predicate over Rule fields can do neither.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD, at the cap, and what it does and does not buy. The
unresolved count is now published unconditionally in the check's summary --
"162 resolved ...; 14 declared total(s) resolve to no line" -- so span loss moves
a figure fisc verify prints on every run whether or not the predicate calls it a
finding. Breaking a spanning rule now reads 161 and 15. That removes the SILENCE,
which was the worst of it. It does not make the loss a failure, and a reader has
to notice a number moved.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS:
  (a) A part or rule DECLARES that it prints no stated total, with the reason --
      "the total prints on p128, the last page of this block" -- and the check
      fails on any unresolved total that is not declared, AND on any declaration
      that has stopped being true. That is declaredVacuous's exact shape.
  (b) The 14 are enumerated once, as data rather than as a predicate, so adding
      a fifteenth is a reviewable diff rather than a silent widening.

RECOMMENDATION (a). (b) is the cheap version and would already have caught all
three guesses.

NOTE the count 14 is a property of today's corpus and will move; re-measure it
rather than quoting this bead. The check prints it.
acceptance_criteria: an unresolved stated total is exempt only where a declaration says so with a reason, and fact-offset-is-not-a-stated-total fails both on an undeclared one and on a declaration that has stopped being true; proven by mutation on a spanning rule and on a label-less part
notes:
2026-09-06, re-priced P2 -> P1 during a backlog characterization pass.

PREMISE RE-DERIVED AGAINST THE TREE, not taken from the description: guess 3 is
still the shipped predicate. internal/check/statedtotals.go:143 reads

    if !rule.TotalSpansParts && p.LabelsFrom == 0 && rule.TotalRow != "" {

which is the clause the description measures as hiding ten of the eleven
total_spans_parts rules. The break-each-total_row measurement itself was NOT
re-run in this pass; what was confirmed is that the code it was taken against is
unchanged at 582ee1e.

WHY P1. It is the only open task/bug/decision in the tree that leaves a
provenance check unable to refuse what it exists to refuse. Every other open
item carrying FAIL-OPEN or WRONG-OUTPUT in its text negates it explicitly
("Not FAIL-OPEN, measured"). At P2 it sorted alongside doc-comment corrections,
which is the priority drift AGENTS.md, "Issue tracking" says to look for.

Not claimed and not implemented -- re-pricing only.
2026-09-17, L3.4: unprojectedScopes (internal/check/coverage.go) no longer exists; facts-are-projected was deleted against structure.Covered. The idiom this bead points at survives as declaredVacuous (internal/check/vacuity.go) and, for cuts, as structure.Residue and structure.Exception -- each a declaration with a reason and a bead, refused when it stops matching. The recommendation (a) stands with those as the shape to copy.

title: The column kind, proven end-to-end on ACFR p177
description:
IMPLEMENTS fisc-9tn4's DECISION, AND PROVES IT ON THE SMALLEST PAGE THAT CAN
PROVE IT. Nothing else in E12 may be written before this lands.

WHY p177. It is already a committed fixture (testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt) with
arithmetic already proved against it (internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go): nine
of its ten rows tie to the city's printed totals and FY2024 is short by exactly
its own Financed Purchases column, $176,292. So the amount side is settled and
what this bead adds is the two non-amount columns, with nothing else in the way.

WHAT p177 ACTUALLY HAS, measured off the fixture (header at lines 9-11):

  cols 1-8   amounts, per debt type, both activity classes
  col 9      "Total Primary Government"  -- amount
  col 10     "Percentage of Personal Income (1)"  -- "2.5%", "1.2%".
             amount.Parse REJECTS it. Loud.
  col 11     "Per Capita"  -- "$ 1,009", "922", "713".
             amount.Parse ACCEPTS it. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: it is a
             well-formed grouped dollar amount whose UNIT is dollars-per-capita
             rather than a total, so a disposition that only fixes the grammar
             swallows it as money and every guard downstream stays green.

  The row LABEL is a bare fiscal year ("2016"), and the header spans three
  printed lines with group headers "Governmental Activities" and "Business-Type
  Activities" plus a "(1)" footnote marker. Both bear on the anchor and on the
  column_headers declaration for the geometry guard.

WHAT TO BUILD, per fisc-9tn4:
  - Column (internal/mapping/rule.go) gains a KIND. Default is the amount kind,
    so every committed declaration keeps its meaning and no existing rule moves.
    Assert that: rebuild and cmp facts.jsonl before and after the schema change.
  - The non-amount grammars live BESIDE internal/amount, not inside it.
    internal/amount stays strict about money.
  - A recognised non-amount column is READ, so the row is fully accounted for and
    checkGap stays whole, and is NOT PUBLISHED as a fact.

THE PROOF OBLIGATIONS, per AGENTS.md "Prove it can fail". Each needs a mutation,
and the second and third are the ones that would otherwise ship a check that
cannot fail:
  (1) The rule reads p177 whole -- ten columns, ten rows -- and publishes
      EIGHT amount columns as facts and neither non-amount column.
  (2) DECLARING col 10, Per Capita, AS AN AMOUNT MUST BE REFUSED, or at minimum must be
      visible. This is the defect the whole decision exists for and it is the
      one no arithmetic catches: the figures parse, the row is complete, and
      $1,009 per capita enters a store whose invariant is integer cents of
      city money. If nothing can refuse it, say so explicitly and file what
      would.
  (3) DELETING THE KIND from col 9, the percentage, must go red, and red for the RIGHT reason --
      amount.Parse rejecting "2.5%" -- not because the part failed to resolve
      for some unrelated anchor reason. Check the message, not the exit code:
      see AGENTS.md, "green because the gate fired".

AND CHECK THE EXISTING TEST STILL MEANS WHAT IT SAYS.
internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go reads the row off the fixture today WITHOUT a
production rule. If this bead adds one, the test and the rule must not become two
readings of one page that can drift apart.
acceptance_criteria: a production rule reads p177's eleven columns; nine amount columns publish as facts and neither non-amount column does; facts.jsonl is byte-unmoved by the schema change alone; deleting col 10's kind goes red on amount.Parse rejecting the percentage, verified by message and not by exit code; declaring col 11 as an amount is refused, or the reason nothing can refuse it is stated and filed
notes:
P177 CARRIES TEN COLUMNS, AND MISCOUNTING THEM AS ELEVEN IS THE EASY ERROR:
the eleventh thing on the line is the FISCAL YEAR, which is the row LABEL.
Measured off testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt by splitting each year row on runs of
two or more spaces and counting the values after the row label:

  every year row carries TEN values.

  cols 1-7   the seven debt columns  (gov: Certificates of Participation, Notes
             & Loans Payable, Financed Purchases and SBITA; business-type:
             Certificates of Participation, Financed Purchases, State Loan,
             Financed Purchases and SBITA)
  col 8      Total Primary Government   -- amount
  col 9      Percentage of Personal Income (1)  -- percentage; amount.Parse
             REJECTS it, loudly
  col 10     Per Capita  -- amount_per_unit; amount.Parse ACCEPTS it, and that
             is the whole reason fisc-9tn4 was settled the way it was

So the acceptance criterion is: EIGHT amount columns publish as facts, and
neither non-amount column does.

THE ROW-TOTAL IDENTITY HOLDS AND IS THIS PAGE'S GUARD. Cols 1-7 sum to col 8
exactly: 2016 gives 88,896,362 against a printed 88,896,362 and 2025 gives
91,015,277 against 91,015,277. It is a COLUMN-DIRECTION total -- Rule.TotalRow
and Rollup are both row-direction -- so it cannot be expressed in the rule
schema and belongs in internal/check over the published facts.
2026-09-05, IMPLEMENTED, AND TWO OF THIS BEAD'S PREMISES WERE STALE AGAINST THE TREE — both re-measured before the rule was written, per AGENTS.md 'A bead's text is a claim, not a fact':

(1) 'EIGHT AMOUNT COLUMNS PUBLISH AS FACTS' CANNOT HAPPEN YET, and not because of the quantity channel. Measured: Fact.FiscalYear comes only from Column.FiscalYear and the year here is the ROW label; the seven debt columns plus the total share one (fund_group, fund, fiscal_year, basis) identity, which validateRule refuses on non-skip columns; and no mapping.Kind states outstanding debt (fisc-7jtl, whose 'these tables publish nothing until Kind grows' turned out to be the accurate claim). Filed as fisc-xmh2. So the landed rule (acfr-p0177-debt-by-type) READS all ten columns and publishes nothing: amount columns and rows skip: true, and facts.jsonl is byte-unmoved by the rule as well as by the schema change. The page's arithmetic guard is internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go, which reads the page THROUGH the rule with the skips lifted in memory — ten rows by eight amount cells, nine rows tying cols 1-7 to col 8 exactly and FY2024 short by exactly 176,292, its own Financed Purchases cell. The internal/check version lands with publication (fisc-xmh2 carries it).

(2) 'p177 CAN CARRY column_headers' IS FALSE, measured. Its headers are declarable, but the footnote '(1)' is its own -layout line and sits 2.6pt above its sentence, inside geometry's 4.66pt line tolerance, so the substrates disagree 23 lines to 22 and buildPairing refuses — p41's failure mode. Pinned by TestACFRDebtPageCannotCarryTheColumnGuard; docs/acfr-statistical-section.md corrected in the same commit. The geometry proof obligation therefore became a refusal proof: declaring the headers goes red on the pairing, and the page reads unguarded with the rule saying so.

WHAT LANDED: mapping.Quantity (amount default + amount_per_unit, percentage, number; closed slice, valid(), quantityList(), Kind's shape), Column.Quantity, Row.Quantity (the whole-row arm, in this schema change as the survey asked; its p169 proofs are batch one's), Row.EffectiveQuantity(Column) beside EffectiveKind; internal/quantity (stdlib + internal/amount only) with the three grammars; parseRow dispatching quantity before skip, read-not-published; validation refusing explicit 'amount', unknown values, counterpart on a non-amount row, total_row over a non-amount column, and deltas on one.

THE PROOFS, off real runs: deleting col 9's quantity → 'row "2016" column 9: cannot parse amount "2.5%": not a recognized number' (message checked, not exit code; also permanent as TestACFRDebtPercentageColumnNeedsItsQuantity). Declaring col 10 as amount → NOTHING refuses it, build green and facts byte-identical, because '$ 1,009' is well-formed money — stated explicitly and filed as fisc-54vn (the p180 cross-tie is what would); pinned as TestACFRDebtPerCapitaParsesCleanlyAsAmount. Row arm: TestRowQuantityOverrideIsLoadBearing goes red on 'cannot parse amount "6.6%"' without the override.
close_reason: LANDED: the quantity channel, proven end-to-end on ACFR p177 — with the bead's publication premise corrected rather than met. mapping.Quantity (four values, Kind's closed-set shape), Column.Quantity + Row.Quantity (both arms in one schema change), Row.EffectiveQuantity, internal/quantity's three grammars, parseRow dispatch (read-not-published, quantity before skip), and the closed-vocabulary validation. The production rule acfr-p0177-debt-by-type reads all ten columns of the page that was unreadable when this bead was filed — and publishes NOTHING, because the amount side is blocked three ways the bead's text did not know (fisc-xmh2: no per-row fiscal year, no column identity axis; fisc-7jtl: no truthful Kind). facts.jsonl byte-unmoved by schema change AND by the rule, both measured by rebuild-and-cmp; fisc verify --strict 45 passed, 0 failed. Mutations off real runs: col 9's quantity deleted → red on 'cannot parse amount "2.5%": not a recognized number' (message read, not exit code); col 10 declared amount → green everywhere, stated and filed (fisc-54vn); column_headers declared → red on 23-vs-22 substrate disagreement, so the bead's geometry hope was also stale (survey corrected). The page's column-direction check (cols 1-7 = col 8, FY2024 −176,292) waits on publication and rides fisc-xmh2; until then acfr_p177_test.go reads the page through the rule with skips lifted and carries the arithmetic. See this bead's 2026-09-05 notes for the full measurement.

title: Classify all 28 Statistical Section tables by column kind, before any is mapped
description:
THE FIRST CHILD OF E12 AND THE ONE THAT SIZES IT. Nobody has classified the
Statistical Section's tables, and both the epic's cost and its reader payoff
depend on the classification.

WHY A SURVEY RATHER THAN JUST MAPPING. fisc-9tn4 settled that a recognised
non-amount column is READ but NOT PUBLISHED. That decision is right and it has a
consequence nobody has priced: a table whose columns are ALL non-amount produces
zero facts. p181 Population Demographics, p183 FTEs by Function, p184 Capital
Assets Statistics and p185 Operating Indicators look like exactly that. Mapping
one is real work that publishes nothing, and that may still be worth doing for
the reader surface -- but it must be a decision made in advance, not discovered
on the fourth table.

WHAT TO PRODUCE, per table across pp.163-194 (28 tables; see the epic for the
enumeration, which was measured off the page title lines):

  - the column count and what each column IS: amount, percentage, count,
    amount-in-a-coarser-unit, or something else
  - whether the table is TEN YEARS or "Current Year and Nine Years Ago" -- p182
    is captioned the latter and p175 follows the same convention, so the shape
    is not uniform and a lane assuming it stops there
  - whether the table carries ANY publishable money
  - the declared unit where it is not dollars. p180's Total Personal Income is
    THOUSANDS: 3,573,663 against p177's own ratio, 88,896,362 / 0.025 = 3.56
    billion. The document derives its own unit and that is the good case.
  - the shapes that fit no grammar. Known: p182 prints RANGES -- "5600-6000",
    "1000-1400" -- where a competitor's headcount is not disclosed exactly.
    A range must fail closed or be declared omitted. It must NEVER be read as
    its lower bound, which is the plausible-wrong-value failure this corpus is
    built to refuse.
  - the sparse rows. p182's GILLIG, FormFactor and Lam Research have no 2016
    columns at all, because they were not in that year's top ten. That is a
    genuine absent-is-not-zero case and the read has to say so rather than
    borrowing the next row's tokens (see labelledValues in
    internal/mapping/resolve.go, and AGENTS.md's "The extraction boundary").

WHERE IT GOES: a section of docs/ or the epic's own notes, whichever the batches
will actually read. Not a memory -- it is a table, and bd prime injects memories
into every session whether or not anyone is working this lane.

THIS IS A READING TASK AND IT WRITES NO YAML. Its output is what lets the
batches be scoped, and it is the cheapest thing in the epic.
acceptance_criteria: every table in pp.163-194 has a recorded column count, column kinds, year shape, declared unit where not dollars, and a yes/no on whether it carries publishable money; the shapes that fit no grammar are named with their page
notes: 2026-09-05 DONE; the classification is docs/acfr-statistical-section.md. ONE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD'S OWN NOTE WAS STALE, measured: 'Every table in this section heads its columns with BARE YEARS' is true of 14 of 28 tables, not all. The transposed tables (p173, p176, p177, p180, p194), the snapshots (p178, p181, p186-p188, p190-191, p193) and p192 (headers 'FY2016-17', which amount.Parse rejects) head columns with text the parser accepts, so THEY can declare column_headers -- including p177 itself. The 14 that cannot (all of batch one among them) are named in fisc-wiyg; arithmetic remains their only guard, and the survey records it per table.
close_reason: Produced docs/acfr-statistical-section.md: all 28 tables of ACFR pp.163-194 classified off the extracted pages -- column count and quantities, year shape (16 ten-year, 3 two-column, p192 nine-year, p194 9-actual+8-projected, 7 snapshots), money (17 yes / 11 no), declared and derived units, no-grammar shapes, sparse rows, and per-table arithmetic guards. Beyond the acceptance criteria it measured: four row-shaped non-amount tables (p169, p179, p189, p192), seven printed-arithmetic defects (p164's business-type total row right-shifted 2017-2023; 2023 cells copied from 2022 on p165/p166/p169/p189; p192 FY16-17 incremental off 100; p187's 2.8-vs-2.77), and that the geometry-guard gap covers 14 tables, not 28 -- the brief's 'every table heads its columns with bare years' was stale and is corrected in this bead's notes. Mechanism recommendation (column quantity + whole-row override, per-cell not needed) and the four-value closed vocabulary (amount, amount_per_unit, percentage, number) are on fisc-oakx.2; batch corrections on fisc-oakx.3; the extension measurement on fisc-9tn4. Filed fisc-wiyg (geometry gap) and fisc-7jtl (no mapping.Kind for stock/valuation figures, 10 of the 17 money tables).

title: E12 The ACFR Statistical Section: ten years of history reaches the reader
description:
TEN YEARS OF HISTORY IS THE LARGEST READER PAYOFF LEFT IN THE CORPUS, and it is
one section of one document: the ACFR Statistical Section, pp.162-194.

WHY IT IS AN EPIC. It supersedes fisc-4ua.4, which was a P1 task under a P2 epic
(E8 Further projections) and had outgrown both. E8 is "further projections";
this is a document section with its own decision, its own column grammar, its own
reader surface and about thirty tables. E10's precedent applies to the id: a
dotted id reading fisc-4ua.4 under a parent reading E12 would put two answers to
"whose child is this" in one line, so fisc-4ua.4 is SUPERSEDED rather than
reparented, and its content is here.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, measured 2026-09-05 by reading the title line of every
page from p162 to p195 rather than by quoting the earlier bead:

  p162      Description of Statistical Section Contents   (prose, no table)
  p163      Net Position by Component
  p164-166  Changes in Net Position
  p167      Fund Balances of Governmental Funds
  p168-169  Changes in Fund Balances of Governmental Funds
  p170      Taxable Sales by Category
  p171      Direct and Overlapping Sales Tax Rates
  p172      Principal Sales Tax Payers
  p173      Assessed Value and Estimates Taxable Property
  p174      Direct and Overlapping Governments Property Tax Rates
  p175      Principal Property Taxpayers
  p176      Property Tax Levies and Collections
  p177      Ratios of Outstanding Debt by Type
  p178      Direct and Overlapping Governmental Activities Debt
  p179      Legal Debt Margin Information
  p180      Demographic and Economic Statistics
  p181      Population Demographics
  p182      Principal Employers
  p183      Full-Time Equivalent City Government Employees by Function/Program
  p184      Capital Assets Statistics by Function/Program
  p185      Operating Indicators by Function/Program
  p186      Water and Sewer Rates
  p187      Water System - Revenues by Class of User
  p188      Sewer Connection Fees
  p189      Sewer System - Summary of Historical Operating Results
  p190-191  Schedule of Insurance
  p192      Redevelopment Project - Historical Tax Revenues
  p193      Redevelopment Project - Ten Largest Taxable Property Owners
  p194      Redevelopment Project - Actual and Projected Tax Revenues and Debt
            Service Coverage

TWENTY-EIGHT TABLES OVER pp.163-194. p195 is blank and p162 is prose. The prior
figures -- "~25 ten-year tables", "pp.162-195", "fund balances p163-171" -- were
each wrong in a different way and are corrected here rather than carried forward.

THREE THINGS THE OLD FRAMING GOT WRONG, and each changes the plan:

(1) NOT EVERY TABLE IS TEN YEARS. p182 Principal Employers is captioned "Current
    Year and Nine Years Ago" -- two columns, not ten. So is p175 by the same
    convention. A lane that assumes a uniform ten-column shape meets these and
    stops.

(2) THE COLUMN KINDS ARE AT LEAST FIVE, NOT TWO. fisc-9tn4 settled the decision
    on p177's two (an amount and a percentage), and that is the right decision,
    but the section holds more. Measured on three pages:
      - amounts                       p177 cols 1-9
      - percentages                   p177 "2.5%", p180 "6.2%", p182 "16.91%"
      - counts                        p180 Population 88,138; p183 FTEs;
                                      p184 and p185 are counts throughout
      - amounts in a DECLARED COARSER UNIT   p180 Total Personal Income
                                      3,573,663, which is THOUSANDS -- it
                                      reconciles against p177's own ratio
                                      (88,896,362 / 0.025 = 3.56 billion), so
                                      the unit is derivable from the document
                                      and is not a guess
      - RANGES, which are not numbers at all   p182 prints "5600-6000" and
                                      "1000-1400" where a competitor's headcount
                                      is not disclosed exactly
    A range is the one shape no grammar in the decision covers. It must fail
    closed or be declared omitted; it must never be read as its lower bound.

(3) SOME TABLES CARRY NO MONEY AT ALL, and under fisc-9tn4's decision -- a
    recognised non-amount column is READ but NOT PUBLISHED -- those tables
    produce ZERO FACTS. p181, p183, p184, p185 look like the clear cases and
    p171, p174 and p182 like the likely ones. That is not a reason to skip them,
    but it IS the reason the first child of this epic is a survey rather than a
    mapping: the epic's cost and its reader payoff both depend on which tables
    carry money, and nobody has classified them.

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT. It is not the whole ACFR. pp.1-161 -- the auditor's
report, the MD&A beyond pp.34-46, the basic statements and the notes -- stay out.
It is not the CIP.

THE STANDARD IT INHERITS, from E10's acceptance criterion and the sentence that
kept E10 open on one page: publishing facts without a check that can fail on them
makes an epic a bucket rather than a milestone. E10 cleared that bar thinly --
the ACFR's 20 facts carry no detail-ties-to-spine check and cannot, because there
is nothing on the spine to tie FY2025 audited to. THIS section can do better and
must: it is ten years of one document's own history, so the tables corroborate
EACH OTHER. p177's ratio column against p180's personal income is one such tie
and it is already measured above. Every batch lands with at least one.

Filed 2026-09-05 in a backlog and roadmap review, superseding fisc-4ua.4.
acceptance_criteria: every table in pp.163-194 is classified by column kind before any is mapped; each mapped batch publishes at its own scope with at least one check proven failable by mutation, and no batch publishes a non-amount column as a fact; a reader can see ten years of the city history without opening a PDF
notes: 2026-09-05 fisc-oakx.1 DONE: docs/acfr-statistical-section.md classifies all 28 tables. The epic's own figures held up (28 tables, pp.163-194, p162 prose, p195 blank; the five column kinds; p175/p182 two-column; p182's ranges). Measured refinements: 17 tables print publishable money and 11 none -- the epic's 'likely' zero-fact list (p171, p174, p182) is confirmed and p172, p186, p188, p190-191 join it; p192 is NINE year-columns and p194 seventeen year-rows (9 actual + 8 PROJECTED) despite both being titled 'Last Ten'; four tables print row-shaped non-amounts (p169, p179, p189, p192); four have no arithmetic guard at all (p172, p184, p185, p190-191). The corroborate-each-other standard needs care: the survey's 'Printed defects, measured' section lists seven printed-arithmetic defects and three cross-table ties that DO NOT hold (p163<->p166, p167<->p169, p192<->p194 after FY2020-21), plus two that do (p187<->p189 to the dollar; p193<->p192 x1000).
close_reason: END CONDITION MET, measured against each acceptance criterion: (1) all 28 tables were classified before any was mapped (fisc-oakx.1, docs/acfr-statistical-section.md); (2) every mapped batch published at its own scope with a mutation-proven check -- p177 read whole and published nothing under fisc-9tn4's decision, pp.167-169's 310 facts corroborated by excess-of-revenues-identity holding in all ten columns -- and no batch published a non-amount column; (3) a reader can now see ten years of the city's own history without opening a PDF: history.html and balances.html render all 310 statistical-section facts as server-rendered tables, every figure linked to the page it was read from (fisc-oakx.4). CLOSED WITH MOST OF THE SECTION UNMAPPED, deliberately: an epic closes on its end condition, not on exhausting the section. What remains is tracked at top level -- fisc-7jtl (no Kind for the 10 stock/valuation tables), fisc-311g (p163 net position, blocked on fisc-7jtl), fisc-wiyg (bare-year headers refuse the geometry guard), fisc-y242 (the dead p41 anchor), fisc-s7ia (a chart over the series, P4).

title: (DECISION) How a rule reads a table whose columns are not all amounts
description:
THE GATE ON THE ACFR STATISTICAL SECTION, AND IT WAS FILED NOWHERE. This decision
exists only in fisc-4ua.4's 2026-08-21 note, which says in as many words "SO THIS
LANE OWNS A DECISION IT DID NOT KNOW IT HAD" and then leaves it unowned. Filed
2026-09-04 in a backlog review, so it can be settled before any YAML is written
for pp.162-194.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE LARGEST READER PAYOFF LEFT. ACFR pp.162-194 is roughly 25
ten-year tables -- net position pp.163-166, fund balances pp.167-169, sales tax
pp.170-172, assessed value p173, demographics p180, principal employers p182,
capital assets p184, operating indicators p185, redevelopment debt coverage p194.
Ten years of history is what a resident actually wants and what the site cannot
answer today. A statistical section is full of ratios, per-capita figures and
percentages, and the rule schema has no channel for a column that is not an
amount.

THE THREE THINGS THAT DO NOT WORK, each verified rather than assumed (fisc-4ua.4,
2026-08-21):
  - amount.Parse rejects "2.5%" as "not a recognized number", correctly.
  - A rule cannot simply stop at column nine. labelledValues advances the cursor
    to the end of the last MAPPED token and checkGap then requires the text to
    the next row's label to be whitespace; the unmapped tail
    "$ 88,896,362  2.5% $ 1,009" is not, so the read fails as an unmapped row.
  - skip: true does not help. parseRow calls amount.Parse BEFORE it consults
    row.Skip || col.Skip (internal/mapping/resolve.go), and that ordering is
    deliberate -- a skipped column still has to be a cell -- so this is not a bug
    to fix in passing.

THE OPTIONS:
  (a) A COLUMN KIND parsed by a different grammar (ratio/percent). A real
      extension of Column in internal/mapping/rule.go, plus a parser beside
      internal/amount.
  (b) A COLUMN DECLARED PRESENT-BUT-UNPARSED. Weakens "every cell is a cell" and
      must be fail-closed about what it will swallow.
  (c) A PART THAT STOPS MID-ROW. checkGap has to learn that a row can end before
      its printed line does.

RECOMMENDATION (a), and the argument is the project's own fail-closed rule. It is
the only option that turns a ratio column into a RECOGNISED SHAPE rather than a
hole. (b) is the "guess to keep the pipeline green" move AGENTS.md refuses by
name. (c) weakens checkGap, which is the only guard standing over the majority of
the corpus (see blind-scan-invents-rows) -- paying for one section by weakening
every page is the wrong trade.

A SEPARATE QUESTION THIS DECISION MUST ALSO ANSWER, and the default should be NO:
whether a parsed ratio becomes a FACT. Amounts are integer cents and facts are
figures the city printed in money. A ratio column that is RECOGNISED and NOT
PUBLISHED is a complete answer to the blocker, and it keeps the store's units
invariant intact. Deciding otherwise means saying what fact.Fact's units field
becomes.

WHERE TO PROVE IT FIRST: ACFR p177. It is already a committed fixture
(testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt) with arithmetic already proved against it
(internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go): nine of ten rows tie to the city's printed
totals and FY2024 is short by exactly its own Financed Purchases column,
$176,292. Its tenth column is the "2.5%" that motivates this. Smallest
end-to-end proof that whatever is chosen actually works.

ALSO CORRECT WHEN THIS IS SETTLED: fisc-4ua.4's description says the section runs
pp.162-195 with fund balances at pp.163-171. Its own note measured pp.162-194
(p195 blank) and fund balances at pp.167-169.
notes:
2026-09-05 MEASURED BY fisc-oakx.1's SURVEY (docs/acfr-statistical-section.md): THE DECISION STANDS AND NEEDS ONE EXTENSION IT DID NOT FORESEE. Settled on transposed p177, where the non-amount is a column; in the section's dominant orientation (years across) the non-amount is a ROW spanning every year column, and FOUR tables print one: p169 (debt service as % of noncapital expenditures), p179 (% of debt limit), p189 (LAVWMA coverage ratio), p192 (Percentage Change). A column kind cannot express those, skip cannot either (parseRow parses before consulting skip, and the trailing arm refuses a figure-bearing line after the last mapped row). Extension: a whole-row quantity override on the existing Row.Kind / Row.EffectiveKind idiom, carried by fisc-oakx.2. Zero tables need per-cell. Not a reopening -- read-not-published and the column channel are unchanged.
2026-09-05 IMPLEMENTED BY fisc-oakx.2, TO ITS LETTER WITH TWO NAMED DIVERGENCES. The channel is spelled 'quantity', not 'kind' — mapping.Kind was taken by the fact kind — with the four-value closed vocabulary the survey argued (amount default, amount_per_unit, percentage, number), and the row-override extension this bead's own 2026-09-05 note asked for landed in the same schema change (Row.Quantity beside Column.Quantity). Read-not-published held exactly: a recognised non-amount cell never becomes a Value. The 'default no' on non-amount facts stays undisturbed. What this bead did not foresee, measured while implementing: even the AMOUNT columns of p177 cannot publish — the fiscal year is the row label and the debt columns share one column identity (fisc-xmh2, beside fisc-7jtl's kind question) — so the whole rule is read-only and the Per Capita hazard is today fenced by the declaration alone (fisc-54vn).
close_reason: SETTLED as option (a): a Column gains a KIND with its own grammar, living beside internal/amount; a recognised non-amount column is READ so the row is fully accounted for and checkGap stays whole, and is NOT PUBLISHED as a fact. Facts stay integer cents. The argument turned out stronger than the bead made it: p177 has TWO non-amount columns, not one, and the second is why option (b) is wrong rather than merely weak -- 'Per Capita' ($1,009, 922, 713) PARSES CLEANLY as money, so a disposition that only fixes the grammar swallows a dollars-per-capita figure into a store whose invariant is city money in cents. The channel has to carry the UNIT. Implementation and its mutation proofs are fisc-oakx.2; the wider column-kind surface the section actually holds -- counts, coarser units, and p182's RANGES like '5600-6000' which fit no grammar at all -- is surveyed by fisc-oakx.1. Not decided, deliberately: whether a non-amount column ever becomes a fact. Default no; the day something needs it, that is a decision about fact.Fact's units field and gets its own bead.

title: projection-scopes-are-disjoint measures a 6-field key while netCells collides on a 3-field one
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03, found by the second review pass over the departmentwide lane (174cae9^..8889970) after a fix from the FIRST pass walked into it.

THE TWO KEYS ARE DIFFERENT AND ONLY ONE OF THEM CAN DOUBLE MONEY.

  internal/check/scopepairs.go  sharedKeys() builds cellAddress =
      (Kind, Category, FundGroup, Fund, FiscalYear, Basis)   -- SIX fields
  internal/project/sankey.go    netCells() keys on cellKey =
      (kind, category, fundGroup)                            -- THREE fields

ARM 2 of projection-scopes-are-disjoint is the only thing that verifies a
disjointScopes declaration against the corpus, and it measures the SIX-field
key. A projection that co-selects two scopes and nets them collides on the
THREE-field key. So a pair can share zero six-field addresses, be declared
disjoint, pass ARM 2 on every run, and still merge cells.

MEASURED ON THE COMMITTED STORE, all-funds-gross against
acfr-general-fund-summary:

    netCells cellKey (3 fields)     15 shared
    sharedKeys cellAddress (6)       0 shared

The 15 are the General Fund's ten revenue categories, both transfer directions
and the three fund-balance lines. They share no six-field address only because
one scope is FY2025 audited and the other FY2026/FY2027 adopted -- fiscal_year
and basis are in the six and not in the three.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the route matters. The first review pass over that
lane found that departmentwide-expenditures had not been added to
reconciledScopes. The fix added a general test requiring every committed scope to
be paired with the spine, and that test immediately reported
acfr-general-fund-summary as undeclared -- correctly. The fix for THAT was to
declare the pair disjoint with the reason 'they share no cell key'. The reason
was measured with sharedKeys, so it passed; under the key netCells uses it is
false. A declaration asserting safety that does not hold is worse than the
undeclared pair it replaced, because ARM 3 no longer reports it. That entry has
been reverted and the pair is now a NAMED gap pointing here.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY 'CHANGE THE KEY'. The six-field key is right for what ARM
2's finding SAYS -- 'these scopes share N keys of (kind, category, fund_group,
fund, fiscal year, basis), so a projection selecting both would publish that
money twice'. Widening the check to the three-field key would report the ACFR
pair as colliding, which under today's projections it does not: no projection
selects both, and the fiscal_year/basis difference is real. The question this
bead owns is which claim the table is making -- 'these cannot collide in any
projection anyone could write' or 'these do not collide in the ones that exist'
-- and the two need different mechanisms. fisc-gkv point B is the decision this
sits under.

NOT URGENT AND STILL REAL: no projection selects a pair that would merge today,
and projections-build plus published-projection-built would both go red on a
doubled cell. What is defective is the guard that exists to make that
unnecessary.
acceptance_criteria: either ARM 2 verifies a disjointScopes declaration against the key internal/project actually nets on, or the declaration states which of the two claims it makes and a check can fail on the other; the all-funds-gross / acfr-general-fund-summary pair is decided either way
notes: 2026-09-17 WHERE THE COARSE-KEY ARM WENT, recorded before Lane 3 L3.4 deletes scopepairs.go. The arm this bead added -- a disjointness declaration must hold under the coarsest key a projection can reach, cellAddress minus fund -- existed because a spine cell (no fund) and a detail cell (fund) could meet on one key. In internal/structure that pair is a CONTAINMENT: the spine is at fund-group-by-category and the detail at fund-by-category, each side is projected separately at the meet, and no key ever holds both. Two cuts at ONE level are compared on the level's own key by peers-overlap-only-by-declared-identity, and the ACFR pairs this bead was about are refused for sharing no basis (Cut.Bases, L3.2) rather than declared disjoint. What remains of the hazard is project.cellKey dropping the fund, which is L3.3's subject (fisc-w11l).
close_reason: ARM 2 now validates a disjointness declaration against BOTH the six-field cellAddress and the three-field netCellAddress that internal/project's netCells actually collides on. The bead asked which of two claims the table makes; the answer is neither -- a declaration must hold under the COARSEST key any projection uses, while the finest key remains the right test for whether a pair could collide at all. Re-measured: the gap is 5 of 21 pairs, not the 15 this bead's note claimed (15 is the shared-key count for one pair), and two of the five are reconciled pairs ARM 3 already refuses. Reddens nothing today. Also corrected cellAddress's doc comment, which argued the safety direction backwards and is why the gap survived review. Two tests, both proven failable.

title: The three lanes' fifth-pass fixes shipped unreviewed: 400 lines, 43 of them in site/app.js
description:
AGENTS.md's loop reviews the range, fixes, and re-reviews -- but the LAST pass's
own fix is never read by anything. It is committed after the final review and
the lane closes.

MEASURED at 8010fd1 over the three 2026-08-31 lanes, insertions excluding
.beads:

  caveats  2b38c0d   74 insertions   (site/index.html.tmpl 20, style.css 12,
                                      Go 28, Go tests 12, docs 1, app.js 1)
  drill    cae4b61  135 insertions   (app.js 31, drill.mjs 46, chart.html.tmpl
                                      15, style.css 6, Go 7, Go tests 30)
  badge    9c85d73  191 insertions   (app.js 11, jscheck 68, Go 59, Go tests 53)

400 insertions total. site/app.js is served to readers exactly as committed --
no bundler, no module system -- so its 43 lines here reached production without
a review pass. Every one of these commits is a FIX for a finding, which is the
class this project measures as most likely to introduce a defect: 27 of the
115 findings in those three lanes were defects an earlier pass's own fix
introduced (see fisc-yj4w notes).

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS: either a narrow /code-review over each of those
three diffs alone, or a rule that the fifth pass's fix must be small enough to
state why it needs none. The second is the cheaper answer and is what the
AGENTS.md change proposes; this bead is the first, for the three commits that
already shipped.

NOT A HYPOTHETICAL RISK CLAIM: nothing here asserts a defect is present. It
asserts that the one gate this project has was not applied to 400 lines.
notes:
2026-09-04 STEP 8 DISCHARGED FOR THE SEAMS LANE (471c56a^..6ec0d62), by the second route rather than the first.

That lane ran the full five passes. Its fifth-pass fix, 6ec0d62, is 47 insertions and 9 deletions across THREE files, none of them under site/ -- internal/check/scopepairs.go 31+/8-, internal/check/scopekeys_test.go 15+, mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml 1+/1-.

WHY IT NEEDS NO EXTRA PASS, stated rather than assumed:
  - ONE behavioural change: canMerge extracted and applied to the FINE arm as well as the coarse one. Measured -- it changes no pair's fine-grain count on the committed store -- and proven failable, since making canMerge return true unconditionally reddens TestTheMergeableMeasurementSkipsFactsNetCellsRefuses twice, on the 8-key count and on a named department-bearing fact.
  - ONE one-word correction: a dead bead id in a YAML comment, fisc-b0dq -> fisc-eaic.
  - The remaining ~35 lines are comment and one package qualifier.
  - ZERO lines of site/app.js, which is the class this bead was filed about: readers are served that file verbatim and tools/jscheck is the only thing standing behind it.

For contrast, the three lanes this bead was filed for had fifth-pass fixes of 74, 135 and 191 insertions with 43 lines of app.js between them.
2026-09-05 STEP 8 DISCHARGED FOR THE CORRECTNESS LANE (3666326^..7c28b54), by the
second route rather than the first, and the numbers are why.

That lane ran the full five passes. Its fifth-pass fix, 7c28b54, is 134
insertions across THREE files, all under internal/check, NONE under site/.

WHY IT NEEDS NO EXTRA PASS, stated rather than assumed:

  - 69 of the 134 added lines are comments and blank lines; 65 are code.
  - 55 of those 65 are ONE new test plus its helper
    (TestLosingAnExemptSpanStillMovesThePublishedCount, unresolvedIn).
  - subject.go's 12 changed lines are comment only -- a false claim corrected,
    no behaviour.
  - So the PRODUCTION-BEHAVIOUR change is about five lines: an `unresolved`
    counter incremented at one site, and one format string.
  - Both are covered, and covered by mutation rather than by assertion: delete
    the counter and TestLosingAnExemptSpanStillMovesThePublishedCount is the
    only test in the package that reddens; the format string is read back by
    unresolvedIn, which parses the figure a reader sees rather than recomputing
    it beside the check.

THE CONTRAST WITH THE THREE COMMITS THIS BEAD IS ACTUALLY ABOUT is the point. Those
put 43 lines into site/app.js, which readers are served verbatim with no compiler,
no types and no test framework. This one puts nothing there.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD IS UNCHANGED: 2b38c0d, cae4b61 and 9c85d73 still owe
the narrow pass, and 400 insertions is still the figure.
2026-09-17, L3.4: internal/check/scopepairs.go, whose fifth-pass fix this bead counts among the unreviewed lines, is deleted whole; scopekeys_test.go with it. The mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml lines it names are untouched.
PART OF THE UNREVIEWED SURFACE NO LONGER EXISTS, re-derived 2026-09-20. The drill lane's 15 insertions in chart.html.tmpl are gone: fisc-1osz deleted the template whole, so those lines cannot be reviewed and cannot ship a defect either. 400 insertions becomes 385 by that arithmetic, and the shape of the debt is unchanged -- the number was never the point.

WHAT THE POINT WAS AND STILL IS: site/app.js is served to readers exactly as committed, so its 43 lines across the three lanes reached production with no pass over them, and every one of these commits is a FIX for a finding, which this project measures as the class most likely to introduce a defect. Those 43 lines are untouched by the deletion.

AND THE SAME DEBT HAS ACCRUED AGAIN SINCE, which is worth knowing before this is claimed: e13-sankey-merge's own loop (fisc-lghb) has never run, and the lanes on it -- fisc-r0t6, both stages of fisc-phtp.2, fisc-jf8x, fisc-xozz and fisc-1osz -- deferred their review by the same rule. Whoever takes this should take it as one range with that one rather than as a separate audit of three older lanes.

title: The Revenue and Spending pages, and the retirement of drilldown.html
description:
Two views over project.FundFlowsProjection: Revenue at RenderTiers {0,2} drilling to {0,3}, Spending at {3,4} drilling to {4,5}. Nothing refuses two views over one projection -- Options.validate (export.go:381) refuses duplicate PATHS, assertPublishedReachable (data.go:396) builds a SET, and buildSite's collect (page.go:774) says in as many words that two views citing one page is the ordinary case.

Retire the drilldown.html view. Move tools/jscheck/fold.mjs:454's pins -- currently the exact string '52 flows between 40 nodes, from 280 facts' -- onto the two new pages with FRESHLY MEASURED values. Update docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md's 'Drawing it' section, whose {0,2,4} measurements this supersedes, and README.md:48-54, which names four pages and describes drilldown.html by name.

WHY SPENDING OPENS AT {3,4}: it draws as a single-source fan, General Fund into 23 divisions, which is a stacked bar wearing the site's visual language, and that is fine -- the division split is the question the page answers. The measured alternative {0,3,4} (revenue category -> General Fund -> division) lays out nearly as well: 33 links, 2 sub-pixel ribbons against 1. DECLINED because putting the revenue column on the EXPENSES page is the conflation this split exists to undo, not because it does not draw. {3,4,5} undrilled is the one that genuinely does not work: 68 nodes, 11 sub-pixel ribbons.

WHY REVENUE OPENS AT {0,2} AND NOT AT NAMED FUNDS: a citywide {0,3} capped to the top 8 funds names the General Fund at 49.18%, Wastewater 10.61%, Water 6.46% -- more informative on its face, but it lays out worse (8 sub-pixel ribbons against 5) and flattens the hierarchy the drill navigates, leaving the fund-group legend describing nothing on screen. Filed separately.

Spending's lede states plainly that ONLY THE GENERAL FUND IS DECOMPOSED: Budget Book pp.167-170 decompose that fund alone, and the other six groups' revenue ends at their funds. The money is not missing; the schedule that would break it down is not published.
close_reason:

WHAT THE BEAD GOT WRONG: it said Spending opens at {3,4} as a plain declaration. That tier set does not draw without View.Root -- see fisc-yj4w.6. title: Filter-and-rescale: the drill that this d3-sankey can actually draw
description:
filterToNode(doc,id) + capColumn(doc,tier,n) beside foldDocument in app.js, a drill stack, a breadcrumb, Escape to pop.

WHY NOT PER-NODE EXPANSION: fisc-ppkq, measured. The vendored build takes column count from topology and clamps the align into it.

WHY THE CAP IS NOT OPTIONAL, and this CORRECTS fisc-ppkq: that bead says 'rescaling is what makes special-revenue's 32 funds legible'. MEASURED FALSE. Rescaled to its own total, special-revenue still puts 22 of 49 ribbons under a pixel, because the concentration is WITHIN the group -- fund/200 alone is 34.916%, the bottom two are 0.034%. Capping to the top N by value and folding the tail into one aggregate fixes it: at N=8, 22 sub-pixel ribbons becomes 2; capital goes 4 -> 0. That is better than the SHIPPED drill-down, which has 7. Re-measure with the real fold before pinning N.

The aggregate is the same summing operation foldDocument already performs, so it inherits the locator union and cites nothing away. It must carry a label saying what it is ('24 smaller funds') and must NOT be presented as a printed figure.

THE GESTURE. fisc-ppkq's third objection is that node click and keydown are already setIsolated behind the keyActivation echo guard, and a second meaning on one activation is a new interaction contract. Resolved PER VIEW, not by overloading: a drill flag in FISC_CONFIG makes node activation drill on the two new pages and leaves it isolate on Overview. Isolation earns its keep on a three-column graph and means almost nothing on a two-column one, so the pages that drill are exactly the pages that do not need it. #detail also grows an explicit 'Show its 32 funds' button, so the affordance is discoverable and keyboard-reachable.

seam.mjs:57 requires every querySelector LITERAL in app.js to be in harness.mjs KNOWN_SELECTORS; a COMPUTED selector is reported unanswerable rather than checked, so breadcrumb and drill-button lookups must use literals or they quietly opt out.

DO NOT TOUCH NODE_WIDTH, NODE_PADDING, CHART_WIDTH, CHART_HEIGHT, LABEL_GUTTER, FUND_ORDER, nodeRank: layout.mjs pins 195 crossings / 457,434,169 / 14 stale pairs against them AND requires those figures as quoted phrases in app.js's comments.
close_reason:
Landed in bd0a098 together with .7 -- they could not be split, because a drill with no page to drill on is dead code and this project refuses documents no reader can open.

THREE DEFECTS ONLY MEASUREMENT FOUND, all past a green go build, go test, make js and fisc verify:
(1) layOut aligned on RENDER_TIERS while a drilled document is folded to DRILL.tiers, so every tier-3 node got indexOf -1, d3 clamped it to column 0 and died inside its own ordering pass. A blank chart on the first click of the feature.
(2) Spending's {3,4} could not draw AT ALL -- fund-flows carries eleven tier-0 revenue nodes with no ancestor at 3 or 4. Hence View.Root, which was not in the plan.
(3) Both pages announced themselves to a screen reader as 'by fund and division'. Hence View.ChartSubject.

THE BEAD'S OWN MEASUREMENTS HELD. The cap really does take special-revenue from 22 sub-pixel ribbons to 2, and the gesture really did need declaring rather than overloading.

title: caveats.html: the nine edits, two of them silent
description:
ADDING A VIEW IS NINE EDITS and two are silent if missed. This is the same hazard shape as the adding-a-check-is-five-edits memory, and the guards here are better: five of the nine fail closed with a named message.
  1 site/caveats.html.tmpl                                    --
  2 site/embed.go:31 //go:embed                               SILENT at compile time; runtime 'parse page template'
  3 page.go:24-32 template const                              --
  4 export.go:678 templateRendersADocument -- LEAVE FALSE     an arm makes validate demand a projection this page cannot have
  5 export.go:708 templateIsKnown -- ADD                      refusal with MISLEADING advice; its own doc comment says so
  6 export.go:634 templateRendersLede -- ADD                  loud refusal 'has no {{.Lede}}'
  7 export.go:656/:722 year control, tiers -- NO ARM          correctly refuses a caller who sets them
  8 page.go:829 dispatch + buildCaveatsPage + caveatsPageData loud refusal via default:
  9 pkg/cmd/export/data.go views()                            PAGE NEVER WRITTEN
Unguarded follow-ons: style.css; README.md:48's page count; export_test.go:988 (len(got)!=3) and :1042.

buildCaveatsPage follows buildProvenancePage (page.go:1559) -- the existing shape for a page rendering no projection of its own. Aggregate SHAPE-BLIND over sortedKeys(o.Projections) through a documentCaveats decoder modelled on documentSources (page.go:106), so a shape this package has never heard of still contributes. Refuse: no caveats at all; a caveat with no id or summary; TWO ENTRIES CLAIMING ONE ANCHOR.

DO NOT add an Options/Result field to carry caveats from the command. pkg/cmd/export holds projections as []byte only; decoding there is a second reader of a contract that already has one, which internal/export's package doc forbids.

Footer sources stay EMPTY: TestEachViewsFooterCitesItsOwnSources (views_test.go:155) enforces that a page must not claim provenance for figures it never showed.

Append the view after the drill-down and before the provenance block (data.go:519) so got[0..2] stay stable in TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone.

assertPublishedReachable's drawn&&declared arm (data.go:415) does NOT fire -- the view names no projection -- so the three fund-flows-* unviewedDocuments entries stay valid even though caveats.html LISTS those documents' caveats. Say so in fundFlowsUnviewed's const or the next reader reads it as a contradiction.

THE TEST THAT MAKES THE FEATURE CHECKABLE: walk every summary link on every rendered page and assert its anchor exists as an id= in caveats.html -- the analogue of TestEveryCitationTheClientComposesResolves.
close_reason:
Landed in 99d83d9. The nine edits were nine edits and the guards fired as described: the templateRendersLede omission and the missing dispatch arm both produced named refusals during development.

CONFIRMED: nothing refuses two views over one projection, and nothing refused a view naming no projection once templateIsKnown had its arm.

THE ANCHOR IS PER (DOCUMENT, CAVEAT), not per caveat, and this was forced rather than chosen -- transfer-legs-unpaired carries three different texts across the published columns. caveatAnchor(stem, id) is the single spelling.

TestEveryCaveatSummaryLinksToAnAnchorThatExists is the check the bead nominated and it is the one that matters: every other guard stops at the file, because the filesystem has no opinion about a fragment. Mutation-verified.

ADDED BEYOND THE BEAD: caveats.html asserts it ships no FISC_CONFIG blob, so the p76 substring test cannot regress into passing on machine-readable bytes the way its index.html version had.

title: One-line caveat summaries, and the plumbing for a page that does not exist yet

caveatRef{id,summary,href} as the client-facing shape; chrome.CaveatsPath at page.go:898-910. Templates render {{.Summary}}.

(1) pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go:255 asserts index.html contains the LITERAL strings 'Transfers Out to CIP' and 'fisc-9gh'. Both live in the caveat paragraph that is moving. Its doc comment is a 25-line load-bearing argument that the page is where a reader meets both claims -- REWRITE it to point at caveats.html, do not delete it.
(2) TWO ASSET-WALK TESTS 404 ON A FRAGMENT. export_test.go:164 and views_test.go:236 skip a ref only when HasPrefix('#'), so caveats.html#x is stat'ed verbatim. Both need strings.Cut(ref,'#') -- which is also what lets the walk SEE the new links.
(3) A SINGLE-VIEW SITE HAS NO CAVEATS PAGE. writeGolden and Options.views()'s default (export.go:526) produce one view; an unconditional link fails TestEveryAssetThePageAsksForWasWritten and would ship a dead link. CaveatsPath empty => plain text.

TestYearViewKeysAreTheOnesTheClientReads does NOT break -- it compares top-level keys only -- which is exactly why the inner keys need their own pin: TestCaveatRefKeysAreTheOnesTheClientReads -> {href,id,summary}.

jscheck moves too: year.mjs:29,51,207-212,302,311-315 and harness.mjs:391,585. THE STUB DOES NOT COMPUTE textContent FROM CHILDREN (harness.mjs:102-123), so once caveats are <li><a> those four sites must read the anchor child or they go GREEN BUT DEAD.
close_reason:

ALL THREE PREDICTED TRAPS WERE REAL. (1) The p76 test was passing on window.FISC_CONFIG rather than on anything a reader sees -- measured by stripping the config script, after which neither string remains visible. (2) The asset walks did stat the fragment verbatim. (3) The single-view site does need the conditional href.

title: Caveat becomes a type, so a caveat can be linked to
description:
Caveats []string -> []Caveat{ID,Summary,Text,AppliesTo} on all three document shapes. Pure refactor; the only byte-visible diff is in the goldens.

PRODUCERS: sankey.go:272,667,901-911,1001; fundflows.go:47-56,139,435,444; trends.go:145,346,364-390. Each builder returns error, so a DUPLICATE ID WITHIN ONE DOCUMENT MUST FAIL CLOSED at build time -- the ID becomes a published URL fragment.

TWO PRODUCER SUBTLETIES THAT DECIDE THE ANCHOR SCHEME. sankey.go:1114 transferCaveat has THREE possible texts under one concept (legs match / printed CIP column / plain residual), varying by document. sankey.go:1045 contestedCaveat is FY2027-only and its ID must embed the fund group, or two contestedTotals entries collide on one anchor.

THE DELICATE CONSUMER is internal/check/graph.go:1023-1037. The comparison is WHOLE-STRING EQUALITY -- slices.Contains(caveats, project.ConstraintTierCaveat()) -- and that is deliberate, argued at graph.go:1013 and fundflows.go:52: 'two authors agreeing is not the same claim as the document saying the thing.' Adapt to find by .ID then compare .Text, reporting the two failures apart. ID-ONLY EQUALITY WOULD BE A NEW FAIL-OPEN in the exact place the comment at :1029 was written to close.

Measured at 7a3b705: that check reports over 4 documents, not 2.

TESTS THAT WILL NOT COMPILE and are not obvious from grepping the field: sankey_test.go:767 hasCaveat joins the slice (used :221,289,310); sankey_test.go:641,674,701,735-760,811-867; fundflows_test.go:140 + containsString at :314; checks_test.go:1191-1192,1219. Fixtures that stop unmarshalling: views_test.go:67, export_test.go:544.

NO schema_version BUMP. Measured: the client never reads doc.metadata.caveats, only year.caveats, which the packager builds from freshly built bytes.
close_reason:
Landed in 32f0765. Caveats []string -> []Caveat on all three shapes; both goldens moved with machine-checked diff rules; constraint-tier-vocabulary now finds by id and compares text, mutation-proved that id-only is a fail-open (40 passed 1 failed vs 41 passed 0 failed over the same drifted document).

WHAT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the best thing in the commit: ValidateCaveats was given the document's OWN NODE IDS, and the applies_to arm immediately caught a defect in this commit's own new field. transferCaveat named both legs unconditionally while caveats() emits it when EITHER side is non-zero, so a transfers-in-only document published an applies_to pointing at a node it does not carry. TestLabelFallback builds exactly that document and went red.

That moves the fold hazard the bead files under fisc-yj4w.8 from 'guard against it later' to 'already guarded at build time' for the PUBLISHED document. The fold hazard proper -- an id that survives publication but not foldDocument -- is still fisc-yj4w.8's.

CONFIRMED, against the Plan agent's finding: TestYearViewKeysAreTheOnesTheClientReads does NOT break, because it compares top-level keys only. A new sibling pin, TestCaveatMetaKeysAreTheOnesTheDocumentCarries, is what covers the inner shape.

title: The Overview page's apparatus collapses behind <details>
description:
index.html.tmpl only. What-we-inferred, Caveats and the flow table each go in a closed <details> whose summary states the count; #table-view ships open today and closes. Reuse the details>summary styling at site/style.css:698-829.
