title: A projection schema's required list is enforced by nothing: every key can be dropped from it and the suite stays green
description:
FAIL-OPEN, measured 2026-09-24 while landing Link.Contra (fisc-0ws9).

schema/projection.schema.json's link object states a required list of ten keys.
Dropping any one of them from that list breaks NO test.

MEASURED, four mutations, each confirmed to apply before it was run (a sed that
matches nothing is indistinguishable by exit code from a code that survives):

  drop "contra"      from required -> 0 failing tests
  drop "partition"   from required -> 0 failing tests
  drop "derived"     from required -> 0 failing tests
  drop "transfer_id" from required -> 0 failing tests

over go test ./internal/project/ ./internal/export/ ./pkg/cmd/export/.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. TestTheSchemasStateWhatTheProjectionsCarry compares
schema.NamesDeep against schema.StructNames -- that is the PROPERTIES list
against the struct's JSON names, and it never reads 'required'. So the schema
can state a key, describe it, and not require it, and the two sides still agree.

WHAT IT COSTS. AGENTS.md, 'Where writing goes': the projection contract is that
every key is on every object, which is why Link.Contra ships with no omitempty.
That contract currently lives only in the emitter's struct tags. A projection
that stopped emitting a key would produce documents that still validate, and
internal/export decodes without importing internal/project -- so the far side
reads a zero value with no error anywhere, which is the failure mode the
properties comparison was written to prevent and only half prevents.

THIS IS NOT ABOUT contra. It is general over the link object and was found by
mutating the new field; the same hole was already open on the other nine.

WHAT NEEDS DOING is a schema.RequiredDeep beside NamesDeep, and then a decision
this bead deliberately does not take: WHICH objects in projection.schema.json
must require every property they state. It is not all of them -- metadata's
if/then makes headline conditional by design, and the counts blocks differ by
projection (the same comment that TestTheSchemasStateWhatTheProjectionsCarry
opens with). So the arm is 'required == properties, for this named set of
objects', and naming the set is the work.

NOT FIXED IN THE SESSION THAT FOUND IT, and the reason is AGENTS.md's own rule:
the fix is not one line in a file the pass was already touching, and a wrong
answer here weakens the schema in a way that looks like strengthening it.

title: Only one of the seven declared steps widens, so the column control does nothing on six of them
description:
REPORTED by the owner from a browser session, 2026-09-23: "Increasing columns
only seems to work on some drill downs, was expecting it to work everywhere."

CONFIRMED, and it is a declaration gap rather than a client defect.
pkg/cmd/export/data.go declares seven steps -- fund-group (:683), fund (:775),
division (:853), revenue-category (:876), object-category (:957), transfers
(:1019) and fund-departments (:1092) -- and ONLY fund declares Widen (:800,
Widen: []int{5}). Every other step draws three columns however wide the reader's
window is. DrillStep.Widen (internal/export/export.go:551-572) is where the
permission lives and six steps do not ask for it.

THE ROOM HALF IS ALREADY DONE, so this is not blocked on layout: app.js derives
its ceiling from the steps, composes one media query per column it could offer
(COLUMN_QUERIES, site/app.js:1075) and hands style.css --chart-max. Declaring a
wider step moves the cap, the query and the checker's expected geometry together.

BLOCKED ON fisc-ke1f, and the blocker is load-bearing rather than tidy:
validateSteps refuses a step whose Tiers EQUALS its parent's, but equality is not
containment, and a widened parent makes a child's tier set a strict SUBSET of
what is already on screen. validateSteps accepts that pair and the client then
refuses to open the node. So a Widen added before fisc-ke1f is decided is a
declaration Go blesses and the page will not draw.

WHAT NEEDS DOING once fisc-ke1f is decided: declare Widen on the steps that can
carry it, ONE AT A TIME, each with its rungs.mjs equivalence arm green at widths
3 and 4. Which steps those are is not assumed here -- a step that keeps nothing
is refused a widening by validateSteps' own arm, and transfers keeps nothing.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF ITS NEIGHBOURS. fisc-ipif is about a FIFTH column and the
chain that would ask for one; fisc-ke1f is about the subset arm. Neither states
the reader-facing fact that six of seven steps offer no fourth column at all.

title: Every focus indicator on the page is pure white in dark mode, and no test reads a colour
description:
REPORTED by the owner from a browser session, 2026-09-23: "Still getting a white
border when clicking on things." The extent of the chart's ring was fixed under
fisc-0oth; its PAINT was not, and the paint is what the reader sees.

--ink-1 is #ffffff in BOTH dark blocks (site/style.css:84 and :114), and it is
the paint for every focus indicator on the page:

  site/style.css:279-282  :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink-1);
                          outline-offset: 2px }   -- UNSCOPED, so every
                          focusable element on the page is covered and nothing
                          falls through to a UA ring
  site/style.css:767-771  svg.sankey .node:focus-visible rect
                          { stroke: var(--ink-1); stroke-width: 2 }
  site/style.css:782-784  svg.sankey .link:focus-visible { outline-offset: 0 }
                          -- drops the offset only; the global white box still
                          applies, and a <path>'s bounding box is the whole
                          bezier's rectangle
  site/style.css:439-442  .year-toggle input:focus-visible + label

THREE THINGS MAKE IT READ AS A CLICK ARTEFACT RATHER THAN AS FOCUS:

(1) A RIBBON STILL GETS A WHITE BOX AROUND MOSTLY EMPTY SPACE, which is the
    original complaint. The rule's own comment already names the answer: "If it
    still reads wrong it wants a drawn focus echo rather than a second guess
    here." That is now the measurement rather than a hypothetical.
(2) THERE IS NO g.node[aria-pressed="true"] RULE. clickNode -> setIsolated ->
    applyEmphasis (site/app.js:2259, :4668, :4679) set aria-pressed and .dim on
    the others and nothing else, so the white focus ring is the ONLY visible
    feedback a click has and the reader attributes it to the click.
(3) restoreFocus (site/app.js:2354-2385) focuses PROGRAMMATICALLY after every
    drill -- onto the innermost .crumb-back, or back at the overview onto
    chart.querySelector("g.node"), an arbitrary first mark the reader never
    touched. Programmatic focus matches :focus-visible, so the ring arrives on a
    pointer click as readily as on Tab.

WHAT NEEDS DOING, in this order, because each makes the next smaller:
  - isolation gets its own indicator, so a click has feedback that is not the
    focus ring;
  - a ribbon gets a drawn focus echo instead of the bounding box;
  - the ring's paint moves off --ink-1. --ink-2 is #c3c2b7 and already carries a
    measured contrast ratio.

IT CHANGES UNDER NO GATE UNLESS THE FIX BRINGS ONE, which is why fisc-6at is the
neighbour and not a duplicate. The one CSS assertion in the tree,
TestTheChartsFocusRingIsDeclaredOnTheMarkAndAfterTheDerivedRule
(internal/export/export_test.go), matches SELECTOR STRINGS AND SOURCE ORDER and
never reads a colour -- which is exactly why var(--ink-1) could sit there being
white. fisc-6at names the cheap partial that would have caught it: extract two
known rule blocks by selector string and assert the one property differs, two
string indexes and a compare rather than a parser. The fix should bring that arm.

title: jscheck's arms become node:test tests, module by module, and harness.mjs becomes a helper
description:
DECISION, taken 2026-09-23 on the owner's report: "I honestly don't understand
jscheck. We should probably add unit tests for the JavaScript instead."

WHAT CANNOT CHANGE, so the decision is not mistaken for a bigger one. site/app.js
has no module system by design -- AGENTS.md, "The node boundary". Nothing can
import a function out of it, so a unit test in the ordinary sense is unreachable
and every check must load the whole file into a vm. That is harness.mjs
(loadApp, domStub, the fixtures) and it stays. What changes is its standing: it
stops being a framework and becomes a helper a test file imports.

WHAT CHANGES. The layer above it -- one checks() per module returning
{name, ok, detail} booleans with prose names, no file:line, no diffs, and a
group() wrapper that exists only because run.mjs turns any throw into "a whole
check module threw" and continues.

MEASURED, because the node-boundary rule turns on it: node v22.22.0, and
require('node:test') and require('node:assert') both resolve with NO
package.json and NO node_modules in this tree. So the runner is stdlib, node
stays off the deploy path, and a contributor with only Go can still build, test
and land a change. No dependency decision is owed.

WHAT IT BUYS, named so it can be held to:
  - Per-test isolation: a throw fails one test rather than discarding a module's
    other claims. That is the whole cost paragraph of fisc-bxal, and drill.mjs's
    group() wrapper retires with the module.
  - assert.deepStrictEqual diffs and file:line, instead of a composed sentence.
  - --test-name-pattern, to run one check.
  - An async arm that rejects fails. fisc-dn9 is on record: a synchronous runner
    made Boolean(promise) always true and every async arm unfalsifiable, which is
    why settleCheck exists. Under node:test that defect is structurally
    impossible.

THE COST, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. Most arms print their measured
figures ON PASS, which AGENTS.md, "Before you quote a number" requires: a count
is pinned to the thing that re-measures it, and layout.mjs is named there as what
that looks like. t.diagnostic() preserves it. AN ARM THAT CONVERTS TO A BARE
assert.ok HAS SILENTLY DROPPED A PIN.

THE STRANGLER, and its end state. Converted files are named <name>.test.mjs, the
pattern node's runner discovers; harness.mjs keeps its name and is not
discovered. make js runs BOTH runners while both exist. run.mjs's hardcoded
import list and its literal order array shrink by one entry per conversion --
both, or a module is imported and never run. seam.mjs's settleCheck arms must NOT
retire until the last module leaves run.mjs. The end state is no run.mjs and no
settleCheck.

CONVERSION IS NOT A REWRITE: same measurement, same fixture, same figures, same
words in the test name. A conversion that changes what an arm measures is a new
check wearing an old name, and the diff stops being reviewable. An arm that looks
wrong during conversion is filed, not fixed in the same edit.
notes:
TWO GOTCHAS EVERY CONVERSION AFTER THE FIRST WILL MEET, both measured while
converting layout.mjs.

(1) A VALUE MEASURED IN THE vm IS OF ANOTHER REALM. app.js runs in a node `vm`,
so an array d3 built in there carries THAT realm's Array.prototype, and
assert.deepStrictEqual compares prototypes -- a measured `[]` is not deep-equal
to an `[]` written in a test file. Both sides PRINT IDENTICALLY, so the failure
reads as the assertion library being broken. harness.here() re-homes the
measured side; apply it there and not to the wanted side. Array.from and NOT
.map, because Array.prototype.map builds through the RECEIVER's constructor and
hands back another vm array, so the re-homing silently does nothing.

(2) `node --test` WANTS A GLOB, NOT A DIRECTORY. Handed `tools/jscheck/` it
tries to load that path as a module and fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which reads
like a broken suite rather than a wrong argument. The Makefile quotes
"tools/jscheck/*.test.mjs" so node expands it rather than the shell.

MEASURED ON THE FIRST CONVERSION: layout produced 27 claims under run.mjs and
runs 27 tests under node --test, green both ways. A throw in one describe's
before() cancels that suite's tests AND NAMES THEM, leaves the other suites
reporting, and still exits 1 -- where run.mjs discarded all 27 behind one
anonymous "a whole check module threw". fisc-bxal carries that measurement.

title: A dead check id is a pointer at nothing and no gate refuses one
description:
`make beadrefs` refuses a bead id that names no bead and `make doccheck` a citation naming no section of AGENTS.md, a source path resolving to no file, and a cited Go test name no _test.go declares. A dead CHECK ID is the same pointer at nothing in different clothes, and nothing refuses one: aef3d8f deleted nine checks and left 92 references to them and to six deleted declarations across about thirty files, one of which had already reached README.md as a guarantee the tree does not give.

THE OBVIOUS DESIGN DOES NOT WORK AND THE MEASUREMENTS ARE HERE SO THE NEXT SESSION DOES NOT RE-DERIVE THEM. Measured 2026-09-22 after the sweep:

  (1) THE NAMESPACE IS SHARED, so no syntactic recognizer separates a check id from anything else. `transfers-by-fund` is a scope, `fund-flows-2027` a published stem, `wages-and-benefits` a taxonomy slug, `restricted-by-law` a constraint tier, `p0067-internal-service-is-250000-high-by-object` an exception name, `a-transfer-in-is-printed-at-both-ends` a peer identity, `e13-sankey-merge` a branch. All are lowercase hyphenated tokens of three or more segments, exactly like every live check id.

  (2) THE POPULATION IS LARGE. 1,030 mentions of live check ids in tracked prose and comments, so a convention change -- requiring a canonical citation form the way doccheck does for AGENTS.md sections -- is not a small commit.

  (3) EVEN SCOPED TO BACKTICKS IT DOES NOT NARROW ENOUGH. 54 distinct backticked hyphenated tokens of three or more segments appear in docs/*.md, README.md and AGENTS.md; 23 are live check ids and the other 31 are scopes, published stems, taxonomy slugs, constraint tiers, exception names, peer identities, memory keys, docs/ filenames and a branch name. Before the sweep six more were DEAD check ids, indistinguishable by shape from any of the 31.

A DENYLIST OF RETIRED IDS IS REFUSED, not merely disliked: it is a claim about what USED to exist, which is git's, and AGENTS.md's "History's home is git" applies to a gate's own declaration as much as to prose.

WHAT COULD WORK is a UNION RESOLVER: a token of the shape above must resolve against one of the tree's declared vocabularies -- check.All(), project's scopes and published stems, data/taxonomy.yaml's slugs, data/funds.yaml's groups, the constraint tiers, structure.BudgetBookExceptions' names, the peer identities, docs/ filenames -- or against a declared exemption for the ordinary English hyphenations that remain. A Go tool in the same module can import each of those, so it needs no bd, no Dolt, no node and no network: the standing beadrefs and doccheck already have.

WHERE IT GOES: tools/doccheck, which already walks the path list and already carries the exemption machinery and the floor checks a new arm needs.

MUTATION IT MUST PASS: re-point one comment at a deleted check id and the arm goes red naming the file and the line.
acceptance_criteria: A doccheck arm that resolves a hyphenated token against the tree's declared vocabularies, with its false-positive population measured and declared; the mutation above run and recorded.

title: GESTURE_WIRING pins seven source lines that chart.mjs now measures by dispatch, except one
description:
tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's GESTURE_WIRING asserts seven whole lines of render() appear in site/app.js verbatim, JSDoc casts included. It is the same source-text pin fisc-qw1m retired from layout.mjs, and its justification has the same stale premise -- it says the stub answers no '#chart' selector, that D3.select('#chart').size() is 0 and that an .attr() accessor is invoked zero times. af63b3e made all three false; that paragraph is corrected in place, and the pin is left standing because retiring it needs an arm written.

SIX OF THE SEVEN LINES ARE ALREADY MEASURED BY BEHAVIOUR, on the real corpus, by tools/jscheck/chart.mjs:
  the class -- arm (c) compares m.getAttribute('class') against app.nodeClass(d);
  aria-keyshortcuts -- the same arm's want-set;
  clickNode, doubleClickNode, keyNode and the dblclick wiring -- arm (d) fires them by dispatch and asserts what each did.

THE SEVENTH IS NOT. The .text() call that writes the flag tspan -- the derived diamond and the right-pointing triangle that say a mark opens -- is reachable here only because nodeFlags is NAMED in app.js. chart.mjs's arm (c) walks a mark's <text> children and asserts the tspans carry d.label and the short signed amount; it never reads the FLAG tspan. drill.mjs compares nodeClass and nodeFlags over LAID nodes, which is the rule and not its use.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: read the flag tspan off each drawn mark in chart.mjs and compare it to app.nodeFlags(d), the way the label and amount tspans are compared; then delete GESTURE_WIRING and its arm.

MUTATION THE REPLACEMENT MUST KEEP: drop the nodeFlags .text() call from render() and the flag arm goes red on the marks that carry the triangle and on those that carry the diamond alone.
acceptance_criteria: GESTURE_WIRING and its arm deleted; a chart.mjs arm reads the flag tspan off drawn marks; the mutation above run and recorded.

title: LABEL_SELECTION pins five source lines to work around a stub gap that is closed
description:
tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's LABEL_SELECTION asserts that five whole lines of
render() appear in site/app.js verbatim, JSDoc casts included:

  '.attr("y", /** @param {LaidNode} d */ (d) => labelPlacement(d, lastColumn).y)'

That is not a measurement. It pins code SHAPE, so a behaviour-preserving
refactor of those lines takes the arm red while the page draws identically.

ITS OWN JUSTIFICATION IS STALE. The paragraph above it says: "The stub answers
no '#chart' selector, so no check here can read an attribute back off a drawn
<text>; the rule and its use are two claims and only one of them is reachable."
tools/jscheck/chart.mjs, which landed later, does exactly that -- it reads
attributes off drawn marks with getAttribute (d, stroke-width, aria-label,
aria-pressed and a want-set), and walks a mark's <text> children for their
tspans. So <text> is reachable and the attributes are readable.

THE FIX IS A DELETION. Read x, y, dy and text-anchor back off the drawn <text>
and compare them to labelPlacement's own answer for that node. That checks the
thing the arm cares about -- the placement measured above is the placement
drawn -- instead of the spelling of the lines that produce it. The five pinned
strings and the stale paragraph both go.

MUTATION THAT MUST STILL GO RED, because it is the one the current arm exists
for and the replacement has to keep: revert render()'s label selection to
`d.depth === 0` and leave labelPlacement untouched. The arm's own comment
records that with that mutation "every other arm here stayed green. This is the
one that goes red."

SAME CLASS AS THE STUB GAPS: fisc-uyc2 (classList is a no-op), fisc-2ial (no
contains(), so focusInChart answers false). Each is a check written around what
the stub could not see. This one is the reverse -- written around a gap that has
since closed, and never revisited.
close_reason: Closed at e0abf6b. LABEL_SELECTION's five pinned strings and its stale paragraph are gone; drawnPlacement walks each mark's children for its text.halo the way chart.mjs does and compares x, y, dy and text-anchor to labelPlacement's own answer, over the object-category window because it has an interior column. dy is compared as an ABSENCE, since labelPlacement answers null and d3 turns that into removeAttribute. The mutation this bead required still goes red and is still the only arm in the suite that does: render() reverted to d.depth === 0 with labelPlacement untouched, naming expenditure/wages-and-benefits with all four attributes wrong. The dy line alone reverted also reddens it. AND THE ARM ABOVE IT CLAIMED A MUTATION IT CANNOT WITNESS -- it reads labelPlacement, which that mutation does not touch -- corrected in the same commit. drill.mjs's GESTURE_WIRING is the same pin one file over and is filed as fisc-k3zj.

title: A derived mark's label, rationale and source note are composed in JavaScript
description:
FOUND while auditing the Go/JS boundary, 2026-09-22. site/app.js's markGap
(~:3700) and carryResidual (~:3579) build a derived node's label, rationale and
source_note in the client -- full sentences about what the city's schedules do
and do not decompose, composed from figures the client sums.

IT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN ACCIDENTAL. pkg/cmd/export/rungs.go's drawnMark doc
comment says Go computes which mark exists, its tier and its cents "and NOT its
prose: the rationale and the source note are built from labels and locators the
walk does not decode". That is true: export.GraphNode (internal/export/reach.go)
carries id, tier, role, parent and derived, and NO label. So the fix is one
decoded field plus prose on export.Mark, and the schema arm follows from
rungs.schema.json being additionalProperties: false.

WHY IT IS WORTH MOVING. AGENTS.md's boundary says a claim about the documents is
Go's; three things follow from this one being the client's.

  - THE RESIDUAL'S LABEL IS HARD-CODED "Not broken down by fund". Every residual
    on testdata/rungs.json is on a fund-group rung, so the wording is right today

  - markGap's source_note tells the reader that fisc verify holds that difference

  - tools/jscheck/drill.mjs pins several of these wordings as source-text

NEIGHBOURS: fisc-4lsx (what fisc verify does not witness), fisc-jdsb (the pinned

over).

title: The fund column's order and membership are the packager's, and the client holds no list
description:
DONE in this commit; filed so the change has an id the tree can cite.

site/app.js held the fund groups as two six-element literals -- FUND_ORDER and
FUND_COLOR_VAR -- over a set data/funds.yaml declares seven of and
fy2024-actual publishes all seven of.

WHAT REPLACES THEM: internal/export's fundGroupsOf puts the fund groups a
column draws in a declared order, with a group its sequence does not name
after the ones it does, in id order. schema/column.schema.json states the
shape and enumerates no id, because the set is open.

The client reads that order, composes --fund-<slug> and falls back to --muted
where no stylesheet declares one, and reads role == fund_group rather than an
id prefix.
close_reason:
Landed. internal/export's fundGroupsOf puts the fund groups a column draws in a declared order -- fundGroupDisplayOrder, which carries the CVD measurement that used to sit in site/app.js -- with a group its sequence does not name after the ones it does, in id order. schema/column.schema.json states the shape of fund_groups and enumerates no id, because the set is open; it separately gains the role enum, held to internal/project's declared block in both directions.

MEASURED OVER THE REAL CORPUS, which is what makes the open-set design more than an argument: fy2024-actual publishes SEVEN fund groups and fy2026-adopted six, and permanent comes out last in the first because the sequence does not name it.

site/app.js holds no fund-group list at all now. fundGroupPlace is one rule for nodeRank and buildLegend, fundColorVar composes --fund-<slug> from the served slug and falls back to --muted where no stylesheet declares one, and isFundGroup reads role == fund_group rather than an id prefix.

THREE MUTATIONS, all run. Reversing fundGroupDisplayOrder: internal/export red by name, and make js red on the stale-stacked pair count. Restoring nodeRank's indexOf so an unplaced group scores -1: fold.mjs red, with general first in both the legend and the fund column instead of last. Reverting isFundGroup to the id prefix: fold.mjs red, the oddly-named group gone from the legend entirely.

TWO OF THOSE ARMS HAD TO BE BUILT, and the first version of this lane shipped without them: the -1 and the prefix mutations were both GREEN against the suite as it stood, because every fixture and every published document spells the prefix and the role together and names every group it draws. What made them falsifiable is a column whose fund_groups omits a group its node table carries, and a fund group whose id is not under fund-group/.

A FIXTURE WAS HIDING ONE, found by the role change: five jscheck node helpers stamped role: "" on every node including fund-group ones, which is a document no export can write. They take roleOf(id) now.

facts.jsonl unmoved; testdata/rungs.json unmoved; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped. make pre-commit exit 0.

title: A schedule with no sources draws with provenance missing, and the first pin throws instead of bannering
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-23 by driving the shipped site/app.js over fisc export's bytes at ebdb422 (the app.js audit pass of fisc-lghb), replacing the lifecycle.mjs measurement this bead was filed on. citations() (site/app.js:898) no longer guards either shape: it iterates `sources` and `source.pages` directly. Four shapes, served at the column path with everything else intact:

  (a) the sankey schedule with no `sources`: the chart DRAWS (25 marks), no banner. The first node the reader pins throws TypeError 'sources is not iterable' out of pin() (site/app.js:5136) inside the focus/click handler -- uncaught, so no banner either -- and the detail panel is left half-built: amount, label and chips, no Sources block, applyEmphasis never runs.
  (b) a locator with a doc_id and no `pages`: the chart REFUSES, banner 'The chart failed to draw: TypeError: s.pages is not iterable', 0 marks, 0 table rows. Refused by accident -- the throw is from tableRows' citations() call inside the repaint, caught into fail() -- and the words are a stack trace rather than a refusal by name, but the reader sees no chart and no missing citation.
  (c) a locator whose doc_id CONFIG.docs lacks: draws, no banner, 'Sources:' EMPTY on that ribbon's detail panel and in its table cell (citations()'s `if (!doc) continue`). page.go's unionSources comment names this as the one failure mode the project exists to prevent, and guards it from the Go side: CONFIG.docs is the union of every year's metadata.sources, and sources are derived from the links' own locators.
  (d) a printed link with `locators: []`: draws, no banner, 'Sources:' empty. schema/column.schema.json requires minItems 1 on a non-derived link's locators and fact_ids, so no exported file carries it.

WHY IT STAYS P2. Every shape is refused at the writer: schema/column.schema.json requires `sources` (minItems 1) on every schedule and `pages` on every locator, encodeColumn refuses bytes that fail it, and the generated_by comparison in loadColumn catches a cached copy from before those keys existed. The only route is a hand-edited file served at the column path.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, and it is not restoring a key check: a chart whose ribbons cite nothing is a chart this project should not draw. The honest form is a positive claim -- 'every drawn PRINTED link reached at least one citation' -- asserted after the table is built, a statement about the DRAWING rather than a re-reading of the document's keys. Note the qualifier: markGap's derived ribbon (site/app.js:3776) ships fact_ids [] and locators [] by design, and pinned reads 'Facts:' and 'Sources:' with nothing after either, so a claim over every link would refuse the FY2026-27 services-and-supplies window the site draws today.

DO NOT answer this by adding a key check back to site/app.js. That is the shape tools/jscheck/contract.mjs's boundary arm refuses by name.
notes:
MEASURED, by tools/jscheck/lifecycle.mjs's "a malformed year document never
leaves the words and the chart on different years", over five fixtures at the
commit that deleted drawableSankey. Three of the five are refused with the page
untouched. Two are NOT:

  - a schedule carrying no `sources`
  - a locator carrying a doc_id and no `pages`

citations() guards both -- it returns [] rather than throwing -- so the chart
draws, the words and the chart agree, and every citation is silently absent. The
reader is told nothing.

WHY IT IS P2 AND NOT P1. schema/column.schema.json requires `sources` on every
schedule and `pages` on every locator, and encodeColumn refuses to write bytes
that fail it, so no file `fisc export` produces can be in this state. The only
routes are a hand-edited file served at the column path, or a cached copy from
before those keys existed -- and the second is caught first by the generated_by
comparison in loadColumn. tools/jscheck/contract.mjs holds the schema to those
requirements in both directions.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, and it is not restoring the gate: a chart whose
ribbons cite nothing is a chart this project should not draw, whatever wrote the
file. The honest form is a positive claim -- "every drawn link reached at least
one citation" -- asserted after the table is built, which is a statement about
the DRAWING rather than a re-reading of the document's keys, and so does not
reopen the second-spelling defect that deletion closed.

DO NOT answer this by adding a key check back to site/app.js. That is the shape
tools/jscheck/contract.mjs's boundary arm refuses by name.

title: The structure lattice's wire document is built, tested, and read by nothing
description:

title: Dependency decision: github.com/google/jsonschema-go for machine-checkable artifact contracts
description:
DECISION: add github.com/google/jsonschema-go as this tree's fourth direct
dependency, alongside cobra, go-cmp and go.yaml.in/yaml/v3.

AGENTS.md's "Go" section requires a decision bead in the same change for any
dependency outside that set. This is it.

WHAT IT IS FOR. The artifacts crossing this project's language boundaries --
Python writes data/extracted/*/manifest.json and Go reads it; Go writes the
published documents and the browser reads them -- are specified today in prose
under docs/ plus Go struct tags plus hand-written key checks in site/app.js.
That is three spellings of one shape and none of them is machine-checkable
against the data. A committed JSON Schema is.

WHY THIS LIBRARY, measured rather than assumed:
  - ITS ENTIRE go.mod IS `require github.com/google/go-cmp`, which this tree
    already depends on and AGENTS.md's testing section names. `go get` adds ONE
    module and nothing else: go-cmp is test-only for it.
  - Draft 2020-12 AND draft-07, per its own package documentation.
  - Pure Go, so CGO_ENABLED=0 holds.
  - Same vendor as an already-blessed dependency.

THE ALTERNATIVES, and why each loses on this tree's own terms:
  - santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 is the most complete Go implementation and
    adds golang.org/x/text.
  - kaptinlin/jsonschema pulls 7 direct and 11 indirect modules into a module
    with three.
  - xeipuuv/gojsonschema is draft-07 only, unmaintained since 2019, and depends
    on testify, which AGENTS.md's testing section rejects by name.
  - Hand-rolling a subset validator was the first plan and was rejected: it is
    the second implementation of a standard thing, which is the argument
    tools/jscheck already makes about not writing a selector engine.

ACCEPTED COST: it is v0.4.3, pre-1.0, so its API may move. The surface used here
is Schema.Resolve and Resolved.Validate, which is what makes that acceptable
rather than a reason to take the heavier option.

VERIFIED BEFORE ADOPTING, against the committed corpus: a hand-written fact
schema resolved and validated all 2,382 records of facts/facts.jsonl, refused a
record missing doc_id by naming every missing key, and refused an id breaking its
pattern by naming the pattern. It also caught the schema's own author being
wrong -- `fund` was guessed as string-or-null and is *int, which 1,518 records
proved on the first run. That is the mechanism paying for itself before it
landed.
close_reason: Decision taken and shipped. github.com/google/jsonschema-go v0.4.3 is a direct dependency in go.mod; its only transitive requirement is go-cmp, already blessed by AGENTS.md's testing section. Four artifacts are held to committed schemas by it: the fact record, the extraction manifest, the published column (encodeColumn) and, at 58c83b3, the rung answer (encodeRungs). The case it was opened to settle is settled in the direction it proposed -- each of those refuses at the WRITE, which is what let site/app.js's twelve hand-written key checks be deleted rather than kept in step.

title: The document shape is spelled three times: Go structs, the client's hand-written key checks, and the contract docs
description:
DO: decide whether the artifacts crossing the Go/JS boundary get a committed JSON
Schema that BOTH sides validate against, replacing the hand-written checks on
each side.

THE PROBLEM IS NOT A MISSING CHECK, IT IS THREE SPELLINGS OF ONE SHAPE.
  - Go writes the files from structs with json tags (clientConfig, yearView,
    stepView in internal/export/page.go; rungsDoc in pkg/cmd/export/rungs.go).
  - site/app.js re-states the same shape imperatively: isDocument, understands,
    drawableSankey, readableRungs, answeredRung -- "refuses over every key the
    draw dereferences", key by key, by hand.
  - docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md states it a third time in prose, and
    only its schema_version line is held to Go.

WHY CONSTANTS-EITHER-SIDE IS THE WRONG ANSWER, which is what fisc-okjb and
fisc-4jq0 currently propose. A literal matched across a language boundary is not
a contract, it is two copies plus a test asserting they are spelled the same. It
holds only what someone remembered to pin, it cannot say anything about the data
actually emitted, and the test is a grep over source text.

WHAT A SCHEMA WOULD ACTUALLY HOLD, and this is the case for it:
  - Required keys and types, once, for both sides.
  - Enums: link kind (external, internal_transfer, internal_service,
    fund_balance), mark role (residual, gap, aggregate).
  - ID PATTERNS, which is the interesting one: "^residual/" and "^gap/" in the
    schema is the prefix living in ONE place both sides read, which retires
    fisc-4jq0 properly rather than pinning two literals to each other.
  - And it validates the EMITTED ARTIFACT, so `fisc verify` could hold the
    served files rather than the structs that wrote them -- which is fisc-4lsx's
    open question from the other direction.

WHAT IT WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT, said so the case is not overstated: the legend
defect fixed at 2456ef3. That the client must know every fund group the document
contains is a completeness property between code and data, not a shape a schema
can express.

THE TWO COSTS, both real and both against stated rules:
  (1) A JSON Schema validator in Go is a new direct dependency. AGENTS.md's "Go"
      section names cobra, go-cmp and yaml and says anything else needs its own
      decision bead in the same change. So that decision is part of this one.
  (2) There is no npm here and there must not be, so the JS side is hand-rolled.
      A subset validator -- types, required, enum, pattern -- is perhaps 150
      lines of stdlib JS. That is still ONE generic implementation replacing N
      per-document key checks, which is the trade to weigh rather than a reason
      to stop.

A CHEAPER VERSION EXISTS AND MAY BE THE WHOLE ANSWER: generate the schema FROM
the Go structs at build time, commit it, and have tools/jscheck validate the
committed fixtures and the served artifacts against it. Then Go needs no
validator at all -- its structs are the source -- and only the client-side
subset validator is written.
close_reason:
Answered by deleting the client's spelling rather than by reconciling three. The shape of every artifact crossing Go -> browser now lives once, in schema/: column.schema.json and (new at 58c83b3) rungs.schema.json, each validated against the EMITTED BYTES by encodeColumn and encodeRungs before they are written. site/app.js's twelve hand-written key checks -- drawableSankey's eight and readableRungs' four -- are gone, with understands and the two version gates. docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md's fenced shape block, the third spelling this bead names, is gone too; the prose keeps the argument a schema cannot state.

The two costs the bead weighed both resolved in the direction it hoped: Go needed a validator and got one (fisc-9ao4), and the JS side needed none -- tools/jscheck/contract.mjs compares the schema's required arrays against app.js's source, which is what makes the deletion safe rather than argued, plus a boundary scan refusing a per-key refusal reappearing.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD PROPOSED THAT DID NOT HAPPEN, said so the close is not overstated. The id patterns (^residual/, ^gap/) are not in the schema, so fisc-4jq0 is NOT retired and stays open. And the bead's cheaper version -- generate the schema from the Go structs -- was not taken: the schemas are hand-written and held to the structs by name in both directions instead.

title: The chart opens on the earliest published year, where a reader expects the newest
description:
DO: make index.html open on the most recently published budget year, declared by
Go rather than inferred from list position by the client.

WHY IT OPENS ON THE OLD ONE TODAY. project.PublishedFiscalYears returns
[]int{2026, 2027} ascending; yearStems (pkg/cmd/export/data.go) walks that order,
so View.YearStems is ["sankey", "sankey-2027"] and CONFIG.years[0] is FY 2025-26.
site/index.html.tmpl hard-codes `checked` on years[0], and checkedYear
(site/app.js) falls back to years[0]. Every one of those is position-based.

WHY NOT SIMPLY REVERSE SOMETHING. Three tempting one-liners, each wrong:
  - Reversing PublishedFiscalYears reorders the published DOCUMENT set, which is
    far more than this page's toggle.
  - Reversing YearStems flips the control's left-to-right order too, and a year
    toggle that reads newest-then-oldest is a different decision that nobody has
    taken.
  - Checking the LAST radio in the template makes "most recent" mean "last in
    the list", which is an inference about ordering spelled in a template --
    the construct paintBreadcrumb's comment refuses elsewhere in this client.

SO THE VIEW DECLARES IT. A field naming the stem the page opens on, shipped on
FISC_CONFIG beside `years`, with the template checking that radio and
checkedYear falling back to it rather than to years[0]. The ascending order
stays, which keeps the control reading oldest-to-newest.

WHAT MUST KEEP WORKING, and it is the reason checkedYear is not simply replaced:
its whole purpose is that Chrome and Firefox RESTORE a reader's radio selection
across a soft reload and a Back navigation, with no change event fired. Opening
on the restored year rather than forcing the default is what stops the page
showing one year's chart under another year's toggle. The declared default is
the fallback when nothing is checked, not an override of a restore.

SHIPS WITH ITS jscheck ARM and a Go test in the same commit: that the packager
stamps the newest published year, and that a page whose radio was restored to
the other year still opens on the restored one.
notes:
THE BLOCKER, measured at 833c07e, and it is why this is not a template one-liner.

View.Projection IS THE OPENING YEAR'S STEM, enforced. export.go's validate
refuses a view whose first year stem is not its Projection --

    if i == 0 && stem != v.Projection {
        return fmt.Errorf("view %q opens on %q but its first year stem is %q", ...)

-- and YearStems' own field doc states the contract the same way: "in the order
a reader should meet them, opening year first". So "open on 2027" reads as
"Projection = sankey-2027", not as "check a different radio".

AND PrimaryProjection IS DOING DOUBLE DUTY, which is what makes that expensive.
The constant is both the spine document AND the base year's stem key: data.go
calls stepStems(export.PrimaryProjection, ...) and then picks each step's
default projection with years[export.PrimaryProjection], in five places
(data.go:781, :967, :1048, :1112, :1186). Repointing the view's Projection
without untangling that gives the steps the wrong year's default document.

buildSankeyPage ALSO SOURCES THE RENDERED PAGE FROM v.Projection:
decodeSankey(v.Projection) supplies meta, tilesFor(meta) supplies Hero and
Figures, and DataPath, Scope and Caveats all come off the same document. Those
are what a reader with JavaScript off sees.

TWO WAYS THROUGH, and the choice is a visible one rather than a technical
detail:

  (a) ORDER YearStems NEWEST FIRST and repoint Projection with it. Follows the
      contract as written and needs no new field. Costs: the step defaults above
      have to stop keying on PrimaryProjection, and the toggle then reads
      newest-then-oldest left to right, which is a reader-facing change nobody
      has taken.

  (b) ADD AN OPENS DECLARATION that is presentation only. YearStems stays
      ascending, Projection stays sankey, step keying is untouched, and the
      toggle keeps reading oldest-to-newest. buildSankeyPage picks the opening
      yearView by stem and sources Hero, Figures, ChartTitle, Label, Basis,
      DataPath, Scope and Caveats from it rather than from v.Projection's meta;
      validate's i == 0 rule relaxes to "YearStems contains Projection". The
      risk to design against is the exact defect checkedYear exists to prevent:
      one year's tiles under another year's chart.

WHATEVER LANDS, checkedYear MUST KEEP WINNING OVER THE DECLARED DEFAULT.
Chrome and Firefox restore the radio across a soft reload and a Back navigation
with no change event, so the declared year is the fallback when nothing is
checked, never an override of a restore.

THE CHECK SUITE ASSUMES THE CURRENT ANSWER IN PLACES: "FY 2025-26" appears in 20
arms across year.mjs, lifecycle.mjs, fold.mjs, drill.mjs, layout.mjs and
harness.mjs, and drill.mjs's COLUMNS[0] is stem "sankey". Most drive
twoYearConfig() rather than the shipped config, so the blast radius is smaller
than the count suggests -- but it is not zero and wants measuring before the
edit rather than after.
close_reason: View.Opens splits the order from the opening year; validate now requires only membership. buildSankeyPage renders the opening year's tiles, title and caveats so the static page agrees with the checked radio, and checkedYear falls back to CONFIG.opens while a restored radio still wins. Mutation (1) -- opensOn returning the oldest -- was green until pkg/cmd/export gained the assertion that the spine opens on the newest.

title: WIDE_COLUMNS is hardcoded to 4 in the client, where CONFIG.steps already says what the widest chart is
description:
DO: derive the column ceiling from the declared steps instead of spelling it in
the client, and let the floor stay a design choice if it must.

site/app.js:981 declares `const WIDE_COLUMNS = 4` and stepColumns clamps to it.
Measured against the served config, that is exactly max(len(step.tiers)) over
CONFIG.steps -- the `fund` step's [2,3,4,5]. Every other step declares three or
fewer:

  fund-group       [0,2,3]    keep=[0]  widen=[]
  fund             [2,3,4,5]  keep=[2]  widen=[5]
  division         [3,4,5]    keep=[3]  widen=[]
  revenue-category [1,0,2]    keep=[2]  widen=[]
  object-category  [2,5,4]    keep=[2]  widen=[]
  transfers        [2,3]      keep=[]   widen=[]
  fund-departments [2,3,4]    keep=[2]  widen=[]

  render_tiers (the overview) [0,2,5] -- 3 columns
  distinct tiers across the whole tree: 0,1,2,3,4,5 -- six levels

So the constant is RIGHT TODAY and is a second spelling of a fact the packager
already ships. AGENTS.md's "Go vets, JavaScript renders" names that shape
exactly: a second spelling of one Go already makes is the defect the boundary
exists to name. The client is deciding what the widest possible chart is by
holding a number, when the answer is in the steps it was handed.

WHAT GOES WRONG WHEN IT DRIFTS, and it drifts SILENTLY IN THE DAMAGING
DIRECTION. A step declaring five tiers ships, the packager validates it, Go's
own tests pass -- and the client clamps the budget at 4, so the fifth column can
never be asked for and the step draws short with no refusal and no banner. The
reader sees a chart missing a column that the document declares. Nothing in the
tree goes red: no jscheck arm reads WIDE_COLUMNS against the steps, and
tools/jscheck's own COLUMNS pins are written at 3 and 4.

THE FIX IS A DERIVATION, NOT A NEW WIRE FIELD: the ceiling is
max(len(s.tiers)) over the steps the client already reads, floored at
NARROW_COLUMNS so a config with no steps still has a range. That keeps the
declaration Go's and the arithmetic trivial.

NARROW_COLUMNS = 3 IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION and should not be swept in. It is the
narrowest chart that still reads, which is a judgement about legibility rather
than a fact about the documents, and render_tiers happening to be 3 columns does
not make it derivable.

SHIPS WITH ITS jscheck ARM in the same commit, per AGENTS.md's node boundary.
The arm to write: the ceiling the client clamps to equals the widest tier set
the config declares. The mutation: add a five-tier step to a fixture config and
watch the arm go red where the constant would have drawn four columns quietly.
close_reason: No derivation of a ceiling was needed in the end. WIDE_COLUMNS keeps its stylesheet meaning -- chartWidth(4), which layout.mjs pins -- and its comment now claims only that; the 'widest step' half it also carried is gone, because the steppers now ask the steps directly. Mutation: removing the one declared Widen makes the control go quiet and reddens the arm.

title: markContra composes a claim about the documents in the client, and contraNote a derived difference
description:
FOUND while auditing the Go/JS boundary, 2026-09-20. Both are in site/app.js and neither is covered by the licence the boundary actually grants the client.

WHAT THE LICENCE SAYS, because this finding is only as strong as it: the client may add PUBLISHED SUMMANDS whose membership is Go's -- that is the merged ribbon's cents, and it is allowed because every summand is a figure link-values-tie-to-facts already witnesses and the membership is the packager's. It explicitly DOES NOT reach a derived mark: a residual's cents is a difference and a gap's is a shortfall, neither is a sum over published summands, and both stayed Go's for that reason (fisc-lwh5).

(1) markContra, site/app.js:3105, COMPOSES A SENTENCE ABOUT WHAT THE CITY PRINTED. It walks the UNFOLDED file's parent chain and builds
  "printed as a reduction of " + up.label
That is a claim about a published schedule, written in the client, from a parent lookup rather than from anything the wire says. Go already knows about contra rows -- internal/export/page.go and internal/project/sankey.go publish Partition -- and ships nothing that says "this ribbon is a reduction of X".

(2) contraNote, site/app.js:3177, COMPUTES A DIFFERENCE AND SHOWS IT.
  reduced = sum of the contra ribbons on the heavier side
  shown   = d.value - 2 * reduced
and it renders under the site's own "our reading" diamond. A net-of-reductions figure is a DIFFERENCE, not a sum over summands, so it falls on the Go side of the line the residual and the gap are already on.

WHAT IS NOT BEING CLAIMED. Reading the SIGN off value_cents is fair -- the sign is published. Drawing the ribbon at its magnitude is a rendering decision. It is the WORDS and the NET FIGURE that are the other language's.

WHY IT IS A TASK AND NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: the question is what the wire should carry -- a `contra` string per link the way the projection already carries `partition`, or a net figure per node, or both -- and that is a contract change in internal/export with a jscheck arm on the far side. PARTITION_NOTE (site/app.js:3203) is the shape to copy for spelling a claim once -- though it too is a claim about the documents spelled in the client, the same class as fisc-mx5o's labels.

NOT INVISIBLE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: fisc-zqa3 is the reader-facing consequence of the same drawing decision -- the centre's gross figure is called 'printed by the city' -- and whichever wire shape answers this bead has to answer that one, since the net figure contraNote computes here is the figure the city printed.

Filed 2026-09-20 from the implementation audit; see the sibling bead filed the same day (fisc-mx5o).
notes: Filed 2026-09-20 from the implementation audit; see the sibling bead filed the same day.

title: The artifact test guards a rung's parent and not its children, so a whole step's rungs can vanish
description:
MEASURED on e13-sankey-merge at e577338, mutation 14 of
docs/rung-walk-witness-evidence.md. Suppressing the append in rungWalker.walk
for one step leaves out every rung that step opens: the artifact goes from 99
and 97 rungs to 45 and 45 on the two columns, testdata/rungs.json regenerates,
and make pre-commit, the export tests and the node suite are all green.

WHY NOTHING SEES IT. TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes runs its parentage
guard CHILD TO PARENT -- a rung's opened node must be counted or carried by the
rung above it -- and there is no parent-to-child arm. So a column may list ids
that no rung ever answers for, and the ids the walk opened and then discarded
leave no trace.

Today tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's completeness arm covers it from the other side:
a rung Go answers that the walk never reached, and a rung the walk reached that
Go does not answer, are both red there. That arm is what fisc-phtp.2 retires,
so this is a guard the Go side has to grow before the walk moves, not after.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: for every id a rung counts or carries at a tier some step
declares as its From, with the role that step declares, there is a rung whose
path is this rung's path plus that id -- unless the step's document does not
decompose it, which is export.Openable's answer and is the part to get right.
The invariant reads the artifact and the step declarations and nothing else, so
it says nothing about any figure and is not a second reading of ReachOf.

MUTATION IT MUST SURVIVE: suppress the append for one step in rungWalker.walk,
regenerate testdata/rungs.json, and the guard goes red naming the ids the
artifact opens no rung for -- with tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs blinded, so the
result is not that arm catching it again.
close_reason: Landed in TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes as the mirror of the parentage guard: for every id a rung draws at a tier a later step declares as its From, with the role that step declares and where export.Openable says that step's document decomposes it, there is a rung whose path is this rung's path plus that id. MUTATION, by the method the bead asked for: the append in rungWalker.walk suppressed for the fund-departments step, testdata/rungs.json regenerated from the mutated walk (99 and 97 rungs to 45 and 45), guard red with 106 findings -- 'sankey fund-group/capital: draws "fund/510" at tier 3, which step "fund-departments" opens, and this column answers no rung of that step below it'. Blinding the answeredBelow counter takes it red on its own vacuity arm. IT ASKS export.Openable, WHICH THE WALK ASKS TOO, so it is completeness read from the parent rather than a second reading of the documents, and the comment says so. A later step opening a kept column is refused rather than read, because the role it would be matched on lives on the chart on screen; no shipped step does that.

title: An id behind a folded tail is observable only by the arm the walk's move will retire
description:
tools/jscheck/chart.mjs:38 states it: an id Go accounts for is checked as either a mark on the chart or behind the tail of its own column, so removing one from BEHIND a tail leaves that file silent. Measured while landing the client fold: deleting such an id is caught twice by tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs and not at all by chart.mjs.

WHY THAT IS A PREREQUISITE AND NOT A NIT. rungs.mjs catches it today only because the client still derives its own membership and is compared against Go's answer. fisc-phtp.2's remaining work moves that derivation to Go -- the client reads draws[].ids instead of walking the hierarchy -- and on the day it does, that arm compares the artifact against itself and goes vacuous. chart.mjs is what is supposed to carry the weight afterwards (fisc-xsc8), and behind a tail it cannot.

SO THE ORDER IS: close this, then move the walk. Inverting it opens a blind spot over every id a fold hides, which on the committed corpus is most of what the caps exist to hide.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the rendering arm has to be able to ask a tail what it stands for. The client knows -- capColumn builds the tail's folds list and its label counts the members -- so this is an observability problem in the checker, not a missing figure. Expanding the tail and re-reading the DOM is one route; reading the tail's own folds off the drawn datum is another. Measure which the harness can actually reach before committing to one.

MUTATION IT MUST SURVIVE: delete an id that sits behind a tail on a driven rung, and the rendering arm goes red naming it -- with rungs.mjs blinded, so the result is not rungs.mjs catching it again.
close_reason:
tools/jscheck/chart.mjs grows arm (f): it presses Enter on a drawn tail the way a reader does, re-reads the DOM, and holds the column the page draws out to Go's answer -- every id accounted for at that column reaches a mark, no mark Go accounts for nowhere is drawn beside them, and the tail drew as many marks as the words in it promised (the count is read off the tspans, not off the label capColumn composed).

ROUTE TAKEN: the gesture, not the datum. Measured first: dispatching keydown Enter on the tail mark runs keyNode -> expandTier -> redrawStack and the chart redraws with the column whole, so the harness reaches the real gesture; the tail's own folds list was not read anywhere. Reading folds off __data__ would have been reading the client's intention, which is the distinction this module exists to make.

MUTATION, RUN BOTH WAYS. Deleting fund/580 from the sankey column's fund-group/capital rung in testdata/rungs.json -- an id behind the tier-3 tail on a driven rung -- WITH rungs.mjs BLINDED (its checks() returning []) takes exactly one check red: 'FY 2025-26: a folded tail expands into the ids Go accounts for and no others -- the tail at column 3 drew fund/580, which Go accounts for nowhere at this rung', at both 3 and 4 columns. Nothing else in the suite saw it, which is the silence this bead measured. Unblinded the same mutation takes three: rungs.mjs twice, arm (f) once. fisc-xsc8's own mutation re-run unchanged: render() drawing graph.nodes.slice(1) still takes four checks red naming fund-balance/draw laid and never drawn and the ribbons left hanging off it. Blinding marksIn() takes all six arms red on their own counters, (f) at 0 tails expanded and 0 marks revealed.

COUNTERS: seen.expansions and seen.revealed, both required non-zero by the arm's ok. 3 tails / 42 marks on FY 2025-26, 5 / 84 on FY 2026-27.

Gates: make pre-commit exit 0; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped. Only tools/jscheck/chart.mjs moved -- testdata/rungs.json, site/app.js, facts/, mappings/ and data/ byte-identical. make js 31.5s -> 32.4s.

Left open: fisc-2wsw, the tail this arm cannot expand because a kept flank's fold is not this rung's cap.

title: site/app.js fetches and vets the rung answer and dereferences nothing in it
description:
main() fetches RUNGS_PATH, loadRungs parses and indexes it by (stem, path), and readableRungs refuses a file missing columns[].rungs[].draws[].tier or .ids -- and no function in site/app.js reads a draws entry. The fold is the client's fitting step (fisc-lwh5), so capColumn ranks the column it filtered and asks the answer nothing.

THE CONSEQUENCE TO WEIGH, because it is on the deploy path today: main() does `if (!rungAnswers) return;`, so a missing or malformed rungs.json leaves the reader a page that drew nothing -- gated on an artifact the page does not read. It fails closed on a condition with no bearing on what it renders.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a decision rather than a deletion: readableRungs's rule is 'every key the page DEREFERENCES, and no more', which the draws arm no longer satisfies. Either fisc-phtp.2's membership stage lands and the arm is right again, or the arm shrinks to what loadRungs indexes and the fail-closed guard over draws goes with it. Do not simply make the failure non-fatal: that trades one wrong state for a quieter one, and the stage that spends this answer needs it fail-closed again.
notes:
WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRITTEN DOWN, found while writing the contract's rung-answer section (fisc-b5dn): main()'s comment above the fetch in site/app.js says 'Which nodes a column holds is Go's answer now, so a page that cannot read it can draw no rung'. No function reads a draws entry, so the second clause is true only because the fetch is a hard gate and the first is not true at all. Whichever way this is decided, that comment moves with it.
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-20 against the tree, and the comment this bead quotes has moved. Verified: 'rungAnswers' is assigned at main()'s fetch and READ NOWHERE (the only other mentions in site/app.js are its 'let' and rungKey's doc), and the only '.draws' dereferences in the file are inside readableRungs' own schema gate. So the bead's premise holds in the stronger form -- the page does not read a rung, not merely not a draws entry.

WHAT CHANGED, and what did not: the comment above the fetch no longer claims 'Which nodes a column holds is Go's answer now, so a page that cannot read it can draw no rung' (that was fisc-4942's commit). It now says the answer is fetched and vetted and no function in the file dereferences a rung of it, that filterLinks and capColumn derive the membership, that it is a gate rather than an input, and that this bead is where what it gates on is decided. The fetch, loadRungs, readableRungs and 'if (!rungAnswers) return;' are untouched, so the decision recorded here is still entirely open.
close_reason: Closed by the membership stage of fisc-phtp.2: site/app.js now dereferences the rung answer on every drill. shapeFor looks the path up (answeredRung), heldFor reads draws[].tier, .ids and .carried into the id-to-column map each half of a window is filtered by, and the early return in main() gates on a file the page cannot draw a rung without. readableRungs' rule -- every key the page DEREFERENCES, and no more -- holds again without shrinking the arm, and the comment above the fetch says the input it now is. The decision this bead asked for is therefore the first of its two options, taken rather than deferred.

title: docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md names the rung answer nowhere, so a client change can contradict it with nothing going red
description:
grep for 'rungs.json', 'rung answer' or 'RungsPath' across docs/*.md returns zero hits. The contract states the fold rule -- 'So the client folds', and the caps table -- and says nothing about the artifact that carries Go's half of it.

WHY THAT COST SOMETHING, measured rather than supposed: the client was changed to fold to ids Go pre-computed, which contradicts that contract's own rule, and no doc went red because no doc mentioned the artifact. git blame dates the inversion to cd02623 and its Go-side supporting sentences to 99db5a8, c70abaf and 83693a1 -- two days, in the client, while internal/export/export.go's DrillStep.Caps and DrillStep.Widen doc comments went on correctly describing both as declarations the client spends.

WHAT TO DO: give the contract a section for the rung answer -- what it carries, what it does not, and which side spends each declaration -- so that a future change to either side has a document to contradict. AGENTS.md's 'Where writing goes' puts a frozen output contract in docs/ until its package exists; the rung answer's emitter is pkg/cmd/export, so decide whether this belongs in the contract doc or in that package's doc comment, and put it in exactly one.

Neighbour: fisc-lwh5, the ruling this would have caught the drift from.
close_reason: docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md gains a 'Go's half: the rung answer' section -- what the artifact carries, what it deliberately does not and why each absence is a decision, and which side spends caps and widen -- and pkg/cmd/export's TestTheContractStatesWhatTheRungAnswerCarries holds its shape block to the emitted structs' JSON names and to rungsSchemaVersion. The contract doc was chosen over pkg/cmd/export's package comment because the reader who needs the seam stated is the one editing site/app.js or tools/jscheck, the field-by-field spelling is already in rungs.go's type comments, and the caps table and 'So the client folds' are in this file.

title: rungs.mjs's completeness arm cannot see fisc-qics: both sides walk the unexpanded space and agree about a set neither covers
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.2's MEMBERSHIP STAGE (cd02623). tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's check 'Go answers every rung the walk reaches, and no other' is completeness both ways and reads as the arm that would catch a rung Go does not answer. It cannot catch fisc-qics.

WHY. The 'walk' the arm performs is the drill walk over the UNEXPANDED chart -- the same space rungsOf enumerates. So the arm compares Go's coverage against a traversal that never expands a folded column either. Both sides are silent about the same 466 hidden marks, and silence on both sides reads as agreement.

THIS IS THE 'GREEN BECAUSE THE GATE FIRED' SHAPE at the level of a corpus rather than a fixture, which is the variant AGENTS.md's 'Prove it can fail' is hardest to apply to: the check is not vacuous, it compares real sets, it just cannot reach the states where the defect lives. A count of 76 rungs visited against 76 answered is true and tells a reader nothing about the expand-then-open space.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT is not obviously an extension of this arm: a walk that expands would need Go to answer expanded rungs first, which is fisc-qics. Until then the honest move is for the arm's detail line to say WHICH space it is complete over, so the number is not read as coverage of everything a reader can reach.
close_reason: The arm walks the expand-then-open space now that Go answers it: 99 and 97 rungs visited against 99 and 97 answered, pinned per column as expandedViews, and the detail line names the space rather than leaving a number to be read as coverage of everything a reader can reach.

title: classList is a no-op in domStub, so the dimming that IS the isolation is still unobservable
description:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING fisc-xsc8's rendering arm (4d9db66). domStub's node().classList has add, remove and toggle as empty functions. applyEmphasis() expresses the isolation through .classed('dim', ...) and .classed('hot', ...), so the visual effect of isolating a node -- which is the whole of what the gesture DOES for a sighted reader -- writes nothing the stub can read.

WHAT THE RENDERING ARM DOES INSTEAD, so the gap is not hidden: its gesture arm reads app.isolated and the legend's aria-pressed. Those witness that the page RECORDED the isolation and announced it; neither witnesses that any ribbon dimmed.

WHY IT NEEDS DESIGN RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE FIX. Making classList real changes the class attribute that the rendering arm's (c) compares against nodeClass(d): today class is written once by .attr('class', nodeClass(d)) and is stable, and afterwards it would carry dim/hot too, so (c)'s comparison has to say which part of the class is the mark's own rule and which is the emphasis of the moment.

Neighbour: fisc-6at, nothing here renders CSS -- so even with classList real, this witnesses a declared class and never a painted pixel.
close_reason: Closed at 810e72e, and the fix was a DELETION rather than an implementation: d3 reads node.classList || new ClassList(node), and its own fallback adds and removes through getAttribute/setAttribute, which the stub node already answers. The three empty functions satisfied that || and shadowed the working path. New arms say the isolation dims -- at least one ribbon and one other mark, never the isolated node's own flows or the node itself, and nothing left dimmed after release -- measured at 367 and 419 marks and ribbons over the two published years. Arm (c)'s class equality is split: every token nodeClass composes is present, and anything else is dim or hot. Five mutations, all red, including the no-op classList put back (20 findings) and a predicate that dims everything (10, on the invariant half alone).

title: domStub's node has no contains(), so focusInChart() answers false for a mark inside #chart
description:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING fisc-xsc8's rendering arm (4d9db66). focusInChart() asks `chart.contains(activeElement)`. The stub's node() defines no contains, so the call is not a function and the realistic state -- a reader who tabbed to a drawn g.node and pressed Enter -- reads as "focus is not in the chart".

WHY IT IS FAIL-OPEN RATHER THAN A GAP. The existing focus arms reach focusInChart only by setting activeElement to #chart ITSELF, which is not a state a reader can be in: a reader's focus is on a mark, and a mark is a descendant. So the branch those arms drive is the one no one uses, and the branch everyone uses is answered false by the stub rather than by the page.

THE THIRD DISJUNCT IS DEAD FOR THE SAME REASON. focusInChart has three: `active === chart`, `chart.contains(active)`, and `active.closest(".breadcrumb")`. The stub has no closest either, so TWO of the three are "not a function" and only the first can ever answer true.

IT IS NOT MORE THAN A ONE-LINE STUB CHANGE PLUS THE ARM THAT WAS MISSING, measured 2026-09-22: every arm that sets focus sets it to getElementById("chart") -- lifecycle.mjs:704, drill.mjs:1585, 3314, 3455, 4741 -- and NONE sets a descendant, so adding contains changes no existing arm's behaviour and make js is green on the stub change alone. There is no re-reading of the existing focus assertions to do.

WHAT IS OWED IS THE ARM: put focus on a real drawn g.node, open it, and read back where restoreFocus put it, since a drill destroys the element focus was on.

Neighbour: the rendering arm now puts focus on a real g.node after Escape, which is the state this makes askable.
close_reason: Closed at 30eff4f. contains AND closest both added -- this bead named only the second disjunct and the third was dead for the same reason. THE COST ESTIMATE IN THE DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED THERE: no existing arm sets activeElement to a descendant, so adding contains changes none of their behaviour and make js is green on the stub change alone. What was owed was the arm, which puts focus on a real drawn g.node and reads back where restoreFocus put it after the drill destroyed it: 6 drills per published year. Three mutations red at 6 findings each, including taking contains off the STUB with the page left whole, which is the one that says the stub was the blindfold.

title: The evidence-doc contract becomes a gate, in both directions
acceptance_criteria: A declared evidenceDocs map is checked in both directions and wired into make pre-commit: each declared file exists, opens with the evidence marker, names a section of AGENTS.md that resolves, and is linked from AGENTS.md exactly once; and a marker file that nothing declares is a failure. Mutations, one per direction: delete a declared doc's marker and it goes red; add a marker file with no declaration and it goes red. Landing fisc-08ee does NOT close this -- that bead is about source paths in prose, this one about the evidence docs' own contract.

title: A fourth prose gate: refuse a comment or doc that cites a source path the tree does not have
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-18, after an audit of what reaches an agent UNASKED. make beadrefs refuses a fisc-* id naming no bead and make doccheck refuses a citation naming no section of AGENTS.md. NOTHING refuses a citation of a FILE that does not exist, and that is the gap four of this session's five prose defects fell through.

WHAT A SWEEP FOUND, at HEAD before the fix: 29 repo-shaped paths named in a tracked comment or doc that the tree does not have. Five were real and are fixed (806231f); the other 24 are build output (dist/data/sankey.json cited as data/sankey.json), package-relative testdata, or -- in four cases -- a deliberate reference to a file that was never created, which internal/check/check.go's comments say outright.

SO THE RULE HAS TO BE NARROWER THAN 'every path resolves', and the false-positive classes are what make it writable:
  REFUSE  a path under internal/, pkg/, cmd/ or tools/ ending .go or .mjs that
          names no tracked file. Zero false positives in the sweep; it would have
          caught all four of the aef3d8f-deleted-file citations, two of which were
          in testdata/README.md, which AGENTS.md tells agents to read first.
  IGNORE  data/, dist/, facts/, site/*.html -- build output and served artifacts
          whose repo-relative spelling is not their path.
  IGNORE  a bare testdata/... path, which is package-relative by Go convention.

AND AGENTS.md ALREADY PREFERS THE FIX OVER THE GATE: 'a comment names a symbol; it does not say where the symbol lives'. So a hit is usually repaired by dropping the path, not by correcting it -- which is what 806231f did, and which makes the gate's population shrink rather than grow. Model it on tools/beadrefs, which is already the shape and already walks tracked files.

THE MEMORIES CANNOT BE GATED THIS WAY and the same audit found seven stale ones, so say why in the tool rather than leaving it to be rediscovered: memories live in the Dolt DB and in no git artifact, which is the reason AGENTS.md gives for make narration's memory arm warning and continuing rather than failing. The right home for a memory-path audit is that existing arm, on the same warn-and-continue terms.

WHY P2 AND NOT P3: the two testdata/README.md hits pointed a reader at internal/check/drillreconcile.go and internal/check/departmentwide.go for the argument behind two committed fixtures. A reader who cannot find the file cannot check the fixture's reason, which is the one thing that page exists to give them.

The 105 byob beads are in THIS graph -- they are rows of .beads/issues.jsonl like any other -- so bd show resolves them and beadrefs could check them without asserting anything about their lifecycle. 'Never claim or close' is a rule about what an agent may DO to a bead, not about whether a citation of one should resolve.
