title: A published caveat can name a check that does not exist, and the golden that pins the caveat is what makes it durable
description:
MEASURED on e13-sankey-merge. Two shipped caveats named checks deleted at aef3d8f: sankey.json's transfer-legs-unpaired cited projection-scopes-are-disjoint and department-funding.json's two-of-the-four-columns cited funding-sources-tie-to-spine. Both shipped for 20-odd commits with fisc verify 44 passed, every golden byte-identical and make pre-commit exit 0.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the part worth keeping. The goldens pin the caveat TEXT byte for byte, so they redden the moment the text changes -- they caught the FIX. What they cannot do is notice that the text refers to something that stopped existing: the string and its golden drifted into agreement about a check that is not there. Nothing in the tree compares a check id named in published prose against check.All(). This is the 'green because the gate fired' shape from AGENTS.md's 'Prove it can fail', one level up: the fixture is in perfect agreement and guarantees nothing about the referent.

WHAT A GUARD LOOKS LIKE, and why it is not a one-liner. The naive rule -- every hyphenated token in a caveat must be a live check id -- false-positives on the caveats' own ids, which are the same shape: thirteen of the fifteen check-id-shaped tokens in the committed goldens are caveat ids (working-capital-is-a-stock, one-figure-is-two-ribbons, the-ribbons-are-a-cross-tab and so on), not references. A sound rule has to distinguish a REFERENCE from an ID. Two candidates:
  (a) A hyphenated token in the same sentence as the word 'check' must be a live check id. Both real instances satisfy this ('the citywide check this project runs over these rows (X)' and 'the X check holds'); no caveat id does today. Cheap, and it fails closed on the phrasing that actually occurs.
  (b) Caveats reference a check through a constructor that validates the id. Sound rather than heuristic, but internal/check imports internal/project (subject.go builds projections), so internal/project cannot import internal/check to validate -- the constructor would have to live in check or export and the caveat text be assembled there, which is a bigger change than the defect warrants.

(a) is the recommendation, as a Go test over the built documents rather than a registered check -- adding a check is five edits and this guards prose rather than money.

ALSO IN SCOPE, measured: site/app.js is served verbatim and carries three references to deleted checks in comments (drill-reconciles-across-documents, projection-scopes-are-disjoint, spending-window-reconciles). site/chart.html.tmpl carries a fourth in an HTML comment. Those are fisc-5aw0's sweep, but a guard of shape (a) would catch the app.js ones too if it read the shipped file.

Found while trimming beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: structure.IsAntichain is dead AND states a different rule from the one NewView enforces
description:
TWO SPELLINGS OF THE ANTICHAIN TEST, AND THE DEAD ONE IS WRONG. Measured at d2a2136 with golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode over ./... including tests: internal/structure/lattice.go:166 IsAntichain is unreachable -- nothing calls it, not even a test. Alongside it internal/structure/lattice.go:155 LevelsComparable and internal/structure/containment.go:237 Comparable are unreachable too; those three are the ONLY functions in the tree dead to both the binary and the tests.

THIS IS NOT MERELY DEAD WEIGHT. The live refusal is an inline loop in NewView, internal/structure/identity.go:243-257, and it applies a STRICTER PRECONDITION than the dead helper:

  NewView      refuses only when kindsMeet(a, b) -- the two cuts describe
               overlapping money -- and then one level refines the other.
  IsAntichain  refuses on level refinement ALONE, with no kinds test.

So they disagree on a case fisc-w11l calls out by name: pp.127-140 beside pp.167-170 is NOT refused, because one prints revenue and the other expenditure. IsAntichain would refuse it. The dead helper is the wrong rule.

WHY IT IS A TRAP RATHER THAN A TIDY-UP. IsAntichain carries the authoritative-sounding doc comment -- 'whether no level in the set refines another, which is the condition for their cells to be summable without double counting' -- and even documents the repeated-level case. A future refactor that notices NewView's hand-rolled loop and 'reuses the helper' would narrow the view discipline and refuse valid views, with the comment reading as though that were correct. That is the second-source failure AGENTS.md's 'Where writing goes' names, in its most dangerous direction: the dead copy is the one that looks canonical.

FIX, EITHER DIRECTION, BUT NOT NEITHER: delete IsAntichain and its two dead siblings, OR make NewView call it after the kindsMeet filter so there is one spelling. Deleting is the smaller change and loses nothing, since the kinds precondition is not expressible in a level-only helper.

THE MUTATION: give NewView the spine beside pp.127-140 (refused today, 'is not an antichain: revenue-detail (fund-by-category) decomposes spine (fund-group-by-category) and both print [revenue transfer_in]') and the spine beside pp.167-170 (allowed today). A helper-shaped rewrite reddens the second. Both are live in internal/structure's tests already.

Found while auditing dead code under AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders'.
close_reason:
DELETED, the direction the bead preferred. IsAntichain, LevelsComparable and Comparable are gone; NewView's inline loop is now the only spelling of the antichain test, and the kinds precondition it applies is not expressible in a level-only helper.

WHAT THE DELETION ALONE DOES NOT DO is stop the trap coming back, since nothing pinned the case the two spellings disagreed on -- identity_test.go asserted only refusals. TestTheAntichainIsOverMoneyBothCutsPrintAndNotOverLevelsAlone now pins the admission: revenue-detail (fund-by-category, revenue+transfer_in) beside general-fund-departments (fund-by-department-by-category, expenditure) is admitted, and the view admits facts from both scopes so the assertion is not green over an empty view. It opens by asserting the levels are still comparable and the kinds still do not meet, because if either stopped holding the admission would be green from the pair having become uninteresting rather than from NewView testing kinds, and the two are indistinguishable by exit code.

THE MUTATION: dropped 'if !kindsMeet(a, b) { continue }' from NewView (identity.go:245-247), which is exactly the level-only rule IsAntichain stated. The new test goes RED -- 'view "drill" is not an antichain: "general-fund-departments" (fund-by-department-by-category) decomposes "revenue-detail" (fund-by-category) and both print []' -- and note the empty kind list in that message, which is the tell that the rule being applied has nothing to do with money. Restored, green.

MEASURED after the deletion: deadcode -test ./... reports no findings; golangci-lint run reports 0 issues. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, 0 errored; all ten testdata/*.golden.json byte-identical.

title: A lens is a flow restriction: upstream/downstream of an anchor, drawn but never totalled
description:
THE FOURTH STRUCTURE DECISION, and the first about the FLOW graph rather than the containment one. fisc-0qyo makes grain explicit; fisc-n6yq decides tree-or-DAG; fisc-w11l decides what a view is as a cut of GRAIN. This decides what it means to restrict a view by where money GOES.

THE OWNER'S INTENT, 2026-09-18: see the whole city budget, drill into specific sub-funds, and visually see how money moves -- with a restriction that includes only the nodes upstream or downstream of an anchor such as the General Fund.

TWO GRAPHS, AND THIS IS THE OTHER ONE. fisc-w11l's cut is an antichain of the CONTAINMENT lattice plus a subtree: how finely money is decomposed. A lens follows RIBBONS. Conflating them is how a total over a non-antichain gets computed, which is the failure fisc-l25 named and NewView now refuses.

NOTHING IN THE TREE DOES THIS TODAY, measured at b394b44: site/app.js's filterLinks keeps a link whose near end is inside withinNode(doc, id) -- the node's PARENT-CHAIN subtree -- which is one hop of flow out of a hierarchy subtree, not a closure. internal/export/reach.go's ReachOf is the same rule in Go. A grep for a transitive flow walk over internal/, pkg/, site/ and tools/ returns none.

THREE DECISIONS TAKEN BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-18.

(1) A LENS RESTRICTS WHAT IS DRAWN AND NEVER WHAT IS SUMMED. The headline stays a named cut over an antichain; a lens publishes no total. So no figure the city never printed acquires a headline, fisc-l25's doubling stays structurally impossible rather than merely avoided, and a lens needs no provenance of its own because it introduces no number -- it selects among figures that already carry theirs.

(2) A WALK STOPS AT A TRANSFER EDGE. Transfers make the flow graph cyclic: the General Fund pays Capital and Capital can pay back, so an unrestricted downstream closure loops and can swallow most of the city. 'Downstream of the General Fund' ends where the money leaves that fund's own story, and the transfer is drawn as an endpoint -- which is how the spine already draws transfers/in and transfers/out. It terminates by construction rather than by a depth limit a reader cannot account for.

(3) GO PRECOMPUTES CLOSURES FOR DECLARED ANCHORS. Not for every node, and not in the client. AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders' puts the reachable set on the Go side, where a check can fail on it; a declared anchor set is the part that can also be held to the documents. The client renders a set it does not walk.

SIZE IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, measured over the committed goldens at b394b44 and WITHOUT decision (2)'s stop rule, so these are upper bounds:
  sankey       25 nodes / 58 links   -- every node, both directions:    264 ids, largest closure 17
  fund-flows  238 nodes / 412 links  -- every node, both directions: 12,556 ids, largest closure 89
Even the exhaustive version is small. Decision (3) is therefore about what can be CHECKED, not about payload.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES: the anchor declaration's syntax and where it lives; whether an anchor is a node id or a cut; what the lens is called on the wire; the check that fails when a closure disagrees with the links it was built from; and the mutation that proves it can fail.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR fisc-phtp. The shaping moves to Go whether or not lenses exist; a lens is a new thing Go emits, not a precondition for emitting the rest.

title: Extend the rung equivalence arm past capped tiers: uncapped columns, derived marks, and the transfers step
description:
tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs holds site/app.js to testdata/rungs.json on every rung at 3 and 4 columns, but only for the TIERS A STEP CAPS: how many document nodes the column draws and how many its tail hides. Three things it declares out of scope by name and should not stay so:

1. UNCAPPED COLUMNS. Go's rungsOf already computes the candidate set at every outward tier; the artifact carries counts only for capped ones. Shipping the count (or the ids) for every drawn tier and comparing them is the cheap half.

2. DERIVED MARKS. The client's residual, gap and carried endpoints are excluded from the comparison because Go does not compute them. check.ResidualNodes and the spending-gap declaration are the Go side of two of them; the arm could read the artifact's derived expectations from those rather than from app.js. Until then a derived mark competing with a cap turns the arm red by design (rungs.go's doc comment).

3. THE TRANSFERS STEP keeps no flank, so rungsOf has no window direction to walk and skips it by name (the artifact's `skipped` list). It is the one rung per column the arm does not answer.

The mutation for each: perturb the corresponding figure in testdata/rungs.json and name the rung and width.
notes:
2026-09-19 ITEM 2 LANDED at 668599b (gap) and 5f2a825 (residual) on e13-sankey-merge, schema_version 4 of testdata/rungs.json. Go computes both of the client's own marks -- existence, tier and cents -- and tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs compares them by id both ways with a counter per mark. Measured off the regenerated artifact: 12 rungs answer a residual (fund-group/general, capital and internal-service, at 3 and 4 columns, in both published years) and 2 answer a gap (expenditure/services-and-supplies at 3 and 4 columns, FY2026-27 only; FY2025-26 ties to the cent). Every mark stands at a tier its rung draws, and no mark survives onto a later rung's flank; both are asserted as pinned zeroes in TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes.

THREE THINGS THIS BEAD'S TEXT OR ITS PLAN HAD WRONG, measured while landing it. (1) The body's item 3 names 'the artifact's skipped list'; there has been no such field since c70abaf and testdata/README.md's rungs.json row no longer says so. (2) Dropping the object-category step's Gaps map is NOT a mutation that provokes the undeclared-gap refusal: a step declaring no gap makes no balance claim and rungsOf builds with the difference unstated, which is markGap's own first rule. The refusal is proven by a declaration naming another node, TestRungsRefuseADriftTheStepDoesNotDeclare. (3) The fallback to the document one depth up (carryResidual's above(), threaded as walk's from) is never taken on the committed corpus: every residual's out is 0 because no {0,2,3} window decomposes its group, and every inflow endpoint sits on the kept flank at tier 0. The unit row in internal/export/marks_test.go is its only witness.

The marks' prose (rationale, source note) is not ported; drill.mjs pins it. site/app.js is untouched; deleting its copy is fisc-phtp, which this unblocks.
close_reason: All three items landed on e13-sankey-merge: uncapped columns (schema 2), the transfers step (c70abaf), and the derived marks -- carried endpoints at schema 3, the residual and gap marks at schema 4 in 668599b and 5f2a825. Measured off the regenerated artifact: 12 rungs answer a residual at both budgets in both years, 2 answer a gap at both budgets in FY2026-27; rungs.mjs compares every one both ways.

title: Ship the structure as an index plus per-view, per-column slices (fisc-kbuo's answer), replacing the single structure.json
description:
fisc-kbuo was answered at 6d2060f by measurement: candidate (b). What ships today is candidate (a)'s single dist/structure.json (868,612 raw / 68,658 gz), because measuring needed the whole built. Nothing in site/app.js reads it.

NOT TO BE DONE. This bead exists only to implement fisc-kbuo candidate (b), and the owner decided (a) on 2026-09-18 against the gzipped measurement: the whole structure is 68,658 bytes gzipped, where ONE drill costs 19,111 today (data/fund-flows.json, to draw 39 nodes and 37 links). Closed rather than deferred: the work is not smaller-later, it is work against the decision. If (a) is ever reversed, the measurements to re-read are in fisc-kbuo's notes, not here.

title: Comments, docs, mapping notes and app.js name checks L3.4 deleted: one sweep, each hit read rather than replaced
description:
Filed from L3.4, which deleted nine checks (projection-scopes-are-disjoint, facts-are-projected, expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine, revenue-detail-ties-to-spine, transfers-detail-ties-to-spine, funding-sources-tie-to-spine, departmentwide-ties-to-spine, drill-reconciles-across-documents, spending-window-reconciles) and the declarations unprojectedScopes, disjointScopes, reconciledScopes, fundingSourcesExceptions, departmentwideExceptions and toCIP.

Prose naming them survives in files that commit did not otherwise edit, and each is now a claim about a symbol that no longer exists. Deliberately NOT swept in the deletion commit: AGENTS.md's rule is to drop such text in the file already being edited and never in a sweep, and the same check id states different propositions in different files, so each hit has to be read and either re-pointed at cuts-tie-along-the-lattice / peers-overlap-only-by-declared-identity / structure.BudgetBookExceptions or deleted.

RE-MEASURE with:
  grep -rnE 'projection-scopes-are-disjoint|facts-are-projected|detail-ties-to-spine|tie-to-spine|drill-reconciles-across-documents|spending-window-reconciles|unprojectedScopes|disjointScopes|reconciledScopes|fundingSourcesExceptions|departmentwideExceptions|toCIP' --include=*.go --include=*.md --include=*.mjs --include=*.js --include=*.yaml .

At the deletion commit that grep hits internal/check (rowfunds.go, rowfunds_test.go, rulefunds.go, vocabulary.go, facts.go, vacuity.go, vacuity_test.go, report.go, statedtotals.go, trends.go, trends_test.go, fundbalance_test.go, transfersscope_test.go), internal/project (fundflows.go, fundflows_test.go, departmentspending.go, departmentspending_test.go, departmentfunding.go, departmentfunding_test.go, project.go, series.go, history_test.go, trends_test.go, transfersbyfund.go, sankey.go, sankey_test.go), internal/mapping (revenuedetail_test.go, departmentdetail_test.go, acfr_p0041_test.go), internal/structure/structure_test.go, internal/export/export.go, pkg/cmd/export (data.go, export_test.go, linetier_test.go), pkg/cmd/verify/report.go, site/app.js, mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml, data/taxonomy.yaml, testdata/README.md and docs/ (general-fund-drilldown-contract.md, sankey-contract.md, revenue-trends-contract.md, acfr-history-contract.md).
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18, and THIS BEAD'S OWN RE-MEASURE COMMAND IS BLIND TO THE HIGHEST-STAKES HITS. Its grep passes --include for *.go, *.md, *.mjs, *.js and *.yaml and NOT *.json, so it could not see the two deleted check ids that were shipped to readers in published caveats: projection-scopes-are-disjoint in sankey.json's transfer-legs-unpaired and funding-sources-tie-to-spine in department-funding.json's two-of-the-four-columns, each in two year-variants, four goldens in all.

The guard that should have caught it is fisc-1p08.

ADD *.json AND *.tmpl TO THE GREP. site/chart.html.tmpl carries a fourth reference in an HTML comment and the bead's include list misses it too.

WHAT IS LEFT, measured at HEAD with the corrected grep: 97 hits across about 30 files, the largest being mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml (8), internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go (6), pkg/cmd/export/data.go (5) and docs/sankey-contract.md (5). site/app.js has 3 and is served verbatim, so those are shipped bytes rather than source comments even though a reader has to view source to meet them.

AND THE GREP OVER-MATCHES, which the next person should know before they start reading: toCIP's 8 .go hits are all internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go's LOCAL VARIABLE of that name, live and unrelated to the deleted declaration. Two more classes to expect: unprojectedScopes has 25 occurrences and staleDeclarations 9, every one of them a COMMENT about a symbol deleted at aef3d8f -- those are real sweep work, and they are why fisc-a8dm and fisc-6u2d closed as obsolete rather than as done.

NINE BEADS CLOSED AGAINST aef3d8f in this session (fisc-hxbb, fisc-4vnu, fisc-91go, fisc-wmq3, fisc-6gp2, fisc-o1fv, fisc-d0ro, fisc-6u2d, fisc-a8dm), all of them describing a check that no longer exists. fisc-a5ii stays open: it is the one proposition facts-are-projected carried that Covered did not replace.
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-22 at 74dddf2 with the corrected grep (json and tmpl
included, dist/ excluded): 92 hits, down from 97 and not by sweeping -- the drop
is site/chart.html.tmpl being deleted and the doccheck fixture being re-pointed.
Largest are mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml 8, transfers_p76_test.go 6
(still the live local variable, still not sweep work), pkg/cmd/export/data.go 5,
docs/sankey-contract.md 5, internal/project/project.go 4.

AND THE CLASS HAS NOW COST A READER-FACING CLAIM, which this bead's P3 was set
before. README.md said "`fisc verify` declares each undrawn schedule with the
reason it is undrawn, and retires the declaration by itself the moment a
projection starts drawing one". No check it runs does that: the sentence
described unprojectedScopes, which is named in seven comments and declared

exist, for as long as the name survived in prose. Corrected at 74dddf2 by saying
what is true instead -- measured by differencing the store's scopes against every
published document's, which leaves acfr-general-fund-summary as the only one no
projection draws.

THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR A GATE RATHER THAN A SWEEP, and it is the shape
`make beadrefs` and `make doccheck` already have: a dead check id or a dead
`pkg.Identifier` is a pointer at nothing wearing different clothes, and the only
reason those two are gates is that somebody wrote the arm. A tool that resolves a
check id against check.All() needs no bd, no Dolt, no node and no network, which
is the standing both existing gates have.
SWEPT 2026-09-22 AND CLOSED. 92 hits before, 8 after, and the 8 are not work:
6 are internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go's live local variable named toCIP,
which this bead's own grep over-matches, and 2 were site/app.js's, fixed in
their own commit because they ship to readers verbatim. 84 hits read, in 44
files.

THREE CLASSES, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, which is why this could not
have been a replace.
  RE-POINTABLE: the four <kind>-detail-ties-to-spine checks and
  departmentwide-ties-to-spine are cuts-tie-along-the-lattice's comparisons;
  projection-scopes-are-disjoint is peers-overlap-only-by-declared-identity;
  toCIP, fundingSourcesExceptions and departmentwideExceptions are entries of
  structure.BudgetBookExceptions; staleDeclarations over unprojectedScopes is
  staleDocumentDeclarations over uncheckedDocuments.
  ARGUMENT RESTING ON A DELETED MECHANISM: five comments justified publishing
  all four printed columns by "unprojectedScopes' declaration retires only when
  the schedule is drawn EXHAUSTIVELY". Renaming that would have kept a false
  argument under a true name; the surviving reason is stated instead.
  A CLAIM ABOUT WHAT A CHECK PROVES, which had to be checked before being
  re-pointed. internal/export/export.go credited spending-window-reconciles with
  holding a difference to a declared FIGURE; the comment three sentences above
  it says the amount is not declared, and what takes that difference is GapOf,
  at export time, off the drawn graph.

NO GATE SHIPPED WITH THE SWEEP, and the reason is measured rather than assumed:
fisc-k3yh carries the three measurements that kill the two obvious designs and
the union-resolver design that could work. What DID ship is the narrower gate
the sweep's own reading turned up -- tools/doccheck now refuses a cited Go test
name that no _test.go declares, which found ten dead pointers, five of them
naming a test that pins a contract and does not exist.
close_reason: Swept at 6fa7967, 0cf899c and caf6214. 92 hits before, 8 after, and neither of the surviving classes is work: 6 are transfers_p76_test.go's live local toCIP, which this bead's grep over-matches and its own notes warn about, and the app.js pair went in its own commit because those bytes are served to readers. 84 read, in 44 files, each re-pointed, restated or deleted according to which of the three classes it was; the notes carry the classification. codehash over all 39 edited .go files says 38 are comments-only and one moved, pkg/cmd/export/data.go, whose two unviewedDocuments reason strings were the only code involved. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify zero failures; make pre-commit exit 0. No gate shipped with it and that is a measured decision, not an omission -- fisc-k3yh.

title: The lattice edge fund-by-department-by-category -> fund-by-department holds by axes and not by the documents: the department axis is two tiers
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 in Lane 3 L3.1 by probing structure.Contain over every refining pair of the six Budget Book cuts at 96fda0d, not only the two structure_test.go pinned.

MEASURED: general-fund-departments (pp.167-170, expenditure-by-department) -> funding-sources (pp.171-176, department-funding-sources) is a refining pair by the declared lattice (LevelFundByDepartmentByCategory refines LevelFundByDepartment), meets at fund-by-department, and reports 104 of 116 cells disagreeing over four columns. The money is the same; the KEY is not. pp.167-170 populate the department axis with 23 DIVISION slugs (city-clerk, fire-administration, engineering...) and pp.171-176 with 11 DEPARTMENT slugs (city-manager, fire-department, community-development). data/departments.yaml says so in its header -- 'TWO TIERS, AND THE FACTS NAME THE LOWER ONE' -- and pp.85-125's upper block (departmentwide-expenditures) carries 29 division slugs.

So one Axis (department) is populated at two grains by rule, and the lattice has no level distinguishing them. This is the same shape fisc-0qyo found for fund vs fund_group, one axis over.

WHAT L3.1 DID: fail closed, cheaply. Cut gained DepartmentTier ('division' | 'department'), required by ValidateCuts on any cut whose level carries the axis, and restrict() refuses a pair compared at a level with the department axis whose tiers differ. The pair is therefore refused by name rather than compared, and the containment check's committed-corpus test pins the refusal text. Mutation (standing, exception_test.go): declare both tiers equal and the comparison runs and reports 100+ findings.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS: whether the department axis should be TWO axes (division, department) in the lattice, with fund-by-division-by-category refining fund-by-department-by-category via data/departments.yaml's division->department link -- which would make pp.167-170 comparable to pp.171-176 through a fold this package does not do today -- or whether the tier declaration on the cut is the right permanent answer and the lattice edge should be documented as holding only between cuts at one tier. Either way, the refinements table's claim that FxDxC decomposes FxD is currently exercised by no comparable pair in the corpus.

title: parseStepShapes refuses an unreadable Keep or Widen but is blind to any new DrillStep field
description:
FAIL-OPEN, and the one most likely to bite the structure work.

tools/jscheck/harness.mjs parses pkg/cmd/export/data.go's DrillStep literals as
TEXT -- slicing by tab indentation (/^\t{3}\{/gm), which data.go:1093-1098 says
in words ("ONE GUARD AND NOT TWO NESTED ONES, so the literal below sits at the
indent every other step literal here sits at").

IT HAS READ-OR-REFUSE GUARDS FOR EXACTLY TWO OPTIONAL FIELDS
(harness.mjs:1218-1223):
    if (/Keep:/.test(body) && !keep) throw ...
    if (/Widen:/.test(body) && !widen) throw ...
Each was clearly added after someone hit it. NEITHER GENERALISES. A NEW
DrillStep field is not matched, not guarded and not reported: every drill.mjs
check keeps measuring a step shape missing the new declaration, and stays GREEN.
That is a declaration the site draws from and no check can see -- the exact
condition the Keep guard's own comment calls "worse than either".

SO: any lane adding a DrillStep field adds its own read-or-refuse arm in the
same commit. Better, make it structural -- enumerate the fields present in the
body and refuse one this parser does not know, so the default for a new field is
refusal rather than silence.

RELATED, same file, same class: parseSpineRenderTiers (harness.mjs:1117-1122)
requires `RenderTiers: []int{...}` with digits and commas only, at exactly two
tabs inside `spine := export.View{`. `[]int{tierRevenueSource, ...}` or
`spineTiers()` throws. That one throws BY NAME, which is the safe direction --
it is a blocker to sequence, not a defect.

MUTATION: add a field to one DrillStep literal in data.go, e.g. `Grain: []int{2}`.
Today: make js stays green and drill.mjs measures a shape without it. With the
fix: refused by name, naming the field and the step.
notes:
2026-09-17, L4.2: the premise holds and this lane adds no DrillStep field, so parseStepShapes is no blinder than before. tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs is NOT a fourth reader of data.go: it reads testdata/rungs.json, computed by pkg/cmd/export's rungsOf from the built documents and pinned by TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes, so the client is held to what Go computed rather than to a regex over the file that generated its config. It does still drive app.js with PAGE.steps parsed here, so the blindness this bead names is the one thing between the artifact and the wire.
RE-DERIVED AT HEAD 2026-09-18 AND THE BEAD UNDERSTATES ITSELF. It is written as a hazard for a lane that ADDS a DrillStep field. Measured, nine existing fields are already in exactly the state it describes.

export.DrillStep declares seventeen fields: Key, After, From, Side, Role, Projection, YearProjections, Tiers, Keep, Widen, Caps, Back, Tail, Noun, Description, Residual, Gaps.

tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's parseStepShapes matches EIGHT of them -- After, From, Keep, Key, Role, Side, Tiers, Widen -- and the guard coverage over those eight is three tiers, not one:
  UNCONDITIONAL REFUSE   From, Tiers, Key, After
  READ-OR-REFUSE         Keep, Widen  (the two the bead names)
  READ, NO GUARD         Side, Role -- matched into a local and never checked, so
                         a declaration the regex cannot read becomes null in
                         silence. Side's pattern special-cases the literal
                         export.SideSource by name, so a SECOND Side constant
                         parses as null and refuses nothing.
  NOT READ AT ALL        Projection, YearProjections, Caps, Back, Tail, Noun,
                         Description, Residual, Gaps -- nine.

SO THE CONDITION THE Keep GUARD'S COMMENT CALLS 'worse than either' IS THE TREE'S CURRENT STATE for more than half of DrillStep, not a risk a future lane introduces.

AND IT MEETS fisc-kops ON ONE FIELD. That bead is DrillStep.Residual reaching the wire by a json tag nothing checks; Residual is also among the nine parseStepShapes never reads. So the residual declaration is invisible to the harness AND to the round-trip test, from two directions, which is why neither side caught it.

THIS RAISES THE STAKES FOR fisc-phtp rather than lowering them: that lane moves shaping into Go, which means more declaration and more fields, and the structural fix this bead asks for -- enumerate the fields present and refuse an unknown one -- should land before it rather than after.
close_reason:
Answered structurally, which is what the bead's own note asks for rather than a third read-or-refuse arm.

parseStepShapes now enumerates the fields present in each data.go literal and refuses one it has not been taught about, by name. The set is DECLARED in harness.mjs as KNOWN_STEP_FIELDS and deliberately NOT read off export.DrillStep -- a set derived from the struct grows the moment the field is added there, so the very change this catches would teach it to accept one. The struct is the other half of a pair and tools/jscheck/contract.mjs compares them, so a field added to the struct and to no literal reddens there.

AND THERE IS NOW A THIRD PARTY the bead could not have named: schema/page.schema.json, validated by encodeConfig against the bytes window.FISC_CONFIG is rendered from, with additionalProperties: false on the step object.

MUTATION, the one the bead states: Grain []int added to export.DrillStep and Grain: []int{2} to one literal.
  - make js: refused by name at the parse -- 'step 0 in data.go declares Grain, which this parse has not been taught about'.
  - fisc export: refused by name -- 'does not match page.schema.json ... unexpected additional properties ["grain"]'.
  - go test: two struct-to-schema parity tests red.
Before this lane all three were green and drill.mjs went on measuring a step shape without the field.

The bead's RELATED note about parseSpineRenderTiers is unchanged and was correct: it throws by name already, which is the safe direction.

title: chartAllowance reads the first rule whose selector ends in .chart-wrap, and reads only one
description:
FAIL-OPEN in the check that guards the chart's width. Found while tracing the column control; line refs re-measured 2026-09-23.

tools/jscheck/layout.mjs:381 is `/\.chart-wrap\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(css)` -- first match wins, and the capture then reads that block's body as if it were the real declaration. Two ways it returns a WRONG ANSWER rather than refusing:

(1) ANY EARLIER SELECTOR ENDING IN .chart-wrap MATCHES. `.card:fullscreen .chart-wrap {` contains `.chart-wrap {` as a substring. Today style.css:643 is the first {-bearing occurrence -- style.css:626, :811 and :1172 are prose inside comments, not followed by { -- so the function is correct by luck of source ordering, not by construction. fisc-dphn's fullscreen rule is exactly the change that would break it, and it would break it SILENTLY.

(2) IT READS ONE RULE. Moving --chart-room under a @media block leaves the base rule matched and the override invisible, so queryRoom compares COLUMN_QUERIES against a cap that does not apply at that width.

The function's own doc comment already says 'nothing here parses CSS' and claims 'the direction it fails in is the safe one' -- which is true of the clamp() case it was written about and NOT true of either case above.

FIX: anchor the match at a rule boundary (start of text, `}`, or `*/`) so a descendant selector cannot win, and refuse when MORE THAN ONE .chart-wrap rule declares --chart-room rather than silently taking the first.

MUTATION: add a `.card:fullscreen .chart-wrap { --chart-room: min(400px, 100vw) }` rule ABOVE style.css:643 and confirm the allowance arm reports 400 today; with the fix it must refuse by name.

title: layout.test.mjs dereferences a regex match unguarded, and throws out of a hook instead of refusing by name
description:
FAIL-OPEN by a wrong answer, and a loss of coverage bounded to one suite.

tools/jscheck/layout.test.mjs, in the four-column window's before() hook:

    const at = Number(/\(min-width:\s*(\d+)px\)/.exec(q.query)[1]);

`[1]` is dereferenced with no null check, over every entry of COLUMN_QUERIES
(site/app.js). Any entry that is not a min-width-in-px query -- a max-width, a
range `(400px <= width)`, an orientation or a resolution query -- throws a
TypeError.

WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED 2026-09-23 by adding
`{ query: "(orientation: landscape)", columns: NARROW_COLUMNS }` to
COLUMN_QUERIES and running `node --test tools/jscheck/layout.test.mjs`: the
throw lands in one suite's before() hook, so that suite's 7 tests are cancelled
AND NAMED, the other 20 claims run and pass, and the run exits 1. `make js`
exits 2. So the gate goes red, the lost claims are identifiable, and nothing is
silently skipped.

THE ENTRY CHOSEN FOR THAT PROBE MATTERS: an entry declaring a column count
above the floor also breaks drillDown, which fails a further nine claims for a
different reason and makes the measurement read worse than it is.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG is the refusal itself rather than its blast radius. A
harness should refuse a question it was never asked BY NAME rather than
throwing out of a hook: harness.mjs's matchMedia stub models the same query
grammar and throws by name for anything else, and its comment says why -- a
stub that answers a question it was never asked "does not fail, it stops
testing". The parse here should be a named failing test carrying the query it
could not read, so the reason is in the report rather than in a stack.

WHY IT MATTERS: adding a client condition is a three-file change (app.js's
COLUMN_QUERIES, harness.mjs's matchMedia stub, this parse), and this is the one
of the three that fails for the least informative reason.

MUTATION for the fix: the probe above. Today the four-column suite's hook
throws and its 7 tests cancel; with the fix one named test goes red carrying
the query, and the other six still report.

title: The focus ring on a chart node encloses its gutter label, not the mark the reader clicked
description:
Found by clicking the shipped site: "a weird white outline when you click on
something".

THE ONLY WHITE OUTLINE IN THE TREE is the unscoped global rule at
site/style.css:279-282 -- `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink-1);
outline-offset: 2px }`. --ink-1 is #0b0b0b in light and #ffffff in dark, declared
twice (style.css:84 under prefers-color-scheme: dark, style.css:114 under
[data-theme="dark"]). So in dark mode it is a 2px white ring. There is no
outline:none anywhere and no other :focus outline; the remaining :focus rules
(style.css:916, 1028, 1053, 1098) are colour and border only.

WHY IT LOOKS WRONG. render() makes the NODE GROUP focusable, not the rect:
app.js:4193-4194 sets tabindex and role="button" on the <g>, and the <g> then
gets a rect (app.js:4275) AND its label text (app.js:4289), which labelPlacement
anchors up to LABEL_GUTTER = 250px away (app.js:479). An SVG outline follows the
union bounding box, so the ring encloses mark + label + value + flag glyphs -- a
wide box floating out into the gutter, nothing like the 14px-wide mark that was
clicked. svg.sankey { overflow: visible } (style.css:645) lets it paint outside
the SVG box too.

THE FIX for nodes: turn the box outline off and draw the indicator on the
geometry --
    svg.sankey .node:focus-visible { outline: none; }
    svg.sankey .node:focus-visible rect { stroke: var(--ink-1); stroke-width: 2; }
placed AFTER svg.sankey .node.derived rect (style.css:734-738), which is equal
specificity (0,2,1) so source order decides, and which sets its own
stroke-dasharray that must be reset.

RIBBONS ARE THE WEAKER HALF and are deliberately not fixed the same way. A
<path> can carry only one stroke and its stroke IS the data (linkColor via
paint(), app.js:4331; .contra overrides it at style.css:700), and the dash
patterns already carry meaning (.derived 5 4, .partition 1 4). So a focus
indicator cannot reuse stroke or dash without colliding with a published
distinction. A ribbon's bbox is at least roughly the ribbon, so outline-offset:0
is the proposed interim. If that still reads wrong, it needs its own bead and
probably a drawn focus echo path -- not a second guess here.

ALSO ABSENT: no -webkit-tap-highlight-color rule anywhere, so touch gets the UA
default highlight on every focusable mark.

NOT VERIFIED FROM HERE: which browser-and-mode combination raises :focus-visible
on a pointer click for a tabindex'd SVG group. The union-bbox defect above holds
however focus arrives, including via restoreFocus (app.js:2108-2139), which moves
focus programmatically after every drill.
close_reason: The node turns the global box outline off and draws a 2px --ink-1 stroke on its rect; the ribbon keeps the box and loses the 2px offset, since its stroke and dashes are both published distinctions. Ordering against .node.derived rect and the dasharray reset are pinned by TestTheChartsFocusRingIsDeclaredOnTheMarkAndAfterTheDerivedRule, both mutation-proven. Declared only -- whether it paints right is a browser question (fisc-6at).

title: The column control reports the budget where the reader reads a count of drawn columns
description:
FALSE-CLAIM, reader-facing. Found by clicking the shipped site.

syncColumns (site/app.js:5062-5073) writes `columnBudget + " columns"` into
#column-count, which is also the control's aria-live region. columnBudget is what
the chart MAY draw; drawnColumns() (app.js:1482) is what it DOES draw. They
differ in both directions:

  ON THE OVERVIEW the chart is drawn at RENDER_TIERS whatever the budget --
  activeTiers (app.js:1457) returns it unconditionally when drilled is empty --
  so pressing + updates the label to "4 columns", disables +, and changes no
  column. applyColumns' own comment (app.js:5086-5089) documents the no-redraw
  as deliberate but not the label divergence.

  ON A RUNG DECLARING NO WIDENING the step is "returned whole at any budget"
  (activeTiers' comment, app.js:1448), so the control can read "4 columns" over
  a three-column chart.

HOW OFTEN: of the seven steps pkg/cmd/export/data.go declares, exactly ONE
(`fund`, data.go:780) declares a Widen. Every other view plus the overview is a
state where the control moves a number and nothing else. That is what a reader
reports as "the column count +/- didn't seem to do anything".

THE FIX IS A LOOKUP ONCE THE CLIENT WALKS A STRUCTURE (fisc-w11l): #column-count
reports drawnColumns(), and each stepper disables when no other cut exists at
this position -- the same "disabled at the bounds is how the floor is
discoverable" doctrine the control already uses, extended to "disabled because
this chart has no other width". Until then it is still a lie worth its own bead.

Note setColumnBudget (app.js:997) clamps only the lower bound; all three callers
pre-clamp, so it is an unguarded invariant rather than a live defect.
close_reason: The count reports drawnColumns() and each stepper disables when the chart has no other width at that position, derived by asking activeTiers at budget+1 and budget-1. syncColumns joined redrawStack's repaint list so a drill repaints it. drill.mjs drives the button's own listener over the overview, a step without a widen, and fund/100.

title: What the client walks: the whole structure, or an index plus lazily-fetched cuts
description:
Once a view is a cut (fisc-w11l), the client stops shaping and starts walking.
This decides what crosses the wire.

MEASURED AT 8aa9116, and the numbers argue against the intuition that one
structure is bigger:

  dist/data/  19 documents      2,149,657 bytes raw    166,007 gzipped
  facts/facts.jsonl  2382 facts 1,211,036 bytes raw     75,388 gzipped

THE WHOLE FACT STORE GZIPS TO LESS THAN HALF OF WHAT THE SITE ALREADY SHIPS.
The 19 documents are larger than the facts they are built from because they
redundantly re-publish overlapping cuts: fund-flows.json alone is 276,657 bytes
and there are four year-variants of it (1,133,636 bytes for one document's four
columns). A structure carrying every node and edge ONCE, with provenance, is
bounded near the store's own size.

WHAT THE READER PAYS TODAY. Opening a fund group fetches fund-flows.json at
276,657 bytes to draw 39 nodes and 37 links (the figures pinned at
pkg/cmd/export/data.go:611-613).

THE TWO CANDIDATES.
  (a) Ship the structure. One fetch, then every drill is a walk with no further
      network. Costs the whole payload up front on a page whose headline view
      needs one cut.
  (b) Ship a lattice index plus lazily-fetched cuts. The index says which cuts
      exist and what each opens into; a cut is fetched when opened. Costs a
      round trip per drill, and needs the index to be small.

DO NOT DECIDE THIS FROM THE ESTIMATES ABOVE. The gzipped-store figure is an
upper bound on (a)'s payload only if the structure adds no bytes per node beyond
what a fact carries, which it will not -- edges, parents and locator sets are
not free. Build the structure first (it is Lane 1, publishing nothing) and
measure it.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded answer to: (a) which of the two candidates, with a MEASURED byte
figure for the structure as built rather than the bound above; (b) gzipped and
raw, since the site is served static; (c) what a reader pays for the headline
view and for the first drill, compared with the 276,657 bytes they pay today;
(d) whether provenance (fact_ids + locators) ships with the structure or is
fetched on pin.
notes:
2026-09-17, L4.1 (6d2060f): BUILT AND MEASURED, off go test -v -run TestTheStructureShipsOnTheAssetChannelAndIsMeasured ./pkg/cmd/export (Go's gzip DefaultCompression; best-compression in brackets). structure.Build carries every fact any summing document's view admits ONCE with id, locator and token, one view per projection naming its facts by index, and the cut/identity/lattice declarations.

  today: data/fund-flows.json     raw 276,611  gz 19,111 (18,573)   [276,669 from ./bin/fisc export; the bead's 276,657 moves with metadata.generated_by's version string]
  today: data/sankey.json         raw  36,379  gz  3,991
  (a) whole structure, 2048 facts raw 868,612  gz 68,658 (64,361); without provenance raw 645,408 gz 30,937
  (b) sankey slice, 240 facts     raw  97,283  gz  8,163 ( 7,773); without provenance raw  71,511 gz  3,972
  (b) fund-flows slice, 1120      raw 467,334  gz 37,090 (34,867); without provenance raw 345,145 gz 16,766
  (b) fund-flows slice, FY2026 adopted column only: 280 facts raw 117,208 gz 11,804 (Python-encoded, a few bytes off Go's)
  (b) sankey slice, FY2026 adopted column only:     120 facts raw  48,968 gz  4,583 (same)

ANSWERS. (a)/(b): (b), an index plus lazily fetched slices, sliced per view AND per column. The whole structure costs the headline page 68,658 gz before its first pixel -- 17x today's sankey.json and 3x today's headline-plus-first-drill (23,102 gz) -- while a per-column headline slice is 4,583 gz against 3,991 today, and a per-column fund-flows slice is 11,804 gz against 19,111. The intuition the bead warned against was right to be warned against: the structure is NOT bounded near the store's gzipped size (75,388) when sliced whole, and it only wins per cut.
(c) headline: 4,583 gz per-column slice (8,163 all columns) vs 3,991 today; first drill: 11,804 gz per-column (37,090 all four columns) vs 19,111 today.
(d) provenance SHIPS WITH THE SLICE, id included. Dropping the id alone saves 30% of the gzipped whole (70,676 to 49,882, Python-encoded), but the id cannot go: the store's 2,382 facts share 2,338 distinct (doc_id, page, offset); the 44 collisions are p76's transfer rows each read once as transfer_in and once as transfer_out, so a locator does not name a fact. Fetching provenance on pin would need the id to find the record, and the token is the field fact-offset-points-at-token verifies against; dropping token alone saves a further 12%, not worth a second fetch per pin.

WHAT SHIPS TODAY is candidate (a)'s single file, dist/structure.json, because that is what measuring needed; shipping the index plus slices is fisc-02mf. Nothing in site/app.js reads either yet.
Closing waits on fisc-w11l, which blocks this bead and is still open although bb83d33 records its answer; the acceptance here is met by the notes above.
2026-09-18 DECIDED (a), SHIP THE WHOLE STRUCTURE, by the owner against the gzipped measurement this bead asked for and then was not read with.

THE (b) RECORD CAME FROM THE RAW FIGURE. L4.1's hand-off note records this bead as 'answered by measurement, candidate (b)', citing dist/structure.json at 868,612 bytes. That is the raw size; nothing serves raw. This bead's own L4.1 note already carried the gzipped pair and they point the other way.

MEASURED, gzipped, which is what crosses the wire:
  whole structure                     68,658  (64,361 best; 30,937 without provenance)
  what ONE drill costs today          19,111  (data/fund-flows.json, to draw 39 nodes and 37 links)
  all 19 documents the site ships    162,772
  every document + rungs + structure 218,714 as one blob
  the same blob without structure    152,405
  testdata/rungs.json alone            4,506  (290,026 raw -- it is MarshalIndent, and this data compresses about 65:1)

So (a) costs about three and a half of today's drills, ONCE, and then no network at all. (b) costs a round trip per drill forever plus an index that must be kept in step with the cuts it indexes. The reader pays less on the second drill and every drill after.

THE SIZE OBJECTION DOES NOT SURVIVE MATERIALISATION EITHER, which is the shape that could have broken it: the 300 rungs carry 1,764 node slots in all, about 6 per rung, because the caps keep every drawn chart small (the widest column holds 10 ids). At 192 bytes a node record that is ~331 KB compact before compression.

fisc-02mf existed only to implement (b) and is closed with this.
2026-09-19, CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S FRAMING, NOT ITS DECISION.

THE DECISION STANDS AND WAS RE-MEASURED TODAY, gzipped, which is what crosses the wire: structure.json 70,671; all 19 documents in dist/data 172,565; the rung answer testdata/rungs.json 13,340; one drill today (fund-flows.json) 18,864. Candidate (a) is still right by a wider margin than the close reason recorded -- the whole structure is under half of what the site already ships.

WHAT IS STALE IS THE OPENING SENTENCE: 'Once a view is a cut (fisc-w11l), the client stops shaping and starts walking.' THE CLIENT WALKS NOTHING. fisc-phtp supersedes that framing in terms -- 'L4.3 is written as the client walks the structure, which still has the client walking; the lane is Go emits the walk, the client renders it.'

WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS RATHER THAN A POINTER: this is the bead that decided the WIRE FORMAT, so it is the one a session reads when it asks what crosses the wire, and it would send that session away building a walking client. The two questions are separate and both are answered: kbuo decides HOW the data is delivered (one blob, no slicing, no per-drill network); phtp decides WHO WALKS IT (Go, emitted vetted).

THE LINE IS AMOUNTS. A client that walks the structure on request decides the fold, the cap and the window, and computes the residual's carried cents and the gap's difference. AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders' puts those on Go's side by name -- 'which nodes, which links, which columns, which folds, which derived marks and their amounts'. A figure the client derives is one fisc verify cannot witness.

SO THE SHAPE IS BOTH, and it is cheaper than either alone was assumed to be: ship the structure (what the client renders FROM, one fetch) and ship the rung answer (what it renders ACCORDING TO, ids plus the derived marks with their amounts). ~84K gzipped against today's 172K, with no network on any drill.

dist/structure.json ships today at 868,612 raw and NOTHING IN app.js READS IT; grep finds only pkg/cmd/export/data.go:28, the Go side that writes it.
2026-09-19, OWNER'S DECISION: ONE STRUCTURE PER YEAR, not one monolith. This refines (a) along an axis (a) and (b) did not name, and does NOT reopen (b).

MEASURED, minified and gzipped, which is what crosses the wire:
  whole structure            66,438
  scaffolding only            5,449   (levels, cuts, identities, views)
  scaffolding + FY2026       26,623   (the default year, 594 facts)
  scaffolding + FY2027       26,577   (594 facts)
  scaffolding + FY2025       21,816   (430 facts)
  scaffolding + FY2024       22,298   (430 facts)

The facts partition cleanly on fiscal_year -- 594/594/430/430 summing to all 2,048, no fact in two years. So first paint is ~27K rather than 66K, a 60% cut, and the 5,449 of scaffolding ships always.

WHY THE YEAR IS THE RIGHT AXIS AND THE DRILL IS NOT: site/app.js ALREADY FETCHES ON YEAR CHANGE and that path is already guarded -- showYear tells drew, superseded and failed apart, including the overtaken-request case, with a jscheck arm pinning all three. Per-year structures reuse a fetch path that exists and is checked. Per-drill fetching would need a new one, which is what (b) was and why it lost.

THIS IS NOT (b). (b) was an index plus lazily-fetched CUTS -- slicing per interaction, which is why structure.Document.Slice was deleted with it (fisc-dh6d). Per-year is a static partition along the dimension the reader already switches on: no slicing logic, no per-drill network, every drill still local.

ALSO SETTLED, and it was never a real question: the column budget needs no fetch at all. Go answers both budgets in one artifact (rungWidths = {3,4}) and the client holds both, so switching between 3 and 4 columns is a local lookup.
close_reason: Decided (a): ship the whole structure, one fetch, no server-side slicing. Measured gzipped, which is what crosses the wire: the whole structure is 68,658 bytes against the 19,111 ONE drill costs today (data/fund-flows.json, fetched to draw 39 nodes and 37 links). The (b) record in L4.1's hand-off came from the 868,612 RAW figure and nothing serves raw. Full measurements, including the materialised-blob case, are in the notes. fisc-02mf, which existed only to implement (b), is closed against this decision.

title: funding sources reconcile to departmentwide per department, and no check says so
description:
MEASURED BY fisc-2a97 AND NOT SHIPPED AS A CHECK. Budget Book pp.85-125 print, on each of the 14 pages, a Total Department Funding Sources that equals that page's Total Department Expenditures -- so the two blocks of the same eleven pages reconcile to each other per DEPARTMENT, by construction of the page rather than by our arithmetic. fisc-2a97 measured all 11 departments exactly, rolling the 29 divisions of the upper block up through data/departments.yaml's division -> department parentage.

WHY IT IS A DIFFERENT LANE FROM fisc-ko1j.12.9. That wave projected the lower block (department-funding) and added no tie check at all, because funding-sources-tie-to-spine already reconciles the lower block against pp.66-67 per FUND GROUP and needed nothing new. This check is a different claim: it ties the LOWER block to the UPPER one, department by department, and it is the only arithmetic in the corpus that would catch a row landing under the wrong department in one block and not the other -- which every fund-group sum is blind to, because both blocks would still sum correctly citywide.

WHAT IT NEEDS. The two scopes are departmentwide-expenditures (division slugs) and department-funding-sources (department slugs), which is the tier split fact-departments-resolve's summary reports; the join is Registry.Divisions()[i].Department. It reads FACTS and needs no graph, as funding-sources-tie-to-spine does.

ONE THING TO RE-DERIVE BEFORE WORKING IT: whether the identity holds in all FOUR printed columns or only the two adopted ones. fisc-2a97's measurement was of the adopted columns; five of the eleven departments miss their own printed total by exactly one dollar in the FY2023-24 Actual column (declared as stated_total_deltas on funding-city-attorney, funding-administrative-services, funding-library, funding-police and funding-public-works), so a check written over all four needs to say what it does about those.
notes: 2026-09-17, L3.4: funding-sources-tie-to-spine is deleted; the per-fund-group tie it made is the funding-sources ~ spine agreement in cuts-tie-along-the-lattice. The per-DEPARTMENT cross-block tie this bead asks for is still made by nothing, and the DepartmentTier refusal L3.1 added (division on pp.167-170 and pp.85-125's upper block, department on the lower block) is the seam it would have to cross.

title: A fifth column has room on the page now, and no step that asks for one
description:
THE ROOM IS DONE. app.js derives its ceiling from the steps, composes one media
query per column it could offer, and hands style.css --chart-max; no width is
written down in either file or in tools/jscheck/layout.mjs. Declaring a wider
step now moves the cap, the query and the checker's expected geometry together,
with no second edit to find.

WHAT IS LEFT IS A STEP THAT ASKS. pkg/cmd/export/data.go's widest declaration is
the fund step at Tiers {2,3,4,5}, so no chart on the site wants a fifth column
even though the page would now give it one.

THE CHAIN IS THE THING WORTH DECLARING: fund-flows carries tier 0 revenue
categories, 1 revenue lines, 2 fund groups, 3 funds, 4 departments and 5 object
categories, and a reader cannot today see where money came from and where it
went in one chart.

BLOCKED ON fisc-ke1f. Widening the fund-group step to that chain is accepted by
export.validateSteps and answered correctly by Go, and it breaks drillDown into
fund/100 -- the fund step's tier set becomes a subset of the widened window's.
The notes carry every measurement taken, so this does not need re-deriving.
notes:
2026-09-22: THE ROOM HALF IS DONE AND THE ASKING HALF IS BLOCKED. Re-derive
against the tree rather than against this bead's description, which was written
when both halves were open.

THE ROOM IS NO LONGER A NUMBER ANYWHERE (96c1035). app.js derives OFFERED_COLUMNS
from the longest `tiers` on the page, composes one media query per column it
could offer at chartWidth(n) + CHART_CUSHION, and hands style.css --chart-max;
the stylesheet names the property and carries no width. So "raising the cap" is
not a step any more: declare the tiers and the cap, the query and layout.mjs's
expected geometry all follow. MEASURED by adding one Widen entry to data.go and
touching nothing else -- the cap moved to 1846px and a second query appeared at
1902px, which is this bead's own predicted threshold.

THE ASKING HALF IS BLOCKED ON fisc-ke1f, measured 2026-09-22. Widening the
fund-group step to the fund-flows chain (Tiers {0,2,3,4,5}, Widen {4,5}, caps
{3:8, 4:24, 5:8}) is ACCEPTED by export.validateSteps and produces a correct
Go answer -- but it breaks drillDown(fund/100): the fund step's {2,3,4,5} becomes
a subset of what the widened fund-group window already draws, and the drill into
the fund fails outright. That is fisc-ke1f's subset-versus-equality question with
a consequence attached, and it has to be decided before the chain can ship.

WHAT THE WIDENING WOULD GIVE, all measured off the regenerated artifact, so a
session taking this up does not have to re-run it:
  - Only fund-group/general fills tiers 4 and 5. Every tier-4 node is a
    department of fund/100, so Go answers the other five groups' fund-group
    rungs with tiers 4 and 5 carrying ZERO ids and dropEmptyColumns takes them
    back to three columns. 196 rungs before and after; no rung added or removed;
    12 rungs change and only general gains ids, 12 -> 79 (= 12 + 23 + 44).
  - The five-column window draws 49 nodes, 68 links, bands 10/1/23/30, right
    edge 1596px, and 3 sub-pixel ribbons -- against 2 of 54 on the four-column
    fund window the site already ships. Same proportion at a chart 333px wider,
    so the caps above need no tightening.
  - export.ResidualOf then gives general's residual an OUTGOING leg:
    14,737,222 in FY2025-26 and 15,830,303 in FY2026-27, with ends gaining
    fund-balance/reserve-increase and transfers/out. Those are exactly
    fisc-ko1j.29's hand-measured figures, to the cent, in both years.

ONE DEFECT THAT REACHING IT EXPOSED IS ALREADY FIXED (af76bb9): carryResidual
placed an outgoing endpoint at the step's DECLARED last tier rather than the
drawn one, so at an unbought widening the ribbon ran backwards to column 0.
2026-09-23, THE READER-FACING HALF IS NOW STATED SEPARATELY. fisc-84y5: six of the seven declared steps declare no Widen at all, so a reader widening their window sees nothing change on any drill but the fund step. This bead is about a FIFTH column and read as a capability gap; the consequence of the fourth being declared once -- fisc-ko1j.12.3 widened the fund step 'to prove it' -- was written down nowhere until the owner reported it from a browser.

title: Nothing confirms .chart-wrap's breakout in a browser
description:
fisc-5e2b gave the chart figure its own width: .chart-wrap sets --chart-room: min(1513px, calc(100vw - 56px)), takes its width from it, and centres a box wider than its 1180px container with margin-inline: calc(50% - var(--chart-room) / 2).

tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's arm 'the stylesheet lets a four-column chart draw at the width app.js lays it out at' reads that DECLARATION as text and compares it with app.js's chartWidth(4). Mutation-measured both ways: dropping the rule reports '.chart-wrap declares no --chart-room cap', and capping it at the prose measure reports 'style.css allows the chart 1180px and app.js lays four columns out at 1513px, so it draws at 78% of that'.

What that cannot say, because nothing in this tree renders CSS (fisc-6at): that the negative margin actually centres the figure, that the breakout does not overflow the prose column, that the 56px cushion is enough for a classic scrollbar at viewport widths between 1180 and 1569px, and that the @media (max-width: 720px) block still meets a .chart-wrap the same width as the prose. All four are a browser walk after 'make site', and none of them has had one.

Confirm at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 375 CSS px, in one browser with overlay scrollbars and one with classic.
notes:
W4 (fisc-ko1j.12.5) ADDS TO THIS WALK rather than opening a second one, for the reason W3's note gives: same browser, same widths, one pass.

WHAT W4 ADDS, all browser-only because nothing in this tree renders CSS (fisc-6at) and nothing in it draws the chart at all (fisc-xsc8):
  - the `opens` marker is distinguishable from the derived diamond AT A GLANCE. They share one tspan.flag and one fill (--muted): confirm the right-pointing triangle and the diamond are told apart in light, in dark, and under forced-colors, and in greyscale. A check can say the right glyph is in the right string and nothing more;
  - the COMPOSED marker. nodeFlags draws the pair with nothing between them, and drill.mjs pins that no mark on either committed capture is both derived and openable -- so this case is LATENT and cannot be walked on the shipped corpus. Walk it by hand: give a drillable node derived:true in a local copy of testdata/sankey.golden.json, rebuild, and read the label. The question is whether the pair reads as two marks or as one unfamiliar glyph in a gutter already at its edge;
  - a REAL double click does not flash the isolate. clickNode acts on the first click rather than waiting out ACTIVATION_WINDOW, deliberately -- debouncing would put 500ms of lag on every isolate -- so the two clicks under a double click genuinely dim and undim the chart before doubleClickNode restores it and the drill redraws. Whether that is imperceptible or a visible strobe is a frame-timing question no harness here can ask. Watch it with prefers-reduced-motion both ways: svg.sankey .node carries a 120ms opacity transition under no-preference, which is the setting most likely to make it visible;
  - Space does not scroll the page. keydown preventDefaults Enter and Space on a focused node, and the node is an SVG g[role=button] inside a scrolling document;
  - a screen reader announces the split. nodeDescription now ends with what each gesture does and aria-keyshortcuts carries "Enter Space" on every node; that the two are read in an order that makes sense, and that aria-pressed on a node that OPENS (which it did not carry before W4) is not announced as though opening were the toggle, are observations no DOM assertion makes.

W5 (fisc-ko1j.12.6) ADDS TO THE SAME WALK, for the same reason.

WHAT W5 ADDS:
  - the `expands` marker, and the COMPOSED pair which is NOT latent here. Every folded tail is derived -- capColumn writes it, because the city printed no line called "24 smaller funds" -- so the plus always draws beside the diamond, as "  diamond-plus", on 9 of the 44 views the chain opens. W4's composed-marker question is therefore answerable on the shipped corpus without editing a fixture: open fund-group/special-revenue and read the tail's label. Does the pair read as two marks or as one unfamiliar glyph? And is the plus told from the triangle at a glance, in light, in dark, under forced-colors and in greyscale?
  - the breadcrumb chip. It is a <button class="crumb-expanded"> reading "showing all 32 funds x", dashed where .crumb-back is solid, and it sits AFTER the crumb-here span. Confirm it reads as a control rather than as a caption; that at 375px a bar holding three return controls, the current node and a chip wraps rather than pushing the trail out of view; and that the focus ring on it is visible in both themes.
  - the expanded chart itself, which is the shape the cap exists to prevent: 42 ribbons of which 9 lay out under a pixel, against 19 and 0 capped. The reader asked for it, so the question is not whether it is dense but whether it is usable -- can a sub-pixel ribbon be hovered at all, and does the chart still read as a chart?
  - WHETHER FIVE LABELS ACTUALLY OVERFLOW. fisc-mvrt: measured at layout.mjs's deliberately pessimistic 0.6em advance, 5 of the expanded column's labels are wider than the 250px gutter, the worst (fund/221, "Asset Seizure - Dept of Justice") by 36px of a 276px estimate. At a realistic 0.5em all five fit. Read them at 1920 and 1440 and settle it.
  - Escape out of a deeper rung lands focus on the RETURN control and not on the chip. restoreFocus now filters the bar by class for exactly this reason; confirm the ring lands where the check says it does, and that a screen reader announces the chip's aria-label ("Showing all 32 funds; fold the smallest back into one mark") rather than reading the x as "times".
THE WALK SHEET, BROUGHT UP TO 8f6087b (2026-09-14). W3, W4 and W5 added to this
bead as they landed and W6, W7 and W8 did not, so what follows adds their
browser-only questions and corrects two counts the earlier entries quote.

HOW TO STAND IT UP
  make site
  python3 -m http.server -d dist 8000
site/app.js fetches its step documents, so a file:// walk draws the spine and
refuses every drill. Six pages ship: index.html (the chart), trends.html,
history.html, balances.html, caveats.html, provenance.html. revenue.html and
spending.html are gone.

TWO COUNTS IN THE ENTRIES ABOVE ARE STALE. Do not go looking for them.
  - "9 of the 44 views the chain opens" (W5's entry, and site/app.js:2933,
    :2969, :4214): 44 was one number for both budget columns and the tree no
    longer has one. drill.mjs's COLUMNS pin openedViews 76 for FY2025-26 and 74
    for FY2026-27. Filed as fisc-0lnb.
  - "five of the expanded column's labels are wider than the gutter" (W5's
    entry, and fisc-mvrt): layout.mjs's EXPANDED pins over: 12, worst fund/221
    at 55.8px, since the open marker landed on 32 newly-openable labels
    (fisc-2gyh). The arm's own NAME still says five, filed as fisc-ieei. Read
    twelve labels, not five.

WHAT W6, W7 AND W8 ADD
  - SIXTY FUNDS THAT NOW OPEN, which is the largest thing on screen this branch
    changed. 54 of 60 open in FY2025-26 and 52 of 59 in FY2026-27, into the
    departments pp.85-125 print a funding row for. Open fund/240 -- the widest
    window in the schedule per fisc-zlxo -- and then try fund/511, which is one
    of the six that does NOT open: confirm a shut fund offers no affordance and
    that the two are told apart at a glance, not only by clicking.
  - THE OPEN MARKER ON 32 MORE LABELS is what moved the overflow count, and
    fisc-2gyh is the decision this walk is for: should an expanded column draw
    the marker at all, draw it only on hover or focus, or should the gutter
    widen for an expanded tier? All three are client changes with a jscheck arm
    each; none is a data question.
  - THE TRANSFERS RUNG (W6). transfers/in is the one step that keeps no flank,
    and p76's two legs are drawn as separate ribbons carrying one figure. Read
    whether "drawn once on each side, under the same name" is legible or reads
    as double counting.
  - THE TRAIL'S NEW QUALIFIER (8f6087b). The chart title and the <desc> now read
    "opened into General Fund (fund group), then General Fund (fund)". Confirm
    it reads as two rungs rather than as an apology, and that the longer title
    does not wrap badly at 1280 and 375. The question underneath it -- whether
    that rung should exist, given the group holds exactly one fund -- is
    fisc-ru2r and is a decision to take with the chart in front of you.

THE ROUTE, both budget columns where a figure differs
  1. the spine untouched -- the .chart-wrap breakout centres and does not
     overflow the prose column (this bead's original four questions)
  2. fund-group/general -> fund/100 -> a division -- the trail, three rungs in
     the bar, and fisc-ko1j.28's unspent difference standing with no ribbon
     under it
  3. fund-group/special-revenue, tail expanded -- the composed diamond-plus
     pair, the 32-label column, and the twelve labels layout.mjs flags
  4. fund-group/capital -> fund/551 -- fisc-8cx0's joint-worst label, -35px
  5. the Intergovernmental revenue category -- fisc-8cx0's other joint-worst
  6. transfers/in -- the non-window step, and fisc-zyya's dropped caveat
  7. an object category -- the declared 250,000 gap mark, FY2027 only
  8. fund/240, then fund/511 -- W8's sixty funds, and one that does not open

CONDITIONS: 1920, 1440, 1280 and 375 CSS px; one browser with overlay scrollbars
and one with classic, which is what the 56px cushion claims; light, dark,
forced-colors and greyscale; prefers-reduced-motion both ways for the
double-click strobe; and print preview, whose rules style.css's own comment says
nothing in this tree witnesses.

QUESTIONS TO BRING RATHER THAN FINDINGS TO RE-DISCOVER. Each is already filed
and each is a decision rather than a defect: fisc-hrfd (the inferred list says
the residual carries 4 flows and then lists 1), fisc-rgzz (the residual's
tooltip calls max(in, out) its "total"), fisc-dzby (FY2026 figures quoted in the
FY2027 chart's rationale), fisc-ko1j.28, fisc-2gyh, fisc-mvrt, fisc-ru2r.
WALK SHEET ADDENDUM, de45bb2. The over-gutter labels are now named by make js rather than counted, per column, so take the list off a run rather than off this bead: layout.mjs's arm 'the marks whose words run past the gutter are the ones this file names, and no others'. 23 marks in FY2025-26 and 26 in FY2026-27, over 76 and 74 views. TWO ARE WORTH SEEING FIRST and neither was in any earlier entry here: gap/expenditure/services-and-supplies is the widest label the tree draws anywhere, 98px past the gutter, and it is a DERIVED mark drawn only in the FY2026-27 object-category window -- open expenditure/services-and-supplies in that column; and residual/fund-group/general, which carries a different endpoint's words in each column. Route step 7 covers the first and step 2 the second.
GETTING A BROWSER ON A MACHINE THAT HAS NONE. Chrome for Testing's bucket serves any object path directly -- HEAD on storage.googleapis.com/chrome-for-testing-public/141.0.7390.54/linux64/chrome-linux64.zip answers 200 -- while REFUSING to list, so a version is pinned by hand the way .golangci-version pins the linter rather than discovered at fetch time; googlechromelabs.github.io's last-known-good-versions.json is unreachable. cdn.playwright.dev and deb.debian.org are blocked, so `npx playwright install` and `apt-get install chromium` both fail at the download and are the wrong route. No apt-get is needed: every Chromium shared library is already present (ldconfig -p answers libnss3, libnspr4, libatk-1.0, libatk-bridge-2.0, libatspi, libcups, libdrm, libxkbcommon, libgbm, libexpat, libpango-1.0, libcairo, libasound, libdbus-1, libglib-2.0, libXcomposite, libXdamage, libXfixes, libXrandr, libXext, libXi, libXtst, libXrender). Driving it needs no npm: node 22 has a global WebSocket and a global fetch and unzip is on PATH, so a CDP client is stdlib only -- which AGENTS.md's "The node boundary" requires and a vendored playwright-core would break.

THAT DOES NOT SETTLE THIS BEAD. A headless engine measures a box, reads a computed style and drives a gesture; it cannot say whether the chart READS well, which is what the route below is for. The four claims above stay owed to a person at a real browser.

WHAT A CLOUD SESSION CAN DO INSTEAD, and it is not nothing: serve dist/ over HTTP and drive the committed app.js against the SERVED artifacts with the packager's own config out of dist/index.html. That is a different witness from make js, which drives testdata goldens under a fixture config, and it catches a packager-to-client mismatch that jscheck structurally cannot. It renders no CSS and lays out no box, so it says nothing about any of the four above.

SIBLINGS WAITING ON THE SAME MACHINE: fisc-yj4w.18 (the print stylesheet's disclosure rules) and fisc-6at (the stylesheet's state indicators and contrast numbers). Whoever gets a browser should take all three in one walk.
2026-09-23, PRICED BY A DEFECT IT DEFERS. fisc-mvrt and fisc-8cx0 both send 'which labels actually overflow' here, and fisc-6at sends every rendered-state question here. In one browser session the owner found two reader-facing defects (fisc-4w20, fisc-84y5), neither of which any gate in the tree can see. The browser walk is not a tidy-up; it is the only thing that looks at what is served.

title: builtinLabels' doc comment says a registry label wins, and it loses
description:
internal/project/sankey.go:266 ends builtinLabels' doc comment with 'A registry label wins over any of these, which can only happen for a node that has a category slug.'

That is inverted. All three label resolvers consult builtinLabels FIRST and return on a hit -- sankey.label (sankey.go:909), fundFlows.label (fundflows.go:1187), departmentSpending.label (departmentspending.go:404) -- so a BUILT-IN wins and the registry never gets the id. sankey.label's own comment 30 lines below says so ('builtinLabels wins over the registry, which is the opposite of what you would expect'), and so does docs/sankey-contract.md:304 ('Node labels: a built-in wins over the registry').

So the tree carries two contradictory statements of one rule, and the wrong one is the one attached to the map. fund-balance/reserve-increase is the worked case: the taxonomy says 'Reserve Increase / (Use)' and the drawn label is 'Addition to Reserves', which is only possible because the built-in wins.

Found while re-deriving the labelling rule for fisc-og1n. Not fixed there: FALSE-CLAIM in a file that pass was not touching (AGENTS.md, 'Review is a loop'). The fix is the one sentence; nothing in the tree can check it, which is why it drifted.

title: The fund window's fourth column draws six marks labelled Wages & Benefits, because a tier-5 cell is labelled by its category alone
description:
Measured at fisc-ko1j.12.3 over testdata/fund-flows.golden.json, both published columns: fund-flows carries 44 tier-5 nodes under fund/100's 23 divisions -- each division's Services & Supplies and Wages & Benefits cell, one 4->5 link each. Their labels are the CATEGORY alone ('Wages & Benefits'), and which division a cell belongs to is only in node.parent.

So the widened fund window, capped at 8, draws a column of: Wages & Benefits, Services & Supplies, Wages & Benefits, Wages & Benefits, Wages & Benefits, Services & Supplies, Wages & Benefits, Wages & Benefits, and '36 smaller categories'. Six marks share one label and a reader can tell them apart only by following the ribbon back to the division it came from.

No reader can see this yet: the column budget is 3 for everyone until the control lands, which is why this blocks fisc-ko1j.12.4 rather than being a live defect. Options measured or considered, none taken: label the cell with its division in internal/project (changes every document that carries tier 5, including the division window where the short label is right); have the client compose 'Patrol, Wages & Benefits' for a column whose parents are all distinct; or drop Widen from the fund step and widen somewhere the fourth column is legible. The sub-pixel measurement that forced the cap is on the step's comment in pkg/cmd/export/data.go.
close_reason:
Fixed at 39666c3, but NOT where this bead proposed and not in internal/project at all.

Premise re-measured and held: fund-flows carries 44 tier-5 nodes and exactly 2 distinct labels (23 'Services & Supplies', 21 'Wages & Benefits'), the same in both years' goldens and in dist/data/fund-flows.json.

Both options this bead named were refused by measurement, with layout.mjs's own estimator over the drawn windows:
  - 'label the cell with its division in internal/project': a division's own window draws that division's two cells side by side, so it reads 'Patrol' twice. Mutation-measured -- relabelling tier 5 by its parent in the inner window turns the new arm red with 'column 2 draws 2 marks reading "Patrol / Patrol"'.
  - the pair on one line, wherever it is composed: 'Fire Administration — Services & Supplies' wants 348px of a 250px gutter. Six of the eight drawn marks came out between -22px and -108px of clearance, and a division's own window is worse ('Public Works Administration — Services & Supplies', 49 chars). The pair does not fit at 3 columns or at 4.

So the ambiguity is a property of the COLUMN, not of the node, and the fix is in site/app.js: labelQualifiers gives a mark whose label another mark in the same column also carries a second line naming its parent. Every other mark draws what it drew before (the qualifier tspan is empty and carries neither an x nor a dy). No published document changed and no golden moved; the three label resolvers in internal/project are untouched, so docs/sankey-contract.md's built-in-wins rule is untouched too.

Cost measured: the tightest pair of label blocks in the qualified fourth column clears by 3.9px, against 3.2px between two single-line labels in the same window's third column. Horizontal clearance in that column is unchanged at 50-79px.

department-spending does not move, checked not assumed: its object node is expenditure/<category>, one per category, on a separate resolver. Over all six committed goldens, fund-flows is the only document with two nodes sharing a label within a tier.

Check: tools/jscheck/layout.mjs, 'no column of the fund window or of a division's own draws two marks a reader would read the same'. Mutation: the pre-fix label, by returning before labelQualifiers records anything. RED naming all six ids.

Filed: fisc-baff, fisc-xhqt.

title: A window that draws a rung's own decomposition makes that rung's step a redraw, and validateSteps' arm compares equality
description:
internal/export/export.go's per-parent arm refuses a step whose Tiers slices.Equal its parent's: 'opening a node would redraw the chart it was opened from'. With the fund step widened to {2,3,4,5}, the division step draws {3,4,5} -- a strict SUBSET of what is already on screen at four columns. Clicking a division then opens a window whose every column the reader can already see, and the arm cannot say so because equality is not containment.

Measured at fisc-ko1j.12.3: at a column budget of 4 the fund window draws 34 nodes and 54 links over tiers {2,3,4,5} (tools/jscheck/drill.mjs COLUMNS[].fundWide); the division step's {3,4,5} is contained in that set. At the shipped budget of 3 the fund window is {2,3,4} and the division rung adds tier 5, so nothing a reader can reach today is affected.

The fix is not obviously 'refuse a subset': a window rescales to the opened node, so {3,4,5} of one division is a different chart from the same three columns of the whole fund even though the columns are the same. What the arm can say is that it is checking a weaker property than its sentence claims. Decide which, and make the sentence and the check agree.
notes:
2026-09-22: THE SUBSET CASE NOW HAS A MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, and it is a drill
that stops working rather than a chart that reads oddly.

Widening the fund-group step to the fund-flows chain -- Tiers {0,2,3,4,5},
