title: W5 Expanding an aggregate redraws its column uncapped
description:
expanded: Set<number> on the Rung typedef (app.js:753-775), beside id/doc/step/chart. sideOf reads it in the cap loop -- one line, and the filter->cap->fold order is untouched: if (!cap || (rung.expanded && rung.expanded.has(tier))) continue;

WHY THE RUNG AND NOT A MODULE VARIABLE. The stack is the path and an expansion is a property of one chart on it. Tier 3 is capped in the fund-group window and drawn whole in the fund window; a module variable would carry an expansion across both and across a pop.

IT SURVIVES A DRILL BY CONSTRUCTION. rung.chart is recorded rather than recomputed -- the typedef's own comment insists on it -- so a window opened from an expanded chart keeps the expanded flank with no extra code. That is the argument for the rung as its home.

IT MUST NOT SURVIVE A YEAR SWITCH, and that is a decision. showYear already drops stepDocs because a step's document belongs to the year it was opened in. 'Show the 24 smaller funds' names a column of one year's document; the other year's has 23. Pin it in year.mjs, not drill.mjs.

THE WAY BACK. The aggregate is gone once expanded, so there is nothing left to double-click to collapse, and making Escape depth-dependent is worse. A dismissible <button> chip in #breadcrumb: 'showing all 32 funds x'. restoreFocus filters bar.children to button and takes the LAST -- the chip must not be last, or a keyboard drill lands focus on it instead of the return control.

WHAT THIS FEATURE IS FOR, measured: no department column is aggregated. The tier-4 division cap is 24 against 23 divisions and drill.mjs pins it INERT. What folds is fund-group/special-revenue (32 funds -> 8 + '24 smaller funds'), fund-group/capital (11), and five revenue-line columns over the cap of 8 -- charges-for-services 19, other-taxes 15, licenses-and-permits 14, property-taxes 14, miscellaneous 11.
acceptance_criteria: COLUMNS[].uncapped {links:42, hairlines:9} and capped {links:19, hairlines:0} ALREADY EXIST, measured by calling capColumn with a raised cap. This wave makes the uncapped shape reachable, so that pin stops being hypothetical and becomes an assertion on the drawn chart -- state that in the commit. Mutations: make sideOf ignore rung.expanded (measures capped); recompute rung.chart instead of reading it (the expanded flank is lost through a drill); leave the set across a year switch (FY2026-27 draws 32 funds where it has 31). RISK: aggregate.folds retains the tail plus orphaned() descendants so caveatsFor reaches a caveat about a folded node. Expanded, those nodes return and folds is empty -- verify caveatsFor does not double-report. Latent today, and latent is how it would ship.
notes:
W4 (fisc-ko1j.12.5) DELIBERATELY LEFT THE AGGREGATE'S AFFORDANCE TO THIS WAVE, and this wave must now ship it. W4's own bead asked nodeClass for an `expands` class beside `opens`, with a marker and a cursor. It shipped `opens` complete -- class, marker, cursor, aria-label, aria-keyshortcuts and both gestures -- and shipped NO `expands` anything.

WHY, and it is W4's own first sentence applied to W4: an affordance with no gesture behind it is half a contract. Nothing in site/app.js can expand an aggregate until this bead lands. MEASURED over the chain: 9 of the 44 views it opens draw an aggregate, so a class and a marker promising an expansion would have been a promise broken on nine charts. site/app.js's nodeClass doc comment records this and names this bead.

SO THIS WAVE OWES, beyond its own acceptance: the `expands` class in nodeClass; a second marker in nodeFlags (which already composes two and pins `both: 0` in drill.mjs's MARKS as latent -- an aggregate that also opens cannot happen, but a THIRD glyph changes the label width layout.mjs now measures through app.nodeFlags); the sentence in nodeDescription; whatever aria-keyshortcuts should say when Enter expands rather than opens; and the chart hint, which W4 rewrote to name both gestures on every view.

THE GESTURE IS ALREADY THERE TO HANG IT ON. keyNode branches on `key === \"Enter\" && drillable(d)`, and doubleClickNode on `drillable(d)`; an expand is a third branch in each, not a new handler. Both are named functions reachable from tools/jscheck -- see fisc-xsc8 for why they had to be.

W4's CSS FINDING APPLIES HERE TOO: cursor: pointer stays on svg.sankey .node and did NOT move onto .node.opens, because a single click follows one node's money on every mark. An expandable node is not an exception to that.

PREMISE RE-MEASURED AT f8e6d50, AND THE 'NO DEPARTMENT COLUMN IS AGGREGATED' LINE ABOVE IS TOO NARROW. It is true of the CHAIN's division column -- fund/100 draws 23 divisions against the fund step's tier-4 cap of 24, and drill.mjs pins that cap inert. It is NOT true of the object-category windows: expenditure/services-and-supplies folds 21 divisions and expenditure/wages-and-benefits folds 18, both dept/* nodes at tier 4 under the object-category step's cap of 8. So the owner's '20+ smaller departments' names a real column after all, and this wave expands it like any other.

MEASURED, the nine aggregate-bearing views of the 44 the chain opens (FY2025-26, at the shipped three-column budget): revenue/charges-for-services 11 lines, revenue/taxes/other 7, revenue/licenses-and-permits 6, revenue/taxes/property 6, revenue/miscellaneous-revenue 3; fund-group/special-revenue 24 funds, fund-group/capital 3; expenditure/services-and-supplies 21 divisions, expenditure/wages-and-benefits 18. At four columns the fund window adds a tenth: 36 categories folded at tier 5.

AND 'EXPAND, THEN OPEN' IS REACHABLE IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE. Measured: of the nine views above, NONE offers anything to open -- the five revenue and two object-category windows are ends of the chain, and the fund step's role leaves every fund but fund/100 closed. The one chart that draws a tail AND opens something is the fund window at four columns, where the tier-5 tail sits beside 23 openable divisions. That is where the drill arm runs, and it is why the acceptance criterion's 'expand special-revenue, open one' could not be written as stated.

title: W4 A node that opens says so, and the gestures split
description:
The affordance and the gesture ship together: an affordance with no gesture behind it, or a gesture with nothing signalling it, is half a contract.

nodeClass (app.js:2311-2313) gains 'opens' (drillable(d)) and 'expands' (isAggregate(d.id)). style.css:664-666 moves cursor:pointer OFF svg.sankey .node onto .node.opens, .node.expands -- today every node claims to be clickable and most are not.

The visual channel cannot be colour (contrast rule), the dashed rect (.derived), --critical (.contra) or a dash pattern (partition/derived on ribbons). Use the tspan.flag slot app.js:3450-3455 already owns for the diamond derived marker: a right-pointing triangle for opens, a boxed plus for expands. Survives forced-colors and greyscale, and is read aloud.

nodeDescription ends '-- press Enter to open' / '-- press Enter to show all 32 funds'; add aria-keyshortcuts.

MOUSE. Adding dblclick to a <g> that also has click fires two clicks first. DO NOT DEBOUNCE THE CLICK -- that puts 500ms of lag on the isolate. Reuse the construct already in the file: keyActivation's 500ms same-id echo guard (app.js:3404). Add clickIsolate {id, at, was}; click records the prior isolated and toggles as today; dblclick checks the same window and RESTORES was before opening.

KEYBOARD. Enter opens/expands, Space isolates, always. The owner does not care which binding; this one invents nothing (both keys already activate), mirrors the mouse split, and reduces to one teachable sentence. The honest cost: role=button conventionally activates on Space, so it must be announced -- paintChartHint gains '; Space highlights its flows'.

REWRITE THE COMMENT AT app.js:3388-3400. It currently argues 'the pages that drill are exactly the pages that do not need to isolate, and no page has to do both from one gesture.' This wave makes that false. AGENTS.md's 'Where writing goes' forbids an erratum: keep the rule (a second meaning on one activation is a new interaction contract) and state that the contract is now two gestures. It also answers fisc-ppkq's third objection differently than it stands.

title: W3 The column budget: responsive via matchMedia, with a manual override
description:
A module-level `let columnBudget` does NOT violate RENDER_TIERS' 'must never become a constant in this file' rule, and the comment must say why: RENDER_TIERS is WHICH TIERS a document is drawn at, a property of a hierarchy. A budget is a property of the reader's window and NEVER NAMES A TIER -- every tier drawn is still one the step declared.

Seed from localStorage['fisc-columns'], the theme's precedent and the only storage this page uses. Viewport via matchMedia, NOT resize -- matchMedia is already feature-checked at app.js:4092 and the harness stub already answers and records it; a resize listener needs a new stub and a new seam arm for no benefit. (min-width: 1500px) -> 4, (min-width: 1900px) -> 5.

The manual override wins until cleared; viewport applies only in its absence.

Plus/minus buttons in .head-controls beside the year fieldset and theme toggle, disabled at the bounds, with a polite live region reading '3 columns'.

THE FLOOR IS 3 AND RESPONSIVENESS IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL -- the viewport can add columns above 3 and never remove one, because CHART_WIDTH is a fixed design width scaled by viewBox and app.js:429 already argues a sankey's labels do not reflow. Say that rather than implying behaviour the code does not have.

A budget change is redrawStack(drilled) -- rung.doc and rung.chart are both already recorded. It must not pop, refetch or move focus, and it must take showYear's lay-out-then-repaint order (fisc-bsg).
acceptance_criteria: lifecycle.mjs, which owns listener wiring: a viewport that can carry four gets four and a manual decrement holds against it (mutation: do not persist the override and the next media change silently overrides the reader); a budget change redraws the rung without popping it (mutation: redrawStack(drilled.slice(0,-1)) and the breadcrumb loses a rung). Plus a seam.mjs arm that the stub's matchMedia can be FOLLOWED for a width query -- otherwise the first two are green because the seam answers nothing.
close_reason:
Landed as f68e4aa. columnBudget moves from two places that agree about precedence: COLUMN_QUERIES asked through matchMedia (one tier, (min-width: 1569px) -> 4), and a +/- control in .head-controls recording columnOverride into localStorage['fisc-columns']. The reader outranks the viewport while the override is set, and stepping to the count the viewport itself would give clears it.

DIVERGED FROM THE BEAD IN TWO PLACES, both measured:
  - the breakpoint is 1569px and not 1500px. .chart-wrap gives the chart calc(100vw - 56px) below its cap, so at 1500px a four-column chart has 1444px against the 1513px app.js lays it out at, and draws at 95%. 1569 is chartWidth(4) + that same cushion; layout.mjs re-derives it from the two shipped files.
  - the (min-width: 1900px) -> 5 tier is not shipped. chartWidth(5) is 1846px against a 1513px cap (82%), and no step data.go declares has five tiers, so a budget of 5 would change no chart even with room. fisc-ipif carries both halves of reopening it.

Checks in the same commit: the seam arm (the stub's matchMedia answers and can be followed for a WIDTH query), two lifecycle arms (a wide viewport gets four and a step down holds against it; a budget change redraws the rung without popping or refetching), a third on saved-choice round-tripping, two layout arms (every viewport the page adds a column at has room for it; the cap is asked of app.js's ceiling rather than of a literal 4), and a Go arm that the templates actually render the control disabled -- the jscheck stub fabricates any id in TEMPLATE_IDS, so no JS arm could tell an absent control from a working one.

Six mutations run, all red, listed in the commit message. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 50 passed, 0 failed, 1 vacuous (declared), 1 skipped; make js 208 arms. PAGE.openedViews 44, carryingViews 20, worstDeep and every COLUMNS[] tuple unmoved -- the harness reports no viewport, so it still opens every page at NARROW_COLUMNS.

title: W2 The client draws N columns, and the fund step widens to prove it
description:
windowFor (app.js:2102-2116): the guard generalises to keep-contiguous, outermost kept tier at index 0 or tiers.length-1, tiers[keep.length] === step.from. The two sideOf calls take tier SLICES instead of pairs -- filterToNode/filterFromNode are already tier-count agnostic. The splice loop and the carried_from rule are untouched.

activeTiers() returns the set trimmed to the budget by dropping widen entries from the end of the widen order. alignFor, openableColumns and paintChartHint read it and need no change.

Geometry: chartWidth(n) = 2*LABEL_GUTTER + BAND*(n-1) + NODE_WIDTH*n with BAND 340, so N=3 is byte-identical to today. LABEL_GUTTER does not grow -- gutters serve the two end columns only, because W0 moved interior labels above their rects. layout.mjs builds its own sankey from these, so it must call chartWidth() and the harness must export it.

pkg/cmd/export/data.go: the fund step gains Widen: []int{5}. The widened declaration lands IN THIS WAVE -- a client change with no declaration exercising it is a check that cannot fail.

DROP A WIDENED COLUMN THAT COMES OUT EMPTY and re-lay, rather than refusing. d3 takes the column count from topology (o = max(depth)+1, alignFor clamped into it), so a column budget is only ever a REQUEST. Five of six fund groups have no tier-4 node and refusing turns their windows into a banner.
acceptance_criteria: A drill.mjs arm drives drillDown at budget 4 and pins the widened fund window per column in COLUMNS[].fundWide. Mutation: set Widen back to nil -- the wide pin reddens while the narrow one stays green. Plus a layout.mjs band count (3 at N=4; bands() already throws on a span != 1) and an arm for the empty-column drop. NO PINNED FIGURE MOVES because the default budget is 3 and the harness stub answers matchMedia not-matching -- openedViews 44, carryingViews 20, worstDeep 51.38 and every COLUMNS[] tuple stand. Say that in the commit.
notes:
2026-09-14, from W1 (fisc-ko1j.12.2), which landed the seam: THE FUND STEP NEEDS BOTH DECLARATIONS, not just Widen. A widen entry is a COLUMN OF Tiers that is optional, so the fund step becomes Tiers: []int{2, 3, 4, 5} AND Widen: []int{5}; validateSteps refuses a Widen naming a tier Tiers does not draw at the end away from the kept flank (arm: 'a widened column is on the opened node's side'). Declaring Widen alone is refused by len(Tiers) != len(Keep)+2+len(Widen).

That is also what makes activeTiers() trivial on this side: the full order is on the wire in step.tiers and the budget drops widen entries from the end of the widen order, with no side to re-derive in JS.

Also from W1: DrillStep.Keep may now hold a flank more than one column deep (contiguous, nearest-centre first), and export.go's kept-flank arm is slices.Contains(p.keep, s.From). site/app.js's windowFor still refuses keep.length !== 1 and tiers.length !== 3 -- that generalisation is this bead's, as written.
close_reason: Landed at c8f88c6. windowFor generalised to keep-contiguous/centre-at-keep.length mirroring validateSteps; activeTiers() trims by a module-level column budget (NARROW_COLUMNS for every reader, setColumnBudget is W3's seam); chartWidth(n) with BAND 319 so N=3 is 1180 to the pixel; an empty widened column is dropped and the rung reshaped; the fund step declares Tiers {2,3,4,5} + Widen {5} with a tier-5 cap of 8 named 'categories' -- uncapped it lays 11 sub-pixel ribbons and 11 height-less nodes. Checks: COLUMNS[].fundWide per column, the narrow window beside it, the empty-drop pair on a widened fund-group step, and layout.mjs's band/geometry/label arms at N=4. title: W1 Keep becomes a list of adjacent tiers, and Widen arrives
description:
Seam only. Every shipped step still keeps one tier and declares no widen, so nothing on the wire moves.

DrillStep.Keep (export.go:559-574): keep the argument, rewrite the claim -- a window keeps ONE FLANK, and a flank may be more than one column deep. Entries nearest-centre first, contiguous in the parent's column order.

New Widen []int `json:"widen,omitempty"`: the tier added for each column beyond three, in the order added. The SIDE is derived (adjacent to exactly one current end; neither or both is refused), so the caller declares only what cannot be computed.

validateSteps, five arms: len(Keep)>1 becomes contiguous-and-one-side; len(Tiers)!=3 becomes len(Keep)+1+K; Tiers[1]!=From becomes Tiers[len(Keep)]; adjacency fi+/-1 becomes fi-M..fi-1 or fi+1..fi+M with the sign still deciding the side.

THE FAIL-OPEN THIS BEAD EXISTS TO FIX. export.go:1326 reads `len(p.keep) == 1 && p.keep[0] == s.From`. It is the arm refusing a click on a kept flank, measured at 157,797,110 of node height with no ribbon under it. It stops working the instant Keep can hold two entries. It becomes slices.Contains(p.keep, s.From) IN THE SAME COMMIT as the type change, never after.
acceptance_criteria: harness.mjs parseStepShapes learns Widen, declared-or-refused, never defaulted. Two seam.mjs arms. Mutations: revert the Keep parse to \{(\d+)\} and a two-deep flank ships as one-deep while every window check still measures green; reflow the Widen literal across lines and the parse must throw rather than return undefined. Refusal rows in internal/export/views_test.go for each new arm. No five-edit check registration.
notes:
2026-09-14, measured while working it: TWO CLAUSES OF THIS BEAD WERE WRONG AGAINST THE TREE AND WERE NOT IMPLEMENTED AS WRITTEN.

(1) "no entry already in Tiers" is inverted. A Widen entry must BE a column of Tiers. fisc-ko1j.12.3 requires activeTiers() to return "the set trimmed to the budget by dropping widen entries from the end of the widen order", and activeTiers() returns step.tiers -- so a tier the step does not draw cannot be trimmed out of it, and a client that had to splice one in would be re-deriving in JS a side the packager already derived. So Widen names optional COLUMNS of Tiers, in the order they are dropped, and validateSteps holds the two declarations against each other: the widened columns are the len(Widen) columns at the end of Tiers away from the kept flank, outward in widen order. Two parties recording one shape, which is a real check; one declaration restated would not be.

(2) "adjacent to neither, or to both, is refused" -- there is no both-ends arm, because in a linear column order an entry is at one end or at neither. Adjacent to both would need an empty base shape, which the len(Tiers) == len(Keep)+2+len(Widen) arm refuses first, so an arm for it would be green because the earlier gate fired: AGENTS.md, 'Prove it can fail'. Adjacent to neither is real and has a row.

(3) Tiers[len(Keep)] != From is right only for a LEFT flank. Shipped: which end the flank is at is read off Tiers once (Tiers[:M] == reversed(Keep), or Tiers[n-M:] == Keep), and the centre is then Tiers[M] or Tiers[n-1-M]. With M=1 both are index 1, which is why today's steps are unaffected.

MEASURED, off data.go through the jscheck harness: the spine ships FIVE windows and not four -- fund-group keeps [0], fund [2], division [3], revenue-category [2], object-category [2] -- and no step's From is in any of its parents' keeps, so the tightened arm refuses nothing that ships.
close_reason: Landed as 733aef2. DrillStep.Keep is a flank of one or more contiguous columns nearest the centre first; DrillStep.Widen names the columns of Tiers a narrow client drops, in drop order, with the side derived from the end of Tiers away from the flank. validateSteps' window arms are arithmetic on len(Keep)+2+len(Widen) rather than on the number three, the flank walks out from the centre against every parent, a tier drawn twice is refused, and the kept-flank-open arm is slices.Contains(p.keep, s.From) -- the fail-open this commit's own type change introduced, fixed in it, with a refusal row over a two-deep flank whose OUTER kept column a child opens. Mutations run, all four red then green. jscheck: parseStepShapes reads Widen declared-or-refused, drill.mjs's stepAs copies it, two new seam.mjs arms. Gates: make pre-commit clean, fisc verify 50 passed 0 failed, facts.jsonl unmoved, dist/ unmoved but the build stamp and 8 comment lines of app.js. Two clauses of this bead were wrong against the tree and are recorded in the notes above, with the same correction added to fisc-ko1j.12.3 so W2 declares Tiers and Widen together.

title: W0 Review defers to the merge, and label anchoring stops keying on d.depth
description:
Two things, together because the second is what makes the rest of the lane measurable.

(1) AGENTS.md, 'Review is a loop, not a pass': on a branch of several lanes, run the loop once at the MERGE rather than per lane. Same triage, same three-to-five passes. What does NOT move must be said explicitly, or the rule reads as permission to defer the check too: each lane still ships its jscheck check and its stated mutation in its own commit (fisc-rx1d), and every unfixed finding is still a bead in the session it was found in. Evidence in docs/review-loop-evidence.md, where fisc-6lfh already measured that deferral inflated pass-1 yield to 24 against a per-commit baseline.

(2) site/app.js:3441-3442 anchors labels on d.depth === 0. d.depth is d3's LONGEST PATH, not the assigned column. Anchor on activeTiers().indexOf(d.tier) -- app.js's own declaration, not d3's clamped d.layer, which would be a second source. Column 0 anchors end left of x0; the LAST column anchors start right of x1; interior columns anchor middle at y0-5, above the rect. That is the only placement with room and it is already needed at N=3, where the fund window's middle labels run into the plot.

title: A fund's window states its unspent difference in a sentence, where every other window has a mark
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 through drillDown over both committed captures. The fund window {2,3,4} draws fund/100 taking 157,873,470 from its group and paying 144,650,802 to its divisions in FY2025-26, and 164,358,147 against 149,014,579 in FY2026-27. d3-sankey sizes the node at the larger, so 13,222,668 and 15,343,568 of node height stand with no ribbon under them. The step's Description names what it is -- what the city transfers out of the fund and adds to its reserves, which pp.66-67 print for the fund GROUP -- and tools/jscheck pins both figures, but a sentence is not a mark.

NEITHER FIELD FITS TODAY, which is why it was not fixed in the lane that found it. DrillStep.Residual and DrillStep.Gaps are both refused by validateSteps on a step that switches no document, and this step draws fund-flows under fund-flows. The refusals are right in their own terms: a residual is what one document prints at a grain another does not, and a gap is one cell two documents print at two figures. This is neither -- a fund's revenue and its divisions' spending are two different quantities that need not be equal, and the difference is real money pp.66-67 print at group grain.

IT IS NOT NEW. The same 13,222,668 stood on fund/100 in the {0,3,4} chart this replaced, where the residual beside it made the COLUMN balance while the fund did not. What Lane G changed is that fund/100 is now the node the reader clicked.

A THIRD FIELD, OR A THIRD READING OF Residual whose endpoints are the GROUP's and whose node hangs off the fund, would state it as a mark. Decide before the drill grows a fourth rung.

title: StepStems resolves a schedule-less step's document from the previous DECLARED step, not from its parent
description:
internal/export's StepStems walks the declared steps in order with `prev = stem` at the foot of the loop, so a step naming no schedule draws whatever the step BEFORE IT IN THE LITERAL drew. validateSteps resolves the same question from the step's After -- it refuses a projection-less step whose parents draw two different documents, naming both -- so the two disagree about what "the document before it" means.

LATENT, NOT LIVE. Measured 2026-09-13 against the shipped declaration: the order is fund-group (fund-flows), fund (""), division (""), revenue-category (fund-flows), object-category (department-spending), and each projection-less step's predecessor in the literal IS its parent, so every rung draws the right file. Declaring the object-category step between fund-group and fund would hand the fund rung department-spending with every gate green -- it is appended in its own block, which is the only reason it is last.

ONE SPELLING NOW, AND THE BUG IS STILL IN IT. The page builder and the rung walk had two copies of this resolution and they disagreed on a second axis as well; both now call export.StepStems, so the defect is in one function and a fix lands once. That is a smaller bead, not a closed one.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND A TEST: resolve the stem from the step's parents (they are always earlier, and validateSteps has already refused parents that disagree) rather than from the declaration order, and add a case declaring a document-switching step between a parent and its child.

title: The fund group and its fund print the same label, so the breadcrumb reads it twice
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 off dist/, both published columns. data/funds.yaml names fund 100 "General Fund" and internal/project's builtinLabels names fund-group/general "General Fund". Lane G made the fund a rung of its own, so the breadcrumb at depth 2 reads "General Fund > General Fund" and the chart title reads "opened into General Fund, then General Fund". Both are true and neither is readable.

IT IS A LABELLING DECISION, NOT A CLIENT ONE: paintBreadcrumb and labelOfRung take the node's own label, which is what they must do. The fix is one of the two labels -- "General Fund group" for fund-group/general, or the fund's own name off pp.258-261 -- and either moves the spine goldens, the legend, and every check quoting the string. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs already relabels the spine's copy to "General Fund group" in its fixture, which is how its checks tell the two apart, so that relabelling is also a fixture property to re-derive.

The other five groups do not have this: their funds carry printed fund names.
notes:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED 2026-09-14 AGAINST ee3a9e5, AND THE FIX MENU DOES NOT SURVIVE
IT. This bead says "the fix is one of the two labels". Measured: BOTH labels are
the city's own printed words, for two different things.

  p0066.txt:8   "General Fund" as a fund-group COLUMN HEADER, beside
                "Enterprise Funds"; p0067.txt:8 prints the other four.
  p0255.txt:262 "100 General Fund" as fund 100's NAME.

internal/project/sankey.go:301-312 states the rule this makes live: the six
fund-group entries in builtinLabels "are the column headers Budget Book pp.66-67
print over the columns this projection reads, so they are the city's words
rather than ours". The same comment records p66's words winning over the
taxonomy's for fund-balance/reserve-increase ("Addition to Reserves" against
"Reserve Increase / (Use)"). So "General Fund group" would make one of the six
ours while its five siblings stay the city's, and falsify that comment.

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY IS. Not a labelling decision: the ambiguity is the city's,
which prints one phrase for a fund group on p66 and for a fund on p255, and
neither box can be relabelled without inventing words for it. The rung
COMPOSITION is what has to disambiguate.

THE MATERIAL FOR THAT IS ALREADY AT THE SEAM. DrillStep.Back ("All fund groups")
and DrillStep.Tail ("funds") are both declared plural nouns, and their doc
comments give this bead's own reason for being declared rather than derived --
"a tier number does not know what the reader calls the things in it", and Tail
records app.js having once derived `tier === 3 ? "funds" : "categories"`, the
construct paintBreadcrumb's comment refuses. A singular noun for the rung a step
creates is that same declaration once more, and labelOfRung (site/app.js:2472)
and the title composition (:2162) are where it would be spent.

NOT DECIDED HERE. Costed and put to the owner 2026-09-14: relabel anyway and
amend sankey.go's comment to say five are the city's words and one is ours, or
qualify the rung from a declared noun, or leave it for the browser walk.
close_reason: Closed against 8f6087b, and NOT the way this bead asked. Its menu was 'one of the two labels'; both are the city's printed words (p0066.txt:8 for the group column, p0255.txt:262 for fund 100), so neither could move. Resolved in the TRAIL instead: DrillStep.Noun is declared per step and site/app.js's trailOfRungs qualifies every member of a colliding set, so the title and the chart <desc> read 'General Fund (fund group), then General Fund (fund)'. The breadcrumb bar was never part of this -- it draws return controls plus the current rung, and repeats nothing. Two jscheck arms on openedAsShipped, which builds the chain over the documents' own words because every other builder relabels the spine's fund-group/general and would have passed either way.

title: A window's counts line reports the kept flank's facts against the drawn document's total
description:
paintCounts (site/app.js) counts every drawn link's fact_ids into `cited` and reports that against the DRAWN document's counts.facts. On a window the kept flank's links come off the chart above, so their fact ids are another document's.

MEASURED 2026-09-13 on the object-category window, FY2025-26 services-and-supplies: the counts line reads "14 flows between 15 nodes, from 34 of the document's 73 facts". Of those 34, 5 are spine facts carried in with the kept fund-group flank and are not among department-spending's 73 at all; the other 29 are. The sentence is therefore a claim about one document made partly out of another's.

NOT NEW WITH LANE F AND NOT ITS TO DECIDE. windowFor is Lane C's (d7086dc) and Lane D's revenue-category window will read the same way the moment it lands, so the fix is one decision taken once.

THE MECHANISM FOR IT ALREADY EXISTS: paintCounts already sets residual links aside and reports them as "and N flows carried unchanged from the chart above". A kept flank is carried in exactly that sense -- its nodes carry carried_from -- so the shape of the fix is probably to exclude a link whose source or target is a carried mark from `cited` and count it into `carried` instead. What needs deciding is the sentence, because on a window that is a THIRD of the ribbons rather than a footnote.

tools/jscheck/drill.mjs pins the current wording per column (COLUMNS[*].object.counts), so the fix moves those pins and they must be re-measured by hand.
notes:
MEASURED AGAIN ON LANE D'S WINDOW, 2026-09-13, and the bead's prediction holds exactly: the revenue-category step now declares Keep [2] / Tiers {1,0,2} and every one of the twenty category views reads the same way. Per published year, 26 of the facts the ten counts lines cite are SPINE facts carried in with the kept fund-group flank and are not among fund-flows' 280 at all -- one per kept fund group, so 1 on Fines, Licences and Sales, 2 on Property Taxes, Other Taxes and Contributions, 4 on Charges, Intergovernmental and Miscellaneous, and 5 on Use of Money. Property Taxes reads "11 flows between 12 nodes, from 19 of the document's 280 facts" where 17 of the 19 are pp.127-140's.

NOT FIXED IN LANE D, deliberately. The defect is one seam (paintCounts) shared by Lane F's four object windows, Lane D's ten category windows and Lane G's still to come, and the wording pins for all of them move together -- COLUMNS[*].object.counts and now COLUMNS[*].category.counts and .views. Fixing it inside a declaration change would also decide, in passing, whether a kept flank's ribbons are "carried unchanged from the chart above": on a category window that is 1 of 11 ribbons on Property Taxes and 5 of 13 on Use of Money, which is the sentence this bead says needs deciding rather than assuming.
close_reason:
FIXED IN ed0873c on e13-sankey-merge.

THE SENTENCE NOW SPLITS THE RIBBONS BEFORE IT GIVES EITHER FACT COUNT, and reports the two documents apart with a total each. FY2025-26 services-and-supplies now reads "14 flows between 15 nodes: 9 citing 29 of the document's 73 facts, and 5 carried unchanged from the chart above, citing 5 of its 120 facts"; Property Taxes "11 flows between 12 nodes: 9 citing 17 of the document's 280 facts, and 2 carried unchanged from the chart above, citing 2 of its 120 facts", the same sentence in both columns; the General Fund at depth 1 "13 flows between 15 nodes: 1 citing 86 of the document's 280 facts, and 12 carried unchanged from the chart above, citing 12 of its 120 facts".

WHY THAT WORDING RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE CLAUSE. The bead asked for the sentence to be decided. Two things decided it. First, the flank is not a footnote: measured over both columns it runs from 1 of 10 ribbons (Licenses & Permits) to 12 of 13 (the General Fund), so a trailing count of flows would have left "from 29 of the document's 73 facts" reading as a claim about all 14 ribbons when it is one about 9 -- the same misattribution one clause over. Splitting the flow count first is what makes each fact count a claim about a stated number of ribbons. Second, the two documents are named by POSITION and not by title, because the client has no title to name them with: sankey, fund-flows and department-spending all carry doc_id livermore-budget-fy2026-2027, and metadata.sources distinguishes them only by page list (pp.66-67 / pp.127-140 and 167-170 / eleven scattered pages of pp.85-125), which will not fit a counts line. The two totals -- 73 against 120, 280 against 120 -- are what let a reader see which figure came from where, which was the owner's stated purpose for naming them.

THE PARTITION IS BY THE STEM A CARRIED MARK RECORDS, NOT BY THE FLAG, which the bead's proposed shape would have got wrong. The fund and division windows keep a flank of the SAME document they draw, so excluding anything carried would have stopped counting 1 ribbon at depth 2 and 1 at each of the 23 division views. title: The spine must declare its column order before any root step can keep a flank
description:
The spine declares no RenderTiers, and export.validateSteps now refuses a kept
flank against a chart drawn whole -- so no ROOT step of index.html can declare
a window until the spine declares its column order.

MEASURED AT 5acce4b. pkg/cmd/export/data.go's spine view sets no RenderTiers
and dist/index.html carries no "render_tiers" key. site/app.js:2753 aligns on
tiers.indexOf(d.tier) only while activeTiers() is non-empty and otherwise hands
the graph to D3.sankeyJustify, so a document drawn whole has no DECLARED column
order at all -- which is why validateSteps refuses `Keep` there rather than
guessing a side. Lane B's own refusal-table case "a window on a page whose chart
is drawn whole" is that arm.

WHAT THIS COSTS THE LANES THAT DECLARE WINDOWS. fisc-ko1j.19 (the revenue
category, Keep 2 / Tiers {1,0,2}), .21 (the object category, Keep 2 / Tiers
{2,5,4}) and .22 (the fund group, Keep 0 / Tiers {0,2,3}) all hang off the
spine's own chart, so each needs RenderTiers []int{0, 2, 5} on the spine view in
the same commit. In the spine's order 0,2,5 every one of those windows is
adjacent as declared: the revenue category keeps the group column to its right,
the object category keeps it to its left, and the fund group keeps the category
column to its left.

AND IT IS NOT FREE, WHICH IS THE PART TO MEASURE FIRST. The spine's document
carries exactly tiers 0, 2 and 5 (12, 6 and 7 nodes, measured off
dist/data/sankey.json), so foldDocument would fold nothing -- but the ALIGNMENT
changes from d3's sankeyJustify to tiers.indexOf, and nothing here has measured
whether the drawn spine moves. tools/jscheck/layout.mjs pins the spine's
geometry; run it before assuming this is a no-op, and if the layout does move,
that movement belongs in its own commit rather than inside a window lane.

THE ALTERNATIVE, IF THE LAYOUT MOVES: teach the arm to place a kept flank
against the parent DOCUMENT's own tier order when the parent declares none.
validateSteps holds the built projection bytes already. It is more code and a
weaker declaration -- the column order would then be an accident of the document
rather than something a caller said -- so it is the second choice, not the
first.

Lanes D, F and G may declare RenderTiers in their own commits; it does NOT need one of its own.

TWO THINGS IT DOES BREAK, both prose rather than geometry, and each belongs to whichever lane declares RenderTiers first.

ONE: site/app.js:2746-2752 says "The spine is drawn whole and keeps sankeyJustify exactly, which is why the crossing figures pinned in tools/jscheck do not move." The conclusion survives; the REASON stops being true the moment the spine declares a tier set. Rewrite the sentence to say the figures were measured equal under both aligners, and drop the clause that makes sankeyJustify load-bearing.

TWO, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH CATCHING: tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's own layout() helper HARDCODES .nodeAlign(app.d3.sankeyJustify) (~:42), while taking every other constant off the page precisely so a harness cannot drift into checking a chart the page does not draw -- its own comment at :30-34 says so. removes that by construction, matches the model's own words, lets the kept flank
carry a capped tail or a residual, and keeps filterLinks' fail-closed guards
applicable because the drawn chart is a well-formed document.

Each half is capped and folded SEPARATELY, so foldDocument never sees two
documents' parent chains at once -- the invariant carryResidual already
preserves at :2230-2250 -- and the halves are then spliced on the centre. The
centre's node record comes from the ON-SCREEN chart.

  - windowFor and the splice.
  - carried_from set on the kept flank where absent, NEVER cleared; and
    carriedSource() (:3130) resolving BY STEM rather than the hardcoded
    docAt(0). Its comment says "Only step 0 carries a residual, so one accessor
    covers every carried mark" -- every window carries a flank, so this is the
    day carried_from's own comment at :2205-2215 anticipated. Without it a
    depth-2 carried mark's caveatsFor/caveatHref resolve against the spine: a
    badge that silently links to the wrong document. fisc-bccu one rung deeper.

    docAt(depth). Its comment's argument -- which step opens it is a question
    about that node, its tier and its role -- survives; only the document it is
    asked of changes.

    A kept-flank fund group is carried AND MUST OPEN; that is the whole feature.
    A blanket "carried => not drillable" is the obvious wrong simplification, so
    the jscheck pins both sides in one check.
  - openableColumns (:1717) SORTS ASCENDING to name columns left to right. That
    is now wrong on {2,5,4} and produces a hint telling a reader to click the
    wrong column. It reads activeTiers() in declaration order, and

    openable columns currently read "the left-hand or middle or right-hand
    column".
  - the partition link flag in linkClass (:1994), the tooltip and
    nodeDescription, parallel to contra.

labelOfRung's comment (:1782) resolves a rung's label from the document one
depth up BECAUSE opening a node removed it. That premise dies here: rewrite the
comment, do not delete it.

title: Lane B: After becomes a list and DrillStep declares its kept flank
description:
fisc-ko1j.12 made Steps a TREE read by key: After names ONE earlier step, and
validateSteps places From in that one parent's Tiers. The window model needs two
things that shape cannot express.

ONE: A STEP IS REACHABLE FROM SEVERAL CHARTS. A fund group is clickable on the
spine, in the revenue-category window ([lines | category | fund groups]) and in
the object-category window ([fund groups | category | divisions]), and all three
open the same chart. After becomes []string.

THE CYCLE ARGUMENT SURVIVES VERBATIM, which is why this is safe: every entry
must name an EARLIER step, so every parent chain strictly decreases and
terminates in at most len(Steps) hops. A cycle stays UNDECLARABLE rather than
detected, which is the property export.go:476-478 is about, and a step still
cannot name itself -- the guard that stops the Patrol-into-Patrol loop
site/app.js:330-336 records.

TWO: A STEP MUST DECLARE WHICH FLANK IT KEEPS. DrillStep gains
Keep []int -- A SLICE AND NOT AN INT, because tier 0 is a real tier and its zero
value cannot mean absent. That is this project's absent-is-not-zero rule at the
seam. At most one entry; validateSteps refuses two.

  len(Keep) == 0  today's semantics, byte for byte: filter, cap, fold, the
                  opened node filtered away.
  len(Keep) == 1  a window.

validateSteps' arms, each stating a property of the model rather than a taste:
  - the placement arm and the same-tiers arm run ONCE PER PREDECESSOR. From must
    be a tier of EVERY chart the step claims to open from -- stronger than
    today, and the right refusal: a step reachable from a chart whose columns do
    not include its From is a rung nothing can reach.
  - uniqueness becomes uniqueness over the (after, from, role) CROSS PRODUCT.
  - rootOutsideRenderTiers tests slices.Contains(s.After, "").
  - Keep[0] must be in every predecessor's tier set, and ADJACENT to From in
    that parent's column order. The SIGN of that adjacency is what tells the
    client which way the window pushes -- declared and positional, not a
    tier-number inference of the kind paintBreadcrumb's comment refuses.
  - len(Tiers) == 3 with From in the middle and Keep[0] at the end the adjacency
    names. The window becomes a property of the type.
  - Side and Keep together are REFUSED. A window's side is both sides, one per
    half, so a step declaring each would be two declarations of one thing.

TIERS IS NOW A COLUMN ORDER AND MAY BE NON-MONOTONIC. {2,5,4} is legal and
necessary. layOut's nodeAlign = tiers.indexOf(d.tier) (site/app.js:2760) is
ALREADY declaration-order rather than sorted, which is the single fact that
makes the whole design cheap; say so where it is now load-bearing.

THE TRAP IS THE HARNESS PARSER. tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's parseStepShapes
(~:720-788) reads After:\s*"..." and cross-checks entry count against From: and
Key: markers. A list literal makes After silently default to "" -- every step
read as a root, and drill.mjs measuring a tree the site does not ship. That is
the same class of defect the function's own comment at :724-731 records. Rewrite
it here, keep the two independent markers, give Keep the same required/absent
discipline Key and After have, and have seam.mjs drive it over literals data.go
does not contain, including a reflowed After and a Keep on its own line.

build timestamp -- lane D's proof at 096962a.

title: Lane A: the revenue-line rollup, so a category can be the centre of a window
description:
The window model puts the clicked node in the CENTRE column, and a revenue
category can only be the centre if something flows INTO it. Nothing does:
fund-flows carries (1,3) line->fund links and (0,3) for the eight tier-0 nodes
with no lines, and no (1,0) link at all. tier 0 and tier 1 are two grains over
the same money.

WHAT TO EMIT. One link per (line, kind) from revenue-line/<slug> to its parent
revenue/<category>, value the sum of that line's own printed cells, carrying
every one of their fact_ids, kind the cells' kind, derived FALSE.

PER KIND AND NOT PER LINE. A revenue line can reach funds under two kinds --
external into most funds, internal_service into the five ISF funds, which
site/app.js:2545-2553 records. One rollup per line collides two kinds on one
pair and checkDistinctLinks fires. Same rule foldDocument uses: one ribbon per
kind between a folded pair.

PUBLISHED, NOT SYNTHESISED IN THE CLIENT. A published link is held by
link-values-tie-to-facts, link-locators-match-their-facts,
link-kinds-match-their-facts, graph-acyclic, fund-flows-counts-reconcile and a
byte-for-byte golden; a client-side sum is held by one jscheck. capColumn and
carryResidual are precedents for client-side derivation only where the claim
cannot live in a document -- the cap is about this page's pixel budget and the
residual is a statement about a PAIR of documents. A rollup over printed rows is
neither. It is the tier-3 -> tier-4 rule (internal/project/fundflows.go:371-395)
applied a second time.

IT DRAWS NOTHING NEW, and that is the lane's proof rather than its hope.
Verified by reading: at {0,3,4} the link folds to a self-loop and foldDocument
drops it (site/app.js:2540); at {1,3} the tier-0 end is not placeable and
filterLinks drops it through scoped's quiet branch. So every per-view pin in
tools/jscheck/drill.mjs must be UNMOVED, and that must be ASSERTED rather than
observed.

MEASURED 2026-09-13 against dist/data/, both published years: each of the ten
revenue categories' line sum equals the spine's category cell to the cent.
Property Taxes is 14 lines summing to 69,459,414 = 64,143,762 general +
5,315,652 special-revenue. transfers/in (480,400 / 486,735 short) and
fund-balance/draw (nothing beneath it) do not tie and are exactly the two nodes
the role gate already closes.

WHAT MOVES: counts.links, counts.facts_cited_twice, the four fund-flows
goldens, and the mixed-grain-double-counts caveat, which names one overlap today
and must name two.

MUTATION: emit per line instead of per (line, kind) -> checkDistinctLinks red on
the ISF lines. Drop one line's zero cells from the rollup's fact_ids ->
link-values-tie-to-facts red.

Emitting one rollup per line trips nothing. So the lane had to widen the pair rule to (source, target, kind) in checkDistinctLinks AND in sortLinks -- sort.Slice is not stable, so a pair with two ribbons and no tie-break is byte-unstable -- and in docs/sankey-contract.md's determinism sentence. title: addParents invents a published node for any revenue/ or fund-group/ suffix, so a category slug nothing declares ships as a tier-0 box
description:
internal/project/fundflows.go, addParents. Both on-demand arms match on PREFIX
ONLY:

  case strings.HasPrefix(p.parent, prefixFundGroup):  -> builds the node
  case strings.HasPrefix(p.parent, prefixRevenue):    -> builds the node
  default:                                            -> refuses by name

So `revenue/typo` and `fund-group/typo` are each built as a published node with
a label slugged from the suffix, and only a parent matching neither prefix is
refused. The registry is never asked whether the slug is a declared category or
fund group, although data/taxonomy.yaml and data/funds.yaml both know.

AGENTS.md's rule for this package is that every guard stays a refusal and not a
skip: a fact this document cannot place is a mapping defect, and inventing a box
for it publishes a city with a category the city does not have. The default arm
is written to that rule. The two arms above it are not.

MEASURED by lane C's third mutation (2026-09-12), parenting one line at
revenue/typo: the projection builds the phantom, node-tiers-are-declared counts
1021 nodes against 1017 and reports nothing -- correctly, since declaredTier
cuts at the first slash and `revenue/typo` IS tier 0 by that form -- and
node-hierarchy-well-formed stays green because the node it points at now exists.

WHAT GUARDS IT TODAY, and what does not. fisc-ko1j.10's
revenue-lines-tie-to-their-categories arm 2 catches the revenue case at verify
time, by requiring a line's parent to equal revenue/ + the category taxonomy.yaml
declares that line under. That is why this is P2 and not P1. But it is caught
after publication rather than refused at build, it is one document's check
rather than the projection's own invariant, and THE FUND-GROUP ARM HAS NO
EQUIVALENT -- fundEndpoint asks data/funds.yaml for the fund's type, so today
the only parent reaching that arm is a type funds.yaml itself supplied, which
makes the arm unreachable-by-construction rather than guarded. A second caller
is all it would take.

THE FIX is for both arms to resolve the slug and refuse when it is absent,
leaving the default arm as it is. Prove it can fail with the mutation above:
the projection must refuse by name where today it builds.
notes: 2026-09-17, L3.4: revenue-lines-tie-to-their-categories was kept precisely because its arm 2 is the guard this bead relies on; nothing in internal/structure makes that claim. The P2-not-P1 reasoning here still holds.

title: A tier-1 line with no parent is DROPPED by filterToNode, not refused, and the ribbon it folded into grows by its value
description:
Found by mutation while landing fisc-ko1j.9 (lane B). site/app.js only.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, over testdata/fund-flows.golden.json through the shipped
entry points:

  as published:    revenue/taxes/property -> fund/100 = 6414376200 over 13 facts
  parent blanked:  revenue/taxes/property -> fund/100 = 7931876200 over 12 facts

Blanking revenue-line/taxes/property/eraf's parent and opening
fund-group/general at {0,3,4} draws Property Taxes at $79,318,762 against the
$64,143,762 p127 prints -- $15,175,000 too high, because ERAF is a CONTRA row
and dropping it removes a negative. Node and link counts are unchanged (34 / 33
both ways), so nothing on the page looks different.

WHY THE REFUSAL DOES NOT FIRE. foldDocument does refuse a node it cannot place,
and over the whole document it does: "cannot draw fund-flows: node
revenue-line/taxes/property/eraf is tier 1 and no ancestor of it is a tier this
page draws (0, 3, 4)". But a rung filters first, and filterToNode's own
placeability test -- `foldTarget(byID, src, drawn) !== ""` on both ends -- drops
the link before the fold ever sees the node. The comment there calls a dropped
link "one the declared tier set has no column for, which is a statement the view
made when it declared them"; that is true of a tier the view left out and false
of a node whose parent chain is BROKEN, and the two are indistinguishable to
that test.

NOT REACHABLE FROM THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTS TODAY: internal/project always sets a
line's parent from the cell it was netted from, so this needs a hand-edited or
third-party fund-flows.json. fisc-ko1j.10's second arm (every tier-1 node's
parent is revenue/ + its own category segment, and that node exists at tier 0)
is what keeps it unreachable at verify time -- so it is load-bearing rather than
a refinement.

A FIX HAS TO TELL THE TWO CASES APART. Candidate: filterToNode drops a link
whose end folds to nothing only when that end has NO parent chain to follow at
all by design (a flow endpoint), and refuses by name when the chain exists and
breaks. Belongs with lane E (fisc-ko1j.11), which is already rewriting
filterToNode's neighbourhood, with the jscheck arm in the same commit.
close_reason:
Fixed at 8372396, in site/app.js's scoped(), which both filters now consult in place of the bare 'foldTarget(...) !== ""' placeability test.

THE TWO CASES ARE TOLD APART, which is what this bead asked for. A parent naming a node the document does not carry is refused outright. title: The taxonomy goes recursive, and pp.127-140's 101 printed revenue lines get slugs
description:
LANE A OF E13's REVENUE SIDE, and it exists because fisc-ko1j.8's answer collided
with a validator that bead does not anticipate. internal/registry and
internal/check only; no projection, no client.

## Why this is not just "add 102 entries"

data/taxonomy.yaml is validated ONE LEVEL DEEP, hard, in two places:
internal/registry/load.go:588 refuses a slug with more than one parent segment,
and validateParent (load.go:719-745) refuses a parent that is itself a child.
load_test.go:372 pins the refusal for taxes/property/secured BY NAME. A line item
under taxes/property is a grandchild and cannot load.

DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-12: the taxonomy becomes RECURSIVE, arbitrary
depth. Not two levels, and not a second data file -- so a further breakdown (the
object categories under a division, say) never needs another file either.

## Recursive is FEWER rules than today, measured

validateParent computes the expected parent with strings.Cut(c.Slug, "/"), which
cuts at the FIRST slash. Cut at the LAST slash instead and the rule becomes "a
slug's parent is the slug minus its last segment", which is recursive. Then
DELETE the segment-count arm at load.go:588 and the grandchild arm at
load.go:740-744.

IT IS PROVABLY A NO-OP ON TODAY'S FILE: all 38 existing categories are depth <= 1,
and at depth 1 the first-slash and last-slash cuts are the same string. The
mutation is the proof -- the change must move no test that does not concern depth.

CYCLES ARE IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION and this is worth stating in the comment
rather than checking: a parent slug is a strict prefix of its child's and so is
strictly shorter, so no cycle can be spelled.

## The 102

MEASURED 2026-09-12 off facts/facts.jsonl: 102 distinct (row_path, row_label)
pairs over all 924 revenue-by-fund facts, and no row_label maps to more than one
category. Per category: charges-for-services 21, taxes/other 15,
licenses-and-permits 15, miscellaneous-revenue 14, taxes/property 14,
intergovernmental 7, use-of-money-and-property 7, fines-and-forfeitures 3,
contributions-outsourced 2, taxes/sales 2, other-financing-sources 1,
transfers/in 1.

A line entry REUSES EXISTING FIELDS -- slug, label, parent, and document_term for
the printed row_label, which the file already publishes verbatim -- with aliases:
for a re-typeset row. No new field and no new file.

## Two paragraphs of the header become false and are rewritten

- "deliberately NOT used below the ten revenue categories ... Those detail lines
  are a rule's label, not a category. Giving each one a slug would invent a
  classification the city does not make and would double the surface on which two
  spellings of the same thing can drift apart." The answer to the first half is
  that a slug NAMES a printed row rather than classifying it; the answer to the
  second is the check below, which refuses drift in both directions.
- "Every parent node below is therefore our grouping, not the city's ... each is
  derived: true and assignable: false". pp.66-67 PRINT taxes/property itself, so
  a parent may now be assignable. No validator enforces this -- it is prose only,
  confirmed by reading load.go -- which is exactly why it has to be corrected by
  hand.

## The check: fact-revenue-lines-resolve

internal/check/revenuelines.go, shaped on factDepartmentsResolve. BOTH DIRECTIONS,
and either alone is fail-open:
  - every revenue-by-fund fact of kind revenue resolves (Category, RowLabel) to
    exactly one entry -- an unresolved row is one the projection must refuse at
    build time, and this says so before anyone builds;
  - every declared entry is printed by at least one fact -- an unprinted entry is
    a node nothing can ever draw.

REGISTRATION IS FIVE EDITS. Read the counts off a rebuilt ./bin/fisc verify run,
not off this bead.

## Authoring 102 entries reviewably

Generate from facts/facts.jsonl -- fisc build has already proved each string is at
its offset -- selecting the scope and kind, emitting (category, row_label, page,
offset), unique on the pair, ordered by first (page, offset) so the file reads in
PRINTED ORDER and its diff is one row per printed row against pp.127-140. The
generating command goes in the commit message verbatim.

THE SLUG RULE IS STATED IN THE HEADER AND DELIBERATELY NOT ENFORCED against the
label. Enforcing slug == slugify(label) would make identity content-dependent
again, which is the thing the owner refused in choosing authored slugs over a
slugified row_label.

THREE WITNESSES, NOT ONE: a test that every entry's label is a label: under the
same category: in mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml and back (registry
vs rules, at go test time); the check above (registry vs facts, at fisc verify
time); and a page test over testdata/pages mirroring the departments one
(registry vs the printed page).

## Acceptance

Green: the registry loads and the check passes over the corpus. Red: delete an
entry -> the check names the facts that no longer resolve. Add an entry nothing
prints -> the check names it. Re-point an entry's parent -> the mapping test and
both check arms go red. And the recursion change alone, with no entries added,
moves no test that is not about depth.

Filed 2026-09-12 from fisc-ko1j.8's answer.
notes:
2026-09-12, measured off the tree at d439acb while working fisc-ko1j.9.

THE TITLE'S 102 IS STALE AND THE COMMIT THAT CLOSED THIS BEAD ALREADY SAID SO.
The count is 101 printed revenue lines, over 141 taxonomy entries (40 categories
+ 101 lines) and 139 distinct (row, page) claims. Read off the registry pins at
internal/registry/registry_test.go:368,795,799 and
internal/check/revenuelines_test.go:277,282, not off either plan document. 102
is the distinct (row_path, row_label) count over ALL revenue-by-fund facts,
which includes ("transfers/in", "Transfers In") whose kind is transfer_in and
which is not a line -- lane B keeps transfers/in at tier 0.

Lane B confirms the 101 from the other side: fund-flows FY2025-26 adopted
publishes 93 tier-1 nodes, the other 8 declared lines printing a dash in every
fund of that column.
close_reason: Landed in d439acb. validateParent cuts at the last slash; the segment-count and grandchild arms are gone; measured no-op on the 40 committed entries (one subtest moved, from a depth message to the grammar one). 101 line entries generated from facts.jsonl (not 102: the transfer_in row is not a line), spliced under their categories in printed order with #@cite lines. fact-revenue-lines-resolve checks both directions; page test and mapping test are the other two witnesses. Mutations all red for their stated reasons; re-pointing parent alone is refused by the loader first, so that mutation moves slug and parent together. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 vacuous, 1 skipped.

title: The inferred list says the residual carries 2 flows and then lists 1, and prints the same derived link twice
description:
WRONG-OUTPUT at the low end, or DESIGN -- the rule is pre-existing and the residual is what made it visible.

site/app.js buildDerivedList (~:5195) counts only DERIVED links touching a derived node -- `links = projection.links.filter((l) => l.derived)` -- and the sentence does not say that is what it is counting.

MEASURED 2026-09-23 by driving the shipped site/app.js over fisc export's bytes at ebdb422, 'What we inferred' with fund-group/general opened:

  FY2025-26  the residual's entry reads 'Carried, not computed: 2 flows of the chart above with figures and citations unchanged -- FY 2025-2027 Budget Book p.66.' immediately followed by '1 flow totalling $1,034,154: Fund Balance Draw -> Not broken down by fund'. Both sentences are true of different sets -- 2 carried ribbons (fund-balance/draw and transfers/in), of which 1 is derived -- and they sit two lines apart with nothing distinguishing them. A reader takes the second as a correction of the first.
  FY2026-27  the residual carries one ribbon (transfers/in, printed), so its entry is the 'Carried, not computed: 1 flow' sentence alone; the shape does not arise there today.

TWO MORE CONSEQUENCES OF THE SAME RULE, both measured on the FY2025-26 rung:
  - the one derived link is ALSO listed under the carried endpoint node (Fund Balance Draw: '1 flow totalling $1,034,154: Fund Balance Draw -> Not broken down by fund'), so it appears twice in one list;
  - a capped tail ('N smaller funds', 'N smaller divisions') gets no flows line at all, because its links are printed rather than derived.

WHY IT IS FILED AND NOT FIXED: the fix is a decision about what the inferred list counts -- derived links, or every link the derived mark carries -- and that rule governs the aggregate, the gap and the residual together. Changing it moves drill.mjs's pinned wording. Related: fisc-rgzz and fisc-dzby, the other two reader-facing questions about this node.

title: carryResidual returns the drawn chart unchanged when a document-switching step ships no residual, and the unreconciled figure draws in silence
description:

What would settle it is a Go-side guarantee that a step carrying Projection always ships Residual -- and note fisc-hbqu measured the opposite direction (residual ids naming no node are accepted by validate, and the client's rule is that an unmatched residual draws nothing, so a typo is already silent).

notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-20 AGAINST THE TREE: THE CLIENT-SIDE HALF OF THIS BEAD IS GONE AND THE QUESTION MOVED TO GO. carryResidual no longer gates on step.residual at all -- fisc-phtp.2 made it `if (!mark || !from) return drawn;`, where mark is the residual export.ResidualOf answered for this rung. The UNPROVEN half this bead named is now the whole of it.

AND THE COUPLING IT WARNED ABOUT IS ALREADY SPENT: drill.mjs's residual arm no longer deletes step.residual to make the node vanish -- it takes the mark out of the served answer instead, which is the same perturbation one language over. A fix on the Go side no longer has to move that check.
