title: A step document's caveat has no link at depth 1: caveatHref resolves through the spine year's refs
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 in fisc-ko1j.3, over the merged chain fisc-ko1j.4 declares, through tools/jscheck/harness.mjs: open the spine into fund-group/general (fund-flows at {0,3,4}), pin fund/100. caveatsFor(fund/100) returns only-the-general-fund-is-decomposed -- correct, it reads the DRAWN document's metadata.caveats -- and caveatHref of that id returns "", so pin() renders the summary with no 'Read it in full' link.

WHY. caveatHref looks the id up in shownYear.caveats, which are the YEAR's refs: the packager builds them per (document, caveat) from the view's own projection, and on the merged page that is the spine. A step document's caveats are never in that list, so at depth >= 1 over a switched document every caveat on a mark loses its link, silently -- caveatHref returns "" by design when a site has no caveats page, and this is indistinguishable from that.

NOT FIXED IN fisc-ko1j.3 because the fix is the packager's: caveatHref's own comment refuses to compose the anchor client-side ('rebuilding the fragment here would be a second speller of a rule internal/export owns'). The per-year step join fisc-ko1j.4 writes in place of yearStems is where the step document's caveat refs can be shipped beside the year's -- one list per (year, depth), or the step's refs merged into the year's with the stem the anchor is composed from.

Today's shipped pages are unaffected: revenue.html and spending.html draw one document, so the year's refs ARE the step's. This bites on the first merged page.
close_reason: Fixed in 8c53b4a by the per-year step join: the packager ships each year's steps entries (stem, path, caveat refs composed per (stem, caveat)) and app.js's caveatHref reads the rung document's refs at depth >= 1 instead of the year's. Witnessed both sides: TestEachYearOpensIntoItsOwnStepDocumentWithItsOwnCaveatLinks pins the anchor per year and step, and drill.mjs pins the depth-1 href as caveats.html#caveat-fund-flows--only-the-general-fund-is-decomposed with the panel's 'Read it in full' present. Mutations: caveatRefs dropped from stepDocuments -> Go test red on all four (year, step) pairs; caveatHref reading shownYear.caveats at every depth -> drill.mjs red with href ''.

title: The chain becomes a tree: two openable tiers at one depth
description:
E13's chain is a LINE and the revenue side makes it a TREE. This is the seam
change that costs, and it is filed separately because fisc-ko1j.2 freezes the
type it changes.

## What the line cannot express

At depth 0 a reader could open a fund group (tier 2) or a revenue category
(tier 0), and the two go to different places. fisc-ko1j.2 declares

  type DrillStep struct { From int; Projection string; Tiers []int; ... }
  View.Steps []DrillStep

with ONE From per step, and validate's walkability arm -- Steps[0].From in
RenderTiers, Steps[i].From in Steps[i-1].Tiers -- reads Steps as a path. Two
openable tiers at one depth is not a longer path; it is a second edge out of the
same node, and []DrillStep as declared has nowhere to put it.

DO NOT SOLVE THIS BY ADDING A SECOND VIEW. That is revenue.html again, which is
what E13's end condition retires.

## The decision this bead owns

WHETHER THE REVENUE STEP EXISTS AT DEPTH 1 AS WELL AS DEPTH 0.

At depth 1 a fund group is already open. Clicking a revenue category there means
TWO constraints at once -- this group AND this category -- which is a filter
that ACCUMULATES rather than replaces, and is a third thing again beside
filterToNode and fisc-ko1j.11's source-side sibling. Every filter in the client
today replaces.

DEPTH 0 ONLY IS A LEGITIMATE AND MUCH CHEAPER ANSWER, and it is probably the
right one: at depth 1 the chart is already tiers {0,3,4}, so the reader can see
which funds a category feeds without opening anything. Say which, and say why.

## The rungs

paintBreadcrumb, labelOf and paintChartName all compose rungs assuming one path,
and fisc-ko1j.3 rewrites all three for a stack. State what a breadcrumb reads
when two rungs can sit at one depth -- and what Escape pops, since main's
handler pops one rung and "one rung" is unambiguous only on a line.

restoreFocus focuses bar.children[0], which fisc-ko1j.3 already notes is the
outermost rung rather than the one the reader came from; a branch makes that
worse rather than differently wrong.

## Acceptance

The walk is by mouse AND by keyboard, in light and dark: open a fund group,
Escape, open a revenue category, Escape, and confirm the breadcrumb, counts
line, legend and flow table each describe the chart actually on screen at every
rung -- including the two different depth-1 charts.
notes:
2026-09-14, measured against 99472f6: THIS BEAD'S SEAM CHANGE HAS ALREADY LANDED AND ITS DECISION IS ALREADY SETTLED. Both sections above are stale as statements about the tree; they are kept as the record of why the shape is what it is.

THE SEAM. "What the line cannot express" says []DrillStep has nowhere to put a second edge out of one node. It has: internal/export/export.go:503 declares `After []string`, and the walkability arm the bead quotes -- Steps[0].From in RenderTiers, Steps[i].From in Steps[i-1].Tiers -- no longer exists (grep for Steps[i-1] and Steps[0] in export.go returns nothing). The tree landed across d439acb..096962a.

THE DECISION. "Whether the revenue step exists at depth 1 as well as depth 0" is answered DEPTH 0 ONLY -- pkg/cmd/export/data.go:776 ships `After: []string{""}` on the revenue-category step, and the same is true of object-category. So the accumulating filter the bead feared was never written, and every filter in the client still replaces. That is the cheaper answer the bead itself predicted was probably right.

WHAT IS STILL LIVE, and all of it is the acceptance walk rather than the seam: the mouse-and-keyboard walk in light and dark, plus the two items in the 2026-09-13 note (the partition ribbon against a derived and a contra one, now that fisc-ko1j.21 has shipped one; and paintChartHint's three-openable-columns sentence read aloud).

This bead is now the parent of a nine-wave drill-down expansion lane agreed with the owner 2026-09-14: N-column windows, a reader-facing column budget, a gesture split (double click expands, single click focuses), an affordance for what opens, expanding a capped column, and two new projections (transfers-by-fund, department-funding-sources). The waves are filed as children.
close_reason: Closed against this bead's own 2026-09-14 note, re-verified: the seam landed across d439acb..096962a. internal/export/export.go declares After []string and its comment at :258 states that two openable tiers at one depth are what After expresses; the walkability arm the bead quoted no longer exists.

title: The client opens a revenue category
description:
site/app.js and tools/jscheck, in ONE commit. This lane runs under fisc-rx1d's
rule, so the jscheck is listed here rather than discovered by a review pass.

## The comment that becomes false

drillable's doc comment argues today that "offering to open a revenue category
would promise a decomposition the document does not carry". After fisc-ko1j.9
the document DOES carry it. REWRITE THE COMMENT, DO NOT DELETE IT: drillable
rests on the claim, and the same species of rewrite is what fisc-ko1j.3 requires
of drilledInto's one-hop premise. Its "ONE TIER AND NO OTHER" clause is
separately wrong once fisc-ko1j.12 lands.

## A source-side filter, if fisc-ko1j.8 picked the child model

filterToNode's rule is TARGET IN THE SUBTREE, BOTH ENDS PLACEABLE, and its doc
comment states the asymmetry deliberately: the source side is kept as context.
A revenue category has nothing pointing at it, so filterToNode returns an empty
graph -- with no error, because the id IS known and the guard that would fire on
an unknown one does not. d3-sankey then dies on the empty graph with "RangeError:
Invalid array length", which is the failure that function's own comment records.

A source column needs reachability over LINKS, which is a different notion of
"inside" from ancestry. So it is a filterFromNode SIBLING and not a parameter on
filterToNode -- the two disagree about what the word means, and one function
answering both questions is how a caller gets the wrong one.

If fisc-ko1j.8 picked the target model, none of this is needed and the lane is
the comment rewrite plus the three traps below.

## Three traps, each already recorded somewhere in the file

- capColumn RANKS BY INFLOW ONLY: its size map is keyed on l.target. A source
  column must rank by outflow, or the cap keeps the wrong lines. THE CAP IS
  NEEDED, measured 2026-09-08: fund/100 charges-for-services is 18 nonzero rows,
  taxes/other 14, licenses-and-permits 14, taxes/property 13.
- THE COLOUR. fundGroupOf returns "" for a tier-0 revenue node BY DESIGN --
  "money arriving, not money held" -- and callers treat "" as no categorical
  slot, which is what --muted means. So a line-item column and its aggregate
  draw grey among coloured siblings: verbatim the defect capColumn's own comment
  records as already fixed once for the fund aggregate, whose parent was ""
  before. Decide what hue a source column has BEFORE writing the fold, because
  the fix there was to re-point the parent and a line item's parent is a revenue
  node with no hue either.
- THE AGGREGATE ID. fisc-ko1j.3 already makes AGGREGATE_ID per-tier for the two
  spending caps. A revenue cap is a third, at a tier those two do not use;
  confirm the per-tier scheme covers it rather than assuming it.

## The jscheck owed, same commit

- A revenue category opened through the REAL entry points, not by calling the
  filter -- the drill's defect history is checks that measured the chart already
  there.
- The cap engaging on fund/100 charges-for-services, and inert where it should
  be.
- The aggregate marked derived, with a rationale, a source note and its folds.
- No 100%-of-column share: a category whose lines are one row would otherwise
  draw a column of one, which columnShare's guard already handles for the fund
  column and has to be shown to handle here.
- Any new selector declared in seam.mjs's KNOWN_SELECTORS, or the
  undeclared-selector arm goes red by name.
notes:
2026-09-10, lane 3 (fisc-ko1j.3): THE LEGEND IS EMPTY ON EVERY OPENED VIEW BY RULE (buildLegend returns after clearing when drilled.length > 0). Reason: an opened view is one node's subtree, every mark resolves to the one fund group above it, and the swatch is a toggle on a NODE id that setIsolated dims against -- a swatch for a group not drawn would dim the whole chart. A revenue category's subtree spans groups, so this bead is where that rule has to change, and the isolation it rests on has to become per-group (fundGroupOf) rather than per-node before a legend at depth 1 can toggle anything. drill.mjs's 'an opened view draws no legend' probe is the arm to retire or rewrite with it.
2026-09-12, re-derived against site/app.js before working it. This bead's three
traps are each partly wrong, and it misses three others.

TRAP (a), capColumn RANKS BY INFLOW: true, and the consequence is overstated. The
source-side REMAP already exists -- app.js remaps both l.source and l.target when
folding into the aggregate -- so only the RANKING is inflow-only. Rank by
max(inflow, outflow), d3-sankey's own node value, which is provably a no-op on
today's columns: every tier-3 fund's outflow is at most its inflow (fund/100:
144,650,802 out of 157,873,470) and a tier-4 division's equals its inflow by
construction, so no depth-1 or depth-2 pin moves. What IS new and this bead does
not name: the tier-3 tail in a CATEGORY view spans fund groups, so its aggregate
must get parent "" while the tier-1 tail is parented to the category. The per-cap
parent becomes an argument.

TRAP (b), THE COLOUR: the premise is wrong for this column. Only fund-group/ ids
ever take a hue (nodeColor, linkColor), so EVERY revenue -> fund ribbon at depth 1
is ALREADY muted today. A line column drawn muted is not "grey among coloured
siblings"; it is what the revenue half of every opened view already looks like.
The real gap is different and is worth its own bead: a category view's fund column
spans fund groups and nothing on it says which fund is in which. Filed.

TRAP (c), THE AGGREGATE ID: confirmed by reading, not assumed. aggregateID(tier)
is already per-tier, so a third cap at tier 1 gets aggregate/tail/1, distinct from
/3 and /4. No change needed; pin it.

THREE TRAPS THIS BEAD MISSES.

- ENDPOINT ROLES AT TIER 0. The spine's transfers/in and fund-balance/draw sit at
  tier 0 beside the revenue categories. Under drillable's "d.tier === step.from"
  they would offer to open into a document that carries nothing beneath them.
  drillable needs a role gate, and the rule is DERIVED rather than hardcoded: a
  revenue node opens iff the drawn column carries a tier-1 node beneath it.
  (transfers/in cannot have lines anyway -- node-hierarchy-well-formed refuses a
  node parented to a flow endpoint.)
- CONTRA ROWS. See fisc-ko1j.9's note. The owner decided 2026-09-12 they draw
  REVERSED at |value| with contra styling and text reading "printed as a reduction
  of Property Taxes". The drawn lines still sum to the spine's net cell.
- SINGLE-LINE CATEGORIES. other-financing-sources has exactly ONE distinct printed
  label citywide, so opening it draws a line column of one. It still opens -- it
  shows which funds carry it -- and columnShare's siblings < 2 guard already
  suppresses the share chip. Pin that case rather than discovering it.

THE LEGEND, answering this bead's 2026-09-10 note: keep it EMPTY on the category
view for this lane, and rewrite the comment rather than the rule. buildLegend's
STATED reason ("every mark resolves to the one fund group above it") is indeed
false for a category view, whose subtree spans groups. But the surviving reason
holds: a swatch toggles setIsolated on a NODE id and no fund-group/ node is in a
{1,3} view. A legend here needs per-group emphasis through fundGroupOf inside
applyEmphasis -- a SECOND emphasis model, which does not belong inside the largest
client change of this epic. Filed as its own bead.

Plan: /home/ubuntu/.claude/plans/fisc-ko1j-7-12-e13-s-revenue-side-inherited-bubble.md
The two beads split out of this lane above are fisc-b4a6 (the muted ribbon / fund column legibility) and fisc-0jy9 (per-group isolation, which is what a legend on an opened view needs). The contra-row sibling found in the same sweep is fisc-9psv.
2026-09-12, FROM LANE D. The seam now declares the tree and does NOT ship it: DrillStep's Key, After, Side and Role are `json:"-"`, because no client reads them and a key on the wire would be a second declaration of a tree nothing walks. internal/export's TestAStepsDocumentIsCitedByThePageThatOpensIt pins that absence, so this lane has to change that test in the same commit as the JSON tags and the client code that reads them -- and declare the revenue step's Side as export.SideSource rather than inferring a source side from tier numbers.
2026-09-12, LANE E LANDED (client + jscheck + seam tags), measured rather than argued.

WHAT THE CLIENT DOES NOW. site/app.js walks the tree by key: stepFor(node) matches a step's after against the rung on screen's key, from against the node's tier, and role against node.role where the step names one; stepAt(depth) is gone and STEPS drops a step with no string key/after (a keyless step matched itself: Patrol opened into Patrol without end under a harness config). filterFromNode is the sibling of filterToNode, both over filterLinks; an empty result is refused by name. The revenue step is declared in data.go: Key revenue-category, After "", From 0, Side export.SideSource, Role revenue_source, Tiers {1,3}, Caps tier 1 at 8 ("lines") and tier 3 at 8 ("funds"). DrillStep's key/after/side/role ship (side and role omitempty); TestAStepsDocumentIsCitedByThePageThatOpensIt pins presence with a second root step, and reverting Side or the cap Tail to json:"-" goes red.

THREE THINGS THIS BEAD'S TEXT DID NOT ANTICIPATE, all measured through the shipped entry point over both goldens:
(1) ONE NOUN CANNOT SERVE TWO TAILS. Both of a category's columns fold on the corpus -- five categories print more than nine lines (charges-for-services 19) and four land in more than nine funds (use-of-money-and-property 34) -- so TierCap gained Tail (json tail,omitempty), the client reads cap.tail || step.tail, and the fund-group step's latent tier-4 cap now says "divisions". parseStepShapes reads the cap Tail and Side spelled as export.SideSource (it read "" for the constant before).
(2) THE FOLD REFUSED A CATEGORY'S FUND TAIL. use-of-money-and-property would not open: its tail of 26 funds spans every group and the five internal-service funds (700-740) take the line's money as internal_service beside external money into the rest, so the cap put two kinds on one (line, tail) pair and foldDocument's kind guard threw. Measured over all four goldens at {0,3,4}, {4,5}, {1,3} and {0,2,5}: NO parent-fold pair carries two kinds, only the cap's value-fold does. foldDocument now merges on (source, target, kind), one ribbon per kind; no shipped ribbon moves and every depth-1/2 pin is unchanged.
(3) "REVERSED" CANNOT BE A REVERSED LINK. A fund->line link gives the line d3 depth 2, the vendored d3-sankey sizes its column count from the deepest node, and a {1,3} view came to three columns with the third empty -- computeNodeLayers throws on the hole. Contra rows draw FORWARD at |value| with class contra (--critical), a U+2212 sign on every figure the mark prints, the sentence "printed as a reduction of Property Taxes" on the link, and contraNote on the fund mark (the General Fund reads gross, $81,129,101, and the note says $64,143,762 net of $16,985,339 -- p127's total). Filed fisc-utzw for a direction cue. By magnitude both contra rows rank inside Property Taxes' top eight, so neither folds into the tail on either column.

THE CAP PARENT IS ASKED OF THE DOCUMENT: a tail is parented to the opened node when every node of its column is inside it (lines, funds under a group, divisions), and "" when the column spans groups (a category's funds). capColumn ranks by max(sum|in|, sum|out|); under inflow every line ties at zero and the eight kept are the first eight ids -- drill.mjs demonstrates inflow would have kept 3 other lines of charges-for-services.

FIGURES PINNED IN tools/jscheck/drill.mjs COLUMNS[].category, both years: Property Taxes 14 nodes / 12 links / 0 sub-pixel, counts "12 flows between 14 nodes, from 17 of the document's 280 facts"; all ten categories open (contributions 7/5/0 in FY2026, 6/4/0 in FY2027; intergovernmental's tail 10 then 9 smaller funds). The single-line category (no adopted column prints one; other-financing-sources is not a spine category) is a built probe: it opens, the line gets no share chip, the two funds do; a category with no lines is refused by name. fisc-ng17 fixed in scoped(): ERAF's parent blanked, or naming a missing node, stops the fund-group drill with a banner naming the node; as published Property Taxes -> fund/100 draws 6414376200.

NO BROWSER IN THE SESSION'S ENVIRONMENT: the walk of dist/index.html was done by driving the SHIPPED dist config and data files through the harness stub, both years (open a group, Escape, open Property Taxes, Escape, open Use of Money, Escape), and each rung's breadcrumb, counts line, legend, hint and table read as the chart on screen. The mouse-and-keyboard walk in light and dark is fisc-ko1j.12's acceptance and is still owed by a session with a browser.

2026-09-13, REVIEWED AND LANDED at 8372396 (branch e13-sankey-merge), 11 files, +1,257/-177.

title: A check that line items tie to their category, and that no fact reaches the reader twice
description:
internal/check only. What the line-item tier makes checkable, and what it makes
newly breakable.

## The arithmetic it asserts

Per (kind, category, fund_group), the tier-1 links must sum to the spine's cell.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 off facts/facts.jsonl -- an independent path to the figure
fisc-ko1j took off the two goldens, and it reproduces. At FY2026 adopted there
are 30 NONZERO (kind, category, fund_group) cells across all-funds-gross and
revenue-by-fund, and 29 are equal to the cent. The one exception is

  (transfer_in, transfers/in, general)   spine 480,400   detail 0

Counting all cells including printed zeros gives 68 pairs, 67 equal -- the same
result on a different basis. WHICHEVER BASIS THE CHECK USES, ITS FINDINGS MUST
SAY WHICH, because the two counts are both true and a reader comparing them
against fisc-ko1j's link-level 30 will otherwise read a contradiction.

SHARE revenueDetailRestriction's EXISTING EXCEPTION rather than re-declaring it.
internal/check/revenuedetail.go already carries that one exception with its
reason -- pp.127-130 print no General Fund Transfers In row, and it is handed
off to transfers-by-fund. A second copy is the drift fisc-ko1j.1 declares its
residual node set as a constant to avoid.

## Two arms the tier makes possible and nothing covers today

- EVERY TIER-1 NODE'S parent RESOLVES TO A TIER-0 CATEGORY. Without it a line
  item whose parent is misspelled folds to nothing and vanishes from the {0,3}
  view, which fisc-ko1j.9's fold test catches only if the fold refuses rather
  than drops.
- IF fisc-ko1j.8 PICKED THE TARGET MODEL, the tier-0 -> tier-1 and tier-1 ->
  tier-3 links over one fact are DECLARED rather than accidental. A fact cited
  on two links is the shape fisc-gxa.2 already publishes as
  counts.facts_cited_twice on the expenditure side; unchecked, it is
  indistinguishable from a double-count.

hierarchyTiers in internal/check/nodetiers.go gains its tier-1 row, and the
"TIER 1 IS ABSENT AND THE ABSENCE IS ASSERTED" comment above it goes -- see
fisc-ko1j.8, which owns that decision.

## Registration is five edits, not one

Missing any one fails the suite in a way that looks unrelated to the check.
All(); a row in TestTheCommittedCorpusVacuitySplit; a row in checks_test.go;
the Counts{Pass,Vacuous,Skipped} literal in that same file AND the separate
lenient.Counts.Vacuous assertion below it -- two assertions, not one; and the
check's own table test, go-cmp rather than testify.

READ THE COUNTS OFF A REBUILT ./bin/fisc verify RUN, not off this bead.

## What it cannot witness

Both sides are built from one fact slice in one process, so it cannot witness a
wrong amount -- fact-offset-points-at-token does that. It catches a line item
classified under the wrong category, a row dropped from the projection, and the
two schedules drifting apart. The doc comment has to say so, per
internal/check/check.go's own standard.

## Acceptance: the mutation, both directions

- Re-point one line item onto a neighbouring category -> BOTH categories red,
  with equal and opposite unaccounted amounts. That is the shape a real
  classification error takes, and it is the case fisc-ko1j.9's fold test is
  green for.
- Drop the shared exception -> exactly one subject red at 480,400. Restore.
notes:
2026-09-12, measured landing this bead (47c4f8e, lane C).

THE CITED-TWICE ARM IS VOID AND NO ARM WAS WRITTEN FOR IT. Under the model the
drill-down ships, the tier-0-to-3 revenue flow was REPLACED by the tier-1-to-3

FundFlowsCounts.FactsCitedTwice is unchanged -- it is still the expenditure

title: fund-flows publishes the line-item tier, and the {0,3} fold reproduces today's links exactly
description:
internal/project only. The projection lane for E13's revenue side; the client is
fisc-ko1j.11 and the check is fisc-ko1j.10.

## What changes

internal/project/fundflows.go:

  revKey            gains the row identity fisc-ko1j.8 decides. It keys
                    (kind, category, fundGroup, fund) today, which is exactly
                    why p127's thirteen property-tax rows collapse into one
                    cell.
  revenueEndpoint   gains a line-item form beside revenue/<category> and
                    transfers/in. It errors on any third kind today and must
                    keep doing so.
  addParents        parents each line item to its category.

EVERY GUARD IN netFundFlows STAYS A REFUSAL AND NOT A SKIP. That is this
package's own rule and the file says so: a fact this document cannot place is a
mapping defect, and dropping it publishes a smaller city with no error anywhere.
A row the new key cannot address is refused by name.

## THE MUTATION PROOF IS THE FOLD

Reproduce green first, then:

- Fold the new document to {0,3} and compare against today's committed links.
  SAME VALUES, SAME fact_ids, SAME LOCATORS, SAME ORDER. A line-item tier that
  does not fold back to what it replaced has changed the document rather than
  refined it, and this is the only test that can tell the two apart.
- Break one line item's parent pointer -> the fold refuses ("no ancestor of it
  is a tier this page draws"), red. Restore.
- Re-point one line item onto a different category -> the fold is still green
  because the totals are unchanged, and fisc-ko1j.10's per-category tie is what
  goes red. State that both are needed and neither is enough.

Both the green and the red belong in the commit message.

## The 47 zero rows are not nodes

MEASURED 2026-09-08: FY2026 adopted has 231 rows of which 184 are nonzero. The
other 47 are cited but not flowed today -- "a printed dash is a fact and not a
flow" -- and counted in FundFlowsCounts. THEY MUST STAY THAT WAY. A printed dash
becoming a line-item node draws a row the city prints as zero as though it were
a thing that happens, and absent-is-not-zero is not the only thing at stake:
d3-sankey gives a zero-height node, which is the undrawable case fisc-ko1j's own
cap measurement exists to avoid.

title: What a revenue line item IS in the graph: its tier, its id, and whether it is its category's child or its target
description:
THREE CLAUSES, NONE DECIDABLE FROM THE CODE ALONE, and all three are settled
before fisc-ko1j.9 writes a line. Blocked on fisc-ko1j.7: if the answer there is
"refuse the tier", this bead never runs.

## (1) THE TIER NUMBER

node-tiers-are-declared requires a link's source tier to be STRICTLY LESS than
its target tier (internal/check/nodetiers.go), and it is that ordering claim,
not the hierarchy, that makes d3 draw left to right with no backward ribbon. A
line item is finer than its category (tier 0) and feeds a fund (tier 3), so it
sits between them and tier 1 is the only free number.

TIER 1 IS NOT MERELY UNUSED, IT IS DECLARED ABSENT WITH AN ARGUMENT, in three
places that would all have to move together:

  internal/project/sankey.go     the tier constant block
  internal/check/nodetiers.go    hierarchyTiers, and its "TIER 1 IS ABSENT AND
                                 THE ABSENCE IS ASSERTED" comment
  docs/sankey-contract.md        the tier table and the paragraph under it

WHAT THAT ARGUMENT ACTUALLY REFUTES is a CONSTRAINT tier: a constraint tier is a
property of a fund, the fund groups do not partition along it, so a layer whose
parent edge is undefined is not a layer. It refutes that layer and not every
possible layer. A revenue line item's parent edge IS defined -- one category per
row, measured below -- so the refutation does not reach it. Retiring the
declaration is still a decision and not an edit, because "a node claiming tier 1
is a node claiming a layer nothing can define" is asserted today and would
become false.

The alternative is a tier outside 0-5, which the contract's id-form table
forbids in as many words ("Do not coin new ones").

## (2) THE NODE ID

MEASURED 2026-09-08 off facts/facts.jsonl: over all 924 revenue-by-fund facts
there are TWELVE distinct row_path values and NONE maps to more than one
category. row_path IS the category slug. So the fact store carries no line-item
slug, and the only line-item identity in it is row_label -- free text off the
page.

Three candidates:

  (a) SLUGS IN data/taxonomy.yaml. Content-independent, matches every other id
      form, and is the largest piece of work: a slug per printed line, authored
      and reviewed.
  (b) A SLUGIFIED row_label. Coins an id form the contract forbids, and makes
      identity content-dependent -- the thing "Identity and integrity are
      separate" refuses, because a re-typeset label would become a different
      node rather than the same node changed.
  (c) fact.SeriesID, which already hashes (DocID, RuleID, RowPath, RowLabel,
      ColumnPath) and is ALREADY PUBLISHED in revenue-trends.json. Nothing to
      build. But ColumnPath carries the fund, so it is per-fund BY
      CONSTRUCTION and a citywide line-item node is not expressible under it --
      and use-of-money-and-property spans 39 funds, intergovernmental 27,
      miscellaneous-revenue 26. Whether a line item is per-fund or citywide is
      therefore decided by picking (c), which is a reason to decide it first
      rather than inherit it.

## (3) CHILD OF ITS CATEGORY, OR TARGET OF IT

Only one of these needs new client machinery, and the cheaper one costs
something else.

  CHILD. The line item's parent is revenue/<category>; links stay tier-1 -> 3
  only. Drawing {0,3} folds the line items back into their categories through
  the parent chain and reproduces today's document -- which is fisc-ko1j.9's
  mutation proof and is the strongest acceptance test available here. THE COST:
  filterToNode keys on the link's TARGET, so a category still has nothing
  pointing at it and opening one needs a source-side filter that does not exist
  (fisc-ko1j.11).

  TARGET. Emit a tier-0 -> tier-1 link as well as tier-1 -> 3. A category then
  has inbound links, opens under today's filterToNode with no new filter, and
  the drawn chart is the category exploding into its lines. THE COST: every
  revenue fact is cited on two links. That is not novel -- fisc-gxa.2 had to
  publish counts.facts_cited_twice for exactly this reason on the expenditure
  side, because a sankey needs a link at each adjacent tier pair it can be drawn
  at -- but it is a second place the same money appears inside ONE document, and
  the checks that would have to be taught about it are named in fisc-ko1j.10.

STATE WHAT EACH COSTS AND PICK ONE. Do not leave it to the projection lane; the
choice decides whether fisc-ko1j.11 is a new function or a comment rewrite.
notes: MEASURED 2026-09-12 in fisc-ko1j.14: 'THE SIZE OF THE JOB IS 102' counts ('transfers/in', 'Transfers In'), kind transfer_in, among the pairs. Restricted to kind revenue it is 101 pairs over 864 facts. Since clause (3) and the plan keep transfers/in at tier 0, the line registry holds 101 entries (d439acb).
close_reason:
DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-12. All three clauses.

(1) THE TIER: 1. As this bead argued -- a line is finer than its category (tier
0) and feeds a fund (tier 3), and tier 1 is the only free number. The declaration
that tier 1 is absent retires in three places together: internal/project/sankey.go's
constant block, internal/check/nodetiers.go's hierarchyTiers and its "TIER 1 IS
ABSENT AND THE ABSENCE IS ASSERTED" comment, and docs/sankey-contract.md's tier
table and the paragraph under it. The constraint-tier arithmetic in each STAYS,
as the reason tier 1 was empty; what changes is that a line's parent edge IS
defined where the constraint tier's was not.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN CITATION, measured against the tree: clause (1)
says the alternative is "a tier outside 0-5, which the contract's id-form table
forbids in as many words ('Do not coin new ones')". It does not.
docs/sankey-contract.md:259 governs SLUGS -- "The slug in every id is a
data/taxonomy.yaml slug. Do not coin new ones" -- and says nothing about tier
numbers or id forms. The "coined id form" reading is internal/check/nodetiers.go's
own gloss on that sentence, not the contract's. That sentence is also ALREADY
false against the tier table three lines above it, which cites fund/<number>
(funds.yaml) and dept/<slug> (departments.yaml). It is corrected in the same lane.

(2) THE NODE ID: authored slugs, nested in data/taxonomy.yaml. Not fact.SeriesID
-- ColumnPath carries the fund, so a citywide line is not expressible under it --
and not a slugified row_label, which makes identity content-dependent and is what
"Identity and integrity are separate" refuses.

THE SIZE OF THE JOB IS 102, NOT 924. Measured 2026-09-12: there are 102 distinct
(row_path, row_label) pairs citywide and no row_label maps to more than one
category. 94 of the 102 appear in exactly one fund; the widest spans 38
(use-of-money-and-property). Clause (2) gives "39 funds, 27, 26" for the three
widest -- measured at FY2026 adopted they are 38, 26, 25, and this bead does not
state its basis.

ID FORM: revenue-line/<category>/<line>. A NEW PREFIX IS REQUIRED and this bead
does not anticipate it: declaredTier cuts an id at the FIRST slash, and
revenue/taxes/property is already tier 0 with a slash inside its slug, so neither
prefix nor segment count can tell a line from a category under revenue/. The
precedent is expenditure/<division>/<object>.

WHERE THE SLUGS LIVE, decided 2026-09-12 after a collision this bead does not
anticipate: data/taxonomy.yaml is validated ONE LEVEL DEEP, hard, at
internal/registry/load.go:588 and in validateParent at load.go:719-745, with
load_test.go:372 pinning the refusal for taxes/property/secured by name. A line
under taxes/property is a grandchild. The owner's answer is to make the taxonomy
RECURSIVE rather than either two-level or a second data file, so a further
breakdown never needs another file. Measured: recursive is FEWER rules than
today -- change strings.Cut(c.Slug, "/") at load.go:721 to cut at the LAST slash,
then DELETE the segment-count arm and the grandchild arm. Provably a no-op on all
38 existing entries, every one depth <= 1, where the two cuts coincide. Cycles
are impossible by construction: a parent slug is a strict prefix and so strictly
shorter. A line entry reuses existing fields -- slug, label, parent, and
document_term for the printed row_label, with aliases: for a re-typeset row.

The cost is that data/taxonomy.yaml's own header argues the opposite in two
places and both are rewritten: "deliberately NOT used below the ten revenue
categories ... Those detail lines are a rule's label, not a category", and "every
parent node below is therefore our grouping, not the city's" (pp.66-67 print
taxes/property itself, so a parent may be assignable -- no validator forbids it,
only the prose). The answer to the first is that a slug NAMES a printed row
rather than inventing a classification, and the drift it fears is what the new
check refuses in both directions.

(3) CHILD OF ITS CATEGORY. Links stay tier-1 -> tier-3 only; each revenue fact is
cited on exactly one link. The {0,3} fold reproducing today's committed links is
the acceptance test the whole lane rests on, and the target model weakens it
where it matters most. The cost is real and is fisc-ko1j.11's: filterToNode keys
on the target, so opening a category needs a filterFromNode sibling.

CONSEQUENCE FOR fisc-ko1j.10: the facts-cited-twice arm this bead describes under
the target model is VOID. FactsCitedTwice is unchanged by this lane.

title: May the chart publish pp.127-140 at the grain trends.html already publishes it at
description:
THE FIRST BEAD OF E13's REVENUE SIDE, AND IT REOPENS A DECISION RATHER THAN
BUILDING ON ONE. Nothing in fisc-ko1j.8 through fisc-ko1j.12 may start before
this is answered.

## Why the revenue side is empty today

E13's chain decomposes SPENDING TWICE -- fund group -> fund -> division ->
object category -- and revenue not at all. At every depth the source column is
the same ten taxonomy categories pp.66-67 print. fisc-ko1j's "Not in scope"
records the mechanical reason (filterToNode filters to a subtree by parent chain
and a revenue category has no descendants), but the mechanical reason is not the
binding one.

## fisc-awe is the binding one

DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-08-30, on fisc-awe: ONE SCHEDULE, ONE PUBLISHED VIEW.
Two documents may not publish the same money at the same grain. Its worked
example is verbatim this case -- "revenue-trends already publishes all 924
revenue-by-fund facts as 231 four-point series, and a revenue drill-down graph
would republish 190 of them per adopted year as links" -- and that decision is
what sent the fund-flows drill to expenditure-by-department instead.

FUND-FLOWS SURVIVES THAT DECISION ONLY ON A GRAIN DIFFERENCE. It draws
pp.127-140 at (category, fund); revenue-trends draws them at (line item, fund).
A line-item tier collapses the difference, and then the chart and trends.html
publish one schedule at IDENTICAL grain on two pages, which is the thing
fisc-awe refuses by name.

It is reopenable rather than closed against: fisc-awe's own acceptance criteria
asks "and if so what tells a reader they are the same money", so the case where
the answer is yes was contemplated.

## Measured 2026-09-08, off facts/facts.jsonl rather than the goldens

  231 rows at FY2026 adopted, 184 of them nonzero
  149 distinct (fund, category) cells; 70 funds carry revenue
  fund/100 carries 92 of the 231 rows
  nonzero line items in fund/100: charges-for-services 18, taxes/other 14,
    licenses-and-permits 14, taxes/property 13, miscellaneous-revenue 10

So the reader-facing prize is real -- "Property Taxes" opening into thirteen
printed lines is the true mirror of division -> object category -- and so is the
doubling.

## Three answers, and the cost of each

1. REFUSE THE TIER AND POINT AT THE TABLE. Opening a revenue category hands the
   reader trends.html filtered to that category. Cheapest by far, keeps one
   schedule one view, and fisc-s7ia is precedent that this project will answer
   "a table is a table by design". Costs the click-through the USAFacts pattern
   is for.

2. PERMIT IT AND RETIRE THE TABLE VIEW. The chart BECOMES pp.127-140's one view;
   trends.html (nav "Revenue tables", pkg/cmd/export/data.go) changes or goes.
   This is consistent with fisc-awe rather than an exception to it, and it is
   the same move E13 already makes for revenue.html and spending.html.

3. PERMIT BOTH AND WRITE THE SENTENCE. fisc-awe's acceptance criteria demands
   what tells a reader the two are the same money. A caveat is the mechanism
   this site has for that; whether a caveat is enough is the question.

## What the answer must record

WHICH NAV ENTRY A READER ENDS ON, under each option. E13's whole premise is that
three nav entries over one subject is the defect, so an answer that leaves the
chart and the table as two destinations has to say why that is different from
the case E13 is undoing.

Answering 1 closes fisc-ko1j.8 through fisc-ko1j.12 unbuilt, and that is a
legitimate outcome of this bead.
close_reason:
DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-09-12: PERMIT BOTH, AND WRITE THE SENTENCE. Option 3.

The chart gets the revenue line-item tier AND trends.html stays. fisc-awe's
acceptance criteria contemplated this answer and demanded what tells a reader
they are the same money; the caveat is that mechanism and lane D of the plan
ships it on BOTH documents under one id.

THE FACT THAT DECIDED IT, and it is not on this bead or on fisc-awe: trends.html
publishes FOUR budget columns -- FY2023-24 actual, FY2024-25 revised, and both
adopted years -- and the chart publishes ONE. Only the FY2026 adopted column is
genuinely doubled, and the table is the sole home of the other three. So option 2
(retire the table) is not the clean swap fisc-awe's logic suggests: it would
delete three columns no chart depth shows. That asymmetry is what the caveat
sentence carries, and it is why "one schedule, one view" does not settle this
case the way it settled the drill-down's scope.

WHICH NAV ENTRY A READER ENDS ON, which this bead required the answer to record:
both remain. "Budget flows" is the chart, "Revenue tables" is the four-column
table. That is different from the case E13 undid -- three nav entries over one
subject with nothing relating them -- because the caveat on each document names
the other and says they are one schedule, and the chart's step Description points
at the tables by name. The relation is published rather than left to the reader.

MEASURED 2026-09-12 off facts/facts.jsonl, re-deriving this bead's own figures:
231 rows at FY2026 adopted and 184 nonzero (this bead and fisc-awe both say
"190"; 182 nonzero at FY2027), 149 distinct (fund, category) cells, 70 funds
present and 61 carrying nonzero, fund/100 carrying 92. Nonzero line items in
fund/100: charges-for-services 18, taxes/other 14, licenses-and-permits 14,
taxes/property 13, miscellaneous-revenue 10. Every other figure reproduces.

AND ONE MEASUREMENT THAT SIMPLIFIES WHAT .9 THROUGH .12 MUST BUILD: restricted to
the revenue kinds, ALL TEN revenue categories tie TO THE CENT citywide between
the spine (all-funds-gross) and pp.127-140 (revenue-by-fund). The only gap is
(transfer_in, transfers/in) at 480,400 -- already the sole entry in
revenueDetailExceptions. So a revenue category opened at depth 0 needs NO
residual machinery, unlike the fund-group step fisc-ko1j.5 built one for.

title: The residual on the chart: what the fund-level schedule does not decompose
description:
The second half of fisc-ko1j's owner decision 3. fisc-ko1j.1 guarantees the
identity; this makes it visible, so a reader who opens the General Fund and sees
144,650,802 flowing out of a 159,388,024 node is told why rather than left to
notice.

## What ships

One derived node per opened group in the fund column: residual/<group>,
derived: true, labelled for what it is ("Not broken down by fund"), with

  rationale   pp.127-140 and 167-170 stop at fund; pp.66-67 print these figures
              at group grain, so the schedule that would split them is not
              published.
  source_note the carried links' own locators.

Its inflow (e.g. general 1,514,554) and outflow (14,737,222) differ by
construction, and THAT VISIBLE IMBALANCE IS THE RESIDUAL.

## Carried, not computed

The client copies the spine links' value_cents, fact_ids, locators and kind
VERBATIM. It computes no amount. Those links are already covered by
link-values-tie-to-facts and link-locators-match-their-facts, so the figure on
screen is a published one with its provenance intact.

DO NOT RE-POINT THE GROUP END ONTO A FUND. Capital has 11 funds and
internal-service 5; pp.127-140 do not say which one a draw belongs to.
Re-pointing would invent an allocation.

APPLY THE RULE UNIFORMLY, INCLUDING general, where the group has one fund. The
cost is that general's transfers out and reserve increase draw BESIDE fund/100
rather than out of it -- conservative, never wrong, and it keeps the client's
rule free of a branch it would have to invent.

THE NODE SET IS fisc-ko1j.1's DECLARATION, not a second copy. That is the whole
reason the check declares it as a constant with reasons rather than inlining
four ids.

Precedent: AGGREGATE_ID in capColumn is already a client-only derived node with
derived:true, a rationale and a source note, checked by drill.mjs and not by
derived-nodes-justified. This is a weaker claim, because the aggregate sums and
this copies. AGENTS.md's derived-node rule binds PROJECTIONS; the client is
neither a projection nor a scenario, and the residual is a statement about the
PAIR of documents, which neither document may hold -- the page is the only place
both exist at once. Say that in the comment, because the next reader will ask.

## The jscheck owed, same commit

- The node is marked as ours: derived true, both fields non-empty, and it
  appears in buildDerivedList and in the tooltip chip.
- Its value_cents, fact_ids and locators are BYTE-EQUAL to the spine link's.
  Mutate one and it goes red -- three arms, three mutations.
- The imbalance is drawn rather than silently balanced: general's residual node
  has both an inflow and an outflow and they differ.
- A group with a zero residual (special-revenue, enterprise, debt-service) draws
  NO residual node at all. An aggregate-of-nothing is the defect drill.mjs
  already has an arm against one tier up.
notes:
2026-09-11, lane 6 (this bead), measured off fisc export's own sankey.json, sankey-2027.json, fund-flows.json and fund-flows-2027.json before the client was written. The description needs these adjustments:

(1) THE ONE-DECLARATION PROBLEM IS ENGINEERED, NOT ASSUMED. The declaration is a Go map and the client is JavaScript, so 'the node set is fisc-ko1j.1's declaration' had to be made true by a seam: export.DrillStep gained Residual map[string]string (json residual, omitempty), views() fills it from check.ResidualNodes(), the packager ships it on step 0 of FISC_CONFIG.steps, and app.js reads step.residual and spells no endpoint of its own. On the check side, tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's residualDeclaration() parses the map literal out of internal/check/drillreconcile.go, so drill.mjs measures the client under the set the site ships and carries no copy either. The alternative -- a JS literal held equal to Go by a test -- was rejected because it is the second copy this paragraph names. Limit: TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone pins views() to check.ResidualNodes()'s current value and cannot tell a read from a copy until they drift, which is when a copy goes red.

(2) THE FIGURES ARE PER COLUMN, AND FY2027 IS NOT THE EXAMPLE GIVEN. 'general 1,514,554 in, 14,737,222 out' is FY2026 adopted (1,034,154 draw + 480,400 transfers in; 4,699,425 reserve increase + 10,037,797 transfers out). FY2027 adopted general is 486,735 in (transfers in only -- no draw) and 15,830,303 out (2,351,098 fund-balance/contribution + 3,332,607 reserve increase + 10,146,598 transfers out). capital draws 2,500,213 / 10,129,416 in and internal-service 6,147,533 / 7,160,645 in (FY2026 / FY2027), inflow only, since neither is decomposed. special-revenue, enterprise and debt-service draw no node in either column, as the description says; measured rather than trusted, since lane 1 found the FY2026-only set misleading once.

(3) 'THREE ARMS, THREE MUTATIONS' IS ONE ARM NAMING THE FIELD. drill.mjs compares every carried link to its spine link on value_cents, fact_ids, locators, kind AND derived (the draw link is derived: true on the spine and stays so), and reports which field differs; the three mutations each go red under it by name. Three arms would have repeated the walk three times to say the same thing.

(4) 'THE CARRIED LINKS' OWN LOCATORS' ARE p.66 ALONE FOR GENERAL. All four of general's spine endpoint links cite p66 (general and enterprise print on p66, the other groups on p67), so the source note reads 'p.66' there and the check reads the expected pages off the links rather than typing them. Lane 1's reasons named a single page per endpoint ('p67's Change in Working Capital row'), which is right for capital and internal-service and wrong for general, where that text is now on screen; corrected to pp.66-67 in drillreconcile.go this session.

(5) THE ID IS residual/<opened node id>, e.g. residual/fund-group/general, not residual/general: the aggregate went per tier for the same reason (one id per document, unique by construction), and the opened node's full id is what is unique per rung.

(6) TWO CONSEQUENCES THE DESCRIPTION DOES NOT NAME. fund/100 no longer sits alone in its column, so its tooltip carries a share ('our 91.5% of this column' in FY2026) where columnShare used to suppress it; and the counts line counts the carried flows apart ('from 141 of the document's 280 facts, and 4 flows carried unchanged from the chart above'), because their facts are the spine's and would otherwise be reported as a share of the wrong document's total.

(7) NEEDS A SECOND SPINE GOLDEN. drill.mjs served the FY2026 spine under both years' paths because the drill read nothing off the spine but the clicked id; the residual reads the spine's links, so testdata/sankey-2027.golden.json is captured and pinned like fund-flows-2027's. Neither existing golden moved.

title: The merge: one chart page, revenue.html and spending.html retired
description:
This is fisc-ko1j's end condition. views() collapses to one view with the
two-step chain; revenue.html and spending.html are deleted; nav drops to one
chart entry.

## The declaration

  out := []export.View{{
      Path: export.IndexPath, Nav: "Budget flows",
      Template: export.SankeyTemplate, Projection: export.PrimaryProjection,
      YearStems: yearStems(export.PrimaryProjection, projections),  // unchanged
      Steps: []export.DrillStep{
          {From: 2, Projection: project.FundFlowsProjection,
           Tiers: []int{0,3,4}, Caps: []export.TierCap{{3,8},{4,24}},
           Back: "All fund groups", Tail: "funds"},
          {From: 4, Tiers: []int{4,5}, Caps: []export.TierCap{{5,8}},
           Back: "All divisions", Tail: "categories"},
      },
  }}

The two retired pages' ledes and caveats move into the depth-1 and depth-2 chart
descriptions. Spending's lede carries the claim that only the General Fund is
decomposed, and that claim is now visible in the chart itself -- five of six
groups end at their funds -- so it can be shorter, not dropped.

## yearStems IS THE WRONG JOIN FOR A STEP

yearStems walks project.PublishedDocuments() in DECLARED order, which for
fund-flows is {2024-actual, 2025-revised, fund-flows, fund-flows-2027}. A step
wants "spine stem -> step stem of the same Column". That is a new helper joining
PublishedDocuments() on Columns.

AND THAT DISSOLVES fisc-zojk's OBSTACLE (1) OUTRIGHT: the step is not a
YearStems list, so View.validate's "first year stem is not its own projection"
arm never applies and there is no opening-year decision left to make.

## unviewedDocuments

- fund-flows-2027 becomes reachable through step 0's per-year join -> DELETE the
  entry, or assertPublishedReachable fires ("a view now renders it ... delete
  that entry").
- fund-flows-2024-actual and fund-flows-2025-revised STAY, with REWRITTEN
  reasons. The current text names revenue.html and spending.html, which will not
  exist, and cites fisc-zojk's stem-order obstacle, which no longer applies. The
  true new reason is simpler and stronger: pp.66-67 print no actual and no
  revised column, so there is no spine year to open them from.

## assertPublishedReachable must widen

pkg/cmd/export/data.go: `reachable` is built from v.Projection and v.YearStems.
Add each step's Projection and its per-year stems, or both fund-flows documents
are reported unreachable.

## What else moves

- drill.mjs's PAGES becomes the merged chain; fold.mjs's REVENUE and SPENDING
  constants retire.
- docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md and docs/sankey-contract.md get their
  drill sections rewritten.
- The nav is emitted on every page, so trends/history/balances/caveats/
  provenance all change output. Expect the whole dist/ to move.
- pkg/cmd/export/data.go loses two long comment blocks arguing the split. Their
  measurements are the ones fisc-ko1j records; do not simply delete the numbers.

## Acceptance

- ./bin/fisc verify green, count read off the run.
- facts/facts.jsonl byte-unmoved (nothing here touches the fact store).
- No dist/ page links to revenue.html or spending.html; grep the built tree.
- 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 walks by mouse AND by keyboard (Tab, Enter, Escape one
  rung at a time), in light and dark, with the breadcrumb, counts line, legend
  and flow table each describing the chart actually on screen at every rung.
notes:
2026-09-10, lane 4 (restarted; the first attempt was cut off with the work uncommitted and its diff was audited, not trusted). Corrections measured against the tree:

(1) 'docs/sankey-contract.md gets its drill section rewritten' -- it has none. grep -in 'drill|step|opens' finds three lines (29, 211-213), all still true. A paragraph under 'On the spine' now says the six tier-2 nodes open and points at the drill-down contract.

(2) The declaration in this bead has no Description per step. validateSteps now requires one, sentence-terminated, because the client's <desc> at depth 1 otherwise announced the opening state's sentence -- 'revenue categories flow into six fund groups' -- over a chart of one group's funds. The retired ledes live in those two descriptions, which TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone pins and drill.mjs's PAGE copies.

(3) Lane 3's flagged failure mode -- fundGroupOf's --muted result when the hierarchy merge resolves against the wrong document -- did not occur. The failing check was drill.mjs's own predicate: it took an id prefix for 'on the fund side', and the spine's four tier-5 expenditure/ uses (parent '', muted by design) failed it on the overview. app.js was right; the check now reads the goldens' parent field.

(4) fold.mjs's REVENUE/SPENDING retirement takes with it the through-main() page check (counts 29/17/190 and 23/24/49 over tier sets no view declares) and the legend-order check, which is re-homed on the spine; the {0,2,4} fold-clause checks stay. year.mjs's chainedYears fixture threw because it packaged no per-year steps entry -- a module that throws is a check that cannot fail, and it hid that the cache-drop arm was also red.

(5) The merge exposed a WRONG-OUTPUT in caveats.html: buildCaveatsPage's drawn map read projections and year stems only, so with no view over fund-flows the page said the charts do not flag its marks -- while drill.mjs proves fund/100 is chipped and linked at depth 1. Fixed with the step arm and TestTheCaveatsPagePromisesAChartFlagOnAStepsDocument.

(6) unviewedDocuments: the three entries shared one const; replaced by fundFlowsNoSpineColumn for the two that stay. fund-flows-2027 deleted, reachable through step 0's join. assertPublishedReachable widened with the step arm.

(7) Acceptance walk 0->1->2->1->0: jscheck witnesses Escape one rung at a time through the handler main() attached, each breadcrumb control closing to its own depth, counts/title/desc/hint/legend/flow-table rows/focus at every rung, and the step fetched once. NOT witnessed: mouse clicks on SVG marks, Tab order and Enter on a focused mark, and light/dark rendering -- owner at a browser (fisc-yj4w.18).

(8) fisc-ko1j.13 closed here: the per-year join ships each rung's caveat refs in the year's steps entry; caveatHref reads them; drill.mjs pins the depth-1 anchor as fund-flows', and the mutation (year's refs at every depth) goes red.

Measured: dist/ moves whole -- nav on every page; data/*.json and facts/index.json differ from a clean-tree baseline only by the generated_by stamp.

Step documents joined per year on Column (stepStems), resolved by the packager into each year's steps entry with that document's caveat refs; fund-flows-2027 reachable and its unviewedDocuments entry deleted; the two actual/revised entries stay under fundFlowsNoSpineColumn. Seven numbered findings in the commit, each with its mutation; the WRONG-OUTPUT among them was caveats.html withdrawing the chart-flag promise on fund-flows. Gate: facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 47 passed, 0 failed; make js 97 pass; make pre-commit green. jscheck witnesses the 0->1->2->1->0 walk by Escape and breadcrumb with every rung's words read back; mouse, Tab/Enter and light/dark need the owner at a browser. Stale premises corrected in notes.

title: The client's drill becomes a stack over two documents
description:
site/app.js and tools/jscheck. Still driven over ONE-STEP chains, so the shipped
site's behaviour is unchanged -- this lane pays for the machinery, and
fisc-ko1j.4 spends it.

## The state change

`let drilledInto = ""` becomes a stack of {id, doc, step}. Its doc comment's
premise -- "ONE LEVEL, NOT A STACK, because the drill is one hop by
construction: DRILL.from names a single tier, so a node in the drilled view is
never itself drillable" -- becomes FALSE and must be REWRITTEN, not deleted:
drillable() rests on it. Every `if (drilledInto)` becomes `drilled.length`.

`let fetched` becomes one document per depth. Fetch the step document LAZILY on
first drill, not eagerly per year.

## Every function that changes, and the trap in each

  activeTiers      current step's Tiers, else RENDER_TIERS. A wrong answer is
                   not a wrong-looking chart, it is a THROW inside d3-sankey's
                   ordering pass -- the defect drill.mjs's header records.

  shapeFor         per-step tiers and PLURAL caps. TWO capColumn CALLS COLLIDE
                   ON THE SINGLE AGGREGATE_ID. Latent on the committed corpus,
                   because tier 4's cap never engages where tier 3's does, and
                   latent is how it ships -- the id must become per-tier. Also:
                   the aggregate's parent is re-pointed AFTER the fold and must
                   be the CURRENT rung, not the first. And ROOT is spine
                   vocabulary and must not reach the step document.

  drillTo          becomes async, split into drillDown/drillUp. Depth 1 fetches,
                   so every guard in showYear -- the switching token, isDocument,
                   understands, drawableSankey, the file:// sentence -- gains a
                   caller that is a CLICK, which today is synchronous. Its
                   "SHAPE AND LAY OUT BEFORE MUTATING ANYTHING" contract
                   (fisc-bsg) must survive the await: the token check sits
                   between fetch and repaint. Its restore-on-throw becomes a
                   stack restore.

  drillable        `!drilledInto` becomes "a step exists at this depth". Today a
                   drilled node is never drillable; on a chain a depth-1 tier-4
                   node IS. The AGGREGATE_ID exclusion must survive per-tier ids.

  labelOf          reads fetched.nodes. Rung k's label lives in the document
                   rung k was opened FROM, not the one drawn.

  paintBreadcrumb  N rungs, each popping TO that depth. restoreFocus focuses
                   bar.children[0], which under N rungs is the outermost rung
                   and not the one the reader came from.

  paintCounts      must read the DRAWN document's counts. shownYear.counts.facts
                   is the SPINE's total; at depth >= 1 it would read "from 33 of
                   the document's 120 facts" over a fund-flows chart, weighing
                   one document's ribbons against another's file. The whole "THE
                   FACT TOTAL IS THE DOCUMENT'S" argument in its doc comment
                   needs restating for two documents.

  paintChartName   compose N rungs. baseDescription and tablePointer are captured
                   on first paint from the SERVED description; a depth-2
                   description must still end with the table pointer -- that
                   sentence is the only route to the flow table a screen reader
                   has (see aeedfa5).

  paintChartHint   asks whether a step exists BELOW. "Nothing here opens further"
                   is now false at depth 1.

  caveatsFor       reads projection.metadata.caveats (the step document's at
                   depth >= 1) and groupIndex. The folds[] escape hatch must
                   survive per-tier aggregates.

  columnShare      the column-of-one guard now fires on depth-1 general
                   (fund/100 alone in its column), exactly as on spending.html.
                   drill.mjs's sharesColumn flag was per PAGE and becomes per
                   DEPTH.

  showYear         clears the whole stack AND drops the cached step document.
                   The switching token must cover the DRILL's fetch too, or a
                   year switch mid-drill draws the year the reader left.

  layOut           groupIndex merge lets `fetched` win over the drawn doc. With
                   the wrong fetched the hue walk resolves against the other
                   document's hierarchy -- the failure fundGroupOf's comment
                   records as "every mark rendered in --muted".

  main's Escape    pops ONE rung. Keep "an opened node is closed only when there
                   is nothing inside it to clear", per rung.

  buildLegend      at depth >= 1 filterToNode drops the tier-2 group nodes, so
                   the legend empties and buildLegendCount() goes 0. Already
                   true on the drilled pages; on the merged page the legend
                   VANISHES ON THE FIRST CLICK from a page that had one. Decide
                   what it does and say so.

## The jscheck owed, in this same commit

AGENTS.md's node boundary: "A change to app.js ships its check in the same
commit." This is the first lane run under fisc-rx1d's rule, which was written
because the drill originally shipped with zero checks and drill.mjs was then
built under review pressure across five passes.

- harness.mjs: the stack and the two-document state into NAMES. plannedFetch is
  already keyed by path and needs no change; goldenGraph() + goldenFundFlows()
  give a two-document plan in one line. Confirmed 2026-09-08.
- drill.mjs: drive 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0 through the real entry points.
- FOUR ARMS FOR THE DRILL FETCH'S REFUSAL PATHS -- 404, non-JSON body, wrong
  schema_version, null body. Each guard gains a new caller and has no coverage
  from one; four arms, not zero.
- A synthetic document engaging BOTH caps, since the committed corpus cannot
  reach the aggregate collision. Same shape as the existing "descendants half,
  which the corpus cannot exercise" arm.
- year.mjs: a year switch resets the stack AND drops the step document. Watch
  fisc-xixn -- year.mjs already holds a literal copy of paintCounts' wording,
  and paintCounts is changing here.
- seam.mjs: any new selector declared in KNOWN_SELECTORS, or the
  undeclared-selector arm goes red by name.
notes:
2026-09-10, lane 3, measured against the tree while landing the stack. Corrections to this bead's text:

(1) THE EXAMPLE SENTENCE IN paintCounts MIXES TWO COUNTS. It reads 'from 33 of the document's 120 facts'; 33 is depth-1 general's LINK count. Measured through app.js's own functions on the chain (spine opening into fund-flows at {0,3,4}): depth 1 general draws 34 nodes and 33 links, reproducing fisc-ko1j's figures, and its ribbons cite 141 of fund-flows' 280 facts. The wrong sentence would have read '141 of the document's 120 facts'; the shipped one reads '141 of the document's 280 facts', pinned by drill.mjs.

(2) 'let fetched becomes one document per depth' landed as: fetched stays depth 0's document, every Rung {id, doc, step} carries the document its chart is shaped from, and docAt(k) reads them as one sequence. One document per depth is that sequence, not a second array beside the stack.

(3) 'Rung k's label lives in the document rung k was opened FROM' is true and UNWITNESSABLE ON THE CORPUS: both goldens label fund-group/general 'General Fund'. drill.mjs's chain fixture relabels the spine's copy 'General Fund group' so labelOfRung reading the wrong document goes red; mutated, two arms fail.

(4) buildLegend 'already true on the drilled pages' is true by CONSTRUCTION of filterToNode on every declared step and on the chain, so the early return that makes the rule explicit is witnessed only by a probe whose step opens a fund into {2,4}, where the group node survives the filter (drill.mjs). Decision recorded there and on fisc-ko1j.11: an opened view draws no legend.

(5) The aggregate id is now aggregate/tail/<tier> (aggregateID, isAggregate); AGGREGATE_ID is gone. The collision is witnessed by a synthetic document with both caps engaged (four funds, four divisions, caps of 2), which is the only place it can be: the corpus never caps tier 4.

(6) Of the functions listed, caveatsFor, columnShare, fundGroupOf, citations, filterToNode, foldDocument and buildDerivedList needed no edit; what moved is upstream of them (groupIndex's source in layOut, the per-tier ids, the per-depth stack). capColumn did change: it takes the opened node and the noun as arguments.

(7) The caps are applied in the step's tier order, coarsest first, and that order is argued in shapeFor's comment rather than witnessed: on the synthetic document the fine-first order produces the same drawing. Not a defect; stated so nobody reads a mutation into it.

(8) Line numbers in the description predate lane 2 and were not used.
close_reason: Landed in bff54f1. drilledInto is a stack of Rung{id, doc, step}; fetched stays depth 0 and each rung carries its document; step documents are fetched lazily through loadDocument (shared with showYear) and dropped on a year switch; aggregates are per tier (aggregate/tail/<tier>); drillTo is drillDown/drillUp over redrawStack with the overtaken check between fetch and repaint. Shipped site unchanged: only app.js moves in dist/ with the stamp normalised. jscheck in the same commit walks 0->1->2->1->0 over both goldens, refuses the four fetch faults, and engages both caps on a synthetic document; seventeen mutations red at named arms, the aggregate collision only on the synthetic document. Legend decision: empty on every opened view by rule, recorded on fisc-ko1j.11. Eight stale points in this bead's text corrected in its notes; fisc-ko1j.13 filed for caveatHref over a switched document. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 47 passed, 0 failed.

title: The export seam takes a chain: View.Drill becomes View.Steps
description:
internal/export and pkg/cmd/export. Lands as a PURE REFACTOR: views() still
declares the two existing pages, each with a one-element Steps list, and the
only output change is an empty hidden breadcrumb on the spine page. The merge
itself is a later lane.

## The type

  type TierCap struct{ Tier, Cap int }
  type DrillStep struct {
      From       int        // tier whose nodes open
      Projection string     // "" = same document as the previous step
      Tiers      []int
      Caps       []TierCap
      Back, Tail string
  }

View.Drill *Drill -> View.Steps []DrillStep.

Caps IS A SLICE AND NOT map[int]int: deterministic ordering in the shipped JSON,
and validate can refuse a cap on a tier the step does not draw.

THE SURPRISE THAT NEEDS A COMMENT: on a step that switches document, From is a
tier of the PREVIOUS document and Tiers are tiers of THIS one. From:2 is the
spine's fund-group tier; Tiers:{0,3,4} are fund-flows'. validate therefore
cannot relate them, and a reader will assume it can.

## What validate must newly refuse

internal/export/export.go, View.validate:

1. A step with no tiers, per step -- today's single arm restated.
2. THE CHAIN MUST BE WALKABLE: Steps[0].From in RenderTiers, and Steps[i].From
   in Steps[i-1].Tiers for i>0. This is what replaces "a drill is one hop by
   construction". Without it a page ships a breadcrumb rung nothing can reach.
3. A step whose Tiers equal the previous step's -- today's "would be drawn by
   the same tier set it was closed under", now against Steps[i-1].Tiers.
4. Back and Tail PER STEP. One Back on a chain sends a depth-2 reader to depth 0.
5. A cap on a tier its own step does not draw (it folds nothing, silently), and
   a duplicate tier in Caps. Cap < 1 stays.
6. A step naming a projection that was not built -- the same named refusal
   v.Projection gets.

## The arm that would refuse the merged view

  case v.Drill != nil && !slices.Contains(v.RenderTiers, v.Drill.From)

carries a deliberate "NO len(v.RenderTiers) > 0 GUARD" decision. The spine draws
whole (RenderTiers empty) and tier 2 IS drawn, so as written this refuses
fisc-ko1j's merged view. DO NOT RE-ADD THE GUARD -- that is what the comment
argues against. Split into two arms, each stating its own hazard:

  - len(RenderTiers) > 0 && !contains(RenderTiers, Steps[0].From)  -> refuse
  - Template == ChartTemplate && len(Steps) > 0 && len(RenderTiers) == 0
    -> refuse (the original trap: a breadcrumb over an unfolded 61-node column)

## Also required, and easy to miss

- templateRendersDrill (internal/export/page.go) gains SankeyTemplate.
- site/index.html.tmpl has NO #breadcrumb and NO #chart-hint; only
  site/chart.html.tmpl does. Both must be added, and seam.mjs's KNOWN_SELECTORS
  kept in step -- harness.mjs's TEMPLATE_IDS is maintained by hand.
- clientConfig.Docs is built from unionSources(cited) over v.YearStems ONLY. It
  must union each step's document too. citations() in app.js does
  `if (!doc) continue`, so a step document's doc_id missing from that map makes
  its citations VANISH WITH NO ERROR. Both documents share a doc_id today
  (livermore-budget-fy2026-2027), so nothing drops -- that is luck, not design.
  The footer's Sources would otherwise still advertise pp.66-67 under a chart
  drawn from pp.127-140.
- Page TEXT is already safe: buildSite's "EVERY PUBLISHED DOCUMENT SHIPS ITS
  PAGES" loop walks sortedKeys(o.Projections).
- clientConfig.Projections already ships every stem -> data/<stem>.json on every
  page, so the client can already fetch a second document by stem. Confirmed
  2026-09-08; no change needed there.
- The comment on clientConfig.Drill claiming "the spine's config blob has to stay
  byte-identical" retires the moment steps is added. Grepped: nothing pins those
  bytes in a test, only that comment.

## Tests that move

- views_test.go's "render tiers a template does not publish" case is on
  SankeyTemplate and must move to a template that still publishes none
  (TrendsTemplate).
- TestViewsOpensOnTheSpineAndGivesYearsToItAlone asserts the exact Drill values
  field by field; it exists to keep tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's copy honest, so
  both sides move together or neither does.
notes:
2026-09-09, lane 2, measured against a7121cd before working it. Four points of this bead's text are stale:

(1) templateRendersDrill is NOT in internal/export/page.go. It is internal/export/export.go beside templateRendersTiers; page.go has no templateRenders* function.

(2) pkg/cmd/export/data.go does NOT quote "34 nodes". The {0,3,4} comment reads "(33 links, 2 sub-pixel)". The 34-node figure exists only in this bead.

(3) The Drill struct's field order is From, Tiers, Back, Tail, Cap, not From/Tiers/Cap/Back/Tail.

(4) "templateRendersDrill gains SankeyTemplate" is the wrong cut. That predicate gates FOUR validate arms -- Drill, ChartSubject, ChartDescription and Root -- and buildSankeyPage publishes none of the last three, so widening it admits a Root or a ChartSubject on the spine that the page drops in silence, the exact trap the family exists to refuse. Landed instead as a new templateRendersSteps (Chart + Sankey) for Steps alone; the other three keep a ChartTemplate-only predicate. views_test.go's "a root on a template that publishes none" and its two siblings are the cases that go red under the bead's cut.

Also measured: "tiers equal the previous step's" is only a refusal when the step draws the SAME document -- across a document switch the numbers belong to different hierarchies -- so that arm is gated on the step's resolved document, and the surprise comment sits on it.
close_reason: Landed as e84b683 on e13-sankey-merge, a pure refactor: View.Drill -> View.Steps []DrillStep over TierCap, validateSteps reading the chain as a path (its comment says that is an assumption; fisc-ko1j.12 owns the widening), the From arm split in two rather than re-guarded, templateRendersSteps split from templateRendersChartDeclarations, stepSources unioning each step's document into the footer and the client docs map, #breadcrumb and #chart-hint on the spine, and app.js reading one hop off CONFIG.steps[0] with the cap looked up by tier. views() still declares revenue.html and spending.html with one step each; the merge is fisc-ko1j.4. Measured: site diff at a7121cd vs e84b683 with the build stamp normalised is the two spine elements, the two chart pages' drill->steps blob and the shim; facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 47 passed, 0 failed; nine mutations red, listed in the commit body. Four stale points of this bead's text are in its notes.

title: A check that the drill's two documents still agree: drill-reconciles-across-documents
description:
internal/check only. Worth having whether or not fisc-ko1j's merge ever lands,
which is why it is first and why it blocks nothing but the residual lane.

money at two grains, and E13's drill puts one inside the other. Nothing today

title: E13 One chart page: the spine opens into funds, then into divisions
description:
The site publishes three chart pages over one subject. index.html draws the
`sankey` spine -- 11 revenue categories into 6 fund groups into 7 uses.
revenue.html and spending.html draw `fund-flows`, one document split at its
seam, each with a one-hop drill. A reader who wants to follow a dollar from
"Property Taxes" to "Patrol" has to notice three nav entries and know which is
which.

The three pages already ARE the levels of one chain, laid out side by side
instead of nested. Owner asked for the USAFacts pattern (start simple, click to
go deeper) on 2026-09-08, citing
https://usafacts.org/articles/this-chart-tells-you-everything-you-want-to-know-about-government-spending/

END CONDITION: index.html draws the two-step chain below, and revenue.html and
spending.html no longer exist.

## The chain

  depth 0  `sankey`      drawn whole, 25 nodes / 58 links. Tier 2 (the six
                         fund groups) opens.
  depth 1  `fund-flows`  click a fund group -> tiers {0,3,4}, caps PER TIER
                         {3:8, 4:24}. Tier 4 (divisions) opens.
  depth 2  `fund-flows`  click a division -> tiers {4,5}, cap {5:8}. Leaf.

## Measured 2026-09-08

Driven through site/app.js's own filterToNode, capColumn, foldDocument and
layOut via tools/jscheck/harness.mjs against testdata/sankey.golden.json and
testdata/fund-flows.golden.json. Re-derived independently a second time; both
runs agree.

Depth 1, per group -- nodes / links / sub-pixel ribbons / narrowest ribbon:

  general           34  33  2   0.26px
  special-revenue   17  22  2   0.07px
  enterprise        13  21  4   0.01px
  capital           13  17  1   0.55px
  debt-service       4   3  0  60.23px
  internal-service   7   6  0   4.88px

Depth 2, worst of the 23 divisions (dept/patrol): narrowest ribbon 51.38px.

TWO RESULTS DECIDE THE SHAPE.

CAPS MUST BE PER TIER. A single cap on the finest tier leaves special-revenue's
32 funds uncapped at {0,3,4}: 40 nodes, 22 sub-pixel ribbons, 9 zero-height
nodes -- undrawable. Today's Drill.Cap is one int and one tier; that is the
field that has to change.

ONLY THE GENERAL FUND HAS TIER-4 NODES, so the other five groups' charts end at
their funds. That is what spending.html's lede says in prose today, and here it
becomes a property of the drawn chart.

Enterprise's 4 sub-pixel ribbons at 0.01px are NOT introduced by this design:
today's shipped revenue drill at {0,3} measures identically.

The depth-1 general figures (34 nodes, 33 links, 2 sub-pixel) are the ones
pkg/cmd/export/data.go already quotes for {0,3,4} and DECLINES, on the grounds
that "a revenue column on the SPENDING page is the conflation this split exists
to undo". That objection retires with the split, and the comment holding it
must go with the page.

## The reconciliation

Depth 0 -> 1 crosses documents and the totals do not match. Measured off the two
goldens (both FY 2025-26, same source document livermore-budget-fy2026-2027;
spine pp.66-67, fund-flows pp.127-140 and 167-170), in dollars:

  fund-group/general   spine in  159,388,024   fund-level in  157,873,470
    gap 1,514,554 = 1,034,154 fund-balance draw + 480,400 transfers in
                       spine out 159,388,024   fund-level out 144,650,802
    gap 14,737,222 = 10,037,797 transfers out + 4,699,425 reserve increase
  fund-group/capital            gap 2,500,213 = fund-balance draw
  fund-group/internal-service   gap 6,147,533 = fund-balance draw
  special-revenue, enterprise, debt-service   gap 0

29 of the 30 revenue-category x fund-group pairs are equal between the two
documents; the exception is transfers/in -> general, which fund-flows carries
into 210/310/400/401/402/610/622/642 and into no fund of the general group.

EVERY GAP IS EXACTLY ACCOUNTED FOR by four spine node kinds: fund-balance/draw,
transfers/in, transfers/out, fund-balance/reserve-increase.

## Owner decisions, 2026-09-08

1. Depth 0 is today's spine chart, unchanged. Its server-rendered hero and tiles
   stay; the change is that its fund groups become openable.
2. revenue.html and spending.html are RETIRED. Nav drops to one chart entry.
3. The residual gets BOTH a `fisc verify` check and a visible mark on the chart.
   Not one or the other.

## The residual is carried, not computed

The client copies the four spine links' value_cents, fact_ids, locators and kind
VERBATIM onto one derived residual/<group> node in the fund column. It computes
no amount.

IT MUST NOT BE RE-POINTED ONTO A FUND. Capital has 11 funds and internal-service
5, and pp.127-140 do not say which fund a draw belongs to; attributing it would
invent an allocation. The imbalance between the node's inflow and outflow is the
residual and is meant to be visible.

NOT IN THE PROJECTION, and this is a refusal rather than a preference. Adding
these to fund-flows puts all-funds-gross and revenue-by-fund in one
Options.Scopes, which internal/check/scopepairs.go's projectionScopesAreDisjoint
ARM 3 refuses by name -- correctly, since they are the same money at two grains.
It would also move testdata/fund-flows.golden.json, break drill.mjs's and
fold.mjs's pinned counts, and SILENTLY FLIP A CAVEAT: spendingSides()
(internal/project/fundflows.go) would read a tier-4 residual under capital as
"capital is decomposed", so truncatedGroups drops 5 -> 4 and fundFlowsCaveats'
`decomposed` goes false, dropping the only-the-General-Fund caveat entirely.
That is a wrong-output defect a reviewer would not see in the diff.

Precedent for a client-side derived node: AGGREGATE_ID in capColumn is already
one, with derived:true, a rationale and a source note, checked by
tools/jscheck/drill.mjs. This is a weaker claim than that one, because the
aggregate sums and this copies.

## Not in scope

- Opening a tier-0 revenue category. filterToNode filters to a SUBTREE by parent
  chain; a revenue category is a source with no descendants, so following it
  needs a different filter that does not exist. Worth its own bead if wanted.
- Opening a tier-5 use on the spine. fund-flows decomposes only the General
  Fund, so a citywide "Wages & Benefits" has nowhere to go.
