title: The source pages render as a book, not as a raw .txt link
description:
OWNER, 2026-09-07: 'i somewhat wonder if we should render the source pages into a book like structure instead of txt pages.'

TODAY: withPageText (internal/export/export.go:1187-1209) copies each cited page's extracted text verbatim to dist/extracted/<doc>/pages/pNNNN.txt, and every footer and the provenance table link the raw file. A reader who follows a citation gets a plain-text file in a new tab. There is no styled page view anywhere on the site.

WHAT TO BUILD: a server-rendered HTML page per cited page -- the document title, 'page N', prev/next across the cited set, the PDF #page=N link, and a <pre> of the verbatim page text with each fact's token wrapped in a <mark> at its byte offset, linking to that fact's record.

THE DATA ALREADY SHIPS AND IS ALREADY SHAPED FOR IT. Confirmed by reading dist/facts/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027/pages/p0066.jsonl at 8444911: every record carries offset, token and id beside the amount.

IT REUSES AN INVARIANT THAT IS ALREADY CHECKED. fact-offset-points-at-token asserts the extracted page text AT the fact's offset IS that token, so the highlight is that check's arithmetic performed at render time rather than a second, weaker reading of the same page.

MUTATION THAT PROVES IT CAN FAIL: shift one record's offset by a byte and the <mark> lands off the token.

TWO CONSTRAINTS:
  - Go only, server-rendered. No app.js, so the node boundary is untouched and a contributor with only Go can still build it.
  - THE RAW .txt KEEPS SHIPPING. It is the audit artifact -- byte-identical to data/extracted, hashed in the manifest. A rendered view is a second reading of it, never a replacement, and a citation must still be able to name the bytes.

OFFSETS ARE BYTES, NOT RUNES. Slice with []byte in Go. A rune-indexed slice would drift on any page carrying a non-ASCII character and the drift would be invisible on the ASCII pages that are most of the corpus.

title: Pass 4's fixes ship unreviewed: doccheck's near-miss rule was rewritten and the audited sweep was done by hand
description:
The e12-claims review loop stopped at pass 4 for budget, not because the stopping rule was met. AGENTS.md, "Review is a loop, not a pass" says a pass's own fix ships unreviewed unless something is done about it (fisc-i92i is the standing instance); this is that record for commits f57cf8e and 06822fc.

WHAT THE LOOP DID, AND WHERE IT STOPPED.

- Pass 1 (before this session): six findings. Four fixed in dab61bc and a266a80, one filed as fisc-97n8, one folded in.
- Pass 2: three findings. One WRONG-OUTPUT fixed in 0fe6e67; two filed (fisc-97n8 again, fisc-lk62).
- Pass 3: four findings. Two WRONG-OUTPUT and one FAIL-OPEN fixed in df42a54; one was fisc-97n8 a third time.
- Pass 4: six findings. Three fixed in f57cf8e, two in 06822fc, one was fisc-97n8 a fourth time.

Pass 4 returned WRONG-OUTPUT and FAIL-OPEN findings, so the stopping rule -- stop when a pass returns neither -- was NOT met. A pass 5 is owed.

THE TWO DIFFS THAT NOBODY HAS REVIEWED, and what to look at first:

1. f57cf8e rewrote what doccheck considers a near-miss citation. The old rule was structural (anchor, bounded gap, quoted run that opens like a title) and produced a false positive in three consecutive passes. The new rule requires the quoted title to RESOLVE against the AGENTS.md anchors, and replaces the 40-character bound with a sentence-end rule. That is a different gate, not a narrowed one: it cannot refuse prose that quotes a non-section, and it can no longer catch a malformed citation of a since-renamed section or a near-MISSPELLED title. Both are declared in the comments and pinned; the review question is whether the declaration matches what the code does, and whether the sentence-end rule has its own false-positive shape the three previous ones did not.

2. 06822fc corrected five copies of the claim that ten years of the ACFR's (Unaudited) statistical section are audited, across a verify reason, a doc comment, a test message, two rule notes and README.md. The sweep was done by READING each hit, per AGENTS.md, "Before you quote a number" -- which also means no check confirms it was complete. The review question is whether a true "audited" was corrected by mistake, and whether a false one was left. The hits deliberately left alone are p54's statement, the Basis enum, and the FY2024-25 transfer and revenue rules.

ALSO UNREVIEWED, from earlier passes but never re-reviewed after their own fix: the drawn-state counts arm in tools/jscheck/year.mjs (dab61bc) pins the "N of the document's M facts" tail as a literal in the checker, because no template renders it -- disclosed at the time as an honest limit, and worth a second opinion against AGENTS.md, "The node boundary".

NOT A BLOCKER FOR LANDING, a record of what a pass 5 should cover. Gates at 06822fc: make pre-commit exit 0, fisc verify 46 passed 0 failed, facts.jsonl byte-unmoved against a fresh rebuild.

title: The ten-year pages label all ten columns 'audited' under the caveat saying the opinion does not cover them
description: Found by /code-review over main..HEAD on e12-claims (the pass that also produced dab61bc and a266a80). Not fixed in that pass: the cheap fix is a display seam, and the honest one is a re-basis whose cost is recorded below. WHAT SHIPS. Measured off `make site` at a266a80: - dist/history.html: 10 `audited` column chips, 10 `data-comparable-group="audited"`, and a cell tooltip on every one of its 22 rows x 10 columns reading `FY 2015-16 audited: $...`. - dist/balances.html: the same 10 chips and groups over 9 rows x 10 columns. All of it sits immediately below `statistical-section-unaudited`, which tells the reader p161 labels this section `(Unaudited)` and quotes p29 disclaiming all assurance over it. One page, two claims about the same ten columns. WHY THE GUARD DID NOT SEE IT. The audit-claim scan added in c76f4c8 (pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go, TestAPageDoesNotHeadItselfWithAnAuditClaimItsCaveatWithdraws) reads only each view's Title and Lede. Everything above is rendered from the column and cell data, which that scan never looks at. WHERE THE WORD COMES FROM, AND WHAT A RE-BASIS COSTS. The word is `Fact.Basis`. It is component 7 of `fact.MakeID` (internal/fact/fact.go:171), so re-basing the ACFR statistical-section facts rewrites every one of their ids and moves facts/facts.jsonl -- the audit trail CI compares byte for byte. `HistoryColumns` (internal/project/history.go:36) hard-codes `mapping.BasisAudited` for all ten columns, so both documents build empty unless it changes in lockstep. And both `disjointScopes` reasons (internal/check/scopepairs.go:60,67) open 'FY2016-FY2025 audited against ...'; a re-basis makes both false while leaving them green, which is the fail-open shape this project refuses. WEIGH THE DISPLAY FIX FIRST. A basis LABEL distinct from the basis ENUM, chosen per document, changes what these two pages print without touching a fact, a fact id, or facts.jsonl. It needs its own guard: the audit-claim scan widened past Title/Lede to the rendered column chips and cell tooltips, so a page cannot label a column with a word its own caveats withdraw. Whatever is chosen, the check is the deliverable as much as the wording -- a page that stops saying 'audited' with nothing pinning it will say it again.

title: A transposed table has no publication channel: no per-row fiscal year and no column identity axis
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 while implementing fisc-oakx.2, against the tree at 6ad828f. fisc-9tn4's quantity mechanism lets a rule READ ACFR p177 whole, but nothing lets it PUBLISH, and the blockers are schema, not vocabulary:

(1) NO PER-ROW FISCAL YEAR. In a transposed table (years as rows: p173, p176, p177, p180, p194) the fiscal year is the ROW label, but Fact.FiscalYear comes only from Column.FiscalYear (fact.FromValues), and Row has no override. Every non-skip column must declare a fiscal_year (internal/mapping/parse.go), and there is no honest one to write.

(2) NO COLUMN IDENTITY AXIS. Column identity is (fund_group, fund, fiscal_year, basis) and validateRule refuses duplicates among non-skip columns. p177's seven debt columns plus its total are the same fund scope in the same (per-row) year: they cannot be told apart in the schema at all, so even granting (1) they would collide, both at the parser and in fact ids.

(3) And the kind vocabulary, which is fisc-7jtl and stays there.

So the p177 rule (acfr-p0177-debt-by-type) reads all ten columns and publishes nothing: its amount columns are skip: true, its rows are skip: true. WHEN PUBLICATION LANDS, THE PAGE'S CHECK LANDS WITH IT, in internal/check over the published facts: cols 1-7 sum to col 8 per year row (measured off testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt: 2016 ties at 88,896,362, 2025 ties at 91,015,277, and 2024 is short by exactly 176,292, its own Financed Purchases cell). Until then the arithmetic guard is internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go, which reads the page through the production rule with the skips lifted in memory.

Whoever takes this should decide (1) and (2) together: a Row.FiscalYear override alone still leaves the columns indistinguishable.

title: doccheck's citePattern sees only the canonical citation form: a citation by verb, in backticks, or with no quoted title is invisible
description:
FOUND BY /code-review OVER f1691a3^..e387166, SECOND PASS.

citePattern requires ',' or ''s' immediately after the AGENTS.md anchor. Real citations in the tree do not all take that shape, and four of them were left pointing at text that had moved to docs/ WITHOUT doccheck saying a word:

  internal/mapping/acfr_p0041_test.go:548  AGENTS.md calls that guard "the designed answer"
  mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml:169  AGENTS.md calls the geometry guard "the designed answer"
  internal/project/sankey.go:111           AGENTS.md's review-loop table   (no quotes at all)
  testdata/README.md:74                    `AGENTS.md` names under "..."  (backtick separator)
  internal/check/departmentwide_test.go:421 "the shape the same file names one paragraph later"

All five are re-pointed at the docs/ file that now carries the text, so the tree is correct. WHAT IS NOT FIXED IS THE GATE: it still cannot see a citation whose verb is 'calls' or 'names', one wrapped in backticks, or one carrying no quoted title.

DO NOT JUST WIDEN THE REGEX. beadrefs' first run returned 73 findings and every one outside its own fixtures was false, because fisc- was an overloaded prefix; 'AGENTS.md' followed by loose prose has the same shape of risk, and narration's Makefile comment argues the general case -- a prose detector refuses true sentences and teaches people to reword around it.

Two options worth measuring against each other before choosing:
  (a) accept a bounded run of words between the anchor and the quote, then run it over the tree and check EVERY new finding by hand before wiring it in.
  (b) require the canonical form in new writing and let this check refuse the others as malformed, which is narrower and makes the rule teachable.

A citation with no quoted title at all is out of reach either way and should be said so rather than silently missed.
acceptance_criteria: tools/doccheck either resolves a citation whose anchor is separated from its quoted title by a bounded run of words, a backtick or a verb, or refuses those forms by name as malformed -- with the choice between the description's (a) and (b) MADE AND RECORDED, not left open. Whichever lands: run over the whole tree first, with every new finding checked by hand before it is wired into make pre-commit; the no-quoted-title case declared out of reach in doccheck's own doc comment rather than silently missed; and a mutation showing a citation of each newly-covered shape going red. RE-POINTING THE FIVE CITATIONS THE DESCRIPTION LISTS DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. They were fixed when this bead was filed and the gate was not; the description says so and this line repeats it because it is the way this bead gets closed wrongly.
notes: 2026-09-19, released and re-measured: tools/doccheck/main.go:78 is unchanged and still reads AGENTS\.md(?:'s|,), so the gate is exactly as this bead found it. Retitled the same day -- the old title led with the four dead pointers, which are gone, and a bead whose one-line form names its symptoms is one bd ready invites a session to close by re-checking them.

title: doccheck scans its own test fixtures, so it cannot have a negative-path fixture and its main() is untested
description:
FOUND BY /code-review OVER f1691a3^..af400d9.

The Makefile path list includes tools/, so doccheck walks tools/doccheck/main_test.go and treats the citations inside its synthetic fixture string literals as real ones. Two consequences, both confirmed:

(1) A FALSE POSITIVE ON A RENAME. Folding 'green because the gate fired' reported main_test.go:53 and :107 alongside the one real orphan in internal/check/statedtotals.go. The fixture is not a claim about the tree and should not have been counted.

(2) A NEGATIVE-PATH FIXTURE CANNOT BE WRITTEN AT ALL. A test wanting a deliberately dead citation would make the gate red over its own suite, so the exit-1 path of main(), the sort that makes a run read like a grep, and the len(anchors)==0 refusal are all untested. That last one is the arm that stops an unparseable AGENTS.md from passing every citation in the tree, and nothing exercises it.

beadrefs has the answer already: an 'exempt' map keyed by path with a reason, plus checkExemptions, which fails when a declared exemption names a file that is gone. Lift it. Its own declaration is tools/beadrefs/main_test.go, 'its fixtures are ids that must NOT resolve', which is exactly this case.

NOTE THE TRADE BEFORE COPYING IT. doccheck deliberately has no exemption list today, because the only other citation in main.go is the one its failure message prints and that one is worth checking. Exempting the TEST file alone keeps that property; exempting main.go would not.
close_reason:
Fixed while resolving a fail-open it was load-bearing for. tools/doccheck now carries an 'exempt' map with tools/doccheck/main_test.go declared ('its fixtures are citations that must not resolve'), plus checkExemptions, which fails when a declared exemption names a file that is gone -- the beadrefs pattern, lifted as this bead said to.

WHAT MADE IT URGENT rather than tidy: the fourth review pass found that the len(cites)==0 tripwire could not fire for the partial-pattern-loss regression its own comment names, because 8 of the 27 citations it counted were this command's own fixtures. Exempting them stops the fixtures standing in for a tree that is no longer being read.

The trade this bead warned about is kept: main.go is NOT exempt, because the only citation in it is the one the failure message prints and that one is worth checking.

title: Re-measure the finding mix: the prose share is the one number this project acts on
description:
RE-RUN THE PER-FINDING CLASSIFICATION the way AGENTS.md's audit did, and compare
the PROSE-NEW and FALSE-CLAIM shares against the 17% and 32-of-115 baselines.

WHAT THE REMEDY IS NOT, ANY MORE. This bead opened as the falsification of a
refactor -- "if the shares rose, the cut was wrong and the amputated arguments go
back inline" -- and that trade is settled the other way by the owner's decision
of 2026-09-22: this repository has no users, so documentation is for the people
working on it and a paragraph defending a rule is a paragraph to keep true for
nobody. docs/agents-md-charter.md, which was the argument, is deleted, and
AGENTS.md's "Where writing goes" says to argue for no rule anywhere.

SO THE MEASUREMENT IS STILL WORTH TAKING AND THE LEVER IT MOVES IS DIFFERENT. A
rising prose share now says the RULES are not carrying what the arguments used to,
which is a reason to sharpen a rule or to make one machine-checkable -- the
answer make narration, make beadrefs and make doccheck are each an instance of --
rather than a reason to write the argument back.

THE THIRD LANE'S NUMBERS ARE ALREADY IN THE NOTES and they got worse: 11 of 31
findings introduced by an earlier pass's own fix, 35% against 23%. That is about
the review loop rather than about the prose split, and fisc-i92i is where it
lands.
notes:
2026-09-08 A THIRD LANE'S NUMBERS, which is the re-measurement this bead asks for. It got worse.

fisc-yj4w.14, ec07625..f85a4c1, nine commits, presentation only. Five /code-review passes to AGENTS.md's cap, then one narrow pass over the last fix per fisc-i92i:
  pass 1  8      pass 4  4
  pass 2  6      pass 5  3
  pass 3  4      narrow  3
28 from /code-review, plus 2 golangci-lint caught in the fix commits' own new tests and 1 a mutation caught. 31 total.

DEFECTS INTRODUCED BY AN EARLIER PASS'S OWN FIX: 11 of 31, 35%, against the 23% fisc-yj4w recorded over its three 2026-08-31 lanes. Classified one at a time from the commit bodies, by which commit introduced the line the finding is about:
  lane's own feature commits   20
  introduced by a fix           11
  pre-existing                   0
The share rises with pass number the same way the earlier lanes' did, and harder at the end: all 3 of pass 5's findings were written by pass 4's fix, and all 3 of the narrow pass's by pass 5's.

NO PASS DECAYED TO ZERO. Pass 5 -- the last before the cap -- still found a defect a reader would have met: a drill replaced the chart's <desc> and dropped the pointer to the flow table, which the fold had just made a screen reader's only route to it.

THE DOMINANT SHAPE WAS AN ASSERTION WRITTEN AGAINST ONE RENDERING OF A THING, five times, and it is worth naming because it is not the "check that cannot fail" the earlier lanes counted -- each of these COULD fail, just not for the case it was named for:
  - a marker ending in ">", so an `open` attribute made strings.Index miss the element and the ships-closed arm was unreachable
  - a character class matching `open` and `open>` but not `open=""`
  - an anti-vacuity arm grepping the whole file for "max-width: 1180px" rather than the container rule
  - a heading arm that computed </summary> and never used it
  - a fixture ending in a period, in the commit whose subject was that periods hid the defect
Every one was fixed by widening what the check can SEE, never by loosening what it asserts.

CAVEAT ON COMPARABILITY: this lane is templates, CSS and one client function, where the earlier three were Go and mappings. A finding here is usually a sentence or an attribute, which is cheap to introduce and cheap to fix -- so the RATE may not be comparable to the 2026-08-31 lanes even though it is measured the same way. Whoever puts the evidence back should say so rather than tabling 23% and 35% side by side.
2026-09-12, A FOURTH LANE'S NUMBERS -- E13's spine merge (fisc-ko1j.1-.6), range 0923016..HEAD, reviewed in four passes by Fable lenses over a Fable-implemented lane. This is the re-measurement this bead asks for, on the first lane where the implementer and the reviewer were both Fable.

YIELD BY PASS. Four passes, stopping on AGENTS.md's condition rather than at the cap:
  pass 1  24  (four lenses: check, export seam, app.js, jscheck+claims)
  pass 2  16  (three lenses: the pass-1 fixes, app.js as shipped, check+claims)
  pass 3   4  (one lens: the pass-2 fixes)
  pass 4   3  (one lens: the pass-3 fixes) -- no WRONG-OUTPUT, no FAIL-OPEN, so the loop stopped
  total   47, of which 16 were fixed in-pass and 31 filed.

DEFECTS INTRODUCED BY AN EARLIER PASS'S OWN FIX: 15 of 47, 32%, classified one at a time by which commit wrote the line the finding is about.
  pass 1   0 of 24  (no prior pass)
  pass 2   8 of 16
  pass 3   4 of 4
  pass 4   3 of 3
Against the 23% fisc-yj4w recorded over the three 2026-08-31 lanes and the 35% this bead recorded for fisc-yj4w.14. THE SHARE RISES WITH PASS NUMBER HARDER THAN EITHER EARLIER MEASUREMENT: by pass 3 every finding was the previous pass's, and it stayed that way.

THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, worth reading before the next lane. Pass 3's own fix (1) was the defect it cited a bead for: stepShapes' guard counted the same marker its parse sliced on, which is fisc-0flg exactly, committed after fisc-0flg was closed by the same session. Pass 4 then found the same shape AGAIN in pass 3's seam arm -- an unguarded control call taking the module down -- and fixing it moved the defect one line into the detail string rather than removing it, which the run caught.

SO THE PATTERN IS NOT 'the loop introduces new kinds of defect'. It is that a fix reproduces the defect class it was written for, in the code it writes to check itself. Three of the four passes contain an instance.

WHAT DID NOT GET WORSE: PROSE-NEW. Of the 47, false claims in text this lane wrote run at roughly a quarter and every one was caught by grepping the corrected figure for its copies -- which is how the fifth copy of a stale tuple, and two doc sentences pass 1 wrote, were found. The refactor this bead is about is not implicated either way by this lane; the prose defects were in commit messages and doc comments, not in AGENTS.md's own arguments.

CAVEAT ON COMPARABILITY, in the spirit of the one this bead already carries: this lane is Go seams, a client, and a jscheck suite -- closer to the 2026-08-31 drill lane than to fisc-yj4w.14's templates-and-CSS. Its pass-1 yield of 24 is also inflated relative to the earlier lanes because review was DEFERRED to the end of a six-commit lane rather than run per commit, so pass 1 was reading 4,824 hand-written insertions where those lanes' first passes read one commit's worth.
2026-09-14 THE DEFERRAL FINDING OF THE 2026-09-12 NOTE IS NOW IN docs/review-loop-evidence.md, under 'Deferring the loop to a merge concentrates its yield into pass 1', written up at 94ec524 as the evidence for AGENTS.md's new merge-time-review rule: the four-pass 24/16/4/3 yield, the 4,824 insertions pass 1 read, the 15 of 47 introduced-by-fix against the 23% and 35% baselines, and a paragraph naming what it does NOT show. The rest of this bead's re-measurement is untouched -- the PROSE-NEW and FALSE-CLAIM shares the bead was opened to compare are not in that section, because the rule it supports is about WHEN the loop runs, not about the refactor.

title: two comments in the Budget Book mapping say column_headers is required and all-or-none; checkColumnGrids skips a part without it
description:
mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml SAYS TWICE THAT EVERY PART DECLARES
column_headers, and once that omitting it is a hard error. Both are false, and
the second is the one that matters because it describes a guard.

  line 71: "Every part below declares `column_headers`, one entry per column"
  line 3324: "EVERY PART DECLARES column_headers ... checkColumnGrids is per
             (doc_id, page) and all-or-none: a later part on one of these pages
             that omitted the list would be a hard parse error, not a silently
             weaker read."

MEASURED over the committed file: 166 parts. 152 carry `rows:` and every one of
those declares column_headers. FOURTEEN DO NOT, and all fourteen are
total_row-only rollup parts with no rows -- dept-city-council, dept-city-manager,
dept-city-attorney, dept-library and ten more. So the substantive claim is true
of the parts that read columns and the sentence as written is false of the file.

THE ALL-OR-NONE CLAIM IS FALSE OF THE CODE, not merely imprecise.
checkColumnGrids (internal/mapping/parse.go) opens its loop with

    if len(p.ColumnHeaders) == 0 { continue }

so a part omitting the list is SKIPPED. What the function actually enforces is
that any two parts on one page which BOTH declare must declare the same grid. A
later part on p167 omitting the list is exactly the "silently weaker read" the
comment says it cannot be.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A P2. AGENTS.md's "The extraction boundary" points at the
geometry column guard as the designed answer to a borrowed-token read, and its
force depends on the declaration being universal among row-reading parts. That is
true today by convention and NOT by any check, and the comment asserting a check
is what would stop the next reader from noticing.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE. Either correct both comments to what the code does, or
make the code do what they say -- a part with rows and no column_headers is a
parse error, which is enforceable and is probably the rule that was wanted. The
second needs a test proving a rows-bearing part without the list is refused AND
that a total_row-only part without it is still accepted.

Found while re-deriving AGENTS.md's own "all 139 parts" claim for fisc-vtvp; that
count was also false (166) and is deleted there.

title: narration's Go arm cannot see an erratum that wraps across two comment lines
description:
make narration's GO ARM IS A LINE-BASED grep, so the phrase it refuses --
"this comment used to say" -- is invisible the moment it wraps. Five words at
roughly 77 columns is a phrase that will wrap, and the wrap point is chosen by
whoever formats the comment rather than by whoever writes the erratum.

MEASURED IN THE SIBLING ARM, which had the same defect and is where this was
found: memcheck's patterns used a literal space, and
{"k":"The rule is X. This memory\nused to say Y."} exited 0 while the same text
on one line exited 1. There, 38 of 49 bodies span lines. The fix there was to
make every gap \s+, which a single-line grep cannot do.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS. The comment BLOCK is the unit, not the line: gather each run of
consecutive //-prefixed lines, join them with a space, and match the phrase over
the join. That is a small Go program of the tools/codehash shape and cannot be a
grep, which is why this is filed rather than folded into the arm.

WHAT IT WOULD COST TO GET WRONG. Joining across a blank line or across a
non-comment line would match a phrase spanning two unrelated comments; the test
has to include a fixture where the words are adjacent across such a boundary and
must NOT match.

NOT MEASURED: whether any comment in the tree carries a wrapped instance today.
The arm is green, which proves only that no UNWRAPPED one survives.

Found by /code-review over b2e67aa^..d86b4b3.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED after the fifth review pass of the same lane. The Go arm's grep
anchor `^[[:space:]]*//` was dropped at 22ba3be's successor, which closes the
TRAILING-COMMENT case (a review credit after code on the same line, which the
anchored form missed and a mutation confirmed). Two cases remain and both need
the comment-block scanner this bead is about:

  1. THE WRAP, which is what this bead was filed for.
  2. A BARE LINE INSIDE A /* */ BLOCK, which carries no // at all and so is
     invisible to any grep for //.

The second is rare in Go and rarer in this tree, but it is the same hole and the
same fix reaches both: gather the comment, join it, match over the join.
close_reason: Fixed. tools/narration/main_test.go pins the erratum wrapped across two line comments (:21), inside a block comment interior (:43) and inside a star-decorated block (:53). make narration is an arm of make pre-commit and is green at HEAD.

title: Compact AGENTS.md: convert checkable rules into gates, delete the prose they replace
description:
AGENTS.md IS 1,136 LINES AND ~13k TOKENS, and with bd prime's ~9.7k of memories
that is roughly 23k tokens of standing instruction before any work begins.
Measured 2026-09-05.

THE EVIDENCE THAT LENGTH IS NOT THE WHOLE PROBLEM, and it decides the shape of
this work. Over one lane (the fisc-eaic correctness lane, five review passes) the
rules FOLLOWED and the rules BROKEN split cleanly, and not by distance into the
file:

  FOLLOWED, every one a numbered or enumerated imperative: the eight-step review
  loop, the five-class triage, three-passes-at-least-five-at-most,
  adding-a-check-is-five-edits, prove-it-can-fail, nothing-leaves-a-pass-unfiled,
  rebuild-and-cmp, read-the-count-off-a-fresh-binary, never push, bd not
  TodoWrite, step 8.

  BROKEN, every one a prose paragraph mid-section: "History's home is git" (17
  times, in one lane), "one edit per script" (once), "do not write a bead id
  before filing it" (twice).

"History's home is git" sits at line 887 of 1136, twenty-nine lines into a
seventy-seven-line section whose first half is about a different topic. It was in
context the whole time.

SO THE FIRST MOVE IS NOT TRIMMING, IT IS CONVERTING. A rule that can be a gate
should be one, and the prose that asked for it is then deletable. `make
narration` already does this for the two phrases that only ever introduce history
into a source comment, and it would have caught all seventeen. Look for the
others: "one edit per script" is not checkable, but a bead id that does not exist
IS -- a commit-msg hook could resolve every fisc-* id it names.

THE RULE FOR THE PROSE THAT REMAINS:

  1. DELETION-BIASED, LESS IS MORE. Do not rewrite for concision. fisc-pm8f
     priced a rewrite at 42.5 minutes and 411k tokens for 148 lines, and
     AGENTS.md's own finding is that verification cost attaches to claims written
     or KEPT -- so deleting is cheap and restating re-imports the whole cost.
  2. NO MEASUREMENTS OF THINGS INTRINSIC TO THE REPO, in this file or in source
     comments. A count of our own rules, checks, parts, spans or files goes stale
     on the next commit. The file's own "Before you quote a number" section says
     this and the file does not always follow it.
  3. AN EXTRINSIC MEASUREMENT THAT IS CRITICAL TO THE IMPLEMENTATION MAY STAY,
     AND IT GOES WHERE THE VALUE IS USED -- immediately above the code that
     consumes it, not in a type doc or a section header a hundred lines away.
     Locality is the point: a figure next to its use is re-checked by whoever
     edits that line, and a figure in a distant doc comment is not.
  4. THE MEASUREMENTS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING PART AND ARE NOT THE TARGET. Every
     count against the documents, every reconciliation, and every "measured at
     <commit>" that pins a judgement stays verbatim. The failure mode to refuse
     is keeping an assertion while deleting the evidence behind it, which would
     leave the file making claims it can no longer support.

A SPECIFIC CANDIDATE, offered rather than decided: 334 of the 1,136 lines -- 29%
-- are the seven sections about the review loop, and the review loop is the
process that keeps hitting its five-pass cap. Whatever those words are buying, it
is not compliance. That is the section to read first, and it is also the one
holding the 115-finding audit, which must survive.

DO NOT DUPLICATE A RULE TO MAKE IT MORE VISIBLE. This file opens by explaining
that three files carrying overlapping copies of the same rules is how the copies
drift. Where a rule needs to be visible from the loop, use a cross-reference --
the file already links [Prove it can fail] and [Before you quote a number] that
way.
acceptance_criteria: every rule that can be mechanically checked is a gate and its prose is reduced to a pointer; no measurement of the repo's own contents remains in the file; every extrinsic measurement that stays is adjacent to the code or decision that uses it; every count against the documents and every pinned measurement survives verbatim; no rule is duplicated to make it visible; before and after line and token counts are in the close reason
notes:
CORRECTION TO THE CLOSE REASON'S FIRST MEASUREMENT, recorded here rather than by
rewriting it, because a close reason is a record.

It says "1,136 lines and ~14,202 tokens -> 1,105 lines and ~13,760". The second
pair was quoted from a measurement taken mid-lane rather than from the tree as
committed. Re-measured at f1d0815: 1,126 LINES AND ~14,082 TOKENS. So the
reduction is 10 lines and about 120 tokens -- under one percent, not the 2.7%
claimed.

The number was written from an earlier run instead of the run being described,
which is the defect AGENTS.md's "Before you quote a number" exists to name,
committed in the close reason of the bead that deleted three instances of it.

THE SMALLER FIGURE IS ALSO THE MORE HONEST RESULT AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE
CONCLUSION. The deletions were real -- the epic enumeration, three lane
anecdotes, both errata blocks, three intrinsic counts -- and roughly as much text
went back in describing the two new gates and correcting the false claims five
review passes found. The bead's own premise was that length is not the problem
and compliance is, so a lane that converted two prose rules into targets that go
red and left the file the same size did what it set out to do. Anyone quoting a
token saving from this lane should quote ~120, and should probably not quote it
at all.
close_reason:
DONE at 0158bf6..f1d0815 -- the two gates, the AGENTS.md compaction, and five
review-fix passes.

MEASURED: 1,136 lines and ~14,202 tokens -> 1,105 lines and ~13,760. That is a
2.7% reduction and it is NOT the result worth reporting, because the bead's own
evidence said length was not the problem. The result is the first acceptance
criterion.

CONVERTED, which was the stated first move. Two rules this file broke as prose
are now targets that go red:

  make beadrefs   refuses a fisc-* id naming no bead, over a path list covering
                  AGENTS.md, docs, source, site, mappings, data and testdata. It
                  resolves against .beads/issues.jsonl, which is committed, so it
                  needs no bd and no network and IS A CI JOB and in pages-build's
                  needs.
  make narration  gained a memory arm (fisc-kc3j, b2e67aa) refusing an erratum in
                  an injected memory.

`fisc-` TURNED OUT TO BE AN OVERLOADED PREFIX rather than a namespace, which is
why beadrefs is a Go command and not a grep: fact ids are fisc-f-<hash>, series
ids fisc-s-<hash>, the export marker .fisc-export, a scratch dir
.fisc-write-probe-*. The first run returned 73 findings and every one outside the
tool's own fixtures was false. Two live tokens are neither -- site's fisc-theme
and fisc-year -- and are declared with what each actually is.

DELETED: three counts of the repo's own contents, TWO OF THEM ALREADY FALSE.
"twelve epics and five open" (thirteen, and E10 had closed while E12 did not
exist in the list); "all 139 parts" (166, and the substantive claim is about the
152 that read rows); app.js's line count and the page-fixture count, both true
and pinning nothing. Every count against the DOCUMENTS survives verbatim.

CONSOLIDATED: three lane anecdotes into "What fifteen passes measured", which
proves the same claim over 115 classified findings. What was carried across is
what the audit does not state -- the four introduced-by-fix shapes, "a fix that

FIVE PASSES, 5-8-5-5-8 findings, stopping at the CEILING and not at step 6's

WHAT THE PASSES ACTUALLY FOUND, because it is the argument for the loop:
  - THREE SEPARATE COVERAGE GAPS in the gate, one per pass: .js/.tmpl/.py, then
    .css and requirements.txt, then .json. Each was the same class as the last.
  - THREE GUARDS THAT COULD NOT FAIL, all of them the loop's own output. The
    fourth pass's fix for the self-anchor rule shipped a test that passed on an
    unrelated error message; deleting the guard left the suite green.
  - A COMMIT MESSAGE ASSERTING TWO FIXES THAT WERE NOT IN THE TREE. `git show
    ab71b7a -- Makefile` is empty; the edits had been made and then reverted by a
    `git checkout -- Makefile` cleaning up a mutation test for a different fix.
    AGENTS.md names this class and not this route.
  - TWO LIVE COMMANDS quoted with answers they no longer gave (9 vs 14, 61 vs 92
    passes), partly because this session added review-fix commits of its own. Now
    pinned to ab71b7a or described rather than quoted.
  - A WRONG EXEMPTION DECLARATION caught by tightening the rule that was meant to
    police it: fisc-year was declared as living in site/app.js and lives in the
    templates.

FILED, all still open: fisc-wwft (P2 -- two comments in the Budget Book mapping
say column_headers is required and all-or-none; checkColumnGrids skips a part
without it, so the second is false OF THE CODE), fisc-ycs6 (P3 -- beadrefs would
silently drop a bead id carrying a second hyphen; latent, all 433 ids are
single-hyphen).

RANGE AUDIT over 0158bf6^..f1d0815, 27 claims from the seven commit messages
checked against the tree in one script: all 27 true.

title: Compact the 49 injected memories: delete errata, intrinsic counts, and what AGENTS.md already says
description:
THE MEMORIES CARRY THE DEFECT AGENTS.md FORBIDS IN SOURCE COMMENTS, and they are
worse placed for it: bd prime injects all of them into every session
automatically, so a stale line arrives in context whether or not anyone opens the
file it is about.

MEASURED 2026-09-05: 49 memories, ~7,500 words, roughly 9.7k tokens injected per
session. FIFTEEN of the 49 carry at least one stale-correction or errata line --
"CORRECTED 2026-08-29", "This memory used to say X", "the bead text describing it
as blocked is historical", "TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS MEMORY WERE WRONG".
AGENTS.md measured ten of 52 at 44be60d, so the RATE IS RISING rather than
falling. The eight largest memories are about 40% of the total words.

THE WORST OFFENDERS by errata count: transfers-lane-is-complete (6),
substrate-is-page-text (4), bd-reasserts-push-instruction (3),
fact-store-is-published (3), funding-sources-tie-by-fund-group (3),
scope-pages-are-dense (2). Re-measure rather than trusting this list.

THE RULE FOR THIS WORK, and it is deliberately narrow because the expensive
mistake is available in both directions:

  1. DELETION-BIASED, LESS IS MORE. Delete errata, history, and duplication.
     DO NOT rewrite for concision. AGENTS.md prices this: verification cost
     attaches to claims written or KEPT, so a deletion is the cheap half and a
     restatement re-imports the whole cost -- fisc-pm8f measured 42.5 minutes
     and 411k tokens for 148 lines of rewrite.
  2. KEEP THE RULE, DROP THE HISTORY THAT ARGUED FOR IT. A memory ending
     "CORRECTED: this used to say X" keeps the corrected statement and loses the
     sentence about X. Where the history IS the evidence for the rule, that is
     the hard case and it stays -- no filter separates those, so it is read by
     hand.
  3. NO MEASUREMENTS OF THINGS INTRINSIC TO THE REPO. A count of our own rules,
     checks, facts, scopes or files goes stale on the next commit and tells a
     reader nothing they could not measure. AGENTS.md's "Before you quote a
     number" already says this and the memories do not follow it. Counts against
     the DOCUMENTS stay verbatim -- "pp.85-125's 78 rows", "the corpus is 786
     pages", the reconciliation arithmetic -- because those are the project's
     subject and they are what stops a session re-deriving them.
  4. NO RULE THAT AGENTS.md ALREADY STATES. Both are injected into every
     session, so a memory restating AGENTS.md is the duplication that file was
     merged to end, arriving through the other channel.
  5. NO LIST OF OPEN BEAD IDS. transfers-lane-is-complete already learned this
     the hard way -- it named five open beads and four had closed. bd is the
     source of truth for status.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a cull. A memory that carries a document quirk, an arithmetic
proof or an environment trap earns its place however long it is.
fund-names-come-from-p256 and blind-scan-invents-rows are the good case.

MEASURE BEFORE AND AFTER, with the grep that produced the numbers above, and put
both in the close reason. Note that memories live in the Dolt DB and in NO git
artifact, so the commit message of the session doing this is the only record any
superseded memory leaves.
acceptance_criteria: no memory contains a stale-correction or errata line; no memory quotes a count of the repo's own contents; no memory restates a rule AGENTS.md states; no memory lists open bead ids; counts against the documents and arithmetic proofs are unchanged verbatim; the before and after token measurements are in the close reason
close_reason:
DONE at b2e67aa..729ba84 -- the compaction, plus five review-fix passes.

MEASURED, before and after, with `bd memories --json` piped through a word count:

  before: 49 memories, 7,628 words, ~10,145 injected tokens
  after:  49 memories, 6,364 words, ~8,464 injected tokens   (-1,264w, -17%)

Seventeen memories edited, none deleted. The acceptance criteria are met on the
first four points: no memory carries a stale-correction or errata line, none
quotes a count of the repo's own contents, none restates a rule AGENTS.md states,
none lists open bead ids, and every count against the documents and every
reconciliation is unchanged verbatim -- 786 pages, 36 mapped, pp.85-125's 78
rows, 223 of 786, the fund-group arithmetic, tocip-constants-are-printed.

THREE MEASUREMENTS WORTH KEEPING, because they are the reason the bead's own
list was a floor rather than an answer.

(1) THE ERRATA GREP FOUND 14 WHERE THIS BEAD SAID 15, and the difference is not
a counting error in either -- it is that no grep is the criterion. Two of the
memories the grep flagged carried history that IS the evidence for their rule and
were kept whole (amounts-fail-closed's account of the xberg transcription, which
is why the parser rejects a leading minus the current corpus never contains), and
one the grep missed was found by reading.

(2) THREE OF THE FIVE `:NNN` LINE NUMBERS IN adding-a-check-is-five-edits NO
LONGER LANDED on what they named. internal/check/check.go:162 was a comment line
rather than All(); checks_test.go:114 and :136 were a map entry and a comment
rather than the two assertions the memory sends you to. So the intrinsic-count
rule earned itself inside a single memory.

(3) test-tempdir SAID testdata/pages/ HOLDS 24 AND IT HOLDS 25.

THE GATE, which was not in the acceptance criteria and is what stops this
regressing: tools/memcheck, run as a second arm of `make narration`. It refuses a
past-tense claim about a memory's own former text. The phrase list is narrow on
purpose and the boundary was found by testing rather than by argument -- a first
pattern refused "the city corrected 2024's printed total", which is a true
sentence about the corpus.

THE ARM IS ADVISORY BY CONSTRUCTION and this is the thing to know before trusting
it: memories live in the Dolt DB and in no git artifact, so nothing in a checkout
lets CI read them. It warns and continues whenever bd is absent, failing, or
holding no memories at all. narration's GO arm is now a CI job (it reads
committed source) and is in pages-build's needs, so that half is a real gate.

FIVE REVIEW PASSES, 6-7-4-5-4 findings, and the loop stopped at the CEILING
rather than at step 6's condition -- the fifth pass returned two FAIL-OPEN
findings. Two passes found a defect an earlier pass's own fix had introduced, and
the fifth found that the fourth's commit message asserted a correction that had
not landed. The lane's central fail-open was found by the FOURTH pass: every
pattern used a literal space while 38 of the 49 bodies are hard-wrapped, so the
check had been half-blind since it landed, and no test could reach the case
because the fixtures' hand-rolled quote() emitted a raw newline that
encoding/json rejects.

Filed and still open: fisc-h5vu (the 23 generic Go/byob memories, ~1,400 words,
ruled out of scope by the owner), fisc-fv71 (the same wrap hole in narration's Go
arm, which needs a comment-block scanner rather than a pattern change), fisc-kaq1
(memcheck's two SHAPE patterns can refuse a true sentence about the corpus),
fisc-rrev (the nested-value refusal has no escape hatch if bd's JSON shape
changes), fisc-1mln (a dated line-leading CORRECTED is reported twice).

Because memories leave no git artifact, b2e67aa's commit message is the only
record that the deleted text existed.

title: The reader surface: a ten-year view, server-rendered like trends.html
description:
THE PAYOFF. Ten years of history is what a resident wants and what the site
cannot answer today, and facts nobody can see are not the product.

WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON, measured 2026-09-05 rather than assumed:
pkg/cmd/export/data.go builds six views -- index.html (the spine sankey),
revenue.html and spending.html (fund-flows), trends.html (revenue-trends),
caveats.html and provenance.html. export.View already carries Path, Nav,
Template, Projection and optional YearStems, so ADDING A VIEW IS AN ENTRY IN A
SLICE plus a template. The multi-view shell is done (fisc-qkh) and E11 landed
the pages on it.

trends.html IS THE FORM TO COPY, not a new chart. It is rendered ENTIRELY
SERVER-SIDE and loads no script (see trendsPageData in internal/export/page.go),
which is the property this view wants too: a ten-year table works with
JavaScript off, needs no d3, and needs nothing from site/app.js -- so it does not
owe a tools/jscheck module, which is the expensive half of any client change
here (see AGENTS.md, "A change to app.js ships its check in the same commit").
A chart over these series is a LATER and separate change; do not bundle it.

THIS ABSORBS WHAT IS LEFT OF fisc-f75. That bead's stated acceptance -- a toggle
between documents, and empty/error states -- was already met by E11 and its
description was stale in three ways. What was actually left of it is that no view
renders the ACFR, and this is that view.

THE unprojectedScopes CONSEQUENCE, and it is the part that is easy to miss.
acfrGeneralFundScope is a DECLARED entry in unprojectedScopes
(internal/check/coverage.go), and staleDeclarations refuses an entry that has
stopped being true. So the first ACFR view retires or rewrites that declaration
IN THE SAME COMMIT, and the entry's reason string is printed verbatim by
fisc verify on every run -- an overstatement there is published, per the
detail-ties-to-spine-shape memory's point (4). Count what the view actually
draws before writing the string.
acceptance_criteria: a view renders the Statistical Section's published series without JavaScript; the acfr scope's unprojectedScopes entry is retired or rewritten in the same commit and its reason describes what is actually drawn; no tools/jscheck module is owed, or the reason one is owed is stated
notes: 2026-09-06 THE DESCRIPTION'S unprojectedScopes PREMISE HAD AGED, measured before working it: it names acfrGeneralFundScope as the entry the first ACFR view retires or rewrites, but lane 3 (5e474ae) added two MORE entries -- acfr-fund-balances and acfr-changes-in-fund-balances -- and this view draws THOSE scopes, not p41's. What actually happened: both statistical entries were RETIRED (facts-are-projected went red demanding it the moment the projections landed, before the deletion), and acfrGeneralFundScope's entry was REWRITTEN, not retired -- p41 stays undrawn, still shares zero keys with the published set at the full and mergeable grains (measured over the committed store), but its 'the site draws budget years' sentence was false once history.html drew ten audited years, and verify prints that string verbatim.
close_reason: Landed on e12-statistical-section. TWO DOCUMENTS AND TWO VIEWS: the two schedules are two row axes, so each got its own projection on the seriesSpec core (fund-balances, changes-in-fund-balances; the pair share zero keys at the full and the mergeable grain, measured) and its own one-word page -- history.html (nav 'Ten-year history', 220 figures under Revenues/Expenditures/Excess) and balances.html (nav 'Fund balances', 90 figures under the two printed blocks). Server-rendered on site/history.html.tmpl, no app.js, no jscheck module owed. Columns floor stated in HistoryColumns; mutation: narrowing it to FY2017+ turned TestPublishedDocumentsAreWhatTheCorpusBuilds red on both stems. Missing-series mutation: with reconcileSeriesCounts removed, a document short a mid-section series exported clean and TestTheHistoryViewRefusesADocumentShortASeries went red saying 'was accepted'. Both statistical unprojectedScopes entries retired with facts-are-projected red first; acfrGeneralFundScope's entry rewritten (see notes). The inherited series.go extraction proved output-neutral: all seven pre-existing documents byte-identical minus generated_by against 5e474ae. Contract: docs/acfr-history-contract.md. Chart follow-up filed as fisc-s7ia. facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify --strict 46 passed, 0 failed.

title: Batch one: net position pp.163-166 and fund balances pp.167-169
description:
THE FIRST MAPPED BATCH, and it is the two table families a resident actually
reads: what the city owns and owes, and what its funds held, over ten years.

  p163      Net Position by Component
  p164-166  Changes in Net Position          (one table across three pages)
  p167      Fund Balances of Governmental Funds
  p168-169  Changes in Fund Balances of Governmental Funds  (one table, two pages)

WHY THESE FIRST. They are the closest thing in the Statistical Section to money
the site already draws, so they are the batch whose reader payoff needs the least
new chart. Two of the four straddle a page break, which is the shape
CheckSpanningTotals (internal/mapping/resolve.go) already exists for -- nine such
blocks are already handled in the Budget Book lanes -- so the hard part is
exercised early rather than discovered late.

BLOCKED ON THE SURVEY AND ON THE p177 PROOF, and not merely by convention: these
tables' column kinds are unclassified, and the Changes-in-Fund-Balances family
conventionally carries a "debt service as a percentage of noncapital
expenditures" column, which is exactly the shape fisc-9tn4 was settled for.

THE TIE THIS BATCH OWES, per E12's acceptance criterion. Ten years of one
document's own history means the tables corroborate each other, and a batch that
publishes without one is the bucket E10's text refuses. The candidates, to be
confirmed rather than assumed:
  - p163's Net Position by Component against p164-166's Changes in Net Position:
    the change from one year to the next must equal the year-over-year movement
    in the total.
  - p167 and p168-169, the same relationship on the fund-balance side.
  - the FY2025 column of p167 against ACFR p41, which is already mapped and
    published at acfr-general-fund-summary. If those tie, the Statistical
    Section is anchored to a page the corpus has already checked, which is a
    stronger claim than anything internal to the section.
That third one is the valuable one. Measure it before writing the check, and if
it does not tie, the reason is a finding worth its own bead.

SCOPE: its own, per the one-scope-per-schedule rule (see the
detail-pages-double-the-spine and detail-ties-to-spine-shape memories). These are
AUDITED figures for fiscal years the Budget Book does not print, so they do not
double the spine -- but the scope and its unprojectedScopes entry land in the
commit that lands the facts and never before.
acceptance_criteria: the four tables publish at their own scope with an unprojectedScopes entry landing in the same commit; at least one corroboration check ties two of them, or ties p167's FY2025 column to the already-published ACFR p41, and it is proven failable by mutation; no non-amount column becomes a fact
notes:
2026-09-05 FOUR CORRECTIONS FROM fisc-oakx.1's SURVEY (docs/acfr-statistical-section.md), each measured off the pages.

(1) THE 'debt service as a percentage of noncapital expenditures' SHAPE IS A ROW, NOT A COLUMN -- p169's last row, percentages across every year column. This batch therefore needs the row-level quantity override fisc-oakx.2's note records, not only the column kind.

(2) BOTH INTERNAL CORROBORATION CANDIDATES FAIL AS PRINTED. p163 year-over-year deltas equal p166's Change in Net Position for 2017 ONLY (2018: delta 6,840,766 vs printed 19,161,491; 2024: 7,628,754 vs 15,415,297; 2025: 41,770,382 vs 43,098,461 -- restatements are not shown). p167 deltas vs p169's Net change: ties 2017 only (2018 off 190,263; 2025 off 2,667). The p167 FY2025 <-> ACFR p41 tie is the remaining candidate and is unmeasured.

(3) THE PAGES CARRY PRINTED DEFECTS THE RULES MUST DECLARE (stated_total_deltas). p164's Total business-type activities expenses row is RIGHT-SHIFTED one year for 2017-2023: each printed total equals the PREVIOUS year's column sum, and the true 2023 sum (51,821,693) is printed nowhere. 2023 cells copied from 2022: p165 Net (Expense) Revenue governmental (prints -95,830,768, recomputes -101,560,632), p166 Change in Net Position governmental (prints 10,611,708), p169 Total other financing sources (prints -1,767,367, recomputes -2,299,891) and p169 Net change in fund balances (prints -16,975,824, recomputes 19,139,098). Downstream totals on each page are internally consistent with the wrong figures.

(4) NO TABLE IN THIS BATCH CAN CARRY column_headers -- all five pages head columns with bare years (fisc-wiyg) -- and p163's kind is unresolved: net position is not a fund_balance (fisc-7jtl). pp.164-169 fit existing kinds; decide what p163 does before mapping it.
2026-09-05, WHAT fisc-oakx.2 LEAVES FOR THIS BATCH: Row.Quantity exists and is validated (a percentage row needs no category and may not carry a counterpart); p169's row is written as {label: "Debt service as a percentage of noncapital expenditures", quantity: percentage} — mind the wrapped label if the page breaks it. The row arm's mutation proof obligation lands here (TestRowQuantityOverrideIsLoadBearing shows the shape on an inline page; this batch owes it on the real p169). Grammar limits to know: quantity.Percentage takes no dash-zero and no parenthesized negative, and quantity.Number takes no dash — extend fail-closed in internal/quantity if a page prints one. Also: total_row over a NON-AMOUNT COLUMN is refused at parse (p168-169 is fine — its percentage is a row, and a row override does not trip the refusal), and p163's kind question is fisc-7jtl as this bead already says.
REVIEW DEPTH ON THIS LANE, recorded because it departs from AGENTS.md's three-pass minimum and the log alone would not say why. Two passes ran over 6ad828f..HEAD, not three: pass one (opus, filed fisc-us6f/t2qd/1wix/fdff), pass two (four fable lenses, filed fisc-7hyv/q559/7jb5/r21r/vypw/g7bf/m4sg/gqvi/m5cl/efo8/s9c2/haum/plus the scopepairs one). Neither pass returned a WRONG-OUTPUT or FAIL-OPEN finding. The owner stopped at two on the ground that Fable implemented the lane and reviewed it, and merged to main locally at dc42d6d. Nothing shipped unreviewed by that choice: pass two fixed nothing, so AGENTS.md's 'the last pass's own fix ships unreviewed' hazard does not apply here -- the only file pass two touched is the generated .beads/issues.jsonl export. The one fix that DID land mid-loop, cab0c73's tie correction, was inside pass two's range and was independently recomputed by two of its four lenses.
close_reason: Landed at lane 3 on e12-statistical-section, NARROWED from four tables to the two that could publish honestly (the bead's authority to narrow was explicit): p167 Fund Balances (scope acfr-fund-balances, 90 facts) and p168-169 Changes in Fund Balances (scope acfr-changes-in-fund-balances, 220 facts incl. the ten printed excess cells), FY2016-2025 audited, 310 facts in all, every total-bearing rule tying exactly in all ten columns. The corroboration criterion is met by excess-of-revenues-identity (within-p168: revenues - expenditures = printed excess, all ten columns, mutation-proven). p163 -> fisc-311g (blocked by fisc-7jtl); pp.164-166 -> fisc-xd6r (defective as printed); p169's Other Financing block reads whole and publishes nothing -> fisc-qyrw. Acceptance line 'the four tables publish' was corrected in notes: two publish, and no non-amount cell became a fact.

title: A total_row consumed by one rule can be published as a fact by another, unguarded
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04, found by the FOURTH review pass over the seams lane (471c56a^..f4080b5).

fisc-2x7y's fact-citations-are-declared refuses two facts citing one (doc_id, page, offset) without a declared counterpart. It covers the case it was written for and NOT this one.

THE SHAPE. ACFR p41's acfr-p0041-gf-fund-balances declares three rows skip: true so their figures are consumed rather than left as unexplained text. Two of them -- "Transfers in" and "Transfers (out)" -- are rows the sibling rule acfr-p0041-gf-other-financing-sources PUBLISHES, so un-skipping one makes two facts share an address and the check refuses it. The third, "Total Other Financing Sources (Uses)", is that rule's TOTAL_ROW. A total_row's figure is consumed as a total and cited by NO fact, so un-skipping it collides with nothing and the check has nothing to compare.

MEASURED, and note the second reading is the one that matters:

  un-skip it, category transfers/out, kind transfer_out
      -> 43 passed, 1 FAILED, but the failure is
         fact-transfer-orientation-is-declared complaining the row prints
         "(25.19)" while declaring sign positive. Nothing about the doubling.
  un-skip it, and ALSO declare sign: netted, which is CORRECT for that figure
      -> 44 passed, 0 FAILED. The store publishes the block's own printed
         total as a third transfer_out fact: ACFR transfers/out becomes
         25.72 + 25.19.

So the plain mutation is caught for an unrelated reason -- the green-because-the-gate-fired shape -- and an author careful enough to declare the sign correctly gets no objection at all.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY fisc-2x7y AGAIN: there is no shared address to key on. What is doubled is a figure the corpus uses as a TOTAL against rows it also publishes, which is a relationship between a rule's total_row and another rule's facts, not between two facts.

WHAT A GUARD WOULD HAVE TO DO: notice that a fact's (doc_id, page, offset) is the offset some rule's total_row resolves to. That needs the resolved total position, which CheckTotals already computes at build time, so the information exists and is thrown away before internal/check sees it. Whether it belongs in the build report or in a check is the open question.

NOT URGENT: the committed rules declare the skip correctly and the rule file now says which two of the three are guarded and which is not. It is an unguarded hazard on a page that already demonstrated the last one.

title: Make the real API usable from its doc alone: the 442 cross-package identifiers, 24% of them under-documented
description:
Make the API usable from its documentation alone, over the surface that is
actually an API: THE 442 IDENTIFIERS REFERENCED FROM ANOTHER PACKAGE, minus
whatever fisc-jbu4 unexports -- not the 1,422 that revive's `exported` rule
currently forces a doc onto.

WHY THIS IS THE PRIORITY. It is the only measured defect in this whole line of
work that can cause a bug at a CALL SITE. fisc-b8z0 judged 143 exported symbols
from `go doc -all` alone with the bodies hidden:

    SUFFICIENT         86   60%
    UNDER-DOCUMENTED   34   24%
    LEAKY              15   10%
    MISSING             8    6%   (Error()/Unwrap() on documented error types)

A QUARTER OF THE SAMPLED PUBLIC API CANNOT BE USED CORRECTLY FROM ITS DOC. That
sample is 143 of ~542 exported identifiers revive requires a doc on, so roughly
three quarters of the surface has never been assessed at all.

THE FIVE WORST, already named and still true:
  - iostreams.Test returns three identical *bytes.Buffer and never says which is
    which, so a wrong guess passes silently.
  - cmdutil.Hintf's nil passthrough is undocumented while its sibling WithHint
    documents it -- a nil turns success into reported failure.
  - geom.Grid.Band states no bounds contract while its sibling Index returns -1
    by design (fisc-yjjb; a fix exists on the abandoned comment-sweep branch).
  - The four singular registry lookups are silent about copying while the plural
    forms promise copies, on a type that promises concurrency safety.
  - amount.Parse never says a rejection is a *ParseError nor whether ErrAbsent
    is bare or wrapped.

WHAT AN EXPORTED DOC MUST COVER, per AGENTS.md: error conditions and which
errors are sentinels worth matching; behaviour on zero, empty and nil; whether
an argument or receiver is mutated; ordering or sortedness guarantees; units;
whether a returned slice or map is safe to retain or modify; panics;
concurrency safety. "Restating what the code does" is not a defect here -- it is
the job.

THE VERIFICATION IS THE OWNER'S OWN FRAMING, and it is falsifiable: HIDE THE
BODY, HAND AN AGENT ONLY THE DOC, AND SEE WHETHER IT CAN USE THE SYMBOL
CORRECTLY. That is how the 24% was measured in the first place, so the same
method scores the fix. Where it cannot, the doc is not finished.

THIS PASS MAY GROW THE TREE and that is correct. The exported side measured 6%
droppable against 51% on the internal side -- the API needs more prose, the
internals need less. Do not let a volume target leak into this bead.

BLOCKED BY fisc-jbu4. Documenting a symbol that should not be exported is wasted
twice.

title: Unexport the 104 non-field identifiers no other package references
description:
Unexport the 104 non-field candidates from fisc-ynuo's analysis: exported
identifiers with NO reference from any other package, excluding struct fields,
which are riskier and are a separate bead.

  7 funcs, 48 types, 26 non-interface methods, 18 consts, 5 vars

WHY FIRST. They carry 958 doc-comment lines between them and the fields, written
to satisfy revive's `exported` rule. Documenting a symbol that should not be
exported is wasted twice -- once writing it, and again every time it goes stale
-- so this precedes any work on the API docs.

THE GATE IS THE COMPILER, which makes this the cheapest kind of change to
verify: go build ./... && make test && make lint. If it still builds, the
identifier really had no external user.

EXCEPTIONS THAT STAY BY DECISION, NOT BY USAGE (~8 of the 104):
  Options and Options.Validate() in pkg/cmd/{build,export,verify} --
  byob-command-shape.1 wants Options + NewCmdXxx, byob-input-validation.5 wants
  Validate() first. The shape is the decision; usage does not govern it.

ONE TRAP: mapping.Kinds MUST NOT BE UNEXPORTED. It shows as reachable only from
tests, and it is exported precisely so another package can iterate the closed
set -- TestKindsIsTheClosedSet says so, and internal/registry must refuse a
taxonomy kinds: member that is not one of these while being unable to import
mapping (the edge closes a cycle in the test build). Same reasoning for
iostreams.Test.

LEADS WORTH DECIDING INDIVIDUALLY RATHER THAN MECHANICALLY:

  amount.ParseOrZero HAS NO CALLER AT ALL -- confirmed by x/tools deadcode from
  ./cmd/fisc as well as by the reference analysis. AGENTS.md's provenance-
  invariants section presents it as the sanctioned opt-out: "ParseOrZero opts
  out only where a rule has declared that blanks mean zero for that table." So
  the tree documents a mechanism nothing uses, and the question is delete-vs-keep
  rather than export-vs-unexport. Deleting it means editing AGENTS.md in the
  same commit.

  mapping.Parse -- no cross-package caller, confirmed by grep as well.
  mapping.Load -- unreachable from main.
  iostreams.IsStdinTTY / IsStdoutTTY / IsStderrTTY -- zero callers outside the
    package, which fisc-gyg9 already found from the other side: the comment
    saying "the only decisions this drives are colorizing and prompting" is
    false because nothing colorizes and nothing prompts. Unexporting these and
    fixing that comment belong in one commit.
  site.Assets -- reachable through site.FS(), so the var itself can go
    unexported; the //go:embed directive is attached to it and must not move.

METHOD, and its known false positives. The list came from a go/packages analysis
resolving every exported identifier to the set of OTHER packages referencing it
(kept at /tmp/exports; table at /tmp/sweep/exports.txt -- /tmp is not durable,
re-run if cleared; see fisc-ynuo for whether it becomes a committed tool).
THREE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES WERE FOUND AND FIXED while building it and they
are why this list is 104 and not 366:
  - GENERIC TYPE PARAMETERS. [K comparable], [V any] are TypeName objects and
    report Exported() true for any single capital letter, so they scored as
    exported types with no users.
  - -ldflags -X vars. internal/build's Version/Commit/Date are set by the linker
    by symbol path and have no Go reference by design.
  - INTERFACE-DISPATCHED METHODS. A call through an interface records against
    the interface method, never the concrete one, so 290 methods looked unused.
A fourth class may remain: anything reached only via reflection, a template, or
//go:embed. Re-run the analysis rather than trusting the stored list.

VERIFICATION. go build ./... ; make pre-commit ; make lint ; rebuild bin/fisc
and read the check count off THAT run; fisc build --output bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl
and cmp against facts/facts.jsonl. facts.jsonl must not move.
close_reason: 76 of the 104 unexported at 4c91136; the other 28 recorded in that commit body with the class each belongs to. Six stay by byob-shape decision (Options/Validate x3), four have zero callers anywhere and are a delete-vs-keep decision now at fisc-6ule, seven were name collisions the compiler caught (registry.Error would have become the builtin `error`), four are used by an external test package, four are sentinel errors, and three appear in an exported signature. Gate: go build and go test clean, make lint 0 issues, facts.jsonl byte-identical to a rebuild, fisc verify --strict 42 passed 0 failed off a binary built from that tree, and 667 insertions against 667 deletions. The analysis defect this exposed is recorded on fisc-ynuo; the pre-existing API wart it found is fisc-fhq6.

title: (BUG) NewGrid's doc claims a guard it cannot perform, and the key-names claim is false in two files
description:
Two false claims in internal/geom, both measured, NEITHER RECORDED ANYWHERE
ELSE. Checked against fisc-gyg9 with `bd show`: it carries the page-orientation
claim from the same file but not these two.

They are filed separately because the branch that fixed them is being
abandoned. Fixes exist at comment-sweep 123eca1 and can be cherry-picked; this
bead is so the findings survive if it is not.

(1) internal/geom/grid.go, NewGrid's doc: "Headers must be in printed order and
    must not overlap, because the caller's list is a claim about column ORDER:
    a page that dropped a column has to fail rather than shift every figure one
    place."

    NEWGRID CANNOT DO THIS. Built with Budget Book p167's four real header
    spans, and then with the second one dropped, BOTH SUCCEED:

        full grid     err=nil  bands (265.75,328.305] (328.305,406.44]
                               (406.44,484.49] (484.49,+Inf)
        dropped       err=nil  bands (265.75,367.365] (367.365,484.49]
                               (484.49,+Inf)
        Index(477.82)  full=2  dropped=1
        Index(555.94)  full=3  dropped=2

    Every figure right of the drop files one band early, silently -- exactly the
    outcome the comment says the check prevents. `h.Lo <= prev.Hi` only rejects
    out-of-order or overlapping spans, which a dropped column never produces.
    Dropped-column detection lives in matchHeaders in internal/mapping/geometry.go,
    whose own doc states it correctly: "In-order matching catches a page that
    DROPPED a column -- an entry simply stops matching."

    CLASS: prose asserting a guard performs a check its condition cannot
    perform. Same shape as the green-because-the-gate-fired failure mode, one
    level up -- a reader takes the rationale as coverage that is not there.

(2) internal/geom/geom.go, on Word.UnmarshalJSON: "at 208k words in this corpus
    the key names would outweigh the values" -- AND THE SAME SENTENCE at
    tools/extract.py:301-302. Two copies, one defect each, per fisc-xbd4.

    MEASURED by re-encoding all 208,221 committed words both ways:

        flat rows [x0,y0,x1,y1,"text"]      7.32 MiB
        object rows {"text":…,"x0":…}      12.68 MiB
        pure value bytes                    6.13 MiB  (30.86 B/word)
        key-name overhead                   5.36 MiB  (27.00 B/word)

    Keys are 0.87x the values, not more. Counting bare key names without quotes
    and colons gives 2.5 MiB against 6.13, which is worse for the claim. The
    flat shape is still the right choice and the argument for it survives; the
    comparison does not.

    Two independent measurements agreed. NOTE THE METHOD FAILURE WORTH KEEPING:
    the first attempt to verify this claim "confirmed" it by finding the same
    sentence in tools/extract.py -- confirming a claim against a second copy of
    itself. That is fisc-xbd4's duplication problem operating on the checker
    rather than the checked.

    Adjacent, already filed as fisc-fbnj: extract.py's neighbouring
    "18.7 MiB against what fits in 7.6" figures do not reproduce either, though
    that sentence's whitespace argument holds under every variant.

Both found by an adversarial verification pass that attacked all 77 factual
claims in internal/geom/{geom.go,grid.go}; 68 survived. The other six that did
not are fisc-sn7v.

title: Only 31% of exported identifiers are used outside their package; 356 are unexport candidates carrying 958 doc lines
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03. Two tools, neither added to go.mod: x/tools' deadcode via
`go run ...@latest`, and a go/packages analysis (kept at /tmp/exports, table at
/tmp/sweep/exports.txt) that resolves every exported identifier to the set of
OTHER packages referencing it.

THE HEADLINE. 1,422 exported identifiers -- package-level declarations, methods
and struct fields. Only 442 (31%) are referenced outside their own package. 57
(4%) are referenced only by another package's TESTS. 923 (64%) are never
referenced outside the package that declares them.

THE 923 SPLIT IN HALF, and the split is the whole result:

  567 MUST STAY EXPORTED and have no reference BY DESIGN
      290  methods dispatched through an interface -- the call is recorded
           against the interface method, never the concrete one
      274  struct fields carrying a json/yaml tag: serialization contracts
        3  internal/build's Version/Commit/Date, set by `-ldflags -X`, which
           names the symbol by path

  356 ARE GENUINE UNEXPORT CANDIDATES, and they carry 958 doc-comment lines --
      8% of all production comment prose, written to satisfy revive's `exported`
      rule on identifiers that did not need to be exported.
        7 funcs, 48 types, 26 non-interface methods, 18 consts, 5 vars,
        252 untagged struct fields

  For context: 3,948 comment lines sit on exported identifiers at all, of which
  1,869 (47%) are on the 923.

DEADCODE, from ./cmd/fisc, found nine unreachable funcs. The intersection with
"no cross-package use" is the strongest signal, and three are worth naming:

  amount.ParseOrZero HAS NO CALLER. AGENTS.md's provenance-invariants section
  presents it as the sanctioned opt-out -- "ParseOrZero opts out only where a
  rule has declared that blanks mean zero for that table" -- so the tree
  documents a mechanism nothing uses.

  mapping.Parse has no cross-package caller (confirmed by grep as well as by
  the type analysis); mapping.Load is unreachable from main.

  iostreams.IsStdinTTY / IsStdoutTTY / IsStderrTTY have zero callers outside
  their package, which fisc-gyg9 already recorded from the other direction: the
  comment saying "the only decisions this drives are colorizing and prompting"
  is false because nothing colorizes and nothing prompts.

  Genuinely dead unexported funcs: check.declaredToCIPGroups,
  pkg/cmd/export.buildProjections. Also unreachable: export.Write,
  project.ContestedTotals, project.GroupExpenditure, mapping.Kinds,
  iostreams.Test -- the last two used only by tests, which are not entry points.

CAVEATS, because an unchecked number is a defect here.
  - THREE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES WERE FOUND AND FIXED while building this, and
    the first is a warning about the method: generic TYPE PARAMETERS ([K
    comparable], [V any]) are TypeName objects reporting Exported() true, and
    scored as exported types with no users. Also the -ldflags vars, and
    interface-dispatched methods. A fourth may remain: anything reached only
    through reflection, a template, or //go:embed.
  - The byob command shape REQUIRES some of these. byob-command-shape.1 wants
    Options + NewCmdXxx, and byob-input-validation.5 wants Options.Validate();
    that is roughly 8 of the 104 non-field candidates, and they stay by
    decision rather than by usage.
  - The 252 untagged-field candidates need per-case care: a struct marshalled
    without tags serializes by field NAME, so unexporting one silently drops it
    from the output. Take the 104 non-field candidates first.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE DOCUMENTATION QUESTION, which is why it was asked. The
API surface that actually needs a contract a consumer can use without reading
the code is 442 identifiers, not 1,422. fisc-b8z0 measured 24% of a 143-symbol
sample as UNDER-DOCUMENTED; applying that to the real surface is a far smaller
and better-targeted job than documenting everything revive currently forces.

SO THE ORDER IS: unexport first, then document what is left. Documenting a
symbol that should not be exported is wasted twice -- once writing it, and again
every time it goes stale.
notes:
2026-09-04 THE CLASSIFIER MERGES AN EXTERNAL TEST PACKAGE INTO THE PACKAGE IT TESTS, so the 31% headline and the 356 count are both slightly overstated. Found while landing fisc-jbu4 (4c91136), by the compiler rather than by re-reading.

internal/export, internal/registry and pkg/cmdutil each have `package foo_test` files. Those are DIFFERENT packages, and an identifier they reference is referenced across a package boundary. The analysis scored four such identifiers NO-EXTERNAL-USE anyway -- export.PageTextDir, export.SchemaVersion, export.LocalPageTextBase and export.Write -- and unexporting them failed to compile.

Only four surfaced because only the 104 non-field candidates were acted on. The same misclassification applies to the 252 untagged fields fisc-vo7o owns, where the failure mode is silent rather than a build error, so re-run with external test packages treated as separate before touching those.

RE-MEASURED AT 4c91136 (before the unexport), the totals had also drifted from the 2026-09-03 figures in this description: 1,428 exported identifiers rather than 1,422, and 296 interface-dispatched methods rather than 290. The 104 non-field candidate count was unchanged.

THREE MORE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES beyond the three this bead names, all recorded on 4c91136: an external test package (above); a type appearing in an exported signature, which is API whether or not another package names it; and a sentinel error, which errors.Is is the only way to consume. Together they account for 11 of the 28 identifiers held back.

title: (BUG) buildPairing's doc says none of the 124 disagreeing pages is mapped; ACFR p41 is
description:
internal/mapping/geometry.go:57-58, buildPairing's doc: "on 124 of the corpus's
786 pages the two disagree about how many lines the page has, and on 99 more
they disagree about the tokens on a line. NONE IS A PAGE ANY RULE MAPS."

The last sentence is false. ACFR p41 is mapped -- four parts in
mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml declare `- page: 41` (lines 219, 280, 332,
414) -- and it is one of the 124.

THE TREE ALREADY SAYS SO, in the file that maps it. That YAML's own comment at
:160 reads "the geometry/text line pairing fails on this page anyway. The stray
'0.0' of (1) sits 0.32pt below the Miscellaneous row's baseline, inside the
4.945pt line tolerance", and at :349 "giving 51 geometry lines against" 52 text
lines. So one mapping file states the disagreement while another package's doc
states that no mapped page has one.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: buildPairing is only reached for a part that declares
column_headers, and p41's four parts declare none. The claim is therefore
latent -- the guard is not in force on the one page that refutes its stated
coverage, which is why no test could go red.

CLASS. This is prose asserting a guard's coverage is wider than it is, which is
the green-because-the-gate-fired shape one level up: a reader takes "none is a
page any rule maps" as licence to treat the pairing as universal over the
mapped set.

FIX IS NOT JUST THE SENTENCE. Decide what the true statement is -- "one is
(ACFR p41), and it declares no column_headers so this never runs for it" -- and
check whether the 124/99 counts still hold, since they were measured before the
ACFR entered the corpus.

Found by the adversarial verification pass over fisc-b93j's first unit
(internal/geom), which reached this from the other side: the geom rewrite cited
the same 0.32pt cluster as evidence that line-clustering margins are wide.
close_reason: Corrected at the commit below. The 124/99 counts still hold exactly, re-measured over all 786 pages: 563 pair, 124 disagree on line count, 99 on tokens. What was false is the last sentence: ACFR p41 IS mapped and IS one of the 124 (52 text lines against 51 geometry). The true statement is that it declares no column_headers so buildPairing never runs for it, and it is the ONLY one of the 36 mapped pages that fails pairing. Pinned by TestEveryMappedPartWithHeadersCanCarryTheColumnGuard, which asserts the invariant that matters -- every part ASKING for the guard can carry it -- rather than a count that would move with the corpus. Proven failable: removing the ColumnHeaders condition makes it red on ACFR p41 naming the substrate disagreement. The two comments in mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml that state the same disagreement were checked and are accurate.

title: The comment sweep, by rewrite: a Fable agent per unit, adversarially verified
description:
Rewrite this repository's Go comments to the shape AGENTS.md states, one unit at
a time, by handing each unit to a Fable agent that has the rules and the files
and nothing else. Production Go and tests are in scope; site/app.js,
tools/jscheck and printed strings are not.

WHY REWRITE RATHER THAN EDIT, and this inverts what fisc-b8z0 recommended.
fisc-pm8f measured hand-editing at roughly two new false claims per ten blocks,
invisible to every gate: 33 review findings over nine commits, not one of them a
pre-existing defect the lane had not itself created, about two thirds introduced
by an earlier pass's own fix. fisc-b8z0 concluded from that that any paraphrase
is dangerous and recommended delete-then-restore-VERBATIM.

Its own follow-up experiment (aa9ada7) refuted that. Fable, given only the
written rules and the original text of internal/geom -- 28 blocks, 147 comment
lines -- produced ZERO new false claims, found and corrected a planted one
unaided, deleted the file's one fully-RECOVERED block, corrected the CONTRADICTED
one, gave the UNDER-DOCUMENTED one its missing panic contract, and stopped at
-11% against an independent oracle's -14% ceiling. Rewriting is safer than
editing. The residual risk is not false claims; it is over-compression of the
reasoning that makes a guard's importance legible, plus one enumeration that came
back incomplete rather than false. Both are designed against in the rules pack.

THE UNIT. One package where the package is small, one file or a small group
where it is not; target <= ~450 comment lines and <= 3 files. Roughly 29
production units and ~20 test units, tiered A leaf / B mid / C composition root /
D projection / E mapping / F export / G checks, run A B C G D E F. Tests follow
their own package immediately, while the production diff is still fresh.

PER UNIT. Pre-register the codehash, the comment-line count and (for an audited
