caught by funding-sources-tie-to-spine -- but a wrong fund of the same type
would not, and neither would a wrong fund on a row whose group sum is checked
only in aggregate. Same failure mode as p76 (see p76-is-published), where the
payer at each row's far end is hand-typed and the page cannot check it.

THE FIX IS NOT FREE, which is why this is a bead and not a line in that lane. A
bare-label arm on rowAnchorPrefixes would try EVERY row label in the corpus
against FundByLabel -- p127's "Current Year - Secured", p167's object
categories, the spine's "Wages & Benefits". Most would not resolve and would be
skipped, but the ones that accidentally do are the hazard, and the check would
go from 88 subjects to thousands. Design the opt-in: probably a per-rule or
per-part declaration saying "these rows name funds", so the claim is made by
the rule author and the check enforces it, rather than inferred.
acceptance_criteria: a rule can declare that its row labels name funds, and a wrong fund number on such a row makes fisc verify fail; proved by mutating one of pp.85-125's rows
notes:
2026-08-29 TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD, both found in peer review of a landing
plan and both verified by reading the tree rather than by re-running the
measurement.

(1) THE TITLE AND DESCRIPTION OVERSTATE THE HOLE. "checked by nothing" and
"caught by nothing" are false as of cd1192c.
internal/check/fundingsources_test.go:326-338, inside
TestEveryFundingSourceFactMatchesThePrintedRow, already resolves EVERY
funding-source fact's RowLabel through s.Vocabulary.FundByLabel and asserts both
entry.Number == f.Fund and entry.Type == f.FundGroup. Its own comment at :312-325
says so outright: "with these two assertions the 640 -> 641 swap above is red."
Measured in review: the Water 640 -> 641 mutation is RED under `go test` and
GREEN under `fisc verify` (40 passed, 0 failed).

So what is unguarded is THE GATE, not the corpus. This bead's acceptance
criterion -- "a wrong fund number on such a row makes fisc verify fail" -- is
still unmet and still correct. The work is to move the guarantee from one lane's
test into fisc verify, as a declaration any schedule can opt into, which is what
that test's own comment already anticipates: "That does not retire fisc-90fp --
which is about a mechanism the whole corpus can use rather than one lane's test."

(2) THE DESCRIPTION CONTRADICTS ITS OWN NOTES ON FUND TYPES. It says "Every CIP
twin is type: capital, so a wrong-twin fund moves money out of its group". That
is true of p76's five twins and FALSE of the four on pp.85-125, which is what the
2026-08-29 note below then says correctly. Measured in data/funds.yaml: 610/611
(:712,:720), 620/621 (:736,:744) and 640/641 (:767,:775) are all `enterprise`;
740/741 (:845,:858) are both `internal-service`. Not one of the four is capital.
Read the notes, not the description, on this point.

ALSO MEASURED while scoping the work, and useful to whoever takes it: the 78 rows
carry 63 distinct labels forming 63 distinct (label, fund) pairs, no label
declared against two funds. All 63 resolve -- 58 by funds.yaml `name` and 5 by
`aliases[].term` (Asset Seizure - Dep of Justice 221, Cal Home Reuse 205,
California Begin Program 206, Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow 470, Facilities Rehab
Pgm 740). Zero of the 78 carry skip: true. So an opt-in arm lands GREEN with 78
subjects: not vacuous, no declaredVacuous entry owed, and a mutation proof
mandatory.

AND A TRAP FOR THE MUTATION PROOF, because fundingsources_test.go is already red
on it: "apply the edit and run the suite" proves nothing about the new arm --
green because the OTHER gate fired, which is the shape AGENTS.md names. The proof
must call (&rowFundsMatchTheirAnchors{}).Run(...) in isolation and assert on the
returned Result, the way TestRowFundsCatchesTheTwinSwapNothingElseSees does.
close_reason:
Landed at 4b78c1e. Rule.RowLabelsNameFunds (yaml: row_labels_name_funds) declared on the eleven funding-* rules, a third fail-closed arm on row-funds-match-their-anchors reading the printed label whole through FundByLabel, and a parse-time guard refusing the declaration on a rule with an unfunded non-skip row.

MEASURED: Water 640 -> CIP Water 641 in funding-public-works now gives fisc verify 39 passed, 1 failed (row-funds-match-their-anchors, 1 finding over 118 row anchors) where 02156a7 gave 40 passed, 0 failed. fact-funds-resolve and funding-sources-tie-to-spine both stay PASS on the same mutation -- both funds are enterprise, so no sum moves. Subject count 40 -> 118. facts.jsonl unmoved.

NOTE FOR THE RECORD: this bead's title said 'checked by nothing' and that was false since cd1192c -- TestEveryFundingSourceFactMatchesThePrintedRow already caught the swap under go test. What was unmet, and is what this closes, is the acceptance criterion: 'makes fisc verify fail'. Five committed strings asserting the hole were corrected with it, two of them printed by fisc verify on every run.

title: Projection links carry fact_ids and no locators, so no panel can resolve by locator
description:
fisc-4ua.8 requires the provenance PANEL to resolve by locator rather than by fact id, and shipping the store (1d6cc2d) did not achieve it. The URL scheme is in place -- facts/<doc>/pages/pNNNN.jsonl, computed from (doc_id, page), no lookup -- and nothing on the chart can use it.

MEASURED. site/app.js:1094 (pin) and :1197 (buildTable) print link.fact_ids as inert text. project.Link carries fact_ids []string and nothing else about provenance (internal/project/sankey.go:346). So the client holds ids and the resolver takes locators, and app.js cannot compose one from what it has. Turning a fact id into a link would be resolution-BY-ID, which fisc-4ua.8 forbids in so many words and for a stated reason: fact.MakeID hashes rule_id, so revising a rule moves every id on a page while the page cannot move.

THE ONE PROJECTION THAT ALREADY CARRIES IT is revenue-trends: project.Point publishes doc_id, page, offset and token (internal/project/trends.go:220-233), which is why revenue.html's cells can already link per figure. The spine and the drill-down publish neither.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES: a decision on where the locator lives on a Link. A link is an aggregate of facts, so it has no single locator -- the options are a per-link list of (doc_id, page) pairs, or the page set already implied by fact_ids resolved server-side. Cheapest correct move is probably a page-level link ('facts on p67') composed from a new page_facts_base in clientDoc, which needs a tools/jscheck case; the fuller move is locators on the link. Note the cost of the cheap one: a drill-down flow-table cell already carries 36 links and this adds 18.

DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN in the commit that shipped the store, so that the store's own guarantees landed without a client change riding along.
acceptance_criteria: a mark on the spine or the drill-down resolves to the records behind it by locator, not by fact id; the rule is spelled once; a jscheck case covers whatever the client composes
notes:
2026-08-29 LANDED, 94ba9a7..6979b4f. The decision this bead asked for, plus the
measurement that made it easy.

WHERE THE LOCATOR LIVES: on the Link, as Locators []project.Source -- the type
metadata.sources already uses, so the JSON is byte-identical and app.js's
citations() accepts a link's list VERBATIM. A flat {doc_id, page} would have
forced a second URL-composition site, which internal/export/page.go:1543
refuses on the Go side.

THE BEAD'S OWN TRADE-OFF IS DEAD, and this is why the fuller option was
affordable. It asks whether to take a cheap page-level link or the fuller
per-link locators, and notes the cheap one adds 18 links to a cell already
carrying 36. Measured across all six published documents: EVERY link resolves
to 1 or 2 (doc_id, page) pairs -- 830 with one, 16 with two. After the client
fold, max 5. So per-link locators are the SMALL option, not the large one.

AND THE 36-LINK CONCERN WAS BACKWARDS. The flow table rendered the document's
18 pages x 2 URL shapes identically on all 52 folded drill-down rows -- 1,872
anchors, none about the row it sat in, under a header reading "Source". It is
now 237. Publishing locators made the page smaller.

SCHEMA VERSION: NOT BUMPED, owner decision taken this date. Pre-release, so the
number is not yet a promise to any reader outside this tree; project.SchemaVersion,
export.SchemaVersion and app.js's SCHEMA_VERSION stay at 1 in lockstep.
Recorded because docs/revenue-trends-contract.md says a bump is a decision and
not a number someone increments -- the NEXT additive key is re-decided, not
waved through on this precedent.

THE DEPLOY WINDOW IS A KNOWN, ACCEPTED TRADE. drawableSankey now hard-requires
links[].locators and links[].locators[].pages, and the site publishes no
cache-busting on data/<stem>.json (fetched lazily on click). A browser holding
a pre-deploy document beside a post-deploy app.js gets a refusal banner. Not
fixable by weakening the guard -- pin and buildTable dereference the key, so
citations(undefined) would throw AT the reader instead -- so the BANNER now
names a stale cache first and tells them to reload, before blaming the file.
Same exposure fact_ids has carried since fisc-60r.

WHAT CHECKS IT: link-locators-match-their-facts (tier 1, 846 links), which
re-derives the grouping rather than calling project.sourcesOf;
TestTheRecordsBaseComposesBackToTheShardPath; TestEveryShippedDocumentCanResolveItsRecords;
Options.validate's exact-directory rule; and four jscheck cases.

THREE REVIEW PASSES, EIGHT FINDINGS, all fixed and all in the commits. The two
worth remembering: drawableSankey shipped links[].locators WITHOUT
links[].locators[].pages, which is a real fisc-bsg half-repaint (0 rows against
58, "TypeError: source.pages is not iterable"); and it was invisible because
harness.mjs's twoYearConfig carried docs: {}, so citations() returned at
`if (!doc) continue` before reaching source.pages in EVERY lifecycle check --
every required-key case for a [].pages key was passing because the gate fired,
not because a throw was prevented. docs is now populated. Check that when
adding the next [].pages arm.
close_reason: Landed 94ba9a7..6979b4f: Link.Locators, link-locators-match-their-facts, records_base, and per-mark citations in the client. Three review passes.

title: The drill-down's other three years, and a seventh fund group no check can see
description:
drilldown.html renders fund-flows (FY2025-26) and lists NO year stems, so the other three published columns still ship as data no reader can open -- unviewedDocuments declares all three with this bead's reason. Giving the page a year control is not a line in views(), and both obstacles were measured while landing E9.

(1) THE STEM ORDER NO LONGER REFUSES THE VIEW. yearStems walks project.PublishedDocuments() in declared order, which for fund-flows is 2024-actual, 2025-revised, 2026, 2027, so the bare 'fund-flows' stem is THIRD -- and that is now fine. View.validate's arm requiring the first year stem to equal the view's projection is gone; it requires only membership, and a page opens on the LAST year rather than the first. Which year the drill-down opens on is therefore answered by the order, the same way the spine's is, and is not a decision this bead has to take.

(2) FY2023-24 CARRIES A SEVENTH FUND GROUP. fund-flows-2024-actual.json folds to SEVEN fund-group nodes, not six: fund-group/permanent appears in that column alone, and department-funding-2024-actual.json carries it too. Both sit in unviewedDocuments, so this is latent rather than live -- one step declaration away.

WHAT THE PAGE DOES WITH ONE IS NOW DECLARED RATHER THAN EMERGENT. internal/export ships the fund groups a column draws in a declared order, with a group its sequence does not name after the ones it does; site/app.js holds no list of its own and reads that order for both the legend and the fund column. A group site/style.css has no hue for draws --muted, last, in both. tools/jscheck/fold.mjs drives three shapes for it: a seventh group, a served list short by one, and a fund group whose id is not under fund-group/.

SO WHAT REMAINS OF THIS ITEM IS THE COLOUR DECISION AND NOT THE PLUMBING. site/style.css:1011-1018 argues that a seventh hue would invalidate a measured result -- the six were chosen by enumerating all 720 orderings against a CVD validator, and seven means 5040. 'NO SEVENTH HUE, and record why' is a legitimate answer and the likely one: permanent is one group in one of four columns. Six is the palette's CAPACITY now, which is a rendering limit and stays on the client's side; it is no longer a membership list the packager has to agree with.

(3) Column shapes differ by year and any fixture or pin taken over FY2025-26 alone does not cover them: nodes 145/149/155/144, links 175/191/191/173, object columns 44/47/49/44, and FY2023-24's tier-5 labels include Debt Services and Capital Outlay, which FY2025-26's do not.

Related: fisc-u8o (permanent is a seventh fund type with no spine column), fisc-y0k (the CVD re-run, which this bead's answer feeds).
notes:
2026-09-10, fisc-ko1j.4: OBSTACLE (1) DISSOLVED, MEASURED. stepStems (pkg/cmd/export/data.go) joins the spine's documents to fund-flows' on Columns, giving {sankey: fund-flows, sankey-2027: fund-flows-2027}; TestStepStemsJoinsOnColumnNotOnDeclaredOrder reads the bare stem's position off PublishedDocuments (2, third of four) and pins the join, and the mutation -- joining on declared order instead -- pairs BOTH spine years with fund-flows-2024-actual and goes red in two tests. View.validate's first-year-stem arm (export.go, 'opens on %q but its first year stem is %q') reads YearStems alone, and a step is not a YearStems list, so no opening-year decision remains.

2026-09-21: item (2)'s plumbing is fisc-cc4y's and is done; the description above says what it leaves. 2024-actual and 2025-revised stay in unviewedDocuments under fundFlowsNoSpineColumn: pp.66-67 print no actual and no revised column, so there is no spine year to open them from. Item (3) is unchanged.

title: Expansion is not per-node on this d3-sankey: filter to one group, or it does not draw
description:
fisc-5miz.1 settled the chart form as a STATIC fold to tiers {0,2,4}. The other half of the decision -- click a fund group to expand it into its funds -- was measured during that work and DOES NOT DRAW on the vendored d3-sankey. Filed with the measurement rather than as a follow-up idea, because the obvious implementation is the one that fails.

WHY PER-NODE EXPANSION CANNOT WORK. site/vendor/d3-sankey.min.js derives the column count from TOPOLOGY (o = max(node.depth) + 1) and then clamps whatever the align function returns into it. Fold fund-flows.json to {0,2,4}, expand fund-group/enterprise alone, and lay it out with an explicit tier->column align: the graph's longest path is still 3 hops, so o = 3, tier 4 clamps to layer 2, and THE FUNDS AND THE DEPARTMENTS ARE DRAWN IN THE SAME COLUMN while the five unexpanded fund-group->dept ribbons span two. tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's bands() throws on exactly that (span !== 1), so the check nominated as the safety net cannot run on the graph it is meant to guard.

AND THE AFFORDANCE DELETES ITSELF. Expanding re-attributes the clicked group's links to its children, so fisc-5miz.2's rule ('draw only the nodes the folded link set touches') removes the node that was clicked: 5 fund groups remain of 6, and there is nothing left to click to collapse it.

AND THE GESTURE IS TAKEN. app.js's node click AND keydown both drive setIsolated, behind the keyActivation echo guard, which took three defects to get right. A second meaning on the same activation of the same element is a new interaction contract, not a reuse.

THE SHAPE THAT DOES WORK, and what this bead should build: FILTER TO ONE GROUP. Clicking a fund group re-renders a graph restricted to that group's funds, rescaled to that group's own total, with a breadcrumb back. Every tier set stays uniform, which is the only shape this d3-sankey lays out, and rescaling is what makes special-revenue's 32 funds legible -- they share 9.1% of the column today, so at the citywide scale most of them are sub-pixel whatever the tier set.

STILL OWED WHATEVER THE MECHANISM: expansion state, collapse, keyboard and aria, its interaction with isolated/pinned (both hold node ids expansion can delete -- app.js already resets them on a YEAR switch for this reason), and its interaction with the counts line and the flow table, which now describe the folded document.
notes:
CORRECTED AGAIN BY fisc-ko1j.12.5 (W4). This bead's third objection STILL HOLDS as a rule and its resolution in the notes above is now stale in both halves.

THE RULE STANDS: a second meaning on the same activation of the same element is a new interaction contract, not a reuse. W4 did not overload one gesture; it added a second one. A single click and Space isolate, on every node of every view; a double click and Enter open the nodes that open. The note above says the gesture was 'resolved by declaring it per view (export.View.Drill)' -- that is no longer how it is resolved. It is resolved by two gestures, and no view has to choose.

AND THE PREMISE UNDER THAT RESOLUTION IS FALSE, measured rather than argued. The note's reason was 'a two-column chart has nothing worth isolating'. MEASURED with tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's own walk over the shipped declaration, both committed captures: all 44 views the chain opens draw THREE columns at the page's own budget, and at a four-column budget one of them draws four. None draws two. The two-column shape the argument rests on was left behind when a window became the drill's form. Every opened view has a middle column, so every one of them has ribbons an isolate dims.

WHAT MADE THE SPLIT NECESSARY RATHER THAN MERELY POSSIBLE: over those 44 views, 24 of the 343 drawn marks open. Leaving the single click on the drill gave 7% of an opened chart's marks one meaning and 93% of them another, on the same mark shape, told apart only by trying.
close_reason: Built in bd0a098 as export.View.Drill plus filterToNode/capColumn/drillTo in site/app.js. See the notes for the correction to this bead's own remedy -- rescaling alone is measured insufficient and the cap is not optional.

title: A drill-down page must not invite a reader to sum a column
description:
The document's own caveat states the constraint the page design has to respect:

  'This document holds the same money at more than one grain, so summing every link double-counts: 44 fact(s) are behind both a department's object rows and the fund-to-department link that totals them. Fold within one tier pair, never across the whole graph. It publishes no headline for this reason.'

fund-flows-counts-reconcile already publishes the numbers per column (280 facts = cited + uncited, with 44 to 49 cited twice depending on the year).

So a page that offers a column total, a 'total spending' tile, or a flow table a reader can add up would be wrong in exactly the way this project exists to prevent -- and it would be wrong QUIETLY, because every figure on it ties to a fact. The spine page's whole rhetorical structure is a headline plus tiles; this document cannot have one.

Filed as its own bead rather than a line in the template bead because it is a design constraint on the page, not a packaging detail, and it is the reason the drill-down cannot simply reuse the spine's chrome.
close_reason:
Landed 19c70ae as site/drilldown.html.tmpl: no hero tile, no figures row, no headline, and buildDrilldownPage hands the client no Hero and no Figures either, so a year switch cannot put one back.

The page says the constraint in its own words where a reader meets it -- 'Read one pair of columns at a time', with the reason: the same money appears at more than one grain, so a total would look right and count part of it twice.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT BUDGET, both found by peer review.

THE COUNTS LINE AND THE FLOW TABLE WOULD HAVE CONTRADICTED THE CHART. paintYearWords printed the document's 175 links over 145 nodes beside a chart drawing 52 over 40, and buildTable tabulated all 175 rows. Both now read the FOLDED document. Nothing is cited less precisely: the fold unions the fact ids it merges, measured at 239 before and 239 after.

el() THROWS on a missing id, so any id the new template omits takes the page down three repaints in. The template keeps every throwing id -- legend, tooltip, chart, detail, derived-list, flow-table, theme-toggle -- and drops only maybeEl-guarded ones (figures, year-toggle).

AND THE EDITORIAL PROBLEM THE BEAD DID NOT NAME: the folded columns run $321.0M -> $321.0M -> $144.7M, because only the General Fund has a spending side, so the chart is correct and LOOKS like 55% of the city's money evaporates mid-picture. Answered on the chart, not in a caveat three screens down.

title: The packager's share of a drill-down page: a third template, a plural scope, and a Lede guard that would refuse it
description:
What internal/export needs before a fund-flows view can render, each verified against the tree at 259bb7c.

(1) A THIRD TEMPLATE ARM, not a relaxed refusal. decodeSankey (internal/export/page.go:556-572) refuses a document with no fiscal_year_label OR a zero headline expenditure. fund-flows.json carries the label but NO headline key at all -- deliberately: its own caveat says 'It publishes no headline for this reason', because the document holds the same money at more than one grain. The refusal is correct and must stay; buildSite's switch (page.go:699) already says every template is an explicit arm and the unknown one is refused. revenue.html.tmpl cannot host it either -- it is a server-rendered table with no #chart, no legend and no app.js.

(2) scopes IS PLURAL. fund-flows metadata publishes scopes []string (internal/project/fundflows.go:70-76) and no singular scope. chrome.Scope is one string, and the footer sentence and buildSankeyPage's cross-stem scope refusal both assume it.

(3) counts DOES NOT FIT. The document publishes FundFlowsCounts (facts_cited_twice, facts_uncited, no partition); page.go's countsRef has Facts/Nodes/Links.

(4) THE LEDE GUARD WOULD REFUSE THE VIEW. internal/export/export.go:372 is 'case v.Lede != "" && v.Template != TrendsTemplate'. A fund-flows view that sets a lede is refused today. Widen it as a PROPERTY OF THE TEMPLATE (which templates render a lede) rather than adding a second !=, or the same list goes stale again the next time a template lands.
close_reason:
Landed 19c70ae. All four points confirmed against the tree and acted on, with one correction and one addition.

(1) A third template arm: DrilldownTemplate, decodeDrilldown, buildDrilldownPage, a case in buildSite's switch. decodeSankey's two refusals are correct for a spine and stay.
(2) scopes is plural: drilldownPageData carries Scopes []string. chrome.Scope was NOT widened -- it is embedded in both other page types and rendered in both their footers, so widening it edits two shipped pages and the prose pinned about them.
(3) THE counts POINT WAS A NON-ISSUE. decodeDocument uses plain json.Unmarshal with no DisallowUnknownFields, so the three extra keys are ignored, which is what we want. Dropped rather than built.
(4) The Lede guard is now templateRendersLede(name), a property of the template rather than a second !=, exactly as the bead asks.

ADDED: View.RenderTiers, shipped as FISC_CONFIG.render_tiers with omitempty so the spine's config blob is unchanged byte for byte. The packager declares the fold and never applies it.

Also: site/embed.go had to list the template or it is not in the embedded tree, and the view opens on FY2025-26 with NO year stems -- yearStems walks PublishedDocuments() in declared order, which puts 2024-actual first, and View.validate refuses a view whose first stem is not its projection. That trap and the seventh-hue one are recorded on the surviving unviewedDocuments entries.

title: No committed fixture lets any harness lay out a drill-down, which is why fisc-y0k's criterion is unreachable
description:
tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's goldenGraph() reads testdata/sankey.golden.json and nothing else. There is no committed fund-flows document any check can lay out.

fisc-y0k's acceptance criterion is 'worst-case CVD deltaE recorded for light and dark AT THE NEW TOUCHING PAIRS'. Ribbons stack in column order, so which pairs touch is a property of the LAYOUT -- and no harness in this tree can produce that layout for this document. The criterion cannot be evaluated as written.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a testdata/fund-flows.golden.json in the same shape as the spine's -- hand-derived, byte-compared by a test in internal/project -- plus harness support for loading a second document. Note the spine golden is 25 nodes and this one is 145, so 'hand-derived' means something different here and that cost should be faced rather than discovered.

AND THE SEVENTH HUE IS WORSE VALUE THAN IT LOOKS. permanent appears in exactly ONE of the four columns (fund-flows-2024-actual.json), so a seventh legend entry appears and disappears across the year toggle. Justifying a seventh slot means enumerating 7! = 5040 orderings against the CVD validator, for one column of one year. site/style.css:984-988 already says in writing that a seventh hue would invalidate a measured result. Weigh 'no seventh hue, and say why' seriously.
close_reason:
Landed as testdata/fund-flows.golden.json plus goldenFundFlows() in the harness (c3a337d), and the bead's cost estimate was answered differently from how it framed the question.

'Hand-derived means something different here' -- peer review's answer is that it means it should not be attempted: 280 facts over 18 pages would be a second transcription of the schedules the mapping rules already read, and any error in it would be invisible. The fixture is a CAPTURE, the one in the tree that is, and testdata/README.md says so plainly. TestTheFundFlowsFixtureIsTheDocumentTheSiteDraws compares it line for line against what fisc export writes (metadata.generated_by excepted), so it cannot drift into describing a document that is no longer ours. The fold's semantics are pinned by a hand-authored miniature written inline in fold.mjs instead, where the fixture and the assertion read on one screen.

AND IT FIXED SOMETHING THE BEAD DID NOT KNOW WAS BROKEN. layout.mjs never called layOut -- it rebuilds its own d3.sankey -- so every figure it pins stayed green no matter what layOut did. layOut and foldDocument are exported now and fold.mjs compares the two on the golden spine; mutating nodePadding fails that check, where before it failed nothing.

fisc-y0k's criterion is now reachable: a harness can lay a drill-down out. The seventh hue is NOT decided here -- fund-group/permanent appears only in FY2023-24 and the page ships FY2025-26 alone, so it moves to the years bead.

title: [site] drawableSankey's guard omits two keys the repaint dereferences, so the fisc-bsg split page is still reachable
description:
site/app.js's drawableSankey states its own rule -- 'every key the draw DEREFERENCES before it could report a failure' -- and does not meet it. It checks nodes, links, metadata and metadata.sources, and the repaint goes on to dereference two more:

  - buildTable does l.fact_ids.join(" ") (app.js ~:939)
  - citations() does source.pages (app.js ~:387)

MEASURED PATH: a schema_version 1 data/sankey-2027.json whose links lack fact_ids passes drawableSankey AND passes layOut (neither key is touched there), then throws inside buildTable -- which runs AFTER paintYearWords, buildLegend and buildDerivedList and BEFORE render(laid). The reader is left with FY2026-27's tiles, caveats, lede, <title> and footer citation sitting over FY2025-26's chart, plus a generic banner from wireYears' .catch.

That is the fisc-bsg split repaint reached one function later, which is exactly why metadata.sources was added to the guard list in the first place. links[].fact_ids and sources[].pages belong beside it.

Found by /code-review of the drill-down branch, 2026-08-27, and independently by a second reviewer in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: drawableSankey refuses a document missing links[].fact_ids or metadata.sources[].pages; a jscheck case proves the page is unchanged rather than half-repainted
close_reason:
Landed in 485c3d2, together with the fisc-rqq harness fixes it needed to be provable -- that ordering was load-bearing, since lifecycle.mjs's only fixture with a sources array was the one fisc-rqq fixed.

drawableSankey now refuses links[].fact_ids and metadata.sources[].pages. Both are one element deeper than the top-level Array.isArray arms, which is why a correctly-shaped document passed the gate AND passed layOut and threw inside buildTable, the last step of the repaint.

THE SPLIT PAGE IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. With the fact_ids arm removed the new check reports the page reading 'FY 2026-27 adopted' over a flow table of 0 rows against 58 before the click, under 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading join)'. With the arm, 'FY 2025-26 adopted' and all 58 rows, and the banner names the missing key.

Two jscheck cases, one per key, asserting the row count is UNCHANGED rather than merely that a banner appeared -- a half-repainted page also shows a banner. Each arm removed independently reddens only its own case.

title: Two documents would publish the same money at the same grain, and no check objects
description:
The revenue-trends document already publishes all 924 revenue-by-fund facts, as 231 four-point series. A revenue drill-down GRAPH at the same scope would publish 190 of them again per adopted year, as links.

NOTHING IN internal/check OBJECTS, and that was measured rather than assumed: factsAreProjected unions fact ids into one 'projected' set, so a fact in two projections is projected twice and counted once; trend-points-tie-to-facts' 'published exactly once' map is per-document; published-projection-built keys on (name, scope) so two projections at one scope do not cross-satisfy each other's declarations; and revenue-by-fund is no longer in unprojectedScopes, so staleDeclarations is not reached. Every check stays green.

SO THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER IT IS CHECKABLE. It is whether it is right, and it is a READER question the gate cannot answer: the same 99,969,007 arriving on two pages, once as a table of series and once as a chart of flows, is either a genuine second view of one thing or a second source of truth a reader has to reconcile by hand. fisc-l25's answer -- 'the site becomes several distinct interactive views over different aspects of the budget, more like USAFacts than like a single chart' -- reads as though it permits this, but it was answering whether the SPINE and the DRILL-DOWN are one picture, not whether one schedule may appear twice.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DECIDED: it is unowned. fisc-gxa.2 assumes the drill-down is new coverage; it is not, at this scope. If the answer is that one schedule gets one view, the drill-down's scope is expenditure-by-department (196 facts, drawn by nothing) and not revenue-by-fund, which changes what fisc-gxa.2 builds.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded on whether one schedule may be published by two documents, and if so what tells a reader they are the same money
notes:
2026-09-08: fisc-ko1j.7 REOPENS THIS DECISION'S CONSEQUENCE FOR pp.127-140. Not the decision itself, which stands.

E13's merged chart decomposes spending twice and revenue not at all, and the owner asked for a revenue line-item tier. That is the case this bead's close reason argues against by name: revenue-trends already publishes all 924 revenue-by-fund facts as 231 four-point series, and a line-item tier in the graph republishes them as links.

WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE 2026-08-30 IS THAT ONE OF THE TWO DOCUMENTS NOW EXISTS. fund-flows ships and DOES select revenue-by-fund -- at (category, fund) grain, one level coarser than this document's line item, which is the only reason it does not already violate this decision. A line-item tier collapses that difference and puts one schedule on two pages at identical grain.

This bead's own acceptance criteria contemplated the yes answer -- 'and if so what tells a reader they are the same money' -- so fisc-ko1j.7 asks that question rather than routing around this one.
close_reason:
DECIDED BY THE OWNER, 2026-08-30: ONE SCHEDULE, ONE PUBLISHED VIEW.

A schedule gets exactly one published view. Two documents may not publish the same money at the same grain, and the question the bead framed as unowned is now answered.

THE CONSEQUENCE, which is the part that changes work rather than records a preference: the drill-down's scope is expenditure-by-department (196 facts, drawn by nothing today), NOT revenue-by-fund. revenue-trends already publishes all 924 revenue-by-fund facts as 231 four-point series, and a revenue drill-down graph would republish 190 of them per adopted year as links. fisc-gxa.2's text assumes the drill-down is new coverage at that scope; it is not, and that assumption is now wrong. Noted on fisc-gxa.2.

WHAT THE BEAD MEASURED IS UNCHANGED AND STILL TRUE: nothing in internal/check objects. factsAreProjected unions ids into one projected set; trend-points-tie-to-facts' published-exactly-once map is per-document; published-projection-built keys on (name, scope); and revenue-by-fund is no longer in unprojectedScopes so staleDeclarations is not reached. The decision is therefore a rule a human upholds, not one a gate enforces, and nothing here proposes to make it one.

THE ADJACENT CASE THIS DOES NOT COVER, recorded so a later session does not read the answer too widely. The ACFR facts landed at 0448a5b are a DIFFERENT year on a DIFFERENT basis -- FY2025 audited against a spine of FY2026/FY2027 adopted -- so they share no (kind, category, fund_group, fund, fiscal year, basis) key with anything published and no doubling is possible. That scope is unprojected for a reason this bead does not reach: nobody has decided whether an audited prior year belongs on a page of adopted figures. The unprojectedScopes entry says so.

AND A REAL DOUBLING HAZARD WAS FOUND IN THE SAME SESSION that this bead does not cover, because it is within ONE document rather than across two: two rules over one page section can publish the same printed figure twice with every check green. Filed as fisc-2x7y.

title: The contract's tier 1 is a NODE and the code's is a FIELD, and one of the two has to go
description:
docs/sankey-contract.md's tier table gives tier 1 as 'constraint tier', id form 'constraint/<tier>' -- a NODE, sitting in the hierarchy between the revenue source and the fund group. project.Node.ConstraintTier is a string FIELD on every node. These are two different designs for the same thing, both shipped, and nothing has ever had to choose because the spine populates neither.

THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. As a node, a constraint tier is a column the money flows THROUGH, it aggregates, it takes a colour, and derived:true plus a rationale is honest about it because we invented the node. As a field, it is an attribute a reader sees in the provenance panel -- site/app.js already renders it as a chip, guarded on truthiness -- it does not aggregate, and marking it derived means marking the whole NODE derived, which for a published fund is false.

fisc-gkv ALREADY MEASURED THE NODE VERSION and the roadmap should not price it as more than it is: four nodes, with the General Fund alone on one of them. 'Not a rich tier.'

WHICHEVER SURVIVES, THE OTHER MUST BE RETIRED IN THE SAME CHANGE -- the table row deleted, or the field removed from the schema and the client. A contract that describes a design the code does not implement is the class of false claim this repository files beads about.

Related: the bead on constraint_tier being DERIVED. The node answer makes that problem go away; the field answer does not.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: exactly one of the two designs exists in the tree; docs/sankey-contract.md and project.Node agree; the retirement is in the same commit as the choice
close_reason: Decided by arithmetic and landed in c94680a: the contract's tier-1 constraint/<tier> NODE is deleted and project.Node.ConstraintTier the FIELD survives. THE NODE DESIGN IS IMPOSSIBLE, not merely unattractive: a constraint tier is a property of a FUND and the fund groups do not partition along it. data/funds.yaml by type x constraint_tier gives capital = 3 committed + 43 restricted-by-law and special-revenue = 37 restricted + 2 unknown + 1 committed, so fund-group/<t>.parent = constraint/<tier> has no single answer and a layer whose parent edge is undefined is not a layer. Both halves moved in the one commit as this bead required: the table row is gone and the field's doc comment is re-scoped to say the type now has more than one producer. Tier number 1 is left UNUSED rather than renumbering -- tiers 2-5 are published in node.tier today and shifting them would silently change every document already written.

title: node.tier is emitted on every node and read by no check
description:
project.Node.Tier is published on all 25 spine nodes and asserted by nothing. Grepped: no check in internal/check reads n.Tier. aggregation-invariance reads only n.Parent; constraint-tier-vocabulary reads only n.ConstraintTier; graph-acyclic reads links.

TODAY THAT IS NEARLY HARMLESS, because the spine emits three tier values from three constants and internal/project/sankey_test.go pins eight node ids to their tiers by hand. It stops being harmless the moment a document populates the hierarchy: fisc-gxa.2 describes tier population as its deliverable, and every tier value it writes would land unasserted by the gate.

WHAT A CHECK WOULD CLAIM, and none of it is expensive: every node's tier is one docs/sankey-contract.md's table declares; a link's source tier is above its target tier (the contract's flow endpoints sit outside the hierarchy and need naming as exceptions, not as a hole); a node's tier is strictly coarser than its parent's is finer -- which is the structural half of the fold and is filed on fisc-1wr.1.1.

NOTE THE ORDER THIS IS WORTH DOING IN. A tier check written now would be pinned to the spine's three values and would need rewriting for the first document with more. It belongs in the commit that populates tiers, and this bead exists so that commit does not treat the field as self-evidently right because it is already in the schema.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: a check reads node.tier and is proved failable by mutating one; the contract's tier table and the values the code emits are compared by something other than a reader
close_reason: Landed in 0f25117 as node-tiers-are-declared, non-vacuous on day one over 50 nodes and 116 links. Both acceptance clauses met: a check reads node.tier and is proved failable by mutating one (four cases -- wrong tier for the id form, a coined id form, the unused tier, and a reversed link), and the contract's tier table is compared against the emitted values by something other than a reader, keyed on the id FORM the table's own column declares. The bead's third suggested claim -- 'a node's tier is strictly coarser than its parent's' -- is deliberately NOT here: that is the fold, it reads node.parent rather than node.tier, and it belongs with aggregation-invariance's rewrite (fisc-1wr.1.1). The bead's ordering advice was to wait for the commit that populates tiers; taken half way -- the id-form claim needed no such commit and the spine was already publishing 50 unasserted values, while the tier-1 absence became assertable only once fisc-0ro deleted the layer. The five flow endpoints are named as exceptions rather than left as a hole, as asked.

title: A fund node's constraint_tier is DERIVED, and there is no channel to publish it as one
description:
data/funds.yaml's own header says it in writing: 'constraint_tier and restriction_note are DERIVED -- our reading of the Description of Funds narrative (pp. 258-261) -- and must not be presented as something the city printed.' internal/registry/registry.go says the same about why 'unknown' is a member of the closed set.

So the moment a graph node carries one, the site publishes an editorial classification. derived-nodes-justified requires a derived node to carry a rationale AND a source_note, and fisc-gkv spells out the consequence for the tier-1 layer: 'a tier-1 node needs derived: true plus a rationale and a source_note or derived-nodes-justified fails'.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE NODE IS NOT DERIVED AND THE ATTRIBUTE IS. A fund node's EXISTENCE is published -- pp.127-140 print the fund and its revenue -- while its constraint tier is our reading of a narrative. project.Node has ONE derived flag, one rationale and one source_note, and they are about the node. Marking the whole node derived:true would claim the city did not print the fund, which is false and is the opposite error.

MEASURED, so the size is known rather than guessed: of the 70 funds a revenue-by-fund document would draw, 59 are restricted-by-law, 8 committed, 2 unknown and 1 discretionary. All four declared values appear, so constraint-tier-vocabulary would exercise its whole vocabulary on day one -- and all 70 nodes would be publishing a derived attribute through a channel built for derived NODES.

OPTIONS, none free: (a) a per-attribute derivation channel on Node, which is a schema change and therefore a real schema_version question; (b) constraint_tier as a tier-1 NODE rather than an attribute, where derived:true is honest because we invented the node -- see the contract's own tier table, and the bead about the two designs; (c) publish no constraint_tier until (a) or (b) is decided, which is where the corpus is today and is not costing anything.

DECIDE BEFORE POPULATING THE FIELD. Publishing an editorial classification unmarked is the single thing this project's premise refuses.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: a node carrying a constraint_tier says, in the document, that the tier is our reading and not the city's; or nothing carries one and the reason is declared
close_reason: Answered in c94680a, and the answer is NOT the document-level caveat first planned. internal/check never reads metadata.caveats, so routing the whole published-is-not-derived disclosure there would put it in the one key fisc verify has never examined; and data/funds.yaml:12-15 draws the line at FIELD granularity in writing. So the contract now requires: a node carrying a non-empty constraint_tier also carries source_note (the funds.yaml + pp.258-261 citation) and rationale (that fund's restriction_note), while node.derived stays FALSE -- setting it would claim the city did not print the fund, which is the opposite error, and derived-nodes-justified skips non-derived nodes so this costs nothing today. The caveat sentence is still required, but as a check arm rather than as prose: it becomes a constant in internal/project so the caveat and the check cannot drift. Option (a), the per-attribute schema channel, is NOT taken -- it would add keys to the shared Node type and move the spine's golden file. Also settled here: "" (this document does not classify) and "unknown" (we read pp.258-261 and could not tell) are different claims and the contract now says so; collapsing them would be absent-is-not-zero in a new field. The enforcing check lands with the first document that populates the field.

title: [site] Two controls that lie: the year toggle after a reload, and the theme button after an OS switch
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26. Two independent defects in site/app.js, filed
together because they are the same class -- a control whose label contradicts
what the page is showing -- and because the year fieldset's own template comment
says a control that lies is worse than no control.

(1) THE YEAR TOGGLE NAMES A YEAR THE PAGE IS NOT DRAWING, AFTER A RELOAD OR A
BACK-NAVIGATION. site/index.html.tmpl hard-codes `checked` on the first year and
wireYears never reads which radio is currently checked -- main() unconditionally
does `await showYear(years[0])`. The radio groups carry no autocomplete="off",
and Chrome and Firefox both persist form-control state across a soft reload (F5)
and across Back. Concrete: a reader selects FY 2026-27, follows the nav to
revenue.html, presses Back -- the toggle comes back showing FY 2026-27 while the
lede, the tiles, the chart, the footer basis and the data-year-path citation are
all FY 2025-26. Fix either way: read the checked input in wireYears and open on
that year, or force input.checked back onto years[0] when wiring.

(2) THE THEME BUTTON INVERTS WHEN THE OS SWITCHES THEME UNDER IT. wireTheme's
`sync` is a local closure and the prefers-color-scheme listener is wired to
`paint` alone. A reader with no stored theme opens in light mode (button reads
"Dark mode", aria-pressed="false") and the OS auto-switches to dark at sunset:
the CSS media rule darkens the page and paint() re-reads the palette, but the
button still announces aria-pressed="false" on a dark page -- and because
prefersDark() now returns true, clicking the button labelled "Dark mode" makes
the page LIGHT. Wiring the listener to a function that calls both sync() and
paint() fixes both halves.

A THIRD, IN THE STYLESHEET, and it is the one with a measured number attached.
site/style.css's `.year-toggle:disabled { opacity: 0.55 }` silently invalidates
the contrast table 20 lines below it, in exactly the state that comment says a
no-JS reader sees for the WHOLE VISIT. The table measures the selection ring at
7.11:1 light / 8.26:1 dark against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 -- opaque-element numbers.
The fieldset ships `disabled`, so with JS off (or if app.js 404s) the group
composites at 55% over --plane throughout. Recomputed with the model that
reproduces their 7.11 exactly: ring vs fill falls to 2.51:1 in light (BELOW
3:1) and 3.47:1 in dark, and the selected year's label text to 4.17:1 (below
1.4.3's 4.5:1). Since the fill is identical between checked and unchecked --
the comment's own 1.000:1 finding -- that 2.51:1 ring is the ONLY remaining
signal of which year is on screen for a no-JS reader in light mode. Dim
something other than the whole group, or re-derive the ring token for the 0.55
case. See fisc-6at, which is about the same stylesheet's numbers being pinned
by nothing.
acceptance_criteria: the year toggle names the year the page is drawing after F5 and after Back; the theme button's label and aria-pressed follow an OS theme change; the disabled fieldset's ring meets 3:1 or the measured table says what it actually measures
notes:
2026-08-27 THE YEAR-TOGGLE HALF IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, twice, in /code-review of the drill-down branch.

site/app.js's main() ends with showYear(years[0]) and never reads the radio's checked state, and index.html.tmpl ships the year radios with no autocomplete="off". So: select FY2026-27, press F5. The browser restores the user-modified radio to FY2026-27, wireYears re-enables the fieldset, and the page draws data/sankey.json -- the toggle reads FY2026-27 while the tiles, lede, <title>, footer basis and chart all read FY2025-26. No change event fires, so it never self-corrects.

That is verbatim the state index.html.tmpl's own comment calls worse than no control. Either autocomplete="off" on the inputs or opening on the checked radio closes it; the second is better, because it makes the restored selection do what the reader expects rather than discarding it.
close_reason:
Landed in 96542e6, all three defects, each proven by reverting it independently.

(1) YEAR TOGGLE: main() now opens on checkedYear(years) rather than years[0]. Took the bead's preferred branch -- honour the restored selection rather than force the radio back -- because discarding a reader's selection looks like the page ignoring a click. Reverting it reports the page drawing 'FY 2025-26 adopted' while the control is checked on sankey-2027, AND fetching data/sankey.json, which is the same lie one layer down.

(2) THEME BUTTON: wireTheme's sync closure became file-scope syncTheme and the prefers-color-scheme listener calls it as well as paint. Reverting reports 'Dark mode / aria-pressed=false' on a dark page.

(3) STYLESHEET: the opacity moved off the FIELDSET onto the legend and the UNCHECKED pills, so the selected pill stays opaque and every figure in the measured contrast table remains true of what ships. NO NEW RATIO WAS COMPUTED -- deliberately. The bead offered 'dim something other than the whole group, or re-derive the ring token'; the second would publish a second hand-computed number into a tree that parses no CSS (fisc-6at), doubling the unpinned surface rather than closing it. Pinned by TestTheDisabledYearToggleDoesNotDimItsOwnSelectionRing, in the same string-assertion shape as its fisc-36r sibling and for the same stated reason.

THE HARNESS GREW TWICE, both times to model what the template ships: it now plants the year radios (checkedStem is the browser's form-state restore) and matchMedia's matches is a getter over a mutable flag with setOSDark. Without those, (1) and (2) were not assertable at all -- only 'a listener is attached', which is what let (2) sit there.

fisc-6at is untouched and still open. This change was shaped specifically not to make it worse.

title: Sankey.Graph validates its column count and never its scope, so the spine is the one document that does not fail closed on a foreign schedule
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-26, reproduced by calling the function.

internal/project/sankey.go's Graph checks len(o.Columns) and never looks at
o.Scope. Trends.Document does (internal/project/trends.go), refusing a foreign
scope with a hint. So:

  (&Sankey{}).Graph(facts, Options{Columns: []Column{{2026, BasisAdopted}},
                                   Scope: TrendsScope, Version: "x"})

returns a FULLY FORMED GRAPH built over the pp.127-140 revenue-by-fund rows:
netCells groups them by (kind, category, fund_group) and emits
revenue/<cat> -> fund-group/<group> links, with metadata.scope
"revenue-by-fund" and a headline.all_funds_gross_revenue_cents that is a
DIFFERENT total from the spine's.

UNREACHABLE TODAY and that is not the point. Sankey.Slices and slicesOf's
fallback both pin PublishedScope, so nothing in the tree calls it this way. The
asymmetry is the defect: Options.Scope's own doc comment says the field exists
to stop the fisc-u2v doubling, and the one document the site publishes as its
headline is the one that does not enforce it, while the newer and smaller
document does.

FIX: the same refusal Trends.Document makes, in the same shape and with the
same hint, so the two projections agree about what Scope is for.

A SECOND, SMALLER THING FROM THE SAME REVIEW, filed here because it is one line
in the same file: Sankey has `var _ Projection = (*Sankey)(nil)` but no
`var _ Sliced = (*Sankey)(nil)`, unlike Trends which asserts both. Sliced is
consumed ONLY through runtime type assertions (pkg/cmd/export/data.go,
internal/check/subject.go). If Sankey.Slices' signature ever drifts -- someone
drops the `version` parameter -- everything still compiles, both assertions
silently return false, `fisc export` falls back to
PublishedFiscalYears() x PublishedBasis and `fisc verify` to factSlices, and
the spine stops being built over the years it declares with no compile error
anywhere. That is the blank-ident-assert idiom, and the spine is the case it
matters most for.
acceptance_criteria: Sankey.Graph refuses a scope it is not of, in the shape Trends.Document already uses; Sankey carries a compile-time Sliced assertion; a test calls Graph with a foreign scope directly
close_reason:
Landed in 2949e96. Sankey.Graph refuses a foreign scope in Trends.Document's shape and with the same hint; Sankey gains the var _ Sliced assertion it lacked. TestGraphRefusesAForeignSchedule calls Graph directly, which is the only way to reach it, and was proved failable by removing the guard.

ONE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, measured while landing it. The text says the foreign-scope build returns 'a headline.all_funds_gross_revenue_cents that is a DIFFERENT total from the spine's'. IT IS THE SAME TOTAL -- 29,996,900,700 both -- and necessarily so, because revenue-detail-ties-to-spine is the check that makes pp.127-140 sum to pp.66-67's figure to the cent. The defect is STRUCTURAL: 17 nodes against the spine's 25 and 29 links against its 58, with no expenditure side, no fund balance and no transfers out, published under the spine's contract. A reader looking for the wrong number would not have found one.

title: publishedProjectionBuilt unions each projection's columns, so verify passes a corpus export refuses
description:
SPLIT OUT OF fisc-rmx, whose 2026-08-26 note ends "whoever takes this should
decide whether that asymmetry is its own bead". A slice touching
internal/check/coverage.go four times opened that file and did not fix it, so it
is filed rather than left in a note on a bead about something else.

THE DEFECT. publishedProjectionBuilt (internal/check/coverage.go) keys its
built-set on struct{name, scope} and UNIONS each matching projection's columns.
So a spine carrying two BASES for one fiscal year -- an FY2026 revised column
mapped beside the adopted one -- unions to {2026 adopted, 2026 revised, 2027
adopted} and satisfies every published document. The check passes.

`fisc export` REFUSES the same corpus. stemFor tells documents apart by
project.PublishedStem(name, o.Columns[0].FiscalYear) -- year alone -- so the two
FY2026 slices compute the same stem and the duplicate-stem guard fires, taking
the whole export down including the files that were fine.

WHY IT MATTERS SEPARATELY FROM fisc-rmx. fisc-rmx owns making the stem a
function of the whole column list, which is a four-site change across
pkg/cmd/export and internal/project plus published URLs. THIS is the smaller
and differently-shaped claim: verify's job is to tell you before export does,
and here it tells you the opposite. A check that greens a corpus the next
command in the pipeline rejects is worse than no check, because it is the one a
reader trusts to have looked.

Whether the fix is to key the built-set on the columns rather than union them,
or to have this check compare against what stemFor would produce, is the
decision. The first is local to coverage.go; the second couples a check to a
command's naming scheme, which this package has avoided elsewhere.

Found by /code-review 2026-08-26, and independently in fisc-rmx's own planning
pass the same day.
acceptance_criteria: a spine carrying two bases for one fiscal year is reported by fisc verify rather than passing; the finding names the collision export would hit
close_reason:
Landed in be735a5. The union is gone: a published document is covered by ONE slice, and a slice no published document claims is reported naming the stem it would take and the document already there.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD LEFT OPEN IS ANSWERED: the check asks project.PublishedStem, not pkg/cmd/export's stemFor. PublishedStem is the shared declaration and its own doc comment says it lives beside the year list 'because fisc verify has to name the same documents the site serves in order to say one of them was not built'. Reaching into the command's helper would have been the coupling this package avoids elsewhere.

BOTH HALVES MEASURED END TO END. verify reported PASS on a spine carrying FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted, and fisc export over the same corpus printed 'the sankey and sankey projections both want the stem "sankey": FY2026 adopted and FY2026 revised' and wrote NO file at all.

A SECOND DEFECT OF THE UNION THIS BEAD DOES NOT NAME, and it is the quieter one: N single-column slices satisfied an N-column document. project.MissingColumns returns empty for revenue-trends' four declared columns against a union of four one-column slices, so a Trends returning one slice per column would ship four files with verify green and the file at the declared stem covering a quarter of what it declares. Export SUCCEEDS there -- no loud guard -- so it would have shipped.

title: The stylesheet's state indicators and its contrast numbers are pinned by nothing
description:
FOUND while landing fisc-8qx, 2026-08-26, and verified rather than assumed.

NOTHING IN THE TREE RENDERS OR PARSES CSS. tools/jscheck reads site/style.css only to harvest custom-property NAMES (harness.mjs, the FUND_COLOR_VAR check); no Go test and no jscheck module reads a declaration. The one CSS assertion that exists, TestTheDisabledYearToggleKeepsItsSelectionUnderTheCursor in internal/export/export_test.go, matches SELECTOR strings and is green through any change to what those selectors declare -- deliberately, and its own doc comment argues why a specificity calculator or a CSS parser would be worse.

WHAT THAT LEAVES UNPINNED, measured:

(1) THE MEASURED CONTRAST TABLE in the revenue mark's comment block (six ratios for --ink-2, --ink-1, --critical and --muted, light and dark). Changing any of those four tokens in any of the three palette blocks silently falsifies it. fisc-36r's commit called it 'pinned'; it is not, and that correction is where this bead starts.

(2) THE YEAR TOGGLE'S SELECTED STATE, as of fisc-8qx. The checked ring is var(--ink-2) at 7.11:1 light / 8.26:1 dark against the composited fill, and the hover fill is var(--wash). Setting them back to the same value -- which is the defect fisc-8qx fixed -- reddens nothing.

(3) THE THREE PALETTE BLOCKS AGREE BY HAND. :root, the prefers-color-scheme block and the [data-theme=dark] block define the same tokens; the two dark ones are byte-identical by design and nothing asserts it.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS WHAT TO DO, which is why this is a bead rather than a patch. The honest options each cost something: a headless browser puts a second runtime on the check path that the node boundary in conventions.md deliberately keeps narrow; a CSS parser in Go is the second implementation of a browser thing jscheck refuses to write one layer up; and computing composited contrast in a test means re-implementing alpha compositing plus sRGB linearisation, which is small and real but only pins the arithmetic if the test also knows which rules apply to which element -- back to a selector engine.

A CHEAPER PARTIAL that may be the whole answer: assert that named PAIRS of declarations differ, by extracting two known rule blocks by their selector string and comparing the one property in question. Not a parser -- two string indexes and a compare -- and it would have caught (2) exactly. It cannot catch (1).

Note the cost of getting this wrong is not a broken build: it is a page that looks fine to whoever changed it and is unreadable to somebody else, or a comment full of numbers that were true once.
notes:
2026-08-29 PATH CORRECTION: this bead's description cites `conventions.md` for the node boundary. That file was merged into AGENTS.md and deleted (5794a60); the rule now lives in AGENTS.md under "The node boundary". Nothing about the bead's substance changes.
2026-09-08, from fisc-yj4w.14: --measure is a third unpinned declaration, and this bead's premise still holds exactly as written.

style.css now carries `--measure: 68ch` in :root, pointed at by .lede, .caveat and one rule covering the prose that previously inherited main's 1180px. TestTheStylesheetHasOneTextMeasure was added in the same lane and its doc comment says what it witnesses: ONE DECLARATION, NOT ONE RENDERING. It asserts the token is declared once, that at least three rules use it, that the two literals it replaced are gone, and that the container rule survives verbatim -- the last arm because grepping the file for "max-width: 1180px" passed over a stylesheet that split that rule and clamped main to the reading measure, which was measured green.

NOT witnessed by it, and not witnessable by anything here: that the property applies to any element a template renders, that a line comes out at 68 characters, or that the chart and the wide tables stayed at the container width.

THE LANE EXTENDED THE STRING IDIOM RATHER THAN INTRODUCING A PARSER, which is this bead's "cheaper partial" taken one step: the assertions extract known rule text by its selector string and compare, exactly as the two year-toggle tests beside them already did. That is now three tests in that shape, which is worth knowing before anyone re-opens the headless-browser question.

ALSO NEW AND UNPINNED: @media print gained `details > *:not(summary) { display: block }` and `details::details-content { content-visibility: visible }`, because folding five sections took them off a printed copy. Whether either override works is fisc-yj4w.18.
2026-09-23, PRICED BY A DEFECT IT PREDICTED. The owner found a reader-facing one by clicking the shipped site: every focus indicator on the page is var(--ink-1), which is #ffffff in both dark blocks, so a click draws a white border -- and a ribbon's is a box round its whole bezier. fisc-4w20 carries it.

THAT IS THIS BEAD'S OWN COST SENTENCE COMING TRUE -- 'a page that looks fine to whoever changed it and is unreadable to somebody else' -- and it is why P3 was wrong. The cheap partial named here, two rule blocks extracted by selector string and one property compared, would have caught it: it is the same shape as arm (2), the year toggle's checked ring.

title: A projection's stem must be a function of its whole column list, not its first fiscal year
description:
SPLIT OUT OF fisc-lmz, whose two safe halves landed in 19a580f (the unchecked Columns[0] index and the guard's misattributed message). This is the part that is NOT a one-function fix, and the split was made on peer review of the landing plan.

THE DEFECT. Sankey.Slices derives one slice per (fiscal year, basis) pair the spine carries; stemFor tells the resulting documents apart by project.PublishedStem(name, o.Columns[0].FiscalYear) -- YEAR ALONE. So the instant the spine carries two BASES for one year (an FY2026 revised column mapped beside the adopted one), Slices declares two slices, stemFor computes the same stem for both, and the duplicate-stem guard fires. Sankey.Slices' own doc comment presents mapping a revised column as needing no other change; that claim is false while stemFor is year-keyed.

NOTE THE GUARD FIRING IS CORRECT. It fails closed with a good message, and that is not what to fix. What the bead objects to is that the collision is REACHABLE -- and that it takes 'fisc export' down entirely, so no file is written including the ones that were fine.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-FUNCTION CHANGE, measured: stems are computed in THREE places -- pkg/cmd/export/data.go stemFor, pkg/cmd/export/data.go yearStems (the client config's per-year 'stem' field), internal/project/project.go PublishedDocuments -- compared in TWO more (internal/check/subject.go, internal/check/coverage.go), and rebuilt in internal/check/fixture_test.go. Changing only stemFor splits the written files from the config's stems, from assertPublishedBuilt, and from published-projection-built.

AND STEMS ARE PUBLISHED URLS. data/sankey.json is promised by docs/sankey-contract.md, data/revenue-trends.json by docs/revenue-trends-contract.md, and the stem is the year radio's value in site/app.js (years.find(y => y.stem === target.value)). A scheme that renamed them would break both the contract and the toggle.
acceptance_criteria: a spine carrying two bases for one fiscal year exports two distinct stems and does not abort; the stem is derived from the whole Column list in ONE place that all three current call sites use; a test pins the literal strings sankey, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends unchanged for today's corpus; docs/sankey-contract.md and Sankey.Slices' doc comment agree with whatever ships
notes:
2026-08-26, from planning-time exploration rather than implementation. THREE CORRECTIONS AND ONE ADDITION to this bead's own text.

(1) IT CITES TestStemForDistinguishesAYearFromAWhole, WHICH EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE TREE. It was a phantom citation in pkg/cmd/export/data.go's comment, corrected in 034dfa8 for exactly this reason; the bead text inherited it. The real test is TestStemForAsksHowManyDocumentsNotHowManyColumns (pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go), and it pins only ONE of the two directions this bead claims: every case uses PublishedBasis or a basis that is unique per year, so no case exercises two bases for one year.

(2) STEMS ARE DERIVED IN FOUR PLACES, NOT THREE. The bead lists data.go stemFor, data.go yearStems and project.go PublishedDocuments. internal/check/fixture_test.go spineDocuments is a fourth, and it hardcodes PublishedBasis alongside the year.

(3) yearStems IS THE ONE THAT BITES, and the bead does not say why. It re-derives PublishedStem(name, y) over PublishedFiscalYears() and filters to what was built -- so a stem stemFor produced that yearStems cannot reconstruct FROM A YEAR ALONE gets written to disk and never offered to the reader. Any scheme keyed on more than the year has to change both or the toggle silently loses a document.

THE ADDITION, and it is worth more than the corrections: fisc verify WOULD NOT CATCH THIS. publishedProjectionBuilt (internal/check/coverage.go) keys on struct{name, scope} and UNIONS each projection's columns, so a spine carrying two bases for 2026 unions to {2026 adopted, 2026 revised, 2027 adopted} and satisfies every published document. verify passes a corpus export refuses. Whoever takes this should decide whether that asymmetry is its own bead.

AND A FIFTH SITE, outside Go: site/index.html.tmpl renders the year radios as id="year-{{$y.Year}}" with <label for=...> keyed on the same integer. Two documents for one fiscal year produce duplicate DOM ids and a label pointing at whichever radio parsed first -- independently of what the stem is called.
close_reason:
Landed in a197be7. project.Stem is the one spelling of the rule, reading the whole column list; stemFor delegates, yearStems reads the declared stems instead of rebuilding them (the fourth derivation is gone, not moved), and site/index.html.tmpl keys the year radio ids on the stem rather than the year.

THE LITERALS ARE UNCHANGED AND PINNED: sankey, sankey-2027, revenue-trends (TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged). Verified end to end: a spine carrying FY2026 revised beside FY2026 adopted now exports sankey, sankey-2026-revised, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends and does not abort. Before, dist/ was empty.

/code-review CAUGHT THE SAME MISTAKE ONE LEVEL DOWN and it is worth recording, because the bead's acceptance criterion did not reach it. Stem first took a COUNT of documents, and the count meant three different things at its three call sites: pkg/cmd/export counted the slices a projection DECLARED, internal/check counted the ones that BUILT and only within one scope, and PublishedDocuments counted published YEARS. One spelling of the rule over three spellings of its input establishes nothing. Stem takes the declared list itself now, and internal/check assembles it from the built and the refused together -- which is the list export names its files from.

A COHERENCE PROPERTY NOTHING HELD, found reproducing that review finding: Stem gives the bare name to PublishedFiscalYear while PublishedDocuments walks PublishedFiscalYears(), and nothing made the constant the list's first entry. Editing one alone makes the declaration name a stem every derivation computes differently. Pinned by TestTheOpeningPublishedYearOpensTheYearList.

fisc-lmz closes with it -- its remaining half was this bead.

title: The footer's scope, basis and cited pages are the opening year's, and paintYearWords never repaints them
description:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, alongside fisc-yi4 and distinct from it. fisc-yi4 is about clientConfig.Docs; this is about the footer's own prose.

site/index.html.tmpl:196 renders 'Scope {{.Scope}}, basis {{.Basis}}' and :184 renders the list of cited pages, both from the OPENING year's metadata. paintYearWords writes year.basis into #lede-year and #chart-title and rewrites [data-year-path], but touches neither of these.

yearView carries a per-year Basis precisely because it varies. Publish a year on a 'proposed' basis, or one citing pp.68-69 instead of pp.66-67, and after a switch the lede reads 'FY 2026-27 proposed' while the footer three screens down reads 'basis adopted' and cites the other year's pages -- one page stating two different things about one document.

LATENT TODAY because both published years are adopted and cite the same two pages. Same shape as fisc-yi4 and probably wants the same landing: the union across years for the page list, and a per-year repaint for the basis.
close_reason: The footer's basis follows the year through #page-basis. The cited-page half of this bead was already fixed by 19a580f (unionSources) and the bead text was stale; the footer's <h3> now says it covers every year the page can show, rather than leaving a reader to assume the narrower set. Scope is NOT repainted and must not be: it cannot vary (Sankey.Slices fixes it) and the lede states the same claim again in prose that no switch touches, so a repaint would fix one of two copies. buildSankeyPage refuses a year stem whose scope or generated_by disagrees instead. Both extra guards and the lede/footer coupling pin came out of /code-review of this change.

title: A year document that parses but throws while drawing leaves the page split across two years
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, while fisc-8cg was landing. It is the residue
of that fix rather than something it caused, and it is filed because the fix's
own harness drives the exact document and asserts only half of what matters.

site/app.js showYear: the try now covers the fetch AND response.json(), which is
what fisc-8cg widened it for. It does NOT cover the drawing that follows.
paintYearWords(year) runs FIRST, then buildLegend / buildDerivedList /
buildTable / render, none of them guarded.

SO: a year document that parses, passes the schema gate, and is structurally
wrong -- a null or absent nodes array is enough, and nothing validates that the
keys the schema_version promises are present -- throws in buildLegend. The
change handler's .catch paints a banner, and the page is left with THE NEW
YEAR'S tiles, caveats, lede, <title> and [data-year-path] over THE OLD YEAR'S
chart and flow table.

That is a page whose words and whose figures are about different fiscal years,
with a citation link pointing at the year that is not drawn. It is the same
class fisc-fjy and the [data-year-path] repaint were about, reached from the
other side.

WHY THE HARNESS PASSES ON IT TODAY. The last case in tools/jscheck/lifecycle.mjs
-- "a year document that parses but will not draw is reported, not swallowed" --
feeds precisely this document and asserts ONLY that a banner appears. It does
not look at what the rest of the page now says. So `make js` is green over the
split state, and the check is right as far as it goes: extend it rather than
replace it.

TWO CANDIDATE SHAPES, and the choice is a real one.

  (1) DRAW FIRST, PAINT WORDS LAST. Move paintYearWords below render() so a
      throw leaves the page wholly on the old year with a banner over it. Small,
      and it makes the failure atomic in the direction that matters -- a page
      consistently showing the previous year is honest, a page showing two is
      not. Check the ordering does not break the tile/hero measurements
      year.mjs pins.

  (2) VALIDATE THE DOCUMENT'S SHAPE where understands() validates its version.
      Stronger, and it is what the schema_version gate already implies it does:
      the version is a promise about which keys exist and nothing checks that
      the promise was kept. More work, and it needs a decision about how much of
      the document to validate client-side when internal/check validates all of
      it server-side.

(1) is the smaller and probably right one; (2) is worth stating in the bead so
it is not re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: a year document that parses and then throws while drawing leaves the page wholly on the year it was already showing, with a banner; the existing lifecycle.mjs case is extended to assert the lede, tiles and data-year-path, not only that a banner appeared; year.mjs's tile and hero checks still pass
close_reason: Landed in 2439af3. render() is split into layOut(doc) (computes, touches nothing) and render(laid) (draws), and showYear lays out BEFORE repainting -- that ordering, not the gate, is what makes a failed draw leave the page wholly on the previous year. Mutation-verified both ways. Neither of the bead's two candidate shapes was taken: re-ordering the repaint only moves which half is stale, and widening the try would have left both .catch handlers with no reachable case (lifecycle.mjs says that makes them unfalsifiable claims). drawableSankey() beside understands() buys the MESSAGE only -- measured: nodes.map throws inside layOut, so with the gate deleted the page still refuses without splitting; what changes is 'the file is truncated' vs a TypeError shown to a reader. The check asserts the wording for that reason. The last-resort .catch keeps a reachable case via a new and more honest fixture: a link naming a node the document does not carry.

title: The trends page trusts counts it never checks, and buildCells drops a point it cannot place
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26, and reproduced with an overlay test.

internal/export/page.go's buildCells SILENTLY DROPS any point whose
(fiscal_year, basis) is not among metadata.columns, and its own comment
justifies that with "which is why the caller compares counts.points against what
it rendered". THE CALLER DOES NOT. trendsMetadata.Counts.Points is decoded and
read nowhere -- only .Facts and .Series are used -- so:

  A 1-column document with a 2-point series exports successfully, renders ONE
  cell, loses the other figure with NO error, and the lede still prints
  "1 columns, 2 figures in all".

That is a published page whose own prose contradicts what it drew, which is a
plausible wrong value with provenance disagreeing with it -- the class this
project exists to refuse. The same gap runs the other way: .Count is
counts.series and is never compared with len(body.Series).

NOT REACHABLE THROUGH internal/project TODAY, because Trends.Document filters
points on the same o.Columns the metadata is built from. So this is a packager
that does not fail closed, not a live corruption -- and the fix is the
comparison the comment already promises, not a redesign.

RELATED, SAME FILE, SAME SHAPE: internal/check/trends.go's two checks jointly
claim to cover the published document and do not cover this one corruption.
Verified: build a Trends document over [{2026 adopted}], append a GENUINE FY2027
point (every field matching its real fact), and trend-points-tie-to-facts passes
over 3 points while trend-series-are-complete passes over 2 series. comparePoint
compares a point only against its own fact, and the reverse sweep walks only
factsFor(p.Options); nothing compares a point's COLUMN against metadata.columns.
Fix both together or the packager's guard is the only one.
acceptance_criteria: buildTrendsPage refuses a document whose rendered cell count disagrees with counts.points, and whose series count disagrees with counts.series, naming both numbers; a test builds the 1-column-2-point document directly and shows the refusal; internal/check gains an arm comparing each published point's column against metadata.columns, with the append-a-real-point mutation as its evidence
close_reason: Landed in the packager/check commit. buildCells now reports what it PLACED and buildTrendsPage reconciles that against counts.points, plus len(series) against counts.series, naming both numbers; two points in one column is refused separately because the counts still reconcile in that case. The check gains a column-membership arm -- measured as invisible to both existing arms, since comparePoint compares a point to its own fact and the reverse sweep filters facts on the same columns. Evidence is a GENUINE appended FY2027 point, with trend-series-are-complete asserted green in the same run. fisc-ewt's QUIET block now asserts, and records the two checks as OVERLAPPING on a dropped point rather than dividing labour, reproduced by running the mutation.

title: Four checks in internal/check report a wrong verdict or wrong wording, and uncheckedDocuments has no test
design:
FOUND BY /code-review, 2026-08-26. Four defects in one package, none of which
changes a published figure and all of which send a reader to the wrong place.
Filed together because they share one cause: an arm added for a shape that no
longer exists alone. Each was reproduced with a throwaway test.

(1) documents-are-checked CAN REPORT PASS HAVING EXAMINED NOTHING, which
documents.go's own comment calls the one thing this package exists to prevent.
`subjects` is len(s.Projections), which COUNTS projections exempted by
uncheckedDocuments, so the `nothing:` branch is unreachable once every
projection is declared. With uncheckedDocuments = {"blob": ...} and one
shapeless projection named blob: PASS, summary "0 projections structurally
checked (), plus 1 of \"blob\" (no checks yet) declared unchecked". Note also
the empty "()" from describeShapes over an empty map.

(2) THE STALE-DECLARATION FINDING HARDCODES THE GRAPH SHAPE
(documents.go:116). A declared projection carrying only a TrendsDocument reports
"every projection of that name now carries a graph" -- in the check that was
widened precisely so a document need not be a graph. It sends a reader looking
for a graph that does not exist.

(3) staleDeclarations ARM 1 MASKS ARM 3 (coverage.go:553). Arm 1 tests only
len(drawnSlices) > 0 && len(liveSlices) == 0 and never consults `carried`, so a
scope carrying NO facts reports "all 0 of its facts are in some projection's
slice; the declaration is exempting nothing and must be removed" whenever any
projection merely DECLARES that scope. The correct diagnosis -- carried == 0,
meaning no rule writes it, which is the mistyped-scope case the map exists for
-- is unreachable.

(4) STRANDED-FACT COUNTS ARE DOUBLE-REPORTED (coverage.go:385). `n` is summed
over keysOf(f.Options) for each ProjectionFailure independently while `refused`
is keyed only on (year, basis, scope), so two failures sharing a slice key each
claim the full count. Message-only, and the number is what a reader triages on.

AND THE REASON ALL FOUR SURVIVED: uncheckedDocuments (documents.go:29) SHIPS
WITH NO TEST AT ALL -- no emptiness guard, no exercise of its stale branch --
unlike its sibling incompleteSeries, which has TestIncompleteSeriesIsEmpty,
TestAStaleIncompleteSeriesDeclarationIsCaught and a withIncompleteSeries swap
helper. (1) and (2) are exactly what that missing test catches. Write it first.

FIFTH, SMALLER: subject.go's ProjectionFailure doc comment is left dangling by
an earlier edit -- "Neither is a verdict about the corpus: the first is a
programming error and the second is..." describes two items that no longer
exist, and mislabels the single remaining hard error. Line 174 is 105 chars,
past the file's wrap.
