site/app.js's capColumn doc opens "WHY A CAP IS NEEDED AT ALL" with figures pinned to 7ded1c6 and to dist/data/fund-flows.json: special-revenue "still puts 22 of its 49 ribbons under one pixel" rescaled, "At cap 8 the same graph comes to 2 sub-pixel ribbons, and the capital group from 4 to 1". Those were measured on the {0,3,4} chart the merge retired. The baseline is stated, so the sentence is not false about the past -- it is a claim a reader cannot check against the tree, which is what AGENTS.md's "The node boundary" refuses ("Quote what the current code does").

MEASURED TODAY through tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's openedWide(3, [group]) plus expandAll, laying the drawn document out with app.js's own layOut:

  fund-group/special-revenue  capped 19 ribbons, 0 sub-pixel, smallest 3.971px
                              expanded 42 ribbons, 9 sub-pixel, smallest 0.124px
  fund-group/capital          capped 14 ribbons, 0 sub-pixel, smallest 9.741px
                              expanded 16 ribbons, 2 sub-pixel, smallest 0.108px

so at today's {0,2,3} the cap leaves NO sub-pixel ribbon where the old chart left 2, and the uncapped column is 9 of 42 rather than 22 of 49. The argument (a distribution rescaling cannot fix; the cap is what makes the column drawable) survives the re-measurement; only its figures do not.

WHAT TO WEIGH BEFORE REWRITING IT: pkg/cmd/export/data.go's fund-group cap comment already states "9 of its 42 ribbons" and "capped it draws 19 ribbons and none of them is sub-pixel", and tools/jscheck/drill.mjs pins capped {links:19, hairlines:0} / uncapped {links:42, hairlines:9}. Copying those into app.js would be a third spelling of one measurement. The fund/200 share (34.9%) and the bottom two funds (0.034%) are the part of that paragraph nothing else in the tree states, and are what the comment is actually for.
close_reason: Re-measured and pinned. The comment now quotes FY2025-26's {0,2,3} window as the page draws it -- 9 of 42 sub-pixel drawn whole, smallest 0.124px, largest fund 34.9% and smallest 0.034% of the column; 19 ribbons and none sub-pixel at the step's cap of 8, smallest 3.971px; capital from 2 of 16 to none of 14 -- and the argument survived the re-measurement with only its numbers moving. The half the bead did not ask for but needed: tools/jscheck/fold.mjs re-measures all six through openedWide and expandAll and matches them as whole quoted phrases, so the drift that made these stale unseen now fails. Mutations: a figure edited in the comment reddens it by name, and widening the declared cap in data.go so it stops engaging reddens it with the measurement that follows.

title: drill.mjs's expandAll walks past a tail the page refuses, so the rung walk's expansion count is silently short
description:
tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's expandAll() finds a tail with app.expandable and stops at the first iteration that finds none, returning how many it expanded. A tail the page will not draw out -- an aggregate folded into a kept flank by the chart above, which is what fisc-2wsw named -- answers false there for the same reason it does on the chart, so expandAll returns as though the chart were fully drawn out.

WHAT THAT COSTS. rungs.mjs's walk expands every fold before taking a rung's offers, and its own detail line says so: "every folded column expanded before a rung's offers are taken, so a node a cap hid is one this walk opens". A refused tail makes that sentence false without making any check red -- the nodes behind it are never opened, so the rungs they would have reached are never visited and never compared against Go's answer, and the walk's expansion count reads as a full sweep.

MEASURED: latent on the committed corpus. chart.mjs's arm (f) counts 0 refused tails at both budgets, so no state reached today has one.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: expandAll (or its caller) distinguishes "no tail left" from "a tail left that the page refuses", the way chart.mjs's arm (f) now does, and the walk's claim about itself says which it saw. fisc-2wsw landed that distinction in one module only.

title: The page offers no way to draw out a tail an outer chart folded into a kept flank
description:
site/app.js's expandable() offers the Enter gesture only where THIS rung's step names the tail's tier in step.caps, so an aggregate that arrived inside a KEPT FLANK -- folded by the chart above -- is drawn to the reader as "N smaller funds" and nothing on the chart draws it out. The mark carries the fold marker and the words promise a number, and the only way to see what it stands for is to leave the rung.

THIS IS OPTION (2) OF fisc-2wsw, which landed option (1) instead: tools/jscheck/chart.mjs's arm (f) now counts a tail it was shown and could not expand and goes red when one appears, so the day a kept flank first folds is a red check rather than a silent hole. The checker no longer hides the case; the page still has it.

WHAT TO DECIDE BEFORE PATCHING, and it is a reading question rather than a predicate question: whether expanding a column that an OUTER chart capped is a state a reader should be able to reach at all. Expanding it redraws the chart the reader is on with a column the rung above decided did not fit, and the breadcrumb chip that folds it back is per-tier on the current rung -- so the fold it would undo is not the one this rung made. Measured on the committed corpus at both budgets: no such tail is drawn, every kept flank being a single-node column, so this is latent and would ship latent.

IF IT IS DONE: it is a client change with its own review, and arm (f) is what witnesses it -- the counter this bead's parent added goes from counting a refusal to counting an expansion.

title: site/app.js declares @ts-check and says it is checked with tsc, and nothing checks it
description:
site/app.js:1 is '// @ts-check' and its header says the file is 'Plain browser JavaScript with JSDoc types, checked with tsc --checkJs'. Measured: no Makefile arm, no CI step and no node_modules run tsc. The claim is false about this tree.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A STALE SENTENCE. The annotations are load-bearing prose -- fisc-e87i is a typedef that stopped describing the wire (FiscDrillStep never declared widen, which activeTiers reads) and survived precisely because nothing reads the types. A convention nobody enforces decays silently, and the header tells a reader it is enforced.

AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REFUSED BY A RULE. Running tsc needs a package.json and node_modules, and AGENTS.md's node boundary says node stays off the deploy path and there is neither. So this cannot be closed by adding the gate the sentence promises.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a decision rather than an edit: either the header stops claiming tsc checks it and says what the annotations actually are -- a convention a contributor may check locally, which nothing enforces -- or the node boundary gains a stated exception for an optional local typecheck that is not a gate. The first is cheap and honest. The second is a change to a rule and belongs to the owner.

Neighbour: fisc-e87i, which is one instance of what goes wrong meanwhile.
close_reason: Closed at b36f6ec by deleting the sentence rather than by adding the gate it promised, which is the option this bead named as the cheap and honest one. app.js's header now says the JSDoc types are a convention nothing enforces, names what IS enforced -- seam.mjs compares each typedef against the Go struct's JSON keys and schema/page.schema.json -- and keeps // @ts-check, which costs a served page nothing. Adding npm to CI stays the owner's call and AGENTS.md, "The node boundary" still refuses it.

title: chart.mjs's tail arm can only ask a tail this rung's own cap folded, so a kept flank's fold stays unobservable
description:
tools/jscheck/chart.mjs's arm (f) asks a tail what it stands for by pressing Enter on the drawn mark and reading the column the page draws out. So it reaches exactly the tails site/app.js's expandable() answers for, and that predicate requires the tail's tier to be named in THIS rung's step.caps: an aggregate that arrived inside a KEPT FLANK was folded by the chart above, the gesture is not offered on it, and the arm breaks out of its loop leaving it folded. An id behind such a tail is invisible to chart.mjs for exactly the reason fisc-lzkn named.

MEASURED, on the committed corpus at both budgets: every tail the arm meets is expandable -- 3 expansions over FY 2025-26's answered states and 5 over FY 2026-27's, none left folded -- so the gap is latent rather than live. site/app.js's expandable() doc comment says the same of the affordance: "Latent on the committed corpus, whose kept flanks are single-node columns, and latent is how it would ship."

WHAT TO DO, and it is a decision before it is a patch. Either (1) the arm grows a counter for a tail it was shown and could not expand, and goes red when one appears -- which turns the day a kept flank first folds into a red check rather than a silent hole, and is the cheaper half; or (2) the page offers the gesture there too, which is a client change with its own review and its own reading of whether expanding a flank folded by an outer chart is a state a reader should be able to reach at all. Do not do (2) as part of a checker commit.
close_reason:
OPTION (1), the counter, and not option (2): tools/jscheck/chart.mjs's arm (f) now meets tails by name and expands them by predicate. isAggregate finds every tail the chart DREW; app.expandable answers for the ones the page will draw out; a tail shown and refused is carried out of the loop, counted in seen.refused and pushed onto wrong.tails, so it reddens the arm naming the rung, the tail's id and label, and the ids Go accounts for at that column that reach no mark. The arm's ok is unchanged -- seen.expansions > 0 && seen.revealed > 0 -- so 'no unexpandable tail was seen' and 'no tail was seen at all' still leave by different doors: refused is a count of holes whose passing value is zero, and expansions is what stops that zero meaning nothing was met.

FORCED FAILURE, because the case is latent and cannot be reached with the committed corpus. Wrapping the harness's own expandable -- app.expandable = (d) => real(d) && d.tier !== 3, three lines in checks(), site/app.js untouched -- takes (f) red at both budgets and nothing else: 'FY 2025-26 at 3 columns, fund-group/capital: the tail at column 3 (aggregate/tail/3, "3 smaller funds") is drawn and the page offers no gesture that draws it out, so what it stands for is unaskable here -- 3 id(s) Go accounts for at that column reach no mark: fund/550, fund/553, fund/580', and the same at 4 columns and on FY 2026-27. Restored, green again.

A SECOND FAIL-OPEN FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: refused is only filled by the loop's break, so a state that hit the 32-expansion bound would have said 'no tail was left folded' about a chart it never finished reading. The bound is now named once (LIMIT) and a state that reaches it is a red line of its own; lowering it to 1 takes (f) red on three states of FY 2025-26 and five of FY 2026-27, restored green.

fisc-lzkn's OWN MUTATION RE-RUN against this arm: deleting fund/580 from the sankey column's fund-group/capital rung in testdata/rungs.json still takes (f) red at both 3 and 4 columns -- 'the tail at column 3 drew fund/580, which Go accounts for nowhere at this rung' -- and nothing else in the module. Blinding marksIn() still takes all six arms red on their own counters, (f) at 0 expanded and 0 revealed. testdata/rungs.json restored and byte-identical (sha256 8c2d4c5b...).

COUNTERS on the committed corpus, this run: 3 tails expanded / 42 marks revealed / 0 refused on FY 2025-26, 5 / 84 / 0 on FY 2026-27.

Gates: make pre-commit exit 0; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped. Only tools/jscheck/chart.mjs moved.

LEFT OPEN: fisc-f59o, option (2) -- whether the page should offer the gesture on a tail an outer chart folded, which is a client change with its own reading. fisc-09fx, drill.mjs's expandAll walking past the same refusal with nothing counting it.

title: internal/export still carries the fold's Go-side machinery, and nothing production calls it
description:
DELETE SEVEN DEAD SYMBOLS FROM internal/export. Each has no production caller and is green only because its own unit test exercises it -- the shape AGENTS.md, "Prove it can fail" says to hunt for.

  internal/export/chart.go   aggregatePrefix, RoleAggregate, AggregateID, IsAggregate, (*Chart).Within
  internal/export/reach.go   Reach.In, Reach.Out  (written in ReachOf, read nowhere)

THE DECISION IS MADE; DO NOT RE-LITIGATE IT. The case for deciding later rests on fisc-phtp.2's stage 2 emitting drawn ribbons, so that a ribbon re-pointed at a tail would want AggregateID back. That premise is dead: fisc-lwh5 supersedes fisc-hz2u and NO RIBBONS SHIP. Go never names a tail.

THE EVIDENCE, measured, and it is stronger than "unused":
  - testdata/rungs.json contains the string "aggregate" zero times, so nothing Go emits names a tail.
  - site/app.js:3102 declares AGGREGATE_PREFIX, so the client owns the spelling.
  - Go's copy is therefore a SECOND SPELLING of a client-owned constant, which is the defect AGENTS.md's node boundary exists to name -- not merely weight.
  - Reach.In/Out were the ranking key for capColumn. Ranking a column against a cap is fitting, and fitting is the client's (fisc-lwh5).

WHAT THE PROOF IS, because a deletion has no mutation in the usual sense: the compiler plus the gates. `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean, `make pre-commit` exit 0, `make js` green, `./bin/fisc verify` unchanged, testdata/rungs.json and facts/facts.jsonl byte-identical. If anything goes red, a symbol was not dead and that is the finding.

TESTS GO WITH THEM. internal/export/chart_test.go and marks_test.go are their only callers; delete the arms that exist solely to exercise a deleted symbol rather than rewriting them against nothing. An arm that covers something else as well keeps that part.

DO NOT TOUCH: site/app.js (the client's fold is not in scope), the wire format, testdata/rungs.json, or Reach.At / Reach.Drawn, which are read by rungWalker.answer.

READ ONLY THESE: internal/export/chart.go, internal/export/reach.go, internal/export/chart_test.go, internal/export/marks_test.go. Skip pkg/cmd/export, internal/check and tools/jscheck entirely.
close_reason: Deleted, with the compiler and the gates as the proof: go build and go vet clean, make pre-commit exit 0, make js green, fisc verify 44 passed 0 failed, facts.jsonl and testdata/rungs.json byte-identical. Nothing went red, so none of the seven was alive. The test arms went with them rather than being rewritten against nothing -- TestChartSplicesAsWindowForDoes keeps its three splice rules with an ordinary node where the tail stood, TestMarkIDsAreTwoPrefixes drops its third prefix, TestReachOfCarriesTheFoldedChart keeps the Fold claim and loses the In/Out keying. GapOf's comment and Reach's own are restated where they named a deleted symbol.

title: rungsFor names the rung answer only to the view at IndexPath, so a second stepped page would fetch nothing and refuse every click
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.2's MEMBERSHIP STAGE (5ab0175). internal/export.rungsFor puts rungs.json into FISC_CONFIG only for the view at export.IndexPath that declares steps, and TestTheRungAnswerIsNamedToThePageThatCanUseIt pins it both ways. That is correct today and deliberately fail-closed: the walk behind the artifact starts at the spine, so any other page would be handed a file answering none of its clicks.

WHAT TO WATCH: the coupling is now silent in the other direction. A second stepped view added later gets no answer, and since the client refuses a rung it has no answer for, EVERY click on that page becomes a banner. The failure is loud at the reader and invisible at the author -- nothing in the Go tests says 'this view declares steps and has no rung answer'.

The fix when it matters is for rungsOf to walk every stepped view rather than the spine alone, and for the test to assert over the set of stepped views rather than over IndexPath.

title: year.mjs's chainedYears fixture lost its two-cap widened shape when the client started reading Go's answer
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.2's MEMBERSHIP STAGE (cd02623). chainedYears declared tiers [0,3,4] with caps at 3 and 4; it now declares [0,2,3] with a cap at 3, because the fixture must match a shipped step for the shipped rung answer to apply to it.

WHAT WAS LOST: that fixture was the only one in year.mjs exercising a two-cap window with a widened column. The shape is still modelled in drill.mjs, so it is not unwitnessed -- but it is now witnessed in one place instead of two, and the year-switching path no longer drives it at all.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, worth naming because this lane will do it again: once the client reads Go's answer, a hand-made fixture can only describe a rung Go actually answers. Fixtures that invented their own shapes must either be adopted into the shipped view or lose the shape. Each such trade should be recorded rather than absorbed.

title: unfolded() builds a rung answer that is internally inconsistent: hidden deleted, cap left beside more ids than it allows
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.2's MEMBERSHIP STAGE (cd02623). tools/jscheck's unfolded() helper produces a drawnTier with hidden removed but cap left at 8 beside 32 drawn ids -- an answer Go would never emit, because a column of 32 under a cap of 8 has a tail. capColumn returns before it notices, so the fixture works; a stricter client would refuse it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. A fixture that could not come out of the emitter is a fixture that stops predicting the emitter. The client now READS these answers, so a helper that fabricates an impossible one is testing behaviour against input the real path cannot produce -- and the day capColumn checks cap against ids, this fixture breaks for a reason that has nothing to do with the code under test.
close_reason: The helper it names is gone with the pre-computed fold: a column carries no cap and no hidden count, so there is no answer for a fixture to make inconsistent. Raising DrillStep.Caps past the column is what disengages a fold now, and uncappedSteps() in drill.mjs is the one spelling of it.

title: The rendering arm samples five rungs per budget, where the equivalence arm drives all of them
description:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING fisc-xsc8's rendering arm (4d9db66). tools/jscheck/chart.mjs drives 10 states per published year -- the overview plus a sample of rungs at each budget -- against the 76 and 74 rungs per budget that tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs walks in full.

DELIBERATE, AND THE REASON IS THE COST: rungs.mjs compares computations, and this arm RENDERS, so a state costs a full d3-sankey layout and a DOM read. make js went from 11s to 28s at the current sample.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH RECORDING. After fisc-phtp.2 the equivalence arm stops being a real comparison, and this module becomes the thing that witnesses the client. A sample is the right trade while rungs.mjs still drives every rung; it is a different trade once that is no longer true. So this bead should be re-read WHEN fisc-phtp.2 lands rather than on its own schedule -- either widen the sample, or write down why the sampled states are the ones that can fail.

Neighbour: fisc-phtp.2, whose landing is what changes the answer.
notes: fisc-phtp.2 LANDED 2026-09-20, which is the condition this bead said to re-read it on. The equivalence arm is not merely weakened: tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs's membership, split and marks comparisons are DELETED, because the client reads draws[].ids and the rung's marks rather than deriving either, so all three compared the artifact against itself. What rungs.mjs still walks in full is the column order, the cap and the fold. So chart.mjs's sample is now the only thing that renders, against a module that no longer compares what it draws -- the trade this bead names is live, and the choice is to widen the sample or to write down why the sampled states are the ones that can fail.

title: appendChild, append, prepend and replaceChildren do not detach from a previous parent, as insertBefore now does
description:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING fisc-xsc8's rendering arm (af63b3e). insertBefore was fixed there to honour its reference argument and to DETACH the node from its previous parent first; the measurement that forced it is worth keeping: with the old unshift form, d3's order() re-attached without detaching and 25 marks answered a g.node lookup 49 times while 58 ribbons answered path.link 115 times -- with both id SETS still agreeing, so a set comparison saw nothing wrong.

THE SAME CLASS OF DEFECT REMAINS in appendChild, append, prepend and replaceChildren, which still push a node onto a new parent's children without removing it from the old one.

NOTHING IN app.js RE-PARENTS THROUGH THEM TODAY, which is why this is P3 and not P1: the corruption is unreachable from the shipped client. What makes it worth a bead is that the failure is invisible by construction -- a duplicated node agrees with itself on every id, label and attribute -- so the day something does re-parent, the arm that should catch it counts the same ids twice and passes.

The rendering arm's (a) now counts DISTINCT marks for exactly this reason; that count is what would go red.

title: drill.mjs's GESTURE_WIRING pins render()'s gesture lines as source text, which the rendering arm now supersedes
description:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING fisc-xsc8's rendering arm (4d9db66). GESTURE_WIRING pins seven lines of render() AS TEXT. fisc-xsc8 measured what that is worth: a source-text pin fails when someone edits the line and passes when the line is right but the selection it sits on is empty -- it witnesses spelling, not behaviour.

THAT IS NO LONGER THE BEST AVAILABLE WITNESS. tools/jscheck/chart.mjs takes the listeners off a drawn g.node and invokes them: a click isolates and a second releases, Space isolates, the click Space synthesises does not undo it, a held key does nothing, and a double click and Enter each open a node Go answers a rung for. That is strictly stronger over the same seven lines.

RETIRING IT IS NOT MERELY DELETING IT. The three gestures were extracted from render()'s closures into named functions (clickNode, doubleClickNode, keyNode) PURELY so a check could reach them. If the text pin goes and nothing else names that extraction, the reason those functions are not closures stops being written down anywhere -- so whatever replaces the pin should carry that sentence.

title: The structure export test's stray-file arm keys on a filename prefix, not on a declared set of shipped paths
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.1 (62b8615). TestTheStructureShipsOnTheAssetChannelAndIsMeasured refuses a shipped structure.json, and finds the per-year parts, by matching the 'structure' prefix over built.Files' keys. structurePath(year) is the only writer of those names, so the test and the code agree by convention rather than by construction.

THE SHAPE THIS LEAVES OPEN: a part written under a name that does not start with 'structure' is invisible to the arm, and so is a second writer adding a 'structure-' file that is not a part. Measured today the test does catch the collapse case -- structurePath made to ignore its year is caught four ways, including a per-id comparison of a part's facts against the whole restricted to that year -- so this is about what the arm could stop seeing later, not about a hole in it now.

The fix is for buildStructure to return the paths it wrote and for the test to assert over that set.

title: testdata/README.md still describes rungs.json as pinned to rungsOf, not to the bytes the site serves
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING fisc-phtp.1 (51bca4a). TestTheRungArtifactIsWhatGoComputes no longer calls rungsOf: it reads built.Files[rungsServedPath] and pins testdata/rungs.json to the bytes buildAll ships at rungs.json. testdata/README.md's entry for the fixture still says it is pinned to what Go computes via rungsOf, and does not say the artifact is now SERVED as well as committed.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TYPO: the README is where a session learns what a fixture is for, and 'a copy of a computation' and 'a copy of what the site serves' license different edits. The second forbids regenerating it to make a test pass without asking what the site now ships.
close_reason: Closed by the sweep it asked for, widened: the README entry was not one stale sentence but four, because fisc-phtp.2 landed between the filing and the fix. It now says the file is the page's INPUT -- served as well as committed, read by heldFor and by carryResidual/markGap -- which is the licence the bead was filed to state, and names what holds it at each end: the two Go tests, and the page's own refusals rather than a comparison in tools/jscheck.

title: AGENTS.md's line budget becomes a gate, and the alarm that priced it has reversed
description:
ARM D OF fisc-ak39, split out 2026-09-19 when arm B landed and the parent's single priority stopped fitting its four arms.

A gate guarding AGENTS.md against regrowth. Not an intrinsic count -- the number is a budget, chosen, and the point is that crossing it is a decision someone makes rather than a drift nobody notices.

THE URGENCY IS GONE AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY, which is the reason this is P3 and not P1 as the parent was. The bead was filed against 'the file went 690 to 1126 lines in seven days'. Measured 2026-09-19: AGENTS.md is 513 lines, less than half that peak. The parent's own note said 486, so it has grown 27 lines since that note was written -- slow regrowth, which is evidence the gate still has a point, and nothing like the rate it was filed against.

docs/agents-md-charter.md already says outright that nothing stops the file growing back, rather than claiming a gate that does not exist. That disclosure is the current state of the art here and is honest; this bead replaces it with a check.

WHAT TO DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING: the budget is a number in a file, and a number nothing re-derives is the shape AGENTS.md's 'Before you quote a number' refuses. Either the budget is pinned with its own justification beside it, or the gate reports growth since a recorded baseline. Choose and say which.
acceptance_criteria: make pre-commit refuses an AGENTS.md over its declared budget; the budget carries its justification where it is declared, or the gate measures growth against a recorded baseline -- the choice made and stated rather than left to the reader; and the mutation is AGENTS.md padded past the budget going red, with the red message naming the budget and the overage.

title: Comment-block length becomes a gate: threshold 40, 60 for a package doc comment
description:
ARM A OF fisc-ak39, split out 2026-09-19 when arm B landed and the parent's single priority stopped fitting its four arms.

One arm of the doccheck binary, following tools/beadrefs/main.go's house pattern: hand-declared exemptions with staleness guards that fail when an exemption loses its subject.

Scope: cmd internal pkg site tools, over .go/.mjs/.js. Threshold 40, and 60 for a package doc comment.

MEASURED BEFORE THE TOOL WAS SPECIFIED, and the distribution is why 40: blocks at 20+=136, 25+=70, 30+=45, 35+=29, 40+=20, 50+=8, 60+=5. At 40 the finding set is 20, which is lane-sized rather than beadrefs' first-run 73. Re-measure before building -- this distribution is from 2026-09-05.

LENGTH IS A PROXY FOR KIND AND IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a 39-line essay passes, a 45-line transcribed column grid fails and needs an exemption. The package comment must say so rather than implying the threshold means anything on its own.

MAINTENANCE RULE: if the exemption list passes twelve, the threshold is wrong; raise it, do not grow the list.

This is a hygiene gate, not a fail-open one, which is why it is P3 where arm C is P2.
acceptance_criteria: make doccheck (or its own target) refuses a comment block over 40 lines, 60 for a package doc comment, over cmd internal pkg site tools; exemptions are hand-declared with a staleness guard that fails when an exemption's subject is gone; the package comment states that length is a proxy for kind and wrong in both directions; and the mutation is a block grown past the threshold going red.

title: mapping.Kinds's doc comment says internal/registry would re-spell the five values without it; registry re-spells them anyway, on purpose
description:
MEASURED at the prune lane. internal/mapping/rule.go:65-70 says Kinds is 'exported for readers OUTSIDE this package that must agree with this vocabulary -- data/taxonomy.yaml declares kinds per category, and internal/registry has to refuse a member that is not one of these. Without it that package would re-spell the five values, which is the second copy the taxonomy's own header argues against.'

BOTH HALVES OF THAT ARE WRONG ABOUT THE TREE. internal/registry does not call mapping.Kinds() at all -- the only three call sites are internal/registry/kinds_test.go:69,97,136. And registry DOES re-spell the five values, at internal/registry/registry.go:105-111 (factKinds), deliberately: registry.go:95-104 sets out the argument for duplicating rather than importing, cites fisc-iki's 2026-08-29 note for the measurement, and says the pin is behavioural via kinds_test.go because an unexported list is invisible from an external test package.

SO THE TWO COMMENTS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER and the wrong one is the one a reader of mapping/ meets first. This is the 'Where writing goes' second-source failure again: registry.go's comment is right and knows what it is doing; rule.go's is a claim about another package that nothing keeps in step.

THE FIX IS ONE COMMENT, not a code change. Kinds is genuinely exported-for-a-test and that is fine -- ContestedTotals and GroupExpenditure are exported for the same reason and say so honestly. Rewrite rule.go's paragraph to say what is true: the vocabulary is pinned from outside by a test that may import both packages, registry holds its own copy by decision, and the returned slice is a copy so a caller cannot move the vocabulary. Do not say where the pin lives beyond naming it; the file path is the second source.

WHY P3 AND NOT FIXED ON SIGHT: the prune lane that found it was not touching internal/mapping/rule.go, and AGENTS.md's review rule is to file rather than widen a pass. Found while deciding fisc-ko1v's do-not-delete list.

title: structure.Document.Slice has no production caller, and fisc-kbuo (a) means it will not get one
description:
MEASURED at d2a2136: internal/structure/document.go:172 (d Document) Slice(name string) is called from exactly two places, both tests -- pkg/cmd/export/structure_test.go:78 and internal/structure/document_test.go:119,122. No production caller. deadcode does not flag it because the tests reach it, which is the shape AGENTS.md's 'Ask what the fixture is hiding' names: a function kept alive only by the test written for it.

IT WAS BUILT FOR A DECISION THAT WENT THE OTHER WAY. fisc-02mf's first line reads 'structure.Document.Slice already narrows to one view', and fisc-02mf existed to ship the structure as an index plus per-view, per-column slices -- candidate (b) of fisc-kbuo. The owner decided (a) on 2026-09-18, one blob, no server-side slicing, and fisc-02mf is closed against that decision. So Slice has no caller and no prospect of one.

NOT SIMPLY DELETE-ON-SIGHT, which is why this is a bead and not a commit. Slice is also the only executable statement of what a named view NARROWS TO, and its test is the only place that claim is exercised. Three ways out, in preference order:
  1. Delete Slice and its tests. Smallest, and loses a claim nothing else makes.
  2. Keep it and give it a production caller -- if fisc-phtp's emitted blob turns out to want per-view narrowing on the Go side for any reason other than payload size, this is already the function.
  3. Keep it explicitly as a specification with a comment saying it has no caller and why, which is honest but adds a second source for what View.Admits already decides.

DECIDE UNDER fisc-phtp, not before it: that lane is what learns whether anything wants to narrow a view on the way out. Until then this bead exists so the function's status is recorded rather than rediscovered.

Found while auditing dead code under AGENTS.md's 'Go vets, JavaScript renders'.
close_reason:
DELETED, option 1 of the three this bead listed, on the owner's decision to prune aggressively before fisc-phtp rather than to decide under it. Slice, TestSliceReindexesOneViewAndRefusesAnUnknownOne, and the candidate-(b) slice rows of TestTheStructureShipsOnTheAssetChannelAndIsMeasured are gone; the whole-structure measurement and the 'today:' comparison stay, because those are what candidate (a) ships.

THIS BEAD'S OWN STATED MECHANISM WAS WRONG, and the correction matters beyond this bead. It said deadcode does not flag Slice 'because the tests reach it'. deadcode WITHOUT -test does not look at tests at all, so that cannot be it. The real cause is RTA method over-approximation: a method counts as reachable when its receiver is a runtime type and any interface dispatch in the program has a matching signature, and signatures like func() bool match spuriously. That is why the same audit (9f1df6d) also missed geom.(*Grid).Gutter and the three iostreams TTY accessors, all of which have zero references of any kind. A method-level SELECTOR grep is not redundant with deadcode; recorded as a memory.

NO MUTATION, because nothing here gained a guard: this is a deletion of code no caller reached. What stands in for one is that the measurement figures are unchanged after the trim -- whole structure 2048 facts, raw 868,612, gzip 68,658 (best 64,361), without provenance raw 645,408 gzip 30,937, against today's data/fund-flows.json raw 276,611 gzip 19,111 -- byte for byte the figures this bead's sibling fisc-kbuo recorded at L4.1.

ONE THING THE DELETION EXPOSED: govet's shadow arm went red at pkg/cmd/export/structure_test.go:35, where an 'if err := json.Unmarshal' had shadowed the function's err harmlessly only because nothing used the outer one afterwards. Fixed in the same commit by assigning rather than redeclaring.

facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, 0 errored; make pre-commit exit 0; deadcode -test ./... reports no findings; golangci-lint 0 issues; all ten testdata/*.golden.json byte-identical.

title: The kept flank column is answered by nobody: Go declines it and the arm accepts the decline
description:
testdata/rungs.json at schema_version 2 answers every drawn column of every rung EXCEPT the kept flank, which carries the reason code kept-flank instead of an answer, and tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs accepts that decline. Measured at c70abaf: 296 flank columns declined across the two published columns and both budgets, against 298 outward columns and 296 centres answered by id.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR L4.3. The flank is the half of the chart windowFor CARRIES OVER from the rung above -- kept = sideOf(onScreen, ...) -- and windowFor is one of the four functions L4.3 rewrites. So the splice, the id dedupe that lets the flank's record win, and the carried endpoints that land on it are outside the cross-language comparison entirely, even now that every other column is inside it.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE, measured while planning the schema-2 change: rungsOf walks one document per rung and hands walk() only the node ids, tiers and roles of the chart it leaves on screen. Answering the flank needs the PARENT chart's links as well, filtered to the opened node the way filterToNode does, which is the one part of the client's window the Go side does not model. internal/export/reach.go's ReachOf is now the client's filter/fold/prune in Go and is most of what such an answer would be built from.

Relates to fisc-btb1 (items 1 and 3 landed; item 2, the derived marks, is still open) and to fisc-rx1d, which carries the audit of which of app.js's paths no jscheck module drives.
close_reason: Answered on e13-sankey-merge, schema_version 3 of testdata/rungs.json. The walk carries the whole window as an export.Graph (kept half spliced ahead of fresh half, cap's fold applied) and the flank is export.ReachOf over it on the mirror side; what the client draws but does not count (derived nodes, residual endpoints) is a compared field, carried, not a subtraction. Measured at the regenerated artifact: 296 flank columns answered, 492 ids, 17 distinct, 64 columns of more than one id, 24 carrying a declared endpoint (fund-balance/draw 10, transfers/in 16), 4 answering with nothing of their own; 602 centre and outward columns byte-identical. make js compares 898 columns where it compared 602. Mutations: an id dropped from fund-group/general's tier-0 flank at width 3 is red in the Go test and in the arm by name; transfers/in deleted from that flank's carried is red in both.

title: openableNodes' window arm reads ribbons directly while its Keep-less arm and rungsOf read the hierarchy through export.ReachOf
description: internal/export/reach.go's ReachOf is the client's filter/fold/prune as one rule and is what pkg/cmd/export/rungs.go answers every rung with and what openableNodes' Keep-less arm enumerates stepView.Opens with. The window arm of openableNodes (internal/export/page.go) still answers Opens by reading ribbons out of a node at tier From into the outward tiers, which is a second spelling of the reach. Measured when ReachOf landed: on the committed corpus the two readings agree on every rung (296 rungs unmoved in testdata/rungs.json under the port, and tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's openedViews pins of 76 and 74 held), so this is DESIGN, not WRONG-OUTPUT. The shape that could separate them is a node at From whose only outward ribbon leaves a DESCENDANT rather than the node itself, which the hierarchy reads as openable and the ribbon reading does not; no shipped window document has one. Port the window arm to ReachOf under [From]+outward on the flank's side, with the opened node required to be the only tier-From node the reach touches (the guard rungsOf's answer already makes), and show the existing openable_test.go fixtures still answer the same. The mutation: a fixture where the ribbon leaves a child of the opened node.

title: revenue-lines-tie-to-their-categories arm 1 still sums on detailtie.go's key; re-point it at structure.KeyOf and delete the last of the flat machinery
description:
Filed from L3.4. fisc-c4ip listed revenue-lines-tie-to-their-categories among the twelve; re-derived against the tree, its arm 2 (every revenue-line node is parented to revenue/ plus the category data/taxonomy.yaml declares it under) is a hierarchy claim nothing in internal/structure makes -- the check's own doc measures that re-pointing a line onto a sibling category leaves every other check green -- so the check stays.

WHAT THAT KEPT ALIVE. Arm 1 (the drill-down's flows into funds sum, per (fund group, category), to the spine's cell) is built on internal/check/detailtie.go: detailKey, cellSum, detailSums, reconciledPairs, compareDetail, unionKeys, describePairs. Those were the shared machinery of the five deleted detail-ties-to-spine checks and now have one consumer.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS. Sum the spine side with structure.KeyOf(f, LevelFundGroupByCategory) and key the drill-down's links as structure.Key{Year, Basis, Level, Coords}, reconcile through the same exceptions lineExceptions already reads off structure.BudgetBookExceptions, and delete detailtie.go. Arm 1 is then stated in the cut vocabulary, which is what fisc-c4ip means by 're-pointed at a cut'. Keep the check's existing failability table (revenuelinestie_test.go) green across the rewrite; its summary strings are pinned by TestRevenueLinesTieOverTheFixture.

title: residualNodes is declared beside the structure that determines it, and the whole-or-nothing rule is spelled once in Go's comment and once in site/app.js
description:
WHAT IS TRUE NOW (re-measured at 939273e). internal/check/residual.go declares the five spine endpoints a fund-level schedule cannot decompose, with a reason each, and pkg/cmd/export ships check.ResidualNodes() as the fund-group step's residual map. The whole-or-nothing RULE (an endpoint's inflow is carried where the drawn document carries nothing from it into the opened node, its outflow where the chart decomposes the node and the document carries nothing from inside to it) is now implemented in Go, in internal/export/marks.go ResidualOf, and the rung answer (testdata/rungs.json, served at export.RungsPath) carries each residual's Ends, in_cents and out_cents. site/app.js carryResidual no longer applies the rule: it reads mark.ends off the answer, takes both directions of every listed endpoint off the window (else off the document one depth up), sums what it carried and throws unless the sums equal the answer's cents. So the second spelling this bead was filed against is gone; what remains is that the SET is still restated in prose in residualNodes rather than derived from structure.BudgetBookCuts' kinds and BudgetBookExceptions (revenue-detail {revenue, transfer_in}, general-fund-departments {expenditure}, spine everyKind, plus the general transfer-in exception), and TestTheResidualSetIsTheEndpointSet holds only its KEYS to endpointTiers.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS. Derive the residual set from the cuts and exceptions so the client reads one declaration and residual.go's prose becomes the reason column of a derived table; or record that the map is the declaration and delete the sentence in its doc comment that says the rule lives in app.js alone.

title: Collapse project.PublishedDocuments and internal/check's six builder interfaces into one declaration per document shape
description:
Filed from Lane 3 L3.3, which answered fisc-w11l's (d) narrowly: every document that sums is now constructed as a structure.View (in sankey.Graph, and by the peer check's arm over s.Projections), but project.PublishedDocuments (internal/project/project.go) still enumerates 19 documents by hand and internal/check/subject.go still switches over six builder interfaces (graphBuilder, trendsBuilder, fundFlowsBuilder, departmentSpendingBuilder, departmentFundingBuilder, transfersByFundBuilder) to build them.

fisc-w11l's proposal was that all three collapse into one declaration. L3.3 did not do it because the six interfaces are document SHAPES -- a graph, a set of series, a drill, a cross-tab -- and not grains; what the view discipline replaced was the scope-set-as-arithmetic-claim, not the shape. Whether a shape can be declared beside the view (so that PublishedDocuments becomes 'this view, drawn as this shape, over these columns') is this bead's question. Acceptance: one declaration lists every published document with its view and its shape; buildProjections builds from it with no type switch; the series documents (trends, changes, fund-balances), which are NOT views, are declared as what they are rather than shoehorned.

title: validateLattice's axis-subset arm cannot see a typo'd edge between two levels that share an axis set
description:
FAIL-OPEN, found 2026-09-17 while sizing Lane 3 against internal/structure as
shipped at 513ed04. Reddens nothing today and is filed because the shape it
cannot see is one the package's own doc comment says is expected.

validateLattice (internal/structure/lattice.go:183) refuses an edge whose parent
carries an axis the child lacks, and its comment gives the reason: "an edge whose
direction contradicts the axes is a typo rather than a judgement, and summing
along it would total a coordinate the coarse level does not carry" (:194-196).

The test is notSubset (:211), which returns "" when sub is a subset -- INCLUDING
when the two axis sets are EQUAL. So for two levels with identical axes, BOTH
directions validate, and the guard that exists to catch a reversed edge cannot
catch one. Only declaring both directions trips the cycle check at :203-206.

WHY THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The package doc comment argues exactly this case as
the reason levels are named rather than inferred: "Two levels can share an axis
set and mean different things, and a refinement that holds arithmetically need
not hold in the documents -- pp.167-170 decompose General Fund expenditure by
department, which is a refinement, and the ACFR's fund-balance roll-forward shares
axes with it and is not" (lattice.go:11-16). The lattice is built to admit
equal-axes levels and its validator is blind on them.

MEASURED: the seven levels declared today all have distinct axis sets
(levelAxes, :70-78), so nothing is currently unguarded. The exposure arrives with
the first equal-axes level pair -- and the ACFR cuts Lane 3 may add are the
nearest candidate, since acfr-general-fund-summary sits at the spine's own
fund-group-by-category.

ACCEPTANCE: notSubset's caller distinguishes "strict subset" from "equal", and an
edge between two levels with equal axis sets is either refused by name or
declared to be legitimate with the reason stated. The mutation is a reversed edge
between two equal-axes levels: today it validates, and it must go red.

title: mapping.Column.Fund keeps the fund==0 sentinel after the fact retires it, and ColumnPath makes changing it move fact ids silently
description:
Lane 2 retires the fund==0 sentinel on fact.Fact.Fund and project.Series.Fund
and DELIBERATELY LEAVES IT on the mapping side. This bead is that decision,
filed so the survival is visible rather than looking like an oversight.

WHAT STILL CARRIES IT: mapping.Column.Fund (internal/mapping/rule.go:832),
Counterpart.Fund (:865), Row.Fund (:920), and the zero-checks that read them
at internal/mapping/parse.go:1151, :1558, :1625, rule.go:1034-1035 and
resolve.go:1916-1917.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN THE SAME LANE, and this is the whole of the bead.
fact.ColumnPath (internal/fact/fact.go:238) builds a path segment from
`if c.Fund != 0`, and ColumnPath's output is component 5 of MakeID's hashed
tuple (fact.go:169-180). So a change to mapping.Column.Fund's zero-handling
changes ColumnPath, which changes the id of every fact whose column names a
fund -- AND fact-ids-recompute (internal/check/facts.go:123-127) STAYS GREEN
THROUGH IT, because it re-derives each id from the published fields and finds
the new tuple self-consistent. The check cannot witness this; only a sorted
id-set diff between two revisions of facts/facts.jsonl can.

That is a different and larger change from the one Lane 2 makes, it moves the
audit trail's identities rather than its values, and it needs its own reviewed
commit with the id-set diff as the gate.

SO THE TREE ENDS LANE 2 WITH TWO SPELLINGS OF ABSENCE on two types, which is
the cost being accepted: fact.Fact.Fund is *int and says absent, while
mapping.Column.Fund is int and says it with 0. They do not collide -- the fact
side is what every check and projection reads -- but a reader moving between the
two packages will meet both.

ACCEPTANCE IF IT IS EVER TAKEN UP: mapping.Column.Fund, Counterpart.Fund and
Row.Fund become *int; ColumnPath's behaviour is held FIXED by a test that pins
its output for a fund-bearing and a fundless column BEFORE the type moves; and
the commit's gate is `git show <prev>:facts/facts.jsonl | jq -r .id | sort`
against the same over the new file, diffing empty.

title: Grain is declared on the rule and carried on no fact: what breaks when a consumer needs a fact that describes itself
description:
Owner decided 2026-09-16 that grain lives on the RULE (mappings/*.yaml, beside
`scope:`) and NOT on fact.Fact. This bead is the other horn, filed so the
decision has somewhere to be revisited rather than being re-argued from scratch.

WHY RULE-SIDE WAS CHOSEN. internal/check already holds []*mapping.File
(internal/check/subject.go:340), so a grain declared on the rule is reachable
from every check without touching a fact. Measured: rule-side moves 0 lines of
facts/facts.jsonl for grain; fact-side moves all 2382. And internal/structure
already DERIVES grain correctly and tests the derivation (ruleAxes,
internal/structure/cut.go:25; LevelOfRule :56), at 161 of 161 fact-emitting
rules -- so a fact-side copy would be a second spelling of something already
checked. Keeping the derivation as the comparison is what makes the declaration
worth having: declared-versus-derived disagreement is red.

WHAT RULE-SIDE GIVES UP, and this is the thing to re-measure before reopening:

(1) facts.jsonl STOPS BEING SELF-DESCRIBING, against the grain of
    docs/fact-store-contract.md and internal/fact/fact.go's package doc, which
    argues the record is "deliberately wide and deliberately repetitive --
    every field appears on every line, nothing is omitted when empty".
(2) THE CSV EXPORT CANNOT CARRY IT. pkg/cmd/export/facts.go derives its header
    reflectively from fact.Fact (:320-331), so a reader of the exported CSV has
    no way to see grain at all without also having the mapping.
(3) cellKey CANNOT KEY ON (grain, coordinates) FROM A FACT ALONE. fisc-w11l's
    proposal is that a total is a sum over one antichain; if that ends up
    needing a fact that states its own grain, this bead is the blocker.

REOPEN IT WHEN, and not before: Lane 3's cellKey (internal/project/sankey.go:
585-599) or Lane 4's wire format needs a fact that describes itself, or a
consumer outside the Go tree needs grain. A format migration is cheapest at a
planned lane boundary and worst discovered mid-branch, which is the reason this
is filed rather than left implicit.

NOT A REASON TO REOPEN: tidiness, or symmetry with `scope:` being on both. The
fact carries `scope` because it was doing double duty as grain; that is the
defect fisc-0qyo names, not a precedent to copy.
notes:
2026-09-17 THE THIRD REOPEN CONDITION WAS REACHED AND DOES NOT REOPEN THIS BEAD.
Recorded so the condition is not re-argued when it is met again.

The condition reads: "Lane 3's cellKey (internal/project/sankey.go:585-599) or
Lane 4's wire format needs a fact that describes itself". Measured at 1f3880b, a
key built from facts ALONE still collides: all-funds-gross and transfers-by-fund
share 2 keys on
(fiscal_year, basis, kind, category, fund_group, fund, department), both sides
spelling absence as null for different reasons (13,247,000.00 and 13,330,000.00
against a printed dash). Retiring the sentinel in c549eeb did not separate them;
it made them agree on the same spelling. Only the rule's grain separates them --
fund-group-by-category against fund-by-category.

WHY THAT IS NOT A REASON TO MOVE GRAIN ONTO THE FACT. Every consumer that needs
the separation is in the Go tree, where the mapping files are already held:
internal/check has []*mapping.File at subject.go:340, and internal/structure
already resolves it per rule via LevelOfRule (cut.go:68). structure.Key carries
Level (containment.go:18-24) and so never collides. The join is one map lookup at
the point the key is built.

WHAT WOULD STILL REOPEN IT is unchanged and is the second condition, not the
third: a consumer OUTSIDE the Go tree. The CSV export derives its header
reflectively from fact.Fact (pkg/cmd/export/facts.go:320-331), so a reader of
facts.csv still cannot see grain at all. If Lane 4's wire format ships cells a
client must key without a companion lattice, that is the moment.

title: There is no way to maximize the chart
description:
Found by clicking the shipped site: the reader expects a maximize/fullscreen
affordance and there is none. Measured at 8aa9116: zero hits for fullscreen,
requestFullscreen, fullscreenchange or maximize across site/app.js,
site/style.css and site/*.tmpl.

THE CHART IS ALREADY SCALE-READY. render() (app.js:4163-4165) sets a viewBox and
NO width/height attributes; style.css:641-646 gives svg.sankey width:100% and
height:auto. So a larger box draws a larger chart with no layout work at all.
What caps it is .chart-wrap (style.css:634-639): --chart-room is
min(1513px, calc(100vw - 56px)), and 1513 is chartWidth(4).

FULLSCREEN THE .card, NOT .chart-wrap. site/index.html.tmpl:128-147 nests
legend, then nav.breadcrumb#breadcrumb, then .chart-wrap inside .card. The
breadcrumb is the only way back out of a drill, so fullscreening .chart-wrap
alone strands a drilled reader.

SHAPE IT LIKE THE CONTROLS BESIDE IT: ship the button `disabled` in both
index.html.tmpl and chart.html.tmpl and let app.js enable it only where
requestFullscreen exists -- the progressive enhancement wireColumns
(app.js:5143-5152) and wireYears already use, and for the same stated reason
(a control that lies is worse than one that is absent). A fullscreenchange
listener re-asks the budget and redraws.

SEAMS IT TOUCHES: the new element id must be added to TEMPLATE_IDS
(tools/jscheck/harness.mjs:48-56) or the stub cannot model it; and the change
ships its jscheck arm in the same commit (AGENTS.md, "The node boundary").

HAZARD, and it is fisc-<layout.mjs bead>'s: any :fullscreen rule that re-declares
--chart-room must sit AFTER the base .chart-wrap rule in style.css, or
chartAllowance's regex reads the wrong block.
notes: 2026-09-22: the room half of this is done at 96c1035 -- app.js derives its column ceiling from the declared steps and hands style.css the width, so a wider chart needs no stylesheet edit. What this bead asked for beyond that is the same feature fisc-umuw asks for, and the design question both raise is answered in fisc-ipif. This bead also names site/chart.html.tmpl, deleted at 4e7421f.

title: The General Fund's group rung and fund rung are the same money drawn twice
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-14: data/funds.yaml declares exactly one fund of type general,
fund 100, so fund-group/general and fund/100 are the same money. That is why the
two rungs printed one phrase (fisc-ko1j.25, closed against 8f6087b by qualifying
the trail rather than either label).

THE LABEL IS READABLE NOW AND THE QUESTION UNDERNEATH IT IS NOT ANSWERED. The
two rungs do draw different charts -- the group window {0,2,3} shows what pays
into the group beside its funds, and the fund window {2,3,4,5} shows its
divisions and their object categories -- so this is a re-framing rather than a
partition, and the other five groups do not have it. Whether a reader is served
by a rung that decomposes nothing, or whether the general group should open
straight into fund/100's divisions, is a decision to take with the chart in
front of you.

Belongs beside fisc-ko1j.28, which is the other thing the fund rung leaves a
reader to work out.

title: layout.mjs's expanded arm is named 'five of them past the gutter' and asserts twelve
description:
FALSE-CLAIM in a check's own name, which is the string make js prints. Found
2026-09-14 while preparing the browser walk.

  tools/jscheck/layout.mjs:915  name: "a column drawn out to every mark it holds
                                draws no two labels over each other, and five of
                                them past the gutter"
  tools/jscheck/layout.mjs:886  EXPANDED = { ..., over: 12, ... }

The same paragraph contradicts itself: the doc comment above expandedChecks says
"twelve run past the gutter, the worst by 56px of a 306px estimate" and then
"WHICH OF THOSE FIVE ACTUALLY OVERFLOWS IS A BROWSER QUESTION", two sentences
apart.

W8 (fisc-ko1j.12.9) re-pinned EXPANDED and the paragraph above it when the open
marker landed on 32 newly-openable labels, and left the arm's name and that one
sentence at the old number. fisc-2gyh records the re-pin and does not mention
the name.

THE CORRECTION IS NOT THE FIX. A hand-picked window with a literal count beside
it is why one of the three could move without the others; fisc-8cx0's remedy --
the label arms walking every view the drill opens rather than three windows
somebody chose -- removes the numeral rather than restating it.
close_reason: Closed against de45bb2, by removing the count from the arm's name rather than correcting it: the expanded arm now reads 'and states what the gesture costs the gutter', EXPANDED keeps the pin, and the paragraph's 'those FIVE' sentence reads twelve. The root cause is addressed beside it -- layout.mjs's label arms now walk drill.mjs's everyOpenedView over both columns and pin the SET of over-gutter marks by id, so a lane that widens a label names it in the diff instead of moving a literal.

title: site/app.js's three view counts say 44 where the tree opens 76 and 74
description:
FALSE-CLAIM, found 2026-09-14 while preparing the browser walk. Pinned by
nothing, so make js is green through it.

  site/app.js:2933  "9 of the 44 views it opens draw one" (a folded tail)
  site/app.js:2969  "on 9 of the 44 views the chain opens"
  site/app.js:4214  "all 44 views it opens draw three at the page's own budget"

MEASURED against the pins that do re-derive it: tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's
COLUMNS carry openedViews 76 for FY2025-26 and 74 for FY2026-27, and drill.mjs's
own prose at :154-163 records that the number used to be 45 for both columns
before the fund-departments step opened the other sixty funds.

NOT A NUMERAL TO CORRECT. 44 was one number for both columns and the tree no
longer has one; and the "9 of 44" claims are about how many views draw a folded
tail, which needs its own re-measurement per column rather than a new
denominator. AGENTS.md, "The node boundary": pin the figure to something that
re-measures it, or drop the count and keep the claim.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED in the session that found it: site/app.js was the subject
of that afternoon's browser walk and freezing it was worth more than the
comment. Related: fisc-8cx0, whose own 17-of-368 was taken over 45 views.
close_reason: Re-measured against the drill tree and corrected in site/app.js, with tools/jscheck/appclaims.test.mjs re-deriving every figure and grepping app.js's own sentences for it. The bead named the view count and had the replacement wrong: 76/74 is everyOpenedView's walk, not the 44 the comments said, and the bead's own figures came from comparing against a different walk. Three further figures were also false -- 343 marks where the tree draws 453/446, 24 openable where it is 55/53, and a 7%/93% share that is 12%/88% -- and one CLAIM was never true: 'None draws two' is false of transfers/in in both budgets, a step that keeps no flank and so draws a filter's two columns rather than a window's three. Mutations: the old figure restored, a count off by one, and a tree-side change to expandable, each red.

title: department-funding publishes two historical columns no reader can reach
description:
FILED BY W8 (fisc-ko1j.12.9), AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS SHAPE HAS BEEN DECLARED. department-funding-2024-actual and department-funding-2025-revised are built, published and declared in `fisc export`'s unviewedDocuments, because the fund-departments step joins on Column and pp.66-67 print no actual and no revised column for a spine year to open them from. fund-flows and department-spending each carry the same pair for the same reason.

THAT IS SIX PUBLISHED DOCUMENTS NO CHART REACHES, all for one cause, and the entries say so one file at a time. Reaching them means a spine-less way into a detail document -- the same thing fisc-zojk names for fund-flows, where FY2023-24 also carries a seventh fund group (permanent) that FUND_ORDER has no hue for and buildLegend no entry for.

WORTH NOTING FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: department-funding's historical columns are the ones with the most to say. Its FY2023-24 actual column is the only one where the permanent fund group is non-zero (620,581), and the widest fund window in the whole schedule is fund/240's five departments in that column against three in both adopted years.

title: The expanded fund column now runs 12 labels past the gutter where it ran 5
description:
FOUND BY W8 (fisc-ko1j.12.9) AND RE-PINNED RATHER THAN FIXED. tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's EXPANDED block measured 5 of the expanded column's 41 labels wider than the 250px gutter, worst fund/221 at 36.0px over. With the fund-departments step landed it is 12, worst fund/221 at 55.8px over.

THE CAUSE IS NOT THE LAYOUT AND IS MEASURED. labelWidth measures the words a reader sees, nodeFlags included, and every fund pp.85-125 print a funding row for now draws the open marker beside its figure -- three value-width characters, which is exactly the 19.8px fund/221 moved. The VERTICAL answer did not move at all: the tightest stack is still 2.1px over 32 marks, because a marker widens a label and does not add a line.

WHY IT WAS RE-PINNED AND NOT FIXED. The file's own comment already calls this 'the cost of the gesture stated as a number rather than asserted away', and which of the twelve actually overflows is a BROWSER question -- ADVANCE_EM is deliberately wider than any system face sets, so the direction this can be wrong in is calling a label too wide that fits. fisc-rl4j is where that is settled.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Whether an expanded column should draw the open marker at all, or draw it only on hover/focus, or whether the gutter should widen when a column is expanded. All three are client changes with a jscheck arm each; none is a data question.
notes: MEASURED AS A MUTATION 2026-09-14, at de45bb2. With the open marker removed from nodeFlags -- this bead's first option -- the marks that stop running past the gutter are named rather than counted: FY2025-26 dept/administrative-services, fund/202, fund/282, fund/283, fund/623, fund/730; FY2026-27 the same less fund/202. Six marks and five. That is what option one buys, and it is now re-derived on every make js run by layout.mjs's per-column over-gutter set, so whichever of the three options is taken the diff names which marks moved.

title: drill.mjs reaches fifteen declared steps by position, and a position is not an identity
description:
FOUND BY THE TRANSFERS STEP LANDING, and it had already fired. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs reached the object-category step as PAGE.steps[PAGE.steps.length - 1]. W6 appended the transfers step after it, so that line silently began shaping its chart under a step of a DIFFERENT document that keeps no flank -- and the arm went on passing, because a step is a plain object and any of them has the fields the arm reads.

Fixed in that commit at the one site that broke, by adding stepByKey(key) and using it there. The rest were left because they are stable under an APPEND and the sweep would have been unreviewed churn in an already large commit:

  1085  FUND_TIER = PAGE.steps[0].caps[0].tier
  1086  CATEGORY_TIER = PAGE.steps[1].caps.find(...).tier
  1199  PAGE.steps[0].tail
  1517-1518, 1535, 1538  PAGE.steps[0], [PAGE.steps[0], PAGE.steps[1]]
  2099, 2104, 2146, 2193, 2220  PAGE.steps[0].residual / .from / .tiers
  2625  PAGE.steps[3]  (walkCategory)
  3188  PAGE.steps[0]  (windowChecks)
  3920  PAGE.steps[0]
  3998  const [groupStep, fundStep, divisionStep] = PAGE.steps

Line numbers are as of the W6 commit and will drift; grep for /PAGE\.steps\[/ instead.

THE HAZARD IS AN INSERT RATHER THAN AN APPEND. pkg/cmd/export/data.go declares its steps in three guarded blocks, and a step added to the FIRST block -- the fund-flows one -- shifts every index from 1 up. Every one of the sites above would then measure a different step with no gate saying so, which is exactly how the [length - 1] case behaved.

WHAT TO DO: convert each to stepByKey("<key>"), which already exists in the file, and delete the destructure at 3998 in favour of three keyed lookups. No behaviour changes, so the proof is that make js stays at its current arm count with none failing; the mutation is to insert a no-op step at the head of the first literal in data.go and confirm the suite reddens rather than re-aiming.
notes:
RE-DERIVED AT W8 (fisc-ko1j.12.9), WHICH ADDED A SEVENTH STEP AND DID NOT DO THE SWEEP. The count is unchanged: grep -n 'PAGE\.steps\[[0-9]' tools/jscheck/drill.mjs gives 14 literal-index reads in code plus the destructure 'const [groupStep, fundStep, divisionStep] = PAGE.steps', fifteen positional reaches in all. Every one of them is at index 0, 1 or 3, or is the leading three-element destructure.

WHAT W8 DID INSTEAD, and why it is not the fix. The fund-departments step was APPENDED at index 6 rather than declared beside the fund step it mirrors, so no existing index moved and all fifteen reads still name the step they meant. The commit says so in pkg/cmd/export/data.go beside the declaration, so the next reader knows the ordering is load-bearing until this bead is worked.

AND THE PRODUCING SIDE GREW A KEYED LOOKUP OF ITS OWN. views() now needs to ask whether the fund-group chart exists before it can hang a step off it, and it does that with a new stepByKey(steps, key) helper in data.go rather than by counting how many guarded blocks have run. So the Go half of the rule is in place; this bead is now only about the fifteen reads in drill.mjs.

THE HAZARD IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW LARGER. data.go declares its steps in four guarded blocks; a step added to the FIRST one shifts every index from 1 up, and there are seven steps to shift rather than five.

title: The paying half of p76 is published and no view draws it
description:
transfers-by-fund publishes BOTH ends of every figure p76 prints: a receiving leg (transfer-from/<fund> -> fund/<fund>, tier 2 -> 3) and a paying leg (fund/<fund> -> transfer-to/<fund>, tier 3 -> 5). The transfers step draws the receiving half only, at Tiers {2,3}.

WHY THE OTHER HALF IS NOT DRAWN, and it is the spine's shape rather than an omission. The natural place to open the paying legs from is the spine's transfers/out, which the spine pins at TIER 5. A node decomposing it would have to be FINER than tier 5, and transfer-to/<fund> is AT tier 5 -- so the link would not run coarse to fine and node-tiers-are-declared refuses it. The same asymmetry is already recorded one document over, in internal/project/sankey.go's nodeTransfersOut.

MEASURED, both budget columns: the paying legs sum to the same figure as the receiving ones -- 21,525,997 in FY2025-26 and 21,624,633 in FY2026-27 -- because p76's grand total IS the transfers-in side. So drawing them adds no money the site does not already show; what it would add is WHICH FUND PAYS, from the payer's end.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE, none of it decided: either a tier below 5 for the receiving end (which renumbers a published field), or a second view rooted on the document rather than a step off the spine, or transfers/out gaining a decomposition tier of its own. Note also that p76's grand total is NOT the city's transfers out -- pp.72-75 print the to-CIP transfers p76 does not list, 38,086,737 and 50,762,251 -- so a paying-side chart must carry that caveat or it will read as the whole of what each fund transfers out.

Cited from internal/project/transfersbyfund.go and pkg/cmd/export/data.go as the home of this asymmetry.

title: Expanding a column draws five labels past the chart's gutter
description:
MEASURED, in tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's arm 'a column drawn out to every mark it holds': with fund-group/special-revenue's tier-3 tail expanded, 5 of the window's 41 labels are wider than the 250px LABEL_GUTTER. The worst is fund/221 'Asset Seizure - Dept of Justice' at 276px against 240px of room -- 36px past the chart's right edge. The other four are fund/300, fund/280, fund/289 and fund/320, by 21.6, 13.8, 13.8 and 6.6px.

WHY IT IS NOT A FAILING ARM. layout.mjs measures at ADVANCE_EM = 0.6, chosen to be wider than mixed-case English sets in any system face, so the direction it can be wrong in is calling a label too wide that fits. At a realistic 0.5em the worst comes to 230px and every one of the five fits. Which is true is a question about a rendered face, and nothing in this tree renders one (fisc-6at).

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE. No two labels in that column touch -- the tightest vertical gap is 2.1px against the 12px one line claims -- and no two draw the same words. It is the horizontal gutter alone.

WHY IT ARRIVED NOW. These five funds have always been in the document; the cap is what kept them off the screen, and fisc-ko1j.12.6 is what lets a reader ask for them. The cap's own evidence says the expanded chart is a bad chart (42 ribbons, 9 of them under a pixel) and the reader has asked for it anyway, which is the feature. Whether the WORDS survive it is the part that was never measured.

SETTLE IT IN THE BROWSER WALK (fisc-rl4j), at 1440 and 1920 CSS px, and only then decide between: leave it, widen LABEL_GUTTER for an expanded tier alone, or let the expanded column's labels wrap.
notes: PREMISE SUPERSEDED, NOT CLOSED (2026-09-14). This bead's five labels were measured before the fund-departments step made 32 of that column's funds openable; the open marker widens each of their labels by three value-width characters, and layout.mjs's EXPANDED now pins over: 12 with fund/221 at 55.8px rather than 36.0px. fisc-2gyh carries that re-measurement. THE QUESTION IS UNCHANGED and still belongs to the browser walk: ADVANCE_EM = 0.6 is wider than any system face sets, so the direction this can be wrong in is calling a label too wide that fits, and whether ANY of them overflows a rendered face is unanswered here. Read twelve at 1440 and 1920, not five. The arm's own name still says five -- fisc-ieei.

title: labelLineShift's interior branch is drawn by nothing on the committed corpus
description:
site/app.js's labelLineShift returns a different pair of dy values for an interior label than for an outward one, because an interior label already sits in the NODE_PADDING gap above its rect and has nowhere below to go. The branch is reasoned; it is not measured, and nothing draws it.

Measured over all six committed goldens while fixing fisc-og1n: the only duplicate labels within a tier anywhere are fund-flows' tier 5 -- 23 'Services & Supplies' and 21 'Wages & Benefits', both years -- and tier 5 is the last column of every window that reaches it. department-spending (33 nodes) and the spine (25) have no duplicate label at any tier. So labelQualifiers never qualifies an interior mark and the 'middle' branch never runs.

What would retire this: a synthetic document with two same-labelled marks in an interior column, driven through labelQualifiers with app.projection set, asserting the qualifier lands in the NODE_PADDING gap rather than on the rect above. drill.mjs's crossTabProbe (drill.mjs:3107) is the shape to copy. The vertical arm in tools/jscheck/layout.mjs ('a qualifier''s second line still clears the label stacked below it') would name an interior pair if one ever appeared in a real document, but it measures no synthetic one today.

title: main's 1180px max-width scales a four-column chart down rather than giving it room
description:
site/style.css sets main and .page-head to max-width: 1180px, and the chart is an <svg> with a viewBox and width:100%. chartWidth(4) is 1513px (site/app.js, measured by tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's four-column geometry arm), so a four-column chart in a 1180px container is the same picture drawn at 78% -- every label 22% smaller, on the wide viewport that was the reason to draw a fourth column at all.

Nothing is clipped and no label collides: the four-column window's tightest label still has 16.2px of clearance IN CHART UNITS (layout.mjs, 'every label in the four-column window has room where it was anchored'). What shrinks is the type.

The control that asks for a fourth column (fisc-ko1j.12.4) is the thing that should decide whether main widens with it, which is why this is filed against that rather than fixed at fisc-ko1j.12.3: internal/export/export_test.go pins the 1180px rule by name, with an anti-vacuity arm, so a change there is a change to a pinned contract and not a stylesheet tweak.
close_reason:
Fixed at 39666c3. .chart-wrap now sets --chart-room: min(1513px, calc(100vw - 56px)), takes its width from it, and centres a box wider than its container with margin-inline: calc(50% - var(--chart-room) / 2). main and .page-head keep 1180px, so the prose, the tiles, the cards and the tables are where they were; only the figure breaks out, and it collapses back to the container's width where the viewport is too narrow to want more.

The 1180px rule this bead names as pinned by internal/export/export_test.go is still pinned and still passes -- its anti-vacuity arm is about not clamping the PAGE to the reading measure, which this does not do. Its comment was corrected in the same commit: it claimed nothing in the tree could say the chart stayed at the container width, and now one arm reads that declaration as text.

Check: tools/jscheck/layout.mjs, 'the stylesheet lets a four-column chart draw at the width app.js lays it out at', comparing .chart-wrap's declared allowance with app.js's own chartWidth(4). Mutations, both run: dropping the rule for max-width: 1180px goes RED with '.chart-wrap declares no --chart-room cap'; keeping the shape and setting the cap to 1180px goes RED with 'style.css allows the chart 1180px and app.js lays four columns out at 1513px, so it draws at 78% of that' -- which is this bead's own figure, re-measured.

What the check cannot say, because nothing here renders CSS (fisc-6at): that the breakout actually centres, does not overflow, and still collapses under the 720px block. Browser-only, and not yet walked: fisc-rl4j.

title: The drilldown contract doc says every rung is three columns, which W2 makes false
description:
docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md:381 reads 'Every rung of that chain is a WINDOW: three columns with the node the reader clicked in the middle, one flank kept off the chart they clicked it on and the other its own decomposition.' True of the tree at W1 (fisc-ko1j.12.2), and false the moment fisc-ko1j.12.3 lands Widen on the fund step: that rung then draws four columns at a budget of four and three at a budget of three.

The sentence needs the budget in it, not deletion: three columns is still what a narrow reader sees, and the contract's own table (depth 1/2/3 rows) states each rung's tier set as a fixed list. Say which of those lists are the narrow ones.

Found while landing W1; not fixed there because no rung widens yet and a contract doc that describes a shape nothing ships is the same defect the other way round.
close_reason: Both contract docs now say three columns is the NARROWEST window and which budget draws it, landed with W2 at c8f88c6. general-fund-drilldown-contract.md gains the widen rule (columns of the step's own tiers, dropped from the end of the widen order, at the end away from the kept flank) and the empty-column drop; its depth-2 row states {2,3,4} widening to {2,3,4,5} with both caps. sankey-contract.md's 'every rung is a WINDOW -- three columns' now points at that doc for what each rung draws at what width.

title: A gutter label wider than the gutter runs off the chart, on 17 of the 368 the tree draws
description:
MEASURED WHILE WRITING fisc-ko1j.12.1's LABEL ARM, and deliberately not fixed there: the fix is a design decision about the chart's width, not about the anchoring rule that wave changed.

site/app.js reserves LABEL_GUTTER = 250px outside the first and last columns and anchors those columns' labels 10px clear of the rect, so a label has 240px. A label wider than that runs past the edge of the viewBox; svg.sankey sets overflow: visible, so it paints into the page margin rather than being clipped, but nothing places it and two of them can meet.

MEASURED over all 45 views the drill tree opens (the spine plus 44 opened views), 368 label placements, each label boxed at 0.6em per character -- 12px for the label tspan, 11px for the value tspan, which is the over-estimate tools/jscheck/layout.mjs declares and uses:

  17 of 368 are wider than the 240px they have
  worst -35px: revenue-line/intergovernmental/state-motor-veh-in-lieu-mvil in the Intergovernmental window, and fund/551 in the Capital fund-group window
  1 of the 17 is on the SPINE itself: fund-balance/contribution, -13px

CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT, which is why this is P3 and not P2. 0.6em is an upper bound chosen so that a label the harness says fits, fits on any platform -- the stylesheet asks for system-ui, which is a different face on every one. At 0.55em the spine's own overflow disappears and the drilled ones do not. So the count is an upper bound on a real defect, not a count of it, and the first step is to measure it against a real font rather than to widen anything.

tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's arm 'every label in the object-category window is anchored on a side it has room on' asserts the full rule over the {2,5,4} window, where every label does fit. Widening the arm to every view is what this bead closes with.
notes:
NOTE 2026-09-14: this bead's 17-of-368 was measured over 45 views, and the tree now opens 76 in FY2025-26 and 74 in FY2026-27 (drill.mjs's COLUMNS). The count is therefore a floor over a smaller tree rather than a measurement of today's. The closing condition stated here -- the label arm widened to every view -- is also what would retire the hand-picked windows layout.mjs imports from drill.mjs, whose literal counts are what let fisc-ieei's arm name drift from its own pin. drill.mjs's everyOpenedView is the recursive walker to spend, and it is not exported today.
MEASURED AGAINST THE WHOLE TREE 2026-09-14, at de45bb2, which is this bead's stated closing condition half-landed. layout.mjs now runs labelFit over everyOpenedView in both columns and pins the over-gutter marks BY ID: 23 in FY2025-26 over 76 views and 26 in FY2026-27 over 74, against the 17-of-368-over-45-views this bead was filed on. 0 views stack two labels and 0 draw two marks alike, so the RULE half is zero and carries no literal. The widest label the tree draws is gap/expenditure/services-and-supplies at 98px past the gutter, FY2026-27 only -- a derived mark, which none of this bead's original measurements reached. WHAT IS STILL OWED HERE: the expanded axis. everyOpenedView follows drillable and an expandable tail is the other gesture, so expandedChecks still measures one hand-picked window; walking views x {folded, expanded} is what finishes this. And the browser reading itself is fisc-rl4j.

title: docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md still quotes the {0,3,4} chain's figures in three places
description:
Lane G (8c9456a) replaced the {0,3,4} depth-1 chart with the {0,2,3} window and moved the cap measurements, and three paragraphs of the contract doc were not re-measured with it.

MEASURED 2026-09-13 against tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's COLUMNS, which pins the current figures per column:

(1) 'What the fold does not fix' says 'the General Fund at depth 1 draws 2 sub-pixel ribbons of 37 in FY2025-26 and 3 of 37 in FY2026-27'. The tree draws 13 ribbons with 1 sub-pixel in FY2025-26 and 12 with 1 in FY2026-27 (COLUMNS[*].general).
