NOT FIXED IN fisc-5eni, which re-measured only the counts-line paragraph of that doc because that is the sentence it changed. Each figure above has a live pin in drill.mjs to re-measure it from; none of them is checkable by make doccheck, which reads AGENTS.md citations and not figures.

title: The General Fund group's transfers out and reserve increase are drawn nowhere in the drill
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13, both published columns. carryResidual states the outflow side only where the DRAWN chart carries a flow out of the opened node's parts, and the fund-group window draws {0,2,3} -- the group's funds and no division -- so its funds publish no outflow there. General's 10,037,797 of transfers out and 4,699,425 of reserve increase (FY2025-26) and 10,146,598 / 3,332,607 / 2,351,098 (FY2026-27) are therefore carried onto no residual node anywhere in the drill.

THEY ARE NOT LOST: the spine's own chart draws all three in its right-hand column, at the same figures, and pp.66-67 are where they are printed. What is gone is the second telling, on the opened group, that the {0,3,4} chart used to give.

THE OUTFLOW BRANCH OF carryResidual IS THEREFORE DRIVEN ONLY BY FIXTURES, like fisc-mrkg's Side. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's residual block asserts out == 0 on every group, and the branch itself is exercised by the mutation that reads `decomposed` off the step document instead of the drawn chart -- 9 arms red, with the endpoints laid in the same column as the residual, which is the shape that made the change necessary.

Retiring it or reaching it would need a fourth column on that window, which is not a window.
notes:
2026-09-22: THE FIGURES ARE CONFIRMED BY GO, AND THE OUTFLOW BRANCH IS NOW SAFE
TO REACH.

This bead's last line -- "Retiring it or reaching it would need a fourth column
on that window, which is not a window" -- was tested. Widening the fund-group
step to the fund-flows chain gives the window four and five columns, and
export.ResidualOf then answers general's residual with an OUTGOING leg:

  FY2025-26  out 14,737,222  = this bead's 10,037,797 + 4,699,425
  FY2026-27  out 15,830,303  = this bead's 10,146,598 + 3,332,607 + 2,351,098

Both to the cent, derived from the documents by Go rather than transcribed, with
ends gaining fund-balance/reserve-increase and transfers/out. So the arithmetic
recorded here is right and the money is drawable.

REACHING IT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A DEFECT, now fixed (af76bb9): carryResidual read
the step's DECLARED last tier to place an outgoing endpoint, and a step whose
`widen` the budget has not bought draws fewer columns than it declares -- so the
endpoint carried a tier with no column and d3-sankey clamped it to the FIRST one,
running the ribbon backwards across the chart. The outgoing branch being
fixture-only is exactly why nothing saw it.

STILL BLOCKED, and not on this bead: the widening itself breaks drillDown into
fund/100, which is fisc-ke1f's subset question. fisc-ipif carries the
measurements.

title: isCarried's arm of drillable is inert on every view the page opens
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 by walking the whole tree through the shipped entry points, both published columns: not one carried mark is at a tier a step opens from on a chart a step names, so stepFor answers null before isCarried is ever consulted. drillable's `&& !isCarried(d.id)` therefore refuses nothing the corpus produces.

WHY IT WENT INERT. Lane G's windows put the residual's endpoints in the KEPT FLANK -- they are the chart above's own marks -- and no step names the chart a kept flank sits on, which export.validateSteps now refuses outright. The residual NODE is at tier 3, which the fund step does open from, and it is closed by that step's role instead.

IT SHOULD STAY, as the second gate: the argument for it -- a flow's end is not a container -- does not depend on which gate fires first. What should not stand is a check reading "nothing carried opens" as evidence that THIS gate fired; tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's window arm now says so in its own words and asserts the reason (stepFor null) rather than the outcome alone.

Sibling of fisc-mrkg, which is DrillStep.Side's branch in the same condition.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-20 AND THIS BEAD OVERSTATES WHAT LANDED. It says tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's window arm 'now says so in its own words and asserts the reason (stepFor null) rather than the outcome alone'. It does not: the arm at drill.mjs's residual block asserts `opens.length === 0` over `isCarried(n.id) && drillable(n)` and reads no stepFor. The two arms that DO assert stepFor null are the revenue-category ones, about a category the openable set closes, not about a carried mark. So the inertness this bead measured is still recorded nowhere a check would show it, and the action is the one sentence of assertion it claims is already there.

STILL INERT AFTER fisc-phtp.2, checked: drillable's `&& !isCarried(d.id)` is unchanged at site/app.js, isCarried still reads step.residual, and the residual's endpoints are still flank marks of the chart above that no step names a chart for.

title: DrillStep.Side has no shipped declaration left, and its branch is driven only by fixtures
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13, at Lane D's landing. export.SideSource was declared by exactly one step on the site -- the revenue-category step, which drew {1,3} and opened the node its links came FROM. That step is a window now (Keep [2], Tiers {1,0,2}), and validateSteps refuses Side beside Keep, so no view in pkg/cmd/export/data.go declares a Side at all. grep: the only remaining SideSource literals are internal/export/views_test.go's fixture, pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go's refusal table and tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's parser probe.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE CLIENT. shapeFor branches `step.side === "source" ? filterFromNode : filterToNode` for a step that keeps no flank, and the filterFromNode arm of that branch is now reached only by a jscheck fixture. filterFromNode ITSELF is still on the shipped path -- windowFor calls it for the kept half of every window -- so this is about the one-sided spelling, not the filter.

NOT A DEFECT TODAY and not obviously one tomorrow: a one-sided source step is a shape the packager should still accept, and Lane G may declare one. What is worth deciding is whether a vocabulary with no shipped user keeps its validateSteps arms and its client branch, or whether the branch should be refused until something declares it -- the difference between a feature held by fixtures and a feature held by the site.
notes: CORRECTION, grepped rather than recalled: the remaining SideSource literals are internal/export/views_test.go:956 (the refusal table's 'a side beside a kept flank' case) and :2958 (the two-root fixture), tools/jscheck/harness.mjs:928 (the parser reads the constant as well as the string) and tools/jscheck/seam.mjs:263 (which drives that parser over a literal data.go does not contain). pkg/cmd/export/export_test.go carries none -- it pins views() and views() no longer declares one.
close_reason: PREMISE DEAD TWICE OVER, re-derived against the tree 2026-09-20. (1) 'No view in data.go declares a Side at all' is false: the transfers step declares export.SideSource at pkg/cmd/export/data.go:1110, so the vocabulary has a shipped user and is held by the site rather than by fixtures. (2) The client branch this bead was about -- shapeFor's `step.side === "source" ? filterFromNode : filterToNode` -- no longer exists. fisc-phtp.2 deleted both filters: site/app.js contains zero occurrences of filterFromNode and zero of step.side, because which end of a ribbon is the near one is Go's reading now and the page draws the ribbons between the nodes the answer names, forward through the answer's own column order. There is no one-sided spelling left to decide about.

title: docs/sankey-contract.md enumerates seven published documents; the corpus builds thirteen
description:
docs/sankey-contract.md's stem paragraph reads "Today that is seven: sankey and sankey-2027 ..., revenue-trends, and the drill-down's four" and says all seven are pinned by TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged.

MEASURED 2026-09-13 against that test's own literal: it pins THIRTEEN -- changes-in-fund-balances, department-spending and its three columns, fund-balances, fund-flows and its three columns, revenue-trends, sankey, sankey-2027. The doc's list omits six.

PRE-EXISTING AND NOT LANE F's. It was already wrong before fisc-ko1j.20 added the four cross-tab columns, because changes-in-fund-balances and fund-balances were never in it.

THE FIX IS PROBABLY TO DELETE THE ENUMERATION RATHER THAN CORRECT IT. AGENTS.md's "Before you quote a number" refuses a count of the tree's own contents precisely because it goes stale on the next commit, and this one has gone stale twice. The naming RULE the paragraph states is the part worth keeping; the list is held by the Go test and the doc does not need a second copy.

title: department-spending publishes external on money that includes internal service charges
description:
Every expenditure link of the departmentwide cross-tab carries kind 'external'. It is the weakest claim the document makes, and it is DISCLOSED rather than fixed: the caveat 'the-boundary-is-not-classified-here' says these rows carry no fund group, so boundaryKind's question cannot be asked of them, and names the figure inside them -- measured off the spine, internal-service expenditure is 25,077,367 of 254,095,412 in FY2025-26 and 26,544,515 of 252,854,896 in FY2026-27.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY WRONG: the four kinds docs/sankey-contract.md declares are a closed set with no 'unclassified' member, and a fifth would move every document. transfer_out keeps internal_transfer, which is the one classification these facts DO support and which link-kinds-match-their-facts enforces.

WHY IT IS STILL A DEFECT WORTH TRACKING: a client summing 'external' across documents over-counts by exactly the internal-service share, which is the shape of the false claim fisc-xau measured on the drill-down's transfers. Nothing but the caveat stops it.

Two candidate repairs, neither taken here: (a) a fifth kind, or an explicit 'unclassified', decided on its own bead because it moves the contract; (b) drawing the lower block beside this one so the fund group is available, which is fisc-4ua.2 and needs 'department:' on 78 mapping rows first.

title: department-spending publishes counts no verify check re-derives
description:
The departmentwide cross-tab publishes metadata.counts {facts, facts_cited, facts_uncited, nodes, links} and NO CHECK IN internal/check RE-DERIVES ANY OF THEM.

The spine's block is held by counts-reconcile and the drill-down's by fund-flows-counts-reconcile; this shape reached neither, because both are written against a document type by name and fund-flows-counts-reconcile's own summary line calls its subject 'the drill-down'. Widening it would make its id a false claim about what it reads.

WHAT DOES HOLD THE NUMBERS TODAY, so this is a gap and not a hole: the projection REFUSES at build time any fact that reached no link and is not a printed zero (internal/project/departmentspending.go), which is the identity facts = facts_cited + facts_uncited enforced by construction rather than asserted afterwards, and internal/project's TestTheCrossTabCountsEveryFactOnceOrAsAPrintedZero asserts all five figures over a fixture. What is NOT held is the committed corpus: a count that drifted from the arrays it describes on the four published documents would ship green.

The cheap shape is a check over every headline-less linked document's counts, reading the published links as fund-flows-counts-reconcile does, with the facts_cited_twice arm applied only where the document publishes one.

title: markContra names a window's kept flank in the wrong words, or in none
description:
shapeFor passes the STEP DOCUMENT to markContra as the file to resolve a contra ribbon's parent label from, and on a window the negative ribbon may be in the KEPT half, whose nodes came off the chart on screen and need not be in that file at all.

markContra's under() falls back to "printed rows netting to a reduction" when it cannot find the source's parent, so the failure is a vaguer sentence rather than a wrong figure -- and a wrong one is reachable: if the step document happens to carry the same id under a DIFFERENT parent, the ribbon would be named as a reduction of the wrong thing.

LATENT ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS, measured at d7086dc: no spine (0,2) or (2,5) link is negative, so no kept flank drawn today carries a contra ribbon at all. It stops being latent the first time a window keeps a column whose ribbons can be reductions.

THE FIX IS PROBABLY ONE ARGUMENT: markContra takes the document a link's ends should be resolved against, and windowFor knows which half each link came from. Not done in d7086dc because nothing exercises it and an unexercised branch is the next pass's finding.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of fisc-74m0, found on filing: that bead already names this defect one case earlier -- markContra resolving a link's words through the STEP document's hierarchy when the link did not come from it. The window widens its reach rather than adding a second bug, and fisc-74m0 now carries that half.

title: A rollup's link kind is held by one Go test and by no check
description:
fisc verify cannot see a fund-flows rollup published under the wrong kind. Measured at the lane-A commit by reverting the (line, kind) key to the line alone, so the two-kind lines published one ribbon carrying both: 49 passed, 0 failed. checkDistinctLinks does not fire (it refuses two links of ONE kind on a pair), link-kinds-match-their-facts does not fire (every fact the rollup cites is a revenue row, so its all-transfers and all-fund-balance arms are silent), and link-values-tie-to-facts is indifferent to kind. The only thing that went red was TestALineRollsUpIntoItsCategoryOncePerKind in internal/project, which is a test of the projection and not of the published store -- the distinction funding-sources-tie-by-fund-group records as 'a guarantee inside one lane's go test is not one the fact store carries'.

The same hole covers the existing (1,3) links: boundaryKind is the projection's own rule and nothing re-reads it. A fact carries FundGroup, so a check COULD assert that a link published as internal_service cites only internal-service-group facts and vice versa. linkKindsMatchTheirFacts's own doc comment argues against re-deriving a projection's classification (two copies of a rule agree by construction), so this needs deciding rather than writing: the honest one-way form is probably 'a link whose facts are ALL internal-service-group rows may not be external', which is the mirror of its transfer arm and is NOT a second classifier.
acceptance_criteria: Either a check that reddens fisc verify on a mis-kinded revenue link, with its mutation recorded, or a decision on this bead saying why the one-way form cannot be stated and what holds it instead.

title: No check ties a class app.js sets to a rule style.css carries
description:
FOUND reviewing fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E), 2026-09-13. tools/jscheck only.

harness.mjs scans the shipped stylesheet for CUSTOM PROPERTIES alone -- customProperties is a regex for '--name:' over style.css -- so the stub can tell a var() name the sheet carries from one it does not. Nothing does the same for CLASS names, in either direction.

WHAT THAT LETS THROUGH. Lane E ships four new rules (svg.sankey .link.contra, svg.sankey .node.contra rect, .chip.contra, #flow-table tr.contra) and four new class strings (linkClass, nodeClass, 'chip contra', tr.className = 'contra'). drill.mjs asserts the STRING app.js produces -- linkClass(eraf) === 'link contra' -- and nothing asserts style.css has a rule that selector matches. A typo on either side is a mark that draws in the default ink with every gate green, and the contra treatment is a case where the colour is one of the three signals the design leans on.

THE SAME GAP ALREADY COVERS .derived, .dim, .residual and the rest; this is not a lane-E regression, it is a lane-E-sized reminder.

THE SHAPE: collect class literals out of app.js the way selectorsIn collects selectors, collect class selectors out of style.css the way customProperties collects names, and report both directions -- a class app.js sets that the sheet never styles is a silent no-op, and a rule the sheet carries that no code sets is dead ink. Expect the first run to find pre-existing entries; declare them rather than deleting them blind.

title: markContra names a carried spine link's parent in the step document's hierarchy
description:
FOUND reviewing fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E) before it landed, 2026-09-13. site/app.js only, and LATENT: measured, neither spine golden carries a negative link (testdata/sankey.golden.json and -2027, 58 links each, zero negative), so no published column reaches it.

shapeFor ends 'markContra(carryResidual(reparented, docAt(drilled.length - 1), rung), doc)'. carryResidual splices links copied VERBATIM FROM THE SPINE into the drawn document; markContra's second argument is the STEP document, and its under() resolves a negative link's source through that document's byID map. So a negative CARRIED link would be named for whatever its source id's parent is in the step document -- a different hierarchy -- or, where the step document does not carry the id, for the fallback 'printed rows netting to a reduction', which is a sentence about a capped tail and not about a carried endpoint.

WHY IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT TO FIX BLIND: the right answer is a decision. A carried mark is deliberately 'not of the drawn document' (carryResidual sets carried_from, and caveatsFor and caveatHref already branch on it), so the honest fix is for markContra to resolve a carried link's words through carriedSource() the way caveatHref does -- or for carryResidual to refuse a negative link by name, on the ground that the chart above netted it and this one would not.

TO REPRODUCE: negate a spine link into a carried endpoint (transfers/out on fund-group/general) in a drill.mjs fixture and open that group at {0,3,4}.
notes:
2026-09-13, d7086dc: THE WINDOW WIDENS THIS FROM CARRIED RESIDUAL LINKS TO A WHOLE KEPT FLANK. windowFor splices a half-chart filtered off the chart ON SCREEN beside a half filtered off the step document, and shapeFor still hands markContra the step document alone. So the ids this cannot resolve are now a whole column's rather than a handful of residual endpoints', and the decision this bead says not to make blind is the same one: resolve a link's words through the document its ends came from -- which the splice knows, since carried_from is set on every kept-flank node -- or refuse a negative link on the kept side by name.

STILL LATENT, re-measured at d7086dc: no spine (0,2) or (2,5) link is negative in either published column, so no kept flank any declared window could draw carries a contra ribbon. It stops being latent the first time a window keeps a column whose ribbons can be reductions.

TO REPRODUCE THE WINDOW HALF: negate the spine's revenue/taxes/property -> fund-group/general link in tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's window fixture (WINDOW_STEPS) and read the drawn ribbon's `contra` sentence.

title: A contra ribbon carries no direction cue beyond its colour, sign and sentence
description:
FOUND landing fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E), 2026-09-12. The owner's decision on fisc-ko1j.9/.11 was that a contra row (ERAF, RPTTF Reduction under Property Taxes) draws REVERSED at |value| with contra styling and text. The client draws it FORWARD at |value|, and the deviation is on a measured ground rather than a preference: a link from the fund back to the line gives the line a d3 depth one past the fund's, the vendored d3-sankey sizes its column count from the deepest node, and a {1,3} view came to three columns with the third empty -- its computeNodeLayers loop throws on the hole ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading sort)', the failure layOut's comment already records for a misaligned tier set). Re-measure by reversing a contra link's source/target in markContra and opening Property Taxes.

WHAT SHIPS INSTEAD: class 'contra' (--critical stroke, style.css), a U+2212 sign on every figure the mark prints (tooltip, panel, table, aria), the sentence 'printed as a reduction of Property Taxes' on the link, and contraNote on the fund mark saying what it is gross of. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs pins all of it over both columns.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS: whether a direction cue is wanted at all -- an arrowhead marker on the contra path, a gradient, or a hatched pattern -- and if so its light/dark contrast. A custom path from the fund's LEFT edge to the line's RIGHT edge (the ribbon drawn right-to-left between the same two columns) is the geometry that says 'reversed' without a third column; d3's link y0/y1 stacking does not depend on x, so it is drawable. Not done in lane E because the sign, colour and sentence already say it three ways and a fourth is a design call.

title: FY2024 actual prints a negative revenue row that is not declared contra
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-12, sweeping facts/facts.jsonl for negative amounts in scope
revenue-by-fund. Nine rows are negative; eight carry sign: contra. One does not:

  2024 actual  fund/100  taxes/property  "Prior Year - Unsecured"  -20,033.00  sign=positive

The eight contra rows are ERAF and RPTTF Reduction, in all four columns, and they
are declared: mapping.SignContra exists to say they net into their parent
category. This one is a negative printed figure carrying sign: positive.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. fund-flows-2024-actual is a
PUBLISHED column. Once E13's revenue side lands, a printed line is a node and a
negative amount is a negative-valued link -- and the contra rows get a drawn
treatment decided on fisc-ko1j.9 (reversed, marked as a reduction) precisely
BECAUSE they are declared. This row would be drawn as a plain backward ribbon
with no explanation, or would need the same treatment without the declaration
that justifies it.

THE QUESTION THIS BEAD OWNS, and it is a document question before it is a code
one: is p127's FY2023-24 actual "Prior Year - Unsecured" a contra row the mapping
failed to declare, or a genuine negative actual -- a prior-year unsecured
collection that came back negative after refunds? The two want different answers.
Read the page before changing anything.

If it is the former, the fix is a sign: contra in
mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml and a regenerated facts.jsonl, which is
a fact-store change and its own reviewed commit. If it is the latter, then
"negative implies contra" is NOT an invariant and something should say so, because
the drawn treatment is about to assume it.

NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE HAZARD: nothing is red today. The row nets correctly into
its cell either way, so every check passes and the question only becomes visible
when a line becomes a node.

Found while re-deriving fisc-ko1j.9's premises.

title: A legend on an opened view needs per-group isolation, because a swatch toggles a node id
description:
FOUND while designing fisc-ko1j.11, 2026-09-12, and split out of it deliberately:
it is a SECOND emphasis model and does not belong inside that lane's client change.

buildLegend returns after clearing whenever drilled.length > 0 -- empty on every
opened view, by rule. fisc-ko1j.11's 2026-09-10 note says this bead's case is
where that rule has to change, because a revenue category's subtree spans fund
groups.

RE-DERIVED 2026-09-12: the note is right that the rule's STATED reason fails
there. buildLegend argues "an opened view is one node's subtree, every mark
resolves to the one fund group above it, and the swatch is a toggle on a NODE id
that setIsolated dims against". The first clause is false for a category view --
its subtree spans all six groups.

BUT THE SECOND CLAUSE STILL HOLDS AND IS THE BINDING ONE. setIsolated takes a
NODE id, and no fund-group/ node is in a {1,3} view at all. A legend there would
need emphasis resolved PER GROUP through fundGroupOf inside applyEmphasis, which
is a different notion of "isolated" from the one every other path uses -- the
same species of split as filterToNode vs filterFromNode.

So fisc-ko1j.11 keeps the empty legend and rewrites the comment to the surviving
reason. This bead is the rule change.

WHAT IT OWES: the per-group isolation path; a decision on whether a swatch on an
opened view dims by group while one on the overview dims by node, or whether BOTH
become per-group; and the retirement or rewrite of tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's "an
opened view draws no legend even where a fund-group node survives the filter"
probe, which is the arm that pins today's rule.

Related: the muted-ribbon bead. Either fix makes a category view's fund column
legible; doing both without deciding which carries the claim is how two sources
of truth get shipped.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-13 AGAINST LANE D, AND THE BINDING CLAUSE HAS MOVED. This bead says "setItolated takes a NODE id, and no fund-group/ node is in a {1,3} view at all", which was the surviving reason for the empty legend. The revenue-category step declares Keep [2] / Tiers {1,0,2} now, so its right-hand column IS the spine's fund groups: measured over both published columns, six distinct fund-group nodes are drawn across the ten category windows, each in its own hue, with no key on the page. Lane F's object-category window keeps the same column.

So the second clause is false too, and buildLegend's comment was rewritten in this lane to the reason that survives BOTH: a swatch on a window's kept flank would be a toggle that dims everything the reader opened the node to see. That is a decision rather than an absence, and this bead is still the one that revisits it -- with one case more than it was filed for: a coloured column with no legend beside it, which is a worse state than a legend that cannot be built.
MECHANISM NOTE, 2026-09-20: 'the same species of split as filterToNode vs filterFromNode' names a pair the tree no longer has. Both went with fisc-phtp.2 and fisc-1osz -- the client reads which nodes a column holds out of Go's answer and draws the ribbons between them forward through the answer's own column order, so there is one filter and no side to read. The ANALOGY still holds for whoever takes this: the point was that one function answering two questions by flag is how a caller gets the wrong one, and that argument does not need the example.

title: A ribbon with one group-less end draws muted, so a category view's fund column says nothing about which group a fund is in
description:
FOUND while designing fisc-ko1j.11, 2026-09-12, and deliberately NOT fixed there:
it changes shipped depth-1 views as well as the new one, so it does not belong
inside the largest client change of E13.

MEASURED by reading site/app.js: only fund-group/ ids ever take a hue. linkColor
resolves each end through fundGroupOf and draws --muted unless both ends agree;
fundGroupOf returns "" for a tier-0 revenue node BY DESIGN ("money arriving, not
money held"). So EVERY revenue -> fund ribbon on every opened view today is
already muted, and that is not a defect introduced by the revenue lane.

WHAT IS A DEFECT is what it costs the new view. A revenue category opened at
depth 0 draws a fund column spanning ALL SIX fund groups, with muted ribbons and
(by buildLegend's rule) no legend -- so nothing on that chart says which fund is
in which group. On the fund-group views this does not arise, because the reader
opened one group and every fund on screen is in it.

THE CANDIDATE FIX is one arm in linkColor: where one end has no fund group and
the other does, take the other's hue. That also recolours the revenue half of
every existing depth-1 view, which is a visible change to shipped output and
wants its own before/after and its own jscheck arm.

linkColor's own comment says "Ends in two different groups cannot happen" and
would have to be rewritten with it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS AS AGREED. The muted revenue half may be deliberate -- money
arriving has no group until it lands -- and the honest alternative is to solve
the legibility problem at the legend instead. See the per-group isolation bead.

title: drill-reconciles-across-documents reports VACUOUS with a sentence that is false when a shared column carries no group
description:
HYGIENE. Found by /code-review PASS TWO lens C.

internal/check/drillreconcile.go. Probe by lens C: a shared column whose spine links are nil and whose drill nodes and links are nil returns StatusVacuous with 'no fiscal column is published by both the spine and the drill-down'. The column IS published by both; what is absent is any fund group to reconcile.

So the sentence names the wrong absence. AGENTS.md's vacuity doctrine is that a vacuous check says what is missing -- internal/check/vacuity.go's TestVacuousChecksSayWhatIsAbsent exists for exactly that -- and this one would send a reader looking for a column that is there.

NOT A GATE PROBLEM: the check is undeclared in declaredVacuous and passes on the committed corpus, so --strict is correct today. This only misreports on a corpus that does not exist yet.

Two sentences, split on which case fired, is the fix. Neighbour: fisc-0ytv, which is about the column set having no floor -- the same region and probably the same change.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE. Its whole subject -- internal/check/drillreconcile.go's vacuity sentence -- was deleted at aef3d8f (L3.4), which removed drill-reconciles-across-documents along with eight other checks against the lattice. Verified at HEAD: the file does not exist, and drill-reconciles-across-documents is not among the 44 ids fisc verify reports.

NOTHING CARRIED FORWARD. The bead's substance was that a StatusVacuous sentence named the wrong absence; the sentence is gone with the check. The DOCTRINE it rests on is not lost -- internal/check/vacuity.go's TestVacuousChecksSayWhatIsAbsent still holds every surviving check to it, which is the guard, not this bead.

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: baseDescription's sentinel re-captures whenever the served desc is empty, so a drillUp could announce the drilled sentence
description:
HYGIENE, latent and unreachable on the shipped template. Found by /code-review PASS TWO lens B.

site/app.js:1387 guards the capture with 'if (!baseDescription)'. An empty served <desc> makes that sentinel falsy on EVERY call, so the base is re-captured each time -- and a drillUp would capture the DRILLED sentence as the base, after which the overview would announce 'Opened into ...' to a screen reader.

WHY IT CANNOT FIRE TODAY: the shipped template renders two sentences, export refuses an unterminated description, and tools/jscheck/drill.mjs plants the served text. Lens B confirmed the production path is correct and that this is NOT the historical defect where a drill replaced <desc> and dropped the flow-table pointer -- that pointer is present at every depth, measured.

The shape is 'a sentinel that cannot distinguish not-yet-set from set-to-empty', which is the absent-is-not-zero rule in a string. A separate boolean, or capturing once at wire-up, removes it.

title: stepDescriptions pairs descriptions positionally, and a sibling Description field would throw with a misleading count
description:
HYGIENE, fail-closed. Found by /code-review PASS TWO lens A over b5c7830's own fix.

tools/jscheck/harness.mjs stepDescriptions() returns the Description fields in declaration order and drill.mjs reads STEP_DESCRIPTIONS[0] and [1]. Two consequences:

(1) POSITIONAL PAIRING. A third step, or two steps reordered in views(), pairs the wrong sentence with the wrong step. The guard counts and would not see it, because the count would still match. Keying by something the step declares -- Back, or the tier set -- would pin the pairing rather than the tally.

(2) A SIBLING FIELD COLLIDES. export.View already declares ChartDescription (internal/export/export.go:218). Were one declared in data.go, the decl regex (unanchored on 'Description:') would parse it while the ^\\s*Description: count would not count it, so the function throws with 'parsed N step descriptions from a file declaring M' -- a message naming the wrong problem.

BOTH FAIL CLOSED, which is why this is P3 and not higher: (2) throws rather than returning a wrong pairing, and make js goes red. (1) is the one that could ship quietly, and only if views() gains a step.

Anchoring the regex to the field and keying the pairing would close both.
notes:
ITEM (2) IS GONE WITH ITS SUBJECT, re-derived 2026-09-20. The sibling field it names -- export.View.ChartDescription -- is deleted with the second chart template (fisc-1osz), so there is no View-level Description for stepDescriptions' unanchored 'Description:' regex to parse while the anchored count misses it. The throw that named the wrong problem is now undeclarable rather than merely unexercised.

ITEM (1) STANDS UNCHANGED and is the whole of this bead now: stepDescriptions() returns the Description fields in declaration order, drill.mjs reads STEP_DESCRIPTIONS[0] and [1], and a third step or two reordered in views() pairs the wrong sentence with the wrong step while the count still matches. Key by something the step declares -- Back, or the tier set.

title: fund-flows' own transfers/in node declares no caveat, where the spine declares one over the same id
description:
DESIGN, latent: no rung the site answers draws the node this is about, so nothing
a reader can reach today shows the qualification dropped.

MEASURED 2026-09-23 by driving the shipped site/app.js over fisc export's bytes
at ebdb422, over every rung Go answers in both columns (99 and 97): transfers/in
is drawn at the overview and at the six fund-group rungs, and at every one of
those it is a CARRIED mark (carried_from = sankey), so caveatsFor resolves it
against the spine and returns [transfer-legs-unpaired] with a non-empty
caveatHref. transfers/out is drawn at the overview only. On no answered rung is
fund-flows' own transfers/in a drawn node.

THE DECLARATION GAP. The fund-flows schedule carries a transfers/in node with
eight links (pp.127-140's eight funds in three groups) and declares no caveat
naming it, while the spine declares transfer-legs-unpaired over transfers/in and
transfers/out. Any window that draws fund-flows' transfers/in rather than
carrying the spine's would show the mark with the qualification dropped, by the
drawn route -- the sibling of what fisc-bccu fixed on the carried route.

THE FIX IS A DECLARATION in the fund-flows projection, not a branch in
caveatsFor. A client fallback to the spine for any id would assert that a caveat
about the spine's transfers/in is about fund-flows' transfers/in, a claim about
two documents only the packager can make.

RELATED: fisc-9gh, which is why transfer-legs-unpaired exists; fisc-to3q,
fundflows.go claiming a marking at depth 1 that does not happen.

title: Four small drill.mjs and fold.mjs arms: an unreachable branch, a discarded measurement, a bare-digit match and a stale fixture year
description:
HYGIENE, four items in the jscheck modules, filed together because each is a line or two in a file the next jscheck change will be in. Found by /code-review lens 4 over 0923016..HEAD.

(1) A NEGATIVE BRANCH THAT IS NOW UNREACHABLE. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs ~:625-640 -- both 'where' entries carry sharesColumn: true since the residual divided fund/100's column, so the !tip.includes('of this column') branch and its comment 'EXPECTED WHERE THE COLUMN DIVIDES AND NOWHERE ELSE' describe nothing exercised. columnShare's column-of-one suppression is still witnessed indirectly, by the 'no share reads 100%' scan over depth-2 views. Related: fisc-kcud, which may change what the right pin is.

(2) A MEASUREMENT OF THE WRONG INSTANCE, DISCARDED. drill.mjs ~:913 -- 'const none = residualOf.call(null, general); void none;'. residualOf closes over app, not over undeclared, so it measures the DECLARED instance and then throws the value away. This is the shape docs/review-loop-evidence.md lists as 'a heading arm that computed </summary> and never used it'.

(3) A SOURCE-NOTE ARM THAT MATCHES BARE DIGITS. drill.mjs ~:990 -- source_note.includes(String(pg)) with pg = 66 or 67 would also be satisfied by a title or by 'pp.167-170'. Lens 4 proved it live TODAY (dropping 'where' from carryResidual's note gives 2 FAIL), so it is not vacuous now; it is one title change away. Matching 'p.66'/'pp.66' pins it.

(4) A FIXTURE YEAR CARRYING THE OTHER COLUMN'S COUNTS. tools/jscheck/fold.mjs appDrawing declares {facts: 280, nodes: 145, links: 175}, which are FY2026's, under both columns. Harmless today because nothing asserts the counts line there any more -- which is itself worth knowing, since it means the numbers are decoration.

(3) is the 'widen what the check can SEE, never loosen what it asserts' rule in AGENTS.md, 'Prove it can fail'.

title: isCarried excludes by declared name rather than by what carryResidual actually carried
description:
HYGIENE. Found by /code-review lens 3 over 0923016..HEAD. High confidence on the mismatch, low on reader impact.

site/app.js:1707-1712 -- isCarried refuses any id present in step.residual as openable at that rung, whether or not carryResidual actually added it. drillable's comment says 'the endpoints carried with it', which is not what the code tests.

MEASURED: transfers/in is a real tier-0 node of BOTH fund-flows documents -- lens 3 reports it as the only declared endpoint id present in either step document. Harmless today because tier 0 is never a step's From, so nothing offers to open it anyway.

The gap closes if isCarried asks the drawn graph what carryResidual produced instead of asking the declaration.

SIBLING, from the same probe and worth doing in the same change: carryResidual's 'endpoint already drawn' branch (site/app.js:1858 region) runs in no check -- neither year's general drawn set contains a declared endpoint, so the have.has(e) arm is unexercised on the committed corpus. That is the 'ask what the fixture is hiding' habit; the arm is reachable in principle and covered by nothing.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-20: STILL TRUE, AND THE MISMATCH CHANGED SHAPE. isCarried is unchanged -- it still refuses any id present in step.residual -- but what carryResidual actually carries is no longer its own derivation over the step document: it is the endpoints export.ResidualOf named in the rung's mark (`mark.ends`). So the gap is now between the DECLARATION the packager ships and the ANSWER Go computed from it, which is a narrower and more checkable pair than the one this bead measured: an id in step.residual that the mark's ends do not name is exactly a node isCarried refuses and carryResidual did not carry.

THE SIBLING IS ALSO STILL UNEXERCISED: carryResidual's 'endpoint already drawn' branch (have.has(e)) runs in no check, for the same reason -- neither year's general drawn set contains a declared endpoint.

title: The residual node's tooltip calls max(in, out) its 'total' on a mark whose point is the imbalance
description:
DESIGN, confidence medium. Found by /code-review lens 3 over 0923016..HEAD.

site/app.js:2605 -- nodeDescription uses d.value, which is d3-sankey's max(in, out), and announces it as 'total'. The rationale the same node carries (site/app.js:1796) says in and out 'need not balance'.

MEASURED by lens 3 off the committed goldens, fund-group/general:
  FY2026  in 1,514,554   out 14,737,222  -> announced 'Not broken down by fund, total $14,737,222'
  FY2027  in   486,735   out 15,830,303  -> announced with 15,830,303

The number is a sum of printed figures, so nothing is invented -- this is not a provenance defect. But 'total' on a node whose whole purpose is to make the imbalance visible names one side and calls it the whole, and the reader has no way to see the other side.

Related and filed separately by the lane: fisc-dzby, on the same node's rationale quoting the wrong year's figures.

ALSO, same node, lower: the carried link panel reads '$480,400 Transfers In -> Not broken down by fund ... printed by the city'. The VALUE is printed; the re-pointing onto a derived node is ours. AGENTS.md, 'Published and derived are different things' -- the panel's provenance phrase describes the figure's origin and not the mark's, and on a derived endpoint those differ.

title: views_test's refusal table has no passing control, and two h2 assertions match a stem's own prefix
description:
HYGIENE, two items in the same file from /code-review lens 2 over 0923016..HEAD.

(1) A REFUSAL TABLE WHOSE FIXTURE IS ITSELF REFUSED. internal/export/views_test.go:651 says 'chart below is a well-formed ChartTemplate view'. MEASURED (lens 2, probe H): it is not writable -- the table hands it goldenSankey, which fails with 'sankey metadata declares no scopes'. The cases still go red on a dropped arm because each asserts its own want string, so this is not a check that cannot fail; but the table has no passing control, which its OWN comment presumes ('the message named is the one that arm produces rather than whichever fires first'). TestAStepsPerYearJoinIsExactOrRefused, a few hundred lines down, does have that control and says why -- 'a refusal table over a fixture that is refused for some other reason proves nothing about any arm in it'. Pre-existing, touched by the lane.

(2) AN h2 ASSERTION THAT MATCHES A LONGER STEM. views_test.go:418 and its sibling at :482 do strings.Index(page, "<h2>"+stem). With stem "fund-flows" that also matches "<h2>fund-flows-2027". Correct today only because the sections sort with the bare stem first. The real h2s are '<h2>fund-flows <span ...', so matching "<h2>"+stem+" " pins it.

(2) is the exact shape docs/review-loop-evidence.md lists five times under 'an assertion written against one rendering of a thing' -- and every one of those was fixed by widening what the check can SEE, never by loosening what it asserts.

title: reconcileSide's fund.by[id] read has no ok-check, so an absent endpoint and a zero-cent one are one case
description:
HYGIENE, unreachable on the committed corpus. Found by /code-review lens 1 over 0923016..HEAD.

internal/check/drillreconcile.go:334-337 reads fund.by[id] with no ok-check and its first arm treats 'no fund-level link from this endpoint' and 'fund-level links summing to zero cents' identically -- both become residual. WHY IT CANNOT FIRE TODAY, measured: both projections drop zero-cent links (internal/project/fundflows.go:317, 353, 379) and both committed goldens carry 0 zero-valued links. So no mutation produces a wrong verdict on this corpus.

WHY IT IS FILED ANYWAY: AGENTS.md, 'Provenance invariants' -- absent is not zero, and conflating them invents rows. This is that conflation in a check rather than in a parser, and it is held closed by an invariant declared in a different package. flowSum already counts links, so tracking presence per endpoint is cheap.

Related shape: fisc-8ln, and the map-read-with-no-ok-check that docs/review-loop-evidence.md records leaving a wrong-column guard unable to fail.

title: fund/100's column share now has the residual in its denominator: is 'of this column' the right whole?
description: Since fisc-ko1j.5 the General Fund's opened view draws residual/fund-group/general beside fund/100 in the fund column, so fund/100's tooltip carries a share where columnShare used to suppress it for a column of one: measured, 'our 91.5% of this column' in FY2026 adopted (fund/100 157,873,470 against a column total that includes the residual node sized by d3-sankey at max(in, out) = 14,737,222). The chip is arithmetic over what is drawn and says 'of this column', so it is not false; the question is whether a derived non-fund mark belongs in the whole a printed fund is expressed as a share of, and whether a reader takes 'this column' to mean the funds. Options: exclude isResidual nodes from columnShare's total and say 'of the funds'; keep and say nothing; or drop the chip on a column whose only other mark is derived. tools/jscheck/drill.mjs's tooltip arm pins sharesColumn: true for the General Fund at depth 1 and needs re-pinning with whichever is chosen. notes:
2026-09-11, /code-review lens 3 over 0923016..HEAD: THE BEAD NAMES fund/100 AND THE EFFECT IS WIDER. The residual sits in the fund column (tier 3) for every group that draws one, so columnShare (site/app.js:2703, which sums laidNodes by layer) puts the group-wide draw in the denominator of EVERY fund in that column, not only the General Fund's one-fund column.

  capital           FY2026  8.4%   FY2027 27.4%
  internal-service  FY2026 24.5%   FY2027 26.4%
  general           FY2026  8.5%   FY2027  8.8%

2026-09-11, /code-review PASS TWO lens B: the dilution is in the OTHER TWO COLUMNS as well, and the answer chosen has to cover them.

  left (revenue) column   carried share  0.95% FY2026 / 0.30% FY2027

HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM THE FUND COLUMN, and why lens B flagged it at lower confidence: those are real printed OUTFLOWS of the group, not the max(in, out) sizing that puts the residual in the fund column's denominator. title: The hover-and-tab sentence is above the chart on two pages and below it on a third
description:

WHY IT IS NOT A COPY-PASTE FIX. chart.html.tmpl's version is conditional on {{if .Drill}} and shares its with #chart-hint, which app.js's paintChartHint REPAINTS on a drill -- the sentence a reader sees in an opened view is not the one the template shipped. index.html.tmpl's is unconditional and nothing repaints it. So moving the chart pages' copy means deciding what happens to the repainted text and where paintChartHint writes it, which is a client change and needs a jscheck arm. THE OTHER HALF OF THE DECISION, and it may be the right answer: leave chart.html.tmpl alone and move index's copy BACK into the legend key. The legend is the chart's own furniture rather than prose about it, which is the reason the two mark swatches stayed above the chart in that lane. If that is the call, index's

goes away and the argument for it in the comment above the card goes with it. EITHER WAY, ONE OF THE TWO PAGES CHANGES. What must not persist is the current state, where one sentence sits on opposite sides of the figure depending on which page a reader is on.

THE STATE THIS BEAD REFUSED TO LET PERSIST CANNOT. It named one sentence sitting on opposite sides of the figure depending on which page a reader is on -- index.html.tmpl below the chart, chart.html.tmpl inside the legend key above it. chart.html.tmpl is deleted (fisc-1osz, 2026-09-20) and 'Hover, tap or tab' now appears in exactly one template, measured: git grep -l over site/*.tmpl returns index.html.tmpl alone.

That question stands on its own merits and blocks nobody; the reason it was urgent -- two pages disagreeing -- is gone. Re-file it as a design bead if the placement is still wrong to the eye, rather than inheriting the urgency of a contradiction that no longer exists. title: The print stylesheet's disclosure rules are unverifiable here and need a browser
description:
fisc-yj4w.14 folded five sections behind <details> on every page, which took them off a printed copy: @media print did not open them, so a print or PDF of any page silently lost its sources, its caveats, the derived list, the flow table and index.html's tile row. The same print block already argues the other way about the WIP banner -- "a printed copy is exactly the artefact that outlives the caveat" -- so the fold contradicted a rule the file states about itself.

FIXED IN THAT LANE by adding two rules to @media print, and this bead is what CANNOT be checked about them.

TWO MECHANISMS BECAUSE ENGINES USE TWO, and the fix carries both:
  - a UA display:none on the non-summary children, overridden with display:block
  - a ::details-content slot hidden with content-visibility, overridden with content-visibility:visible

NEITHER OVERRIDE IS WITNESSED BY ANYTHING IN THIS TREE. Nothing here parses or renders CSS (fisc-6at): tools/jscheck reads style.css only to harvest custom-property names, and the Go tests that touch it match selector strings. So a test can say the rules are DECLARED and nothing more. Whether a folded panel actually prints is confirmed in a browser's print preview and nowhere else.

WHAT TO DO: open each page's print preview in a Chromium engine and in Firefox, with the disclosures closed, and confirm the folded content is on the sheet. If it is not, the rule that failed is the one to replace -- not both.

WHY IT IS A BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE: the failure mode is silent and asymmetric. A reader who prints gets a page that looks complete and is missing its caveats, which is the one omission this project treats as a defect however good the rest looks.

title: The sources footer is five copies of one claim
description:
index.html.tmpl, chart.html.tmpl, trends.html.tmpl, history.html.tmpl and provenance.html.tmpl each carry a near-identical footer: an

Sources...

, a
    with two links per cited page composed the same way in all five, and a .subtle paragraph naming every projection file. fisc-yj4w.14 wrapped all five in a closed
    -- five copies of one mechanical edit -- rather than factoring them, and this is that debt written down. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE THERE, measured rather than assumed: - renderPage (internal/export/page.go:1455) does template.New(name).ParseFS(assets, name) -- ONE file. A {{template "sources"}} partial needs a second name threaded through, plus site/embed.go. - AND THE DATA SHAPES DISAGREE, which is the real obstacle: index.html.tmpl and trends/history render {{.Scope}} (singular), chart.html.tmpl renders {{range .Scopes}} with a pluralised label because that document carries two disjoint schedules, and provenance.html.tmpl renders neither. A partial means one shape for five view types. So this is a refactor of five view types, not a template extraction, and it is the class of change that generates review findings. It is filed rather than bundled. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: the .subtle scope/basis paragraph deliberately stays OUTSIDE the disclosure on every page -- with #page-basis and [data-year-path] it states which document is on screen, and a reader must not have to open something to learn which fiscal year they are reading. A partial must keep that split.
notes:
2026-09-08, from fisc-yj4w.14: this bead now has a measurement behind it rather than just an argument. THE FIVE COPIES COST A REVIEW FINDING EACH TIME THEY DIVERGED, twice in one lane: - the footer summary counted documents only, after the fold swept the data-file list in beside the sources, on all five pages at once - the

Sources

position was asserted on two RENDERED pages while five templates carry the same footer; measured, moving the heading past in chart, provenance and history at once left the package green The second is fixed in a way that helps whoever takes this bead: TestEveryFooterDisclosureKeepsItsHeadingInTheOutline reads site.FS() and walks EVERY template that folds a footer list, with a count arm asserting it found six. A partial has to keep that test passing, which is a cheaper acceptance criterion than re-deriving what the footers must do. THE OBSTACLE IS UNCHANGED and is still the data shapes, not the template extraction: index and trends/history render {{.Scope}}, chart.html.tmpl renders {{range .Scopes}} with a pluralised label, provenance renders neither, and caveats.html has no source list at all -- its disclosure is #data-view and holds only the file list, which a partial must not paper over. 2026-09-08: SHRINKS FROM FIVE COPIES TO THREE if fisc-ko1j.4 lands -- revenue.html and spending.html are deleted, and with them site/chart.html.tmpl, which is the one template rendering {{range .Scopes}} rather than {{.Scope}}. That is the data-shape difference this bead names as the actual blocker, so the merge removes it rather than working around it. Worth waiting for rather than solving twice. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-20 AFTER fisc-1osz, AND THE REFACTOR GOT SMALLER IN BOTH DIMENSIONS. It is FOUR copies, not five -- chart.html.tmpl is deleted, so index.html.tmpl, trends.html.tmpl, history.html.tmpl and provenance.html.tmpl carry the footer (git grep -l 'Sources' over site/*.tmpl). AND THE OBSTACLE THIS BEAD CALLED THE REAL ONE IS GONE. It said the data shapes disagree three ways: {{.Scope}} singular on index and trends/history, {{range .Scopes}} pluralised on chart.html.tmpl 'because that document carries two disjoint schedules', and neither on provenance. Measured now: NOTHING renders .Scopes -- zero hits over site/*.tmpl -- so the four remaining templates are two shapes, three rendering {{.Scope}} and provenance rendering none. A partial over two shapes is a different proposition from one over three. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: renderPage still does template.New(name).ParseFS(assets, name) on ONE file, so a {{template "sources"}} partial still needs a second name threaded through it and through site/embed.go. And the note for whoever takes it stands -- the .subtle scope/basis paragraph stays OUTSIDE the disclosure on every page, because a reader must not have to open something to learn which fiscal year they are reading.

title: year.mjs composes the drawn counts tail as a literal: the checker holds a copy of app.js's only wording for it
description:
dab61bc added the drawn-state counts arm to tools/jscheck/year.mjs -- the state every shipped page is in after its first draw, and the one no counts check reached, which is why a check named for an agreement that is false as published stayed green.

THE HALF THAT IS HONEST. The sentence's HEAD is read out of each shipped template by headOf(), so rewording "flows between" or "nodes" in either template reddens the arm. Both templates' heads are also held equal to each other.

THE HALF THAT IS A COPY. The TAIL -- " of the document's N facts" -- is composed as a literal in the checker (tools/jscheck/year.mjs, in the drawn-state arm). No template renders it: paintCounts in site/app.js is the only place those words exist, because the tail depends on which ribbons a fold or drill actually drew, which the packager cannot foresee. So the checker holds the only other copy of a wording app.js owns.

WHY THAT IS THE THING THIS SUITE EXISTS TO REFUSE. AGENTS.md, "The node boundary": jscheck reaches into the shipped app.js rather than copying functions out of it, because a copy would check the copy and let the original drift. The tail is exactly that -- reword paintCounts's tail and app.js and the checker disagree, which the arm catches, but reword BOTH and nothing does. tools/jscheck/fold.mjs pins whole drawn sentences the same way, so this is the established habit rather than a new lapse; it is written down here because it was disclosed at the time and then owned by nothing.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT. Either the packager renders the drawn tail's wording into the document as data the client formats -- which makes it the packager's string, the shape fisc-rn0 and fisc-m1uu both took for the title and the head -- or the gap is accepted and stated where a reader of the check would see it. The arm already throws when the fixture's fact total equals its cited count, so it cannot silently pin the wrong branch; that guard is worth keeping under either answer.

fisc-rx1d carries the audit of which of app.js's paths no module drives, and is the neighbour of this.

title: doccheck declares three shapes out of reach of both citation arms, and none names a bead
description:
f57cf8e rewrote what doccheck treats as a near-miss citation: the quoted title must now RESOLVE against the AGENTS.md anchors. That removed the false-positive class three consecutive review passes had found, and bought it with coverage that is declared in the package comment and in loosePattern's -- but declared with no bead, so nothing carries the question forward.

THE THREE SHAPES, as tools/doccheck/main.go states them:

1. Prose that names a section without quoting it. Out of reach of both arms by construction; the gate reads quoted titles.
2. A malformed citation of a section that has since been RENAMED AWAY. The canonical arm never matches it and the loose arm no longer resolves it, so it passes in silence. This is the one with a real cost: it is exactly the failure doccheck was built for -- a pointer at a heading that is gone -- and it now escapes whenever the citation's form is also wrong.
3. A near-MISSPELLING of a section title. The net catches a near-separator of a real title, never a near-misspelling of one.

Shape 2 is the one to weigh. A fold-and-compare against the anchor set at an edit distance of one or two would catch both 2 and 3, at the cost of a rule that is no longer exact -- and this project has refused fuzzy matching elsewhere for good reasons. The alternative is to accept the gap and say so where a reader of the gate's output would see it, not only in the source.

Also declared in the same comment and not separately owned: a near-miss whose separator itself contains a full sentence escapes, as does one whose sentence ends in ? or ! -- shapes no separator in this tree has taken, which is a measurement that will go stale.

NOT URGENT. The gate is stricter than it was on every shape a reader has actually written. This exists so the exchange is re-decidable rather than inherited.

title: history.html announces the excess phrase three times in a row, in three capitalisations
description: Found by /code-review over main..HEAD on e12-claims (pass 2 of the loop). Not fixed in that pass: it is a DESIGN choice about what the Line cell is for, not a wrong figure. WHAT A SCREEN READER SAYS. Measured off `make site` at 0fe6e67, dist/history.html around the excess row: Excess of revenues over (under) expenditures Excess of Revenues over (under) expenditures Excess of Revenues over (under) Expenditures Three consecutive announcements of one phrase, differing only in capitalisation. A sighted reader skims past the repetition; a screen-reader user hears the same sentence three times before reaching a number. WHERE EACH COMES FROM. adb48b2 gave a section the ability to close itself on a named row and made the excess row's Line cell say the whole printed phrase rather than the wrapped tail `over (under) expenditures` -- which was the right fix for the finding it answered (the Line cell was printing a fragment of a three-line wrapped label as though it were a label). The colgroup heading and the row header already carried the phrase; making the third one whole is what stacked them. The capitalisations are the documents' own -- pp.168-169 print the label across three lines and the case differs between the block head and the row -- so 'normalise the case' is the wrong move: these are printed strings, and this project publishes what the page prints (AGENTS.md, "Provenance invariants"). THE QUESTION TO ANSWER. When a section's own heading already says what the row says, what is the Line cell for? Options worth weighing: drop the Line cell on a row whose section closes on it; keep the cell and hide the redundant heading from the accessibility tree; or keep all three and say why. Whichever is chosen needs a check -- a page can regain the triple the next time a section learns to close on a row.

title: A cheap-model fleet for the deletion-class comment work, and why it must not be a rewrite
description:
PROPOSED 2026-09-06 by the owner, from a backlog characterization session. Not
scoped, not costed beyond what fisc-b93j already measured. This is the METHOD for
the deletion-class comment work, which is why it is filed apart from fisc-a3rp
(class A) and from the class C internal/inline work: the argument below applies
to both and would be buried inside either.

THE PROPOSAL. Orchestrate a fleet of cheap-model agents (Sonnet was the one
named) over comment blocks one unit at a time, each agent given the block, the
code it sits on, and the written rules -- nothing else. Take the proposed change
when it is reasonable rather than iterating toward a perfect comment, on the
grounds that the comments being replaced are already flawed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH KEEPING RATHER THAN RE-DERIVING. The quality half of it is
already settled in this repo's favour and the owner should not have to re-argue
it: fisc-b93j records that Fable, given only the rules and the original text of
internal/geom, produced ZERO new false claims, found and corrected a planted one
unaided, and stopped at -11% against an independent oracle's -14% ceiling.
A context-free agent CAN propose a sound replacement comment.

WHY IT MUST BE POINTED AT DELETION, NOT REWRITE. fisc-b93j closed NO on
economics, not on quality: 42.5 minutes and 411k subagent tokens for one 148-line
unit, extrapolating to ~90 hours and ~52M tokens over 18,718 in-scope comment
lines, and the unit GREW +18%. Swapping in a cheaper model does not fix that,
because the cost is the adversarial verification pass, which a weaker rewriter
needs MORE of, not less. That pass earned its place -- 77 claims attacked, 68
survived, 3 refuted, one of the three introduced by the rewrite itself.

So the saving is not "aim lower while rewriting". It is fisc-b93j's structural
lesson: VERIFICATION COST ATTACHES TO CLAIMS WRITTEN OR KEPT, AND A DELETION
CANNOT INTRODUCE A FALSE CLAIM. Deletion is roughly a tenth of the price and
needs no adversary. Loosening the bar on a REWRITE trades comments that are
known-flawed and filed as beads for comments that are unknown-flawed, which is
the wrong direction for this repo.

Cheap models fit deletion for the same reason: the output is "drop these lines"
and the gate is a diff that only removes.

THREE CONSTRAINTS, all already measured elsewhere and repeated here only as the
shape of the brief:
  - Not grep-and-delete, per fisc-a3rp: keep the rule, drop the history that
    argued for it, judged per block. Every mutation proof stays.
  - Needs go/ast, not a textual filter: fisc-a3rp names 13 lines inside raw
    string literals that look exactly like comments.
  - tools/codehash is the gate. It exists on main already, from fisc-b93j's
    abandoned campaign, and proves no code token changed.

SEQUENCING, so this does not run on text that is about to vanish. fisc-ynuo
measured 958 doc-comment lines sitting on 356 genuine unexport candidates -- 8%
of production comment prose that unexporting deletes or shrinks. Do not point
this at exported identifiers before that lands. fisc-owo4 is deferred on the same
logic. The one additive direction, fisc-mwne, is not this bead's method and
should not be folded into it.

PRIOR ART LEFT ON DISK: branch comment-sweep, three commits (71fd344, 76fec71,
123eca1), abandoned unmerged and cherry-pickable.
acceptance_criteria: either a scoped deletion-only pass over one unit with codehash green and its cost measured against fisc-b93j's 411k-per-148-lines baseline, or a recorded decision not to run it

title: validateRule accepts skip+quantity on one row and a dead category on a quantity row
description:
HYGIENE found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD.

internal/mapping/parse.go refuses quantity+counterpart on a row and quantity-column+total_row, but accepts two contradictory co-declarations:

- `{label: X, skip: true, quantity: percentage}` -- parseRow (internal/mapping/resolve.go) consults quantity before skip and continues on a non-amount quantity, so quantity wins and the skip is inert ink. Two claims about one cell, one of them unchecked.
- a category on a quantity row -- the category arm only REQUIRES one when quantity is empty, never refuses one, so it sits as dead metadata on a row that publishes no fact for it to classify.

No committed rule does either; both are validation gaps, not defects in the store.

Adjacent to fisc-1wix (the schema forces a kind on all-skip rules) but distinct: that one is a required field that cannot be true, these are optional fields that are accepted while meaning nothing. Consider landing them together, with the same mutation shape -- add the co-declaration to a rule, watch validateRule stay green, add the arm, watch it go red.

title: amountRun's comment claims dropCurrencyMarks fails any mark with no figure after it; only a trailing or doubled mark fails
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD, verified by reading the code this session.

internal/mapping/resolve.go, the amountRun doc comment: "A mark with no figure after it fails the whole line, closed, through dropCurrencyMarks' own refusal."

dropCurrencyMarks refuses on exactly two shapes: the mark is the last token, or the next token is another mark (`if i+1 >= len(toks) || isCurrencyMark(toks[i+1].text)`). A mark followed by a WORD is dropped silently and the line proceeds. So "$ 1,061,355 $ Total" reads as a 1-wide run with ok=true, and the whole line did not fail.

Not FAIL-OPEN, measured: the following word still breaks the run in amountRun and still breaks amount.Parse in labelledValues, and both call sites feed comparisons (CheckTotals, rollups) rather than published facts -- a misread total fails its tie rather than shipping. This is the comment claiming a broader refusal than the code makes.

The same sentence is repeated as a comment in internal/mapping/resolve_test.go above TestDetachedCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunIsReadable's second assertion, which asserts only the TRAILING-mark case -- the case the code does refuse. Whichever way this lands, the test comment and the doc comment must say the same thing, and it must be what dropCurrencyMarks does.

dropCurrencyMarks' own doc comment and its error text ("is a currency mark with no figure after it") carry the same overstatement and predate this range.

Fix direction: either narrow both comments to "a mark that ends the line, or is followed by another mark", or widen the refusal to any mark not followed by a parseable amount -- the second is a behaviour change and needs its own mutation proof and a corpus scan first.

title: The history pages claim the tallest bar is a row's largest number; buildMark scales by magnitude
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD, verified on the shipped page.

site/history.html.tmpl: "the tallest bar in every row is that row's largest number". buildMark scales each row by the largest MAGNITUDE (abs64, internal/export/page.go), so in a row whose non-zero figures are all negative, the tallest bar is the row's SMALLEST number.

Proven on balances.html as rendered: All Other Governmental Funds / Unassigned prints $0, (157,775), (66,518), (337,703), four zeros, (454,071), $0. The tallest bar in that row is -$454,071 -- the row's smallest number -- and $0, its largest, renders as dots.

The sentence's next clause describes hanging bars, so the page already tells the reader negatives hang; only the superlative is wrong. One word ("largest magnitude") closes it.

The same sentence pre-exists on site/trends.html.tmpl:56, outside this range, and is wrong there for any all-negative row too. Fix both together, and regenerate the goldens: a template edit moves them, so read the golden diff by eye before re-reviewing (AGENTS.md, "Review is a loop, not a pass" -- there is deliberately no -update flag).
notes:
Premise re-derived against the tree before working it (AGENTS.md, "A bead's text is a claim, not a fact"): the description's 'regenerate the goldens: a template edit moves them' is wrong. Measured this session: testdata/ holds only sankey.golden.json and fund-flows.golden.json, both projection JSON documents; neither is produced from history.html.tmpl or trends.html.tmpl, dist/ is gitignored, and no test compares rendered HTML to a golden. The template edit moved no golden and there was none to regenerate. The rest of the description held: buildMark scales by abs64, and the shipped Unassigned row's tallest bar is its -$454,071 while its largest number, $0, draws as a dot.
2026-09-19, released. Re-derived: the defect is live and untouched -- internal/export/page.go:2620 and :2680 still scale the bar by abs64, so the tallest bar is the largest magnitude and not the largest number. The existing note corrected the description's golden-regeneration premise only; no fix landed.

title: Two Statistical Section tie measurements are recorded wrong: the ties also hold in 2020 and 2022, not 2017 only
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review over 6ad828f^..3286b77 (the E12 range).

Measured off the extracted pages this session, both 'dead tie' records in the survey and the contract understate the matches:

- docs/acfr-statistical-section.md ('p167 deltas vs p169's Net change: ties 2017 only') and docs/acfr-history-contract.md ('match p169's Net change in 2017 only'): measured, p167's combined year-over-year total deltas equal p169's printed Net change in 2017 (17,414,645), 2020 (4,868,219) AND 2022 (-16,975,824). The parentheticals (2018 off 190,263, 2025 off 2,667) are correct.
- docs/acfr-statistical-section.md ('p163 year-over-year deltas do not equal p166's Change in Net Position except 2017'): measured, governmental deltas also equal the printed change in 2020 (8,304,751) and 2022 (10,611,708). The quoted off-figures for 2018, 2024, 2025 are all correct.

The commit message of 6ad828f repeats the error ('both of batch one's planned corroboration ties hold for 2017 only'). The CONCLUSION stands: 3 of 9 columns is dead as a corroboration guard, and 2022's p166 match sits beside the 2023-copies-2022 defect. Only the counts need correcting, in both files in one commit, reading each copy (they state slightly different propositions).
close_reason: Corrected in docs/acfr-statistical-section.md (both bullets) and docs/acfr-history-contract.md. Re-measured this session off data/extracted/livermore-acfr-fy2025/pages/: p167 combined deltas equal p169's printed Net change in 2017 (17,414,645), 2020 (4,868,219) and 2022 (-16,975,824); p163 governmental deltas equal p166's printed Change in Net Position in 2017 (15,880,225), 2020 (8,304,751) and 2022 (10,611,708). All five off-figures already in the docs re-verified correct. Both files now say 3 of 9 comparable years and both record that 2022 is the column p166/p169 copy into 2023, so the tie carries no independent corroboration. 6ad828f's commit message keeps the wrong figure; it is history and is not rewritten.

title: ACFR pp.164-166 Changes in Net Position is defective as printed: a year-shifted totals row and copied 2023 cells
description:
DROPPED FROM fisc-oakx.3's BATCH. Measured for the survey (docs/acfr-statistical-section.md) and re-affirmed at lane 3: p164's 'Total business-type activities expenses' row is RIGHT-SHIFTED one year for 2017-2023 (each printed total equals the previous year's column sum; the true 2023 sum, 51,821,693, is printed nowhere); p165's Net (Expense) Revenue Governmental 2023 and p166's Change in Net Position Governmental 2023 are copies of their 2022 cells, with each page's totals internally consistent with the copies.

THE RULED-OUT EXIT, so it is not retried: stated_total_deltas is fisc-2sd's mechanism for the city's own <=$5 rounding, and a totals row a whole year out of position is not a rounding delta -- a delta sized to it would be fiction (Rule.TotalSpansParts' doc comment names the hazard). Either the rules declare no total over the affected columns and something else guards them, or the table waits. Also blocked by fisc-7jtl for the same reason as p163: change in net position is not a fund_balance. Mapping this table means deciding how a printed defect this large is published without being laundered.

title: ACFR p169's Other Financing block is read and unpublished: its 2023 total and Net change are copies of 2022
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 while landing fisc-oakx.3 (rule acfr-p0169-other-financing, scope acfr-changes-in-fund-balances). The block reads whole and every row is skip: true, because neither guard it would need is honest as printed:

(1) The printed 'Total other financing sources (uses)' ties to its six components in NINE of ten columns and its 2023 cell prints (1,767,367), a copy of 2022 -- the components sum to 39,259,064 (41,558,955 bond proceeds + 6,672,696 transfers in - 8,972,587 transfers out). A total_row fails on that column, and a stated_total_deltas entry sized to a copied cell would be the fabricated declaration Rule.TotalSpansParts' doc comment names.

(2) 'Net change in fund balances' 2023 prints (16,975,824), the same copy (excess 21,438,989 + true OFS 39,259,064 = 60,698,053; excess + PRINTED OFS = 19,671,622; neither is what is printed). Publishing it as fund-balance/change also trips fund-balance-identity's completeness arm: the scope publishes no beginning or ending line.

WHAT PUBLICATION WOULD TAKE: a decision on publishing a block whose own printed total is defective in one column (the transfers in/out and debt-proceeds rows are clean in themselves), and an honest home for the net-change line. The percentage row stays read-only regardless (quantity: percentage, the row channel's real-page consumer).
notes: Review pass two (2026-09-06, fable over main..HEAD) measured a blind spot to know about BEFORE publishing this block: excess-of-revenues-identity's switch silently ignores in-scope facts whose kind is neither revenue nor expenditure nor the excess line. None exist today (measured: 22 facts per year = 9 revenue + 12 expenditure + 1 excess). If this bead publishes p169's transfer legs or bond proceeds into acfr-changes-in-fund-balances, they will pass through that check unseen rather than being refused. Adjacent to fisc-s9c2, which is the same shape one layer up: buildHistoryPage's section key would place a new fund_balance series under the Excess heading with no refusal.

title: Nothing can refuse a per-unit column declared as amount; the corroboration that could is a cross-tie to p180
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 for fisc-oakx.2's third proof obligation. ACFR p177 col 10, Per Capita, prints well-formed grouped dollars ('$ 1,009', '922', '713'): amount.Parse accepts every one, so deleting its quantity: amount_per_unit declaration and letting it parse as money produces no error anywhere — the resolution succeeds, and internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go pins exactly that (TestACFRDebtPerCapitaParsesCleanlyAsAmount). The declaration in the rule file is the only gate, which is fisc-9tn4's finding restated: no grammar, no arithmetic and no structural check can tell dollars-per-capita from dollars.

WHAT WOULD REFUSE IT, when publication exists (blocked today by fisc-xmh2 and fisc-7jtl): a cross-table corroboration in internal/check. p177's per-capita column times p180's population column reproduces p177's col 8 total (survey: 'per capita ties to p180 population'), and its percentage column times p180's personal income does the same — a $1,009 filed as a city total would miss those identities by five orders of magnitude. Until both pages publish, there is nothing to corroborate against and the declaration stands alone.

title: doccheck does not check the docs/ paths that comments now point at
description:
The AGENTS.md split re-pointed five source comments at docs/ files by path (docs/extraction-substrate.md, docs/review-loop-evidence.md). Those paths are claims about the tree exactly as a bead id or a section name is, and nothing checks them: renaming or deleting an evidence file leaves the pointers dead and every gate green.

Arm C of fisc-ak39 was specified for this -- a declared evidenceDocs map, each file existing, each opening with its 'Evidence for AGENTS.md, "<section>"' marker naming a real section, and AGENTS.md linking it exactly once -- and it has not been written. This bead is the narrower half that matters first: a docs/*.md path cited from source or from AGENTS.md must resolve.

Verified by hand at the time of filing: all seven docs/ paths cited from source resolve, and all six linked from AGENTS.md resolve. That is a measurement, not a guarantee, which is the point.
close_reason: Superseded by fisc-08ee (P2, open, filed 2026-09-18), which is the same gate stated over the whole tree: refuse a comment or doc that cites a source path the tree does not have. That bead carries the measurement this one lacked -- 29 repo-shaped paths named in tracked prose that do not exist, five of them real and fixed at 806231f. Closing here so one bead owns the gate.

title: beadrefs drops a bead id carrying a second hyphen, and nothing guards the assumption that none exists
description:
citedIn (tools/beadrefs/main.go) REFUSES A MATCH FOLLOWED BY A HYPHEN, because
`fisc-` is an overloaded prefix in this tree rather than a namespace: fact ids
are fisc-f-<hash> and series ids are fisc-s-<hash>, and the second hyphen is what
tells them from a bead id. Twelve real lines that produced false findings on the
first run are pinned as its test.

THE ASSUMPTION IT RESTS ON IS THAT A BEAD ID HAS ONE HYPHEN. Measured at the time
of filing: all 433 ids in .beads/issues.jsonl are `fisc-<token>` with optional
dotted children, so nothing is wrong today. But bd chooses the token and this
repo does not, and an id like `fisc-drill-down` would be SILENTLY DROPPED -- not
reported, not resolved, just never seen. That is the failure mode the gate
exists to prevent, in the gate.

WHAT WOULD CATCH IT, and it is cheap because knownIDs is already read: assert at
startup that every id in the export is one citedIn would recognise, and fail if
any is not. The check then goes red the first time bd mints such an id, in the
run that would otherwise have started ignoring it -- rather than at some later
point when a citation to it is invented and nobody notices.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. It is latent, the pass that found it was the
fifth and at the cap, and the fix is a new startup check with its own test rather
than a line in a file already being touched.

Found by /code-review over 0158bf6^..916c23e.

title: memcheck's two shape patterns can refuse a true ALL-CAPS or dated sentence about the corpus
description:
THREE OF memcheck'S FIVE PATTERNS NAME THE MEMORY AS THEIR SUBJECT and are safe
on that ground. TWO DO NOT:

  (?i)\bcorrected\s+20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d
  (?m)^CORRECTED\b

Both are house-STYLE forms rather than sentences whose subject is provably the
memory, so each can refuse a true sentence about the documents. The line-leading
one is the likelier: the bodies are hard-wrapped, ALL-CAPS lead words are the
house register, and a true sentence containing CORRECTED needs only to wrap so
that word lands at a line start. Measured on the live set at the time of filing:
17 of 322 memory lines begin with an ALL-CAPS word, so the shape is common; what
is not measured is whether any true sentence would ever use that particular word.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY WITHDRAWN, which is what happened to a third shape pattern
in the same lane. `\(correction[,:]` was withdrawn because it refused a real
parenthetical about a reprinted ACFR figure AND no memory carried the form it was
aimed at -- both halves. These two fail only the first half: the dated form is
the one the compaction lane actually found in the memories, over and over.
Withdrawing them would take out the pattern that catches the observed defect to
avoid a false positive nobody has hit.

THE COST IF IT FIRES. There is no allowlist, no flag and no exemption, and this
runs inside `make pre-commit`, so a false refusal blocks the commit until someone
reads the code. That is the same cost the withdrawn pattern would have had.

WHAT A FIX WOULD LOOK LIKE. An exemption predicate -- a memory declaring the
line, the way internal/check/vacuity.go declares a vacuous check -- rather than a
