looser pattern, because a pattern loose enough to admit the true sentence is
loose enough to admit the erratum. The exemption must name the memory and go
stale loudly if that memory stops carrying the line.

NOT MEASURED: whether any true sentence in the corpus, present or plausible,
takes either shape. Filed at the five-pass cap, with no false positive observed.

Found by /code-review over b2e67aa^..22ba3be.

title: memcheck's nested-value refusal has no escape hatch if bd's JSON shape changes
description:
tools/memcheck REFUSES ANY TOP-LEVEL OBJECT OR ARRAY in `bd memories --json`,
and exits 2 when it finds one. That is deliberate and it is the fix for a real
fail-open: an envelope moving the bodies down a level
({"schema_version":1,"memories":{...}}) passed the count rule as long as one
stray top-level string sat beside it.

THE RESIDUE. bd is not pinned in this repo, `make narration` is not a CI job, and
the Makefile's skip arm keys only off bd's EXIT STATUS. So a bd upgrade that adds
one structured top-level field to that command -- a nested `config`, a
`by_project` map, anything -- turns `make pre-commit` red for everyone at once,
with no CI run having caught it first and no flag to get past it. The remedy
would be to edit memcheck, which is correct but is a stop-the-world event rather
than a warning.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. The alternative is accepting a shape the tool
cannot read, which is the fail-open it was written to close, and AGENTS.md's
"fail closed on ambiguity" says which way to err. The cost is a hard failure on a
change nobody made deliberately, which is a real cost and not a hypothetical one:
the block is regenerated by bd and the memories arrive through bd, so bd's output
format is an external dependency this repo does not control.

WHAT A FIX WOULD LOOK LIKE, if one is wanted: refuse only a nested value whose
CONTENTS look like bodies (a map of string to string), and skip any other
structured field the way scalars are skipped. That keeps the envelope refusal and
lets an unrelated new field through. It needs a test proving the envelope is
still caught, because a predicate loose enough to admit new fields is loose
enough to admit the envelope.

Found by /code-review over b2e67aa^..16c3c5d.

title: Drop the 23 generic Go/byob memories, or keep them deliberately
description:
TWENTY-THREE OF THE 49 INJECTED MEMORIES ARE GENERIC GO IDIOMS WITH NO PROJECT
CONTENT: receiver-name, got-want-order, errors-is-as, errors-wrap-w,
errors-message-style, defer-unlock, context-first-param, doc-comment-shape,
blank-ident-assert, goroutine-exit-path, initialism-casing, no-get-prefix,
no-blank-error-discard, pass-by-value-default, principles-dry-kiss-solid,
prompter-tty-check, quote-strings-in-errors, sync-oncevalue, test-cleanup,
test-helper, validate-at-boundaries, atomic-rename-samedir (first paragraph
only), decisions-lookup.

MEASURED 2026-09-05, before the fisc-kc3j compaction: ~1,400 of 7,628 words,
about 18% of what bd prime injects. After it, the same 23 are a LARGER share,
because the compaction only touched the project memories.

THE ARGUMENT FOR DROPPING THEM. byob is their source of truth and it is already
in the same database -- AGENTS.md says to read the decisions with
`bd show byob-<id>` rather than infer them from the code, and `bd list
--type=byob --no-parent` browses them on demand. A memory is the wrong channel
for a rule nobody needs in context until they are writing the code it governs,
because injection is unconditional and browsing is not.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST. Injection is exactly what makes an idiom get followed;
a decision you have to go and look up is one a session will not look up. Nothing
here has been measured either way, and a wrong call costs the idioms rather than
tokens.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE. The owner ruled it out of scope for fisc-kc3j
on 2026-09-05, on the grounds that that bead says in as many words "WHAT IT IS
NOT: a cull". This is the same finding, filed so the decision has somewhere to
live that is not a paragraph in a session summary.

If the answer is keep, close this with that as the reason rather than deleting
it -- the next session to measure the injected token count will otherwise find
the same 18% and re-derive the same question.

title: p140's unassertable rollup total is locatable by nothing, so republishing it is unrefusable
description:
FOUND while wiring rollups into fact-offset-is-not-a-stated-total on the third
review pass of the fisc-eaic lane. Measured 2026-09-05: of the 14 declared
rollups, 13 resolve a span and ONE does not.

  other-funds-total-sources, p140, covers: [], unassertable:
    "p140 prints this as the closing line of pp.131-140 and no rule structure
     here can assert it. It exceeds the 69 printed fund totals it closes by
     58,773,547 / 58,836,449 / 56,492,834 / 57,373,508 -- a different amount in
     every column, so neither rounding nor one omitted fund."

WHY IT IS SKIPPED AND WHY THAT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY WRONG. Resolver.RollupTotalSpan
returns ErrNoStatedTotals for a rollup covering no rule, because the width it
passes to rollupStatedTotals comes from the first covered rule's bearer part.
With no covers there is no column count, and without one there is no way to say
which run of tokens on the line IS the total.

WHAT IS LEFT OPEN. p140 prints a real citywide total and a fact republishing one
of its four figures as a row would be refused by nothing:
fact-offset-points-at-token is satisfied (the token IS printed there),
fact-citations-are-declared sees no second fact at the address, and this check
contributes no span. It is the same hazard fisc-eaic named, on the one printed
total in the corpus that no rule structure reaches.

THE OPTIONS:
  (a) LET AN UNASSERTABLE ROLLUP DECLARE ITS WIDTH, so the span is locatable even
      though the sum is not. Small, and it separates "we cannot check this
      figure" from "we cannot even find it" -- which are different claims that
      the unassertable field currently conflates.
  (b) TAKE THE WIDTH FROM THE PAGE: the longest run of parsable amounts on the
      anchored line. Needs no declaration and is a guess, which is the shape this
      project refuses.
  (c) LEAVE IT, and say so where a reader would look -- the rollup's own
      unassertable string, which fisc verify does not print, or the check's
      summary, which it does.

RECOMMENDATION (a), then (c) as the note that goes with it. (b) is out: guessing
a column count to locate a total is how a wrong figure gets a provenance link.

NOT URGENT. It is one line on one page, no rule maps pp.131-140's closing total,
and the four figures it prints are already known not to reconcile to anything --
which is why it is unassertable in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: either an unassertable rollup can declare the width that makes its printed total locatable, and fact-offset-is-not-a-stated-total covers p140's closing line; or the gap is recorded where fisc verify prints it

title: The label-less widening in fact-offset-is-not-a-stated-total has no witness in the committed corpus
description:
FOUND BY /code-review over 3666326^..cac087f, the second pass over the
correctness lane, and filed because the arm it names has no witness.

THE ARM. factOffsetIsNotAStatedTotal.Run iterates EVERY rule and EVERY part
rather than only the rules declaring a total_row, because
mapping.(*Resolver).totalAnchor tests LabelsFrom BEFORE it tests TotalRow: a
label-less part's stated total is wherever its block ends, via stop_at, whether
or not its rule declares one.

NO COMMITTED PART EXERCISES IT. Measured 2026-09-05, after
Resolver.TotalRowSpan was fixed to require an actual totals run:

  - 5 parts are label-less.
  - 2 of them, spine-revenues and spine-expenditures on p67, resolve a real
    stated total -- and they also DECLARE a total_row, so the narrow filter
    would have reached them anyway.
  - The other 3 -- spine-transfers-in, spine-transfers-out, spine-fund-balance
    -- declare no total_row, and their p67 anchor is the block TERMINATOR: the
    fund-group header line for the first, and the running footer "BUDGET FY
    2025-27 Page 63" for the other two. Neither prints a totals run, so
    TotalRowSpan correctly refuses all three and they contribute no span.

So the widening is correct in principle and guards nothing measurable. That is
precisely the shape this project files beads about: an arm a reader would count
as a guard, with nothing standing behind it.

WHY IT WAS KEPT RATHER THAN REVERTED. Narrowing it back to `rule.TotalRow != ""`
would reintroduce the LabelsFrom-before-TotalRow trap the same lane hit three
times, and would be wrong the day a rule declares a label-less part with no
total_row whose stop_at lands on a real totals line. Mirroring totalAnchor is
the right shape; the missing thing is the proof.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS: a synthetic rule -- inline YAML over a committed page
fixture, the way internal/mapping/tolerance_test.go builds one -- with a
label-less part, no total_row, and a stop_at anchored so the block ends on a line
that DOES print a totals run. Then plant a fact on it and assert the check
refuses it, and assert the narrow filter makes that test go red. Probably belongs
in internal/mapping as a TotalRowSpan test plus one check-level test, rather than
in internal/check alone.

NOT URGENT. The hazard it covers requires a mapping shape nobody has written, and
the check's other three tests are load-bearing and proven failable.
acceptance_criteria: a synthetic label-less part with no total_row whose stop_at lands on a real totals run is covered by the check, proven by a test that goes red when the rule loop is narrowed to rules declaring a total_row

title: factOffsetIsNotAStatedTotal's missing-resolver arm cannot fire, and reads as a guard
description:
FOUND BY /code-review over 3666326^..d58c898, the first pass over the correctness
lane. Filed rather than fixed, per AGENTS.md's triage: it is neither WRONG-OUTPUT
nor FAIL-OPEN, and it is more than a single line.

THE ARM. internal/check/statedtotals.go, in factOffsetIsNotAStatedTotal.Run:

    r, ok := s.Resolvers[f.Path]
    if !ok {
        findings = append(findings, finding(f.Path,
            "no resolver was built for this rule file, so its totals cannot be located"))
        continue
    }

IT CANNOT FIRE. Subject.openDocs (internal/check/subject.go) iterates s.Files and
builds a resolver for every entry, returning an error if NewResolver fails -- so a
Subject either has a resolver per rule file or Load never returned one. The
lookup cannot miss.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. It reads as a guard, and this project
counts a check that cannot fail as a defect (README.md, and
internal/check/vacuity.go). A reader auditing what stands over the fact store
would count this arm as one of the things standing there. It is also the shape
that hides real gaps: the same file shipped a genuine fail-open in its first
draft, and unreachable defensive code is where an author's attention goes instead
of to the reachable path.

THE OPTIONS, and this is the part to settle rather than assume:
  (a) DELETE IT and index s.Resolvers directly. Simplest, and correct as long as
      the invariant holds. If it ever stops holding, the check panics on a nil
      resolver -- which is loud, and arguably the right answer for a broken
      Subject.
  (b) KEEP IT AND MAKE IT REACHABLE by asserting the invariant where a test can
      break it, so the arm has a witness.
  (c) MOVE THE INVARIANT to where it belongs: if "every rule file has a resolver"
      is a property of Subject, say so on Subject.Resolvers' doc comment, and
      then (a) is justified BY that sentence rather than by a reader's grep.

RECOMMENDATION (c) then (a): the invariant is real and undocumented, and writing
it down is what makes deleting the arm a decision instead of an omission. Note
that no OTHER check in internal/check does this lookup defensively -- grep
s.Resolvers -- so the arm is also inconsistent with its siblings, which is
evidence for (a).
acceptance_criteria: either the arm is deleted and Subject.Resolvers' doc comment states the invariant that justifies deleting it, or the arm has a test that makes it fire

title: projection-scopes-are-disjoint's summary cannot witness its own coarse-key arm
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by the first review pass over the Stage 2 seams lane (471c56a^..a50f26a), in the fix that closed fisc-tlbp.

ARM 2 now validates a disjointness declaration against BOTH cellAddress (six fields) and netCellAddress (three, the grain internal/project's netCells collides on). The FINDING path is correct and is pinned by TestADisjointnessDeclarationIsCheckedAtTheGrainProjectionsNetOn, which is proven failable.

WHAT IS NOT COVERED IS THE SUMMARY. The `held` string and the byCheck / byKey / byBoth counting that feeds it still read `shared` alone. So:

  - the coarse measurement is invisible on every passing run -- verify prints "6 restate the same money: 5 related by a reconciliation check, 2 by a shared (kind, category, fund_group, fund, fiscal year, basis) key, 1 by both", and says nothing about the 11 pairs that collide at the netCells grain;
  - THE PASS LINE WOULD BE BYTE-IDENTICAL IF sharedNetKeys RETURNED NOTHING. That is the shape AGENTS.md names: the summary cannot distinguish the arm working from the arm being dead. Only the test can, and only for one pair.

NOT FAIL-OPEN, which is why it was filed rather than fixed in the pass: the check still fails correctly on a bad declaration, measured. What is missing is the run's own account of what it measured.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE: count and report both relations, being careful not to imply the two routes partition the pairs -- the existing comment on byCheck/byKey/byBoth already refuses that arithmetic for the two routes it has, and a third makes it worse. Measured at a50f26a: 21 pairs, 11 sharing a netCellAddress, 5 of those sharing zero cellAddress.

RELATED: fisc-a8dm, which is the same shape on other summaries (reasons and Descriptions that compute their counts).
notes:
2026-09-04 THIS BEAD'S TEXT WENT STALE INSIDE THE SAME LANE THAT FILED IT, and the third review pass is why.

It names `sharedNetKeys` and `netCellAddress` and describes them as netCells' three fields. Both were wrong and both are gone. The type is now `mergeableAddress` and carries FIVE fields -- (kind, category, fund_group, fiscal_year, basis) -- because project.netCells has one caller, sankey, which is handed selectFacts' output and refuses more than one column, so every fact reaching it already agrees on year and basis. The three-field version refused TRUE disjointness declarations for the ACFR pairs; see fisc-tlbp's second note.

The test named here, TestADisjointnessDeclarationIsCheckedAtTheGrainProjectionsNetOn, is now ...ProjectionsCanReach and asserts both halves rather than one.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWNS IS UNCHANGED and the re-measurement makes it sharper. projection-scopes-are-disjoint's `held` summary and its byCheck/byKey/byBoth counting still read the fine key only, so the coarse measurement is invisible on a passing run and the pass line would be byte-identical if sharedMergeableKeys returned nothing. Re-measured at the fifth pass, over facts canMerge admits: 21 pairs, of which 3 share a mergeable address and 2 share a fine one. The summary reports the 2 and never the 3.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE. projection-scopes-are-disjoint was deleted at aef3d8f; verified at HEAD, the id is not among the 44 fisc verify reports and scopepairs.go does not exist. The held summary, the byCheck/byKey/byBoth counting and sharedMergeableKeys all went with it.

THE SHAPE IT NAMED IS THE VALUABLE PART AND IT IS NOT LOST: a summary that would be BYTE-IDENTICAL if one of its arms returned nothing cannot distinguish the arm working from the arm being dead. That is written down where it survives this bead -- AGENTS.md's 'Prove it can fail' ('a test that is green because the gate fired is indistinguishable by exit code from one green because the defect was prevented') and docs/review-loop-evidence.md. Its sibling fisc-a8dm, the same shape on other summaries, is closed against the same deletion.

MEASURED WHILE CLOSING, because the obvious worry is that the replacement inherited the defect: no surviving check Description() carries a computed or hand-typed count. The one numeral in any of them is 'pp.127-140', a page range. cuts-tie-along-the-lattice's summary names every cell count, every held-apart exception and every refused pair individually rather than totalling them, so there is nothing in it that a dead arm could leave byte-identical.

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: mapping.NewResolver takes an unexported doc, so no other package can call it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by a go/types probe written for fisc-jbu4 (4c91136) to catch the class of regression that unexporting a type can introduce.

internal/mapping/resolve.go:136

    func NewResolver(d doc, f *File) (*Resolver, error)

`doc` is unexported. NewResolver is exported, so another package can see it and cannot call it -- there is no way to name the argument type. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the unexport sweep: `doc` was already lowercase before it.

WHY NOTHING REPORTS IT. The compiler is content -- an unexported type in an exported signature is legal Go. revive has a rule for exactly this, `unexported-return`, and .golangci.yml does not enable it (the enabled set is exported, var-naming, receiver-naming, unused-receiver, error-strings, context-as-argument). And it only covers RESULTS, not parameters, so it would not have caught this one either.

THE PROBE that found it walks every exported package-level object's signature -- params, results, and the signatures of exported methods on exported types -- and reports any that mentions an unexported named type from this module. Run over the tree at 4c91136 it returns exactly three, and the other two were introduced by that commit and reverted before it landed (build.Get -> build.Info, corpus.Doc -> corpus.ExtractionError/Warning). So this is the only standing instance.

WHAT TO DECIDE: either export `doc` (it is the resolver's input document and arguably API), or unexport NewResolver if nothing outside internal/mapping calls it -- which should be measured, not assumed. Note the analysis behind fisc-jbu4 did NOT list NewResolver as an unexport candidate, so something outside the package does reference it.

RELATED: fisc-lpus asks whether the export-surface analysis becomes a committed tool. This probe is a second candidate for the same decision, and unlike the reference analysis it encodes a rule that could fail in CI.

title: The four identifiers with no callers at all: delete-vs-keep, not export-vs-unexport
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 while landing fisc-jbu4 (4c91136). Of its 104 candidates, four have ZERO uses anywhere -- not in production, not in tests, not cross-package:

  internal/geom/grid.go:102     (*Grid).Gutter
  pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go:29 (*IOStreams).IsStdinTTY
  pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go:32 (*IOStreams).IsStdoutTTY
  pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go:35 (*IOStreams).IsStderrTTY

WHY UNEXPORTING THEM IS NOT THE ANSWER. `unused` is enabled in .golangci.yml. An EXPORTED identifier with no callers is invisible to it; an UNEXPORTED one is a lint failure. So unexporting these does not discharge an obligation, it swaps revive's `exported` rule for `unused`. They were excluded from fisc-jbu4 for that reason and are untouched.

THE IOSTREAMS THREE CASCADE, which is what makes this a decision rather than a chore. Deleting the accessors makes the stdinIsTTY/stdoutIsTTY/stderrIsTTY fields dead, which makes isTerminal dead, which makes System()'s three assignments dead. That is the whole TTY-detection capability, not a stray method.

AND THE COMMENT ABOVE isTerminal IS FALSE TODAY, which fisc-gyg9 found from the other side. It reads "the only decisions this drives are colorizing and prompting, and neither is observable when the output is discarded". Measured: the three accessors have zero callers, and a grep for color/ansi/escape/prompt across ./cmd ./internal ./pkg returns nothing that colorizes or prompts. The flags drive NOTHING, so the sentence excusing the /dev/null false positive is excusing an inaccuracy that cannot reach anything. Whatever is decided here, that comment must not survive unchanged.

SAME CLASS AS amount.ParseOrZero, which fisc-jbu4 already flags -- except the bead says ParseOrZero has "no caller at all" and it has one, in a test; deadcode from ./cmd/fisc cannot see tests. ParseOrZero was unexported and its delete decision is still open.

OPTIONS: (a) delete each capability and its cascade, editing AGENTS.md where it advertises one; (b) keep them exported and declare why, the way fisc-jbu4's byob-shape exceptions are declared; (c) keep and add the caller that justifies them.
close_reason:
ANSWERED BOTH WAYS, which is what this bead asked for: delete-vs-keep decided per identifier rather than export-vs-unexport swept.

DELETED: internal/geom (*Grid).Gutter. Zero references of any kind; the gutter FIELD stays and Index reads it, so nothing about the geometry changed. Verified by build plus the geom suite.

KEPT, and this is a decision rather than a deferral: the three pkg/iostreams TTY accessors. The bead is right that deleting them cascades -- the three private fields become write-only, System() stops calling isTerminal, and isTerminal goes with them, which is the whole TTY-detection capability rather than four accessors. That is a capability decision (does fisc ever colorize or prompt?) and not a prune, and the owner took it as KEEP on 2026-09-18 when the prune lane put the question. They stay as declared surface for the --color/prompt decision nothing has made yet.

ON isTerminal's COMMENT, which this bead calls false today: it is not. Read at HEAD it documents its own known false positive (/dev/null is a character device) and says outright 'do not build a correctness-bearing behavior on it'. Nothing does. The bead's claim about it was stale.

MEASURED after the deletion, by the method-level selector sweep this lane wrote (deadcode's RTA answer is unsound in the permissive direction for methods, so it does not find these): every production method with zero production callers is now exactly six stdlib interface-dispatch methods (UnmarshalJSON, two UnmarshalYAML, three Unwrap), the three TTY accessors kept above, and registry.(*Registry).departmentEntry with three test callers. Nothing unaccounted for.

facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, 0 errored; make pre-commit exit 0; golangci-lint 0 issues; deadcode -test ./... no findings.

title: Department entries' pages name pp.167-170 only, and no test covers the department tier
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the fourth review pass over the departmentwide lane (174cae9^..2f5a129).

data/departments.yaml holds two tiers. The departmentwide lane added each DIVISION's pp.85-125 page to its `pages` list, so a division entry now names both schedules that print it. The eleven DEPARTMENT entries were not touched and still say pp.167-170 only.

They are printed on the pp.85-125 pages too: each of those eleven pages opens with the department's ALL-CAPS heading, which is what `document_term` carries -- "ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT" at p97:1, "COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT" at p101:1, and so on.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING NUMBER. The file's header says what `pages` means, and the lane rewrote it. It now reads "every DIVISION entry's `pages` names both where it applies" and points here for the department half -- narrowed on purpose rather than left claiming something untrue of half the file. Before this bead, the sentence claimed it of both tiers.

AND NOTHING CAN CATCH IT. TestEveryDivisionIsPrintedOnItsPages, added by the same lane, reads each DIVISION's cited pages and asserts its label is in the label column. There is no department arm. A department's `pages` can name any page at all and no test objects.

THE WORK: add each department's pp.85-125 page, and give that test a department arm matching `document_term` rather than `label` (the heading is ALL CAPS and the label is not). Note the two tiers need different search rules -- a division is found in the LABEL COLUMN, cut at the first object-category name, while a department heading is a line of its own above the block, so the division helper will not find it unchanged.

Then restore the header sentence to speak for the whole file.

Filed rather than fixed in that pass because it is a data change across eleven entries plus a second arm on a test, and the pass had already fixed two fail-open guards and a false published string.
acceptance_criteria: each department entry's pages names every page printing its document_term, and a test fails when one does not

title: The five-rounding-divisions count is written in eight places and only one can fail
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 by the third review pass over the departmentwide lane (174cae9^..b29be00).

"FIVE of the 29 division blocks miss their own printed Division Total by exactly one dollar, every one in the FY2023-24 Actual column" is true, and it is written in EIGHT places:

  mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml   x5, byte-identical, one per
                                                  stated_total_deltas note on
                                                  dw-risk-management, dw-finance,
                                                  dw-information-technology,
                                                  dw-airport and
                                                  dw-public-works-administration
  internal/check/coverage.go                    the unprojectedScopes reason
  internal/check/departmentwide.go              the check's doc comment
  internal/check/departmentwide_test.go         the rounded != 5 assertion

Two of those eight are strings fisc verify prints on every run. The test one is the only copy anything can falsify.

SO A SIXTH ROUNDING DIVISION IS EIGHT COORDINATED EDITS, seven of which nothing checks. That is exactly the shape fisc-xbd4 measures -- the badge lane's "the other six fund groups" was wrong in three files and cost one review pass per copy -- and this is a fresh instance rather than a survival of an old one.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE PASS THAT FOUND IT: the five YAML copies are the real problem and de-duplicating them is a schema question, not an edit. A stated_total_deltas note is per-part by construction, so either the five notes each say only what is true of THEIR OWN part (dropping the corpus-wide count, which is the useful sentence) or the rule file grows a way to name a shared note. Both are design choices this lane had no basis to make.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIX, if the schema is left alone: cut the count from the five YAML notes so each says only "the city's own rounding, stated minus mapped, in this part", and let the count live in the two Go strings plus the assertion that can fail. That is three copies instead of eight, and the one that can go red is among them.

Related: fisc-xbd4 (a figure repeated in prose across files costs one review pass per copy), fisc-a8dm (unprojectedScopes' reasons compute their counts).
acceptance_criteria: the count of rounding divisions on pp.85-125 exists in a number of places a single edit can keep true, and at least one of them goes red when the count changes
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18, and the count is in SIX places now, not eight. Two of the eight went with aef3d8f, which deleted nine checks against the lattice:
  internal/check/coverage.go        the unprojectedScopes reason  -- GONE with the map
  internal/check/departmentwide.go  the check's doc comment       -- GONE with the check

THOSE WERE THE TWO THIS BEAD CALLED OUT AS 'strings fisc verify prints on every run', so the highest-stakes half of the problem was removed by a lane that was not about it. What remains is five byte-identical stated_total_deltas notes in mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml (lines 3538, 3578, 3758, 3810, 3878) and one assertion.

AND THE ASSERTION THAT CAN FAIL SURVIVED, which was the thing to check before assuming this got better rather than worse: internal/check/departmentwide_test.go:168 still reads 'if rounded != 5' with the comment that a sixth would be tolerated here while failing the build. aef3d8f kept that file's page arithmetic and deleted only its check-driving tests.

SO THE BEAD'S STAKES ARE LOWER AND ITS CHEAPEST-FIX PARAGRAPH IS STALE: it proposed cutting the count from the five YAML notes and letting it live in 'the two Go strings plus the assertion that can fail'. The two Go strings no longer exist, so that fix now means five YAML notes plus one assertion -- six copies down to one, not three. Re-decide the fix against that, not against the eight.
2026-09-19, released. Re-derived against the tree and the 2026-09-18 note holds: mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml still carries the byte-identical stated_total_deltas notes and internal/check/departmentwide_test.go:168 is still 'if rounded != 5', the one copy that can go red. Unassigned so it is claimable again.

title: Publish facts.csv as an Open Fiscal Data Package: a descriptor beside it, validated in CI
description:
An external recommendation (2026-09-03) argued this project should decouple its
data layer from its presentation layer, stop hardcoding fiscal arrays in the
frontend, and strictly adhere to the Open Fiscal Data Package standard.

MEASURED AGAINST THE TREE, TWO OF THOSE THREE ARE ALREADY TRUE. site/app.js
carries no fiscal figures at all -- grep -E '[0-9]{6,}' site/app.js returns
nothing outside layout comments -- and it fetches data/<stem>.json at runtime.
The data layer is already separately consumable: facts/facts.jsonl, re-encoded
on export as facts/facts.csv, facts/index.json and one JSONL shard per page,
contracted in docs/fact-store-contract.md and offered as labelled downloads by
factAssets.downloads(). So this bead is ONLY the third claim: OFDP.

WHAT IT IS. A Frictionless/OFDP descriptor at dist/facts/datapackage.json whose
single resource is the already-shipped facts/facts.csv. Purely additive.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BE. Not a replacement for facts.jsonl and not the headline
artifact. OFDP carries no per-cell page/offset/token notion, so the descriptor
is an index over a second encoding, never the audit trail. A version of this
work that demotes facts.jsonl has broken the one thing the project exists to
uphold.

WHAT IT CANNOT CARRY. The projections. OFDP is a flat table standard; a Sankey
is a graph -- nodes, links, transfer legs, derived nodes. data/<stem>.json stays
as it is under docs/sankey-contract.md. The recommendation's framing conflated
the two artifacts.

THE SEAM. buildFactAssets in pkg/cmd/export/facts.go already writes
factsCSVPath and factsIndexPath into assets.Files and holds assets.CSVBytes; a
third path goes in beside them, and a third export.Download entry in
downloads(). THAT DOWNLOAD ENTRY IS MANDATORY, NOT DECORATIVE:
TestTheSiteLinksEveryShardItShips fails any key under facts/ that is neither a
page-index row nor an offered download.

THE TABLE SCHEMA IS DERIVED, NOT RESTATED. Its fields must be factCSVHeader()
in order, with a test asserting the equality. A hand-copied column list is the
restating-a-rule-that-changed-elsewhere defect AGENTS.md measures at 35% of
false-text findings, and this one would go stale the next time a field is added
to fact.Fact.

AMOUNTS STAY INTEGER CENTS. The descriptor declares the scale; it does not emit
a decimal column. docs/fact-store-contract.md already refuses an amount_dollars
column and gives the reason (a float, which AGENTS.md forbids, or a second
decimal spelling of one integer). If OFDP's measure object turns out to have no
scale key that fits, record that here rather than putting a float on the money
path.

VOCABULARY IS A CROSSWALK, NOT A REWRITE. OFDP's phase and direction
vocabularies are close to this project's basis (adopted/revised/audited) and
kind (revenue/expenditure/transfer_out) but not identical. Silently rewriting
our tokens into theirs publishes a classification we inferred as though the city
printed it, which is the published-is-not-derived invariant. Declare the
mapping; keep the tokens.

THE COVERAGE CAVEAT TRAVELS WITH THE PACKAGE. The store is what the mappings
cover, not what the documents contain -- 36 pages of 786, across two of three
registered documents. A descriptor titled "City of Livermore budget" implies a
completeness the store does not have, so its description field must say what
docs/fact-store-contract.md's "What this does not promise" says.

VALIDATION IS A CI JOB, AND THE OWNER CHOSE IT. There is no Go frictionless
library, and stdlib-first (byob-release.10) means a new dependency would need
its own decision bead -- so the validator is Python in
.github/workflows/ci.yml, pip-installing frictionless and running it over
dist/facts/datapackage.json. The precedent is exact: the "app.js layout claims"
job runs node off the deploy path for the same reason. NO COMMITTED TEXT MAY SAY
"valid OFDP" UNTIL THAT JOB IS GREEN. Until then the word is "OFDP-shaped", or
the claim is a FALSE-CLAIM finding waiting to be found. Go-side shape checks
(fields == factCSVHeader(), row count and hash == the shipped CSV) are worth
having as the fast local gate, but they are not what licenses the word "valid".

THE SPEC WAS NOT PINNED. The session that filed this had no network:
fiscal.datapackage.org and specs.frictionlessdata.io both failed. So this bead
deliberately names NO required keys from memory. Step one of the work is
fetching the spec and pinning the version and profile the descriptor targets.

Priority is P3 because this is interop for third parties, not correctness: it
sits behind fisc-av0w and the rest of the P1 bugs, and behind E10's second
document. Filed rather than built, on the owner's decision.

title: (BUG) AGENTS.md names four open epics; there are five, and E11 is not mentioned at all
description:
AGENTS.md:222 reads: "The roadmap is eleven epics and FOUR OF THEM ARE OPEN:
`E5 Verification` (fisc-1wr), `E7 Coverage` (fisc-5gk), `E8 Further projections`
(fisc-4ua) and `E10 The ACFR enters the corpus` (fisc-1p4d)."

MEASURED off `bd list --type=epic --status=all`: TWELVE epics, FIVE open. The
one missing is E11 (fisc-yj4w, "The reader meets the money before the
apparatus", P1, open with five open children). AGENTS.md does not mention E11
anywhere.

THE PARAGRAPH PARTLY DISCLAIMS ITSELF -- it says a count taken from it "is a
claim about the plan rather than about the tracker" and to read it off bd. That
covers the NUMBER. It does not cover the ENUMERATION, which names four epics by
id and is now missing one, and a reader who follows the list rather than the
instruction gets a wrong picture of what is in flight.

RELATED BUT DIFFERENT: fisc-yidr records that commit 8010fd1's subject claims to
close E11 while fisc-yj4w is open. That is the commit-message copy of the same
confusion. This is the AGENTS.md copy, and fisc-xbd4 is the reason both need
fixing in whichever commit touches either.

FIX SHAPE. The same paragraph already argues that this class of count belongs in
the tracker, so the enumeration is the part to drop rather than update -- naming
the four ids is what made it rot. Keep the sentence that says to read it off
`bd list --type=epic --status=all`.
close_reason:
Fixed in AGENTS.md, 2026-09-03. The paragraph now reads 'twelve epics and five of them are open' and names all five, E11 among them.

THE BEAD UNDERCOUNTED ITS OWN FINDING. Its title says 'names four open epics; there are five'. The epic TOTAL was wrong too: the paragraph said eleven, and E0 through E11 is twelve. Both numbers were stale for the same reason -- E11 was filed after the sentence was written and nothing re-read it.

A SECOND FALSE CLAIM WAS FOUND IN THE SAME SECTION and fixed in the same commit, per AGENTS.md's rule that correcting a figure in prose means grepping for its copies. Two paragraphs down: 'That lane is also what unblocks E5 -- the whole remaining tier ladder is downstream of fisc-9hf, E10's first child.' fisc-9hf closed 2026-08-30, took fisc-1wr.2 with it, and E5 did NOT become workable: fisc-1wr.3, .4 and .5.1 are deferred to 2026-11-10 and .7 sits behind fisc-mq4.6 -> fisc-mq4.3, deferred to the same date. The ladder was downstream of two things and one of them moved. That sentence is now replaced by the measurement.

The paragraph's own instruction -- read the count off 'bd list --type=epic --status=all' -- is kept, and the new text says outright that the enumeration is what failed to follow it. Verified against that command before writing: five open (fisc-1wr, fisc-5gk, fisc-4ua, fisc-1p4d, fisc-yj4w), twelve total.

facts.jsonl unmoved; this commit changes prose and beads only.

title: (DECISION) Does the export-surface analysis become a committed tool, given it needs x/tools?
description:
DECISION NEEDED, in the byob sense: does the export-surface analysis become a
committed tool, and if so how, given that it needs golang.org/x/tools?

AGENTS.md is explicit -- "A dependency outside cobra, go-cmp, modernc sqlite and
goreleaser needs its own decision bead in the same change" (byob-release.10, and
see fisc-j8f for the YAML precedent). So this cannot be added to go.mod without
a decision, and it should not be added quietly.

WHAT THE ANALYSIS DOES. Loads the module with go/packages and resolves every
exported identifier to the SET OF OTHER PACKAGES referencing it, classifying
each as USED-CROSS-PKG / TEST-ONLY / NO-EXTERNAL-USE, with interface-dispatched
methods, tagged struct fields and -ldflags vars separated out. It is what
produced fisc-ynuo: 1,422 exported identifiers, only 442 used cross-package.
Source is at /tmp/exports and the table at /tmp/sweep/exports.txt. /TMP IS NOT
DURABLE -- fisc-b8z0's artifacts already had to be re-derived once for this
reason.

THREE OPTIONS.

  A. A SEPARATE MODULE UNDER tools/, with its own go.mod requiring x/tools. The
     main module stays untouched, CI's build and lint never see it, and it is
     durable. Precedent: tools/jscheck is already off the build path in another
     language entirely, and tools/extract.py is Python. Cost: a second module in
     the repo, and `go build ./...` from the root will not cover it.

  B. LEAVE IT AS A DOCUMENTED RECIPE in this bead or a doc under docs/. Costs
     nothing, adds nothing, and is re-derived from scratch each time -- which is
     precisely what happened to the earlier audit's artifacts.

  C. REWRITE IT WITHOUT x/tools, using go/parser and go/ast to resolve selector
     expressions per import alias. Stdlib only, so it could live in the main
     module. Less accurate: it cannot see interface satisfaction, which is what
     made 290 methods look unused before the filter existed.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE BEAD MUST CARRY THE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES, because
re-deriving the tool without them re-derives the wrong answer:
  - GENERIC TYPE PARAMETERS are TypeName objects and report Exported() true for
    any single capital letter, so [K comparable] and [V any] score as exported
    types with no users.
  - -ldflags -X VARS (internal/build's Version, Commit, Date) are set by the
    linker by symbol path and have no Go reference by design.
  - INTERFACE-DISPATCHED METHODS record the call against the interface method,
    never the concrete one -- 290 of them.
  - TAGGED STRUCT FIELDS are a serialization contract, not dead weight -- 274.
  - Suspected and unhandled: anything reached only via reflection, a template,
    or //go:embed.

RELATED AND CHEAPER: x/tools' deadcode needs no decision at all, because
`go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@latest ./cmd/fisc` adds nothing to
go.mod. Whatever is decided here, that invocation is worth recording somewhere
durable -- it found two genuinely dead unexported funcs (fisc-ko1v).

Note fisc-owo4 wants a Go analogue of tools/jscheck/layout.mjs to pin what a
comment sweep leaves behind. If that is built, it and this share a shape and
possibly a home.

title: Split the three oversized files: export/page.go, mapping/resolve.go, check/graph.go
description:
Three files carry enough declarations that finding anything in them means
reading past most of the file. This is the ONLY structural item the
architectural measurement supports, and it is a splitting job, not a redesign.

  file                            code lines   declarations
  internal/export/page.go              1,310             66
  internal/mapping/resolve.go          1,211             59
  internal/check/graph.go                841             77

internal/export carries 3,378 production lines in TWO files.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAID ABOUT EVERYTHING ELSE, so this is not read as the
first step of a larger refactor: the package import graph is ACYCLIC and cleanly
layered, five tiers, maximum fan-out 7; the documented rule that internal/export
must not import internal/project holds in fact; ten interfaces exist and sit
where behaviour varies; pkg/cmdutil, the only near-universal dependency at 13
importers, is five files with one job each. The structure survived the
prototyping. See fisc-jnuf.

SO THE SPLIT IS FOR READABILITY, and the test of a proposed split is whether the
resulting file names say what is in them. Suggested first cut, to be checked
against which declarations actually call which:
  - check/graph.go at 77 declarations is the densest and probably the clearest
    win; internal/check already demonstrates the one-check-per-file convention
    that graph.go does not follow.
  - export/page.go is the largest and the most delicate: it is the page-model
    layer behind the published site, and internal/export/export.go is another
    578 lines.

DO IT AFTER THE COMMENT AND EXPORT PASSES, not before. A split moves
declarations, which moves their doc comments with them, and doing that before
fisc-a3rp and fisc-jbu4 means moving prose that is about to be deleted and
diffs that are about to be re-cut.

VERIFICATION. A pure move should change no behaviour: make pre-commit, make
lint, facts.jsonl unmoved, fisc verify count unchanged off a freshly built
binary. tools/codehash -- in the tree, on main since 2f22036, and run by hand as
`make codehash FILES=...` -- hashes per FILE and so cannot prove a cross-file
move; if that guarantee is wanted, it needs a package-level mode.

title: Review the 252 untagged exported struct fields; unexporting one can silently drop it from the output
description:
252 exported struct fields carry NO json or yaml tag and are referenced by no
other package. They are unexport candidates, and they are held back from
fisc-jbu4 because the failure mode is silent.

THE HAZARD, stated precisely: a struct marshalled WITHOUT tags serializes by
FIELD NAME, and encoding/json skips unexported fields entirely. So unexporting a
field that is reached only through json.Marshal compiles, passes every test that
does not assert on the wire bytes, and DROPS THE FIELD FROM THE OUTPUT. In a
project whose published documents are the deliverable and whose fact store is
compared byte for byte, that is the worst available shape: no compiler error, no
test failure, a smaller file.

SO: do fisc-jbu4's 104 first and learn from them. Then, per field, establish
that the struct it belongs to is never marshalled or unmarshalled -- by grepping
for the type in json/yaml calls, not by trusting the absence of a tag.

THE CHEAPEST GUARD IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT ALREADY HAS: fisc build --output
bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl and cmp against facts/facts.jsonl catches any change to
the fact store, and the export goldens catch changes to the published documents.
Run both after every batch rather than at the end, so a dropped field is
attributed to the field that dropped it.

For context on where these sit: 244 exported fields ARE read across a package
boundary, 162 of them tagged. The tagged ones are the published schema and stay.
58 distinct types expose a field across a boundary at all; the largest are
fact.Fact (20), export.View (12), export.Options (11), mapping.Row (9),
project.Point (9), mapping.Rule (8), project.Headline (8), project.Node (7),
project.Link (7).

title: Delete the dead funcs deadcode found, and decide the four unreachable exported ones
description:
x/tools' deadcode, run from ./cmd/fisc, reports nine unreachable funcs. Two are
dead outright and the rest need a decision each.

    internal/check/transfersdetail.go:325   declaredToCIPGroups
    pkg/cmd/export/data.go:68               buildProjections

Both are UNEXPORTED and unreachable from the binary, so nothing outside their
package can reach them either. Delete, with their tests if the tests only cover
them.

NEEDS A DECISION, all exported and all unreachable from main:
    internal/export/export.go:1091          Write
    internal/project/sankey.go:1052         ContestedTotals
    internal/project/sankey.go:1058         GroupExpenditure
    internal/mapping/parse.go:44            Load
Each is either a seam someone intended and never wired up, or residue. Decide
per symbol; where one goes, its doc comment goes with it, which is the cheapest
comment reduction available anywhere in the tree.

DO NOT DELETE, though deadcode names them: mapping.Kinds and iostreams.Test are
reached only by tests, and tests are not entry points for this tool. Kinds is
exported on purpose so internal/registry's vocabulary can be pinned against it
without importing mapping.

REPRODUCE WITH, and note this adds nothing to go.mod:
    go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode@latest ./cmd/fisc

CROSS-CHECK. The strongest signal is the intersection of this list with
fisc-ynuo's "no cross-package reference" analysis -- two independent methods
agreeing. amount.ParseOrZero appears in both and is handled in fisc-jbu4,
because AGENTS.md documents it as a live mechanism and deleting it means
editing that file in the same commit.
close_reason:
DECIDED, all six, and TWO OF THE BEAD'S OWN PREMISES WERE STALE.

STALE (1): internal/check declaredToCIPGroups no longer exists anywhere in the tree -- grep at HEAD returns nothing. It was deleted by some later commit without this bead being touched.
STALE (2): pkg/cmd/export buildProjections is NOT dead. It is a documented seam: pkg/cmd/export/data.go:37-43 explains that buildAll is thin on purpose so buildProjections can keep its own signature, and names the ~10 direct callers in the test suite as the reason. Keep. (Do not confuse it with internal/check's buildProjections, a different function reached from subject.go and fully live.)

THE FOUR EXPORTED-AND-UNREACHABLE, decided one at a time as the bead asked:

  internal/export.Write            DELETED from production, moved to a test
                                   helper. It was a one-step Prepare+plan.Write
                                   convenience with 41 call sites, every one in
                                   package export_test. The binary deliberately
                                   takes the long road -- Prepare, SafeCleanDir,
                                   plan.Write -- so a render that fails does not
                                   destroy the previous site first. Keeping the
                                   one-step form only in the test package means
                                   that ordering has no shortcut around it in
                                   production, which is a better reason to move
                                   it than symbol count.

  project.ContestedTotals          KEEP. Their doc comments state the reason and
  project.GroupExpenditure         it is sound: exported so an assertion compares
                                   against THIS declaration rather than a second
                                   copy of the same figures.

  mapping.Load                     KEEP, and the bead's framing of it as a lone
                                   unreachable was wrong. Production uses LoadDir,
                                   but Load has 23 test call sites across
                                   internal/mapping (unqualified, in-package) and
                                   internal/fact. It is the natural single-file
                                   counterpart to LoadDir and rewriting 23 sites
                                   onto an fs.FS buys nothing.

DO-NOT-DELETE, as the bead said: mapping.Kinds and iostreams.Test. But mapping.Kinds's OWN DOC COMMENT is false about why -- filed separately rather than fixed here, since this lane is not touching internal/mapping/rule.go.

facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify 44 passed, 0 failed, 0 vacuous, 1 skipped, 0 errored; make pre-commit exit 0; golangci-lint 0 issues; deadcode -test ./... no findings; all ten testdata/*.golden.json byte-identical.

title: The package structure survived the prototyping; the debt is in comments, over-export and three oversized files
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03, asking whether the 442 cross-package identifiers are a
coherent API and whether this is the moment for a structural refactor after a
prototyping-heavy history.

THE ANSWER IS NO, AND THE EVIDENCE IS THAT THE STRUCTURE CAME THROUGH THE
PROTOTYPING INTACT. Three measurements, none of which was expected to come back
this way:

1. THE IMPORT GRAPH IS ACYCLIC AND LAYERED. Five tiers, maximum fan-out 7.
   Leaves with zero internal imports: amount, geom, iostreams, build, site.
   Then corpus/mapping/fact/registry/export, then project/check, then
   pkg/cmd/*, then cmd/fisc. The documented rule that internal/export must not
   import internal/project HOLDS IN FACT and not only in prose. A cyclic or
   flattened graph is exactly what rapid prototyping usually leaves behind, and
   this one is clean.

2. THE INTERFACES THAT MATTER ALREADY EXIST, at the seams where behaviour
   actually varies: check.Check (the plugin set, 40+ implementations),
   project.Projection and Sliced and Labels, mapping.doc, registry.labeler, and
   check's Vocabulary plus its three builder interfaces -- which are the
   decoupling seams that keep internal/project from importing the registry. Ten
   in production code, and none of them decorative.

3. pkg/cmdutil, the only near-universal dependency at 13 importers, is NOT a
   junk drawer. Five files, one job each: the error taxonomy (FlagError,
   ExitCodeError, ErrHint), atomic WriteFile, output-path safety, the Factory,
   and repo-root discovery.

WHAT THE 55%-STRUCT-FIELDS FIGURE ACTUALLY MEANS. Of the 442 cross-package
identifiers, 244 are struct fields and only 86 are behaviour (func + method).
That reads as alarming and is not: this is a pipeline whose stages hand each
other RECORDS -- fact.Fact (20 fields crossing a boundary), project.Node, Link,
Sankey, mapping.Row and Rule, project.Point -- and 162 of the 244 carry a
json/yaml tag, so they are the published serialization schema rather than
accidental exposure. 58 distinct types expose a field across a boundary.
Encapsulating fact.Fact behind getters would add ceremony and remove nothing;
the field IS the contract, and fisc verify checks it.

SO AN INTERFACE-INTRODUCTION REFACTOR WOULD BE ABSTRACTION WITHOUT VARIATION.
Most of these types have exactly one implementation. check.Check earns its
interface because there are 40-odd checks; project.Projection because there are
several projections. A FactStore or Extractor interface with one implementer
buys nothing, and it fails this project's own standard by the same argument it
applies to checks: something that cannot vary cannot be exercised.

WHERE THE PROTOTYPING DEBT ACTUALLY IS, all three measured this session:
  - COMMENTS. 39% of production Go by line. 16% of comment lines sit in blocks
    containing narration. A single file that had already been through a review
    pass yielded 3 refuted and 6 overreaching claims out of 77.
  - OVER-EXPORT. 356 identifiers (25% of 1,422) never leave their package,
    carrying 958 doc-comment lines. See fisc-ynuo.
  - FILE COHESION WITHIN PACKAGES, and this is the only structural item.
    internal/export/page.go is 1,310 code lines and 66 declarations;
    internal/check/graph.go is 841 lines and 77 declarations;
    internal/mapping/resolve.go is 1,211 and 59. internal/export carries 3,378
    production lines in TWO files. That is a splitting job, not a redesign, and
    it is the one place cohesion is visibly thin.

RECOMMENDED ORDER, cheapest and least reversible last: unexport the 356; split
the three oversized files if anything; leave the package graph and the
interfaces alone.

title: (BUG) Six overreaching claims in internal/geom's comments, each true under narrower words
description:
Six claims in internal/geom's comments that an adversarial pass could not refute
outright but found true only under narrower words than they use. All six are
text the sweep KEPT from the original rather than wrote, and all were measured.
Filed rather than fixed so that fisc-b93j's first fix commit stays small --
decay is what a shrinking fix commit looks like.

1. grid.go, the gutter guard: "Index could then never return -1 at all."
   Measured with a gutter at the smallest positive float: Index(0), Index(-5)
   and Index(NaN) all still return -1, because the `x <= g.gutter` arm still
   fires. And the ghost word documented ~35 lines above in geom.go --
   [null,null,null,null,"$"] -> (0,0,0,0) -- has Right() == 0, so it is not
   hypothetical. True as "never for any word a real page produces": the corpus
   minimum x0 is 7.26. The substantive half is confirmed -- with a ~0 gutter,
   Index(250.51) returns 0 rather than -1, so the guard really is disabled for
   the row labels it exists for.

2. geom.go package doc: "What geometry answers is 'which column is this token
   in', AND NOTHING ELSE." The package also exports Lines and
   MedianWordHeight, and internal/mapping uses the line grouping for two things
   that are not column identity: the header search (matchHeaders over
   pr.lines) and the same-printed-line check, whose refusal reads "token %q is
   printed on line %d but this row's earlier figures are on line %d".

3. geom.go: "Line is one printed line of the page." On 124 of 786 pages it is
   not, which the Lines doc twenty lines below says itself. Stated flatly with
   no hedge.

4. geom.go: "MedianWordHeight is the median vertical extent of the page's
   words." hs[len(hs)/2] is the UPPER median. 404 of the 785 non-blank pages
   have an even word count and on 16 of them the two differ. Immaterial to a
   tolerance; still a claim in text this sweep rewrote.

5. geom.go package doc: "lets its whole test suite be arithmetic over numbers."
   The load-bearing half holds -- no fixture, no I/O, no testdata in either
   test file. But geom_test.go is a JSON template plus strings.Replace
   mutations, which is string surgery. True as "inline, without a fixture".

6. geom.go Page.Width/Height, and this one the sweep WROTE: "so neither
   dimension can be assumed from the doc_id." Refuted by the preceding clause
   of its own sentence -- the Budget Book is portrait throughout, 268 of 268,
   so for that doc_id both dimensions are determined. Exact as "for the ACFR or
   the CIP".

Found by the adversarial verification pass over fisc-b93j's first unit. 77
claims attacked, 68 survived, 3 refuted (fixed in the unit) and these 6.

title: Two stale comments the blind-read audit caught, both measured false
notes:
Both found by the blind-read audit (fisc-b8z0) and both confirmed by measurement
before filing, per that plan's rule that a CONTRADICTED verdict counts only when
verified by hand.

(1) internal/geom/geom.go, on Page.Width/Height: "The Budget Book is portrait
Letter (612x792); the CIP is landscape (792x612)."

MEASURED over data/extracted/*/geometry/*.json, which records width and height
per page:

    livermore-budget-fy2026-2027   268 portrait,   0 landscape
    livermore-cip-fy2026-2030      248 portrait,  75 landscape
    livermore-acfr-fy2025          174 portrait,  21 landscape

So the CIP is portrait for 248 of its 323 pages -- the comment is wrong about the
MAJORITY of the document it names. It is also silent about the ACFR, which is
mixed, and which entered the corpus after the comment was written.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and this is the interesting part: the comment describes
Page.Width and Page.Height, and those two fields are copied unvalidated by
ParsePage and READ BY NOTHING (fisc-yjjb). A false statement about fields no code
consults cannot be contradicted by any test, because no test has reason to touch
them. The dead field and the false comment protect each other.

(2) pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go, on the TTY accessors: "the only decisions this
drives are colorizing and prompting."

MEASURED: IsStdinTTY, IsStdoutTTY and IsStderrTTY have ZERO callers outside
package iostreams. Nothing colorizes and nothing prompts. The conclusion the
sentence supports is fine; the reason given for it is a false claim about the
tree, and it reads as licence for future TTY-dependent behaviour that the
codebase has never had.

TWO MORE, scored as over-promises rather than contradictions, in the same pass:
  - build.Get's "falling back to the Go build metadata" -- only Commit and Date
    fall back; Version never does.
  - iostreams.System's "called once, from main" -- it is called from cmdutil.New.

NOT FIXED HERE. fisc-b8z0 is a measurement and does not touch the tree. Fixing
(1) means deciding fisc-yjjb first: if Width/Height go, the comment goes with
them and there is nothing to correct.
TWO MORE, from the leaf-b scoring pass, both verified before filing.

(3) pkg/cmdutil/path.go, looksLikeSource: "after one run, `--output site` leaves
index.html and the marker beside site/embed.go, and the NEXT --clean deletes the
Go package. THAT HAPPENED TO BE SPELLED OUT IN THIS COMMAND'S OWN EXAMPLE."

It was not. The export command's Example reads `fisc export --output build/site
--clean`. The string "--output site" appears NOWHERE in the tree except inside
this comment, and `git log --all -S` finds exactly one commit touching it --
d35b06a, which is the commit that ADDED THE COMMENT AND THE EXAMPLE TOGETHER. So
the sentence was false in the same commit that wrote it.

This is the never-true-when-written class, which fisc-pm8f's audit measured at
23% of false text and which no review pass has ever caught here, because it reads
as a plausible cross-reference and checking it means grepping for a flag string.
The hazard it describes is REAL; only the citation is invented.

(4) pkg/cmdutil/errors.go, ExitCodeError: "Use it when the code itself is the
result -- a verify command reporting how many checks failed, say."

Its ONLY consumer wrote a paragraph rebutting it, by name, at
pkg/cmd/verify/verify.go: "It is a fixed 3 and deliberately not the number of
failed checks, which cmdutil.ExitCodeError's doc comment offers as a possibility:
an exit code is one byte, so a run with exactly 256 failures would exit 0 and a
CI job would go green on the worst result this command can produce."

So the API's doc recommends a use its only user has refuted in writing, and the
refutation lives in the caller where nobody reading the API will see it. One
fact, two homes, IN DISAGREEMENT -- which is worse than the duplicate case, and
is the shape a blind-read oracle finds and a review pass structurally cannot,
because the two files are never in the same diff.
SIX MORE FROM internal/registry, bringing the running total to TWELVE false or
stale claims across three packages. Counts verified independently where cheap.

(5)  load.go:267  "the exceptions are the three rollup nodes, and requiring the
     other TWENTY-TWO to opt in". taxonomy.yaml declares 27 categories of which 3
     are assignable:false, so it is 24. Correct at 87a7223, when there were 25.
     (I first measured 4 rollups with `grep -c "assignable: false"` and was
     wrong -- the fourth hit is a prose line in the YAML's own header. Parsing
     the blocks gives 3. Recording that because it is the same defect one level
     up: a count taken with a grep that could not see what it was counting.)

(6)  load.go:499  "all 8 of 8 category alias blocks are wholly disjoint". There
     are now 14 blocks and 21 entries. Re-measured through registry.Load: all 21
     are still disjoint, so the PROPERTY holds and only the COUNT is stale --
     which is the argument for stating the property and not the count.

(7)  registry.go:286  "five departments share a name with a division -- three
     exactly, City Council, City Manager and City Attorney". Five pairs match on
     slug AND label. Checked at 2a26015, the commit that wrote it: all five were
     exact there too, so this was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN.

(8)  registry.go:352  "This is the whole of the interface internal/project
     declares". project.Labels has three methods. Two other comments IN THE SAME
     FILE (:397, :501) contradict it.

(9)  registry.go:1  "both files are hand-written", three paragraphs after naming
     three files. A survivor of the two-file era.

(10) registry.go:623  the labeler assertion pins 1 of project.Labels' 3 methods,
     so its build-breakage promise is narrower than the comment claims.

THE ONE THAT ARGUES THE OTHER WAY, and it is the strongest single result in the
whole audit. The blind reader concluded that "Assignable defaults to TRUE at load
and FALSE at query", presented it as an inconsistency, and cited lines. IT IS
FALSE: load folds an ABSENT yaml key on an EXISTING category to true, while
Assignable(slug) answers false for a slug NOT IN THE MAP. Different questions.

registry.go:365's doc comment states exactly that distinction -- and it is one of
the comments the strip removed. So this is a comment whose ABSENCE PRODUCED A
DEMONSTRABLE FALSE INFERENCE about a permission flag, by a careful reader working
from the code. That is the clearest evidence a comment earns its place that this
method can produce, and it is worth more than any RECOVERED count.

PATTERN ACROSS ALL TWELVE: nine are COUNTS or set-size claims. Only three are
about behaviour. That is fisc-pm8f's count rule, arriving as evidence rather than
as argument -- and note that in (6) the property survived while the count rotted,
which is the whole case for stating one and not the other.
========== ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THIS BEAD: 8 OF 20 ACCUSATIONS FAIL ==========

A reviewer was told to REFUTE these twenty, not confirm them, and to redo every
measurement rather than accept the accuser's. Result: 12 CONFIRMED, 6 PARTLY,
2 REFUTED. A 40% error rate in findings I reported as verified.

REFUTED OUTRIGHT
  export.go:39  "export.Options.Files has had exactly one user". The sentence
    continues "...BECAUSE UNTIL NOW no Builder could reach it", and `git show
    2adc05b` puts the comment and the second user in the SAME HUNK OF THE SAME
    COMMIT. The accusation cited as counter-evidence the very line the comment
    announces.
  data.go:477  "jscheck pins the figures in these comments". The comment says
    the checks RE-MEASURE and that the figures ARE THE SAME MEASUREMENTS; it
    never claims each is asserted. The reviewer re-drove every figure through the
    shipped app.js and vendored d3 -- revenue {0,2} 17/29/5 sub-pixel, spending
    {3,4} 24/23/1, {3,4,5} 68 nodes/11, {0,3,4} 33 links/2 -- ALL EXACT. I had
    converted "measured" into "pinned" and faulted a guarantee the text does not
    give. This one I had written up as prose-asserting-a-guard, which was wrong.

THE ONE I VERIFIED BY HAND AND STILL GOT WRONG
  path.go:53. I reported it as an invented citation, false the day it was
    written, and said I had confirmed it with `git log --all -S`. I grepped
    "--output site". THE SHORT SPELLING `fisc export -o site` IS THE SAME
    INVOCATION and is committed in internal/project/project.go:4,
    docs/sankey-contract.md:18, pkg/cmdutil/path_test.go:163 and fisc-gxa.1's
    note. path_test.go:163, written in the same commit, reads "(which this
    command's Example ONCE suggested)" -- past tense, matching path.go's own
    "happened to be". So it is a DATED claim about a pre-commit draft whose
    LOCATION is wrong (the contract doc, not the Example). One word to fix, not
    the sentence cut I recommended.

    This is a one-spelling grep, which is the exact defect this session has spent
    its whole length cataloguing -- and I made it while claiming to have verified
    by hand. Recorded rather than quietly amended because the failure is the
    point: verifying is not a state you reach, it is a thing you can do badly.

PARTLY (the substance stands, the framing does not)
  data.go:612   scoped to "this repository", where all four published columns do
                emit three. The two-caveat branch is latent, and fundflows.go
                records it as such.
  iostreams:59  zero callers confirmed, but the same sentence ends "do not build
                a correctness-bearing behavior on it", so the alleged harm is
                backwards.
  iostreams:37  "called once" is right -- one call site; the two "exceptions" are
                in a _test.go and the package doc scopes the rule to commands.
  build.go:24   real but the weakest of the twenty; the var block four lines up
                documents Version's "dev" default.
  errors.go:30  verify refutes the EXAMPLE but follows the RULE. "Advice the tree
                declines" overstates it.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ACCUSERS' OWN MEASUREMENTS
  project.Labels has SIX methods -- Label, FundName, FundType, ConstraintTier,
  RestrictionNote, DivisionLabel -- not three. The comment says "one-method",
  both scorers said "three", and all three are wrong. The finding survives and

  export.go:136's "24 dead links" cannot be checked by grepping static HTML at

geom.go:104 SURVIVED the attack -- 248/75 reproduced independently, and
Page.Width/Height confirmed to have no reader.

SO THE ACTIONABLE SET IS TWELVE, NOT TWENTY, and one of the twelve (Labels) needs
its number corrected before anyone acts on it.

title: geom: Page.Width/Height are dead and unvalidated, and Band panics on Index's sentinel
notes:
Both found by the blind-read comment audit (fisc-b8z0), both verified against the
tree.

(1) geom.Page.Width AND geom.Page.Height ARE CARRIED AND READ BY NOTHING.
ParsePage copies them straight off the wire struct with no validation. They are
the only fields it copies unvalidated, while every word coordinate goes through
the null-rejecting *float64 path. Grepping production code for a read of either
returns nothing: the other .Height hits are Word.Height() and an unrelated
bar.Height in internal/export. So they are dead weight or a future need nobody
recorded. Decide which, then drop them or validate them like the rest of the page.

(2) Grid.Band(i) HAS NO BOUNDS CHECK AND ITS SIBLING Index RETURNS -1.
Band is one line: return g.bands[i]. Index's own doc says it returns -1 for a
position at or left of the gutter, "which is the row-label area and belongs to no
column". So g.Band(g.Index(x)) panics on exactly the case Index exists to signal.
Band has no production callers at all today, which is why it has never fired and
also why it is cheap to fix before one appears. An exported accessor that panics
on the sentinel its sibling is documented to return is a fail-open shape: the
guard exists, it is just in the caller's head.

FILED LATE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. This went into a second bd create
in the same script as fisc-qz2w, and again into a third with a long -d payload.
Both printed "Priority: P3 / Status: open" and NEITHER CREATED A BEAD; only a
read-back caught it. The same command with no -d worked immediately. So the
failure is in the description payload and it is SILENT -- bd exits 0 and prints
what looks like success. Same class as the scripted-edit abort AGENTS.md records:
one bd create per script, no -d heredoc, and read the id back before writing the
sentence that cites it.
CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE, and it matters more than the bug it is attached to.

That note says two earlier bd create calls "printed Priority/Status and NEITHER
CREATED A BEAD". THAT IS FALSE. Both created beads -- fisc-l9o4 and fisc-0vbb,
now closed as duplicates of this one. So did every create in this session.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: `bd list --status=open` and `bd list --status=open --json`
DO NOT SURFACE BEADS CREATED IN THE SAME SESSION. I read back through bd list,
saw nothing, and concluded the create had failed -- then repeated the create
twice, producing three copies of one finding, and wrote the false diagnosis into
this bead and into commit e8a46ff's message.

The reliable read-back is `bd show <id>` or a grep of .beads/issues.jsonl, which
is where fisc-gyg9 was finally found after the same apparent failure.

This is precisely the defect fisc-pm8f's whole lane is about: a claim about the
tree, stated confidently in committed text, made from a check that could not see
the answer. It is also the third time in two sessions I have written a wrong
statement about whether something was filed -- and the previous two were the ones
AGENTS.md already records under "filed as a bead" written without filing.

THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY WORKS: read the id back with bd show, or grep the jsonl.
Never conclude "not created" from bd list.
STATUS, 2026-09-03, and one duplicate to be aware of.

fisc-0vbb IS A CLOSED DUPLICATE OF THIS BEAD -- same title, same two findings,
already closed. Nothing to do beyond knowing it is there if a search turns it
up.

THE COMMENT HALF OF (2) IS ADDRESSED, on the abandoned comment-sweep branch:
Grid.Band's doc now states "i must be in [0, Len())", which was verified against
the code (Band is a bare slice index, so that is exactly the non-panicking
domain). The false Page.Width/Height orientation claim on the same file was
corrected there too, with measured counts: Budget Book 268 of 268 portrait, ACFR
21 of 195 landscape, CIP 75 of 323 -- confirmed twice, by jq over all 786
geometry artifacts and by pdfinfo over the three PDFs, which also agree on the
page counts. That correction covers fisc-gyg9 item (1).

Those fixes are at comment-sweep 76fec71 and can be cherry-picked. The branch is
not being merged.

THE CODE HALF STANDS AND IS UNTOUCHED. Page.Width and Page.Height are still
copied unvalidated by ParsePage and still read by nothing, and Band still has no
bounds check -- only a doc comment saying what its domain is, which is a
narrower guarantee than a check. Deciding the fields is still the prerequisite
for anything else here: if Width and Height go, their comment goes with them and
there is nothing to correct.

Related: fisc-mwne lists Band among the five worst under-documented exports,
because its sibling Index returns -1 by design while Band panics.
