title: TestAConstraintTierWithoutItsDisclosureIsAFinding's rationale does not describe its own subject
description:
FOUND IN fisc-pm8f's LANE 2, and DECLINED there because it is not a comment fix.
Two successive review passes tried to reword this and both rewordings were false;
the third change deleted the clause rather than attempt a fourth.

THE COMMENT, at checks_test.go's TestAConstraintTierWithoutItsDisclosureIsAFinding,
argues that constraint-tier-vocabulary must assert the disclosure BECAUSE a fund
node is not derived, so derived-nodes-justified skips it:

  "A FUND NODE IS THE INVERSE OF A DERIVED ONE: the node is published ... while
   the constraint tier is our reading of the Description of Funds narrative,
   pp.258-261. So node.derived stays FALSE, which means derived-nodes-justified
   skips the node entirely and the disclosure has nowhere else to be asserted."

THE ARGUMENT IS SOUND ABOUT FUND NODES. It is not sound about what this test
actually exercises. Every one of the test's cases mutates
project.NodeFundBalanceDraw, and that node is BOTH derived (it is a key of
derivedNodes in sankey.go, carrying a rationale and a source note) AND named in
derivedNodesJustified's `inferred` list. So for the test's own subject, the
premise "node.derived stays FALSE" is false and derived-nodes-justified does not
skip it.

WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT: the check and the test both pass and both do something
real. This is a rationale that describes a different node from the one under
test, which is the failure mode "a comment that outlived its rule" one step over
-- it never described its subject.

TWO POSSIBLE ANSWERS AND THE CHOICE IS A JUDGEMENT, which is why this is filed
rather than fixed inside a prose sweep:
  (a) The rationale is right and the FIXTURE is wrong -- the test should mutate a
      tier-3 fund node, which is what the argument is about, and NodeFundBalanceDraw
      was reached for because it was to hand.
  (b) The test is right and the rationale should be rewritten to say what these
      three arms actually cover, dropping the derived-nodes-justified comparison
      that has now been wrong three times.

(a) is the stronger guess: the check reads nodes with a non-empty ConstraintTier,
and the nodes the site publishes tiers ON are the fund nodes. But confirming it
means checking whether the fixture's NodeFundBalanceDraw carries a ConstraintTier
at all, and if it does, why.

The interim state, landed: the derived-nodes-justified clause is deleted and the
comment says only that the tier is the editorial half and this check asserts its
disclosure. That is true of both readings.

title: unprojectedScopes' reasons and fundingSourcesTiesToSpine's Description compute their counts
description:
unprojectedScopes' three reason strings carry 106 hand-typed numbers and
fundingSourcesTiesToSpine's Description() carries 53. Both are printed verbatim
on every `fisc verify` run, which makes them the highest-stakes prose in the
project, and neither has any guard over its figures --
TestUnprojectedScopesAreDeclarations checks shape only (non-empty, no two reasons
byte-identical, cites a page or a bead).

fisc-pm8f's lane 3 deletes or delegates the bare counts among them. What it does
NOT do, deliberately, is change the shape: deriving these counts from the Subject
means unprojectedScopes stops being a map[string]string, and that is a design
change that does not belong inside a prose sweep.

The precedent is 9c85d73, which made the caveat figures computed rather than
literal: "Every number in these caveats was a literal until this lane, and every
literal was written for one column." The same argument applies here.

Decide after lane 3 whether enough typed counts survive to be worth the change.
notes:
THIS BEAD NOW OWNS LANE 3, 2026-09-03. fisc-pm8f is closed; its lane 3 -- the
printed strings, which were never started -- passes here, because this bead was
already the largest part of it.

LANE 3 AS pm8f SCOPED IT. The hand-typed numbers in the strings fisc verify
prints to a reader: 204 over 8 files at 823de73, being ~45 page citations, ~49
dollar citations and ~69 bare counts. The page and dollar citations are
EXTRINSIC and stay -- verify them against facts.jsonl and data/extracted/, then
leave them. The bare counts take AGENTS.md's "Before you quote a number":
delegate to the check whose summary already prints it, or compute from the
Subject, as 9c85d73 did when it made the caveat figures computed rather than
literal.

Two anchors that DO reproduce and are not in doubt: unprojectedScopes
(internal/check/coverage.go) carries 119 numbers against the 106 pm8f claimed,
and fundingsources.go's string literals 54 against 53.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE COMMENT WORK THAT SURROUNDED IT. These are not
comments. They are what a reader is shown on every fisc verify run, so a stale
count here is user-facing output rather than a note to a maintainer -- which is
why the original audit's taxonomy undercounted prose defects by roughly half:
22 of 65 false-text instances were user-facing or operator strings and were
filed as WRONG-OUTPUT rather than as prose.

SAFE TO CHANGE: nothing pins these strings.
TestUnprojectedScopesAreDeclarations checks shape only -- non-empty, no two
reasons byte-identical, cites a page or a bead -- and no golden holds verify
output. Keep the no-duplicate-reason property. facts.jsonl must not move, and
diff fisc verify's output before and after: A COUNT THAT VANISHED WITHOUT A
COMPUTING CHECK TAKING IT OVER IS A COVERAGE CLAIM QUIETLY WITHDRAWN.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE, both subjects. unprojectedScopes' three reason strings carried 106 hand-typed numbers and fundingSourcesTiesToSpine's Description() carried 53; the map went with coverage.go's facts-are-projected arm at aef3d8f and the check went in the same commit. Verified at HEAD: fundingSourcesTiesToSpine has zero occurrences in any .go file, and all 25 remaining occurrences of unprojectedScopes are COMMENTS referring to a symbol that no longer exists -- which is fisc-5aw0's sweep, not this bead.

RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because 'the concern moved somewhere else' was the live possibility: scanning every surviving check's Description() body for a hand-typed numeral gives ONE hit, internal/check/revenuelines.go, and it is 'pp.127-140', a page range rather than a count. So the class this bead was opened over -- verify-printed prose carrying typed figures with no guard -- has no instance left in the tree.

THE PRECEDENT IT CITED STANDS on its own: 9c85d73 made the caveat figures computed rather than literal, and AGENTS.md's 'Before you quote a number' now carries the rule ('pin every surviving count to something that re-measures it').

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: Pin what survives: a Go analogue of layout.mjs, scoped after the comment sweep
description:
DEFERRED ON PURPOSE, and the reason is that fisc-pm8f's count rule mostly
obviates it. Scope this only AFTER that sweep reports what actually remained.

tools/jscheck/layout.mjs re-measures every figure site/app.js quotes about itself
and greps app.source for the whole sentence carrying each, so editing a comment
without re-measuring fails `make js`. It is the only mechanical guard over prose
anywhere in this repo and it stops at the language boundary: no Go test asserts
any corpus figure a Go comment quotes.

WHY NOT JUST BUILD IT. Measured at 823de73 there are 663 numeric comment lines in
production Go -- but ~85 of those are INTRINSIC counts that fisc-pm8f deletes
rather than pins. What is left to pin is the second kind of count: arithmetic
that IS the evidence for a decision. That is a much smaller set, and pinning it
is a different and easier job than pinning 663 lines. Building first would guard
text that is about to be deleted.

go/parser and go/ast are stdlib, so byob-release.10 permits this with no new
dependency. Nothing in the tree uses either today.

Two details layout.mjs already got right and a Go version must copy:
  - match WHOLE QUOTED PHRASES, not bare substrings -- includes("14") is
    satisfied by `const NODE_WIDTH = 14`, so the sentence drifts while green;
  - PIN, do not bound -- a `>` comparison lets the rejected alternatives drift.
notes:
A CONCRETE FIRST INSTANCE, from fisc-pm8f's lane 2, 2026-09-02. This bead was
filed as "scope it after the sweep reports what remained". The sweep's first
commit produced one immediately:

coverage.go's fundingSourcesScope reason -- printed verbatim by fisc verify on
every run -- says "The two historical columns, 156 of the 312 facts". The 312 is
pinned, but only obliquely: fundingsources_test.go asserts `moved != 312` over
the FACT COUNT, not over the string. The two can drift apart with nothing red,
and the 156 is pinned by nothing at all.

That is exactly the second kind of count rule 2 keeps -- a coverage claim about
what the check does and does not reach -- so it is not deletable, and it is
therefore precisely the population this bead exists to pin. A Go analogue of
layout.mjs would re-derive the figure from the Subject and grep the reason
string for the whole phrase carrying it.

The lane also confirmed this bead's premise from the other side: the sweep
DELETED ten intrinsic counts and kept every document count and every
evidence-for-a-decision count. What is left to pin really is much smaller than
the 663 numeric comment lines measured at 823de73 -- but it is not zero, and the
printed strings in internal/check are where it lives.
A SECOND, CHEAPER THING FOR THIS BEAD TO CARRY, found the same way, 2026-09-02:
A COMMENT WRAP CHECKER. Not the same job as pinning figures, but the same shape
(a mechanical guard over prose) and far easier.

THE EVIDENCE. Across fisc-pm8f's lanes, FOUR consecutive commits asserted that
the orphaned comment lines left by deletions had been rewrapped, and all four
were false. The mechanism is exact and it will recur: rewrapping only the line
the diff touched leaves the NEXT line short, so each pass sees a fresh orphan one
line down and believes it has finished. gofmt reads comment INDENTATION -- it
caught a broken godoc list item -- and is blind to comment WIDTH, so no gate in
the tree sees any of this.

WHAT WORKED, as a scratch script and worth writing properly:
  - parse each .go file into runs of //-comment lines sharing an indent, broken
    at blank `//` lines and at godoc list items (`//   - `);
  - intersect those paragraphs with the line numbers the change actually touched,
    from `git diff -U0` -- checking whole files is useless here, since the repo's
    existing prose wraps anywhere from 65 to 84 and a global rule flags 242
    lines that are all fine;
  - report a line over 88 chars, or a mid-paragraph line under 48;
  - fix by reflowing the WHOLE paragraph, never the edited line.

It found 3 real defects the fourth commit had left, plus a hyphen break textwrap
itself introduced ("as a one-\n// line file error"). Note the last one: the tool
that reflows needs break_on_hyphens=False, and the checker is what caught the
tool.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE rather than as its own bead: it is the same "mechanical guard
over prose" this bead is for, it uses the same go/parser-or-nothing decision, and
it is the half that would pay for itself immediately. Pinning figures is the
harder half. Do this one first.

title: Note for byob-go-cli: lift the comment rules, prove-it-can-fail, and the self-measuring harness
description:
READY TO PASTE INTO byob-go-cli. This bead is the note; nothing else holds it.
It is a normal task in THIS repo, not a byob-* bead -- those are imported
reference material and must not be authored here.

WHY THESE AND NOT THE REST. The rules below mention no budgets, no provenance and
no PDFs; they are about writing Go comments in any repo. The five-pass review
loop and its counts are deliberately NOT lifted: they are one session's
measurements over three lanes of one project, and the honest scope of a byob
decision is a rule that held somewhere other than where it was measured.

The 21 existing byob decisions have no home for this. byob-testing covers what to
assert, byob-user-docs covers docs shipped to users, byob-agent-onboarding covers
the entry point. None covers comments.

=====================================================================
PROPOSED: a new decision, byob-comments -- "Comments name; they do not copy"
=====================================================================

DECISION 1. A comment names a symbol. It does not say what the symbol does, and
it does not say where the symbol lives.

Both are second sources that nothing keeps in step. The edit that falsifies a
restatement is in the OTHER file, so its author never sees the comment; and a
path goes stale the moment the symbol moves. Go tooling finds a symbol from its
bare name -- qualify with a package only where the name is ambiguous.

  THE EXCEPTION IS SURPRISE. Document another API only where it does not make
  sense on its face, or has to be used oddly for this code to work -- and then
  write down WHAT SURPRISED YOU, not what the API does. That is the one thing the
  other file cannot tell the reader, and the one thing a reader loses by looking
  it up.

  DATA AND ARTIFACT PATHS ARE NOT SYMBOLS AND STAY. A config file, a fixture, a
  served asset: there is nothing to look up by name, so the path IS the reference
  rather than a copy of one.

DECISION 2. Do not report a count of the tree's own contents.

How many facts, nodes, handlers, checks or rules there are goes stale on the next
commit and tells a reader nothing they could not get by looking. A count earns
its place only when EXTRINSIC -- when it says something about a world outside the
code that the code cannot report. "We handle 18 of the 20 status codes" is worth
writing. "This returns 61 nodes" is not.

  Two kinds qualify and nothing else does:
    - A count against the external domain the program is about.
    - A count that IS the evidence for a decision -- an arithmetic proof, or a
      measured comparison against the alternatives that were rejected. It stays,
      AND must be pinned by something that re-measures it.

DECISION 3. History's home is git.

No "found by review" credit lines in source; the commit body is where that
belongs, and it tells the next reader whether a fix was designed or discovered.
No errata: "an earlier version of this comment said X" adds a second claim, about
the past, that nothing can check.

THE EVIDENCE THAT EARNS THEM, from livermore-budget, 2026-08-31 to 09-01:
  - 115 review findings classified one at a time from the commit bodies.
  - Reclassified by WHY the text went false: restating a rule that changed
    elsewhere 35%, never-true-when-written 23%, number drifted 22%, history 15%.
  - Exactly ONE of the 115 was a pre-existing code defect. The passes were not
    auditing the tree; they were reading prose, and then reading their own.
  - The narrative-history hypothesis was tested and is mostly wrong: 247 of
    18,746 Go comment lines (1.3%) carry a history marker.
  - In a 62k-line repo at 30% comment density (40% excluding tests): 159
    production comments naming another file, 173 naming a symbol from another
    package, 102 giving a .go path, ~85 intrinsic count phrases.
  - Counterexample that sharpens decision 2: the repo's own TESTS already refuse
    to pin tree counts, in as many words -- "The counts move with every page that
    gets mapped, and pinning them here would make this a test of the mapping's
    size." The prose never got the memo.

=====================================================================
ALSO WORTH LIFTING -- two additions, cheaper than they look
=====================================================================

INTO byob-testing: "Prove it can fail", and its named failure mode, GREEN
BECAUSE THE GATE FIRED.

  Reproduce the defect green, then show it red, and put both in the commit
  message. The failure mode to recognise: a check that passes because a fixture
  rejected the input BEFORE reaching the guard, not because the guard worked.
  The two are indistinguishable from an exit code and completely different in
  what they guarantee. Worked example: a config carrying `docs: {}` made every
  required-key check for a `[].pages` key pass, because the loader returned on
  the empty map before ever reaching `source.pages`. Populating it and deleting
  the guard gave a TypeError and a table at 0 rows against 58.

  Three occurrences in one repo, each found by accident. So the question is not
  "does the test pass" but "what is this fixture hiding, and what would have to
  break for this to go red?" When one turns up, look for its siblings -- the
  fixture that hid one usually hides several.

A NEW PATTERN, or an addition to byob-testing: A HARNESS THAT RE-MEASURES THE
FIGURES A SOURCE FILE QUOTES ABOUT ITSELF.

  For any asset shipped without a build step or a test framework -- a served
  .js, a generated config, a hand-tuned constant table. Load the SHIPPED file,
  re-measure everything its comments claim, then grep the file's own source for
  the WHOLE SENTENCE carrying each figure, so editing a comment without
  re-measuring goes red.

  Two details that are the whole of it:
    - Match whole quoted phrases, never bare substrings. `includes("14")` is
      satisfied by `const NODE_WIDTH = 14`, so the sentence it was meant to pin
      can drift to a wrong number while the check stays green.
    - PIN, do not bound. A `>` comparison lets the rejected alternatives drift
      while the check stays green, which is the defect such a harness exists to
      remove.

  Reference implementation: tools/jscheck/layout.mjs in livermore-budget. It is
  the only mechanical guard over prose in that repo, and it stops at the language
  boundary -- which is why decision 2 above matters more than building the same
  thing again in Go.

title: 8010fd1's subject says it closes E11; fisc-yj4w is open
description:
git show --stat 8010fd1   ->  chore(beads): close E11 and record what the
                                three review lanes measured
                                .beads/issues.jsonl | 2 +-
  bd show fisc-yj4w         ->  [P1 . OPEN]

The commit's only diff is a one-line rewrite of fisc-yj4w's description and
notes. No status change is in it, and the bead is open today.

LEAVING IT OPEN IS DEFENSIBLE: five children (fisc-yj4w.9 through .13) are open,
all of them scope declined during the session. The subject line asserting
otherwise is not defensible, and it is exactly the class AGENTS.md's "Before you
quote a number" exists to name -- a commit message is a claim about the tree --
in the commit that reports on the review discipline.

WORTH RECORDING AS WELL: the same commit's body reports a range audit of "41
checkable claims across the 21 commit messages, machine-verified against the
tree. Zero false." That audit covered the 21 commits BEFORE it. The one commit
in the session it could not cover is the one carrying the false claim. A range
audit that stops at HEAD^ has this blind spot structurally, not by accident.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD WANTS: either close fisc-yj4w (its eight numbered
children are done and its stated end condition was met -- AGENTS.md's "Issue
tracking" section says a closed epic means its end condition was met, not that
every filed child is done), or leave it open and record in its notes that the
subject of 8010fd1 overstates. Do not amend the commit; the log is the audit
trail.
close_reason:
Answered on fisc-yj4w, 2026-09-03: the epic stays OPEN and the overstatement is recorded in its notes, which is the second of the two options this bead offered. The commit is not amended -- the log is the audit trail.

Both halves of the bead were re-derived before acting. 8010fd1's only diff is a one-line rewrite of fisc-yj4w's description and notes; the bead is open today; and its five children fisc-yj4w.9 through .13 are all still open, all P3.

WHY NOT THE FIRST OPTION. Closing E11 would have been within AGENTS.md's rule -- a closed epic means its end condition was met, and E11's was. It is refused because .9-.13 would then be five beads under a closed epic with no owner, which is the exact condition E10 was filed to fix.

TWO THINGS CARRIED FORWARD RATHER THAN LOST WITH THIS BEAD. (1) The range-audit blind spot it identified is structural, not an accident of that session: an audit over the commits BEFORE it cannot cover the commit making the claim. That is now written on fisc-yj4w beside the overstatement. (2) fisc-yj4w is P1 with only P3 children open -- filed on the epic for the owner rather than acted on, since the priority is theirs to set.

title: A figure repeated in prose across files costs one review pass per copy
description:
MEASURED over the 2026-08-31 badge lane. One pre-existing wrong count -- "the
other six fund groups' revenue ends at their funds", where the document-specific
answer is five for three of the four published columns and six for one -- was
found THREE TIMES, in three files, across three CONSECUTIVE passes:

  75814db (pass 2)  internal/project/fundflows.go:492   the caveat text itself
  5861abe (pass 3)  pkg/cmd/export/data.go:575          spending.html's lede
  4e43cb3 (pass 4)  docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md:186

Three of that lane's 29 findings were one fact. The caveats lane has the same
shape at larger scale: 2b38c0d found "one of them 250 words" false in SIX places
at once (index.html.tmpl, document.go, data.go, year.mjs, README.md, and a copy
written by pass 1's own fix), where the measured longest text is 174 words and
254 is the page total.

THE CHEAP REMEDY is procedural and lands with this change: when you correct a
fact in prose, grep the tree for its copies in the same commit. Note the trap --
`grep -rn "six fund groups"` returns ten further hits that encode a DIFFERENT
and largely true proposition (how many groups the spine prints, not how many
stop at their funds), so the rule is grep-then-read, not grep-then-replace.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is what this bead is for: can anything mechanical help?
A check that a figure appearing in prose in more than one committed file appears
identically in all of them would have caught the "250 words" case and not the
"six fund groups" case, because the second is the same numeral standing for two
different propositions. So the honest scope is probably narrow -- a check over
figures that appear inside a caveat's Text/Summary and are then restated in a
template or a doc. Decide whether that is worth building or whether the grep
rule is the whole answer.
notes:
ANSWERED IN PART, 2026-09-01, by the audit filed as fisc-pm8f.

THE OPEN QUESTION HERE -- "can anything mechanical help?" -- had the wrong shape.
It asked for a check that a figure restated in N files agrees in all of them.
The cheaper answer is to stop having N copies: a count of the tree's own contents
does not belong in prose at all, because it goes stale on the next commit and
tells a reader nothing they could not get by looking. Only an EXTRINSIC count
earns its place -- one about the documents, or one that IS the evidence for a
decision. Both of this bead's worked examples fail that test: "the other six fund
groups" and "250 words" are intrinsic, and under the rule neither would have been
written once, let alone four and six times.

That also dissolves the trap recorded above. The reason a check could not work --
`grep -rn "six fund groups"` returning ten hits that encode a different and
largely true proposition -- is a reason not to automate the FIX. It is not a
reason to keep the copies.

WHAT REMAINS MECHANICAL is narrower and is filed as fisc-owo4: pin the counts
that survive the rule, the way tools/jscheck/layout.mjs already pins app.js's.
Scoped after the sweep, because most of the population is about to be deleted.

The grep-then-read rule stays as written. It is what the sweep itself runs on.

title: A responsive chart: the site has no breakpoints and a fixed 1180x820 viewBox
description:
site/app.js lays every chart out at CHART_WIDTH 1180 by CHART_HEIGHT 820 and scales it with viewBox plus width:100%, and there is no resize listener. site/style.css has exactly ONE responsive rule in 1200 lines -- .series-table .basis { display: none } under 720px -- plus the .figures auto-fit grid.

So on a phone the whole Sankey is scaled to about a third, which takes LABEL_GUTTER's 250px of labels below legibility while leaving the ribbons proportionally correct. Nothing is wrong; nothing is readable.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE: the fix is not a media query. The layout constants feed tools/jscheck/layout.mjs's pinned figures (195 crossings, 57,434,169 of overlap, 14 stale pairs), which are measured at this extent -- so a second extent is a second set of measurements, and app.js's own comments quote the first set in prose that make js verifies. Whoever does this should expect to re-measure rather than to add a breakpoint.

THE DRILL MAKES IT MORE URGENT, not less: an opened view has two columns and far fewer marks, so it is the one shape on this site that WOULD read on a phone.
notes:
2026-09-08, from fisc-yj4w.14: this bead's measurements still hold, and the lane that just landed changed nothing they depend on.

CHART LAYOUT UNTOUCHED. app.js still lays out at CHART_WIDTH 1180 by CHART_HEIGHT 820, there is still no resize listener, and layout.mjs's pinned figures are unmoved. The lane deliberately excluded main, .page-head, .figures, .card, .chart-wrap, .table-scroll and table from the new --measure token, and TestTheStylesheetHasOneTextMeasure has an arm that reddens if the container rule is clamped -- so a future breakpoint has to be added rather than arrived at by accident.

WHAT CHANGED AROUND IT, and it makes this bead cheaper rather than more urgent: prose now sits at 68ch instead of running the container's full width, and every page's apparatus is behind a closed <details>. A phone reader therefore meets a headline, a chart and a short lede, and the panels that used to run past the fold are collapsed. The chart is still scaled to about a third and LABEL_GUTTER's 250px of labels is still below legibility -- nothing here fixes that -- but the page around it no longer needs its own breakpoints.

SO THE WORK IS NARROWER THAN WHEN THIS WAS FILED: a second extent for the chart, and its second set of measurements, with no accompanying layout rework.
2026-09-08: MEASURED SUBJECT for the second extent this bead wants, from fisc-ko1j's design. An opened view is 4 to 34 nodes against the spine's 25, and the ribbon counts differ by an order of magnitude: depth 1 by group (nodes/links/sub-pixel/narrowest) general 34/33/2/0.26px, special-revenue 17/22/2/0.07px, enterprise 13/21/4/0.01px, capital 13/17/1/0.55px, debt-service 4/3/0/60.23px, internal-service 7/6/0/4.88px; depth 2 worst (dept/patrol) 51.38px. debt-service at four nodes on an 820px canvas is the case that argues for a second extent most plainly.

title: The department-funding-sources schedule has no page: 312 facts, pp.85-125
description:
A SECOND PARENT AXIS THE SITE DOES NOT DRAW. spending.html answers which division spends the General Fund and on what. pp.85-125 answer a different question -- WHICH FUNDS PAY FOR A DEPARTMENT -- over 312 facts, 11 department rules, 63 distinct funds and four columns, and no projection selects them.

internal/check/coverage.go declares the scope unprojected with the reason: they are the per-fund decomposition of pp.66-67's TOTAL EXPENDITURES rows, not additional money, so drawing them into the fund-group spine would double the city's expenditure.

THAT REASON DOES NOT RULE OUT A PAGE OF THEIR OWN, which is what fund-flows already is for two other scopes. What it rules out is putting them in the spine.

A TRAP, RECORDED BY THE SURVEY THAT FOUND THE FACTS: they carry the fund but leave Fact.Department EMPTY -- the department is recoverable only from rule_id (funding-city-attorney and so on) and the page. So the projection has to derive a node id from a rule id, which nothing else here does.

AND staleDeclarations WILL FIRE. coverage.go fails RED when a declared scope starts being drawn, and has a partial arm demanding the reason be rewritten when a schedule is only half drawn. Deleting the entry is part of the work, not a follow-up.

Related: fisc-7q6 (the Expenditures by Category block above it), fisc-4ua.2 (department pages).

title: A non-Sankey form for the columns a Sankey cannot draw
description:
THE CAP IS A WORKAROUND FOR A FORM PROBLEM. capColumn folds a drilled column's tail into one aggregate because d3-sankey cannot draw 32 funds whose largest is 34.9% and whose smallest is 0.034% -- measured, and rescaling to the group's own total does not fix it (see fisc-ppkq's correction). The aggregate is honest and it is still 24 funds a reader cannot see.

The columns this is about, all measured against dist/data/fund-flows.json: the 61 individual funds (tier 3) and the 44 division-by-object cells (tier 5). Neither draws as a Sankey column at any canvas height -- docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md carries the arithmetic.

A ranked bar list or a treemap has no such limit: both encode 61 values legibly, neither needs a cap, and both can carry the same provenance links the ribbons do. What that costs is a second mark type in site/app.js, which today draws exactly one.

NOT A CHART-LIBRARY QUESTION. The constraint is that the site vendors d3 and ships app.js unbundled; a bar list is ~40 lines of the d3 already vendored.
notes: 2026-09-08: MORE URGENT UNDER fisc-ko1j, not blocking it. The merged page's depth 1 caps tier 3 at 8, so opening Special Revenue would show 8 named funds and '24 smaller funds' ON index.html rather than on a secondary page. Measured at {0,3,4} with per-tier caps {3:8, 4:24}: capped, special-revenue draws 17 nodes / 22 links / 2 sub-pixel ribbons; uncapped it draws 40 nodes / 49 links / 22 sub-pixel / 9 zero-height nodes and is not a chart. So the cap is still doing what fisc-ppkq measured it doing -- what changes is how prominent the thing it hides becomes. A ranked bar list for that column is the answer this bead already proposes.

title: A citywide {0,3} revenue overview: 61 named funds, and what it would cost to draw them
description:
DECLINED DURING fisc-yj4w.7 AND FILED WITH THE MEASUREMENT THAT WAS WRONG, so the next person does not redo it the same way.

revenue.html opens at {0,2}: eleven revenue categories into six fund groups. The obvious alternative is {0,3} -- straight into NAMED funds -- which is more informative on its face: fund/100 is 49.18% of citywide revenue, fund/620 10.61%, fund/640 6.46%.

THE FIGURE I FIRST DECLINED IT ON WAS FABRICATED. An early probe used a hand-written fold that silently skipped nodes it could not place and reported '8 sub-pixel ribbons'. The real foldDocument REFUSES that set outright: the document's six tier-2 fund-group nodes have no ancestor at tier 0 or 3. So the option does not draw at all as stated, and what it would cost is unknown.

WHAT IT WOULD ACTUALLY NEED: something to say about the tier-2 nodes (a root will not do -- there is no single one citywide), plus a cap, since 61 funds is the same concentration problem one level down from the one that made this document need a fold at all. Whoever picks this up should measure with site/app.js's own shapeFor rather than a probe.
notes:
2026-09-08: RE-SCOPED, not closed. Two things have moved under this bead's framing.

(1) fisc-ko1j MEASURED THE {0,3} FOLD, per fund group rather than citywide, driven through site/app.js's own shapeFor and foldDocument -- which is what this bead asks for and says a probe cannot substitute for. At tiers {0,3,4} with per-tier caps {3:8, 4:24} the six groups give general 34 nodes / 33 links / 2 sub-pixel, special-revenue 17/22/2, enterprise 13/21/4, capital 13/17/1, debt-service 4/3/0, internal-service 7/6/0. The 'something to say about the tier-2 nodes' this bead names is answered by opening ONE group rather than by drawing all six, so the citywide question is narrower than it was, not answered.

(2) WHAT 'A REVENUE OVERVIEW' MEANS IS ITSELF NOW IN QUESTION. fisc-ko1j.7 through fisc-ko1j.12 file a revenue LINE-ITEM tier, so a {0,3} chart may not be the finest revenue view the site has. Do not pick this bead up on its original framing without reading fisc-ko1j.7 first.
MECHANISM NOTE, 2026-09-20: 'a root will not do -- there is no single one citywide' now names a vocabulary the tree does not have. export.View.Root is deleted with the second chart template (fisc-1osz), so a future citywide overview cannot decline the option by reaching for one and would have to say what it does about the tier-2 fund-group nodes some other way. The ARGUMENT is unaffected and is the reason the field's absence costs nothing here: there was no single citywide root to declare. The rest of this bead -- that foldDocument REFUSES the {0,3} set outright, and that whoever picks it up should measure with site/app.js's own shapeFor rather than a probe -- is untouched.

title: A wrapped label that IS a bare number is now neither declarable nor omittable
description:
FOUND 2026-08-30 by the fifth review pass over the ACFR tolerance lane (6df0858..a2dd535). Declined there rather than fixed, because fixing it needs a decision this lane did not have to make and no page in the corpus needs today.

WHAT CHANGED. fisc-hcus added two mirrored refusals to validateRule: a wrapped_labels entry must NOT parse as an amount, and an unmapped_text entry MUST. That closed the dishonest route -- measured, wrapped_labels: ["0.0"] published ACFR p41's whole revenue block with nothing objecting -- and Part.UnmappedText's doc comment now says the two 'cannot be substituted for each other in either direction'.

THE SHAPE IT REOPENS. A page that genuinely wraps a row LABEL which happens to be a bare number -- a fund number wrapped onto its own line, a year, a footnote index -- can no longer declare it. wrapped_labels refuses it as a currency amount; unmapped_text would accept it, under a claim ('this figure belongs to no row') that is FALSE of a wrapped label. So the fragment is refused if undeclared and dishonest if declared, which is fisc-2jk's shape exactly.

NO CONSUMER TODAY. All five committed wrapped_labels entries -- Devel, Development Admin, Services, Administration, Connection -- are words. The refusal costs the corpus nothing, which is why it landed.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUS TO FIX. The parser cannot tell a wrapped numeric LABEL from an orphan FIGURE by looking at the text: both are a bare number in a gap. Options, none free: (a) a third declaration naming which it is, which is a third thing to keep honest; (b) let wrapped_labels carry an explicit note the way unmapped_text does, and refuse an amount only when it has none; (c) decide the case cannot arise and say so, which needs a sweep of the corpus for a wrapped label that parses.

(b) is probably right and is cheap, but it weakens the refusal that was the whole point of fisc-hcus, so it should be decided rather than slipped in.

title: A figure printed BEFORE a block's first row is still neither declarable nor omittable
description:
FOUND 2026-08-30 landing unmapped_text (fisc-hcus). It is the same shape that bead fixed, one gap earlier, and it was left open deliberately rather than missed.

WHERE. checkGap's leading arm (internal/mapping/resolve.go) governs the text between the section anchor and the first mapped row. It honours wrapped_labels and, since fisc-hcus, does NOT honour unmapped_text. So a stray figure there is refused by the digit arm ('figures appear before the first row %q') and there is no honest declaration for it.

WHY unmapped_text WAS NOT WIRED IN THERE, which is the part worth keeping. That gap is where COLUMN HEADERS live, so the arm is already permissive about words: it refuses only text containing a digit. The digit refusal is therefore the ONLY guard standing over the leading gap, and it is what stops a block anchored too early from reading header figures as data. Admitting a declared figure retires it -- and on a total_row_above rule, where the arm already skips the total's own line, there would be nothing left at all.

SO A FIX IS NOT 'also check unmapped_text here'. It needs something that keeps the too-early-block refusal intact: a declaration scoped to the leading gap specifically, or a positional claim ('this figure is on the anchor's line', which is what total_row_above already says for the one case that has come up).

NOT URGENT: no page in the corpus needs it today. ACFR p41's orphan sits between the last row and the total, which unmapped_text now covers. Filed because the asymmetry is real, is written into a code comment as a known gap, and would otherwise be re-derived.

Same family as fisc-2jk, which is why the leading arm marks wrapped_labels used at all.

title: Block's stop_at has no uniqueness guard, unlike section
description:
FOUND 2026-08-30 writing acfr-p0041-gf-general-government (fisc-h96o).

Block (internal/mapping/resolve.go) resolves stop_at with a plain strings.Index from the section anchor and takes the FIRST match. Section goes through anchor(), which supports section_ordinal and refuses an ambiguous match with ErrAmbiguous; stop_at has neither.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN: a stop_at that binds too early leaves rows unfound ('row %q does not occur after ...') and one that binds too late leaves unmapped trailing text, so the downstream arms catch most mis-bindings. What they do not catch is a stop_at that binds early at a point which still happens to leave a well-formed block.

THE LIVE CASE: acfr-p0041-gf-general-government declares stop_at: "Fire" -- a four-character substring, unique after its anchor on p41 today. That is a property of the PAGE, not of the code, so it is asserted in TestACFRp0041GeneralGovernmentStopsAtFire rather than assumed. A guard in Block would make the assertion unnecessary.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE: a stop_at_ordinal mirroring section_ordinal, or requiring uniqueness by default. Note the second would need measuring against all 143 committed parts before it could land -- several may rely on first-match today.

title: A rule claims its printed total on every page of its parts, and it is printed on one
description:
FILED 2026-08-30 while landing fisc-lkx, whose fix introduced this deliberately and said so in the code.

WHAT LANDED. unclaimedFundTotals' `claimed` set gained a page dimension: the key is now (doc_id, page, label) where it was (doc_id, label). A ROLLUP claims on the one page it declares, which is exact -- Rollup.Page is required and its total is printed there. A RULE claims on EVERY page of its parts, which is an over-claim.

WHY THE OVER-CLAIM. A rule's total_row is printed on ONE of its pages. For a plain rule that is whichever part's page carries it; for a total_spans_parts rule it is the one (*Resolver).totalBearingPart finds, and finding it needs the page text. internal/check/rulefunds.go's clause 2 has s.Files and s.Docs but deliberately does not resolve: reaching for s.Resolvers would make a vocabulary check depend on the corpus being readable, so a mapping error would surface as a fund-registry finding.

IT IS STRICTLY NARROWER THAN WHAT IT REPLACED, which is why it was acceptable to land. Before: one mapped total silenced that label on every swept page of the document. Now: on every page of the claiming rule's own parts. The residue is a rule with parts on pages A and B whose total is printed only on A -- an identically-worded unclaimed total on B would still be silenced.

MEASURED TODAY: no fund-bearing rule has parts on more than one page except the eleven total_spans_parts rules of pp.85-125, and no fund-total label repeats across the currently-swept pages at all, so the residue is empty on the committed corpus. It is a latent hole, not a live one.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and they differ in what they cost:
  (a) let clause 2 take the bearing page from the resolver. Exact, and couples this check to the corpus being readable.
  (b) have the parser record which part bears the total at parse time, so File carries it and no resolution is needed here. More work, and the information is useful elsewhere -- CheckSpanningTotals recomputes it on every call.

Prefer (b) if anything else ever needs the bearing part; (a) is not worth the coupling on its own.

TEST TO WRITE EITHER WAY: a two-part rule whose total is printed on the first page, and an identically-worded unclaimed total on the second, reported rather than silenced.
acceptance_criteria: a rule's printed total is claimed only on the page that prints it; an identically-worded total on another page of the same rule's parts is still reported; the committed corpus stays green

title: A subtotal printed ABOVE its own rows cannot be a total_row
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 while mapping ACFR p41 (fisc-9hf), and it is the reason the tier-2 tolerance (fisc-1wr.2) found no consumer on that page.

THE MECHANISM. (*Resolver).totalAnchor (internal/mapping/resolve.go:539) resolves a rule's total_row with strings.Index(text[blk.End:], rule.TotalRow) -- the anchor must occur AFTER the block. CheckSpanningTotals' totalBearingPart does the same. Every schedule mapped so far prints its total below its rows, so nothing has needed otherwise.

THE PAGE THAT DOES OTHERWISE. ACFR p41 prints 'General Government:  18.45' and then its five constituent rows (City Council 0.22, City Manager 5.30, City Attorney 2.66, Administrative Services 7.39, General Services 2.87) BELOW it. The five sum to 18.44 against the printed 18.45 -- a real discrepancy of $10,000 on a page whose least significant printed digit is $10,000, at 5 terms, which is exactly the calibrated consumer a document-derived tolerance wants: 0.5 x 0.01 x 5 = 0.025 million of slack against a 0.01 million error, 2.5 units rather than the 7 a fourteen-term sum would give.

It cannot be expressed. There is no way to say 'the total for these rows is printed above them'.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PAGE. It is the difference between the tolerance mechanism having a real consumer and having none. The page's OTHER printed total, Total Expenditures, ties EXACTLY under the reading the city's own structure implies -- its ten top-level rows sum to 137.01 to the cent (TestACFRp0041ExpendituresTieUnderTheTopLevelReading). The only way to manufacture a discrepancy against it is to descend past the General Government subtotal into its five children and compare fourteen leaves against a total printed over ten rows, which asserts an equality the city never states.

WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE: either a total_above: true flag on the rule, or letting the total_row anchor be resolved against the section text preceding the block. The second is likelier right, since the subtotal sits between the section anchor and the first row -- i.e. in checkGap's leading gap, which today refuses any text containing a digit. That refusal exists for a good reason (a block starting too early reads header figures as data), so this needs care rather than loosening.

BLOCKS fisc-1wr.2 having a consumer in the ACFR MD&A. The other candidate is ACFR p42, whose revenue block misses by 0.1 in four columns and needs the non-amount-column decision instead (fisc-4ua.4).
acceptance_criteria: a rule can assert a total the document prints above its rows; ACFR p41's General Government subtotal is checked against its five sub-rows; a tolerance one printed unit too tight goes red on it
close_reason: total_row_above landed at d9a5b80. A rule may now assert a total the document prints above its rows, bounded by requiring that total to BE the part's section anchor -- so it names one printed line at a position Block already resolves through anchor(), and checkGap's leading arm skips exactly that line and refuses every digit after it. ACFR p41's General Government subtotal is checked against its five sub-rows and is this corpus's only tolerance consumer (fisc-1wr.2). Mutations in the commit message; the one that matters is that moving the anchor one line up to 'Current:' STILL gives 'figures appear before the first row', pinned by TestTotalRowAboveStillRefusesABlockThatStartsTooEarly, which goes red if the skip clears the whole gap. Left open and filed: fisc-km5n, Block resolves stop_at by first match with no uniqueness guard -- the new rule's stop_at 'Fire' is asserted unique by a test instead.

title: row_labels_name_funds over verb-phrased labels asserts nothing, and the parser cannot see it
description:
The bare-label arm of row-funds-match-their-anchors defers to the prefix arm when a row's label carries a rowAnchorPrefixes verb phrase ("Transfer From ", "to "). That is correct -- the prefix arm asserts strictly more, fund AND direction, and resolving "Transfer From General Fund  to Horizons" whole finds nothing -- but it leaves a declaration that asserts nothing new.

A rule whose rows are ALL verb-phrased may declare row_labels_name_funds and the declaration is a no-op: every row is read by the prefix arm exactly as it would have been without it. Measured before the deferral landed: flagging p76-transfers-in-special-revenue took the check to FAIL over 121 subjects with three spurious findings and each row counted twice; with the deferral it is PASS at 118, identical to not declaring it.

That is the 'declaration that cannot fail' shape validateTotalRowKinds and validateRowLabelFunds both refuse elsewhere -- a claim recording an author's belief rather than a property of the page.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED WHERE THE OTHERS ARE. rowAnchorPrefixes lives in internal/check/rowfunds.go and internal/mapping may not read it; the parser has no way to tell a verb-phrased label from a bare one. Options, none free: (a) move the prefix list into internal/mapping and have the parser refuse the declaration where every non-skip row is phrased -- puts a check's vocabulary in the schema package; (b) report it from the check as a finding or a summary clause rather than refusing it at parse -- cheap, and the only place that can see it; (c) leave it, and say so in Rule.RowLabelsNameFunds' doc comment.

(b) is probably right: the check already keeps two counters for rows it cannot claim, and this is a third statement of the same kind.

Found by /code-review over 4b78c1e^..e96fd5b, third pass, and deliberately not fixed there -- the deferral was the correctness half and this is the hygiene half.
acceptance_criteria: a rule declaring row_labels_name_funds over rows the prefix arm already reads is either refused or reported, and the choice is stated in Rule.RowLabelsNameFunds' doc comment
close_reason:
Retired by the fourth review pass's fix, one commit after it was filed, and on a premise that was already wrong.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS FALSE. It said a verb-phrased label under row_labels_name_funds is 'read by the prefix arm exactly as it would have been without it'. It is not: the parser forbids a counterpart on a declaring rule, so far == 0, and a row labelled 'Transfer From X' resolves as the FAR end with want == far == 0 -- so the prefix arm compares nothing. Measured: injecting one drops subjects 118 -> 117, the check stays PASS, and the row is reported under 'no printed anchor on their own line', which is false because the label is printed. The deferral turned a noisy defect into a silent one.

THE FIX IS TO REFUSE, NOT TO DEFER. row-funds-match-their-anchors now reports a finding when a declaring rule carries a verb-phrased label: the author has said something untrue about their own page. That closes the hole AND does what this bead was filed to do -- a declaration that asserts nothing can no longer be written -- so no separate work remains. Subject count is unchanged at 118, which is the assertion that catches both earlier attempts: attempt one inflated it to 121 by reading each row twice, attempt two deflated it to 117 by reading one not at all.

Proved by TestAVerbPhrasedLabelUnderTheDeclarationIsRefused; replacing the refusal's condition with false reports pass over 118 anchors.

title: The fisc-9x1z / fisc-er24 worked example loses its ids when commit-claims-are-checkable is retired
description:
AGENTS.md's 'Before you quote a number' tells the invented-id story anonymously: 'Two commits later, a bead correctly filed was cited under an invented id.' The actual identifiers live only in the retired memory commit-claims-are-checkable and in e630516's commit body -- grep -rn 'fisc-9x1z' over *.md and *.go returns nothing.

THE FACTS, recorded here so the worked example keeps its ids: a bead was correctly filed and then cited in a commit message as fisc-9x1z, which does not exist. The real id was fisc-er24 (still open: whether bd doctor's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md sync check fights the @AGENTS.md import). That is the worst of the three claim-failure modes AGENTS.md names, because the work IS tracked and only the pointer is dead, so nobody looking at the bead graph finds anything wrong. bd create prints the id; read it back.

Also lost with that memory and recorded here: the mechanical cause was a batch of scripted edits with an 'assert s.count(old)==1' in the middle, which aborted at the second edit so every later edit silently never ran, and the message had been drafted from the plan rather than from the diff. The habit that catches it is now in AGENTS.md; the literal assertion form is here.

NOT WORTH DOING NOW -- this bead is the record. Close it only if the story is ever written up somewhere a session reads.

title: Check whether bd doctor's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md sync check fights the @AGENTS.md import
description:
CLAUDE.md is now two lines -- a heading and `@AGENTS.md` -- because AGENTS.md is
the file every other agent tool reads verbatim and `@` is an import rather than
a link, so the text still arrives in context (5794a60).

UNVERIFIED AND WORTH VERIFYING: a review pass reported that `bd doctor` carries
an "AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md in sync" check whose failure message is "user-authored
content has diverged" and whose remediation is to re-sync CLAUDE.md FROM
AGENTS.md -- which would overwrite the import with a full copy and undo the
consolidation. It also reported that a symlink is the form bd blesses.

NOT CONFIRMED HERE, and the reason is recorded so nobody re-derives it: this
checkout runs bd in embedded mode and `bd doctor` refuses to run at all --
"'bd doctor' is not yet supported in embedded mode". So the check could not be
exercised. The finding is plausible rather than measured.

WHAT TO DO. Run `bd doctor` in a checkout where it works (or read the bd source
for the sync check), and then pick one of:
  (a) nothing, if the check tolerates an import;
  (b) make CLAUDE.md a symlink to AGENTS.md, if that is the form bd blesses --
      note this loses the explanatory comment CLAUDE.md currently carries about
      why the direction cannot be reversed, which would have to move into
      AGENTS.md;
  (c) suppress or configure the check.

RELATED AND ALREADY KNOWN: bd regenerates its own "Beads Issue Tracker" block in
BOTH root files and that block asserts agents must `git push`. CLAUDE.md carries
a comment saying the block reappearing below the import is harmless, and that it
must be moved back if it ever lands above. That is a separate mechanism from the
sync check.

Found by /code-review over 5794a60^..HEAD.
acceptance_criteria: bd doctor's behaviour against a CLAUDE.md that is an @AGENTS.md import is measured rather than assumed, and CLAUDE.md is left in whatever form survives it

title: Category pages: required when assignable, deferred because it churns 40 fixtures
description:
validateCategory checks the SHAPE of a category pages list (1-based, ascending, once each) and not its PRESENCE. Presence is defensible on todays data and was deliberately not taken.

THE MEASUREMENT. 3 of the 25 committed categories carry no pages, and they are exactly the 3 assignable: false rollups -- fund-balance, taxes, transfers. So "required when assignable" holds on the committed file with zero violations. internal/registry/registry_test.go TestLoadRealRegistries now cmp.Diffs the page-less slugs against the unassignable ones, so the day that stops being true this bead becomes landable and the test says so.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED. It churns 40 category entries across three fixture files -- 28 in internal/registry/load_test.go, 11 in internal/check/fixture_test.go, 1 in internal/registry/registry_test.go -- and in load_test.go it changes the EXPECTED ERROR STRING of every case whose fault is validated after validateCategory, because the new arm fires first. That is a large diff for a rule with no live violation, and bundling it would have hidden the four refusals that commit did land.

SHAPE. Add the presence arm to validateCategory gated on the assignable flag -- note Assignable is set by loadTaxonomy AFTER validateCategory returns (load.go), so either the arm moves to the caller or the raw pointer is threaded in.

Filed 2026-08-29 while landing fisc-iki; the code comment on validatePagesShape points here.

title: Category pages and contra_rows are checked for internal consistency, never against the printed page
description:
validateCategory now refuses a contra row on a page its category does not list (internal/registry/load.go). That arm is INTERNAL CONSISTENCY ONLY and the code comment says so: nothing bounds Category.Pages to a page the document actually has, so pages: [66, 127, 9999] with contra_rows: [{term: x, page: 9999}] loads clean. Widening `pages` is simultaneously the honest remedy for a contra row on a page the category really is printed on, and the way to defeat the check.

WHY IT CANNOT BE TAKEN AT LOAD. registry.Load(fsys) reads three YAML files and has no corpus to ask. A category also carries no doc_id, so even a page COUNT would not say which document to bound against -- pp.66-67 (Budget Book) and the ACFR pages both appear in this file.

THE SHAPE THAT CAN. internal/registry/registry_test.go already has TestFundAliasesArePrintedOnTheirPages and TestDepartmentsRegistryMatchesThePages, which read the extracted corpus and assert a registry entry is printed where it says it is. A category-alias and contra-row equivalent is the same idea one channel over: for each category alias term and each contra_rows[].term, assert the string occurs in data/extracted/<doc>/pages/pNNNN.txt for the declared page. That also gives the doc_id question an answer -- try the documents and require exactly one to match, or add an explicit doc to the taxonomy schema.

Found by the third pass of /code-review over the fisc-iki lane, 2026-08-29, and confirmed by mutation.

title: [docs] Three contract documents state counts the branch they describe has already falsified
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-27, each verified against the built documents.

(1) docs/sankey-contract.md:184 says 'No document publishes a constraint tier yet, so the paragraph above is an obligation on the first one that does.' fisc verify reports constraint-tier-vocabulary over 247 nodes in 4 documents. Worse, docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md:155 sends readers to that exact section 'for the argument' -- so the drill-down's own contract points at a sentence denying the drill-down exists.

(2) docs/sankey-contract.md:28 says 'Today that is sankey, sankey-2027 and revenue-trends, pinned as literal strings by TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged.' That test pins SEVEN stems; the four fund-flows ones are missing from the prose. The test's own doc comment likewise still says 'the three published paths'. README.md:137 has the matching gap: it lists two of three per-document contracts and never mentions docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md.

(3) docs/revenue-trends-contract.md:82 says 'Eight of the 924 are sign: contra ... and they carry negative amounts', which invites a consumer to find negatives by sign == contra. NINE points are negative; the ninth is Prior Year - Unsecured, General Fund, FY2023-24, token (20,033) -> -20,033, carrying sign: positive. internal/export/page.go:419 already says 'Nine cells ship', and revenue.html renders 18 contra occurrences (9 cells x td + mark bar). The code is right and the contract undercounts.

Same class as the caveat fixed in 22862e0: a true sentence that outlived what it described. These are docs rather than published prose, so they are P3 -- but (1) is load-bearing, because another contract cites it.
close_reason: All three items plus two the bead did not name, in the commit above. Item (3) was worse than filed: the revenue-trends contract undercounts nine negatives as eight AND tells a consumer to filter on 'sign: contra', a key the document does not publish at any level -- unfollowable, not merely stale. Also fixed: TestTheCommittedStemsAreUnchanged's own doc comment said 'the three published paths' while pinning seven, and README listed two of three contracts. Constraint-tier wording is 'non-empty constraint_tier', not 'present': there is no omitempty, so every node carries the key.

title: [site] paintYearWords composes two per-year strings as JS literals that copy the template, and nothing pins either
description:
FOUND BY /code-review 2026-08-27, verified by mutation.

paintYearWords' doc comment states 'every string it writes was built by the packager' -- which is why document.title was moved into Go as sankeyTitle (fisc-rn0). Two writes were left behind:

  site/app.js ~:1302  #chart-title   'Sankey diagram of the ' + year.label + ' ' + year.basis + ' budget'
  site/app.js ~:1297  #counts-line   the same shape

Both are hand copies of site/index.html.tmpl (~:125 and ~:168). Neither is pinned: tools/jscheck/year.mjs's painted() never reads #chart-title at all, and its counts assertion RE-COMPOSES the same literal rather than comparing against the template. Verified: replacing the #chart-title string with obvious nonsense leaves the suite at 0 FAILs, and no Go test greps chart-title.

CONCRETE FAILURE: edit the template's wording -- to name the scope, say -- and the page ships with a server-rendered SVG accessible name that silently reverts to the OLD wording the instant a reader touches the year toggle. That is fisc-rn0 exactly, in the same function, in the writes its fix did not reach.

The #chart-title one is an accessibility label, so the drift is invisible to a sighted reader entirely.
notes:
2026-09-08 STALE ON ALL THREE CLAIMS, re-derived against the tree while landing fisc-yj4w.14, which touched paintYearWords and paintChartName. None of the staleness is from that lane; the writes were moved before it.

(1) "site/app.js ~:1302 #chart-title 'Sankey diagram of the ' + year.label + ..." -- THAT LITERAL IS NOT IN app.js. Measured: `grep -n "Sankey diagram of the" site/app.js` returns nothing. paintChartName now writes shownYear.chart_title, the packager's string, whole. The only occurrences in the tree are jscheck FIXTURES (drill.mjs:107, year.mjs:60, fold.mjs:81), which is where a stand-in for the packager belongs.

(2) "tools/jscheck/year.mjs's painted() never reads #chart-title at all" -- it does, at year.mjs:128, and asserts it equals year.chart_title at :429 ("the chart's accessible name is the packager's chart_title, written whole").

(3) "its counts assertion RE-COMPOSES the same literal rather than comparing against the template" -- it does not. templateCounts (year.mjs:36) reads the #counts-line span out of index.html.tmpl AND chart.html.tmpl by regex and substitutes the numbers, and :350/:363 compare against that. A further arm asserts the two templates' wordings are identical.

THE BEAD'S OWN MUTATION IS THE PROOF, run rather than reasoned about. It says "replacing the #chart-title string with obvious nonsense leaves the suite at 0 FAILs". Replacing both branches of that write with "NONSENSE" now reddens two arms:
    FAIL  each fund-flows page opens, and every word on it describes the chart beside it
    FAIL  the chart's accessible name is the packager's chart_title, written whole
`make js` exits 2 under the mutation and 0 on revert.

Closed as done-by-other-work rather than edited, since nothing it asks for is left.
close_reason: Stale on all three claims, re-derived and mutation-checked 2026-09-08: the #chart-title literal is gone from app.js, year.mjs reads and asserts #chart-title, and its counts arm compares against the template rather than re-composing it. The bead's own stated mutation now reddens two arms.

comments.author: Jon Crussell
comments.text: Premise re-measured 2026-09-07 before working: the two app.js literals this bead cites no longer exist -- paintChartName repaints #chart-title from yearView.ChartTitle (built in Go, internal/export/page.go) and paintCounts composes #counts-line from the packager's counts. The copies survived one seam over: index.html.tmpl and chart.html.tmpl hand-composed both sentences, pinned by nothing (rewording both left go test ./internal/export ok and make js at 0 FAILs), and year.mjs still never read #chart-title and re-composed the counts literal (appending nonsense to the #chart-title write: 0 FAILs). Fixed by handing the templates years[0].ChartTitle -- direction (a), copy removed -- and by pinning the counts wording against the templates' own span in year.mjs, since (a) is impossible for counts: the sentence depends on the drilled/folded projection's ribbon count and cited-fact set, client state the packager cannot foresee.

title: rule-funds clause 2 claims totals per DOCUMENT and reports them per PAGE
description:
unclaimedFundTotals sweeps the pages a fund-bearing rule reads and reports every printed fund total no rule or rollup declares. Its stated claim is per page -- "on the pages a schedule maps, the schedule maps all of it" -- and its "claimed" set is keyed on (doc_id, printed label) with NO page dimension.

So one page mapped total silences an identical printed total on every other swept page of the same document, and an entirely unmapped fund section on a swept page goes invisible: the exact hole clause 2 exists to close.

MEASURED, and no collision exists today: rollup gf-total-revenues (page 130) claims "Total General Fund" for the whole document, and p0166 and p0172 print that same line. Neither is swept yet. But both adjoin pp.167-170, whose 23 division rules now declare fund: 100, so any rule whose parts reach p166 or p172 opens the hole.

AND 1148392 WIDENED THE EXPOSURE in a second way: the set(claimed, ...) call was moved ahead of both guards (correctly, for fisc-948), so rules that declare NO fund and rules whose columns declare two now also plant document-wide claims.

The fix is a page dimension on the key, which needs deciding where a rollup total is considered printed -- a rollup declares one page, a rule declares parts.

Found by /code-review of the drill-down branch, 2026-08-27, and independently by a second reviewer in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: a printed fund total on one page is not silenced by an identically-worded total claimed on another; a test with the same label on two swept pages reports the unclaimed one
notes:
2026-08-29 TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT MAKE THE MUTATION PROOF CHEAP, taken while
scoping a landing plan. Neither changes this bead's premise, which held on
re-derivation: set(claimed, f.DocID, ru.TotalRow) at internal/check/rulefunds.go
and the lookup claimed[docID][label] both carry no page dimension, exactly as
described.

(1) p0166.txt contains exactly ONE line matching "Total" -- "Total General Fund".
So appending mapping.Part{Page: 166} to a fund-bearing rule brings exactly one
candidate into the sweep and no noise. Today gf-total-revenues claims that label
document-wide from page 130, so the check reports PASS: the defect, green. With a
page dimension on the key it should report FAIL with one finding naming p166 and
fund 100. p0172.txt prints the same label and is likewise unswept.

(2) No fund-total label repeats across the currently-swept pages (pp.127-140,
pp.167-170) -- every one occurs exactly once. So the narrower keying should not
redden the committed corpus. That is a prediction until the test runs, not a
measurement of the check's behaviour.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THE BEAD NAMES IS STILL OPEN and is the reason this is not a
one-line fix: a rollup declares one page, but a rule declares parts, and
total_spans_parts means the printed total is on one part while the rows are on
several. A rule claiming its total_row on EVERY page of its parts is an
over-claim, but it is strictly narrower than today's document-wide claim and does
not need s.Resolvers. If that is the route taken, say so in the comment and file
the narrowing separately rather than reaching for the resolver here.
close_reason:
Landed at 3302fb0. unclaimedFundTotals' claimed set is keyed on (doc_id, page, label) where it was (doc_id, label).

THE PREMISE HELD ON RE-DERIVATION, as the 2026-08-29 note said it would: set(claimed, f.DocID, ru.TotalRow) and the lookup claimed[docID][label] both carried no page dimension, while the check's own stated claim is per page -- 'on the pages a schedule maps, the schedule maps all of it'.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THE BEAD NAMED IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THE ROUTE IT PREDICTED. 'A rollup declares one page, but a rule declares parts, and total_spans_parts means the printed total is on one part while the rows are on several. A rule claiming its total_row on EVERY page of its parts is an over-claim, but it is strictly narrower than today's document-wide claim and does not need s.Resolvers. If that is the route taken, say so in the comment and file the narrowing separately.' That is the route, the comment says so, and the narrowing is fisc-id8b.

THE PROOF COMMITTED IS NOT THE ONE THE BEAD PROPOSED. It suggested appending Part{Page: 166} to a fund-bearing rule, since p0166 prints 'Total General Fund' which rollup gf-total-revenues claims document-wide from p130. That works once and leaves nothing behind. TestAClaimOnOnePageDoesNotSilenceAnotherPage is hermetic instead -- two inline pages printing the same line, claimed on one -- and asserts the finding names the unclaimed page and not the claimed one, AND that claiming both silences both, so the fix rejects the unclaimed PAGE rather than the shared label. Proven failable by making the lookup ignore the page: 'findings = 0, want exactly the unclaimed p166 total'.

The bead's prediction (2) held: no fund-total label repeats across the currently-swept pages, so the narrower keying did not redden the committed corpus. rule-funds-match-their-headings still reports 102 rules and passes.

title: [export] the trends page reconciles rendered cells against counts.points and prints counts.facts
description:
internal/export/page.go's buildTrendsPage compares the number of rendered cells against meta.Counts.Points, and the sentence that guard exists to protect prints a DIFFERENT number: revenue.html.tmpl:45 renders {{.Facts}} ('N figures in all'), fed from meta.Counts.Facts.

THE TWO ARE INDEPENDENT BY DESIGN AND THE CODE SAYS SO. internal/project/trends.go's TrendCounts doc comment states that facts is computed off the SELECTION and points off the series actually BUILT, and that 'a document that dropped a series publishes points below facts'. So a document with counts.facts 924, counts.points 920 and 920 rendered cells passes the reconciliation, exports successfully, and publishes a lede claiming 924 figures over a table carrying 920 linked ones -- the 'page whose own prose contradicts what it shows' the guard's own comment claims to have closed.

Two ways out, and they are not equivalent: reconcile rendered against Facts as well (the lede keeps its meaning and a dropped series goes red), or render Counts.Points in the lede (the sentence becomes true and the dropped series stays silent). The first is the one the guard's comment implies.

Found by /code-review of the drill-down branch, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: the number the trends lede prints is the number the packager reconciles against; a test drops a series and the export refuses
close_reason: Reconciled against counts.facts as well as counts.points, in a7abd86 -- the first of the bead's two ways out, which is the one the guard's own comment implies. Settles what the bead left open: reconciling against facts costs nothing legitimate, because trends.go appends exactly one Point per selected fact and counts facts as len(selected), so the producer cannot emit facts != points and a short series is short both. TestAShortSeriesDoesNotShiftItsNeighbours was itself an instance of the defect (it lowered points and left facts) and now sets both.

title: [bug] View.YearStems on a trends view is silently dropped, which is the trap the adjacent Lede rule refuses
description:
Found by /code-review of the fisc-rmx landing, 2026-08-27.

internal/export/export.go declares View.YearStems and Options/View validation refuses a Lede on any non-TrendsTemplate view -- a deliberate, documented refusal, because a field the template will not render is a caller's intent thrown away in silence.

YearStems has the mirror-image hole and no such rule. Only buildSankeyPage reads it; buildTrendsPage does not. So a caller setting YearStems on a TrendsTemplate view gets no year control, no error, and no way to tell which of the two happened. A trends document over four columns has no year to switch between -- fisc-qkh's close reason says exactly that, and it is why Options.YearStems became View.YearStems -- so the field is meaningless there, in the same way and for the same reason a Lede is meaningless on a Sankey view.

FIX: the same shape as the Lede refusal, in the same function, so a reader meets both rules together.

NOT INTRODUCED BY fisc-rmx -- that change rewrote yearStems' derivation, not its validation -- so it is filed rather than folded in.
acceptance_criteria: View.validate refuses YearStems on a view whose template does not render it, in the shape the Lede rule already uses; a test names the field and the template
close_reason: templateRendersAYearControl plus a View.validate arm, in a7abd86. Both arms pinned: the refusal in TestWriteRefusesAnUnrenderableViewSet, the acceptance in TestBothChartTemplatesAcceptYearStems. One correction to the bead: TWO templates render a year control, not one -- the drill-down grew one after this was filed, so 'v.Template == SankeyTemplate' would have been born stale.

title: A drill-down's tier-2 vocabulary is seven fund groups, not the spine's six
description:
docs/sankey-contract.md's tier table has one column, 'on the spine', and gives tier 2 as 6. A second document at another scope does not inherit that number.

MEASURED: revenue-by-fund spans SEVEN fund groups -- general, enterprise, capital, debt-service, special-revenue, internal-service AND permanent. pp.66-67 print no Permanent column at all, which is fisc-u8o. So a revenue drill-down folding tier 3 to tier 2 produces a fund-group node the spine document does not contain, and the two documents' tier-2 vocabularies differ by one.

internal/project's builtinLabels ALREADY carries 'fund-group/permanent' -> 'Permanent Funds', so the label is there and nothing fails. That is exactly why this is worth filing: the difference is invisible until someone compares the two charts and finds a column in one that is absent from the other, with no note anywhere saying which is right.

WHAT IT COSTS: the contract's table needs a column per document rather than a copy of the spine's counts, and site/app.js's FUND_ORDER is six ids -- a seventh group has no place in the measured colour ordering and no swatch, so buildLegend would skip it and linkColor would fall through to --muted. fisc-y0k's CVD re-run has to cover seven, not six.

Found in peer review of a landing plan, 2026-08-27.
acceptance_criteria: the contract states tier counts per document rather than only for the spine; a seventh fund group has a colour and a legend entry, or the document declares why it does not
notes:

2026-09-05 RELEASED FROM in_progress. It has been claimed since 2026-08-27 and
nothing has moved on it, because its own 2026-08-27 note parks the only remaining

That is a correct decision and it is why the claim is wrong -- an issue waiting

ONE OF THE TWO BEADS IT WAITS ON HAS MOVED. fisc-f75 is CLOSED: its acceptance
