DESIGN: either the field goes and the arm's branch with it, or something can populate it and a test shows it doing so. Chose neither in the landing commit to keep that commit's artifact diff exactly the four transfers rungs.
close_reason: Deleted with the decline path: rungsDoc.Skipped, skippedStep, the reasons table and drawnTier.Unanswered are gone from pkg/cmd/export/rungs.go, and the SKIPPED and REASONS branches from tools/jscheck/rungs.mjs, in the commit that answers the kept flank (schema_version 3). Every rung the walk reaches is answered or the artifact does not build; there is no allowance left to populate.

title: A cut no published document draws is undeclared: facts-are-projected's one surviving proposition after Covered replaced it
description:
Filed from L3.4, which deleted facts-are-projected and its unprojectedScopes map.

WHAT REPLACED IT. structure.Covered, run by cuts-tie-along-the-lattice: every fact is admitted by exactly one cut or by a declared residue, and a fact in neither is a finding. That is the cut-grain form of the incident the check was born from -- a rule's scope mistyped to all-funds-gross-detail moved twenty facts out of the chart with every check green -- and TestFactsMovedOutOfEveryProjectionFail now asserts it on that check.

WHAT WAS NOT REPLACED. facts-are-projected also said: every fact is in some PUBLISHED projection's slice, or its scope is declared undrawn with a reason. A scope that is a cut and that no published document selects is now silent. Over the committed corpus that is one scope, acfr-general-fund-summary (ACFR MD&A p41, 20 facts), whose declaration was the map's one entry; its argument moved to docs/acfr-history-contract.md. A second such scope would be a state (a schedule mapped and cut before its document exists, as revenue-by-fund once was) rather than a wrong figure, which is why this is P4.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE THIS. A declaration on the cut -- or beside PublishedDocuments -- that a cut is deliberately drawn by no document, with the reason and the bead; and an arm that fails on a cut no published scope set selects and no declaration excuses, and on a declaration for a cut some document now draws. staleDeclarations in the deleted coverage.go is the shape.

title: structure.Comparable is exported and returns an unexported type, so its result is unnameable outside the package
description:
HYGIENE, found 2026-09-17 while sizing Lane 3 against internal/structure as
shipped at 513ed04. Filed rather than fixed because Lane 3 is the first caller
from outside the package and the right answer depends on what that caller needs.

Comparable (internal/structure/containment.go:161) is exported and returns
(restriction, error), where restriction (:132) is unexported. A caller in
internal/check can bind the value with := and pass it nowhere, because nothing
exported accepts a restriction: Contain (:217) computes its own. So the exported
return value is unusable and the only thing a caller outside the package can take
from Comparable is the error.

That is not obviously wrong -- "is this pair comparable, and if not, say why" is a
real question and the error is the whole answer. But an exported function whose
exported result cannot be named or used is a seam that reads as offering
something it does not.

ACCEPTANCE, whichever Lane 3 finds it needs: either Comparable returns only an
error and the restriction stays internal to Contain's path, or restriction is
exported with a doc comment saying what a caller does with one. Decide it in the
commit that first calls Comparable from internal/check, not in a later sweep.
close_reason: DECIDED in Lane 3 commit L3.1, the commit that first calls internal/structure from internal/check. Comparable now returns only an error: the restriction stays internal to Compare's path (restrict), and the one caller that will need the intersected slice -- L3.2's peer check -- lives inside the package. Measured: no caller outside internal/structure referenced Comparable or the restriction type at 96fda0d.

title: Registry.Departments() returns a slice of an unexported type, so no narrow interface can declare it
description:
internal/registry/registry.go's Departments() has signature []department -- an exported method returning an unexported type. A consumer holding a narrow interface (internal/check's Vocabulary, internal/project's Labels) cannot declare that method at all, because it cannot name the type.

FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING fisc-ko1j.12.8, and worked around rather than fixed: check.Vocabulary needed to ask whether a slug is a department, and the workaround was an exported Department(slug) bool PREDICATE plus renaming the unexported accessor to departmentEntry. A predicate is the right shape for that one caller -- what the check needs is whether the fact joins -- so this is not a defect today.

IT BECOMES ONE WHEN A CONSUMER NEEDS THE ENTRY. Division is exported and Division(slug) returns it; department is not, so anything wanting a department's label or document_term through an interface has no route. fisc-xhw (department pages) is the likely first caller: a page headed by a department will want its label.

THE FIX IS TO EXPORT THE TYPE, matching Division, and the cost is that department and Department would then need distinguishing -- ba1b99f's range already renamed the accessor to departmentEntry, so that part is done.

title: No shipped step keeps a capped column, so an expansion crossing a drill is latent
description:
MEASURED while building fisc-ko1j.12.6 (W5). An expansion lives on the rung (Rung.expanded), and a window's kept flank is a filter of rung.chart -- the chart as the reader saw it -- so a flank taken from a column the reader had expanded would be drawn expanded with no code for it. That path is never taken on the committed corpus.

WHY, measured over both published columns. Every kept flank the five shipped steps declare is either a single-node column (the fund step keeps tier 2, which is the one group; the division and object-category steps keep tier 3 and tier 2, one node each) or the spine's ten revenue categories (the fund-group step keeps tier 0) -- and the spine has no caps at all, being drawn at depth 0 where no step applies. So no flank has ever carried a folded tail.

TWO CLAUSES ARE GUARDS FOR IT AND ONE ARM HOLDS THEM. expandable() refuses an aggregate at a tier this rung declares no cap for, because such a mark can only have come from the chart above and expanding it would redraw the same chart; and it refuses a tier already expanded. Dropping BOTH clauses leaves every arm green except the one that asks the predicate directly with a constructed node (drill.mjs, 'Enter on the folded tail draws its column uncapped') -- measured as a mutation.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT REACHABLE: a step whose Keep names a tier the step above caps, which needs a column of more than cap+1 nodes at a tier that is ALSO a flank. export.validateSteps accepts the shape; no view declares it. If one ever does, the arm to add is that the kept flank comes through expanded and that the chip in the breadcrumb belongs to the rung that made the expansion.

Neighbours: fisc-xsc8 (jscheck draws no chart), fisc-mvrt (the expanded column's gutter).

title: The gap ribbon's Kind cell in the flow table is blank, which reads as a missing value
description:
markGap (site/app.js) gives its link no kind, deliberately: a kind says which boundary the money crosses, and the difference between two schedules crosses nothing either of them printed. buildTable prints KIND_LABEL[l.kind] || l.kind, so the row's Kind cell comes out empty.

MEASURED 2026-09-13, the FY2026-27 services-and-supplies row: ['Services & Supplies category', 'Difference between the two schedules', '$250,000', '', '◇ inferred', '', ''] -- the fourth cell is the Kind column and the fifth says '◇ inferred'.

WHAT IS RIGHT ABOUT IT is that nothing is claimed. What is wrong with it is that an empty table cell is indistinguishable from a value that failed to render, and this is the one row on the page a reader is most likely to interrogate.

OPTIONS, none of them obviously right: a KIND_LABEL entry for "" reading "not classified"; a kind taken from the centre's inflow where every link agrees (it does not here -- the spine's five groups into this category are a mix of external and internal_service); or leaving it and saying so in the caveat. Decide it once, because the residual node's carried links have kinds and this is the only mark on the site that does not.

title: spending-window-reconciles would report a nonzero pp.85-125 Transfers Out row as an extension of the spine
description:
internal/check/spendingwindow.go restricts its subjects to the spine nodes whose ROLE is object_category, which correctly excludes transfers/out, fund-balance/contribution and fund-balance/reserve-increase -- the spine draws all three at tier 5 and pp.85-125 decompose none of them.

The cross-tab side is then compared over the UNION, so a cross-tab link sourced from a node the spine has no object-category node for is reported as 'the cross-tab must decompose the spine's right-hand column, never extend it'. For transfers/out that sentence is true in the letter and misleading in the spirit: the spine DOES draw that node, just not as an object category.

REACHABILITY, measured on the committed corpus: p124's Transfers Out row is 266,798 in FY2023-24 Actual and a printed dash in all three later columns, and FY2023-24 is not a column the spine publishes -- so the finding is unreachable today. It becomes reachable the moment that row is nonzero in a budget year.

The repair is a third arm rather than a wider restriction: a cross-tab source that IS a declared flow endpoint on the spine should be reported as 'this schedule decomposes a flow endpoint the spine publishes whole', which is a different defect with a different fix.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE. internal/check/spendingwindow.go and its check spending-window-reconciles were deleted at aef3d8f. Verified at HEAD: the file does not exist and the id is not among the 44 fisc verify reports.

IT WAS ALREADY UNREACHABLE and the bead says so with the measurement: p124's Transfers Out row is 266,798 in FY2023-24 actual and a printed dash in all three later columns, and FY2023-24 is not a column the spine publishes. So the misleading finding it described could not fire on the committed corpus even while the check existed. P4 for that reason.

THE OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING, if the cross-tab comparison is ever rebuilt: a source that IS a declared flow endpoint on the spine, just not as an object category, should be reported as decomposing a flow endpoint the spine publishes whole -- a different defect with a different fix -- rather than as extending the spine. Recorded here rather than re-filed, because nothing in the tree is in a position to implement it.

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: Two hygiene nits from lane E: the drilldown contract's depth table, and scoped()'s second node index
description:
FOUND reviewing fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E), 2026-09-13. Both cosmetic, neither changes an output.

(1) docs/general-fund-drilldown-contract.md's 'what each depth draws' table now reads 0, 1, 2, 1 down its depth column: the revenue step was appended after the division row rather than beside the other depth-1 row. The prose under it says why two rows share a depth ('The steps are a tree and not a chain'), so nothing is wrong; a reader scanning the depth column meets 1 twice, non-adjacently, before reaching the sentence that explains it. Either move the row up beside the other depth-1 row, or replace the depth column with the step key, which is what the client actually matches on.

(2) site/app.js scoped(doc, tiers) builds 'new Map(doc.nodes.map(...))' and its own drawn Set, and its only caller filterLinks has already built both one scope up. Two full passes over the node list per filter where one would do. It is a few hundred nodes on the largest committed document, so this is reuse and not performance: pass the index in, or have scoped take the map filterLinks already holds.

title: buildTable spells the contra sign a second time and drops the printed/inferred statement
description:
FOUND reviewing fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E), 2026-09-13. site/app.js only, two small things in one function.

(1) A SECOND SPELLING OF THE SIGN RULE. markCents is the one place that decides what figure a mark prints -- negative for a contra ribbon, negative for a node whose every ribbon is one -- and every other reader goes through it (render's value tspan, linkDescription, nodeDescription, showTip, pin). buildTable re-derives it: fmtSigned(l.contra ? -l.value_cents : l.value_cents). It agrees today. markCents takes a LAID mark and buildTable renders the unlaid projection, which is why it was written out rather than called; the fix is either a cents-only helper both share, or markCents accepting either.

(2) THE PROVENANCE CELL IS OVERWRITTEN, NOT ADDED TO. The fifth column reads 'printed' or 'diamond inferred' on every row, and on a contra row it now reads the contra sentence instead. A contra row IS printed by the city -- that is the whole claim -- so the table is the one surface where a reader cannot tell a printed reduction from an inferred one. The sentence already has a home on that row (the sign and the red), so the cell can keep saying 'printed' and the words can go beside it or into the source column.

title: scoped() cannot see a whole tier losing its parents, and the harness cannot tell stepDocFor by index from by depth
description:
TWO GAPS LEFT OPEN by fisc-ko1j.11 (lane E), 2026-09-12, both client-side and both covered elsewhere; filed so they are tracked rather than implied.

(1) site/app.js scoped() -- fisc-ng17's fix -- refuses a link end whose parent names a node the document lacks, or which cannot be placed while OTHER nodes of its tier can. It cannot see a WHOLE tier losing its parents: blank every tier-1 line's parent and the fund-group view drops every line->fund link silently, drawing the General Fund with no revenue at all. No banner; the counts line changes (which is visible) but nothing names the fault. Go-side, node-hierarchy-well-formed and fisc-ko1j.10's line-tier arm refuse that document at verify time, so it is unreachable from a published fund-flows.json. A client-side rule that catches it needs to know which tiers NEST, which is tier-number-to-meaning knowledge this file refuses; the honest options are a per-document declaration of nesting tiers on the wire, or leaving it to verify.

(2) stepDocFor(step) reads the year's steps entry by CONFIG.steps.indexOf(step), because page.go emits one entry per declared step in order. A mutation reading steps[depth] instead is GREEN in tools/jscheck and on the shipped site: every step of a year resolves to the same file (fund-flows for sankey, fund-flows-2027 for sankey-2027), so the revenue step read through the fund-group step's entry fetches the right document by coincidence. Measured: no drill.mjs arm goes red on that mutation. Making it fail needs a harness year whose step entries point at DIFFERENT paths per step, which is a config the packager does not ship today -- and would ship the day a step names a third projection.

title: parseStepShapes' Key count is not separately falsifiable
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-12 landing lane D (fisc-ko1j.12). tools/jscheck/harness.mjs's parseStepShapes cross-checks the entry count against TWO field counts, From and Key. The From count alone catches every shape the Key count does: removing ` || out.length !== keys` leaves seam.mjs's step arm green, including on the nested-literal case that arm was written for, because the From count fires on the same disagreement.

So the Key half of that condition is a marker that cannot be shown to fail on its own. It costs nothing and mirrors From's argument one field over, which is why it was kept; but nothing here should be read as evidence it is load-bearing. If a shape is ever found where the two counts disagree -- a step declaring a Key and no From is not legal Go against the current type -- record it here.

The explicit `if (!key) throw` IS load-bearing and is proved: removing it turns seam.mjs's arm red, because that arm now matches the refusal's MESSAGE rather than merely observing that something threw.

title: drill.mjs's everyOpenedView reads the group list off FY2026's spine for both columns
description: tools/jscheck/drill.mjs everyOpenedView takes its six fund groups from goldenGraph() (the FY2025-26 spine) whatever column it walks; since fisc-ko1j.5 each column serves its own spine (COLUMNS[].spine, testdata/sankey-2027.golden.json) and the residual arms already read col.spine(). Harmless today because both spines carry the same six tier-2 ids (fund-group/permanent is FY2024 actual's alone), and the walk would throw rather than skip if a column lacked one; but the day the columns differ the walk pins FY2026's groups against FY2027's chart. Pass col into everyOpenedView and read col.spine().nodes. HYGIENE, found while adding COLUMNS[].spine in fisc-ko1j.5's session.

title: The residual node ranks 0 in its column, and the depth-1 hint points at a column that now holds endpoints that do not open
description: Two cosmetic consequences of fisc-ko1j.5. (a) nodeRank scores a node by the value-weighted fund-group position of its neighbours and ignores a neighbour in no group; the residual node's neighbours are all endpoints (fund-balance/draw, transfers/out, ...) which belong to no group, so its weight is 0 and it takes rank 0 -- the top of the fund column -- rather than resting beside its own group's funds. Its parent IS the group, so nodeRank could fall back to fundGroupOf(node) itself when no neighbour carries one. (b) paintChartHint at depth 1 on the General Fund says 'Click a node in the right-hand column to open it further', and since the residual that column also holds transfers/out and the reserve increase, which drillable refuses. The sentence is still true of the divisions; it could say 'a division'. HYGIENE, found reading the depth-1 layout in fisc-ko1j.5's session; neither changes a figure.

title: drill-reconciles-across-documents cannot see a declared endpoint's decomposition dropped whole
description:
internal/check/drillreconcile.go decides per (endpoint, group) whether a declared
residual endpoint is residual or decomposed from the documents themselves: residual
where the fund-level document carries nothing from it into the group's funds,
decomposed where it carries it whole, a finding where it is split. That rule cannot
tell "pp.127-140 print no such row for this group" from "every such row was dropped
at once": both read as residual and the check stays green.
TestADecompositionDroppedWholeReadsAsResidual pins the behaviour.

Covered today by a sibling at fact grain: revenue-detail-ties-to-spine holds the
spine's transfer_in cell against revenue-by-fund's per fund group at zero tolerance,
and the only exception it declares is general's. So the hole is a document-level
one over facts another check already sees.

Closing it here needs a per-group declaration -- transfers/in residual for {general}
and nothing else, the other four for every group -- which fails closed both ways
(a dropped decomposition reddens, a newly printed general-fund transfer in reddens as
a stale declaration) at the cost of hard-coding what the corpus prints today into the
set fisc-ko1j.5's client carries. Deferred until a drift the sibling does not see is
found, or until the client needs the per-group form anyway.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE, and both halves of it are gone. The subject was internal/check/drillreconcile.go's per-(endpoint, group) residual-vs-decomposed rule, which could not tell 'pp.127-140 print no such row for this group' from 'every such row was dropped at once'. The SIBLING it named as covering the hole at fact grain -- revenue-detail-ties-to-spine -- was deleted in the same commit. Both went at aef3d8f; verified at HEAD, neither exists.

WHAT NOW COVERS THE MONEY, read off fisc verify at HEAD rather than assumed: cuts-tie-along-the-lattice compares revenue-detail -> spine at fund-group-by-category, 134 cells over FY2026 and FY2027 adopted, with the General Fund transfer-in the only declaration held apart. That is the fact-grain cover this bead described, under a different name.

WHAT IS GENUINELY NOT COVERED is the document-level question the bead was deferring anyway -- it was P4 and explicitly 'deferred until a drift the sibling does not see is found'. Nobody found one, and the document-level check it would have been filed against no longer exists to extend.

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: README.md's source table describes each document in prose nothing checks
description:
06822fc corrected README.md's ACFR p41 row, which described p41 as audited after this lane established it is MD&A's condensed statement in millions. Nothing reddened, and nothing would have.

WHY NO CHECK WAS WRITTEN in that commit: a phrase ban over README.md would refuse the true sentences about p54 in the same file, and a check that passes for the wrong reason is worse than an acknowledged gap (AGENTS.md, "Prove it can fail"). So the gap was stated in the commit rather than answered.

WHAT THE TABLE CLAIMS. Each row names a document, a page range, a fact count, a description of what the page holds, and a basis. The fact counts and page ranges are checkable against data/sources.yaml and the store; the DESCRIPTIONS are free prose and are the half that went wrong.

THE PRECEDENT SHAPE, if this is worth doing: internal/export/views_test.go's TestTheLedesProseNamesThePagesScope couples two independent declarations of one claim rather than pinning a string to itself. The analogue here would couple each README row to the same document's entry in data/sources.yaml or its mapping rule note -- both of which already carry a description of what the page holds. That is also what would have caught the p41 row, since the rule notes were corrected in the same commit.

tools/doccheck and tools/beadrefs already scan README.md for other claim shapes, so a gate over this file is not unprecedented.

P4 because the wrong claim is corrected and the table changes only when a document is added.

title: A disjointScopes entry naming a scope the corpus does not carry is never measured, though its comment says otherwise
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD (raised by the checks lens as an observation, verified and filed here).

internal/check/scopepairs.go, the disjointScopes doc comment: "The reason is required and is checked against the corpus by the measured arm below, so a declaration that stops being true goes red."

Measured by reading ARM 2: it iterates allScopePairs(s.Facts) -- the pairs the CORPUS carries -- and looks each up in disjointScopes, skipping any pair not declared. The iteration is never over the declaration table, so an entry whose scope carries no facts is visited by nothing. A typo'd scope name, or a declaration left behind when a scope is retired, reads as safety and measures zero.

Not FAIL-OPEN, measured: ARM 3 requires every co-selected pair to be positively declared, so a typo'd declaration means the REAL pair is undeclared and arm 3 fires. No unsafe merge can be permitted by this gap; the comment is what is wrong, plus the unmeasured declaration it leaves behind.

Pre-existing mechanism -- two entries were added to the table in this range (5e474ae), neither of them stale.

Fix direction: an arm that walks disjointScopes and fails an entry naming a scope no fact carries, which would also catch a retired scope's leftovers; or narrow the comment to say a declaration is measured only while both its scopes are populated. The first is the one that makes the sentence true.
close_reason:
OBSOLETE. internal/check/scopepairs.go and the disjointScopes declaration table were deleted whole at aef3d8f. Verified at HEAD: zero occurrences of disjointScopes in any .go file.

THE DEFECT WAS THE COMMENT, not the guard, and the bead says so: arm 3 required every co-selected pair to be positively declared, so a typo'd entry meant the real pair was undeclared and arm 3 fired. No unsafe merge was ever permitted. What was wrong was a doc comment claiming the declaration was measured against the corpus when the iteration ran over the corpus's pairs and never over the table.

THE SAME SHAPE IN THE REPLACEMENT IS ALREADY GUARDED: structure.ValidateCuts returns the cuts that admit no fact, and structure.Covered reports a fact in no cut. An empty declaration is named rather than silent, which is what this bead asked for.

Closed while trimming the beads about the nine checks aef3d8f deleted.

title: Two survey wording defects: a dash called a blank, and sources.yaml undercounting the mapped ACFR pages
description:
HYGIENE found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD.

(1) docs/acfr-statistical-section.md's p187 bullet says "a City Distribution Cost of 2.8 and a blank wholesale column". The cell prints "-", not blank. This repo's own invariant is that those are different claims -- a dash is a published zero, a blank means the line does not apply -- so the survey should not use the words interchangeably in the one place a future mapper reads to decide which it is.

(2) data/sources.yaml's ACFR comment says "pp.167-169 of it are mapped". p177 is also mapped, by the read-only rule acfr-p0177-debt-by-type (mappings/livermore-acfr-fy2025.yaml, e3d5b8c), and is in the same Statistical Section. The comment undercounts by a page and by a rule.
close_reason: Both halves fixed. (1) docs/acfr-statistical-section.md:159 now reads 'a - in the wholesale column', not 'a blank wholesale column', so the survey no longer uses the two words interchangeably in the one place a future mapper reads to tell a published zero from an absent line. (2) data/sources.yaml:55 now reads 'pp.167-169 and p177 of it are mapped', counting acfr-p0177-debt-by-type.

title: The excess row's Line cell prints the fragment 'over (under) expenditures' on history.html
description:
HYGIENE found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD.

history.html renders the excess row's Line cell as "over (under) expenditures" -- the tail of p168's three-line label "Excess of Revenues / over (under) / expenditures" -- beneath a section heading that carries the rest. Faithful to the fact's row_label as the page prints it, and the Category column disambiguates, but as the row's visible name it reads as a fragment.

Fix directions, in the order they preserve provenance: leave row_label as printed and give the view a display label; or record the joined label in the mapping with the wrap noted. Do NOT rewrite the fact's row_label to something the page does not print.
notes: Premise re-measured: p168 wraps the label as 'Excess of Revenues' / 'over (under)' / 'expenditures' (data/extracted/livermore-acfr-fy2025/pages/p0168.txt:41-43), and the mapping row anchors only the tail, so the fact's row_label is the fragment and stays so. Fixed at the view layer: export.Section.Rows maps the printed label to the display label 'Excess of Revenues over (under) expenditures' -- the three printed lines joined, not invented phrasing. Line and Category now differ only in the taxonomy's capital E, which matches the page's existing one-row-category pattern (Fire | Fire).
close_reason: Fixed at the view layer, as the bead's preferred direction required, leaving the fact's row_label as p168 prints it. internal/export/history_test.go:239 maps the printed fragment to the display label 'Excess of Revenues over (under) expenditures' -- the page's three wrapped lines joined, not invented phrasing -- and :259 asserts the rendered th.

title: buildHistoryPage's section key places any future fund_balance series under the Excess heading silently
description:
DESIGN found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD.

internal/project/history.go: buildHistoryPage claims series by exact (kind, fund_group). The changes view's "Excess of Revenues..." section is keyed {fund_balance, ""}, so any future fund_balance series with no fund group mapped into acfr-changes-in-fund-balances lands under that heading with no refusal -- p169's Net change line is the concrete candidate, if fisc-qyrw ever publishes it once the 2023 copy defect is dealt with.

The unclaimed-series guard cannot see this: the series IS claimed, by the wrong section. Every other refusal in the view (unclaimed series, empty section, contested key, count reconciliation) fires; this one shape is silent by construction.

Not a current defect -- measured, the scope carries revenue, expenditure and the single excess series only. Worth either a narrower key (row_path, or an explicit series allow-list per section) or a note on the section declaration saying what it will swallow.
notes: Premise re-measured before the fix: dist/data/changes-in-fund-balances.json carries revenue, expenditure and the single fund_balance excess series, so the swallow is a hazard and not a live defect, as the description says. One stale pointer: buildHistoryPage lives in internal/export/page.go, not internal/project/history.go. Fixed by closing the section on a Rows declaration (export.Section.Rows) rather than a narrower key or a note: a non-nil Rows refuses a series it does not name and a name matching no series, and it is the same declaration that carries fisc-efo8's display label, so the two cannot disagree.
close_reason: Fixed by declaration rather than by a narrower key: export.Section.Rows (internal/export/export.go:448) is non-nil for the section, and internal/export/page.go:2098,2163 refuse both a series Rows does not name and a name matching no series. It is the same declaration that carries fisc-efo8's display label, so the two cannot disagree.

title: Two page attributions in quantity_test.go name pages that print neither token
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review pass two over main..HEAD, verified by grep over the whole extracted corpus.

internal/quantity/quantity_test.go, TestAmountPerUnit's token list, comments added by e3d5b8c:
- `"32.50", // p186 meter charges` -- 32.50 appears on exactly one page of the corpus, ACFR p183 (the FTE table). p186 is Water and Sewer Rates and prints it nowhere.
- `"1,044", // p180` -- 1,044 appears on exactly one page, ACFR p188 (Single Family Residential flow, in mg). p180 prints it nowhere.

Both are `grep -l` over data/extracted/*/pages/*.txt, one hit each. The tokens are still valid inputs to AmountPerUnit, so no assertion is wrong; the provenance pointers beside them are.

e3d5b8c's commit message lists the same probe tokens WITHOUT page attributions and is correct as written. The comments invented them.

Fix: name the page that prints each token, or drop the attribution. This is the shape AGENTS.md's provenance rule exists to prevent -- a pointer that resolves to nothing, in a repo whose feature is that every figure's pointer resolves.

title: balances.html's lede says balances are split into five categories over a block that prints four
description:
HYGIENE found by /code-review over 6ad828f^..3286b77.

pkg/cmd/export/data.go, the balances.html view: the lede reads 'split into the five categories that say how spendable each dollar is', and p167's All Other Governmental Funds block prints four (no Assigned row) — which the page's own caveat states directly beneath ('that block has four components, not five'). The sentence is defensible as naming the GASB 54 taxonomy rather than counting rows, but it is published prose in tension with the caveat two paragraphs down. Consider 'the GASB 54 categories' or 'up to five categories'.
close_reason: Fixed by removing the count rather than correcting it: the balances lede (pkg/cmd/export/data.go:1243-1245) now reads 'split into the GASB 54 categories that say how spendable each dollar is', with no number to contradict the block. The four-not-five fact is stated where it can be read against the page, in caveatNoAssignedRow: p167's All Other Governmental Funds block prints no Assigned line in any year.

title: The rule schema forces a kind on rules whose every row skips, so read-only rules declare kinds that are false of their pages
description:
DESIGN found by /code-review over 6ad828f^..3286b77.

acfr-p0177-debt-by-type declares kind: fund_balance for a schedule of outstanding debt, and acfr-p0169-other-financing declares kind: transfer_in over rows that include bond proceeds and escrow payments. Both notes say so honestly ('the kind above is the schema's required field, inert while every row is skipped').

Measured inert, three ways: (1) no facts — every row is skip or quantity, so Row.EffectiveKind is never consulted; (2) no rollup covers either rule, so validateRollupKinds never reads their Rule.Kind; (3) nothing in internal/check reads a rule's kind. Un-skipping anything trips validateRule loudly (no column fiscal_year, shared column identity on p177), so the false kind cannot leak into a fact without other refusals firing first.

But a false-though-inert declaration is the shape this repo refuses elsewhere — the ACFR mapping's own header records fighting wrapped_labels: ["0.0"], a declaration that worked and was untrue. Options: make kind optional when every row is skip/quantity; or a kind value that states read-only-ness; or accept the note as sufficient and close this with that decision. fisc-7jtl (no Kind states a stock truthfully) is the adjacent bead; this one is about the schema forcing SOME kind meanwhile.

title: excess-of-revenues-identity's duplicate arm says the column is excluded, and it is not
description:
FALSE-CLAIM found by /code-review over 6ad828f^..3286b77.

internal/check/excessidentity.go: when a column carries two excess facts, the finding says 'the identity has no single value to check, so this column is excluded from it' — but the loop then treats the column as complete (complete++) and evaluates the identity against the FIRST excess value, so a second finding can fire quoting an arbitrarily chosen side, and the two findings contradict each other. Reachable only on runs that already fail (the duplicate finding always fires), so no green run is wrong; the message is.

Fix direction: track duplicated columns and skip them in the summary loop, or reword the finding to what the code does. Land with a test extending TestExcessIdentityRefusesADuplicatedExcessLine so the dup column is asserted absent from complete.

Related measurement from the same review: 5e474ae's commit message says the +100-cent mutation on the FY2025 excess fact 'reddened exactly this check'. Measured this session: it reddens fact-token-reparses as well (the token no longer reparses to the mutated cents) — any single-field mutation of a committed fact trips a store-level witness beside this identity. The quoted finding text is genuine; 'exactly' is not.
notes: Review pass two (fable, main..HEAD) re-confirmed this from two independent lenses. Also measured there: the +100-cent mutation on the FY2025 excess fact reddens EXACTLY two checks -- excess-of-revenues-identity ('off by $1.00') and fact-token-reparses -- and no third, because fact ids are content-addressed over identity and never over the amount (internal/fact/fact.go). So the correction in 496827f's predecessor is complete, not merely directionally right.

title: A chart over the ACFR ten-year series; history.html and balances.html are tables by design
description: fisc-oakx.4 landed the ten-year reader surface as two server-rendered tables (history.html over changes-in-fund-balances, balances.html over fund-balances, both on site/history.html.tmpl) with no script, which is what let the lane ship no tools/jscheck module. A line or bar chart over these series -- 22 series x 10 audited columns and 9 x 10, in dist/data/changes-in-fund-balances.json and dist/data/fund-balances.json -- is a separate change: it touches site/app.js or ships a new client, so per AGENTS.md's node boundary it owes a jscheck module in the same commit. The per-row Shape sparkline the tables already carry is server-rendered SVG and is not this. Unlike the trends document, every column here is one comparable group (all audited), so a cross-year line is honest -- the comparability objection that keeps growth off trends.html does not apply within these documents.

title: memcheck reports a dated line-leading CORRECTED twice
description:
tools/memcheck carries two correction patterns -- an ISO-dated 'corrected
2026-08-29' anywhere in a body, and an ALL-CAPS line-leading 'CORRECTED'. A
paragraph opening 'CORRECTED 2026-08-29.' satisfies both, so it is reported as
two findings on one sentence.

WHY IT IS TWO PATTERNS AND NOT ONE: the dated form catches a correction quoted
mid-sentence, and the line-leading form catches an undated one ('CORRECTED,
twice over.'). Neither covers the other. Merging them into a single alternation
would work but has to keep both arms falsifiable.

HARMLESS TODAY -- the excerpts are identical, so a reader sees the same line
twice and fixes it once. Filed rather than fixed because it is HYGIENE and
AGENTS.md's triage says a review pass fixes WRONG-OUTPUT and FAIL-OPEN and files
the rest.

THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT is the gap worth noting: the one case
exercising that body asserts only len(hits) > 0, so the duplicate is invisible
to it. Any fix should assert the count.

Found by /code-review over b2e67aa.

title: (BUG) path.go cites the export command's Example for an invocation that lives in the contract doc
description:
pkg/cmdutil/path.go, looksLikeSource's doc comment ends: "...and the NEXT
--clean deletes the Go package. THAT HAPPENED TO BE SPELLED OUT IN THIS
COMMAND'S OWN EXAMPLE."

The location is wrong and it is one word. The export command's Example reads
`fisc export --output build/site --clean`. The invocation the sentence means is
committed, spelled `fisc export -o site`, in internal/project/project.go:4,
docs/sankey-contract.md:18, pkg/cmdutil/path_test.go:163 and fisc-gxa.1's note
-- so it is the CONTRACT DOC, not the Example.

The hazard the comment describes is real and the sentence is a DATED claim
about a pre-commit draft: path_test.go:163, written in the same commit, reads
"(which this command's Example ONCE suggested)" -- past tense, matching
path.go's own "happened to be".

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY. It is the finding fisc-gyg9's author reported as
"verified by hand" and got wrong anyway, by grepping only "--output site" and
missing the short spelling -- a one-spelling grep in a session whose entire
subject was one-spelling greps. It was then downgraded from REFUTED to a
one-word fix by the adversarial pass. It is filed rather than carried in a
closed bead because a P4 about a misleading cross-reference is exactly the class
this project keeps rediscovering years stale.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: pkg/cmdutil/path.go is one of the thirteen files in
this repository carrying a line inside a raw string literal that reads exactly
like a comment (`// ~/documents`), so a textual "only comment lines changed"
check over the diff is unsound here. Prove it with a token-stream hash --
tools/codehash, which is in the tree and on main since 2f22036, run by hand as
`make codehash FILES=...` before and after and diffed.

title: Strip narration: ~3,000 comment lines in blocks that describe the code's past
description:
Delete the comment prose that talks about the code's PAST rather than its
present. AGENTS.md already carries the rule ("History's home is git"); this is
the sweep that applies it.

MEASURED 2026-09-03, at block level rather than line level, because narration
lives in paragraphs and a per-line grep reports 1.1% and badly understates it:

  production Go   1,636 blocks / 10,969 comment lines
                  108 blocks (7%) contain a narration marker = 1,752 lines (16%)
  test Go         1,671 blocks /  7,749 comment lines
                  124 blocks (7%) contain a narration marker = 1,259 lines (16%)

~3,000 lines. Narrated blocks run about 2.3x the average block length.
Commonest markers: "used to" (91), "no longer" (42), "before this" (40),
"the old X" (31), "until now" (15). FIVE "Found by" CREDIT LINES SURVIVE IN
PRODUCTION despite fisc-pm8f's lane 1 deleting 66 -- that pass was incomplete,
not wrong.

WHY THIS IS THE CHEAP PASS. Verification cost attaches to claims WRITTEN OR
KEPT. A deletion cannot introduce a false claim, so this needs no adversarial
verification -- which is what made the abandoned rewrite campaign cost 42.5
minutes and 411k agent tokens for 148 comment lines.

TWO CAVEATS THAT BOUND THE OPERATION.

(1) IT IS NOT GREP-AND-DELETE. fisc-pm8f measured that of 62 comments matching a
    self-correction grep, only 14 were the erratum the rule names; the rest were
    design history explaining why the code has its shape, or mutation proofs.
    The rule is KEEP THE RULE, DROP THE HISTORY THAT ARGUED FOR IT, judged per
    block. Every mutation proof stays -- "reverting `if !ok || !c.Assignable` to
    `if !ok` makes it fail on the status assertion directly" is unrecoverable
    from the code and is the class AGENTS.md's "Prove it can fail" depends on.

(2) A TEXTUAL FILTER IS UNSOUND HERE. Thirteen lines inside RAW STRING LITERALS
    look exactly like comments, six of them in files this sweep touches:
      internal/project/project.go   // verify  (twice)
      pkg/cmd/export/data.go        // verify
      pkg/cmd/export/export.go      // status
      internal/check/coverage.go    // export
      internal/check/facts.go       // build
      pkg/cmdutil/path.go           // ~/documents
    An edit to one builds, passes the suite -- nothing pins most printed strings
    -- and reads as a comment change in the diff. tools/codehash exists for
    exactly this: it hashes the token stream with comments off, so a comments-
    only change is provable rather than asserted. It is on the abandoned
    comment-sweep branch at 71fd344 and can be cherry-picked, or re-derived in
    about 35 lines with go/scanner.

VERIFICATION. codehash identical before and after; gofmt; make pre-commit;
make lint (revive's `exported` rule still requires a doc on every exported
identifier, so a narrated block that IS the whole doc must be replaced, not
deleted); facts.jsonl unmoved; fisc verify count read off a freshly built
binary.
notes:
2026-09-04 THE SWEEP IS CANCELLED AND REPLACED BY A STANDING RULE IN AGENTS.md. P2 -> P4. This bead now owns one question only: did the rule work?

WHY, AND IT IS THIS BEAD'S OWN HEADLINE NUMBER THAT DECIDES IT. The description says '~3,000 comment lines' and reads as deletion volume ('Delete the comment prose that talks about the code's PAST'). It is not. It is every line of every BLOCK a narration sentence sits in -- what you must READ. Deleting the block takes the rule with the history, which caveat (1) already forbids.

MEASURED AT a14b6c2, both granularities:
  per-line  185 of 19,137 comment lines carry a history marker  ~1%
  per-block 2,138 lines across 164 blocks in 62 files          ~11%
The per-line figure is the deletion volume and the per-block figure is the reading cost. This bead argued the per-line grep 'badly understates it'; that is true of the reading cost and false of the work. AGENTS.md had independently measured 247 of 18,746 at 823de73 -- the same 1.3% -- and drew the opposite conclusion from it.

AND AGENTS.md'S CAUSAL AUDIT ALREADY SAID SO. Reclassifying the false-text findings by cause: restating-a-rule-that-changed-elsewhere 35%, never-true-when-written 23%, quoted-number-drifted 22%, HISTORY 15% -- the smallest of the four -- followed by 'the narrative register is the carrier and not the cause, and the hypothesis that prompted the audit came back mostly wrong'. This bead was filed against that finding without engaging it.

WHY OPPORTUNISTIC REACHES IT ANYWAY, measured at a14b6c2: all 62 files carrying narration were touched in the last 100 commits -- ZERO cold files -- and 40 consecutive ordinary commits reach 71% of the narrated lines. The heaviest files are also the highest-churn: internal/check/coverage.go 154 lines / 27 commits, internal/export/page.go 126 / 35, internal/check/check.go 105 / 22. There is no residue a sweep would catch that a lane will not.

TWO THINGS THE SWEEP WOULD HAVE COST that the standing rule does not. It would have shipped ~2,000 lines of deletion UNREVIEWED, since the lane was scoped without a review loop -- the fisc-i92i shape. And it would have judged every block COLD; the hard case is a paragraph whose history IS the evidence for the rule it ends with (internal/check/coverage.go's staleDeclarations entry is the worked example), and telling those apart needs the code open.

WHAT IS LEFT HERE: re-measure the per-line count in a few months. If it has not fallen materially from 185, the standing rule is not being applied and this becomes a real bead again. Nothing else in this bead's description should be acted on; caveat (1) is still correct and caveat (2) is false, per the 2026-09-04 note above.
2026-09-06: fisc-2rud carries a proposed METHOD for this sweep -- a cheap-model fleet, deletion-only, codehash as the gate -- and the argument for why it must not be pointed at a rewrite. Filed apart because it applies to the class C internal/inline work too.

title: (BUG) extract.py's 18.7-MiB-against-7.6 figures do not reproduce; the argument does
description:
tools/extract.py:125 argues for the flat word row with a size comparison:
"instead of ten lines with each bbox float on its own. There are 208,221 [words
...]" and the surrounding sentence's figures -- 18.7 MiB against what fits in
7.6 -- did not reproduce when two agents re-measured it independently today.

MEASURED. Re-encoding all 208,221 committed words: flat rows 7.31-7.32 MiB,
object rows 12.67-12.68 MiB, pure value bytes 6.12-6.13 MiB, key overhead 5.36
MiB (27 bytes per word, exactly). For the indent variants: 12.77 MiB
flat-with-indent1, 8.20 on disk, 19.13 for object-words-with-indent1. None of
those is 18.7 against 7.6.

THE ARGUMENT SURVIVES UNDER EVERY VARIANT -- indent really is the expensive
choice, and that is what the sentence is for. It is the two figures that do not
reproduce, and neither the commit that wrote them nor the file says what they
were measured over, so nothing in the tree pins them.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. The corpus grew after the number was
written; a figure whose baseline no longer exists cannot be checked, only
replaced. Whoever fixes it should state what was encoded and with which
options, per AGENTS.md's rule that a count which is the evidence for a decision
must be pinned by something that re-measures it.

Adjacent and already fixed in fisc-b93j's first unit: the SAME paragraph's
neighbouring claim, "at 208k words the key names would outweigh the values",
was false in tools/extract.py and in internal/geom/geom.go at once -- keys are
0.87x the values. Both copies were corrected together per fisc-xbd4. This is
the third figure in the same argument and the only one still unpinned.

title: acfr_p177_test.go cites testdata/README.md by line number
description:
acfr_p177_test.go's doc comment cites testdata/README.md by LINE NUMBER. Any edit
above that line silently repoints it, and nothing goes red.

A pointer that names a line is a second source of where something is -- the same
defect as a comment giving a symbol's file path, which fisc-pm8f's rule 1
removes. Here the target is a data file with no symbol to look up, so the PATH
stays and only the line number goes. Replace it with the row's own key
(acfr-p0177), which the README's table carries and which survives an edit.

Found while auditing for fisc-pm8f; not fixed there because that sweep does not
touch testdata references.

title: TestEveryShardedPageHasItsExtractedText cannot go red while the store holds one document
description:
pkg/cmd/export/facts_test.go, TestEveryShardedPageHasItsExtractedText (doc comment at :421, func at :434). The test walks assets.Pages and asserts each has committed extracted text under data/extracted/<doc>/pages/pNNNN.txt.

IT CANNOT CURRENTLY FAIL. The store holds one document, livermore-budget-fy2026-2027, whose facts span pp.66-170, while data/extracted/ commits a contiguous p0001..p0268 for it. So every page the store can shard is committed by construction. fact-offset-points-at-token already forecloses the underlying case from the other direction -- a fact whose offset does not land on its token in the committed page text fails verify.

It also has no empty-store guard, so it would pass silently on a store with no pages at all. TestTheSiteLinksEveryShardItShips, further down the same file (the guard is at :489-491), does carry one -- "if shipped == 0 { t.Fatal(\"no fact-store file shipped, so this test asserts nothing\") }" -- which is the shape to copy. It is the SHAPE to copy rather than a sibling of this test: the test it guards never calls buildFactAssets.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH KEEPING: it is a guard for the SECOND document. The p76 case it was written for was real -- the store covered 21 pages and the site shipped 20, because p76 is cited by no projection's metadata.sources -- and what keeps the two equal now is pageIndex() seeding buildSite's cited set (facts.go:471). The comment says all of this as of 18d4ef6.

NOT WORTH DOING NOW. Filed per 'Nothing leaves a pass unfiled' because a test that cannot go red is the vacuity class internal/check/vacuity.go exists for, and this one is not declared anywhere. When a second document lands, check that this arm can fail before trusting it; adding the empty-store guard is a one-liner that can go in at the same time.

Found by /code-review over bcbc4fb^..18d4ef6.
close_reason:
THE EMPTY-STORE GUARD LANDED IN f9bed63. THE BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE, and that is recorded here rather than closed over.

WHAT THE BEAD SAID: 'IT CANNOT CURRENTLY FAIL. The store holds one document ... every page the store can shard is committed by construction', and 'WHY IT IS STILL WORTH KEEPING: it is a guard for the SECOND document.'

MEASURED AT 0448a5b, WHERE THE SECOND DOCUMENT LANDED: the arm STILL cannot fail. livermore-acfr-fy2025 is extracted contiguously and in full, p0001..p0195, exactly as the Budget Book is p0001..p0268. So every page the store can shard still has its committed text by construction, for two documents instead of one. A second document was never what would make this falsifiable; a PARTIALLY EXTRACTED document is. The comment above the test now says that instead of promising the opposite.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is the half that was always worth having and is a different failure: without a guard the test passes on a store with NO pages at all -- the vacuity internal/check/vacuity.go exists for, one package over and undeclared. Proven both ways: with the guard, an emptied assets.Pages fails 'the store shards no pages, so this test asserts nothing'; with the guard removed, the same emptied store passes silently.

A SECOND ARM WAS ADDED THAT THE BEAD DID NOT ASK FOR: the loop must reach at least two documents. A guard that merely counted pages would be satisfied by a store that had silently lost one, which is now the live failure mode rather than a hypothetical one.

Closed on the guard, not on the falsifiability. If a document is ever extracted in part, re-read this test before trusting it.

title: Two byob-derived Go memories name things this codebase does not have
description:
Found auditing the 52 injected memories against the tree. Neither is false about Go; both are wrong about THIS repo, and both are injected every session.

(1) atomic-rename-samedir ends 'Wrap in a WriteFileAtomic helper.' There is no WriteFileAtomic here. The helper already exists and is cmdutil.WriteFile, pkg/cmdutil/atomic.go:35, with the signature func WriteFile(path string, perm fs.FileMode, fn func(io.Writer) error) error. Following the memory literally produces a duplicate helper. Fixed in place in this pass by naming the real one; this bead records why.

(2) prompter-tty-check prescribes checking IO.IsStdinTTY() and returning a sentinel ErrNotTTY from every Prompter method. This codebase has no Prompter and no ErrNotTTY -- only IOStreams.IsStdinTTY() at pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go. fisc is non-interactive and never prompts, so the memory is advice for code that does not exist. Harmless, left as-is, recorded so a future audit does not re-derive it.

The owner's instruction when asked how far to prune the 24 byob-derived generic Go memories was 'Byob stay open forever', which is bead vocabulary and does not clearly settle the memory question; nothing was pruned on the strength of it. See fisc-u2as for the one in that set that is an active contradiction rather than a nit.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-09-18, both items still exactly as this bead describes: pkg/cmdutil/atomic.go:35 declares WriteFile with the stated signature and there is no WriteFileAtomic; Prompter and ErrNotTTY appear in no .go file, while IOStreams.IsStdinTTY does. Nothing to redo.

AND THE QUESTION THIS BEAD LEFT OPEN NOW HAS A NUMBER, which is what it was missing. Of 54 injected memories, 26 mention NOTHING in this project -- no fisc- id, no path under internal/ or site/, no page, no schedule, no bd or Dolt. They are 10,671 of 47,831 characters, 22% of what bd prime injects into every session:

  blank-ident-assert, commit-attribution-names-the-writing-model,
  context-first-param, defer-unlock, delegate-at-commit-boundaries-not-lane-
  boundaries, doc-comment-shape, errors-is-as, errors-message-style,
  errors-wrap-w, git-add-all-sweeps-worktrees, goroutine-exit-path,
  got-want-order, initialism-casing, lfs-quota-and-pointer-text,
  no-blank-error-discard, no-get-prefix, pass-by-value-default,
  principles-dry-kiss-solid, prompter-tty-check, quote-strings-in-errors,
  receiver-name, schema_version, sync-oncevalue, test-cleanup, test-helper,
  validate-at-boundaries

SEVERAL RESTATE A RULE make lint ALREADY FAILS ON, which makes them a second source in the sense AGENTS.md's 'Where writing goes' names, not merely a context cost. .golangci.yml enables errorlint (errors-wrap-w, errors-is-as), errcheck (no-blank-error-discard, blank-ident-assert) and revive (receiver-name, initialism-casing, no-get-prefix) among sixteen. A gate that fails is a better home for those than a paragraph that arrives unasked. The mapping needs reading per memory before any is forgotten -- some carry an argument the linter's message does not.

NOT ALL 26 ARE THE SAME KIND. git-add-all-sweeps-worktrees, lfs-quota-and-pointer-text, commit-attribution-names-the-writing-model and delegate-at-commit-boundaries-not-lane-boundaries are about working in THIS repo even though they name no path in it; they are not generic Go style and should not be swept with the rest.

STILL THE OWNER'S CALL, and still not settled by 'byob issues stay open' -- said again on 2026-09-18, and it is bead vocabulary both times. The memory question is: forget the generic Go style memories that a linter already enforces, keep the rest. Nothing pruned on the strength of an answer about beads.
